540795|2026-06.headline: Dynamic Cables Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to a record Q1 level, with EBITDA up 41% to INR38 crore and order book at INR811 crore.
540795|2026-06.overview: Management reported record first-quarter revenue, up 33% YoY, with EBITDA up 41% to INR38 crore (margin 10.9%) and PAT up 37% to INR25 crore. Growth was largely price-driven: volume grew only 5-6% against a high base of roughly 25-26% last year, as aluminium price spikes led to order postponements in April-May. The company entered the US market in the quarter with first supplies, and the new capacity expansion is on track for commissioning from September 2026, with meaningful revenue expected from Q4. Order book stood at INR811 crore as of 30 June 2026, with customers booking shorter cycles at elevated prices.

segments.name: Railway signalling
segments.commentary: Temporarily held back due to weak margins and competition; not a shutdown. Zero contribution in last Q1, so no base effect this quarter.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: 13% of revenue. US contributed about 15% of exports in its first quarter; Asia, Southeast Asia and Africa remain the core; Middle East negligible.

guidance_outlook: No formal annual guidance; management reiterated 18-20% growth record over the last 10-15 years and aims to sustain a similar long-term rate, with some quarters of higher, others of moderate growth.
New plant (about INR45 crore capex) to commission from September 2026; meaningful revenue expected only from Q4 FY27.

US market: margins initially similar to domestic, with possible incremental margins later; no one-year target given.
capex_capacity: New plant: capex about INR45 crore, commissioning from September 2026 (delay behind, on track per management).
Existing capacity utilisation about 85%.

demand_pricing: Price variation clause in variable-price contracts passes input cost changes to customers; fixed-price contracts are hedged by booking raw material at order time (about 20% of order book is fixed-price).
Order book of INR811 crore; April-May order inflow was weak as customers resisted booking at elevated aluminium prices; orders now limited to near-term (2-4 month) execution.
Order cycles and order sizes have shortened due to global volatility and tariffs; management says dispatches not impacted.
Competition described as healthy for now despite capacity expansion across the industry; demand picking up with expansion.
US market is distribution-led; competition is global (US local makers, Mexico, Turkey, India, China). Management cites large replacement demand over 10-20 years.
Management says some Adani/Birla cable business is for captive use; Birla focused on house wires; sees low risk to orders from these groups.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company protecting margins if copper and aluminium costs stay high?
qa_highlights.answer: Variable-price contracts carry a clause passing input cost changes to customers; for fixed-price orders, raw material is booked at order time to protect margins.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of Q1 volume and realisation growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume grew 5-6% YoY; most of the balance of revenue growth came from aluminium-driven price increases. Base effect was high at about 25-26% volume growth last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why was growth weaker in Q1 and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Base effect, plus customer order postponements after a sharp input price rise in March-May. Management expects improvement as prices settle but calls the environment very uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new plant on schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, regulatory delays are behind; commissioning planned for September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why is order book only about 10% up YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers were reluctant to book at elevated prices in April-May; weak order booking was industry-wide and should pick up as prices stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US export opportunity and business model?
qa_highlights.answer: First US supplies started this quarter after 15-18 months of work on licences and tariffs; US contributed about 15% of exports. Model is distributor-led, with HV/LV and MV cables licensed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off and full-year guidance position?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs; the high growth came from price increases. No annual guidance, but long-term growth of 18-20% is maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue will the new capex add and how fast will it ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Meaningful revenue from Q4 FY27; target 80-85% utilisation by end FY28; asset turnover 6-7x on INR45 crore capex.

qa_highlights.question: Is pricing competition intensifying from capacity expansions?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition is currently healthy; demand is rising in step with industry expansion, and the T&D story is seen as secular.

qa_highlights.question: Why was debt higher versus March 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory value rose 20-25% due to higher raw material prices (quantity unchanged); receivables comparison on last-six-month sales is unchanged in debtor days.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company diversifying into house wires?
qa_highlights.answer: Only the B2B building wire segment, not B2C distribution or branding; positioned as an additional product in similar segments.

Industry-wide capacity additions in HV/EHV could pressure pricing later.

540795|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 31% YoY to INR712 crore and operating margin held at 10.44%, though Q2 gross margin fell to 16-17%.
540795|2026-09.overview: Dynamic Cables reported H1 FY27 revenue of INR712 crore (up 31% YoY), operating profit of INR74.3 crore (up 29%) at a 10.44% margin, and PAT of INR47.1 crore (up 24%). Management attributed the Q2 gross margin decline to product and order mix plus some commodity volatility, and said volume growth was about 6% in the quarter, with the rest of growth from price. The new manufacturing plant's machinery is installed and is expected to contribute from H2 FY27, with a ramp-up over 3-4 quarters. Management reiterated 10-11% EBITDA margin and sub-15%-of-EBITDA finance cost guidance and a long-term ~20% value growth CAGR.

Finance cost to stay below 15% of EBITDA, including the new facility; six-month figure is about 10-11%.

Management says capex will be ongoing, with brownfield or greenfield expansions announced from time to time.

Raw material price pass-through: 80-90% of contracts have price variation clauses; fixed-price contracts are under 20% of the book.
Exports are about 7-8% of order book; US shipments were weak in the quarter due to high sea freight and insurance costs and tariff concerns.
Order booking has improved, per management, and is expected to improve further as aluminium prices correct; aluminium cited at falling from about INR3,800 to INR3,000 per analyst.
Top 10 customers contribute about 40-45% of sales; 70-80% of sales come from repeat customers on a yearly basis.
Management says no impact seen so far from UltraTech's entry (UltraVolt), with housewire the most exposed segment.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in finance cost despite falling quarter-end borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said finance cost is levied on average working capital utilisation plus vendor financing charges; it is not linked to the new plant, and six-month finance cost is about 10-11% of EBITDA, with a stated ceiling of 15%.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue can the new facility generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment of INR40-45 crore at 6-7x asset turn implies INR240-250 crore revenue potential, ramping over 3-4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin decline to 16-17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited product and order mix shifts quarter to quarter and some commodity volatility, which is largely passed through; the margin decline was not due to commodity inflation.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q2 growth came from volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth was about 6% in Q2; management declined to split value growth into price and volume beyond this, and said EBITDA per ton is not the right lens.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 20% long-term value growth but gave no quantitative FY27 or FY28 guidance, citing caution after high H1 price growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is there competitive impact from UltraTech's entry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no impact has been seen so far from UltraVolt; it noted housewire is the segment most likely to be affected first.

540797|2026-03.headline: Shalby Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 9.4% to INR295.5 crore and EBITDA 43.1% to INR37.4 crore, with PAT lifted by a lower tax regime.
540797|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 9.4% YoY to INR295.5 crore and EBITDA rose to INR37.4 crore (margin 12.7% vs 9.7%). Consolidated PAT swung to INR18.5 crore from a loss of INR12.2 crore, helped by the move to the new 25% tax regime. Full-year revenue grew 4.8% to INR1,168.2 crore, and management attributed the slowdown to Gurugram turbulence, the US-Iran conflict affecting international patients, government payment delays and doctor attrition. Standalone EBITDA was flat YoY at INR37.1 crore, with margin down to 16.1% from 17.7%. MedTech revenue grew about 45% YoY to roughly INR40 crore with EBITDA turning positive for a second straight quarter.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said international patients were 60% of Gurugram revenue at healthy margins, hit in Q4 by the US-Iran conflict; April and May showed a strong comeback. Breakeven timing was not given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is debt rising and where is it used?

qa_highlights.question: Why did top-line growth slow to single digits in FY26 after 15-16% CAGR in FY23-25?

540797|2026-06.headline: Shalby Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.6% YoY to ₹338.6 cr, but EBITDA was flat at ₹49 cr and margin fell to 14.5% from 16%.
540797|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 11.6% YoY to ₹338.6 cr while EBITDA was nearly flat at ₹49 cr, pulling margin down about 150 bps to 14.5%. Consolidated PAT rose to ₹10.5 cr from ₹7.7 cr, helped by a lower group tax rate, though PBT fell to ₹19.7 cr from ₹22.7 cr. Hospitals grew revenue about 7% but standalone EBITDA margin fell to 18.4% from 21.6%, while MedTech revenue (about ₹47 cr) and India entity revenue (about ₹36 cr) grew sharply and consolidated MedTech EBITDA turned positive for a fourth straight quarter. Management guided to hospital margins of up to 20% for the full year and to double-digit MedTech EBITDA margins, with both reliant on items not yet visible in the numbers.

financial_highlights.change: down from ₹22.7 cr YoY; PBT margin 5.8%
up from ₹7.7 cr YoY; PAT margin 3.1% vs 2.5%
~+130% YoY per entity figure; ~+98% YoY per call

segments.name: Hospitals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹259 cr (+7% YoY), EBITDA ₹47.8 cr at 18.4% margin vs 21.6%. Occupied beds 701 (+9.8% YoY), occupancy 51%, ARPOB ₹44,711 (vs ₹45,673), ALOS 3.69 days (vs 3.53).

segments.name: Shalby International (Gurgaon)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹26.2 cr (vs ₹23.2 cr YoY), ARPOB ₹91,326, ALOS 3.8 days. Achieved first EBITDA break-even since acquisition, reported at about 7% EBITDA margin; occupancy about 24% per analyst question.

segments.name: MedTech – SMTL India
segments.commentary: Revenue ~₹36 cr per call (+29% QoQ, +98% YoY); management also cited India revenue growth of over 100% in volumes. Figures in the call are inconsistent (₹22.9 cr cited elsewhere).

segments.name: MedTech – US (SATUS)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~₹38.8 cr with about 9% sequential growth; standalone EBITDA marginally negative. US volumes flat YoY; FX headwind cited.

segments.name: MedTech – Singapore (SGTPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹9.9 million, lower sequentially; EBITDA about ₹5.8 million, a significant improvement vs prior quarters.

guidance_outlook: Hospital EBITDA margin: management is 'strongly confident' of reaching up to 20% for the full year FY27.
Gross margin expected to rise 100–200 bps each quarter going forward.

MedTech: double-digit EBITDA margin expected after US cost initiatives; half of progress made, remainder expected over the next 6 months. Monthly cash burn to fall ~₹3 cr/month from initiatives done in Q1 and a further ~₹3 cr/month once a project is implemented by Q4 FY27.
Shalby International occupancy expected to reach ~30% from Q3 or Q4 FY27; PBT break-even targeted around Q3–Q4 FY27 (6–9 months).
Group ROCE, currently ~7% (standalone ~9.5%), expected to reach 11–13% in 1–2 years.
Gurgaon unit to pay no tax for next 2–3 years due to carried-forward losses. Hospital tax rate moved to ~26% from 35%.
Inventory holding days expected to improve about 30%.
capex_capacity: Cumulative capex of about ₹160 cr in recent years, including bunker facility, robotics and MedTech investments; management expects minimal capex in the current and next year.
Bunkers (radiation facilities) installed in units last year; activation in Q1 with further uptick expected in Q2, including government-scheme coverage for bunker treatments.

Mumbai expansion: 200-bed greenfield Asha Parekh Hospital project; discussions ongoing with trustees, no approval yet. Funding by debt or internal accruals to be decided; no further debt for hospitals or MedTech expected.
47 transplants in Q1 (41 kidney, 5 liver, 1 bone marrow); liver transplant and KTP doctors recently replaced, full effect expected from Q2.
demand_pricing: Government share of payer mix rose to 32% from 24% a year ago; mix now 30% self-pay, 38% insurance, 32% government. Management cited a super-specialty rate win at Krishna unit.
TPA renewals underway, with management expecting a 5–7% revenue uplift from renewals and tie-ups in discussion.
Units Krishna, Mohali and Naroda grew ~30% YoY; Surat and Indore underperformed and are recruiting doctors.
International revenue ~42% of Shalby International operating revenue; group international business ~₹13 cr (₹2 cr Gurgaon, ₹11 cr other units).
Consolidated revenue of ₹923 mn in FY25, ₹1.3 bn in FY26, ₹472 mn in Q1 FY27 (MedTech-related, as stated).

qa_highlights.question: Rajakumar (RK Invest): Will hospital margins sustain or improve from here, with no one-offs or headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to improve, citing bunker activation in Q1 with further uptick in Q2, TPA renewals with a potential 5-7% revenue uplift, Gurgaon EBITDA turning positive, and recovery in Krishna, Mohali and Naroda (~30% YoY growth), while Surat and Indore are recruiting doctors.

qa_highlights.question: Rajakumar: Why has the implants/MedTech bottom line deteriorated despite revenue rising from ₹28 cr to ₹42 cr, and why did losses widen from ₹7.4 cr in Q4 to ₹11.4 cr in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to higher interest and full-year depreciation from earlier capex, and said Q4 had a forex gain that did not recur in Q1; gross margin is expected to rise 100-200 bps each quarter. Deferred tax asset is not recognised on US MedTech losses on a conservative basis and will be reconsidered when profitability improves.

qa_highlights.question: Kashish Thakur (Elara): What is driving weak MedTech profitability, especially in the US, and when can sustainable double-digit EBITDA margins come?
qa_highlights.answer: Shanay Shah cited FX (USD/INR) as a major factor, India volumes up over 100%, US volumes flat. Cost initiatives cut cash burn by about ₹3 cr/month, with a further ₹3 cr/month once a project is implemented by Q4 FY27; half the progress is done and the rest is expected over the next 6 months, given 6-9 months to 1 year for US FDA-related changes.

qa_highlights.question: Kashish Thakur: Hospital standalone margin fell ~320 bps to 18.4% despite occupancy at 51%; can FY27 margin guidance be reinstated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to new doctors and specialties taking about a quarter to mature, with TPA renewals and bunker revenue flowing into next quarter. It is 'strongly confident' of an EBITDA margin of up to 20% for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Kashish Thakur: Shalby International occupancy is 24% yet EBITDA-positive; what are the occupancy, margin and breakeven aspirations?
qa_highlights.answer: Occupancy expected to reach about 30% from Q3 or Q4 FY27, with PBT-positive targeted around Q3 to Q4, within 6-9 months; the unit posted about a 7% EBITDA margin in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Kashish Thakur: Tax rate guidance for FY27, and ROCE levers and timelines, plus status of the Mumbai expansion.
qa_highlights.answer: Hospital tax rate moved to about 26% from 35%, a permanent benefit; group ETR fell to 47% from 66%. Gurgaon will pay no tax for 2-3 years on carried-forward losses. Group ROCE is about 7% (standalone 9.5%), expected to reach 11-13% in 1-2 years with minimal capex. Mumbai talks with trustees are ongoing with no approval yet.

qa_highlights.question: Tripti Shukla (Kedia Securities): Why did ICRA downgrade the rating from A+ to A on the ₹830 cr facility, and how is debt being managed given the ₹129 cr Kotak working capital facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the rating move procedural, with outlook revised to stable from negative and possible re-evaluation later. The Kotak facility is a replacement of existing debt at about 30 bps lower cost, not fresh debt; net debt is expected flat to lower.

qa_highlights.question: Tripti Shukla: Is the rise in government payer mix (32% vs 24%) a temporary shift or a volume strategy, and how is the cash conversion cycle protected?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher government share follows rate renewals, including a super-specialty rate win at Krishna; bunker treatments are expected to be covered under government schemes. Receivables are being managed with automated recovery tools, bill-submission follow-up and regular visits to government offices.

qa_highlights.question: Tripti Shukla: Expected cash capex for the 200-bed Mumbai (Asha Parekh) project, and how will it be balanced against ROCE goals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a greenfield project and may need a different ROCE benchmark once finalised. No further debt is expected for hospitals or MedTech; funding via debt or internal accruals will be decided later, with no capex figure given.

risks_watch: MedTech: whether the consolidated EBITDA stays positive beyond a fourth quarter and whether the double-digit margin target (half progress made, rest over 6 months) is delivered, given US FX and flat US volumes.
Hospital standalone margin recovery toward 20% full-year guidance from 18.4% in Q1, which depends on doctor ramp-up, TPA renewals and bunker revenue not yet visible in the numbers.
Rating: ICRA cut the long-term rating to A from A+ (outlook stable); the company said it could be re-evaluated in coming quarters.
Rising government payer mix (32% from 24%) at lower ARPOB (₹44,711 vs ₹45,673) raises receivables and cash conversion risk.
Mumbai 200-bed greenfield project: trustee approval pending, funding and capex amount undecided, with implications for group ROCE.
Data inconsistencies in the call: India MedTech revenue cited as ~₹36 cr and ~₹22.9 cr, and the MedTech EBITDA figure given as ~₹1.7 million and ~1.6 million; reconcile against the filed results.
key_quotes: We are strongly confident as per our estimate to see EBITDA margin of upward to 20% on to the whole year basis.
So this is all underway and half of the progress is already made the other half is expected in the next 6 months from here on.
This is not an increase in the debt level, this is just a replacement.

We do not see our bottom line to worsen off from here rather we are confident to see a better bottom line in the subsequent quarter also importantly by the reason of the upside on to our gross margins which is expected to increase about 100 basis to 200 basis points each quarter from here on.

540879|2026-03.headline: Apollo Micro Systems posted record Q4 FY26 revenue of INR293 crores (+81% YoY) and FY26 PAT margin of 16% standalone, with order book at INR1,432 crores.
540879|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 was the company's highest ever quarter: revenue INR293 crores (+81% YoY), EBITDA INR68 crores (+88%), and PAT INR37 crores (+164%). For FY26, consolidated revenue rose 61% to INR904 crores, EBITDA excluding other income rose 69% to INR218 crores, and PAT rose 91% to INR107 crores. Management said standalone FY26 revenue growth was about 36%, below the earlier 45-50% organic CAGR guidance, which it attributed to customer approvals delaying Q4 execution. The call stressed Vision 2036, new land-systems entry, export pipeline, and new licences, while giving little numerical guidance on IDL Explosives or order inflows.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue around INR380 crores, described as roughly flat expectation going forward; company has been loss-making with negative EBITDA and is in a transformation phase, with revenue and margin guidance promised from Q3 FY27 onwards.

segments.commentary: Standalone FY26 revenue growth about 36% vs prior 45-50% organic CAGR guidance; standalone PAT margin 16% vs internal target of 15%.

segments.name: Air, land and sea platforms
segments.commentary: Heritage in air and underwater (missiles, EW, avionics, torpedoes, sonars, mines); land systems entry planned in FY26-27 with trials scheduled in upcoming quarters. No revenue split given.

Company expects to grow at a similar rate in FY27 and FY28, no formal revenue or margin guidance for FY27 given.

Standalone growth shortfall due to customer approvals pending for projects that had been expected in Q4 FY26.

DAC approval for a large Navy order (mines/torpedoes) said to be expected imminently; no value given.
Export offers submitted; first export order received in FY26; no export revenue quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key tenets and financial parameters of the FY36 Vision?
qa_highlights.answer: Four pillars: global OEM, diversified land/air/sea revenue, Indian and export expansion, and R&D-led innovation; numbers to be shared later.

qa_highlights.question: What is IDL's revenue, utilisation and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: IDL did around INR380 crores in FY26 and is loss-making, with operating losses reduced; revenue and margin guidance to come from Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why a smaller TNT and HMX expansion, and what capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Current licences (500 t TNT, 50 t HMX) are for industrial explosives; larger defence-capacity expansion is at DPR stage and will be disclosed later.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 standalone growth below 45-50% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Some projects planned for Q4 FY26 were delayed by pending customer approvals; management expects to catch up and maintain momentum.

qa_highlights.question: Will the order book be executed in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Some orders will execute in FY27 and others will spill over; management said revenue growth will continue at a similar pace, no numeric estimate.

Pending acquisition by Apollo Defence Industries under NDA; funding not disclosed.

540879|2026-06.headline: Apollo Micro Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 17% YoY to INR156 crores, while consolidated revenue jumped 88% to INR251 crores; standalone PAT up 43% to INR28 crores.
540879|2026-06.overview: Management reported its best June quarter, with standalone revenue of INR156 crores (+17% YoY), EBITDA incl. other income of about INR48 crores, and PAT of INR28 crores, giving record EBITDA and PAT margins of 31% and 18%. Consolidated revenue was INR251 crores (+88% YoY) and consolidated EBITDA excluding other income was INR54 crores (+31%). Management pointed to a standalone order book of INR1,224 crores and a consolidated order book of INR1,704 crores as of 8 August 2026. The company also signed to acquire a 41.33% promoter stake in Premier Explosives for about INR1,550 crores in cash, and reiterated 40-45% growth guidance.

segments.name: Standalone Apollo Micro Systems
segments.commentary: Revenue INR156 crores (+17% YoY) with PAT of INR28 crores and 18% PAT margin, the highest June-quarter PAT. Export revenue is nil.

segments.name: Ideal Explosives (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Turned PAT positive in Q1 FY27 after being EBITDA positive in Q4 FY26, but margins are thin. Management expects full positive contribution from FY28 after 3-4 quarters of restructuring; order book is INR480 crores.

segments.name: Premier Explosives (proposed)
segments.commentary: Acquisition of 41.33% promoter stake for about INR1,550 crores, all cash; open offer timing is with the regulator. Not yet consolidated.

FY28 guidance to be given at the end of FY27.
Consolidated order book expected to reach INR3,500-4,000 crores by end FY27 on the back of a single order of INR2,500-3,000 crores (understood to be MIGM/QRSAM-linked, not confirmed).
Ideal Explosives expected to be fully positive from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How will Premier Explosives be integrated and what synergies arise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Premier gives backward integration into propulsion and explosives, removing dependence on third parties (e.g. MIL) and enabling Apollo to become a prime OEM for weapons. Operations will remain separate for now; Ideal will not merge with Premier.

qa_highlights.question: Will Ideal's losses be resolved, and when will it integrate into defence?
qa_highlights.answer: Ideal is PAT positive in Q1 but margins are low. Bulk explosives volumes are weak; GOCL accessories manufacturing starts in a couple of quarters. Full positivity expected from FY28. Integration plan to come in 2-3 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any FY27 or FY28 revenue or EBITDA margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth guidance of 40-45% is reaffirmed for FY27. No EBITDA margin guidance; management said the momentum will continue, with FY28 guidance at year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Order book trajectory for three years including Premier?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated order book is INR1,700 crores; a single order of INR2,500-3,000 crores expected by FY27-end could take it to INR3,500-4,000 crores. Premier's own order book was not disclosed as it is in the CCI process.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR2,500 crore acquisition funding deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Around INR2,500 crores for the acquisition, around INR500 crores for working capital debt, with the rest for general corporate purposes.

qa_highlights.question: What is R&D as a percentage of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management initially said about 4% for FY26, then corrected it: FY26 R&D was INR72.53 crores on INR764 crores revenue, around 9.5%, with a 6-8% average over the last 3-4 years.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR535 crore (+19%) and EBITDA INR90 crore (+8%). Order book above INR2,600 crore. Sidwal's Faridabad greenfield plant is in trial production with commercial production expected this quarter; FY27 and FY28 growth guided at 30-35% with 16-17% margin.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated margin pressure of 50-100 bps in FY27, described as temporary and expected to normalise as the macro environment improves.
Consumer Durables FY27 growth to track the RAC industry at about 12-13%, after industry growth of about 20% in Q1 FY27.
Electronics FY27 revenue growth of about 40% with 9.5-10% EBITDA margin.
Railways FY27 and FY28 growth of 30-35%, margin 16-17%, subject to no disruption in Indian Railways or Metro offtake.
FY27 gross capex of INR1,800-2,000 crore, of which cash outflow is about INR1,100-1,200 crore after supplier credit terms; FY28 cash outflow about INR1,400-1,500 crore.
Net debt expected to rise to INR700-800 crore by March 2027. PLI receipts: INR49.5 crore received in April 2026 for FY25 and INR78 crore expected for FY26.
capex_capacity: Ascent-K Circuit HDI PCB plant in Noida: construction to start around June 2026, 15-16 months to build, then 3-4 months of trial production; mass production from Q3-Q4 FY28. Backed by over INR4,500 crore of ECMS investment approvals across Ascent-K, Ascent and Shogini.
Ascent Circuits Hosur: construction delayed about one quarter by a pollution consent issue; trial production by Q3 FY27 and commercial production by mid-February 2027.

FY26 total capex about INR1,070 crore, of which INR550 crore capitalised and the balance in CWIP for operations in FY27. FY27 capex of about INR1,200 crore for Ascent plus INR700-800 crore for other entities.

Subsidies: about 48% of plant and machinery via ECMS and 42% from the UP government on building and plant and machinery, received with a 5-6 year lag. Land received at about a 25% discount; the subsidy flow is expected from FY28.

Sri City RAC capacity augmented. Railway Faridabad greenfield plant in trial production. Yujin factory in Korea completed, awaiting RDSO approval (12-15 months), with INR178 crore couplers order book.
demand_pricing: Industry view: RAC volumes were down about 30% in Q1 and Q2 FY26 and recovered in Q3-Q4, leaving FY26 roughly flat. Industry expected to grow about 20% in Q1 FY27 and 12-13% for FY27.

Price increases of about 14% YoY on finished goods: one in January 2026 from the star-rating change and one in April 2026 for commodity costs. Copper clad laminate prices are up more than 60% in one year and still rising; gold is up about 60%.
PCB pricing: Tier 1 EMS pass-through works on a quarterly lag, but PCB (Tier 2) has about a two-quarter lag. Two price increases of about 15% and 18% have been received, with more under negotiation.
Compressor import relief: government allowed imports of about 30% of last year's volumes for compressors below 2 tonne, extended for a year. Management says there is no compressor shortage.
Electronics margin pressure: PCBA about 5% and PCB about 12-13% versus a normal 16-17%. Management expects the price increases to flow through over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What are the RAC industry growth expectations for Q1 and FY27, and which segments face margin pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry expected to grow about 20% in Q1 FY27 and 12-13% for the full year. Margin pressure comes from minimum wage hikes (35% in Haryana, about 22% in UP), CCL and gold costs, and currency depreciation. Indian Railway fixed-price contracts cannot pass costs through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10-12% price increase reasonable?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases are about 14% YoY, from a January star-rating change and an April commodity-driven hike.

qa_highlights.question: Will compressor shortages hurt FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says there is no shortage. Five new domestic manufacturers have come up, and imports of 30% of last year's volumes are allowed. Commercial AC compressors are still largely imported.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Consumer Durables finished-goods share rise, and is it realisation-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Finished goods rose because gas-charging customers moved to ODM solutions, not because of realisation. Finished goods fell from about 80% at listing in FY18 to about 40% now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PCB versus PCBA mix and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 Electronics: PCBA about INR2,281 crore at about 5% margin; PCB about INR600 crore at 12-13%; Power-One about 15% margin; Unitronics not disclosed as it is listed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and net cash outflow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 gross capex INR1,800-2,000 crore with cash outflow of about INR1,100-1,200 crore. FY28 cash outflow of about INR1,400-1,500 crore.

risks_watch: FY27 margin squeeze of 50-100 bps from commodity inflation, currency depreciation and minimum wage revisions in UP, Haryana and other states.
PCB price pass-through lag of about two quarters and the Tier 2 position, which limit near-term recovery.
Net debt rising to INR700-800 crore by March 2027 while capex is heavy; working capital days up to 29 from 9 due to inventory build.
Ascent Hosur construction delay (about one quarter) and Ascent-K HDI timelines; subsidies arrive with a 5-6 year lag.
Non-controlling interest from CCPS: auditors assumed about 30% dilution as a maximum, with actual dilution expected to be lower; NCI remains a balance-sheet item.
Electronics customer shifts from purchase to job-work could cause organic top-line volatility; organic growth was subdued in Q4.

540902|2026-06.headline: Amber Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to INR3,888 crore and operating EBITDA 28% to INR337 crore, with Electronics EBITDA more than doubling.
540902|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to INR3,888 crore and operating EBITDA grew 28% to INR337 crore, with adjusted PAT of INR126 crore (up 19%) before a INR123 crore exceptional loss. Electronics was the standout, with revenue up 29% and EBITDA more than doubling to a 10.8% margin. Railway & Defense EBITDA fell 26% on mix, copper, currency and Haryana minimum wage hikes. Management flagged that PCB margins were compressed by a roughly two-quarter pass-through lag and that cost pressure persists through H1, while Q1 benefited from pre-stocking of compressors and copper. The IL JIN facility incident was a new overhang, with insurance cover and the impact still being assessed.

segments.name: Consumer Durable
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,758 crore (+8%) and EBITDA INR214 crore (+12%) despite commodity and minimum wage headwinds; management attributed the modest growth to a high base. RAC is roughly 55-60% of the division, with the remainder non-RAC.

segments.name: Electronics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR985 crore (+29%) and EBITDA INR107 crore (10.8% margin, up from about 6.4%). Bare PCB margin compressed on copper clad laminate (CCL) costs, and the EMS segment grew more slowly as customers destocked and shifted to job work. Management reiterated FY27 growth of about 40%.

segments.name: Railway Sub-systems & Defense
segments.commentary: Revenue INR144 crore (+18%) but EBITDA fell 26% to INR16 crore on product mix, including first trains supplied through a principal, plus copper, currency and a 35% Haryana minimum wage hike. FY27 revenue growth guided at 30-35% and EBITDA margin at 15-16%.

guidance_outlook: Electronics: FY27 growth of about 40% reiterated; EMS full-year guidance intact per Sanjay Arora.
Railway Sub-systems & Defense: FY27 revenue growth 30-35% and EBITDA margin 15-16%.
Consumer Durable: growth in line with RAC industry, cited as 13-15%; no percentage margin guidance given.
Group margin: earlier 50-100 bps decline guidance for FY27 now moderated, with margins seen normalising if no further currency or commodity disruption.
PCB margin: currently about 12% versus about 16% normal; expected to recover from Q3 FY27 to a 15-16% normalised range, subject to no further CCL price rises.

Oppo mobile: trial production in Q4 FY27, commercial production from Q1 FY28, about 8 million units in year one, rising to 15-16 million in year two; revenue-recognition model to be clarified in 15-20 days.
IL JIN: fundraise enabling resolution up to INR5,000 crore; quantum and form not yet decided. IL JIN production impact being assessed, with guidance expected to be met.
capex_capacity: PCB capex: about INR3,200 crore at Jewar (UP), where construction has started and trial production is about 18 months away; Hosur (Tamil Nadu) about INR1,000 crore, with the plant to be running this financial year; Shogini (Pune) INR500 crore. All three were approved under the ECMS scheme.
Jewar HDI PCB groundbreaking held with Ascent-K / Korea Circuit; air conditioner plant construction planned to start in 2028, with trial production in 2029.
Sidwal greenfield facility in Faridabad (HVAC, pantry, doors, gangways) is now operational.
Asset turn in PCB business about 0.8:1 depending on complexity.
CCL backward integration: Amber in discussion with JV partners; target own CCL plants by 2029-30.
demand_pricing: Consumer Durable: BEE tonnage labelling mandatory from 1 July 2026 has created mixed inventory in the trade; management expects inventory to clear by Diwali, a strong summer from November, and not very high festive demand.
Q1 Consumer Durable margins were helped by pre-buying of compressors and copper ahead of QCO enforcement, and by a premium mix (5-star and 2-tonne). Management said this would not be annualised.
PCB: pass-through to customers is progressing, with some customers raising prices in July. Copper clad laminate prices keep rising, driven by AI and data-centre demand and a shortage.
Electronics TAM: management cited $185 billion of electronics consumption, a $16-17 billion addressable market for PCB, PCBA and power electronics today, and an estimated $35-40 billion by FY30.
Power electronics (PLC, HMI, solar inverters, UPS, BESS) expected to grow 35-40%.

qa_highlights.question: Santhosh Seshadri (Avendus) asked about Oppo mobile export discussions, PLI eligibility, and PCB fixed-price contract exposure.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export talks with Oppo are early and export would be considered after one year of domestic production; three ECMS approvals (INR3,200 crore Jewar, about INR1,000 crore Hosur, INR500 crore Shogini) are in place; PCB pass-through runs on a two-quarter lag as tier-2 supplier, with some customers already raising prices in July. Draft PLI guidelines are awaited.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Bhartia (Investec) asked whether Q1 consumer durable margins reflected raw material inflation and inventory benefit, and about H1 margin outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Gupta said Q1 benefited from pre-stocking of compressors and copper ahead of QCO enforcement and a premium mix (5-star and 2-tonne), which will not be annualised. He said margins are not expected to compress and the full-year outlook remains in line with projections.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Bhartia asked about the operational impact of the IL JIN incident.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh said reconstruction permission was received the previous day and assessment is under way. Guided numbers for the quarter are still expected to be met, and exchanges will be informed.

qa_highlights.question: Dhruv Jain (Ambit) asked why Electronics growth looks lower excluding acquisitions, and about FY27 guidance and railway margin outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Arora said EMS growth slowed because customers destocked and some shifted to job work, and smart meter and smart watch segments declined; full-year EMS guidance is intact. For Railways, Jasbir Singh guided FY27 revenue growth of 30-35% and margin of 15-16%, citing fixed-price railway contracts and first trains supplied through a principal.

qa_highlights.question: Keshav Lahoti (HDFC Securities) asked why minority interest swung from INR28 crore positive to INR19 crore negative, and about the IL JIN incident impact.
qa_highlights.answer: Sudhir Goyal said the swing was checked later: the INR123 crore exceptional loss sits in Electronics entities with minority holders, pushing the minority share negative. Jasbir Singh said assets are insured, production has shifted to other IL JIN locations, and the impact will be quantified within a week.

qa_highlights.question: Sameet Sinha (Macquarie) asked about input cost pass-through timing and local CCL manufacturing.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh said consumer durable is tier 1 with a one-quarter lag, while PCB is tier 2 with a two-quarter lag, so pass-through starts from Q4. A first Wipro CCL plant is nearly operational, two more are planned, and Amber is in JV talks targeting own CCL plants by FY29-30.

qa_highlights.question: Achal Lohade (Nuvama) asked about PCB margin quantum, next-two-quarter margin path, and drivers of the 40% Electronics growth.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh said normalised PCB margin is about 16% versus about 12% now, with Q2 still impacted and recovery from Q3 to a 15-16% range, subject to no further CCL price rises. All three Electronics divisions (PCBA, PCB, industrial power electronics) are expected to drive the 40% growth. Sudhir Goyal said a group-level minority percentage cannot be given.

qa_highlights.question: Bhavik Mehta (JP Morgan) asked whether the consumer durable industry growth and the 50-100 bps FY27 margin decline guidance still hold, and the timing of Oppo revenue recognition clarity.
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Gupta said consumer durable growth is in line with industry, cited at 13-15%. Jasbir Singh said the 50-100 bps decline is moderated, with margins normalising absent further currency or commodity disruption. Oppo revenue-recognition clarity is expected in 15-20 days.

qa_highlights.question: Indrajit Agarwal (CLSA) asked about Oppo revenue booking entity, minority stake in IL JIN, and consolidated net debt.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh said the booking entity (IL JIN or Amber) depends on ERP integration and will be formalised before mid-September. Sudhir Goyal said minority is computed on a diluted basis of about 60% with about 39-40% treated as minority interest, and net debt was about INR1,225 crore at 30 June 2026 versus about INR510 crore at March 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Rahul Agarwal (IKIGAI) asked for an entity-wise Electronics revenue build-up over three years.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh declined a three-year number, citing asset turn of 0.8:1 and the capex plan (Jewar INR3,200 crore, Hosur INR1,000 crore). Power electronics is guided to grow 35-40%, and the Electronics TAM is $16-17 billion today, estimated at $35-40 billion by FY30. He did not accept the INR5,000 crore consolidated electronics sales framing.

risks_watch: IL JIN facility incident: final loss quantification and insurance recovery still pending; management promised an update within a week and a reassessment of the guided numbers.
PCB margin recovery depends on customer price pass-through and no further CCL price increases; Q2 FY27 is expected to remain impacted at about 12% margin versus about 16% normal.
Q1 consumer durable margin benefited from pre-stocking and a premium mix that management said will not be annualised; watch for normalisation as the BEE tonnage labelling mix clears by Diwali.

Net debt rose to about INR1,225 crore at 30 June 2026 from about INR510 crore at March 2026, alongside a fundraise enabling resolution of up to INR5,000 crore at IL JIN with quantum and form undecided.
Oppo mobile: revenue-recognition model (IL JIN vs Amber level) to be decided by mid-September; PLI eligibility depends on draft guidelines not yet issued; trial production targeted for Q4 FY27.
Minority interest swung to negative INR19 crore from positive INR28 crore; the adjusted minority figure was not provided on the call and was to be calculated later.
key_quotes: But what we have seen in July is that there are some customers who have increased the cost. So our margins are coming back to where it was.
But let me tell everybody on the call that the guided number of what we did last quarter, we are hopeful that we should be in line to deliver despite of this disruption.
So we are not looking at any margin compression.
But only subject to no further CCL price increases are happening.

540935|2026-03.headline: Galaxy Surfactants Q4 FY26 EBITDA fell to INR122 crore (from INR135 crore) and EBITDA/MT to INR20,114; Q1 FY27 guided to high end of 6-8% volume growth.
540935|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was hit by West Asia war disruptions to logistics, feedstock availability and customer ordering, with Egypt operations stalled through March. EBITDA declined year-on-year to INR122 crore and EBITDA per metric ton to INR20,114 from INR21,715. India volumes grew 8% YoY in Q4 while AMET volumes fell 15% and RoW fell 7%, with the Americas a relative bright spot after US tariff reversals. Management guided only for Q1 FY27 (high end of 6-8% volume growth and high end of INR19,000-21,000/MT EBITDA), declining to give full-year guidance given the uncertainty.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR135 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA per metric ton (full year FY26)

financial_highlights.change: concentrated in later part of quarter

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Volumes up 8% YoY in Q4; Performance up 3% and Specialty up over 27%. Full-year growth held despite reformulation pressure from key Tier 1 customers, offset by non-Tier 1 and D2C accounts.

segments.name: AMET (Africa, Middle East, Turkey)
segments.commentary: Volumes down 15% YoY in Q4, mainly supply-led via Galaxy Chemicals Egypt raw material and transhipment disruption in March. Management said Jan-Feb growth would have been about 2-3%; the segment is still underperforming versus its prior ~90,000 MT ambition, now about 60,000 MT base.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Volumes down 7% YoY in Q4 (double-digit growth through Q3) due to delayed shipments to Europe and LatAm, freight spikes and repricing; full-year growth was 4%.

segments.name: Americas / US
segments.commentary: Relative bright spot; volumes improved sequentially after tariff reversals. TRI-K premium specialty business performed consistently well, though specialty revenue was flat QoQ due to product mix.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27: volume growth at the higher end of the 6-8% guided range, conditional on current conditions not worsening.
Q1 FY27: EBITDA per MT at the higher end of the INR19,000-21,000 range.
No full-year FY27 or FY28 volume or revenue guidance given; management said clarity expected at Q1 results in August.
India: 8-10% volume growth possible if demand holds; risks include monsoon, energy-price-driven inflation and discretionary spending.
Long-term specialty mix: management expects 60:40 to 65:35 (performance:specialty) even by 2031. Analyst Day target of about INR25,000/MT is backloaded to FY27-FY30.
Growth capex: no major new growth capex committed in FY27 beyond work-in-progress capitalisation and routine brownfield/replacement capex; maintenance capex about INR20-30 crore per year.
capex_capacity: Capex of roughly INR480 crore over the last 3 years, mostly growth capex in Specialty Ingredients; a major portion commissioned in the last 1.5 years, so benefits begin to show from FY26-27.
Maintenance capex about INR20-30 crore per year.
Product launches include Galsoft Lumithic (amino acid-based self-thickening mild surfactant) shown at in-cosmetics Paris.
Management said the company has spare flexibility to gain volume share from supply-constrained competitors, and is already producing an alternative product in India.
EPC/project income recognised on a percentage-of-completion basis; not material in FY26, with bulk expected in FY27.
demand_pricing: Feedstock costs rose sharply in Q4 due to the geopolitical situation; petrochemical feedstocks rose more than oleochemicals, and fatty alcohol prices have more than doubled per management, with availability the main issue.
Ethylene oxide and sulfur prices rising frequently; supply managed through vendor partnerships; management said it was not seeing major supply worries.
Pricing is passed on with a lag of about a month because customers expect price stability; freight-cost increases were also passed through to customers.
Management sees no panic buying in Q4; demand described as healthy in India and AMET/Africa/Turkey, with monitoring of inflation-driven demand weakness.
Competitive pressure in AMET from local players that are backward integrated, who have taken share from global customers.
Mix benefits expected from Americas specialty and Europe project pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why was specialty revenue flat QoQ (INR493 crore to INR498 crore) despite US tariff reversal, and how big is India's specialty mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the flat QoQ figure to product mix in US Q4 as products were shifted after tariff reversal. India specialty base is small, but D2C brands are growing their presence and use specialty ingredients.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term specialty mix outlook and the outlook for FY27-28 volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to grow both segments, expects a 60:40 to 70:30 range depending on performance, and still sees 60:40 to 65:35 by 2031. No FY27-28 volume guidance beyond Q1 given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for fatty alcohol prices and pass-through, and the risk of down-trading?
qa_highlights.answer: Pass-through is possible with a lag of about 1 month. Petrochemical feedstocks have risen more than oleochemicals, and the current challenge is supply availability rather than demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Egypt facility's status on raw materials, logistics and demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand not a challenge; March was disrupted by stuck inbound materials. Operations restored from mid-April, and management expects May and June to run uninterrupted.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Q1 volume guidance rely mainly on supply constraints at competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no; the guidance is driven by India recovery to 8-10% growth, US business revival and AMET supply recovery, with a caveat that the outlook holds only if current conditions do not worsen.

qa_highlights.question: Why has AMET fallen from ~90,000 MT to ~60,000 MT and what is the market outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Local backward-integrated players gained share; Egypt plant idle in March. Management said AMET has likely bottomed, with market growth of about 3-4%.

risks_watch: Logistics: port congestion and elongated transit times persist even as congestion eases; freight rates elevated.

Raw material availability: sulfur and ethylene oxide (ethylene-based supply concentrated in one supplier) and petrochemical feedstock availability; West Asia escalation (Strait of Hormuz) could worsen.

540935|2026-06.headline: Galaxy Surfactants Q1 FY27 EBITDA hit a record INR 252.5 crore (INR 35,458/MT), nearly double YoY; FY27 EBITDA/MT guidance raised to INR 24,000–25,000.
540935|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose to INR 252.5 crore from INR 135.1 crore in Q1 FY26, with EBITDA per metric ton at INR 35,458 versus about INR 20,009 a year earlier. Consolidated volumes grew 5% YoY, with India up 11% and Rest of World up 6%, while AMET volumes fell 4% YoY but rose 19% QoQ after West Asia logistics disruptions cut April–May supply. Management attributed the margin jump to reformulation-led volume recovery, a richer specialty mix, commercial execution and feedstock volatility, and said some of these gains may not persist. FY27 volume guidance of 6–8% was maintained, while EBITDA/MT guidance was raised to INR 24,000–25,000 from INR 19,000–21,000; management implied roughly INR 21,000–22,000 per MT for the remaining three quarters.

540975|2026-03.headline: Aster Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18% to INR 1,182 crore and operating EBITDA 26% to INR 244 crore, with the QCIL merger awaiting NCLT approval.

Core hospitals and clinics posted 32% EBITDA growth at a 23.1% margin, and labs turned sharply profitable. The Quality Care (QCIL) merger has shareholder and creditor approval and awaits NCLT order, which management expects this quarter. Q4 revenue was about INR35-37 crore against an internal expectation of INR55-60 crore. Management said demand has recovered in the first two months of FY27, with monthly growth of 40-50%, and that it is tracking its 50% growth target. Price pass-through is not complete and is expected to finish in about 1.5-2 months, with efficiency and AI-based inspection offsets. The company also disclosed a 34% stake in a new BLDC motor and electronics associate, Tricoree Machmatrix, though no investment figures were given.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H2 FY26 below the expected 30,000-32,000 chimneys per month?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to industry demand softness and geopolitical fears; major buyers were short of orders in Q4. No loss of orders was cited.

qa_highlights.question: Are you on track for 4 lakh chimneys in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said 270,000 in FY26 plus 50% growth implies about 4 lakh, and said the order position covers the planned growth for 2-3 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 revenue growth only about 11% on about 20% volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material share rose to about 75%, plus INR depreciation and gas supply issues; volume weakness was from market demand.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins may be slightly lower but absolute profit should rise; AI-based inspection is expected to cut inspection time by 10-20% in 1-1.5 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company still on SME rather than main board?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not meet two criteria: paid-up capital of at least INR10 crore and net worth of at least INR75 crore. Will migrate once eligible.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory high and what about exports?
qa_highlights.answer: High inventory reflects SKD/CKD imports for refrigerators, ovens and hobs; expected to fall with local manufacturing. Exports are being explored, but India OEM demand of about 6 lakh chimneys is the priority.

541096|2026-03.headline: Bharat Parenterals FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose to INR 15.8 crores from INR 2.7 crores, driven by Innoxel's loss narrowing; standalone revenue fell 23% to INR 234 crores.
541096|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue was broadly flat at INR 345.4 crores versus INR 340 crores, but the mix shifted: standalone BPL revenue fell about 23% to INR 234 crores on deferred export tenders, exits from low-margin volume and about two months of production downtime for upgrades. Innoxel's revenue rose 174% to INR 72.4 crores, its EBITDA loss narrowed by INR 23.5 crores, and it turned EBITDA positive in Q4 FY26 (INR 1.4 crores). Varenyam Healthcare grew 13.7% to INR 58.4 crores and turned profitable. FY27 guidance is given by business: standalone 10-15% growth, Innoxel 35-45% growth, and Varenyam 20-25% growth, with management conceding the standalone base will only partially recover this year.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 234 crores (down about 23%), EBITDA INR 21 crores at 9% margin; capacity utilisation 48% general, 21% beta-lactam, 24% cephalosporins; order book INR 171 crores.

segments.name: Innoxel Lifesciences (complex generics/CDMO, US/EU)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 72.4 crores (up 174%), EBITDA loss INR 6.9 crores; US FDA establishment inspection report received and EUGMP clearance from FAMHP with zero critical and zero major observations; 19 active partners and 42 assets in pipeline.

segments.name: Varenyam Healthcare (domestic branded)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 58.4 crores (up 13.7%), EBITDA INR 2.5 crores and PAT INR 2.3 crores; 45 active brands, top five brands INR 28.7 crores (about half of revenue); Sugammadex over INR 10 crores; PCPM up 31% YoY to over INR 3.85 lakh.

segments.commentary: Facility under construction with approved budget about INR 160 crores and CWIP about INR 33 crores (around 20% complete); commissioning targeted September 2027, first EUGMP filing Q1 FY29, first commercial supply Q4 FY29.

guidance_outlook: Standalone BPL: revenue growth 10-15% and EBITDA margin 10-15% in FY27; management expects only partial recovery this year, with full recovery to FY25 levels targeted in FY28.

Innoxel: revenue growth 35-45% and EBITDA margin 20-25% in FY27; first commercial CMO supply from Q2 FY27, two to three CMO products commercialising in the year, 10 new filings, 20 new partner deals targeted, out-licensing income INR 70-90 crores, first MHRA and Health Canada filings.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 standalone guidance of 10-15% growth on a base of about INR 230-250 crores rather than INR 300 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the base is FY26 revenue. It expects partial recovery in FY27, with disruption from PIC/S and EUGMP preparation and inspections, and full recovery to FY25 levels in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is standalone peak revenue INR 400-500 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 400-500 crores is the target for the standalone business, but sequentially over 3-4 years, with peak revenue framed from a 2030 standpoint.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Varenyam Bio's commercialisation timeline moved from 2027 to Q4 FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the project is running at least one quarter behind schedule, citing geopolitical disruption. Filing now starts around Q1 FY28, first EUGMP filing is Q1 FY29, and commercial supply is Q4 FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Why were FY27 guidances cut across segments, especially Varenyam?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said earlier guidance was not met, so the new ranges are softer and deliberately achievable. Varenyam's earlier INR 75-80 crore revenue ambition was not restated; FY27 growth is 20-25% with heavy investment in field force and a new division.

qa_highlights.question: What drives Innoxel's FY27 margin expansion, and how much is CDMO?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin expansion is mainly from milestone payments and fixed cost leverage. Commercial supply is limited to two or at most three products. Management would not quantify CDMO revenue share, saying own-product manufacturing revenue starts in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing of the two Innoxel 505(b)(2) assets and the CMO commercialisations?
qa_highlights.answer: The two 505(b)(2) assets are targeted for US filing in Q3 and Q4 FY27, filed in partner names. One CMO product commercialises in Q2 FY27 and a second between Q3 and Q4 FY27; Innoxel earns fees and milestones rather than profit share on CMO deals.

541153|2026-03.headline: Bandhan Bank Q4FY26 PAT rose 68% YoY to INR 534 crore, with NIM up to 6.2% and credit cost easing to 2%.
541153|2026-03.overview: Bandhan Bank reported Q4FY26 PAT of INR 534 crore, up 68% YoY and 159% QoQ, with ROA of 1.1% and ROE of 9% for the quarter. NIM rose to 6.2% from 5.9% in Q3 on a 23 bps QoQ fall in deposit costs, while credit cost fell to 2% from 3.3%. Slippages declined to INR 1,028 crore from INR 1,314 crore, led by EEB, and collection efficiency improved. Full-year FY26 PAT was INR 1,224 crore, with NII down 5.8% YoY, and opex was elevated in Q4 by PSLC and IT items.

segments.commentary: EEB book INR 53,906 crore, down YoY (about -5%) but up 8% QoQ; 23% of advances. EEB slippages fell to INR 690 crore from INR 942 crore; 0-90 DPD pool fell to about 3.1% from 4.6%.

segments.name: Non-EEB book
segments.commentary: Non-EEB advances grew 25% YoY and form about two-thirds of total advances. Retail grew 46% YoY (CV, CE, auto, gold loans); wholesale grew 33% YoY.

segments.name: Secured book
segments.commentary: Secured book grew 25% YoY and forms about 56% of advances, against a target of 58% by March 2027.

segments.name: Fee income
segments.commentary: Other income grew 10% YoY and 12% QoQ; third-party distribution income rose 34% YoY and processing fees rebounded.

541163|2026-03.headline: Sandhar FY26 consolidated revenue INR 4,852 crore (+25%), EBITDA INR 513 crore (10.6% margin); FY27 guided to grow over 15% before any price re-trigger.
541163|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: consolidated revenue rose 25% to INR 4,852 crore, EBITDA rose 28% to INR 513 crore at a 10.6% margin, and PAT rose 40% to INR 199 crore. Q4 consolidated revenue grew 29% YoY with an 11% EBITDA margin, and the India business grew 28% in FY26. Overseas subsidiaries swung to break-even at EBT in Q4 after a FY26 loss of EUR 2.56 million, though aluminium pass-through lags are expected to weigh on Q1 FY27. Management cited April manpower absenteeism and raw material shortages as the main near-term disruption, with May reported as better than April.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated Q4 revenue and EBITDA margin

financial_highlights.value: Revenue INR 257 crore, EBITDA INR 28.25 crore

financial_highlights.change: Q4 EBITDA margin 14.6%, EBT about break-even
Working capital debt INR 564 crore; term loans INR 384 crore

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 4,384 crore (+28%), EBITDA INR 472 crore (+32%). Management said industry grew 12.7% while Sandhar India grew 28%; two-wheeler business grew 35.1% vs industry 12.9%.

segments.commentary: FY26 loss of EUR 2.56 million; Q4 EBITDA margin 14.6% and EBT roughly break-even. Revenue of about EUR 46 million with full-year decline of about 8.5% in euro terms, per analyst. Pass-through lag of about 180 days in overseas contracts.

segments.commentary: Five JVs generated revenue of INR 257 crore and EBITDA of INR 28.25 crore in FY26; Sandhar investment about INR 62 crore.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 20 crore; 41,000 battery chargers and 5,500 motor control units sold. Targeted to double in FY27; EBT turnaround expected in FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at over 15% (15-16%), excluding a likely price re-trigger on input cost increases.
EBITDA margin expected to improve by about 0.25% in FY27 for existing businesses; new projects will dilute, with 1.5-2 years to profitability.
Management targets doubling revenue every three to four years, with a stated post-tax ROCE target of 15%, peaking at 20%; at INR 10,000 crore revenue, PAT of about INR 450 crore was cited.
FY27 capex estimated at INR 275-310 crore (5-7% of revenue), covering growth, maintenance and upgradation.
Overseas business expected to return to planned levels once aluminium pass-through lag clears; Romania targeted for break-even in FY28.
Manpower availability expected to normalise by end-June 2026 per management, with May better than April.

Sundaram-Clayton die-casting business shifting to own premises, targeted by end of Q2 FY27.
FY27 capex outlay of INR 275-310 crore expected.

Technology: telematics and smart-key products presented to customers; POCs next, development in FY27, production thereafter. Partnering on royalty-based technology transfer, not JVs; target to take to market within 12 months.
Smart Key locksets at about 5,000 per month and growing.
demand_pricing: Management said domestic auto demand is strong, but manpower constraints limit industry output; absenteeism reached around 20% at one point in April, and state minimum wages rose 30-40%.
Two-wheeler inventory at some customers fell from about 60 days to under 14 days; industry lost an estimated 200,000-300,000 vehicles.

Aluminium and gas costs rose sharply in March-April; India pass-through lag is about three months (aiming for 30 days), and overseas lag about 180 days (aiming for 90 days). Pass-through from June expected to recover April costs.
Price re-trigger expected across the industry as input costs rise; not included in the 15% growth guidance.
Working capital: overseas inventory holding about 54-55 days vs about 12-13 days in India.

qa_highlights.question: How will the planned doubling of revenue every 3-4 years be achieved, and which segments drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited two-wheelers, new businesses in sheet metal and casting, and proprietary products like locks and mirrors; it said a 15-16% growth guide is conservative and excludes the price re-trigger.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the new projects and their profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 342 crore invested generated INR 468 crore in FY26 and is expected to reach about INR 750 crore in FY27; Khed City and Sanaswadi turn around in Q2 FY27, Sundaram-Clayton in Q3 with EBT losses for FY27, EV and Romania in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins improve and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing businesses are targeted to gain about 0.25% in EBITDA margin in FY27; new projects will dilute margins until they mature, with 1.5-2 years to turnaround.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position and debt-to-equity trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt INR 948 crore, of which INR 564 crore is working capital debt; term loans INR 384 crore with about INR 103 crore repayable this year. Management called the debt-to-equity ratio healthy versus peers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did overseas borrowings rise in INR terms despite a small euro increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Bill discounting was reclassified to borrowings under Ind AS, and INR translation at the closing rate (about INR 111 per euro vs INR 108 in March) inflated the INR figure; the euro increase was about EUR 5 million.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company keep the overseas business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the overseas presence supports Indian customer relationships; it will revisit the business after the year but gave no decision.

qa_highlights.question: What is the company's competitive advantage in castings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited integrated capability across high- and low-pressure die casting, machining, zinc, magnesium and aluminium castings, from small to very large parts including engine blocks.

risks_watch: Aluminium and gas cost pass-through lags of three months in India and about 180 days overseas, which will hit Q1 FY27 margins.
Manpower shortages and wage hikes in several states could keep volumes below demand; management expects normalisation by end-June 2026.
New project losses (Sundaram-Clayton, EV, Romania) in FY27 could slow the margin improvement.
Working capital intensity: receivable days at 44 (consolidated) and inventory days at 54-55 for overseas operations; overseas debt in INR rose partly due to reclassification.
Price re-trigger not yet secured; the FY27 growth guidance excludes it.
Overseas business strategy unresolved; management will revisit after the year.

541167|2026-03.headline: Yasho Q4 FY26 revenue rose 33% YoY to INR246.7 crore with EBITDA margin at 18.1%; FY27 utilisation target is 75%+.
541167|2026-03.overview: Consolidated FY26 revenue reached INR830 crore (up 22.7% YoY) with EBITDA of INR144 crore and margin of 17.4%, while Q4 revenue was INR246.72 crore (up 33%) with EBITDA of INR44.71 crore at 18.1%. Growth was entirely volume-led (FY26 volume up 33%), with management saying prices were under pressure until late March when 10-15% price increases started, mostly effective from April. Management guided to FY27 utilisation above 75% (from about 60% in FY26), volume growth of 35-45%, and a FY28 revenue target of INR1,500 crore tied to a 15-year long-term contract with INR51.4 crore advance. Leverage fell to 3.75x debt-to-EBITDA from 4.70x, and INR23.3 crore of FY27 liabilities were prepaid.

segments.name: Industrial Chemicals
segments.commentary: Contributed 87% of revenue in both Q4 and full FY26 and is the key growth driver; management says all volume growth came from the industrial segment, with a slight dip on the consumer side.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Accounted for 62% of FY26 revenue; Americas demand improved in Q4 as tariffs moderated, and Europe is seeing some slowdown. Management is also starting to enter Asia.

guidance_outlook: FY27 utilisation target above 75% (from above 60% in FY26); management also cited 70-75% and about 15 percentage points of utilisation uplift.
FY27 volume growth of 35-45% (clarified after several restatements); EBITDA margin expected at least 2-3 percentage points above FY26, with a stated aim of about 20%.

FY28 revenue target of INR1,500 crore, supported by asset utilisation of 85-90%, the MNC long-term contract going into commercial operation from early FY28, and FY27 capacity additions; management says margins will be maintained.
FY27 capex of INR125 crore, fully funded by internal accruals and entirely at Pakhajan; management says none of it relates to the long-term contract.
Gross margin guided at 40-42%.
Working capital to fall to about 170-175 days over 6-12 months from about 190 days.
Debt-to-EBITDA comfort zone of about 2.5x; absolute debt may rise while the ratio falls.

R&D facility completed October 2025 and fully operational.

Pakhajan has 2 production buildings built, with room for 4 more to be started one by one as demand ramps; a special project of about INR90 crore is running, and a further INR100 crore Pakhajan capex is under consideration.
Utilisation was above 60% in FY26 (60-62% through March); management declined to give plant-wise utilisation.
Management was unsure of the current total capacity figure, which was stated as 12,000 to 32,000 (unit not specified).
demand_pricing: Price increases of about 10-15% versus the pre-war base; these took effect only in the last 10 days of March and from April, as contracts were fixed quarterly or half-yearly until then.
About 40% of revenue comes from regular customers on quarterly or six-monthly pricing; about 60% is spot or relationship-based.
Pricing pressure and margin pressure through FY26, with product mix shifted away from low-margin products.
Import delays of 8-12 weeks versus 3-4 weeks normally; US export transit has risen to 60-70 days from 25 days.
Sulfur availability is challenging but available; solvents and sulfur-based chemistries show strong price volatility.
Chinese competitors described as very strong and aggressive in lubricant additives and industrial chemicals.
India-EU FTA expected around early January; Yasho has a European team about one year old.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR1,500 crore FY28 target visible and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited utilisation rising to 85-90% by FY28, the special project coming on stream in FY28, and new rubber and lube molecules; the visibility is partly customer commitments made on the table.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company moving into CDMO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Yasho is not a CDMO and will not serve small-volume API-type orders of 20-100 metric tons. It will work with large-volume customers, with Pakhajan designed for 500-1,000 metric tons minimum per molecule.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Days have fallen from 215-216 in FY25 to about 190; the target is 170-175 over 6-12 months. Debtors are flat, and stock was useful in the supply crisis.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the FY27 volume growth is from price versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management measures growth in volume terms, and says price increases only started in late March and April 2026. Currency gains are largely offset by imported raw materials.

qa_highlights.question: Does Yasho make its own formulations?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Yasho only makes pure chemicals and does not compete with its formulating customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the MNC project capex included in the FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The INR125 crore FY27 capex is separate; the share of capex attributable to the MNC project is zero.

risks_watch: Supply chain disruption from the Middle East: import delays, raw material shortages, and high petrochemical prices; management says high inventory has offset this so far.
Chinese competition in lubricant additives and industrial chemicals.
Europe slowdown and the timing of the India-EU FTA (expected around early January).
Working capital reduction to 170-175 days depends on raw material availability.
Ramp to 75% utilisation and the FY28 INR1,500 crore target depend on the MNC contract and new molecules; each new molecule targeted at INR50 crore or more.
Ability to hold EBITDA margin as the customer price increases pass through, given management says costs cannot be fully passed on.

EBITDA rose to Rs 74.42 crore (24.2% margin, vs 17% previously cited), with PAT of Rs 36 crore (11.7% margin). Net debt/EBITDA fell to 1.86x from 3.75x at Q4 FY26, bank loan ratings were upgraded to A- by CRISIL and ICRA, and working capital cycle shortened from 190 to 143 days. Management raised FY27 capex from Rs 125 crore to Rs 250 crore for two new buildings at Pakhajan and set a FY28 revenue target above Rs 1,600 crore.

From 3.75x at end of Q4 FY26

segments.commentary: Contributed nearly 89% of Q1 revenue; management expects this to rise to about 90% going forward. Management said new-product revenue is about 30% of sales over the last two years, with revenue rising from Rs 600 crore to Rs 850 crore.

segments.name: Exports / geographies
segments.commentary: Export is about 69% of revenue; US sales recovered after tariff issues eased, and Europe and Middle East are growing. Asia and Africa are early-stage, with margins described as at par or slightly lower than US/Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be sustained, given the Q1 benefit from the April price revision and operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gains to product mix and higher utilisation rather than stock gains, citing commitments from marquee customers to maintain margins.

qa_highlights.question: What changed to move EBITDA margin from the historical 17-20% range to about 24%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher utilisation (about 50% to 65%), higher customer offtake, product mix, and R&D-led process optimisation.

qa_highlights.question: Phasing and revenue potential of the Pakhajan capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 about Rs 100 crore and Phase 2 about Rs 150 crore, at about 2.5x asset turn. Management said the Rs 1,600 crore FY28 guidance excludes these buildings.

qa_highlights.question: Supply chain or raw material risks given the current macro environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is a genuine raw material supply issue, and export container bookings can take three to four weeks. Inventory fell, which drove working capital down.

qa_highlights.question: Margin differential between new and old products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new products earn about 10-12% higher margin than older products. Newly launched products in the last 12 months carry better margins.

qa_highlights.question: Lube-additive and ICE exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see EV adoption as a threat within a 10-year horizon, and that Rs 250 crore capex is not for lube alone.

541195|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 turnover hit a record INR552.7 crore (+34.63% YoY) and PAT rose 38.49% to INR77.75 crore; FY26 turnover INR1,208.63 crore (+12.52%).
541195|2026-03.overview: Mishra Dhatu Nigam reported its highest-ever quarterly turnover of INR552.7 crore in Q4 FY26, with value of production up 19.15% to INR392.19 crore and PBT up 38.67% to INR107 crore. 541195|2026-06.headline: MIDHANI Q1 FY27 turnover rose 40.46% to Rs 239.49 crore, but LPG and raw-material costs compressed EBITDA margin to about 20%.

PBT rose 25.89% to Rs 23.92 crore and PAT rose 27.42% to Rs 16.31 crore. EBITDA was Rs 46.6 crore (up 12.89%), with margin about 20% versus roughly 23% expected, pressured by LPG price spikes and adverse raw-material price variance of about Rs 13-14 crore. Order book stood at about Rs 2,329 crore as of 1 July 2026, now won entirely through competitive bidding.

541233|2026-03.headline: FY26 was Lemon Tree's best year: revenue Rs 1,452.7 crore (+13%), PAT Rs 288.3 crore (+19%), with margin down 126 bps to 48.1%.
541233|2026-03.overview: Lemon Tree reported record FY26 and Q4 FY26 on occupancy, ARR, revenue, EBITDA, PBT, PAT and cash profit, with Q4 revenue of Rs 419.5 crore (+11%) and PAT of Rs 116.5 crore (+8%). Net EBITDA margin fell to 48.1% for FY26 and 52% for Q4, which management attributes to renovation spend, technology investment and the GST change. Management guided that these three cost heads fall to about 3.7% of revenue by FY28, and set out a proposed demerger that would leave Lemon Tree as an asset-light entity and Fleur Hotels as an owner/lessor platform. Q4 demand softened in March and April from the Middle East conflict and airline disruption, with corporate travel weaker and occupancy hitting what management called a ceiling.

from Rs 1,699 crore a year ago

segments.name: Lemon Tree (asset-light, managed and franchised)
segments.commentary: Opened 20 managed/franchised hotels (1,523 rooms) and signed 55 (4,912 rooms) in FY26; total pipeline 22,581 rooms across 268 hotels, of which 131 hotels and 11,811 rooms are operational. Keys RevPAR grew 20% and Aurika 19% for FY25 to FY26 on management's figures.

segments.name: Fleur Hotels (owned/leased)
segments.commentary: Post-scheme, Fleur to have 5,600 rooms across 39 operational hotels; 4 hotels with 875 rooms in confirmed pipeline, including 572 rooms at Nehru Place (estimated capex Rs 700 crore). Fees Rs 95.8 crore, +8% on a same-store basis.

segments.name: Aurika brand
segments.commentary: Highest ARR and margin product; Aurika occupancy rose from 62% to 74% for FY26 with RevPAR +19%, though Q4 occupancy fell 2% as a large Mumbai wet-lease ended. Aurika has only two hotels (Mumbai and Udaipur).

guidance_outlook: Cost heads (GST impact, technology, renovation) expected to fall from 5.8% of revenue in FY26 to about 4.8% in FY27 and 3.7% in FY28 onward, adding roughly 1% of revenue a year, plus Rs 25-30 crore of one-off costs (Delhi property tax ex gratia, labour code) that drop out from FY27.
FY27 renovation spend about 1.9% of revenue, normal renovation thereafter at about 1.3% (possibly 1.0-1.2%); GST impact rising from 1% to 2% of revenue in FY27 as it becomes a full year.
Expected openings of about 2,000 rooms in FY27, rising to about 3,000 in FY28 and 4,000 in FY29; management says openings lag signings by about three years, with signings of about 5,000 rooms a year.

Lemon Tree standalone post-demerger: steady-state flow-through on management fees of 75-80%, currently about 60% pro forma; steady-state PAT about 60% of revenue (per management, after tax and no interest or depreciation).

Fleur targets up to Rs 3,000 crore of deployable capital over 12-18 months (including Warburg primary investment), and plans to add about 2,500 rooms; management does not give fee guidance for FY27-28.
Demerger: CCI approval received in April; SEBI and shareholder/creditor approvals underway; NCLT timing 6-18 months, with management giving 12-18 months as the outer limit.
Debt-to-EBITDA about 2.25x now; consolidated debt may rise to Rs 2,500-3,000 crore if Rs 1,500 crore is deployed, temporarily.

demand_pricing: Mid-March decision to prioritise occupancy over rate; April-May tactical pricing to keep an occupancy premium, with ARR roughly flat YoY; Q4 occupancy reached what management called a ceiling.

Corporate travel slowed in March as companies cut travel due to fares and the war; corporate share of occupancy fell to 55% from 59% in Q4 (negotiated room nights 55.4% for the full year vs 56.1%). Retail filled the gap at lower rates.
Indigo shutdown in December and the Middle East war (from early March, continuing into April) cited as headwinds; May described as surprisingly good.
Mumbai micro-market saw about 2,000 keys added in the last year (from Accor Fairmont to Ginger), creating a temporary supply glut for Aurika Mumbai.
