Indian mid-market: management says demand outpaces supply; cites 2.5 million unbranded rooms in India as a conversion opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Would Fleur's inventory be managed by a non-Lemon Tree operator post-demerger, and how would that work?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Fleur is brand-agnostic and would choose whichever brand makes economic sense, while Lemon Tree should not be discriminated against; it cited a lost 5-star NCLT bid as an example.

qa_highlights.question: Why Aurika RevPAR growth (3%) lags Keys (16%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to micro-market differences and timing; full-year FY26 RevPAR growth was 19% for Aurika and 20% for Keys, with Keys set to keep growing as renovations finish.

qa_highlights.question: How confident are you on conversion of signings into openings, and what fee numbers for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Openings lag signings by about three years; management declined to give fee guidance but expects about 2,000 rooms opened in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-saving path and steady-state margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Renovation, GST and technology costs to fall to about 3.7% of revenue by FY28; pro forma Lemon Tree flow-through is about 60% now, targeted at 70%+ and then 75-80%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised demerger timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: CCI approval came in April; SEBI/shareholder/creditor steps underway; NCLT is the main variable, with 12-18 months the outer limit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did incentive-linked management fees lag for third-party hotels versus Fleur?
qa_highlights.answer: Incentive fees (1-5% of revenue depending on GOP slab) fell as renovation and GST cut owned-hotel EBITDA margins; third-party fees rose 23% from net additions, Fleur fees rose 8% on a same-store basis.

qa_highlights.question: What peak debt level is comfortable after Fleur's deployment?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-to-EBITDA about 2.25x now; consolidated debt could rise to Rs 2,500-3,000 crore temporarily if Rs 1,500 crore is deployed.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation for standalone Lemon Tree post-demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Lemon Tree to be debt-free and cash-generative; Board to decide a dividend or buyback policy; no F&B expansion planned, with a high hurdle for acquisitions.

risks_watch: NCLT timing for the Fleur demerger: management guides 6-18 months, with 12-18 months as the outer limit; CCI approval received in April, SEBI, shareholder and creditor steps still pending.

541233|2026-06.headline: Lemon Tree Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to Rs 346.8 crore, but net EBITDA margin fell 99 bps to 43.8% on GST and SAR provision.
541233|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 9% YoY to Rs 346.8 crore and PAT rose 19% to Rs 57.3 crore, while occupancy rose 314 bps to 75.7% as the company shifted to a volume-led retail strategy. Gross ARR rose only 2% to Rs 6,361 because retail business carries lower net ARR after commissions, and management called Q1 an aberration driven by West Asia-related corporate travel softness. Margin compression came from a GST input-credit loss and stock appreciation rights provision, worth 3.1% of revenue combined. Management expects Q2 to be better, with July described as strong and August as solid. The call also covered the planned demerger of Fleur Hotels and Warburg's Rs 960 crore investment in Fleur.

segments.name: Owned hotels (Lemon Tree)
segments.commentary: Contributed Rs 320 crore of network revenue, 56% of network revenue. Net EBITDA margin hit by GST input-credit loss and renovation spend of about Rs 9.8 crore (2.25-2.3% of revenue).

segments.name: Managed and franchised (asset-light)
segments.commentary: Contributed Rs 256 crore of network revenue. Opened 6 hotels with 334 rooms and signed 13 hotels with 1,020 rooms in Q1. Same-store managed revenue grew 9-10%.

segments.name: Keys portfolio (Fleur)
segments.commentary: RevPAR up 19% YoY to Rs 2,885, with occupancy up 350 bps to 67% and ARR up 13% to Rs 4,311. Renovation is about two-thirds complete across 7 hotels.

segments.name: Fleur Hotels (pro forma)
segments.commentary: FY27 revenue Rs 311.4 crore (+7%), net EBITDA ex-GST Rs 125.1 crore (+10%, margin 40.2%), PAT Rs 34.7 crore (+23%).

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 net EBITDA margin to be better than the ~47% analyst estimate, and sees a path to at least 50% in FY28 as renovation spend drops and ARR improves.
Management targets a long-term Lemon Tree EBITDA margin of 75-80% as fee income doubles and corporate costs fall as a share of revenue.
Management targets Keys EBITDA of Rs 60 crore on revenue of Rs 115-120 crore, implying Rs 6.5 lakh per key EBITDA.
Target of about 2,000 rooms opened in FY27; management says it is broadly confident, with Q1 at 334 rooms.
Renovation spend is expected to fall to about 1% of revenue from FY28. GST impact is about 2% of net revenue and expected to decline gradually.
Demerger of Fleur expected to complete in H1 CY2027, with Fleur listing in late second half of calendar 2027 after SEBI, shareholder, creditor and GST approvals.
Fleur's long-term plan is to keep debt-to-EBITDA around 2x; Fleur targets roughly 15% ROCE after renovations are complete.
capex_capacity: Aurika Shimla (owned, 90 rooms): about Rs 108 crore deployed as of 30 June 2026; opening shortly as finishing and licences are in final stage.
Aurika Shillong (leased, 165 rooms): about Rs 33 crore deployed; opening expected H2 FY28.
Aurika Varanasi (leased heritage, 47 rooms): work begun; opening expected FY29.
Aurika Nehru Place Delhi: approvals pending; opening on or after FY30; DDA letter of award validity extended by one year.
Renovation: 300 rooms renovated in Q1 at about Rs 10 crore; similar number expected in Q2. Management expects 600-700 rooms in H1 and refurbishments of about 800 rooms in H2.

Fleur plans capital deployment of about Rs 2,500-3,000 crore, funded by Warburg's Rs 960 crore and about Rs 200-300 crore of balance-sheet cash. Management targets about 2,500 rooms of operating and under-development acquisitions.
Asset-light pipeline: 23,381 rooms across 279 hotels, of which 11,946 rooms across 135 hotels are operational.
demand_pricing: Q1 ARR growth was driven by a retail-led volume strategy, which lowered net ARR after commissions. Management calls this temporary and says the mix is returning to balance in July and August.

Corporate demand softened in high-density CBD markets such as Mumbai, Hyderabad and Bengaluru during the West Asia conflict, with lower travel, hiring and relocations. Delhi, Bengaluru and Hyderabad still outperformed; Mumbai and Gurgaon did not.
Mumbai airport micro-market absorbed about 2,000 new rooms over the last two years, creating a temporary supply mismatch. Aurika Mumbai pricing is being reset, with the stated aim of higher ARR.
Around 52% of company room sales are below Rs 7,500 (the GST threshold) and 48% above. Management is repricing demand-dense hotels to reduce GST drag.
OTA share of business is in the mid-30s%, and direct channels rose in Q1 with the retail push. Management expects a better negotiated versus non-negotiated mix from Q2.
Management says July was strong and August solid; Q2 demand is significantly better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is Keys' 19% RevPAR growth in line with the pre-renovation plan, and what remains to be spent on Keys renovation?
qa_highlights.answer: Keys is close to the Red Fox ARR target of about Rs 4,500 and is still a work in progress; management expects full performance next year with occupancy near Lemon Tree averages and reiterated a Rs 60 crore Keys EBITDA target. Remaining spend on about 300 rooms is about Rs 13-14 crore, at roughly Rs 4-5 lakh per key for second-tier Keys hotels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ARR grow only 2% despite Keys growth, and is the lower-ARR strategy continuing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the retail push to fill rooms during the West Asia-driven corporate slowdown lowered net ARR after commissions. It called this temporary, with a more balanced occupancy-ARR mix from July and August, and said Q1 was an aberration.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fleur's Rs 2,500-3,000 crore deployment and Warburg's Rs 960 crore be done at peak-cycle prices, and what are the IRR expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no hurry to deploy and that it is not in an up cycle, since India occupancy is in the mid-60s versus a 70-72% up-cycle threshold. It will focus on demand-dense top 6-7 cities, nearby 3-5 hour international markets and leisure locations, using brownfield, operating assets at 6-8x, greenfield and long leases, with returns targeted at about 60% post-fees ROCE and a conservative downturn assumption.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 and FY28 net EBITDA margins recover, given the 47% analyst estimate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 will be well above 47%. It targets at least 50% in FY28 as renovation spend drops to about 1% of revenue and GST drag falls from about 2% of net revenue, with ARR rising 5-6% in Q2 and further in winter.

qa_highlights.question: Is Mumbai guidance being cut, and will Aurika Mumbai reach double-digit RevPAR growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was an aberration and that Q2 will be better, citing about 2,000 new rooms near the Mumbai airport. It said RevPAR is stabilised and the focus is now on repricing Aurika ARR, and declined to give a numerical RevPAR target before Q2 results.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 2,000-room opening target for FY27 slip, given 334 rooms opened in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said slippage is normal in the business but it is broadly confident of about 2,000 rooms, based on the current pipeline and owner relationships.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net room additions lag the 334 rooms opened in Q1, and what was the management fee compounding outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tarudhan Valley (70 rooms) was terminated and Nestor (130 rooms, no fees) was removed, so fee-earning additions were lower. It said about 1,300 rooms were added year-on-year and that about 5,000 managed rooms signed in FY26 are due to open by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the renovation timeline, and how much margin was lost to renovation versus GST and SAR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 renovation spend was Rs 9.8 crore (about 2.25-2.3% of revenue) versus a normal Rs 3 crore, and that about 300 rooms were done in Q1 with a similar number in Q2. It said refurbishments of about 800 rooms are planned in H2 and that the renovation drag disappears in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fleur's acquisition push raise debt above 2x EBITDA, and how will the debt be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt may briefly exceed 2x EBITDA during construction, with a long-term target near 2x. Fleur debt is about Rs 1,100-1,200 crore; group debt is about Rs 1,275 crore after excluding about Rs 200 crore of cash. Warburg's Rs 960 crore will be deployed before listing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demerger timeline and status?
qa_highlights.answer: Kapil Sharma said CCI approval is done and SEBI and exchange scrutiny is in progress, followed by NCLT filing and hearings. Completion is targeted in H1 CY2027, with Fleur listing in the late second half of calendar 2027 as the conservative assumption.

risks_watch: Q2 delivery versus management's claim that July was strong and August solid; the Q2 ARR recovery of 5-6% and the balance of negotiated versus non-negotiated business are unverified until the next print.
GST input-credit loss persists at about 2% of net revenue; the pace of pricing above Rs 7,500 (52% of room sales currently below) determines whether the drag falls as guided.
Mumbai and Gurgaon corporate demand softness and the roughly 2,000-room Mumbai airport supply overhang; Aurika Mumbai repricing may not translate into RevPAR growth.
Execution risk on the ~2,000-room FY27 opening target (334 opened in Q1) and on managed-hotel friction, including terminations that reduce net room additions.
Fleur capital deployment of Rs 2,500-3,000 crore and the debt-to-EBITDA path, plus demerger approvals (SEBI, shareholders, creditors, GST, NCLT) that could delay the H1 CY2027 completion.
Renovation spend and margin recovery depend on the H2 refurb schedule (about 800 rooms) and on FY28 margin of at least 50%, which management itself called a stretch if not achieved.

541301|2026-03.headline: Orient Electric Q4 FY26 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR948 crores and EBITDA margin improved to 8.2%, though gross margin fell to 31% on commodity inflation.
541301|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR948 crores, up 10% YoY, with Lighting and Switchgear up 16% and ECD up 7.6%. EBITDA rose 15.8% to INR77 crores (8.2% margin) and PAT rose 28.9% to INR40 crores, despite gross margin compressing to 31% from commodity inflation, labour shortage and West Asia gas disruption. For FY26, revenue grew 7.5% to INR3,326 crores, EBITDA rose 12.4% to INR229 crores (about 6.9% margin), and PBT before exceptional items rose 24.2% to about INR139 crores. Calibrated price increases of about 4% in Q4 and roughly 6% in April were taken, and management said these do not fully offset cost inflation.

financial_highlights.change: Hit by commodity inflation; about 100-150 bps impact from March price-action lag

segments.name: Lighting and Switchgear
segments.commentary: Revenue up 16% YoY on distribution expansion and premiumisation; consumer lighting grew double digits. High-value luminaires rose to 68% of mix from 63%; professional luminaires were flat. Wires roughly doubled, and switches and switchgear grew high double digits.

segments.name: ECD (Electrical Consumer Durables)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 7.6% YoY despite industry softness. Fans grew high single digit; BLDC grew over 50% and is 25% of domestic ceiling fan revenue. Premium mix is about 35% of domestic fan revenue, up from 30% last quarter.

segments.name: Appliances and e-commerce
segments.commentary: Appliances (heating, garment care) grew high double digits and e-commerce grew high double digits; quick commerce is 10% of digital channel. Exports grew double digits, with TPW a significant part.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q1 FY27 demand to improve, supported by a forecast of a hotter, more prolonged summer and a possible late-season surge in fans and cooling.
Further calibrated price increases are possible if commodity inflation continues; the company says cost recovery is a priority but competitiveness must be preserved.
Management remains committed to reaching double-digit EBITDA margins structurally once commodity inflation and supply disruptions subside; no specific timeline was given.
Gross margin guidance of 32-34% is unchanged, with Q4 running about 100-150 bps below it.
No FY27 numerical guidance was given; no share buyback is planned at present.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad plant utilisation is improving; TPW production is split between Kolkata and Hyderabad, and the plant is a hub for southern and export supply.
Hyderabad capex has been completed, per an analyst question; management did not add detail.
New products include Aero O2 (oxygen-enriching fan, about INR16,000), Aerosilent (under 50 dB, about INR8,000) and an inverter battery backup fan (about 6 hours of backup).
demand_pricing: Price increases: about 2.5-3% in January, 1-1.5% in March, and about 6% in April; fans, lighting and switchgear each about 6%, and wires increased roughly every 2-3 weeks.
Management says the incremental cost impact was slightly lower than the industry because part of its portfolio needed little spec change.
Market share gained about 30-40 bps per third-party data, described as broad-based across channels and markets, not limited to BLDC.
Channel inventory was elevated, and dealers were cautious on replenishment; Q4 channel build was described as normal.
Consumer offtake is about 45% in March-June and 55% in the balance of the year; premium and BLDC demand is more linear.
Cost pressure: labour shortage, commercial LPG unavailability, and minimum wage hikes of 35% in Haryana and 24% in UP.

qa_highlights.question: How much more price hike is needed to pass on the full incremental cost, and where are the fan market share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the price action was staggered (about 4% in Q4, about 6% in April) and the incremental impact was lower than the industry. Market share gains of 30-40 bps were broad-based across channels, not confined to BLDC.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital days rise to over 30 from 23?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to higher inventory built to hedge supply disruptions and higher payables.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the double-digit EBITDA margin target slipped, and when will it be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a 100-150 bps gross margin hit from the lag in price action in March. It remains committed to double-digit margins once commodity inflation and supply disruptions ease, with no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Why has gross margin not improved despite a higher premium mix and price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases do not fully offset commodity inflation, and labour productivity, LPG costs and wage hikes add further cost pressure. Premiumisation has helped EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is 2026 a year of protecting margins, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 FY26 was a washout and H2 exited with better EBITDA margins. It gave no numerical FY27 guidance and said challenges remain.

qa_highlights.question: Is pricing now a structural tailwind toward INR3,000 crore revenue and INR100 crore profit over FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see this as pricing power, calling it a catch-22 industry situation. It pointed to consumer-led product value as the real pricing power and said the aim is INR5,000 crore revenue with double-digit EBITDA.

Hyderabad plant utilisation and cost absorption; the plant is still a fixed-cost drag.

541301|2026-06.headline: Orient Electric Q1 FY27 revenue grew 23.5% YoY with PAT up 79.7% to INR31.5 crores, though gross margin fell to 29.8% on commodity inflation.
541301|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 saw a strong summer-led demand recovery from mid-April, with revenue up 23.5% YoY and ECD revenue up 22.7% to INR669 crores. Gross margin moderated to 29.8% under commodity and labour cost pressure, but EBITDA margin rose 102 bps YoY to 7% as fixed-cost discipline and Project Sanchay savings (INR10 crores) offset the pressure. Management took multiple calibrated price increases across categories, with fans cited at around 15-16% cumulative since December. Management declined to give margin guidance, reiterating only an aspiration of 32-34% gross margin and continued path to double-digit EBITDA margin.

segments.name: ECD (Fans, Appliances)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR669 crores, up 22.7% YoY, with high double-digit fan growth and double-digit appliance growth. BLDC grew 36% YoY and new products were 30% of fan revenue; premium mix reached 36% of domestic fan revenue.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Consumer (B2C) lighting grew high double digits; B2B/C-Loom grew high single digits, with tender business deliberately reduced. Lighting margin declined 40 bps YoY due to a 2-3 week lag in passing on commodity costs. High-value looms share rose to 60%, up 500 bps.

segments.name: Switchgear and Switches
segments.commentary: Both grew at double-digit rates. Management is launching a higher-value MCB subcategory in Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Wires
segments.commentary: Grew more than 200% YoY from a small base. Currently house wires only, sold mainly in North and East markets, with cross-sell through the fan dealer network (about 45% of large fan dealers also sell wires).

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Grew double digits, led by Africa and SAARC; Middle East was impacted. Hyderabad plant certifications completed over the last 2-3 quarters.

guidance_outlook: Management aspires to a 32-34% gross margin, but declined to guide given volatile inflation.
Management is committed to a path to double-digit EBITDA margin; timing depends on inflation. EBITDA margin trend: 5.3% (3 years ago), 6.6%, 6.9%, 8.2% in Q4, 7% in Q1 FY27.
Further Sanchay accruals expected in Q2 FY27 after INR10 crores in Q1.
Long-term aim of a healthy double-digit revenue CAGR; first milestone of INR5,000 crores revenue, with a prior 14-15% CAGR framework.
Marketing spend held at 4.4-4.5% of revenue (5.5% last year on the old basis, per management's comparison).
Management expects employee cost to stay range-bound as a percentage of sales, with automation helping over the long term but not in Q2.
capex_capacity: Ongoing automation of plants and processes to reduce labour cost dependence; benefits expected over the long term rather than in Q2.
Hyderabad plant is a core export base; international certifications completed.
Continued capex on new products, maintenance and capacity enhancement, described as spent as required rather than cut.
New product launches: Aero O2 (oxygen-enriching ceiling fan), Aerosilent (under 50 dB), Ecotech Volt; 3 Red Dot Design awards won.
demand_pricing: Demand: cooling net demand revived from mid-April and stayed robust through May, moderating toward quarter end. Management said Q1 was a balanced sell-in and sell-out quarter with no inventory build-up.

Pricing: fans had 6 price increases from December to June, cumulatively about 15-16%, with about 10% sequential QoQ in fans. Appliances had about 4 increases (high single to double digit). Lighting rose about 10% over 5-6 months. Switchgear rose high double digit. Wires are priced with a 15-day lag to LME.
Competition: management said most leading brands did not take a June price increase, while start-up brands took about half of Orient's increase. Orient says it has priced slightly ahead of peers.
DTM network added about 3,600 retailers in the quarter. E-commerce grew double digits.
Management said Chinese TPW fans are more price-competitive than Indian products; Europe entry is targeted before the next season.

qa_highlights.question: How much of ECD growth came from price increases, and how much more pricing is needed to offset raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was volume plus value across categories, with fans taking about 6 increases from December to June (about 10% sequential in Q1). It said further price action will be calibrated to commodity moves.

qa_highlights.question: Is there trade inventory build-up in Q1, and how do DTM and non-DTM markets compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no inventory build-up and the quarter was secondary-led. Both DTM and MD markets grew healthy double digits with volume growth, and no split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Can gross margin recover in Q2 and what margin range is expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 32-34% gross margin aspiration but gave no guidance. It said some commodity prices reversed in recent days, Sanchay accruals will continue, and it will act calibrated to inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall YoY, and was ad spend cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said marketing spend was flat in value YoY, with a shift from IPL to digital and premium media. Marketing was 4.5% of sales versus 5.5% last year and is planned at 4.4-4.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will employee costs keep rising, and is operating leverage exhausted?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost rose 10.7% YoY because of minimum wage increases, but fell to 8.9% of sales from 9.9% a year ago. Management expects it to stay range-bound as a share of sales, with automation as the lever.

qa_highlights.question: What is the lighting margin decline and B2B performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the 40 bps lighting margin decline to a 2-3 week lag in passing on commodity increases. B2C grew high double digits, B2B C-Loom grew high single digits, and tender business was cut deliberately.

risks_watch: Commodity volatility (copper, aluminium, LME-linked wires) and pass-through lag, which compressed gross margin to 29.8%.
Labour cost inflation from minimum wage increases, with employee cost up 10.7% YoY.
Price-led growth may be tested if the industry does not follow Orient's price increases; start-up brands priced below it.
Quarter-end demand moderation and festive-season sentiment; channel inventory normalisation.
Wires scale-up and the switchgear/switch product pipeline, including the higher-value MCB launch in Q2.
541301|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, volume growth and EBITDA trajectory, but notably cautious and non-committal on gross margin, which management said cannot be guided given volatile commodity and wage inflation. 541336|2026-03.headline: IndoStar Q4 FY26 net loss of INR424 crores on INR326 crores extra SR provision and INR49 crores West Asia overlay, despite 17% QoQ disbursement growth to INR1,306 crores.

Q4 was loss-making because of an additional INR326 crores provision on SRs, a INR49 crores management overlay for West Asia risk, and about INR55 crores of extra ECL charge from the annual model refresh. qa_highlights.answer: Management said about two quarters of lag, with supplies starting in Q4, and 30-35% FY28 growth with EU-GMP. Growth without EU is 10-15%. About 60-70% of growth is attributed to EU.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 8-10 EU MAs need refiling if EU-GMP is delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: No refiling is needed unless the delay goes beyond three to four months. The MA depends on a valid EU-GMP certificate, and the 210-day procedure is near its end.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be double digit at about INR 500 crore revenue, and what are the non-EU economics?
qa_highlights.answer: At INR 410-420 crore margins stay near last year's level. At INR 450-460 crore management said margins would be mid-teens or 13-14%. Q2 results will show whether FY27 overshoots INR 420 crore.

risks_watch: Timing of the EU-GMP final report and CAPA acceptance; management said it could take two to three months after the report for approval, and any delay beyond three to four months may require MA refiling.
Q1 EBITDA margin of 3.7% and PAT loss; investors questioned low ROE (below 5% historically) against a cost of capital around 10%.
Debt of INR 145.2 crore with high debtor days (about 100), and a target to reduce them to about 80.
Dependence on NIP/OTF revenue ramp and on 8-10 EU approvals; partner launches (UK star product, Neuraxpharm) depend on EU-GMP.
Middle East disruption; management said there was an impact in Q1 that appeared to be stabilising.
541400|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the EU-GMP outcome and FY28 growth, but cautious and sometimes evasive on near-term margins and revenue, which management tied to Q2 results. Several answers were vague on numbers, such as the FY28 INR 500 crore question, which was not confirmed.
key_quotes: So, we believe that if without EU, if we look at INR 410-420 number, we would have EBITDA margin similar to last year because of the increased costs.
It's about timing now. So, hopefully, that will come soon enough, and then we can start getting the revenues from EU.
There are no adverse observations. There is no critical observations, which is what is important.
Obviously, if it goes beyond three to four months, it'll have to be redone.

541402|2026-03.headline: FY26 standalone EBITDA margin rose to 14.45% from 8.96% on 4% lower revenue; consolidated PAT turned to ₹6.97 Cr profit from a ₹11.65 Cr loss.
541402|2026-03.overview: FY26 was framed as a transformation year: management chose selective, higher-margin projects over volume, and standalone total income fell to ₹11,093 lakh from ₹16,069 lakh. Consolidated EBITDA swung to ₹1,716 lakh (14.19% margin) from a loss of ₹233 lakh, helped by about ₹151 lakh of GST provision reversal and ₹130 lakh of ODI loan interest in other income. Humro (ARAPL RaaS, 83% subsidiary) secured a ₹48 Cr strategic investment, which will dilute ARAPL's holding below 50% once allotment completes. Management stopped giving numerical guidance, citing only a directional aim to beat FY26 "much much better".

segments.name: Automation (ARAPL, domestic)
segments.commentary: Welding lines for automotive OEMs such as Honda, Magna, Tata, Mahindra and Suzuki. Order book ₹4,496 lakh at 31 May 2026 (opening ₹2,696 lakh plus ₹1,800 lakh new bookings, per the presentation). Management said the verticals' combined book is about ₹127 Cr.

segments.name: Car parking (ARAPL)
segments.commentary: Multilevel parking, with customers including Lodha. Order book ₹820 lakh at 31 May 2026 (opening ₹580 lakh, new ₹155 lakh per the slide). Management plans to start exporting parking products in 6-9 months and to scale domestically.

segments.name: Warehouse automation (Humro / ARAPL RaaS, 83% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Mobile robots and WES for Fortune 50 customers; about 15 units and roughly $25,000 per month of revenue since December 2025. Order book ~$3 Mn (30-35 units, lease model, ₹36 Cr); outright-sale pipeline ~₹60 Cr. Target 225 robots in FY27, which management has not revised.

guidance_outlook: No numerical revenue or margin guidance; management said it has stopped giving number guidance and expects FY27 to be 'much much better' than FY26.
Humro FY27 target of 225 robots maintained; management said demand is 'much more' than supply.
Humro margin target of 15-18% on RaaS and outright sales, described as a moving target. Management said year-one EBITDA is not the focus; the aim is 15-20 good customers.
Next-quarter timing: Q1 is seasonally weak and profitability is expected from Q2 onward.
Humro pricing aim to cut prices by 50% over the next two years, with product-level price deflation.
ARAPL's first new product (exportable) targeted for mechanical completion in June/July 2026 and readiness by November/December 2026; radical growth expected in FY28.
capex_capacity: Five plants covering 350,000 sq ft; around 300 permanent staff and 100 contract workers (per the chairman's remarks).
Humro in-house manufacturing line: first product targeted by end-June 2026, a second model by August, and five products manufactured locally this year.
Humro inventory in the US is about 29 units, of which 5-6 are demos and 5-6 are in sales. About 20 units are to be commercially sold, with 12-15 already deployed.
FY27 deployment schedule: first 15 units ship around end-June/first week of July 2026 and a further 10 around 15 July, for deployment July-September; a further 50-60 units are being built.
Planned US strategic partner to hold local inventory, cutting delivery lead time from about 4 months to about 15 days.
demand_pricing: Humro's ₹36 Cr lease-model book equates to about $100,000 per month of lease rental; about $25,000 per month is currently billing, with $75,000 expected within one to two months.
Management said it is priced around 15-20% below Chinese competitors; named US competitors are Vecna, Seegrid and VisionNav.
Management said the April-May 2026 Humro deployments were nil; 24 units were contracted and expected to deploy over the next couple of months.
Order timelines for automation work have slipped 6-8 months as customers deferred spending (per management), and some orders were rejected on profitability.

Domestic AMR opportunity: management says customers importing more than 500 AMRs from China into India are being targeted as a substitute. Management said it will not take low-margin India execution work.

qa_highlights.question: How many Humro robots were deployed in April-May against the 225-unit FY27 target, and is the target being revised?
qa_highlights.answer: No new installs in April-May; 24 units were contracted for deployment in the following months. Management said there is no revision to the 225-unit target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY26 revenue fall sharply when the Q3 call indicated flat revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it rejected low-margin orders and added a cost-control department. Customers also deferred timelines by 6-8 months from February 2026 amid a global constraint, which delayed dispatch and revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How does Humro compare with competitors on quality and price in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management named Vecna, Seegrid and VisionNav, saying they are about two years ahead. It claims pricing 15-20% below Chinese offers and cites technology, Indian software and easy integration as advantages.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ₹48 Cr investment will go to which uses, and what happens to ARAPL's holding?
qa_highlights.answer: The ARAPL holding is 83% now and will drop below 50% once allotment completes. Most funds go to operations and marketing, with some to product development; management said it does not plan local US manufacturing for now.

qa_highlights.question: Can minority shareholders still benefit after Humro is no longer a subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ARAPL will consolidate its share of around 43-45% of Humro profit, and that minority benefits are intact. No detailed structure was given.

risks_watch: Humro's execution: deployments have slipped, with only about $25,000 per month of revenue against a $100,000 per month lease target.
Dilution of ARAPL's stake in Humro below 50% and the consolidation impact (around 43-45% share of profit), which minority shareholders questioned.
Dependence on imported components (motors, motor controllers and radar sensors) that management said are European or Japanese brands but imported via China.
US tariff exposure, which management said has come down from 50% to 25% (and about 20-22% now), with a further policy change expected within two years.
Order-book slippage in automation: customers deferring timelines by 6-8 months.
Lack of numerical guidance for FY27 and FY28, plus Q1 seasonal losses.
541402|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on margins and the Humro pipeline, but evasive on numbers: management declined to give revenue or margin guidance and repeatedly redirected questions on FY27 revenue and Humro's quantified economics.

We are very, very competitively priced, around 15 to 20 percent lower than what the Chinese are offering.
So, number guidance or margin guidance we have stopped giving.
So, my sole target is to reduce the price by 50% in next two years.

541403|2026-03.headline: Dollar Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13.2% YoY to INR622 crore, but gross margin fell 169 bps to 28.1% on mix and cotton costs; price hikes of 4-6% planned.
541403|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating income grew 13.2% YoY to INR622 crore and volume grew 12.0%, but gross margin compressed 169 bps to 28.1% as the economy segment rose to 47% of revenue and cotton/yarn costs rose. Operating EBITDA grew only 2.0% to INR58 crore (9.3% margin), while PAT rose 11.4% to INR33 crore. For FY26, operating income rose 10.0% to INR1,881 crore, EBITDA 9.3% to INR200 crore (10.6% margin) and PAT 18.0% to INR107 crore. Management implemented a calibrated price hike in April (3-4%) and plans another 2-3% in June, and it deferred FY27 guidance to the Q1 call.

segments.name: Economy (Dollar Always)
segments.commentary: Rose to 47% of Q4 revenue from 45% in Q4 FY25 and about 41% for FY26 (FY25: 39.1%); management cited this as the main driver of lower realisation.

segments.name: Dollar Man / Regular and Big Boss
segments.commentary: Regular 41.5% and Big Boss 36.5% of FY26 revenue; Dollar Man category share fell to 36.5% from 38.8% in FY25.

segments.name: Missy (women's)
segments.commentary: About 7.5% of FY26 revenue, down from 8.0% in FY25.

segments.name: Thermals
segments.commentary: 6.1% of FY26 revenue, up from 5.9% in FY25.

segments.name: Force NXT (super premium)
segments.commentary: Value +16.5% and volume +26.2% in FY26; 4.5% of revenue, up from 4.2%. Q4 value +16.0%, volume +24.3%.

segments.name: Dollar Protect (rainwear)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume +49.9%; FY26 volume +18%; 2.1% of revenue.

segments.name: Quick commerce / non-traditional channels
segments.commentary: Quick commerce grew 437% YoY and rose to 2.5% of revenue from 0.5%; non-traditional channels (MT, e-commerce, QC) grew 24.2% in FY26.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR49 crore (+45% YoY), PAT INR4.9 crore (~10% margin).

segments.name: Pepe Inner Fashion JV
segments.commentary: Only bottom line consolidated (51% stake); revenue not in top line; D2C via large-format stores.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 guidance; management will give full-year guidance on or before the Q1 FY27 call.
Management expects double-digit volume and value growth in FY27 and says margins should be better than FY26 (FY26 EBITDA margin 10.6%; management cited ~10.82%).
Price hikes: about 3-4% in April and 2-3% in June (total 4-6%; CFO cited 6-7%); management says no further hike is needed as cotton and yarn prices stabilise.
Cash conversion cycle to fall a further 5-7 days in FY27, mainly from receivable days.
Modern trade expected to grow 20-25% in FY27.
Debt of about INR264 crore expected to be reduced to zero by FY28; no major capex planned.
capex_capacity: No major capex commitments in the near term; capacity can be flexed 20-30% by adding job workers without capex.
FY26 production volume about 28 crore pieces; knitting, bleaching and cutting are in-house, while stitching (mainly economy and mix) is outsourced to job workers.
Pilot run of Phase 2 of Project Lakshya has started, focused on deepening active retailers in gold states; non-dominant state entry is on hold pending tailored strategies.
Merger of nine promoter (RPT) companies: NCLT application filed and first motion approved; expected to save INR4-5 crore a year in royalty, service charges and rent, with negligible revenue effect.
demand_pricing: Q4 gross margin decline attributed mainly to economy-segment mix (47%) and higher yarn prices that were not passed on; management denied meaningful down-trading and said the shift was temporary.
Demand described as stable; Q4 retail footfall dipped due to heat, which management called timing, not structural.
Management says the price hike has not hurt demand and that competitive intensity is stabilising; no market share loss is expected since peers are also raising prices.
Lakshya contribution to revenue was about 27% in Q4 versus 29% a year earlier, but management said the full-year contribution was flat.

qa_highlights.question: Is the price hike a one-off, how large is it, and does it come with scheme rollbacks?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry-wide hike after about 2 years: 3-4% in April and 2-3% in June, total about 4-6% (CFO cited 6-7%). It is a pure price increase; schemes and discounts are unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Can debt of INR264 crore be substantially reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said debt can be reduced to zero by FY28; about INR50 crore of short- and long-term borrowings were repaid last year. Management expects further cash from a 5-7 day cycle reduction.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 gross margin decline, cotton or competition?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said mix (economy at 47%) and yarn costs were the main factors; prices were unchanged while realisation fell. Management denied meaningful discounting.

qa_highlights.question: Is the economy-segment shift structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is temporary, citing high demand in Tier 2/3 and rural areas, formalisation from unorganised players, and advertising of Dollar Lehar from the past three years. Force NXT grew 25-26%.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin return to double digits and what is the FY27 growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 margins should be better than FY26 and it is eyeing double-digit growth, but gave no specific number and deferred guidance to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory and working-capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days fell from about 130 to 100; management said optimised inventory is 95-100 days given the 90-day production cycle, and receivables are the main lever for the next 5-7 day reduction.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure: Q4 gross margin fell 169 bps; whether June price hike offsets yarn costs and mix is the key Q1 test.
Economy-segment share at 47% of revenue; a continued shift would keep realisation and margin pressured.
Q1 demand softness from heat and footfall; management says it is timing, not structural.
Lakshya Phase 2 pilot results and the pace of new-state entry, which management has put on hold.
Working capital: receivable-day reduction of 5-7 days is targeted; inventory days may not stay at FY26 levels.
Merger of promoter companies (NCLT) and the JV's contribution to consolidated bottom line.

It's not a structural thing which is happening. It's a very temporary thing.
Right now, I'm unable to give you a number and we will surely come back with a number on or before the Q1 earnings call.

rows.why: No specific new product or brand launch was discussed; Force NXT and Dollar Protect growth were cited but no new launches.

rows.why: CCC fell from 160 to 154 days in FY26 and inventory days dropped from about 130 to 100; management targets a further 5-7 day cut, mainly receivables, and debt of INR264 crore to zero by FY28.

rows.label: Modern trade and quick commerce growth
rows.why: Management eyes 20-25% modern trade growth in FY27; quick commerce grew 437% and rose to 2.5% of revenue from 0.5%, non-traditional channels grew 24.2% in FY26.

rows.why: NCLT first motion approved on merger of nine RPT companies, expected to save INR4-5 crore a year in royalty, service charges and rent against FY26 PAT of INR107 crore.

541403|2026-06.headline: Dollar Industries Q1 FY27: operating EBITDA up 11.4% to INR 48 crore at 11.8% margin, on price hikes and no discounting, while volume fell 1.6%.

Rajan Anandan (Peak XV) appointed as invitee and external expert on the Technology Committee for a three-year term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the new TER/BER regulation and how will distribution commissions change?

qa_highlights.question: Why has one-year scheme performance and industry ranking weakened?

qa_highlights.question: Are FY27 and FY28 expense growth targets available?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific guidance is given. Employee and non-employee costs have grown at about 13% CAGR over five years and are expected to grow in line with business and investments.

qa_highlights.question: What was the reason for the other income increase, and how is the balance sheet positioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said balance sheet equity is mainly SEBI skin-in-the-game MF holdings, which saw drawdowns in Q4. The remainder is in liquid and debt funds with modest duration and passive management.

qa_highlights.question: Will HDFC AMC launch new NFOs or SIF products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has secured all regulatory approvals for SIF. It is designing a couple of differentiated products but views the category as strategic rather than immediate. Management will stay selective on new launches.

risks_watch: SEBI base expense ratio change from April 1, 2026: margin effect depends on commission restructuring, and management said the impact is not yet quantified precisely.
Sustainability of flows if markets stay weak for longer; management cautioned that investor behaviour has not been tested over an extended downturn.
HDFC Bank channel share is declining, and management said the bank remains open architecture, with event-driven flow variability.
Rising costs from talent, technology and AI investments versus margin targets, with no formal cost guidance.
Alternatives and PMS economics are thinner for non-discretionary government mandates (EPFO/SPFO), and SIF launch timing is undefined.
Mark-to-market exposure on the SEBI skin-in-the-game equity holdings on the balance sheet.

Revenue from operations rose 14% YoY to INR11 billion and PAT rose 12% YoY to INR8.4 billion. Management said margins were maintained despite a regime change from TER to BER accounting, the removal of the 5 bps exit-load-linked charge, and brokerage rationalisation from 1 April 2026. Debt QAAUM fell and debt market share was under pressure, while SIP and systematic flows kept growing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt AUM fall about 6% QoQ and why are debt outflows strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said investors redeemed debt funds on rupee, rate and crude volatility while liquid funds saw inflows; HDFC AMC has a decent share of both moves.

qa_highlights.question: Is the yield uptick from product mix or the TER/BER change, and what is the PMS/AIF contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not read too much into early-quarter movement post the accounting change. Alternatives earn 80-90 bps management fee; PMS discretionary book is in line with equity margins, non-discretionary is very tight economics.

qa_highlights.question: Has the distribution commission been rationalised and will revenue yield benefit in later quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Changes from 1 April 2026: removal of 5 bps extra TER charged in lieu of exit load, shift from TER to BER plus statutory levies, and brokerage rationalisation. Offset through commission optimisation and cost control; margins maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ESOP cost jump, and is FY27 guidance unchanged?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 cost of about INR23 crore reflects a June 2025 grant under the new plan; FY27 non-cash ESOP cost guided at INR79-80 crore, unchanged at INR67 crore level per analyst reference point is for prior guide. Management said costs should be viewed annually.

qa_highlights.question: Was there an operating cost growth guidance of 12-13% ex non-cash?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said to focus on the 33-35 bps net operating margin corridor rather than quarterly cost trends.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the performance improvement in June?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited top-two-quartile performance over 2 and 3 years on AUM-weighted basis; Balance Advantage Fund in Q1 over 3, 5, 10 years, and Flexicap in Q1 over 2, 3, 5, 10 years.

risks_watch: Debt AUM outflows and debt market share pressure; management said it needs to make debt funds more attractive to retail.

Distributor-channel share shifts toward fintechs; bank share fell to 9.6% from 10.4%.

Yield trajectory under the new TER-to-BER regime; management did not give forward yield guidance.

541729|2026-09.headline: HDFC AMC Q2 FY27: revenue from operations up 14% YoY to INR11.7 billion; operating profit up 16% to INR9.1 billion at 36 bps of AUM.
541729|2026-09.overview: Quarterly average AUM rose 10% YoY and 4% QoQ to INR9.69 trillion, with equity-oriented AUM at 67.1% versus 57.5% for the industry. Revenue from operations was INR11.7 billion (+14% YoY), operating profit INR9.1 billion (+16%), and PBT INR9.8 billion (+12%). Reported PAT is not comparable YoY because the year-ago quarter had a INR468 million tax provision reversal. Management pushed alternatives, PMS and GIFT City as growth areas, and defended cost growth as a mix of routine costs and forward investment.

segments.name: Active equity
segments.commentary: Yield of 61 bps; overall equity yield 58 bps, with a marginal sequential rise attributed mainly to asset mix. Active equity AUM INR6.08 trillion at 12.7% share.

segments.name: Debt
segments.commentary: Yield about 28-29 bps. Debt AUM INR1.62 trillion, 13% market share.

segments.name: Liquid
segments.commentary: Yield 13 bps. Liquid AUM INR860 billion, up 10% YoY.

segments.name: Alternatives and PMS
segments.commentary: Two new alternative funds launched: a Category II late-stage venture/growth fund and a first Category III fund; a Category II private equity fund (fund of funds) is fully committed to 13 GPs. EPFO fixed income mandate went live this quarter; management says AIF fees run 80-90 bps above equity MF fees. Share of non-MF revenue described as small.

segments.name: Passive and GIFT City
segments.commentary: Around 50 passive products; second-largest in index funds among retail-heavy categories. Six inbound and two outbound GIFT City funds.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give timelines for alternatives revenue (e.g., INR100 crore target).

Management expects a steady CSR-related cost skew to unwind; asks investors to assess costs on a full-year basis.
FY27 non-cash ESOP expense expected at about INR79-80 crore.
capex_capacity: Cost commentary: investments in people (alternatives team of over 20 investment professionals; MF team about 40 versus 30 a couple of years back), investor servicing, operations, distribution, international and technology/AI.
Balance sheet cash deployed as seed capital for alternative platforms; Board has distributed almost all post-tax distributable cash profits over the last three years.
Systematic transactions 19 million in September (up from about 17 million in June); monthly SIP flows INR325 billion in September.
demand_pricing: Industry: equity-oriented net inflows INR1,161 billion in the quarter; 67th consecutive month of positive equity flows. Debt funds net outflows INR607 billion; liquid inflows INR457 billion; ETFs INR367 billion.
Systematic flows (SIP + STP) INR48 billion in September, up 6% YoY. Management says softness is in STP (paused by wealth managers when markets were choppy), while SIP-only market share rose.
Unique investors 17.7 million (28% penetration), added 3.2 million in last year versus industry 6.3 million. Live individual accounts 32 million, up from 26 million.

Market share in the quarter was 11.1% versus a prior best of 11.5% per an analyst; hybrid categories such as multi-asset, aggressive hybrid and equity savings saw share correction, with a new hybrid fund manager brought in.
Management said mid-cap fund is above INR1 lakh crore; small-cap fund about INR40,000 crore and ranked second or third in its category.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give timelines; launched two new alternative funds and says the platform now works as full stack.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the comparison is not like-for-like; the softness is in STP, while SIP-only share rose. Systematic transactions rose from about 17 million to 19 million.

qa_highlights.question: Why did staff and non-staff costs fall QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company keeps tight cost control while investing in people, alternatives, international, digital and AI; no split of routine versus investment cost was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the equity yield gap versus peers due to product mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yields vary by fund size; TER falls as AUM rises, and three funds are above INR1 lakh crore. No yield guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is H1 expense growth high?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CSR expenses were taken in Q1, skewing H1; asked investors to look at full-year costs.

541741|2026-03.headline: Fratelli Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR36 crores and EBITDA turned near breakeven at INR1.06 crores for FY26, with FY27 guidance of about 30% growth.
541741|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 net revenue rose about 13% YoY to INR36 crores, with gross margin at 79% and EBITDA loss narrowing to INR3.7 crores from INR7 crores a year earlier. For the full year, revenue was nearly flat at INR184 crores (about 1% growth) because of regulatory disruptions in Maharashtra, Telangana and Uttarakhand in H1, and FY EBITDA was INR1 crore. Management said conditions normalised in H2 and that Q1 FY27 momentum continued, and guided to about 30% growth in FY27 with PAT breakeven at roughly INR240 crores of revenue. The RTD brand Shotgun sold about 100,000 cases in its first year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 3-4% credit cost guidance conservative, given PAR accretion is under 10 bps?

qa_highlights.question: What drives the NIM decline in guidance, and will cost-to-income rise?

541967|2026-03.headline: Sky Gold guides FY27 revenue INR8,100 crore and FY30 PAT INR945 crore, targets 50%+ debt reduction in FY27 with working capital cut to 59 days.
541967|2026-03.overview: Management said Q4 FY26 outpaced industry peers on wedding and festive demand, with B2B volumes steady despite the recent customs duty hike and government appeal to curb gold consumption. Net working capital days fell to 59 from 71 a year earlier, and operating cash flow improved from negative INR272 crore to negative INR45 crore for the year. Management revised its guidance framing: it will no longer give volume guidance, keeps FY30 PAT of INR945 crore, and sees 30-35% revenue CAGR with an advanced gold model that lowers reported revenue but adds margin. Phase 3 is funded wholly from internal cash, with a net debt-free balance sheet targeted by FY30.

Gold metal loan (GML) facility sanctioned INR170 crore; GML outstanding nil at March-end 2026, with use dependent on pricing.
Statutory auditor changed to MSKA & Associates LLP (BDO International member).
demand_pricing: B2B demand stable per management; lightweight and studded jewellery mix is the margin lever; diamond jewellery at about 1.5% of sales.
Management says 18kt is gaining share versus 22kt, which still holds 70-75% of sales; some shift toward bullion and coins noted at retail.
Advanced gold margin is 70-125 bps lower than outright gold sales, but is PAT-accretive as it avoids working capital and interest.
Management says gold price correction of about 10% in recent days is driving customer demand; gold price was about INR1,55,000 per 10g as quoted on the call.
Akshaya Tritiya on 20 April: some Q4 inventory was held back and delivered in early April, which raised inventory days.

qa_highlights.question: Will the customs duty hike and government appeal to reduce gold consumption hit revenue or volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no order softening has been seen at B2B level as the company is focused on lightweight jewellery; the retail gold exchange share reportedly rose from 20% to 40%, and it is too early to call June-July demand.

qa_highlights.question: Is the shift to lower karat and bullion/coins a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is part of the strategy; 9kt, 14kt and 18kt carry better margins, while 22kt remains 70-75% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why has gold metal loan usage dropped to zero?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said GML is currently costlier than local market purchases, so it is used only when PAT-accretive; GML facility of INR170 crore remains sanctioned.

qa_highlights.question: Does the setup of a Dubai office for duty-free gold get affected by the 100 kg advanced licence restriction?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the restriction applies only to advanced authorisation licences, which the company is not using now, so there is no impact; gold availability is not seen as an issue.

qa_highlights.question: Will receivable days return to FY24 levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivable days should return to 22-23 days within 4-6 quarters as export and shorter-credit customers are prioritised.

qa_highlights.question: How does volume growth fit with 30-35% revenue CAGR, and what is the hedging policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 27-28% of growth is volume-led; the company is about 99% hedged, using MCX futures as the only tool available in India, with zero GML now.

541967|2026-06.headline: Sky Gold Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 78% YoY to INR2,013 crores, with gross margin at 9.3% and operating cash flow of about INR30 crores.

Gross margin rose to 9.3% from 9.1% in Q4 FY26, driven by a higher share of non-22KT jewellery and studded products. EBITDA was INR157 crores (7.8% margin) and operating PAT crossed INR100 crores for the first time. Operating cash flow turned positive at about INR30 crores, and working capital days edged up to 60 from 59 in March. Management said it will revise FY27 guidance only after Diwali.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt was INR540 crores at quarter end.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation and capex plans?

qa_highlights.answer: Guidance was set at end-2025 for a five-year horizon; volume discounts of 0.25-0.5% on large 22KT orders dilute margins. Management said guidance may be improved.

FY26 AUM reached Rs 234.5 bn (up 15% YoY) while FY26 disbursements grew 11% to Rs 67.8 bn, below the aspiration. Asset quality improved sequentially, with 1+ DPD at 3.17% (down 63 bps QoQ) and GNPA at 1.05% (down 14 bps QoQ). Management acknowledged weak volume productivity and opex growth outpacing AUM, and is pushing risk-adjusted pricing and direct sourcing to address these.

541988|2026-06.headline: AAVAS Q1FY27: net profit up 23% YoY to Rs 1.71 bn, NII up 18%, but management sees spread falling below 5% over the year.
541988|2026-06.overview: Disbursements rose 41% YoY to Rs 16.1 bn on a low base, and AUM grew 15.4% YoY to Rs 239.3 bn as of June end. NIM rose 22 bps YoY to 7.70% and cost-to-income improved 254 bps to 43.7%. Asset quality metrics improved YoY, with 1+DPD at 3.76% and gross Stage 3 at 1.11%. Management flagged spread pressure from competition and a 10 bps PLR cut in June, taking the cumulative cut to 25 bps since March 2026, and an intent to regain home loan share.

segments.name: Home loans (HL)
segments.commentary: HL disbursement volumes grew 17% YoY in Q1 per management, and the company is refocusing on HL to rebalance the HL/NHL book toward roughly 65:35. HL carries 150-200 bps lower yield than NHL.

segments.name: Non-housing loans (NHL: LAP, MSME)
segments.commentary: Management described NHL as LAP and MSME products. The company said it has no builder loan product.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: 22-23% top-line growth and 17-18% AUM growth; medium-term AUM growth of about 20%.
Management expects spread to fall to just below 5% over the rest of the year, while still expecting ROA and ROE to hold at planned levels.
Target to lift productivity per field resource from Rs 8-10 lakh to Rs 20-22 lakh, to be achieved in about two years.
June disbursements exceeded Rs 600 crore; management aims to keep disbursements on a high run-rate through the next nine months.
Management reiterated credit-quality guidance and said it is confident of holding it.
capex_capacity: Branch network expanded to 440 branches across 15 states during Q1; further branch expansion planned, with focus on faster branch break-even.
Borrowing liquidity: cash, cash equivalents and unavailed CC limits of Rs 18.8 bn; documented unavailed sanctions of Rs 4.85 bn as of June 30, 2026.
demand_pricing: Healthy competition across geographies with spread pressure; management said it is consciously pursuing HL share regain, which will cost some NIM.
Monthly AUM additions rose nearly 50% YoY; management said the company now reaches in three months what took about five months previously.
PLR cut 10 bps effective June 2026 (cumulative 25 bps since March 2026), with the company saying disbursement yield and portfolio yield are now close to each other.
Repayment rates rose to above 19% in the last two quarters versus a historical 16-17%; the uptick was in April and early May, especially in small-ticket loans above 14% interest, and eased in June.

Borrowings: 42% linked to external benchmarks (Repo, T-Bill, MIBOR) and 34% to sub-3-month MCLR, so about 76% reprices quickly; average borrowing tenor is longer than asset tenor, giving positive ALM.

qa_highlights.question: How intense is competition by product and geography, and can operating leverage offset spread compression?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees healthy competition and spread pressure, and expects spread to go below 5% for the full year. It says cost-to-income and revenue-per-resource levers should keep ROE and ROA near plan, even with some compression.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the repayment rate rising, and what is the June disbursement run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Repayments rose in April and early May in small-ticket segments above 14%, then came back to trend in June. June disbursements were above Rs 600 crore, and the company is targeting 22-23% disbursement growth and 17-18% AUM growth over the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the disbursement per branch that underpins the medium-term 20% AUM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected that current-year guidance is 17-18% AUM growth, with 20% as the medium-term target. Productivity is to rise from Rs 8-10 lakh to Rs 20-22 lakh per field resource, which management said it would shorten to two years.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company regain home loan market share, given a low two-year CAGR in HL files?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants to rebalance HL and NHL toward about 65:35, with branch-level targeted acquisition for the next 9-12 months. HL volumes were up 17% YoY in Q1. It accepts a small NIM compression from the HL push.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gap between disbursement yield and portfolio yield after the June PLR cut, and what is the spread outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the two yields are now nearly equal and the reported yield and spread already reflect the June cut. It expects spread to fall a little below 5% for the rest of the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the recent RBI asset classification circular on repossessed assets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the circular is under evaluation and any required change will be made.

risks_watch: Spread compression below 5% from competition and PLR cuts, with HL push adding further NIM pressure.
Stress in tours and travel and restaurant segments, linked to the Middle East conflict and fuel prices; the company tightened policies from February. Rainfall shortfall is also a watch item.
Repayment and part-prepayment trends in small-ticket, higher-yield loans; management says June normalised.
Pending evaluation of the RBI asset-classification circular on repossessed assets.
Interim CFO in place, and the CEO appointment is subject to RBI approval.

542011|2026-03.headline: GRSE posted record FY26: revenue INR 7,002 crore (+38%) and PAT INR 748 crore (+42%), with order book down to INR 15,324 crore.
542011|2026-03.overview: Management reported best-ever Q4 and FY26 results, with Q4 revenue of INR 2,119 crore (+29% YoY) and PAT of INR 303 crore (from INR 244 crore). Eight warships were delivered in FY26, including three on a single day, and the company said revenue from the bridges vertical crossed INR 200 crore for the first time. The order book fell to INR 15,324 crore, the first time it has dropped below INR 20,000 crore in five years, which management attributed to faster execution. The NGC corvette contract (~INR 33,000 crore, GRSE as L1) is still unsigned; management now expects signing in the June quarter, and it pushes NGC revenue recognition to H2 FY28.

financial_highlights.change: vs 8.3% in FY25 (as cited by analyst; includes Q4 provision write-back benefit per analyst)
lower; first time below INR 20,000 crore in five years

segments.name: Warship / defence shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Warship order book about INR 11,361 crore. P-17 Alpha has about INR 5,868 crore remaining, NGOPV INR 5,168 crore and ASW Shallow Water Craft INR 2,035 crore. Eight warships delivered in FY26.

segments.name: Non-defence / commercial vessels
segments.commentary: Order book about INR 3,369 crore across Ocean Research Vessel (INR 749 crore), Coastal Research Vessels (INR 260 crore), Acoustic Research Ship (INR 456 crore), hybrid ferries (INR 207 crore), Multipurpose Vessels (INR 1,345 crore) and dredger (INR 66 crore).

segments.name: Naval guns and portable steel bridges
segments.commentary: Seven naval surface guns delivered in FY26, four completed Sea Acceptance Trials. 110 portable steel bridges delivered, including 30 for export; bridges revenue above INR 200 crore for the first time, export revenue above INR 270 crore.

guidance_outlook: NGC contract (~INR 33,000 crore) expected to be signed in the June 2026 quarter; no revenue planned in FY27 or H1 FY28; revenue to start in H2 FY28, major chunk from FY29.

FY27 revenue accrual expected to be 'very healthy', in line with the last three to four years; FY28 to be padded by remaining projects, NGOPV, commercial vessels and new orders. Management declined to confirm FY28 revenue will not dip.
EBITDA margins expected to be similar in FY27, and management will try to maintain similar margins in FY28 and FY29.
Capacity to rise from 28 platforms to 32 ships by end of calendar 2026 via modernisation; plans for two brownfield and two greenfield yards (West Bengal and Gujarat).

Pipeline of about INR 1,50,000 crore of AoN-accorded RFPs (excluding NGC), with P-17 Bravo (~INR 70,000 crore) RFP expected in the current quarter; MCV (~INR 32,000 crore) and LPD (~INR 35,000 crore) RFPs by end of FY27.
capex_capacity: Current shipbuilding capacity is 28 platforms; expected to rise to 32 ships by end of calendar 2026 through in-premises modernisation.
Planned expansion: two brownfield shipbuilding facilities in West Bengal and two greenfield facilities (one in West Bengal, one in Gujarat).
ASW Shallow Water Craft: four delivered, two at ~80% construction with basin trials done (delivery by mid-calendar 2026), last two at ~60% (delivery in FY27).
P-17 Alpha last ship at ~74% physical progress, delivery targeted in calendar 2026. NGOPV first ship launch planned on 20 May 2026; project completion in FY29.

Ocean Research Vessel ~50% complete, launch planned in calendar 2026. Acoustic Research Ship ~20% complete. 13 hybrid ferries (6 x 200-PAX, 7 x 100-PAX) to finish by end FY27; first two 100-PAX launches planned in May 2026. German 12-ship MPV: keel laid on three ships. Bangladesh dredger launch planned in FY27.
demand_pricing: Next Generation Corvette (NGC): price negotiations complete, ~INR 33,000 crore, GRSE is L1; contract slipped from 31 March 2026 target, now expected in June quarter; management says no red flags. Electronics is 55-60% of equipment cost, with BEL as a major sister-PSU supplier.

Live tenders: Multipurpose Vessels (2 ships, ~INR 1,500 crore, bid submitted), OPV for Coast Guard (5 ships, ~INR 2,000 crore) and 22 Interceptor Boats (~INR 1,000 crore), bids due around end May or early June 2026.

Upcoming RFPs in ~3 months: 120 Fast Interceptor Craft (~INR 3,500 crore, split 80/40), 31 Follow-On Water Jet FACs (~INR 3,500 crore) and seven P-17 Bravo (~INR 70,000 crore, split 4/3). MCV (12 ships, ~INR 32,000 crore, 8/4) and LPD (4 ships, ~INR 35,000 crore, 2/2) RFPs expected by end FY27.

Commercial tenders from Ministry of Shipping: four Platform Support Vessels (INR 1,200-1,500 crore), four MR tankers, six VLGCs and six Aframax vessels. European ship owners are in dialogue, citing pricing and quality versus China and Korea.
Cost escalation: existing contracts are fixed price, and vendor orders were placed earlier, so management reports no material impact; new bids will factor in commodity risk.

qa_highlights.question: Statutory defence committee report shows contracts expected over two years for warships and survey vessels fell to ~INR 18,900 crore from ~INR 42,000 crore. What does this mean for government focus?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said the INR 18,900 crore figure reflects annual fund outflow, not intent. He cited AoNs, RFPs and approved Navy and Coast Guard roadmaps as evidence of continued focus.

qa_highlights.question: Relevance of conventional platforms versus autonomous vessels, and GRSE's strategy in autonomy.
qa_highlights.answer: Conventional platforms remain relevant for armament and endurance. GRSE has developed subsurface and surface autonomous vessels, supplied one to a DRDO organisation, and targets the XL AUV under Make projects in 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the revenue in the 31 March provisional figure materially different from the final reported number?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it had kept a conservative provisional figure because three ships were delivered on the last day. After formalising deliveries and revenue with the Navy, final revenue came to about INR 7,200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NGC delayed, and when will it be signed? Will there be one or two winners on smaller projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Price negotiations are complete. Contract signing was expected by 31 March but is now expected in the June quarter, with no red flags. Smaller projects are mostly single-yard awards, with 120 FAC and P-17 Bravo split between two yards.

qa_highlights.question: When will NGC revenue start and how will revenue and EBITDA margins look for FY27-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: NGC revenue recognition starts in H2 FY28, with the major chunk from FY29. Margins are expected to be similar in FY27 and the company will try to maintain them in FY28-FY29. Management did not confirm no FY28 revenue dip.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY25 and FY26 margins inflated by provision write-backs, and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Analyst cited 8.3% EBITDA margin in FY25 and 11.6% in FY26. Management said the current year margins will be similar but would not give a specific percentage, saying it is only Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NGC vendor ecosystem and electronics content?
qa_highlights.answer: Equipment and systems are ~65% of project cost; electronics is 55-60% of that and machinery and systems 40-45%. First downstream orders expected within three months of contract signing, majority within three to six months. BEL expected to be a key partner.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company take large European commercial orders and target higher margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commercial export projects will be selected for good margins. Warship projects, at ~INR 675 crore per ASW ship, still carry the best money and margins. Hybrid large vessels are being targeted.

qa_highlights.question: How are commodity cost increases handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing contracts are fixed price and vendor contracts are fixed price too, so no material impact was reported. Time delays on steel and industrial gas were marginal. New bids will factor in uncertainty.

risks_watch: NGC contract signing has already slipped from 31 March to June quarter; any further delay would push the revenue ramp and reduce FY28 visibility.
Order book of INR 15,324 crore is down sharply; FY28 revenue is not guaranteed without new order wins, and no revenue recognition from NGC is planned until H2 FY28.

542011|2026-06.headline: GRSE Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 39% YoY to ₹1,815 crore and PAT 44% to ₹173 crore; order book ₹13,596 crore.
542011|2026-06.overview: Management reported total income of ₹1,914 crore (+38% YoY), revenue from operations of ₹1,815 crore (+39%), and PAT of ₹173 crore (+44%) with EPS of ₹15.09 versus ₹10.49. The company said this was its 17th consecutive quarter of upward trend in financials. Order book stands at ₹13,596 crore across 11 projects and 44 marine platforms, and the Next Generation Corvette (NGC) contract is still awaited with management guiding signing within the quarter. Capacity expansion (brownfield and greenfield, roughly ₹4,200 crore combined capex) was the main strategic update, alongside Navratna status granted on 19 June 2026.

financial_highlights.change: First time below ₹15,000 crore in 10 years, per management
Attributed to absence of ship commissioning costs incurred in Q4 FY26
Management called it sinusoidal, tied to delivery phase

guidance_outlook: NGC contract expected to be signed in Q2 FY27; revenue recognition to start in FY28, with eighth ship completion around 2034-35.
Concurrent construction capacity to rise from 28 to 32 platforms by end of calendar 2026; to 43 platforms after Raichak (West Bengal) and western-seaboard facilities.
Management said current quarter's performance can be replicated in coming quarters, citing P-17 Alpha (~₹4,500 crore left) and ASW craft (~₹1,816 crore left) as major execution drivers.
Expects employee cost increase of 15-20% from next pay commission, consistent with past pay commissions.
Bonus or stock split: awaiting directions from administrative ministry and DIPAM.
capex_capacity: P-17 Alpha large ship ~85% complete; delivery targeted by November 2026 (calendar year). First two P-17 Alpha ships delivered ahead of schedule.
Four of eight anti-submarine shallow water craft delivered; remaining four to be delivered in FY27 (fifth ~91%, sixth ~88%, seventh and eighth ~65-70%).
NGOPV: first ship launched, second launched ~11 August 2026; third and fourth launches in Q3 and Q4 FY27; first delivery Q2 FY28, last Q2 FY29.

Expansion capex: ~₹200 crore for two Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port facilities (18-month revitalization, already started); ~₹2,200 crore for Raichak greenfield shipyard in West Bengal (DPR in final stages, 3-5 years to operationalise, infra work from 2027); ~₹2,000 crore for a Gujarat-side total ship solution facility (shipbuilding, green recycling, repair) on PPP model, DPR complete, environmental clearance obtained, ~3 years to operationalise.
demand_pricing: Live defence RFPs ~₹80,000 crore (Navy and Coast Guard): 120 fast interceptor craft ~₹3,500 crore (bid due next month); 31 follow-on water jet FAC ~₹3,500 crore; 22 interceptor boats ~₹1,200-1,300 crore (bids submitted); six NGOPVs for Coast Guard ~₹2,500 crore; P-17 Bravo (DAC AON ₹70,000 crore).
RFPs expected in calendar 2026: mine sounder measure vessel (~₹36,000 crore AON, split between two yards, 8 and 4) and four LPDs (~₹35,000 crore).

Non-defence tenders out via PSU demand aggregation: four MR tankers; six VLGCs and six Aframax vessels (GRSE partnering with a foreign yard and a sister yard); container ship tender expected (partnering with an Indian yard due to lack of dock capacity).
Letters of intent received for four platform support vessels (ONGC) and one green electric tug (SMP Port, Kolkata); GRSE L1 in NGC (~₹ high value, contract awaited).
Water metro opportunity: ₹200-300 crore per metro; ~₹1,500 crore and 30-40 platforms if five states proceed.
Next Generation Destroyer not expected at RFP stage before FY29 per management (no DAC approval yet).
Export strategy: no export orders currently pursued given domestic non-defence demand (~200+ platforms); will consider attractive European orders.
Indigenisation: management says ~80-85% overall by value; weapons ~60%, survival ~70%, float (hull) 100% but ~10% of cost, propulsion engines not yet indigenous; large survey vessel >80%.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Next Generation Corvette contract been delayed, and when would revenue recognition start if signed today?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the contract slipped from FY26-end/Q1 and is now expected to be signed this quarter, with no red flags seen. Revenue recognition would begin in FY28 after a pre-production design and equipment-ordering phase; the eight-ship project completes around 2034-35.

qa_highlights.question: Does GRSE have capability for unmanned and autonomous naval vessels, and does the expansion plan address it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has capability, citing an unmanned surface vessel prototype, a project for NSTL (DRDO) and an autonomous underwater platform prototype tested about a year ago. It is taking part in Navy-steered autonomy projects and was shortlisted for another underwater unmanned platform.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex quantum for greenfield and brownfield expansion, and what capability will it add?
qa_highlights.answer: Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port revitalisation is about ₹200 crore over 18 months. Raichak greenfield yard in West Bengal is about ₹2,200 crore with 3-5 years to operationalise; the Gujarat-side total ship solution facility is about ₹2,000 crore with about 3 years to operationalise. Capacity goes from 32 to 43 platforms, including larger Aframax/VLGC-type vessels.

qa_highlights.question: How will GRSE participate in large commercial tenders (MR tankers, VLGC, Aframax, container ships) given capacity limits?
qa_highlights.answer: MR tankers and VLGCs are being bid with a sister yard and, for VLGC, a foreign yard with proven capability. Container ships are being pursued through a partnership with an Indian yard that has the dock and berth infrastructure, as GRSE lacks physical capacity for them.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 execution momentum be sustained, or will growth slow from the ~35-40% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current quarter's performance can be replicated, pointing to about ₹4,500 crore left on P-17 Alpha and about ₹1,816 crore on anti-submarine craft. It noted FY26 delivered eight ships and that the next quarter should see deliveries and higher contract workforce costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the indigenisation level and where is GRSE still import-dependent?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall indigenisation is about 80-85% by value. Hull/float is 100% but about 10% of cost, weapons about 60%, survival about 70%, and diesel alternators 100%; propulsion engines are not yet indigenous. Bailey Bridge is 100%, deck machinery about 90%, and the diesel engine co-production targets 55-60%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp fall in other expenses and employee costs QoQ, and what is the pay commission impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses fell because Q4 FY26 included commissioning costs for three ships that did not recur. Contract workforce cost is sinusoidal with delivery timing and will rise when a couple of ships deliver. Management expects the next pay commission to add 15-20% to employee costs, in line with past commissions.

Order book fell to ₹13,596 crore; conversion of the ~₹80,000 crore of live RFPs (120 fast interceptor craft, 31 water jet FACs, P-17 Bravo) and the ~₹70,000 crore expected RFPs (mine sounder vessels, LPDs) is key.
