segments.commentary: About 60-65 RMs across 12 locations at closing, managing close to Rs 4,000 crore for 650-plus clients at about 90 bps yield. Management says revenue lags because the broker code change affects revenue only after 12 months.

segments.name: ET Money
segments.commentary: Undergoing strategic and business-model transformation; management expects breakeven in the near term without a specific timeline.

segments.name: Lending
segments.commentary: Largely Lombard / loan against shares, collateralised at 2x. Management reports no NPA and no loss since 2016; margin funding book under Rs 50-60 crore.

segments.name: Alternates carry
segments.commentary: Carryable AUM about Rs 30,000-35,000 crore; carry accrual 5-7 bps in a bad year and 12-15 bps in a good year. Modelling assumption of about 10 bps carry, so about 95-100 bps total Alternates yield.

guidance_outlook: Wealth: target net flows of 12-15% of opening AUM annually; AUM growth of 20-25%; RM count growth of 25-30% a year over the next 3-4 years; Wealth profit growth 15-25%. Management said it may add 25-35 RMs this year.
Cost-to-income: long-term target of 46-48% on the overall business ex-new businesses, and 45-47% over 2-3 years; UHNI/AM core stays at 44-45%.

Transaction and broking revenue: run-rate now seen at Rs 170-180 crore per quarter (earlier Rs 125-130 crore); aspiration north of Rs 200 crore. Management said the Rs 175-200 crore range is not cast in stone and later suggested Rs 160-180 crore.
Equity and equity-related income (ex-banking) expected to nearly double over 3-4 years; equity research revenue on Wealth side of Rs 85-90 crore a year could double or triple in 3-5 years.
Banking: 12 senior investment professionals to hire, about 4 in place; management expects to be more competitive over the next 3-4 months.
Tangible ROE expected to improve as Lending and Alternates capital turns into earnings.
Management expects 2-4% attrition a year and aims to double market share over 3-5 years.
capex_capacity: Senior relationship managers: about 180-190 currently; target 330-340 (team leaders from about 70-75 to 120-130; partners from 110-120 to about 240).
UHNI RM count about 63-64 at closing (about 35-40 on an average basis during FY26), with plans to go to 25-35 extra RMs in FY27.
Wealth market share estimated at 8-10%, with about 4,500 families above Rs 10 crore; target 8,000-10,000 families.
Employee base about 1,800.

demand_pricing: Organic ARR net flows FY26 Rs 35,199 crore, of which Q4 net flows were about Rs 9,000-10,000 crore: advisory about Rs 4,500-5,000 crore, AM about Rs 2,000-2,500 crore, distribution and lending about Rs 2,000-2,500 crore.

Q4 AM gross flows about Rs 5,200 crore (FY26 about Rs 19,000 crore). Net flows reduced by a large credit fund maturity (Rs 1,500-1,700 crore), a real estate fund maturity (about Rs 850 crore) and a 2021-vintage PE fund distribution.

Discretionary PMS flows were softer than desired; the strategy is being pivoted and relaunched around early June 2026. Q4 DPMS retention was inflated by profit share on a small base. Negative distribution net flows of about Rs 212 crore were attributed mainly to corporate treasuries.
Management described 90% of cash segment share in broking, and over 500 mid- and small-cap companies under coverage.

Client base shift: family offices of about 400-500 clients (versus 40-50 five years ago); professionals now 15-20% of clients (from 5-10%); average ticket size rising due to a portfolio-based approach.

UBS collaboration: cross-referrals in NRI, resident and global mandates showing early traction. Regulatory approvals in GIFT City and on the UBS platform slowed progress; expected over the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 transaction revenue (UHNI TBR) so strong, and will the Rs 125-130 crore per quarter benchmark be revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TBR now looks closer to Rs 175-180 crore per quarter, helped by 360 ONE Capital and diversified asset-class mix (fixed income, REITs/InvITs, high-yield fixed income), and is more comfortable with Rs 170-180 crore than the earlier Rs 130-140 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 2 to 3 year yield (ex-carry) decline, and what is the carry model?
qa_highlights.answer: Yield ex-carry seen as broadly stable. Carry is accrued at about 10-14 bps a year on carryable AUM of about Rs 30,000-35,000 crore; modelling assumption is 10 bps carry, so about 95-100 bps Alternates yield.

qa_highlights.question: Is the guided 20-25% AUM growth and RM addition consistent with 15-25% profit growth, given cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost-to-income stays at 44-46% in the core UHNI and AM business, and operating leverage is high; it is willing to front-load RM hiring of 25-35 in FY27. Yield pressure and RM compensation are acknowledged but manageable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 1 April 2026 mutual fund yield cut hit B&K transaction revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is about 2-3% on a base of about Rs 200-225 crore a quarter, which is not material, and is offset by synergies.

qa_highlights.question: Industry consolidation, competition, and attrition in UHNI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes the industry needs 3-4 or more large players but remains fairly consolidated for the next 3-4 years. It expects 2-4% attrition a year and sees 12-15% flows as doable.

qa_highlights.question: Quality of new clients, carry exits, and gross flows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said family office clients are growing and portfolio-based onboarding raises ticket sizes. Sanjay Wadhwa gave AM gross flows of about Rs 5,200 crore in Q4 and Rs 19,000 crore in FY26. Management said the fund-level carry list would be compiled later in a data book.

risks_watch: Execution risk as headcount scales: management calls execution the biggest risk, with about 1,800 employees and plans to add 25-35 UHNI RMs in FY27 while senior RM count moves from about 180-190 toward 330-340.

RM war for talent and compensation: management says it will hire between the 90th and 110th compensation percentile, and says cost-to-income could drift up during hiring; FY26 cost-to-income was 49.9%.
Wealth flow delivery: the 12-15% of opening AUM net flow target is described as a tall order, and management flagged that it gets harder as size increases.
Discretionary PMS outflows and pricing: DPMS flows are soft, the strategy is being pivoted with relaunch around early June 2026, and Q4 DPMS retention was inflated by profit share on a small base.

Alternates and carry: AM Q4 net flows were hit by a credit fund maturity (Rs 1,500-1,700 crore), a real estate fund maturity (about Rs 850 crore) and a 2021-vintage PE distribution; carry accrual depends on hurdle performance and market variation.

B&K/360 ONE Capital: the MF yield cut from 1 April 2026 (about 2-3% impact on Rs 200-225 crore quarterly base), TBR sustainability, and banking hiring (12 professionals, about 4 in place) with IB contribution expected in 12-18 months.
UBS collaboration and GIFT City regulatory approvals slowed progress; management expects movement over the next quarter.

We're investing heavily into middle management leadership depth.

542772|2026-06.headline: 360 ONE Q1 FY27: total revenue up 20% to Rs 870 crore, PAT up 14.8% to Rs 330 crore, cost-to-income 51.3%.

542830|2026-06.headline: IRCTC Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.1% to INR1,370 crore, but EBITDA fell 2.77% to INR386 crore as catering margins and internet ticketing spinoffs weakened.

Margins were pressured by a one-time HR/gratuity charge of about INR20 crore, proof-of-concept costs on six trains, a West Asia-driven resin cost spike in Rail Neer, and lower non-convenience fee income in internet ticketing. Management said the catering and HR effects are non-recurring and that the proof-of-concept trains will wind down by November.

Management attributed the drop to about INR4 crore proof-of-concept cost on six trains and about INR10 crore HR/gratuity charge; catering onboard sales from prepaid trains rose to INR413 crore from INR301 crore.

segments.name: Rail Neer
segments.commentary: Revenue INR109 crore (+2.83%); margin about 10% vs 14-15% prior, driven by resin/petroleum cost rise (material cost INR55 crore to INR61 crore) linked to West Asia crisis. Management said profit fell only about INR4 crore overall.

segments.name: Tourism
segments.commentary: Revenue INR168 crore (+13.5%); EBITDA margin improved to 11.31% from 8.78% on better product mix and cost realisation, despite geopolitical disruption. Non-fare revenue from Tejas naming/wrap rights noted as a new lever.

qa_highlights.question: Vande Bharat catering model and steady-state margin given the GST treatment on prepaid trains?
qa_highlights.answer: IRCTC's model is largely licensing. Vande Bharat catering is outsourced via limited tenders to empanelled licensees, while IRCTC runs catering in 81 Vande Bharat trains. On a Vande Bharat basis, the licence fee plus GST earns about INR105 per unit against INR222 paid to licensees, with about INR11 of non-claimable GST. Management said the 10-12% traditional catering margin range is the target.

qa_highlights.question: Visibility on new train additions and their ramp-up?

Exports fell to zero and OEM sales degrew 14%, while domestic MDF volumes grew 12% YoY and retail MDF grew about 20%. rows.why: 862 branches and 832 ATMs, with transaction banking systems (Vayana, Aurion Pro CMS, trade) going live in 3-4 months and the Dubai representative office approved but delayed; these are systems and offices, not sizeable physical capacity.

rows.why: Advances grew 27% YoY and management targets around 25% loan growth in FY27, but this depends on deposit and CASA build-up (CASA about 20%, bulk deposits about 50% of term deposits) and BLG grew only 2-3% in FY26.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

542867|2026-06.headline: CSB Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 27% YoY to Rs.150 Crores, with NIM at 3.66% and ROA at 1.09%, but other income fell 7%.
542867|2026-06.overview: CSB Bank reported Q1 FY27 net profit of Rs.150 Crores (+27% YoY) and operating profit of Rs.251 Crores (+14% YoY), with NII up 26% to Rs.479 Crores. Deposits grew 26% and advances 24% YoY, both ahead of industry, and CD ratio moved to just under 90%. Other income fell 7% YoY on lower treasury gains (Rs.12 Crores vs Rs.53 Crores) and weaker insurance and gold-linked processing fees. Management called Q1 the worst-case margin quarter and reiterated FY27 NIM of around 3.75% and ROA of 1.3%-1.5%.

financial_highlights.value: Rs.12 Crores treasury profit plus Rs.3 Crores trading profit (total other income down 7%)
Growth 24% YoY vs industry 18.6%; yield on advances 10.65%

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: About 54% of the loan book; yield 11.85% vs 12% QoQ. Management expects the gold mix to stay near 50% in FY27 and fall toward 30% by FY2030. Gold disbursements fell QoQ on regulatory implementation and reduced top-ups; the book was about Rs.21,000 Crores last quarter.

segments.name: Wholesale (WSB)
segments.commentary: About 26% of the book; growing 35%-40% per management. Target is about 32% of the book by FY2030. FIPS book fell to about one-third of WSB from about 70%.

segments.name: SME / BLG
segments.commentary: Yield fell to 9.25% from 9.81% QoQ. Slippages in the quarter; management is deliberately cautious and has raised credit appraisal bars for FY27.

segments.name: Retail (LAS / repledger)
segments.commentary: Repledger LAS book fell from over Rs.2,100 Crores to about Rs.60 Crores and will run off by next quarter, per RBI discontinuation from 1 April 2026. Unsecured retail is only about 2% of the book; focus deferred to FY2028.

segments.name: Treasury and fee income
segments.commentary: Treasury profit was Rs.12 Crores vs Rs.53 Crores a year ago, and insurance fees fell after tighter mis-selling controls. Management targets full-year fee income at 16%-17% of total income, with Q1 other income about 15% of income.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 NIM guidance of around 3.75%; management said it sees no risk to this guidance.
Full-year FY27 ROA guidance of 1.3%-1.5%; management said it would not go below 1.3% this year and internal target is 1.5%.
ROE: started FY27 near 12%; aims to end FY27 above the FY26 exit of 14.14% and try to touch 15%.
Wholesale to grow 35%-40% and gold 30%-35% in FY27; gold mix expected near 50% this year.
CASA to grow in line with deposits from FY2028; CASA to outgrow term deposits from FY2029. FY27 CASA ratio expected to hold at about 19.4% only if deposits grow about 25%.
Fee income guidance of 16%-17% of total income for the full year, with insurance and gold disbursements expected to pick up from Q2.
Unsecured retail push deferred to FY2028; ECLGS disbursement so far about Rs.60 Crores.
capex_capacity: Network of 868 branches and 835 ATMs as on 30 June 2026.
Technology transformation complete: 50+ surrounding systems integrated with CBS, plus transaction banking and ServiceNow; some trade, supply chain and CMS systems to go live in the next 3-4 months.
New retail liability acquisition channel rolling out; retail deposit products launched last year, with sales team being built.
Technology was delayed by about two and a half years, per management, due to a decision delay rather than execution.
demand_pricing: Deposit growth 26% YoY vs industry 13.4%; bulk deposits about 52% of term deposits and about 40% of total deposits; retail about 48% of deposits.
Cost of funds around 6.5%; higher cost driven by bulk deposits, FCY borrowings and CDs, which management expects to ease as liquidity improves.
Q1 NIM hit by flow-through of end-March deposit costs, and by slippages and reduced recoveries; management says Q1 NIM is the worst case for the year.
Gold LTV around 75% vs peers below 65%, driven by agri gold (LTV up to 85%); non-agri LTV about 50%-55%. Board plans to gradually cut agri gold.
Deposit rates showing marginal softening; SME yields expected to improve next quarter as slippages are upgraded in Q2/Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Gold share at 54%, bulk deposits at 52% of term deposits; is the bulk mix the main NIM drag and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the bulk mix (about 52% of term deposits) raises cost of funds (about 6.5%). Retail franchise build starts with CASA from FY2028; management expects no quick reduction in bulk share in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can a wholesale book funded by wholesale money hold margins, and how volatile are slippages?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIM and ROA guidance holds for the year; wholesale is being built as a franchise with ROA and RAROC targets. Q1 slippage about Rs.98 Crores (Q4 about Rs.60 Crores), mainly in BLG/SME, which management expects to be largely upgraded in Q2/Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall 7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury profit was Rs.12 Crores vs Rs.53 Crores a year ago, insurance fees were cut after mis-selling controls, and gold/retail processing fees fell with lower disbursements. Management expects recovery from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 ROA guidance being revised from around 1.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it will not go below 1.3% for FY27, with an internal 1.5% target; the 1.3% comment answered a different question on the year-end run-rate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of IDBI Bank stake sale by promoter Fairfax?
qa_highlights.answer: CSB has had no discussions on this. Fairfax told management to continue business as usual; the bank is run by its own management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gold disbursements fall sharply QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited regulatory implementation (end-use monitoring), fewer top-ups as gold prices stopped rising, and the repledger LAS run-off. Disbursements are expected to pick up as gold prices rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECLGS disbursement and what is the growth guidance for corporate and gold?
qa_highlights.answer: ECLGS disbursements about Rs.60 Crores so far. Management guided wholesale at 35%-40% growth and gold at 30%-35% for FY27.

risks_watch: Asset quality volatility: slippages of about Rs.98 Crores in Q1 vs Rs.60 Crores in Q4, concentrated in BLG/SME; upgrade assumption for Q2/Q3 is key.
Margin pressure from bulk and CD funding (cost of funds about 6.5%); the NIM path depends on deposit repricing and CD rates easing.
Other income recovery depends on treasury gains (AFS book) and insurance and gold fee pick-up from Q2.
Gold regulation: end-use monitoring and the gold mix glide path from 54% toward 30% by FY2030.
Execution of the CASA/retail franchise, with CASA ratio expected to hold at 19.41% only if deposits grow about 25%.
Management said Q1 ROA of 1.09% is below the FY27 guidance of 1.3%-1.5%, so the run-rate must improve materially in later quarters.
542867|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the year-on-year numbers and guidance, but defensive on the quarter-on-quarter dip in NIM, ROA and other income, which it attributes to transient factors. Management was also candid about the delayed technology decision and avoided commenting on the IDBI Bank stake sale beyond saying it was not involved.
key_quotes: We will only improve from here.
In 2027 itself we will touch 1.3%.
I do not see liquidity as a risk for us in the near term.

Except for the technology which got delayed by around two-and-a-half years which was a decision point and not an execution point - almost everything else we achieved the way we had given guidance to the markets.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 NIM of 3.66% is called the worst-case quarter, with FY27 NIM guided at around 3.75%, implying recovery from the Q1 trough as end-March deposit costs flow through and SME slippages are upgraded in Q2/Q3; cost of funds is still high at about 6.5%, so the path is not guaranteed.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new branches or plants quantified; network held at 868 branches and 835 ATMs as of 30 June 2026, with focus on technology go-lives (trade, supply chain, CMS in next 3-4 months) rather than productive capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Deposits up 26% YoY vs industry 13.4% and advances up 24% vs industry 18.6%; FY27 guidance of wholesale growth 35-40% and gold 30-35%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the bank is in a technology completion phase rather than a capacity build, and CD ratio is just under 90% with no capex plan stated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 NIM at about 3.75% and ROA at 1.3-1.5%, and Q1 ROA of 1.09% is well below the 1.3% floor, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 ROA of 1.09% is below the 1.3% FY27 floor and Q1 slippages rose to about Rs.98 Crores from Rs.60 Crores in Q4, so the run-rate must improve materially; if upgrades slip, the ROA floor is at risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Trade, supply chain and CMS systems go live in the next 3-4 months, and a new retail liability acquisition channel is rolling out with retail deposit products launched last year; unsecured retail push is deferred to FY2028.

rows.label: SME/BLG slippage upgrades in Q2/Q3
rows.why: Q1 slippages of about Rs.98 Crores (Q4 about Rs.60 Crores) are expected to be largely upgraded in Q2/Q3, and SME yield fell to 9.25% from 9.81% QoQ, so NIM and asset quality recovery depends on this.

rows.label: Fee income recovery to 16-17% of total income
rows.why: Q1 other income was about 15% of income and treasury profit fell to Rs.12 Crores from Rs.53 Crores YoY; management expects insurance and gold fees to pick up from Q2.

rows.label: Repledger LAS run-off complete
rows.why: Repledger LAS book fell from over Rs.2,100 Crores to about Rs.60 Crores and will run off by next quarter under RBI discontinuation from 1 April 2026.

tone.note: Management was confident on YoY growth and FY27 NIM/ROA guidance and called Q1 the worst-case margin quarter, but defensive on the QoQ dip in NIM, ROA and other income; analysts pushed on ROA below the 1.3% floor, slippages, and the bulk-deposit cost drag.

542867|2026-09.headline: CSB Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 22% QoQ to Rs.183 Cr, with NIM up to 3.81% and ROA to 1.29%.
542867|2026-09.overview: CSB Bank reported Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs.183 Cr, up 22% QoQ and 14% YoY, with net interest income of Rs.510 Cr (up 7% QoQ, 20% YoY). NIM widened to 3.81% from 3.66% in Q1, driven by a higher yield on advances (10.92%) and stable cost of funds. Fee income rebounded 20% QoQ, though overall fee income was down about 22% YoY due to market-linked non-core lines. Asset quality improved on GNPA (1.58%) and NNPA (0.33%), with credit cost at 24 bps, though elevated write-offs of fully provided card and unsecured book were flagged. Management said it is entering a "scale phase" with retail liability build-out, SME growth restarting, and guidance of ROA 1.5% to 1.8% next year.

financial_highlights.change: +20% QoQ; ex-treasury +27% QoQ; fee income -22% YoY
vs 3.66% in Q1 FY27 and 3.81% in Q2 FY26
Yield on advances 10.92% vs 10.65% in Q1
PCR 87.65% (79.19% without PWO); credit cost 24 bps

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book grew 36% YoY, but tonnage fell about 6% YoY and disbursements slowed; management targets gold at about 50% of loan mix by year-end (53% last year, 54% last quarter), with a 32% glide path by 2030. Gold yields rose about 50 bps QoQ.

segments.name: Corporate / wholesale
segments.commentary: Corporate segment grew 44% YoY; wholesale split roughly equally across corporate banking, mid-market and FIs, with corporate and mid-market growing faster.

segments.name: SME
segments.commentary: SME growth remained flattish after exits and customer losses on pricing; management expects SME growth to resume from this quarter after portfolio issues were corrected.

segments.name: Retail (ex-gold)
segments.commentary: Retail growth was muted; the bank degrew loan against security (repledge gold loans, now almost zero) and is keeping unsecured cards, agri and MFI cautious, with unsecured retail to restart around FY2028.

segments.name: Fee income
segments.commentary: Core fee grew about 27% YoY and is just short of 15% of total income; overall fee is just short of 17% of total income (vs 23% last year, which included one-offs). Non-core lines (PSLC, treasury) declined.

guidance_outlook: ROA this year expected between 1.30% and 1.5%; next year (FY28) targeted at 1.5% to 1.8%, closer to 1.5% initially.
NIM guided at around 3.75% to 3.8% this year; around 3.75% next year.
Cost of funds to be brought down from 6.55% to about 6% next financial year.
Fee to total income assumed at 17% to 18%; IRDAI corporate agency draft may cut this by 0.5% to 1%.
Balance sheet growth guided at 30% to 50% faster than the system; system growth was faster this quarter due to FCNR inflows.
CASA to grow faster than term deposits from FY2028, after being slower this year.
Gold loans to fall to about 50% of mix by year-end; SBS 2030 targets continue.
capex_capacity: Network of 872 branches and 844 ATMs as at September 2026.
Core system upgrade and DC-DR switch completed; OFSAA implementation under way.
Technology investments span transaction banking (supply chain, CMS, trade), OBDX, corporate net banking and corporate LOS.
Management plans to launch 3-4 retail liability products every quarter, with current account acquisition the current focus.
Opex up about 11% QoQ and about 3% YoY; other opex up 18% QoQ mainly on technology, plus distribution and infrastructure; staff cost up about 17% YoY.
demand_pricing: Gold disbursements fell as rebooking is no longer shown as new disbursement and gold prices dipped; management says the regulator's LTV cut from 90% to 75% was managed.
Gold loan LTV about 75% vs 60-65% at peers, attributed to a larger agri portfolio where higher LTV is allowed; about 28% of gold book is above Rs.20 lakh ticket size.
Gold yields raised by about 50 bps QoQ, leveraging distribution and competitor pricing.
Lost some SME customers on pricing; exited a list of customers after quality review.
Deposit mix about 48% retail and 52% wholesale; FCY, CDs and borrowings remain significant funding sources.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other opex rise 18% QoQ and is it linked to higher other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said total opex rose about 11% QoQ and 3% YoY; the rise was mainly technology, plus distribution expansion and infrastructure spends. Staff cost was up about 17% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp rise in yield on advances and gold yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Better asset quality, careful yield management in wholesale and SME, and a gold yield increase of about 50 bps QoQ, helped by distribution reach and competitor pricing. Cost of funds was flat QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why were write-offs high while credit cost was low?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wrote off a fully provided vintage of credit card and unsecured loans with low recovery prospects and no PSL benefit; it said this had no impact on credit cost, which was 24 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the IRDAI corporate agency consultation paper on fees?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates a 0.5% to 1% drag on fee-to-income, so guidance may drop from 18% to 17% short term, with the bank aiming to recover through core fee lines.

qa_highlights.question: What is the balance sheet growth outlook and retail deposit traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated growth 30% to 50% faster than system; retail current account acquisition has started, and liability franchise takes two to three years to build. Asset growth is not the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Is Fairfax or IDBI relevant to CSB, and is there a Fairfax deposit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Fairfax has no deposits with the bank and the board has not discussed the Fairfax/IDBI matter; the transaction is still incomplete.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROA and NIM outlooks for this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA of 1.30-1.5% this year, 1.5-1.8% next year; NIM around 3.75-3.8%, with cost of funds targeted at about 6% next year to offset mix shift.

risks_watch: Gold loan tonnage down about 6% YoY and gold disbursements slowing; gold book mix must fall to about 50%.
Regulatory fee risk from IRDAI corporate agency draft; fee-to-income could fall 0.5-1%.
Asset quality trend needs two to three more quarters to confirm; management points to a declining non-gold SMA book.
Cost of funds at 6.55% and reliance on FCY borrowings, CDs and bulk deposits; CASA ratio slipped to 18.96%.
Opex growth (other opex +18% QoQ) and cost-to-income at 64.8% against the fee and NIM outlook.
Interpretation risk on write-offs: elevated write-offs of fully provided book alongside PCR rising to 87.65%.
542867|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on earnings momentum, ROA and the scale phase, but guarded on the timing of retail growth, CASA recovery and the fee impact from the IRDAI draft. Management declined to elaborate on the other income breakup and deflected the Fairfax/IDBI question as not yet relevant.
key_quotes: Overall, we had a fairly good quarter.

We will start seeing the growth on the SME side from this quarter onwards because most of the portfolio-related issues we faced in SME book for the last one-and-a-half years have been by and large corrected now.
I would say that we would aim to bring down the cost of funds to somewhere around 6% next financial year, which will give us a 50-basis points lift.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM at 3.81% in Q2 FY27 vs 3.66% in Q1, guided at ~3.75-3.8% this year and ~3.75% next year, with cost of funds targeted down from 6.55% to ~6% in FY28 but gold yields up ~50 bps QoQ offsetting mix shift; NIM is guided to hold rather than expand further.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Network stands at 872 branches and 844 ATMs as at Sep 2026 with no new branch additions guided; growth is coming from balance sheet and liability products rather than new physical capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Gross advances up 22% YoY and deposits up 18% YoY, with balance sheet guided at 30-50% faster than system; but gold tonnage is down ~6% YoY and SME growth is flattish, so volume growth is concentrated in corporate (+44% YoY) and gold value rather than broad-based.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation metric is disclosed and tech spend is ongoing (core upgrade done, OFSAA under way), but no new capex or branch plan has been announced; a capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 ROA guidance was narrowed to 1.30-1.50%, i.e. effectively a cut from prior implied range, and fee-to-income may fall 0.5-1% from IRDAI draft, so upward revisions look unlikely near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 ROA is guided 1.30-1.50% after a cut, fee-to-income could drop from 18% to 17% under the IRDAI corporate agency draft (0.5-1% drag), and cost-to-income is 64.8% with other opex up 18% QoQ.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans to launch 3-4 retail liability products every quarter, with current account acquisition already started, though unsecured retail (cards, agri, MFI) is only set to restart around FY2028.

rows.label: CASA growth turns faster than term deposits from FY28
rows.why: CASA ratio slipped to 18.96% and CASA grows slower than TDs this year, with management saying FY27 is the last year of that gap and cost of funds targeted at ~6% from 6.55%.

rows.label: SME growth restarts after portfolio clean-up
rows.why: SME growth was flattish after exits and pricing-driven customer losses; management expects it to resume from this quarter, but the asset quality trend needs two to three more quarters to confirm.

rows.label: IRDAI corporate agency draft fee impact
rows.why: Management estimates a 0.5% to 1% drag on fee-to-income, which would move guidance from 18% to about 17%.

tone.note: Management was confident on NIM, ROA trajectory and the scale phase, but cautious on gold tonnage, retail growth timing, CASA recovery and the IRDAI fee draft; analysts pushed on write-offs, other opex and the Fairfax/IDBI matter, which management deflected.

542904|2026-03.headline: Ujjivan SFB Q4FY26: Q4 PAT annualised to ROA 2.1%, but FY27 guidance of ~1.6% ROA, ~25% advances growth and 1.4-1.5% credit cost.
542904|2026-03.overview: Q4FY26 showed strong operating momentum: NII rose 26.4% YoY to INR1,092 crores, NIM improved to 8.5%, disbursements hit a record INR9,811 crores, and gross loan book reached INR40,655 crores (+26.6% YoY). Exit-quarter PAT was INR282 crores (ROA 2.1%, ROE 17.2%) versus FY26 PAT of INR693 crores (ROA 1.4%, ROE 10.9%). The RBI returned the bank's application for voluntary transition to a universal bank; management will reapply later with a more diversified portfolio. Management guided to a higher secured mix (about 56% by March 2027), a board-approved equity raise of up to INR2,000 crores in H2FY27, and FY27 ROA of around 1.6%, below the Q4 exit rate.

segments.name: Secured portfolio
segments.commentary: Reached INR20,079 crores (+43.5% YoY, +12.6% QoQ), now 49.4% of gross book. Housing +43.4% YoY and MSME +57.9% YoY; the housing vertical crossed INR10,000 crores.

segments.name: Micro banking
segments.commentary: Portfolio INR20,709 crores (+6.9%); Q4 disbursements a record INR5,245 crores (+11.9% QoQ). FY26 new customer additions 5.4 lakh. Management guides FY27 growth below 10%, a higher single digit.

segments.name: Newer lines (gold, vehicle, agri)
segments.commentary: Grew 292%, 102% and 127% YoY respectively; together about 6% of loan mix versus 3% in FY25. Gold yield is above 14%; micro mortgage yield is 19.7%.

segments.name: Liabilities
segments.commentary: Retail TD plus CASA INR31,955 crores (70% of deposits). CD ratio 89%, LCR 142%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 advances growth around 25%: secured about 40% and unsecured about 10%, per the Chief Credit Officer.
FY27 credit cost moderates to 1.4-1.5% of average GLB (exit quarter DuPont credit cost about 1.1%, per the call).
FY27 ROA around 1.6%, base case, with upside possible; NIM guided at around 8.5%, in line with the Q4 exit level.
Opex to ATA 20-30bps above FY26 in FY27 due to investment, then expected to decline; cost to income to stay at FY26 levels.
Secured share about 56% by March 2027. CASA ratio about 29-30% (Head of Retail Liabilities said around 30%).

Equity raise up to INR2,000 crores, planned for H2FY27. About 20% branch addition in FY27 (about 140 branches on 776 base). Cost of deposits to benefit about 25-30bps from SA rate cuts; no TD repricing planned.
capex_capacity: Branch network 776 as of March 2026; FY27 plan to add about 20% (about 140 branches, confirmed by management as broadly yes).
Digital, AI and analytics investment on a cloud-led data platform; the spend is driving the opex increase.
Equity raise up to INR2,000 crores, to maintain buffer over the Board-mandated 20% CAR threshold and fund growth for about 3 years.
No inorganic acquisition of secured book is planned.
demand_pricing: Industry bank credit grew 16% to INR219 lakh crore and deposits 13.4% to INR268 lakh crore as of March 31, 2026.
Management cut SA rates in April; expects a 25-30bps reduction in SA cost of funds. SA exit cost of funds was 5.21% in March.
No plan to reprice retail or bulk TDs or MFI yields; management is watching competitors who have raised TD rates.
Gold ticket size rose about 60% YoY, with yields up about 30bps QoQ after lowering rates on small tickets.
Management said deposit growth will match credit growth; a slowdown in deposits in the July-August period was deliberate because of excess liquidity.
MFI slippages for Q4 around INR130 crores; Bucket-X collection efficiency 99.8% in March 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why does ROA fall from about 2% to 1.6% if NIM, opex and credit cost are flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is conservative on opex and credit cost and covers possible stress in a couple of key products; no specific line item was identified. It will update if the number changes materially.

qa_highlights.question: Will the secured mix shift cut yields and margins, and how much cost-of-funds benefit is left?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30bps of deposit repricing benefit remains. Management cites 2-wheeler, gold (above 14%) and micro mortgage (19.7%) yields to offset lower housing and MSME yields. NIM guided at about 8.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when CAR is already strong?
qa_highlights.answer: The asset growth guidance is 25% a year against a Board threshold of 20%, and the bank needs growth capital for about 3 years. The raise is planned for H2FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why not grow MFI faster, with a larger share of new customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Most FY26 acquired customers are not yet eligible for repeat loans, so growth will be mostly repeat-driven. New-to-bank share is about 25%, possibly rising to 30%, but not 40-45%, which would be too risky.

qa_highlights.question: What is the secured mix target and reapplication timeline for universal bank status?
qa_highlights.answer: The RBI gives no ratio. Management expects about 56% secured by March 2027, and the reapplication timeline will be set after a 2-3 year plan, not immediately.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a contingency provision buffer for ECL or universal bank readiness in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No, management has no plan for additional provisions in FY27 beyond the guidance.

risks_watch: ROA guidance of 1.6% sits well below the 2.1% exit rate; management gave no line-item bridge, and the opex investment and mix shift are the main drivers to track.
Secured yield dilution as the mix moves toward housing and MSME; monitor NIM against the 8.5% guide.
Deposit competition: peers have raised TD rates; the bank has no plan to match, so CASA and TD growth need watching.
Micro banking growth held below 10% as repeat-loan-driven; watch the 5.4 lakh new-customer run-rate and any guardrail changes.

543066|2026-09.headline: SBI Card Q2 FY27 PAT rose 75% YoY to INR778 crore on lower credit costs, while spend growth was just 3% and NIM is guided range-bound around 10.8%.
543066|2026-09.overview: SBI Card reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of INR5,141 crore (up 4% YoY) and PAT of INR778 crore (up 75% YoY), driven mainly by lower credit costs. Gross credit cost fell to 5.6% (down 98 bps QoQ and 342 bps YoY) and gross NPA to 1.9%. Total spends grew about 3% YoY to INR1,10,689 crore, with retail spends up 6% to a record INR95,299 crore, and management attributed the weak headline to festive timing shifting into Q3. Management expects receivables to grow from Q3 and retail spend growth of mid-teens to high-teens for FY27, but gave no receivables growth guidance. NIM was 10.8% with cost of funds up 18 bps QoQ to 6.8%, and management expects NIM to be range-bound as rate hikes feed in.

543212|2026-03.headline: Borosil FY26 revenue rose 8% to INR1,195.9 crore but operating EBITDA was flat at INR176.7 crore as Hydra flask supply disruption from the BIS QCO hit margins.
543212|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations reached INR1,195.9 crore (up 8% from INR1,107.8 crore), while pre-exceptional operating EBITDA was flat at INR176.7 crore and margin fell to 15.1% from 16.3%. Q4 FY26 revenue grew 5.2% to INR284.1 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.5% from 14.2%, with the West Asia LPG supply disruption temporarily shutting the borosilicate and opal glass furnaces. Management attributed the Hydra shortfall to BIS/QCO-related supply chain problems and said the company is adding in-house flask capacity and solar power to offset cost pressures. Net debt at consolidated level was INR49.7 crore at FY26 end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margins fall in Q4 despite borosilicate ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Chinese dumping, which Borosil can only partly offset with brand premium, plus higher gas and raw material costs in Q4. A price increase was taken but its impact lags.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA saving from solar?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Anand Sultania estimated about INR28 crore at EBITDA level for FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 90-95%. Growth has slowed, and only debottlenecking is planned. No major opalware capex; focus is on other categories.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost inflation is covered by price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price hikes of 8-10% are enough to cover cost inflation, with 1-2 quarters of lag.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO said gas cost rose by about INR30 crore for all three furnaces. Management put the direct impact at INR30-35 crore a year, with indirect effects via packaging, freight and wages.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital and inventory rise, and when will it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Hydra inventory from last year is largely depleted, but appliance inventory was built for QCO and borosilicate furnace output exceeds sales. Management expects inventory to stop growing this year and reverse next year.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin gain from in-house vacuum bottle manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects at least 10% gross margin improvement, but only after 6-12 months of stabilisation, so not in the first couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company fund rising debt and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt may rise short term by about INR100 crore, but it expects FY27 capex to be similar to operating cash flow of about INR120 crore, so funding is internal.

Hydra flask recovery depends on the in-house plant ramp-up; margin benefit is delayed 6-12 months.
QCO/BIS remediation deadline 1 October 2026 for appliances; inventory build-up exposes working capital.
Opalware growth has slowed and management expects muted growth for about a year without new product innovation.

Related-party arrangement with Borosil Scientific (cost plus about 5%); management said it is less than 10% of Borosil sales and consolidation is uneconomic for now.

qa_highlights.question: Will Gurugram be commissioned by end of this fiscal year and how many beds will open in FY28?

qa_highlights.question: Blended ARPOB for Care Homes once occupancy rises?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the GBS segment margin decline QoQ, and which AI platforms have adoption metrics?

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 12.5% FY27 guidance is covered by won deals versus pipeline conversion?

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in FY27 revenue acceleration, and which verticals will lead?

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for Heltar to contribute meaningfully?

qa_highlights.question: Why was the India segment profit negative and what is the cash conversion outlook?

543230|2026-03.headline: Advait Energy Transitions Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR228 crore and PAT 55% to INR19.96 crore; order book hit a record INR1,304 crore.

Standalone figures were also read out, with FY26 standalone revenue of INR448 crore and PAT of INR46 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 BESS revenue INR46 crore if BOO projects will sell electricity?

qa_highlights.answer: Conductor and transformer contracts have pass-through clauses; OPGW contracts do not. Management said it has factored these into its bid numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why were four subsidiaries created, and who holds the other 20% of one of them?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiaries were set up for focused growth, bank facilities and future equity raises, with AGPL for electrolysers and solar EPC, the battery company for BESS and C&I, Akara for carbon and Aura for assets. The 20% holder was not answered on the call and was deferred to email.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company fund capex and what about dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funding will use both equity and debt in a mix based on business composition, and equity dilution would happen only if it benefits shareholders. No quantum was given.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company move to pure-play solar EPC and what is the solar EPC capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to bid on large tenders including module-supply projects and win some orders this year. Physical capacity is about 100-200 MW a year.

qa_highlights.question: Opex growth of ~10% in FY26 is the lowest in 5 years: how much is deliberate discretionary cost management versus sustainable savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Ram Charan said the cost actions are structural and automation-led, not a one-off squeeze. Headcount rose ~100-120 people YoY, with ReArch hiring offset by a ~70 reduction in core MF operations. Total cost growth was 9% including depreciation and 7.8% excluding it, with QoQ cost growth under 1.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Passive mix shift typically hurts RTA yields more than AMC yields. Is there scope to renegotiate RTA pricing on passives or to gain bargaining power on the active book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said passives are under 10% of AUM and already priced at very low levels, so there is no room to renegotiate. Yield compression QoQ (<1%) came from mix, not from lower rates in any asset class. Ram Charan said the mix shift is an argument to raise with AMCs, but it is not a decisive one.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 3-5 bps AMC fee cut be passed to RTA fees? Is any RTA fee negotiation under way?
qa_highlights.answer: No concrete RTA fee change has been agreed. Discussions may happen, but management said it is comfortable with the price-value equation and does not expect a material impact.

qa_highlights.question: Should yield decline be modelled at the historical 3-3.5% for FY27 and FY28, given that margins have previously dropped from 46-47% to 42-44%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 3-3.5% is the 5-year average and should be used as a conservative model input, with the aim being a lower number, possibly under 3%. On margins, Anuj Kumar said 46% was reached about 5 quarters ago, dropped to 42%, and has now been regained over 4 quarters. He attributed the earlier fall to investments in non-revenue businesses made over 2022-2025.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 guidance for employee cost, overall expenses and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost growth is guided below 5% and total expense growth below 9%, with increments effective from Q2 FY27. No formal margin guidance was given; the aim is to retain the Q4 FY26 margin of ~46.5% after salary increases, investments and yield compression.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~20% non-MF growth be built in FY27 with KRA flat, and what is the breakdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a base of ~INR60-62 crore quarterly non-MF revenue, or ~INR250 crore annualised. It needs ~INR45-50 crore of increment: payments ~INR20 crore, AIF ~INR7-8 crore, Rep ~INR7-8 crore, AA/TSP/pension ~INR15 crore (quoted as INR4-5 crore in one place and ~INR15 crore in another), with ConsenPro and GIFT City adding a few crore.

qa_highlights.question: KRA: what is the price cut, and how is FY27 revenue flat after it?
qa_highlights.answer: The industry-wide ~20% fee cut from 1 April 2026 is expected to reduce KRA revenue by ~INR8 crore on a base of ~INR42-43 crore. NSE KRA integration adds ~INR3 crore, leaving a ~INR5 crore gap that management expects to close through new-logo growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is ConsenPro and what is the market opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: ConsenPro is a commercial DPDP-compliance product built inside Think360 from an internal captive offering. It covers consent management, data discovery, regulatory reporting and consulting. Management expects ~40,000-50,000 Indian companies to need it over ~1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Could a single KYC regime through CKYC reduce KRA pricing or volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CKYC is not yet eligible to substitute for KRA KYC. KRA runs a second verification layer (name match, face match, DOB and address against DigiLocker or UIDAI), so the risk is seen as a watch item rather than an immediate threat.

risks_watch: MF yield: the passive mix shift continues to pull yields down. Any AMC pass-through of 3-5 bps could lead to RTA fee discussions. Management guides yield decline below 3%, against a 3-3.5% historical average, and says no concrete RTA fee change has been agreed.

KRA: a ~INR8 crore fee cut from 1 April 2026 is only partly offset by ~INR3 crore from NSE KRA. FY27 flat guidance depends on new-logo growth to fill a ~INR5 crore gap. A possible single-KYC/CKYC shift is a watch item.

Margin sustainability: management is targeting retention of the ~46.5% Q4 margin through FY27 after salary increases, investments and yield compression. Past cycles show margins falling back to 42-44% after investment phases.

MF AUM and asset growth: AUM fell from INR58.5 lakh crore at a point in Q4 to INR55.1 lakh crore, reflecting Middle East-related market weakness. Management says asset growth is awaited after the last two months, and FY27 MF revenue is not guided.

ReArch execution: a 5-year programme with ~2 years done and ~3-4% behind the schedule curve. The data lake is due in 1H FY27, and the data warehouse and next-gen transaction origination platform are due within 3-4 months. Non-MF margin target is 20% by end FY27.

Non-MF growth dependence: ~20% FY27 growth needs ~INR45-50 crore of incremental revenue. The breakdown includes ~INR20 crore from payments, with a new-logo pipeline (SIFs, ConsenPro, GIFT City) still early.

segments.name: AIF / Alternatives

qa_highlights.question: Expected AUM growth and yield compression behind the 13% blended revenue guidance, and downside risk (line dropped, not answered in full)
qa_highlights.answer: Question was cut off by a line drop before management responded; the outlook was not restated in that exchange.

qa_highlights.question: How does SIF economics work for CAMS?

qa_highlights.question: Why did non-asset MF revenue decline YoY despite transaction growth?

qa_highlights.answer: Account aggregator, pension and CAMS Repository are not yet EBITDA positive; CAMSRep is expected to turn positive on a Q4 basis. Think Analytics is almost at breakeven. Account aggregator adoption faces a bottleneck, mainly on the fintech and lending side.

Wealth model: RM productivity and automation are being used to lower the cost to serve; the second wealth business (₹1 crore to ₹50 crore net worth) is about ₹3,400–3,500 crore AUM.
demand_pricing: Industry volumes moderated sequentially; Angel One said its order decline mirrored industry trends, with lower derivative volumes the main driver.

Cash realization per order rose QoQ on a mix shift (orders above vs below ₹20,000) and on a value-added plan for assisted clients. A November pricing change also contributed. Management said it would not bake in further increases.
Client acquisition cost rose in the IPL period. Management said total acquisition cost (not per-client CAC) is moving with market conditions.
Nifty active client base softened and CDSL-reported client acquisition was softer in recent months, per management.
Average client funding book grew to ₹61.4 billion, while the period-end book reached a record ₹71.5 billion.
Lending: 7 lending partners, mostly banks and large NBFCs, with a couple of fintechs added in the last 2 to 3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why has credit disbursement declined over recent quarters (about ₹710 crore at Q3, ₹610 crore, then ₹530 crore), and what has not worked?
qa_highlights.answer: Saurabh Agarwal cited customer sentiment, lender underwriting and pricing, and platform friction as causes. Management said lenders are recalibrating risk and pricing, and that some funnel friction is being fixed. It maintained that the long-term thesis is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: How is broking trending in July after a weak start, and how should the next quarters look?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish Kenghe said only about 15 days of July were available, so there is too early a read. He said nothing fundamental had changed and that the company does not comment on mid-quarter volumes or MTF run rates.

qa_highlights.question: Wealth management revenue, cost and breakeven plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet Agrawal said wealth and AMC revenue are not disclosed. Burn is about 4% of operating margin this quarter, expected at 3% to 3.5% for FY27, with incremental breakeven in about 3 to 4 years. No absolute quantum was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the AMC's AUM still small after launch, and what is the plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Majumdar said the AMC has been passive-only for about 15 months, with most products launched in the last quarter of FY26. Management expects clearer strategy visibility over the next 3 to 4 quarters and declined to give AUM targets.

qa_highlights.question: Client funding risk if markets fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish Kenghe said risk is limited because margins follow exchange-prescribed levels and sometimes exceed them. Vineet Agrawal added that the company has seen no issues in past market shocks and sees low penetration among its clients.

qa_highlights.question: Employee count decline (from about 4,139 at FY25-end to about 3,300 at FY26-end) and cash realization jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a headcount target or divisional breakdown, citing efficiency gains. Cash realization gains were attributed to order-size mix and the value-added assisted plan. It said it would not bake in further gains.

qa_highlights.question: Acquisition cost rising during IPL, and is there a structural increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish Kenghe said IPL spend is branding, not acquisition cost, and that CAC tends to rise during IPL and then normalize. Long-term equity penetration (5% to 10% of retail wealth) remains the driver.

qa_highlights.question: A retail customer complained about a restricted-basket (RSM) restriction in the app.
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish Kenghe apologised, said the restriction reflects Angel One's own risk policies on top of SEBI rules, and asked the customer to email ceo@angelone.in for an offline follow-up. He did not commit to removing the basket.

Client acquisition cost and active-client trends, with Nifty active clients and CDSL acquisition softer per management.

543235|2026-09.headline: Angel One Q2 FY27: consolidated PAT up 58.2% YoY to ₹3.35 bn on revenue of ₹14.3 bn (+18.9%); standalone OPM 48.9%.
543235|2026-09.overview: Revenue held broadly flat sequentially despite softer trading after regulatory changes, while profit grew much faster on operating leverage and a larger client funding book. Consolidated operating margin rose to 45.1% from 34.5% a year ago; normalised for IPL spend and ESOP reversals it was 43.8% versus 43.6% in Q1. Management kept the standalone broking-plus-distribution margin guidance at about 45% annually and reported record average funding book (₹74.5 bn) and record credit distribution in September (annualised run rate ₹33 bn). Client additions were about 1.5 mn, up 11.6% QoQ. Management said October F&O industry ADTO was up about 39% month-to-date versus September (as of 14 October) and linked near-term upside to the SEBI closing auction session (CAS) circular.

financial_highlights.change: +58% YoY (58.2% as stated in opening remarks)
vs 34.5% a year ago (>1,000 bps); 43.8% normalised vs 43.6% QoQ

segments.name: Broking (direct/assisted)
segments.commentary: Gross broking share fell to ~55% of revenue from ~60% a year ago. Net broking income split is ~75% direct and ~25% AP channel. September average daily orders rebounded to 5.8 mn, up ~12% from August.

segments.name: Market share
segments.commentary: Retail F&O turnover share 22.1% for the quarter, rising to 22.5% in September; cash share moderated. Options premium turnover share 19.7%. Commodities turnover more than doubled YoY with share down to 44% as the market expanded.

segments.name: Lending (MTF/funding)
segments.commentary: Interest income ₹5.1 bn. About 84% of funded clients have exposure below ₹100,000; 82% of closing book is under 30 days old. Lending rate held at 14.99% despite higher RBI-linked borrowing costs. Management said delinquencies remain negligible.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Distribution income ~₹71 crore in the quarter, about 5% of revenue, helped by credit distribution and IPO activity. Management does not disclose the split. Regular plans are about one-third of MF distribution.

segments.name: Wealth (Ionic Wealth)
segments.commentary: AUM ₹160 bn, up 19.1% QoQ. Management said margins will be in line with industry (ultra-HNI industry yields near 0.5%) and that the book is focused on annuity-based assets. Some AUM is in custody and does not earn fees; management called this a very small number.

segments.name: Asset Management
segments.commentary: AUM about ₹6 bn. Management is evaluating a comprehensive play and plans to bring in a new leader; no timeline given.

segments.commentary: Cash burn from new businesses at about 3.5%-4% of EBITDA margin, up from 2.5%-3% about six quarters ago.

Client additions of about 1.5 mn in Q2, up 11.6% QoQ; management says activation trends have improved and NSE active share rose each month of the quarter.
SIP registrations up nearly 12% QoQ; management declined to read much into the September decline.
Management sees F&O pricing as right and is not planning to change it; price elasticity exists but trust is a key driver.
Net broking realisation rose partly on commodities mix; per-segment realisations not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 45% margin guidance include IPL spend and how is employee cost so low?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet said the ~45% annual guidance for broking plus distribution includes all expenses including IPL. Employee cost fell due to attrition and one-time costs in Q1; FY27 employee cost guided at ~₹1,100 crore, flat YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross client acquisition slower than the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish said acquisitions were up 11% vs Q1 and the company is focused on activation and marginal CAC across channels, including AP, performance marketing and organic. Management said it would invest where growth is available at the right price.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SIP registrations drop in September?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish said SIP registration numbers vary month-to-month and can be optical (counting edits); a broader period gives a better read, and management tracks SIP inflows and active SIPs.

qa_highlights.question: How is rising borrowing cost affecting MTF and competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet said lending rate stays at 14.99% with no change planned; borrowing cost rose marginally after the RBI benchmark hike but is within tolerance, with NIMs not materially affected. Bhavin said blue-chip and good stocks make up over 85% of the MTF book.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wealth AUM fee yield and how much is earning fees?
qa_highlights.answer: Shobhit said margins will track industry levels (about 0.5% in ultra-HNI) and most of the book is annuity-based. Amit said assets were acquired through the year, so applying yield to closing AUM overstates revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the drag from new businesses on EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet said the cash burn from new businesses is about 3.5%-4% of EBITDA margin, versus about 2.5%-3% six quarters ago when scale was low.

qa_highlights.question: Will the closing auction session circular help F&O volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish said the circular provides clarity and is a tailwind for near-term F&O, and that pricing is working and not under review.

Cash segment share fell while MTF grew; management attributes this to segment mix, but it is worth tracking.

IPL and brand spend, plus AP channel and new business cash burn of 3.5%-4%, weigh on margins.

543238|2026-03.headline: UTI AMC FY26 standalone normalized PAT fell to Rs 643 crore from Rs 653 crore, while core PAT rose to Rs 460 crore from Rs 447 crore.
543238|2026-03.overview: UTI AMC reported FY26 standalone core income of Rs 1,255 crore (up from Rs 1,180 crore) and normalized core PAT of Rs 460 crore (up from Rs 447 crore). Consolidated normalized PAT fell to Rs 511 crore from Rs 731 crore, and consolidated normalized core PAT fell to Rs 452 crore from Rs 492 crore. Costs rose sharply: consolidated Q4 employee cost of Rs 132 crore was up about 14% YoY even after a one-time VRS and family pension charge of about Rs 130 crore taken in Q3. The company declared a Rs 40 per share FY26 dividend and management said it sees the payout trend at about 95% of profits. Management's single stated priority is growth in MF AUM, with cost discipline as the second.

qa_highlights.question: What was the one-off in Q4/FY26 expenses, and how should employee and other expenses be modelled for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about Rs 130 crore of VRS and family pension one-off was provided in Q3 FY26, plus about Rs 4 crore for the Labour Code. Analyst noted consolidated Q4 employee cost of Rs 132 crore was still up 14% YoY; management attributed this to variable pay and recruitment across three businesses. FY27 guidance: standalone employee cost Rs 90-95 crore per quarter, consolidated Rs 125-130 crore; other admin expenses +7-8% standalone and about 10% consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: How did customer acquisition go during the March volatility, and what schemes attract first-time SIP investors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no sharp pick-up in new investors in March; SIP stoppages rose seasonally. February new SIP additions were better than the industry. First-time investors mainly choose index funds, often with Rs 1,000-1,500 SIP tickets. New PAN acquisition is now a sales metric, with FY26 target to grow the 7.16 lakh count.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of SEBI's revised norms from 1 April, and what is the yield outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Exit load TER cut by 5 bps, plus some base TER rationalisation; management expects the impact to pass through to intermediaries and sees no effect on AMC yield. Yield may dilute by 1-2 bps in FY27 due to mix shift to ETFs and low-duration debt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan to return equity net sales to positive territory?
qa_highlights.answer: Priority is raising SIP book. Management is repositioning sales teams to sell multiple funds across value, GARP and quality growth styles, to reduce pro-cyclicality to performance. Net equity flows were close to zero in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the employee count fall while sales staff grows, and is RM headcount rising further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mix is being corrected toward revenue-generating roles. It does not expect RM count to rise much further from about 260 UFCs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for international business and SIF launches?
qa_highlights.answer: International AUM is under pressure from foreign outflows and currency weakness; management plans to hold ground and bring institutional clients into alternatives. SIF: at least one fund targeted this year, first product unlikely to be priced above plain-vanilla MF yields; higher yield depends on long-short differentiation.

543248|2026-03.headline: RBA India Q4 FY26 SSSG hit 6.3%, the highest in 12 quarters, while Indonesia took a INR120 crore impairment and the company is being acquired by Inspira Global.

Full-year revenue was INR2,271 crore, restaurant EBITDA margin 11.6% and company EBITDA margin 5.8%. Gross margin exited Q4 at 70.2%, ahead of the FY29 target. Indonesia drew a INR120 crore impairment on a DCF valuation, with Popeyes (24 outlets) losing IDR25 billion, and the company is set to be acquired by Inspira Global, with revised outlook promised after the deal closes in Q1.

segments.name: Indonesia (Burger King)

segments.name: Indonesia (Popeyes)

Management said there is no current danger to India operations from the LNG/LPG supply disruption; no restaurants closed for a day, but LPG-dependent outlets faced challenges.

qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose Café split. Early-converted cohorts sit well above average. Target is around INR25,000 per restaurant per day over 4-5 years. Newer Café stores have lower volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Explain the cash burn (about INR350 crore used in operations, cash down from about INR500 crore to about INR150 crore) and the outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Sumit said cash is about INR190 crore as of March, cash from operations rose from INR99 crore to INR132 crore, and India is targeting FCF neutrality in 4-6 quarters. Q4 generated INR40 crore. Analyst confirmed FY28 FCF-positive target; management agreed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was INR120 crore impairment booked, is this a full exit, what is the new promoter's plan, and what is the Indonesia breakeven timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Impairment came from a DCF on consolidated Indonesia business; management called it a one-time provision fully covering the balance-sheet requirement. Varman declined to give a timeline or exit decision until the new promoter aligns. Sumit said the BK side needs about four more quarters to cover its own G&A.

qa_highlights.question: Will Lenexis (promoter's Chinese wok brand) be merged or licensed with RBA, and what protects minority shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Varman said the businesses are separate, no discussions have taken place, and the focus is on Indonesia structural changes. Deal awaits government approvals with no timing given.

qa_highlights.question: Is CCI approval the only pending item for the open offer, and how is LNG supply disruption being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed that CCI approval is pending. On LNG, the new broiler is electric, about half the utilities; electric fryers are being added; LPG restaurants converted to PNG where possible. No percentage split given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of gross margin expansion comes from product mix versus sourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: Varman said it is a combined effort: cluster-based supplier proximity lowers transport and input cost, and premium items and add-ons (fizz drinks, Waffle Cone) carry high margins. No split quantified.

risks_watch: Indonesia: INR120 crore impairment; further funding need and further write-downs not quantified; Popeyes (24 outlets) has no disposal timeline.

543248|2026-06.headline: India SSSG hit 12.6% in Q1 FY27 with revenue up 23.6% to INR682 crore and restaurant EBITDA of INR90 crore (13.2% margin).
543248|2026-06.overview: Restaurant Brands Asia reported a strong Q1 FY27, led by India, where SSSG of 12.6% was driven by traffic rather than price, per management. India gross margin rose to 70.8% and company EBITDA more than doubled to INR52.7 crore. Indonesia remained loss-making at the Popeyes level but Burger King Indonesia reached positive restaurant EBITDA, with consolidated restaurant EBITDA of INR3.3 crore. A new promoter group has closed its stake acquisition, and management is working on a capital allocation plan for the next 3 to 5 years, with no details yet.

segments.commentary: 590 restaurants (+71 YoY, +9 QoQ), 83% of group revenue; SSSG 12.6%, ADS INR1,31,000, gross margin 70.8%, restaurant EBITDA INR90 crore. Management targets around 80 net additions a year.

segments.name: Burger King Indonesia
segments.commentary: 137 restaurants (down from 179 after closing non-profitable units, per management), 15% of group revenue; ADS INR1,02,000, revenue INR124 crore, restaurant EBITDA INR6.4 crore. Bone-in chicken rose from about 30% to 50% of sales; self-ordering kiosks lifted average per check about 4-5%.

segments.name: Popeyes Indonesia

qa_highlights.answer: Management said no significant price increase was taken; the 12.6% SSSG was driven by traffic, and Q2 has started well, though no forward guidance was given. Q1 marketing was 6.6% of revenue, seasonally high, and is expected to amortise to 5-5.5% over the year, which would lift restaurant EBITDA by that amount.

qa_highlights.question: Will SSSG sustain at double-digit levels over the next 4-6 quarters, versus the earlier 5-7% guidance?

qa_highlights.question: How will the new promoters' capital be deployed, and will there be further acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: This is the first call with the new promoters, the deal closed a few weeks ago, and a 3-5 year strategy covering capital allocation, growth rate, efficiencies and back-of-house integration is in progress. Plans will be shared once finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Is Indonesia still on the twin path of fixing profitability or hiving off, and what is the Popeyes update?

qa_highlights.question: Delivery mix rose while peers reported different trends; is this due to lower competition? Also, why did head-office cost differ pre- and post-Ind AS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said delivery growth reflects profitable traffic and some event-driven demand in certain markets, not competitor weakness. CFO said the forex loss sits below EBITDA in finance cost and India G&A is INR37 crore, so it does not affect EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Will the promoters pledge more shares, and will they join future calls?

543252|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue fell 3.2% YoY to Rs 117 crore, but EBITDA margin rose to 6.9% on better domestic realisations as Chinese dumping eased.
543252|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 117 crore, down 3.2% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 8 crore at a 6.9% margin and adjusted PAT of Rs 3.7 crore. Management attributed the margin recovery mainly to better domestic price realisation as Chinese dumping of dimer acid moderated from around February 2026. For FY26, revenue fell 14.5% to Rs 460 crore on volume of 44,000 tonnes versus 54,000 tonnes in FY25. Management guided to 75-80% capacity utilisation on the 80,000-tonne base in FY27 and targets around 8% EBIT margin, with a new 40,000-tonne oleochemical product line planned for commissioning in Q2 FY27.

vs Rs 7.5 per share last year

Export share expected to rise from about 8-10% to around 20%, mainly from US, Europe and Japan; US commercial exports restarted about two months ago on a small scale and meaningful volumes are expected within about six months.

Energy audit completed; investments in electrical equipment, pumps, motors and heat exchangers have cut power and fuel cost to Rs 6 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 8 crore in Q4 FY25. Further reduction is expected, and a second energy audit is under way.
New 40,000-tonne novel-process oleochemical line: lab, pilot and plant stages completed; commissioning around Q2 FY27 with first-phase capex of Rs 20-25 crore.
Bypass fat plant starts next month.

demand_pricing: Paint demand showed a recovery in March 2026 and a stronger recovery in Q4; management says paint sector has been looking up for about two months.
Realisations rose about 8-10% on major products as Chinese dumping eased from around February 2026; management described them as 'fairly good'.
Chinese dumping of dimer acid is said to have been about 800-1,000 tonnes per month; the cause is linked to removal of Chinese export incentives of up to 15%.
Management says sales are spread across inks, paints, polyamides (epoxy hardener) and drilling fluids with no major customer concentration.

Raw material is a buy-sell commodity priced daily from refineries with no long-term contracts; end-product prices with customers are revised at most monthly. Import duty on raw vegetable oil is 16.5%; dimer acid import duty is 7.5%.
Management says the rupee depreciation helps exports more than it raises raw material and coal costs, but no sensitivity figures were given.

qa_highlights.question: Would margins return to FY25 EBIT of about 8%, or expand further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will be better this year and it is confident of reaching 8%; at 95% utilisation margins can creep up, with operating leverage. A later question on 12-15% margins was answered as 'our dream' without a commitment.

qa_highlights.question: What share of FY26 revenue came from dimer acid, isosteric acid and linoleic acid?
qa_highlights.answer: Dimer acid about Rs 140 crore (25-30%), isosteric acid Rs 26 crore (5-6%), linoleic acid around 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 40,000-tonne new product linked to paints or cosmetics, and what revenue and margin can it generate?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an oleochemical-basket product, not paint-related. Management cited Rs 800-1,000 crore at full scale over about five years and margins 'much better' than the traditional business, with the analyst's 15-18% range not disputed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the expansion delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material duties rose from 5.5% to as high as 27.5% and Chinese dumping hit finished products, so the company avoided debt-funded expansion until conditions stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: Can Chinese dumping restart at current prices?

543253|2026-06.headline: Mrs. Bectors Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR548.7 crores with EBITDA margin at 13.1%, targeting 14% by Q4.
543253|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16% YoY to INR548.7 crores and 12.9% QoQ, with exports reported as high-double-digit growth. EBITDA rose 23.8% to INR72.1 crores, margin up 80 bps YoY to 13.1%, and PAT rose 25.5% to INR38.8 crores. Management said price increases and Project IMPACT largely offset input cost inflation in Q1, but expects Q2 to be the most challenging quarter for commodity and packaging costs. Full-year guidance is mid-teens revenue growth and a 14% EBITDA margin by Q4, with about 16% targeted by FY30.

segments.name: Bakery (English Oven, Naturbaked, QSR)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR215 crores, up 17.5% YoY; Naturbaked crossed a monthly revenue run rate of INR1 crore. Bakery EBITDA margin is above company average; B2B/QSR returned to good double-digit growth.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Grew at high-double-digit rate; volume-led. Export contribution is about 35% of revenue; US contribution is about 23-25% per management, and US is back on growth after tariff-related slowdown.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Grew 58% YoY per management; Kolkata bakery unit (commissioned Q4 FY26) now serving East markets.

MP plant opened mainly for exports (closer to port) with fiscal incentive; now starting central-market distribution.
Capex funding: about 60% from internal accruals and 40% borrowings this year.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand healthy across retail and institutional; consumption better than feared at last call.
Competition intense in biscuits, especially Upper North India; company stepped up trade promotion and marketing spend.
Plan to add 40,000 billed outlets above INR200/outlet (about 12-13% increase in billed outlets).
Export orders are month-to-month, not a long order book; management said no restocking benefit in Q1.
Inflation impact about 1-2% over last year; contract manufacturing about 1-1.5% of revenue.
Domestic general trade split roughly 50% Upper North and 50% Rest of India; English Oven revenue about 80% North India, with upcountry and NCR now roughly equal.

543254|2026-03.headline: Antony Waste FY26 operating revenue rose 9% to Rs.920 crores; Q4 revenue up 14% to Rs.254 crores with EBITDA margin ~22%, order book at record Rs.18,000 crores.
543254|2026-03.overview: FY26 marked 25 years of operations, with a maiden dividend of Rs.0.50 per share recommended. Volumes grew strongly: total MSW managed rose 15% to 5.69 million tons, and Q4 processing volumes jumped 32% to 1.15 million tons. Revenue growth was 9% for the year and 14% in Q4, with EBITDA margin held near 22% for both periods, though reported PAT was Rs.92 crores and Q4 PAT of Rs.37 crores was flattered by a Rs.24 crore one-time income in the prior-year base. Management reiterated 15-20% revenue CAGR over five years, citing the record order book and two large AP WTE projects.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs.274 crores (+5%); Q4 Rs.94 crores (+15%). Processing volumes rose ~19% to 3.6 million tons in FY26 and 32% to 1.15 million tons in Q4, driven by biomining and MRF utilisation. Processing is ~60% of the Rs.18,000 crore order book per management.

qa_highlights.answer: Wage inflation and headcount growth raised employee costs; other expenses rose on RDF transport (177,000 tons sold) and hiring. Margin softness from delayed monsoon-hit C&D volumes and extra vehicles at Nagpur, Noida and PCMC.

543254|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6% YoY to ₹269 crore, but EBITDA fell 27% to ₹45 crore (16.8% margin) and PAT dropped to ₹0.7 crore after one-offs.
543254|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 6% YoY to ₹269 crore on higher volumes and tariff escalation. EBITDA margin compressed to 16.8% from 24.4% a year ago, driven by higher transport/hiring costs at the CIDCO site, employee costs rising to 34% of revenue, and about ₹10 crore of deferred Q4 FY26 disposal work. The PCMC WtE plant was shut after a July 8 landslide of legacy waste that killed nine people, and management flagged a ₹22-24 crore impairment (before insurance) as an exceptional item. The company also refinanced ₹140 crore of Antony Lara's term loan from 10.25% to 8.25%, with a ₹7 crore prepayment charge.

vs ₹23 crore in Q1 FY26; includes ₹7 crore one-time prepayment expense

segments.commentary: Revenue ₹156 crore, up 10% YoY; share of revenue 62% vs 60% a year ago. Management said margins are under pressure from repairs and maintenance and ageing contracts.

segments.commentary: Revenue ₹75 crore, up 3% YoY; share 28%, flat. Growth slowed because the CIDCO bio-mining contract ended, and processing volumes rose 5% to about 0.85 million tons.

segments.commentary: Plant suspended after the July 8 incident. Over 20 million green units generated in the quarter before the shutdown; restart expected by first/second week of October. Fixed costs of ₹2.5-3 crore per month (about ₹7 crore total) will run through the quarter.

segments.commentary: Running at 600-650 tons per day against 600 tons per day capacity (±10%), with a 96% recycling rate, after BMC policy required large builders to send waste to the plant.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the PCMC WtE operations and near-term revenue impact, given it is a high-margin business?
qa_highlights.answer: MRF and composting restarted July 28 at about 400 tons/day. WtE plant expected back by first/second week of October; fixed cost of ₹2.5-3 crore per month (about ₹7 crore) sits on the books meanwhile. Tipping fees continue, but power generation and sale revenue is hit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did processing revenue growth moderate, and what is the margin trajectory from Q2/Q3 given cost inflation and wage hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Slowdown is due to the CIDCO bio-mining contract ending (a two-year project). Atkoli going live by Q4 restores growth. Transport and hiring costs pressured C&T margins; renegotiation with transport vendors should give some respite. Labour DA pressure is timing-related, with relief expected in H2 FY27 via escalations. Management says FY27 margins should move back toward historical trend, plus or minus a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Size of the Lara refinancing, the ₹15 crore court-linked receivable, and the Andhra project status?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹140 crore was refinanced at a lower rate. The ₹15 crore receivable is still pending with the Corporation after a favourable court judgement. Andhra: land possessed at Kadapa and Kurnool, JFE India has completed civil designs, civil contractor mobilised at Kadapa, Kurnool to start in about two weeks, financial closure nearly final.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹10 crore CIDCO cost recurring, and what is the payback on the refinancing (prepayment charge was ₹7 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: The ₹10 crore was closure-related disposal cost of inert material for the completed CIDCO bio-mining contract, and is not expected to recur. On refinancing, management cited a 15-year tenor and net benefit of about ₹14 crore after a ₹6 crore prepayment charge; the ₹7 crore figure in the PAT disclosure differs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is RDF sales volume down 28%, and what is realisation per ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a timing issue, with new customers being added and sales from PCMC as well as CIDCO and Kanjurmarg. Net realisation is above ₹300 per ton versus about ₹250 a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What are the C&T revenue per ton and the segment margin, and is the business mix shifting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give per-ton or segment EBITDA for C&T. Some contracts (Thane, Jhansi, Varanasi) are billed per household or trip, and tipping fees range ₹1,800-4,200 per ton. Employee headcount roughly doubled in the last year, per the CEO.
