543258|2026-03.headline: Indigo Paints Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 8.4% to INR397.9 crore; management signals margin sacrifice of 2-2.5pp to chase faster top-line growth.
543258|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 8.4% YoY to INR397.9 crore, with EBITDA of INR91.7 crore (23.0% margin) and gross margin of 48.6% versus 47.4% a year earlier, despite raw material costs rising 50-100% in March 2026 due to the Middle East conflict. PAT fell to INR57.3 crore (14.4% margin) as treasury income dropped to INR0.19 crore on mark-to-market losses. For FY26, standalone revenue grew 4.1% to INR1,330 crore and PAT excluding a one-off gratuity provision grew 4% to INR149.8 crore. Management said it will accept roughly 200-250bp lower gross margin, with EBITDA margin broadly unchanged, to accelerate top-line growth in FY27. It also said no major capex is planned until FY29, with the Jodhpur water-based plant commissioning in June 2026.

segments.commentary: Primers and distemper grew 14.9% value and 9.6% volume; putty and cement paint 12.6% value and 9.5% volume; emulsions 10.5% value and 11.2% volume; enamels and wood coatings 7.2% value and 5.4% volume. All four categories grew in value and volume.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR27.5 crore (+34.7% YoY); FY26 revenue INR75.1 crore (+17.8%). Gross margin around 40% plus/minus 1%. FY27 target is 30%-plus growth.

guidance_outlook: Management is prepared to accept a 2-2.5pp gross margin decline to drive faster top-line growth, while expecting EBITDA margin broadly unchanged.

Gross sales were growing double-digit for five consecutive months from November 2025, including March; the gap to reported net sales growth (8.5% in Q4) came from higher trade and influencer discounts netted off revenue.

Management said it is not guiding a specific net sales number for Q1 FY27 and expects net sales growth well above high-single-digit to low-double-digit levels over FY27, with the caveat that disruptions can set it back.
April growth was driven largely by price hikes; some dealer overstocking has occurred, so May-June demand is uncertain.
Industry price increases of about 12% on the overall basket were implemented; management does not foresee another significant price increase unless the Middle East situation deteriorates.

Apple Chemie targets 30%-plus revenue growth in FY27.
No major capex is envisaged until FY29; FCF is expected to step up from FY27 onwards. FY26 dividend proposed at INR5 per share, up 43% from INR3.5.

New solvent-based plant and expanded putty plant at Jodhpur have already commenced production in recent months.
Network at 31 March 2026: over 19,350 active dealers, over 12,200 tinting machines, 55 depots across all 28 states.
330 kW solar installation at Kochi factory is fully operational.
demand_pricing: Industry demand recovered from November 2025 after roughly 8 quarters of subdued growth; the Iran war from about March 2026 disrupted raw material supply and pushed some input prices up 50-100%.
The industry took about 12% price increases in three phases. Indigo's own unilateral price increase came around 24-25 March 2026, ahead of the market leader's 8 April increase.

Management said water-based paints are fully covered by price hikes; solvent-based enamels and wood coatings (about 17-18% of portfolio) have a small uncovered gap, partly offset by falling mineral turpentine oil prices.
Management said the competitive intensity has moderated over the last couple of quarters; it sees no change in behaviour since JSW's acquisition of Akzo.
Differentiated products make up about 30% of sales and are described as price-inelastic, so margin reduction is expected mainly in the other two-thirds of the portfolio.
Premium emulsions are a growing share; management said value growth has exceeded volume growth in almost all categories over the last 20 quarters or more.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Apple Chemie growth accelerate to 35% in Q4 and what are its margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was muted because government contractors' payments were delayed, but Q3 and Q4 grew about 30%-plus; gross margin is about 40% plus/minus 1%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company pursuing more aggressive market share gains, and will a 200bp gross margin sacrifice be enough to reach about 24% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: The Board judged the company had been too conservative on margins; it will spend more on trade schemes and influencers, lowering gross margin 2-2.5pp while EBITDA margin should hold. Management said yes, 24% growth is achievable.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the gross margin reduction come from, and is competition the reason?
qa_highlights.answer: Extra spend will be netted from revenue through trade discounts and influencer costs, mainly in non-differentiated products. Management said competitive intensity has normalised and the move reflects a wish to grow faster, not a response to competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Reconcile double-digit gross growth with single-digit reported growth, and will net sales be sacrificed?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross sales grew double-digit in each of the last five months, but higher trade and influencer discounts cut Q4 net growth to 8.5%. Management does not expect net sales growth to fall back to single digits.

qa_highlights.question: Will more price increases be needed, and how is pricing held if costs fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect another significant price increase unless the Middle East situation worsens. It said the company now acts independently on pricing and that margins should normalise by Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company growing in metros and dealer productivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tier 1 and Tier 2 coverage is now good, and growth will come from deeper dealer throughput, not city size; with about 19,500 dealers it sees room to double sales per dealer.

543258|2026-06.headline: Indigo Paints Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 18.7% to INR350 crore with EBITDA margin up to 17.7%, its best Q1 margin in four years.
543258|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 18.7% YoY to INR350 crore, with double-digit volume and value growth across all four product categories. EBITDA rose 42% to INR61.9 crore (margin 17.7% vs 14.8%), and PAT rose 60.7% to INR42.4 crore, helped partly by a mark-to-market treasury gain. Consolidated revenue was INR369.7 crore (+19.7%), but subsidiary Apple Chemie's margins were compressed by high-cost inventory and limited B2B pass-through. Management said it will spend more aggressively on trade and influencers in Q2 to widen the growth gap versus the industry, and that the Jodhpur capex cycle is complete.

Solvent-based Jodhpur plant already in production for several months and ramping up.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Indigo not grown faster versus the market leader, and was the IPL advertising pause a missed opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said steep, frequent price hikes benefit the market leader most. The IPL pause was due to raw material uncertainty after the Iran war, not competitor ad intensity or Dhoni's playing status; it intends to put the money back in the coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Is July and August demand holding after Q1 upstocking, and is there a destocking risk for Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel overstocking was not seen at Indigo. July was a very good month with momentum maintained or slightly better than Q1; August was too early to call.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a price cut in H2, and what are the Q2 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No further price hikes are planned for now. A price cut is possible, most likely after Diwali. No Q2 margin guidance was given; management suggested looking at the six-month period.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jodhpur plant opex impact, and what is the competitive intensity after JSW-AkzoNobel?
qa_highlights.answer: The new plant replaces the legacy water-based plant with little opex change. Competitive intensity is unchanged, as JSW and AkzoNobel still operate separately.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new plant be ready for the festive season, and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production is about 10 days away and should stabilise in about a month. The legacy plant is a backup. Management said gross margin may drop a couple of points, and EBITDA margin may move about 1 point either way.

543275|2026-03.headline: Anupam FY26 consolidated revenue rose 65% to INR2,384 crores, with Q4 PAT of INR56 crores versus INR63 crores a year earlier.

543278|2026-03.headline: Kalyan Jewellers Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 118% YoY to INR410 crores on 66% revenue growth to INR10,275 crores.
543278|2026-03.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q4 FY26 was INR10,275 crores (up 66% YoY) and PAT was INR410 crores (up 118%), with India business PAT up 97% to INR366 crores. For FY26, consolidated revenue reached INR35,740 crores (up 43%) and PAT INR1,350 crores (up 89%). Management reported non-GML debt reduced by about INR360 crores in India, with non-GML now at INR300 crores, and Candere turned PAT positive in H2 FY26. Management said April 2026 started well despite a high base, while flagging Adhik Maas as a possible Q1 timing drag.

segments.name: India (Kalyan)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR8,990 crores and PBT INR495 crores (vs INR249 crores); PAT INR366 crores, up 97%. Management said India PBT margin of 5.5-5.6% is expected to stay in this range.

segments.name: Middle East
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,074 crores (vs INR784 crores) with PBT INR20 crores (vs INR15 crores) and PAT INR21 crores (vs INR12 crores). Four FOCO showrooms were temporarily converted to COCO to facilitate a planned Arab investor franchise deal, not yet materialised.

segments.name: Candere

guidance_outlook: Plan to open 150 showrooms in FY27 across Kalyan, Candere and the new regional brand; Candere share about 50-55 of these.
Aim to make India non-GML debt zero in FY27, possibly by H1 FY27, but management declined to guide firmly on timing.

Non-GML repayment of INR300 crores expected to save about INR30 crores in interest in FY27, at roughly 9-10%; about INR20 crores of one-off advance tax interest in FY26 adds to the reduction (around INR50 crores total).
Dividend recommended at about INR257 crores, roughly 20% of FY26 net profit, per the announced policy.
Management does not want to guide SSSG above 10% for the next 3-5 years, though recent SSSG has been 20-30%.

Gross margin expected to face YoY pressure from platinum/silver tailwinds that will not repeat; management cited about INR20 crores of silver benefit, with operating leverage and interest savings as offsets.

capex_capacity: Opened 129 showrooms across Kalyan and Candere in FY26, including the first Kalyan showroom in the UK.
Opened 13 stores in South India in FY26; South expansion to stay at about 13-15 showrooms, mainly in metros like Bangalore, Chennai and Hyderabad; about 60-65 showrooms planned outside South.
Middle East: 2 new showrooms opened and 5-6 renovated into bigger formats; conversion of 4 FOCO stores to COCO worth about INR200-250 crores of inventory.
Q4 showroom count rose gross by 28 but net by about 4, with management saying only one small Madurai showroom closed and the rest were relocations.
Third regional brand launch in a South state delayed until post-election situation settles.
demand_pricing: Management said SSSG for the South was lower than for non-South in Q4; non-South acceleration continued from Q3.
Akshaya Tritiya sales grew strongly; coin sales were lower than estimated this year, unlike Dhanteras when they exceeded estimates.

Management said customers buy to a rupee budget, so volumes fall as gold prices rise; gold rose about 60-70% over the past year. Consumers were pushed to studded jewellery and lower karat (22K to 18K, 18K to 14K).
Management said gold supply is not a concern, with regular bank inventory and imports via GIFT City's India International Bullion Exchange.
Gold metal loan (GML) in India is capped by bank sanctions; Middle East GML is uncapped and rises with gold prices.
Management said inventory rises by only INR30-40 for every INR100 rise in gold price, to protect ROCE.

qa_highlights.question: Why did South SSSG diverge so sharply from non-South in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said South was lower, partly because its base is higher, and non-South acceleration continued from Q3 and was more pronounced in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will non-GML debt be fully repaid by H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to be non-GML debt free in FY27 and could do it by H1, but declined to guide on timing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost rise sequentially, and what is the underlying run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher processing charges and interest on advance tax explain the rise; about INR20 crores is one-off. Non-GML repayment should cut about INR30 crores in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 Adhik Maas period a risk to sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some sales may move between quarters, with possible slower days, but some purchases were preponed; April started well.

qa_highlights.question: How much of gross margin came from silver and platinum, and what is the FY27 impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the silver/platinum benefit was about INR20 crores and will not repeat, but operating leverage and interest savings can help. PBT margin for India should stay near 5.5-5.6%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East FOCO-to-COCO conversion's potential cash release?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only 4 showrooms were converted, worth about INR200-250 crores of inventory, and declined to budget any further conversion or cash release.

543278|2026-06.headline: Kalyan Jewellers Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 38% to INR10,008 crore and PAT to INR349 crore, helped by a one-off customs duty gain.
543278|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue (net of bullion) grew 38% YoY to INR10,008 crore, with EBITDA of INR633 crore (vs INR508 crore) and PAT of INR349 crore (vs INR264 crore). India revenue rose to INR8,503 crore and Middle East to about INR1,320 crore, while Candere turned PAT positive at INR2.1 crore. Management attributed part of profit to a one-time customs duty gain of about INR40-41 crore that was passed to customers via old gold exchange offers, and flagged a 0.2-0.3% PBT margin dilution from exchange. Management said the PBT margin for the full year should hold at or above FY26 levels on a conservative basis.

segments.name: India (Kalyan)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR8,503 crore (+38% YoY) and EBITDA INR500 crore (+15%); PAT INR321 crore (+25%). Management said non-South markets now contribute 50-60% of revenue.

segments.name: Middle East
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR1,320 crore (+29%), EBITDA INR90 crore (vs INR73 crore), profit INR25 crore (vs INR22 crore).

segments.name: Candere (e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR141 crore (vs INR66 crore, roughly double); profit INR2.1 crore vs loss of INR10 crore. Management targets around 50 new Candere stores in FY27 and said Candere stays PAT positive for the year.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 PBT margin expected to be at least in line with FY26 on a conservative basis; exchange dilution of 0.2-0.3% to be offset by cash-for-gold, which is margin accretive.
Customs duty related gain expected at about INR60 crore in Q2 FY27, with some further benefit possible in the running quarter, though management said part may be shared with consumers.
Store expansion target unchanged: 84 Kalyan showrooms and about 50 Candere stores in FY27; H2 is typically heavier than H1. Management cites 70-80 showrooms a year overall.

Non-GML debt to be fully repaid by end-September 2026; second tranche of real estate collaterals to be released thereafter. Management said the company would be debt-free on a non-GML basis in a couple of months.
Recycled gold share to be maintained at 55-60% of revenue going forward.
Real estate sale: agreements signed for two land parcels for about INR102 crore; sale expected to close and proceeds received before end of Q1 FY27 (June quarter).
capex_capacity: Expansion is mainly franchise-led (FOCO model, where the franchisee funds capex and inventory and Kalyan runs the store for a margin share); franchisee ROCE cited at about 14%.
Kalyan ROCE rose to about 20% from the late teens; management expects further improvement from capital-light expansion.

New regional brand Akshaya Thanga Maligai (ATM) for Tamil Nadu: first showroom in Chennai on 21 August 2026, with four more showrooms planned in the following months, including other cities; expansion also to be predominantly FOCO.
Q1 FY27 saw 12 FOCO store openings, per the analyst's question; management confirmed no change to annual targets.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as robust except for about one month of Adhik Maas, when wedding demand slowed in parts of the country. Management said July demand was strong and continuing like Q1, but declined to quantify the trend.
Gold prices corrected about 15-20% over 2-3 months; management said customers buy by budget, so volumes rise when prices fall.
Recycled gold ('Shine with India' campaign) rose to over 46% of revenue in Q1, with June above 55%, as oil-driven forex pressure pushed the company to reduce imported gold.
Cash-for-gold (new product) grew from single-digit share in Q1 to double-digit share as of the call; management said peers are also adopting it.

Exchange transactions are priced at the board rate; cash purchases of old gold are at a discount to spot, which management said is margin accretive. Bullion sales in Q1 were used to fund cash needs of vendors, mainly studded vendors on invoice basis.
Employee cost rose about 54% YoY standalone; management said this is more than the usual annual increment and worth about 0.2-0.3% of revenue, offset by operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any bonus issue planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no bonus share plans as of now.

qa_highlights.question: Ex the one-off gain of INR410 crore, standalone PBT growth was only about 14%, so what drove the margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PBT margin ex-bullion was about 5.1% vs 5.5-5.6% earlier. The gain was partly passed to consumers via exchange offers (INR30-40 crore), exchange dilutes margin by 0.2-0.3%, and platinum/silver one-offs of about 0.2% were absent.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 0.2-0.3% exchange-related dilution persist for the next two to three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no for full year: cash-for-gold should offset exchange dilution, and it expects FY27 PBT margin at least in line with FY26 on a conservative basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gold price fall boosting volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customers come with a budget, so lower gold prices mechanically raise volumes; wedding demand cannot pause more than 2-3 weeks, and discretionary demand may pause about 1-1.5 months.

qa_highlights.question: How much customs duty benefit is expected in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR60 crore in Q2, with some benefit possible in the running quarter but part to be shared with consumers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Candere?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Candere has been PAT positive since 2H FY26, will stay positive in FY27, and will add about 50 stores with focus on inventory throughput in existing stores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the employee cost increase one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not one-time; it is above the usual annual increment, occurs once every few years, and operating leverage should absorb it.

risks_watch: Margin: exchange-led volumes dilute PBT margin by 0.2-0.3%; the full-year margin target depends on cash-for-gold scaling up.
One-off customs duty gains (about INR41 crore in Q1, about INR60 crore expected in Q2) may not recur and partly go to consumers.
Gold price volatility (15-20% correction) may pause discretionary demand and push customers to change grammage/price points.
Employee cost up about 54% YoY standalone; watch whether operating leverage offsets it.
Execution of non-GML debt repayment by September 2026 and the real estate sale proceeds.
Management declined to comment on governance questions raised in the press about related-party transactions; an open overhang for investors.
ATM's ramp-up and whether the regional format can scale beyond the first five stores.

key_quotes: Q1 performance has been very satisfactory given the overall context.
The quarter has started off very well despite the volatility in gold prices.
Candere has been PAT positive for the first quarter and should continue for this financial year.
For the full year, I don't think there will be an impact. Even on a conservative basis, I think we'll be able to maintain the PBT margins of the previous year.

543279|2026-03.headline: Suryoday SFB FY26 PAT rose to ₹152 crores from ₹115 crores; management targets FY27 PAT above ₹300 crores, with credit cost guided at 70-80 bps.
543279|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of disciplined execution and gradual stabilisation after elevated microfinance credit costs. Q4 showed improvement: inclusive finance slippages fell to about ₹74 crores from ₹116 crores in Q3 (the call also cited ₹106 crores on a total-bank basis), and monthly disbursements returned to about ₹500 crores. FY26 net total income rose 10.2% to ₹1,458 crores and PAT to ₹152 crores, with GNPA at 6.5% (₹864 crores) and CRAR at 20.5%. Management guided to 30%+ growth, a 1.2% ROA for Q1 FY27 rising to 1.6% by Q4, and a cost-to-income ratio of 67-68%.

543280|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR 429 crore and EBITDA INR 46 crore, with a PAT loss of INR 82 crore driven by associate losses (about INR 62 crore share of loss) and impairment, mainly on the Moonshine remnant value. Excluding NODWIN's deconsolidation, comparable revenue grew about 9% YoY. Gaming revenue rose 14% YoY to INR 275 crore at a 19.5% EBITDA margin, with heavier user acquisition spend compressing margins at Bluetile, Kiddopia and Curve. Management restructured the Bluetile and BestPlay deal to a fixed $303 million all-cash price, with $89 million at closing and $214 million by 1 April 2027, and named Bluetile founder Raymond Stauffer as Nazara CEO from 1 September 2026.

543280|2026-09.headline: Nazara Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR 803 crore (up 53% YoY) and EBITDA rose 93% to INR 120 crore, helped by Bluetile and BestPlay consolidation from 1 August 2026.

Organic gaming growth was modest at 11% revenue and 17% EBITDA, with the acquired mobile businesses doing most of the lifting. Management, under a new CEO, CFO and Executive Director, framed the next year around platform centres of excellence, AI adoption and gaming focus, and declined to give numerical growth targets. 543287|2026-06.headline: Lodha Q1 FY27 PAT more than doubled to INR 13.7 billion (26.9% margin) on land sales, while pre-sales rose only 4% to INR 46.3 billion.
543287|2026-06.overview: Revenue rose 43% YoY to INR 50 billion and adjusted EBITDA rose 79% to INR 21.5 billion at a 43% margin, with PAT of INR 13.7 billion versus INR 6.8 billion a year ago. Management said the quarter was flattered by roughly half of the year's planned land sales, including data centre park land sold to Digital Edge India at about INR 420 million per acre. Residential pre-sales were deliberately weak because about one-third of normal launches were postponed to Q2 on Middle East conflict concerns. Net debt fell by INR 4.5 billion to under INR 50 billion, with net debt to equity at about 0.2x.

segments.name: Residential (DevCo)
segments.commentary: Pre-sales of INR 46.3 billion with only one Mumbai launch (about 0.4 million sq ft); sustenance sales drove the quarter. Premium and luxury made up almost 60% of sales, and mid-income (below INR 3 crore) about 50% of the portfolio.

segments.name: Land sales
segments.commentary: Data centre and other land pre-sales of about INR 12 billion, with PAT contribution of about INR 6 billion. Management guides land sales of INR 20-30 billion a year for the next several years.

segments.name: Annuity / RentCo
segments.commentary: June exit run-rate of about INR 3 billion with no data centre contribution. Target is over INR 30 billion by FY32, including about INR 20 billion-plus from data centres, INR 6 billion from retail and office, and INR 4 billion from warehousing and industrial.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT guidance of about 20% growth on INR 34.3 billion, i.e. about INR 41 billion; Q1 delivered 33% of this. Management said 20% is an annual target and warned against annualising the quarter.
FY27 pre-sales guidance of INR 240 billion reaffirmed, with H1 at 40-42% of the full year. Q2 pre-sales expected at INR 50 billion or more, with July off to a good start.
Embedded margin excluding land sales was in the early 30s; full-year margin guidance of 32-34% retained, with no expectation of margins in the 40s.
Medium-term PAT growth of about 20% a year, taking PAT beyond INR 85 billion by FY31; ROE expected to move toward 20% from about 16% in FY26 but may not reach it.
DevCo to be net debt-free within 2-3 years; net debt to equity to stay below the 0.5x ceiling.
Pricing to rise 5-7% across micro markets over the year, with room for a further 100-200 bps.
Dividend policy of 15-20% of PAT, then debt reduction, then buyback or special dividend.
capex_capacity: Data centre park: about 660 acres at Palava, with about 3 GW of power tie-up, 5 fibre routes and 5 transmission lines. About 130 acres of the first 370-acre phase is sold; about 150 more acres are to be sold over 3-4 years at about INR 600 million per acre (about INR 90 billion).

Plan to build about 1 GW of powered shell on about 90 acres, generating over INR 20 billion of annual rent by FY32. Leasing of the first box is targeted within FY27, with physical work on the company's own box to start in calendar 2026.
Estimated capex for the power-shell infrastructure is INR 500-700 crore over time, per the CFO-level answer on infrastructure.
Power density is 11-15 MW per acre. Management does not yet plan chips or racks and sees turnkey shell at least two years away.
demand_pricing: Middle East NRI buyers are about 4-5% of sales. Management sees the impact as moderate and expects NRI and US-based buyers to shift some money toward Indian homes.
Construction cost: if energy-linked inflation persists for a full year, management expects a 1-1.5% rise in project cost (35-75 bps project EBITDA impact). Supply chain is about 95% domestic.
Conversion rate reportedly 8% or higher from July, with a long-run aim of 10%.
Sales from new cities (Pune, Bangalore, NCR, MMR) to reach 30-45% of pre-sales in the medium term.

Palava land sale price rose to about INR 420 million per acre from about INR 210 million in calendar 2025. Management puts fair market value at about INR 650 million per acre, reachable in about 18 months.
Competition described as rational. Branded share of MMR is about 30%, which management expects to reach 40-45% by the end of the decade.

qa_highlights.question: What was the value and margin of the land sales in the quarter, and how much did they add to PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,200 crore of land pre-sales including data centre land, with revenue recognised at 85-90% of that. PAT contribution was about INR 600 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the data centre rental estimate appear to fall from INR 30 billion to INR 20 billion-plus?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no change. The INR 30 billion FY32 target is unchanged, and data centres account for INR 20 billion-plus of it. Powered shell rent is a little over INR 20 million per MW a year.

qa_highlights.question: Does the pre-sales guidance factor in the Middle East war, and is there upside if it ends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact has been contained and the guidance is maintained. It will review once the conflict ends. MMR high-value sales have normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any margin outlook beyond the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Embedded margins excluding land were in the early 30s. Management said the 40s-level margin was driven by forward-loaded land sales and that the full-year guidance of early 30s stands.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is needed per acre for a data centre land sale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cost is about 10-15% of the sales price, and the CFO put group infrastructure capex at INR 500-700 crore over time. Most of the sale price flows through to cash after tax.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company compete with its data centre buyers, and what is its competitive edge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company offers powered shell, which no other provider offers, and that its advantages are land, power, recycled water, ecosystem and relationships.

risks_watch: Pre-sales were up only 4% YoY; the FY27 target of INR 240 billion requires H2 weighting, with about INR 250 billion of GDV in the launch calendar.
Land sales are lumpy and drove a large share of PAT; the 20% PAT growth target is annual, so quarterly results will vary.
Middle East conflict is prolonged. Energy-linked construction cost inflation could reach 1-1.5% if it lasts a full year.
Data centre economics depend on signed leases, which are not yet in place. Power beyond the 3 GW tie-up is still under work, and the first lease is expected within FY27.
Connectivity openings (Mulund-Airoli-Palava freeway, Upper Thane connector) are expected after the monsoon. Impact on Palava sales is expected from Q4 and meaningful mainly in FY28.

This was a decision, not an outcome.
The data center build is largely self-funded from land sales inside the same park. It does not add to group leverage, and it does not compete with our DevCo for capital in any significant manner.

543288|2026-03.headline: Deep Industries Q4 FY26 operating revenue rose 49% YoY to INR248.7 crores, but a INR208 crore Kandla receivable write-off drove the reported loss.

A gas leak at Mori-5 well (Andhra Pradesh) in January 2026 delayed production enhancement by 5 to 6 months, and the company dropped its QIP plan.

qa_highlights.question: What drove FY26 volume growth, and which capacities come online in FY27?

543299|2026-06.headline: Shyam Metalics Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23.3% YoY to INR5,455 crore and EBITDA rose 28.3% to INR812 crore, with margin at 14.9%.

Operating EBITDA was INR765 crore at a 14% margin and PAT was INR351 crore (6.4% margin), up 20.6% YoY. The company declared an interim dividend of INR1.8 per share and said the aluminium foil plant in Odisha has begun commissioning, with the aluminium flat roll project on track for Q2. Management also took a 26% stake in Emerge Green Power, a renewable energy vehicle, and shifted its solar strategy from capex to a JV-based model.

543300|2026-03.headline: Sona Comstar Q4 FY26 revenue rose 47% YoY to ₹1,272 crore, a record quarter, though EBITDA margin fell 2.7pp to 24.4%.
543300|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 posted record revenue (₹1,272 crore, +47% YoY), record EBITDA (₹311 crore, +32%) and record PAT (₹192 crore, +17%), with BEV revenue of ₹359 crore at a record 39% share. Margins compressed on commodity inflation with pass-through lag, product mix (lower-margin traction motors and railways) and a PLI income base effect. Management won four new driveline orders, including three from European OEMs in one quarter, and said Europe's EV order flow is returning. Full-year FY26 revenue grew 26% to ₹4,475 crore, with EBITDA margin at 24.7% and adjusted PAT up 11%.

segments.name: Automotive BEV
segments.commentary: Q4 BEV revenue ₹359 crore (39% share, record); FY26 BEV revenue ₹1,154 crore (-6%), weak Q1 drove the full-year decline. 67 EV programs across 35 customers, 37 in production and 30 pending.

segments.name: Traction and suspension motors
segments.commentary: Traction motors about 10% of revenue. Suspension motors expected to grow 3-4x in FY27 volumes, reaching single digit share of revenue in FY26 and possibly double digits in FY27.

segments.name: Differential gears and assemblies
segments.commentary: Legacy products kept growing alongside new products. Q4 saw 7 non-EV differential gear programs from existing customers worth about ₹3 billion.

segments.name: Railway (acquired)
segments.commentary: Lower-margin, high-return business, consolidated during FY26 and funded with about ₹1,800 crore. Q4 approvals for electric control panels (first batch supplied) and HVAC (supply to start this quarter).

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Eastern markets were 60% of Q4 revenue vs 40% a year earlier. India exceeded 50% of mix for full year FY26.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin band guided at 23-25% post railway acquisition, replacing the earlier 24-26% band for the core business.
Commodity inflation (steel, aluminium, copper, freight, packaging, energy) expected to keep pressuring margins in the foreseeable future, as pass-through lags.
Haryana minimum wage hike effective 1 April 2026 expected to add labour cost; to be offset via productivity, tighter headcount addition and workload management.
Novelic India SOP for one customer expected at end of calendar 2026; Europe in-cabin safety NCAP requirement moved to 2027.

Railway growth over 3-5 years framed through capacity/process improvement, white-space variants and new products (HVAC needs about 3 years for full rolling stock coverage; electric panels 12-15 months).
capex_capacity: FY26 capex ₹369 crore; additional land bought for about ₹110 crore.
Gas requirement cut by nearly 20% at company level via electric heating, gas-flow optimisation and process changes; no production loss so far.
Traction motor capacity of about 1 million electric motors, reusable across customers with tweaks.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

543308|2026-06.headline: KIMS Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 35.3% YoY to INR 1,180 crore, with EBITDA pre-Ind AS at INR 222 crore and debt cut to INR 2,570 crore.
543308|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total revenue of INR 1,196 crore (+36.1% YoY, +10.3% QoQ) and EBITDA of INR 240 crore at a 20.1% margin, with PAT of INR 37 crore versus INR 85 crore a year earlier. Growth was driven by IP volumes (+26.6% YoY) and OP volumes (+28.5% YoY), with the Kondapur hospital commissioned in June and Palakkad (Kerala) opened. The QIP raised INR 1,500 crore, of which INR 1,100-1,125 crore repaid debt, and a INR 600 crore promoter preferential allotment is partly pending. Management guided Telangana to 30-35% margins over time, Kerala to 20-22% in two to three years, and Bengaluru to break-even for the full year, while several new units are still ramping up.

financial_highlights.change: +20.1% YoY, +10.9% QoQ; margin vs 20.27% in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated EBITDA pre-Ind AS excluding other income

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 85 crore in Q1 FY26 and INR 33 crore in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 2,570 crore as of 30 June 2026; about INR 2,400 crore after early July repayments

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and equivalents (incl. liquid MF and deposits <12m)

segments.name: Telangana cluster (incl. Kondapur, Secunderabad)
segments.commentary: Management said revenue and EBITDA grew strongly YoY in Telangana and Andhra; Kondapur did INR 45 crore in July (first full month) against INR 32-33 crore monthly previously. Telangana occupancy is about 61% on the adjusted bed base excluding Kondapur and 200 Secunderabad beds under renovation.

segments.name: Bengaluru cluster (Mahadevapura, Electronic City)
segments.commentary: Mahadevapura reached EBITDA break-even in June and did about INR 20 crore revenue in July; Electronic City expected to break even in about one to two quarters. Management aims for zero EBITDA for the cluster for FY27. Census-bed occupancy at Mahadevapura is about 40%.

segments.name: Maharashtra (Thane, Nashik, Nagpur)
segments.commentary: Thane averaged about INR 16 crore monthly revenue in Q1 and did INR 21 crore in July at about 10% EBITDA margin. Nashik reached EBITDA break-even in Q1; Nagpur did INR 30 crore revenue in July. Empanelment delays of four to five months weighed on Q1.

segments.name: Kerala
segments.commentary: Kerala margins are in the single digits currently, with management expecting mid-teens in FY28 and 20-22% over two to three years after a 4-5% entry-cost drag. Palakkad opened, taking Kerala to three units; one more hospital (Thrissur) is due in three to four months.

segments.name: Andhra Pradesh
segments.commentary: Management said AP remains strong. Q1 ARPOB growth slowed from prior quarters (Q4 FY26 about INR 27,000), which management attributed to seasonal case mix. Cancer services were added to most AP hospitals in the last two to three months.

guidance_outlook: Telangana EBITDA margin expected to return to 30-35% over time as new Kondapur and Secunderabad beds ramp up; management said 30% is achievable by FY30 without new beds, and 70% occupancy is targeted in three to four years.
Bengaluru cluster targeted at zero EBITDA for full FY27; Bengaluru ARPOB expected to settle at INR 80,000-85,000 once empanelments complete, versus about INR 90,000+ recently.
Kondapur full potential of about INR 100 crore revenue per month (about INR 1,200 crore a year) within four to five years; model margin around 30%, with 30-32% suggested for the next two years.
ARPOB growth guidance of 4-5% per year; management called 15-16% historical growth too aggressive to model.
Maintenance capex about INR 100 crore per year for three to four years; about INR 100-125 crore growth capex over the next nine months, including Rajahmundry construction (INR 60-75 crore in FY27).
Debt-equity intended to be kept around 2.5:1; surplus cash to go to greenfield and brownfield growth in core states. Minority interest about 10.5% currently, 10-15% longer term.
Empanelment with the remaining 50% of insurers, covering Thane, Nashik and two Bengaluru assets, expected by end-August to mid-September 2026.
capex_capacity: Kondapur hospital commissioned in June 2026 (first patient 20 June); about 450-500 operational beds added in the last 10 days of Q1, and the old Kondapur hospital will run for about six more months with rent of about INR 90 lakh per month plus GST and INR 3-4 crore a year of operating cost.

Palakkad (Kerala) opened in Q1; Thrissur to commence in three to four months; Electronic City and other Bengaluru beds added at Mahadevapura (operational beds up from about 170 to 210, total cluster 280 to 340).
Secunderabad: old 250-bed facility demolished; replacement facility expected by end of next year.

Two O&M agreements (Golden Lan Solutions, Sarvottam Healthcare) approved in draft: a 300-bed Telangana hospital near Kondapur with INR 90-95 crore monthly revenue potential, and a Kakinada hospital currently at INR 7-8 crore a month, targeting INR 15-20 crore. O&M means no losses borne by KIMS.
Future pipeline: greenfield in Karnataka (300-350 beds, expandable by about 100) and acquisitions in Maharashtra, Kerala, Telangana and Andhra; timing and bed count not committed.

qa_highlights.question: Kerala cost increase and steady-state margin, plus whether the Q1 ARPOB jump is structural or seasonal.
qa_highlights.answer: Kerala is in growth phase; single-digit EBITDA margin now, mid-teens next financial year, and 20-22% over two to three years after a 4-5% entry-cost drag. Management said ARPP is the better metric; ARPOB moves with seasonal case mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why Telangana occupancy sits around 50-52% and whether it can rise further.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bed count includes 250 demolished Secunderabad beds not yet operational; ex-Kondapur and ex-200 renovating beds occupancy is about 61%. 70% is achievable in three to four years without new beds.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost impact after the INR 1,100 crore debt repayment.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said QIP proceeds arrived around 24 June and debt was repaid on 27-28 June, so the interest saving was not in Q1 and will show from Q2. Debt was INR 2,570 crore at 30 June, about INR 2,400 crore after early July repayments.

qa_highlights.question: Kondapur losses, pre-operative costs and status of the old hospital.
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-operative costs about INR 1.5-2 crore a month; Q1 losses marginal. Old hospital runs about six more months at about INR 90 lakh a month rent plus GST and INR 3-4 crore a year operating cost.

qa_highlights.question: Thane ramp-up lagging peers and when it turns breakeven.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q1 weakness to a four-to-five-month empanelment delay and seasonality. Thane averaged about INR 16 crore monthly in Q1 and did INR 21 crore in July at about 10% margin; a healthy margin is expected if the trend holds.

qa_highlights.question: Telangana margin: why 30% guidance versus historical 35% peaks.
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 30-35% over time, citing FY25-26 margins of about 31%, Secunderabad at 34-35% and Q4 FY26 Telangana at 38-39%. Return to 30%-plus will take time as new beds ramp.

demand_pricing: IP volumes 72,493 (+26.6% YoY, +14% QoQ); OP volumes 6,58,617 (+28.5% YoY, +8% QoQ); management cited FY25-based annual growth of 15.4% for IP and 25.4% for OP.
Average revenue per operating bed +9.7% YoY and +0.1% QoQ; ARPP +6.8% YoY and -3.8% QoQ. Management said ARPP is the better indicator, as ARPOB moves with ALOS and seasonal case mix.

Kondapur commissioned with first patient on 20 June 2026; July (first full month) revenue about INR 45 crore versus INR 32-33 crore monthly previously. Management said Kondapur full potential is about INR 100 crore per month within four to five years.

Bengaluru ARPOB running at INR 90,000+ for two quarters; management guided INR 80,000-85,000 once empanelments complete, with ARPP said to be similar to Telangana. Mahadevapura census-bed occupancy about 40%.

Telangana occupancy about 61% excluding Kondapur and 200 Secunderabad beds under renovation; management targets 70% in three to four years without new beds, and said about 65% on a prior adjusted basis was also cited. ARPOB growth guided at 4-5% a year; management called 15-16% too aggressive.

Insurance empanelment: about 50% of insurers done; remaining 50% covering Thane, Nashik and two Bengaluru assets expected by end-August to mid-September 2026. Maharashtra Q1 hit by four-to-five-month empanelment delay; Thane July revenue INR 21 crore at about 10% EBITDA margin.
risks_watch: Empanelment: remaining 50% of insurers, covering Thane, Nashik and two Bengaluru assets, due by end-August to mid-September 2026; the Joint Insurance Committee common-empanelment process is unresolved.
Ramp-up of new units: Electronic City breakeven guided in one to two quarters; Thane margin and Kerala single-digit margins still weak.
Bengaluru ARPOB may fall from INR 90,000+ toward INR 80,000-85,000 as empanelments complete.
Telangana occupancy about 61% on the adjusted base; Secunderabad 250-bed replacement not due until end of next year, and the 200 renovating beds are excluded from the base.
Government receivables improving but not fully on time; management said loss funding dropped only a little in Q1.
Acquisitions and greenfield timing not committed; management declined to quantify bed additions for FY28-29 and said the O&M deals (Golden Lan, Sarvottam) are draft-stage.
key_quotes: The first month has been very promising. We grew by almost 40% in less than a month.
As far as Telangana is concerned, we do not see any reason why we cannot ramp up to 70%, in spite of the new Kondapur hospital and the new Secunderabad hospital over the next three to four years.
I think it is too aggressive. Four to five is a good number.
Most likely it will get invested for greenfield and brownfield growth.
543308|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on cluster trajectories and Telangana margins, with management reiterating 30-35% over time and a 70% occupancy target. Cautious and non-committal on acquisition and greenfield timing, and on the ARPOB and empanelment outcomes, which it tied to uncontrolled external factors.

543311|2026-03.headline: India Pesticides FY26 revenue rose 27.9% to INR 1,078 crore and PAT 45.8% to INR 120 crore; Q4 domestic sales up over 50% to INR 183 crore.
543311|2026-03.overview: FY26 crossed INR 1,000 crore revenue for the first time, with EBITDA up 44.7% to INR 194 crore at an 18% margin. Q4 growth was driven by domestic herbicides and intermediates (domestic INR 183 crore vs INR 118 crore), while Q4 exports fell to INR 84 crore from INR 89 crore on geopolitical disruption and pricing pressure. Management said raw material and freight inflation is being partly passed to customers, with sulphur-based inputs seeing the largest increases. Management reiterated the INR 3,000 crore revenue target for March 2031 and guided FY27 revenue growth of 15-20% with EBITDA margin of 18-20%. Dividend was held at INR 0.75, which drew pushback from an individual investor.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 118 crore in Q4 FY25 (>50%)
vs INR 89 crore in Q4 FY25 (decline)

segments.name: Technicals
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 744 crore. Pretilachlor and PEDA intermediates drove volume growth after backward integration; the combined plant capacity is about 8,500 MT, running at an expected 70-75% utilisation with a 3-month seasonal shutdown around Aug-Oct.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 311 crore. Capacity scaled to 10,000 MT, with distribution across 18 states through 24 depots and over 340 sales personnel.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 exports INR 408 crore (about 39% of revenue) across more than 35 countries. Q4 exports were INR 84 crore, down from INR 89 crore on geopolitical issues in March 2026.

segments.commentary: First technical product started with about INR 4-5 crore revenue in FY26. Management expects at least INR 25 crore in FY27 from this molecule and guides total Shalvis revenue of INR 70-80 crore in FY27 including a second block expected by Sep-Oct 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20%.
FY27 EBITDA margin projected at 18-20%; management said 18% holds for the year.
INR 3,000 crore revenue target reiterated for March 2031, with Shalvis contributing about INR 1,000 crore and existing plants (Dewa Road, Sandila, formulations) about INR 2,000 crore.
Net working capital days could improve by a further 10-12 days by FY27, though inventory levels are rising as customers now buy on spot basis.
FY27 capex: INR 45 crore for India Pesticides and INR 90 crore for the subsidiary, mainly funded by internal accruals; a small loan may be taken at the subsidiary.
PEDA and Pretilachlor FY27 volumes expected to be better than FY26 with full utilisation of the capacity commissioned in March 2026.
risks_watch: Raw material and freight inflation tied to Middle East tensions and sulphur-based inputs; ability to keep passing costs to customers.
Export softness from geopolitical disruption and pricing pressure in certain exported products (Q4 exports down YoY).

Competition and margin pressure as new domestic producers enter Pretilachlor/PEDA.
Execution of the Shalvis second block by Sep-Oct 2026 and the Hamirpur new molecules, both key to the INR 3,000 crore by FY31 target.
Management did not state a cause for the paraquat substitution question; no product confirmed as a substitute.
Working capital pressure from higher inventory and dividend payout versus the 5-15% policy; credit rating review in September 2026.

Several answers were vague on quantification (price increases, incremental revenue, Hamirpur timing), and the dividend response was defensive.
key_quotes: A key milestone during the year was India Pesticides Limited crossing the INR 1,000 crores revenue mark for the first time, reflecting the company's strong execution capabilities and expanding market presence.
We have done some long-term arrangements with some of our suppliers who are able to bring the material to us in time.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked how much price increase had been taken across the portfolio and whether demand is holding up because of inventory running out or China price hikes.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said China is also raising prices and the company has passed on some cost differential, with customers accepting increases for some products; an average across the portfolio was not given because sulphur-based products rose more and need more discussion with customers.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about Shalvis and Pretilachlor/PEDA contribution in FY26 and expectations for FY27, including the second Shalvis block.
qa_highlights.answer: Shalvis contributed about INR 4-5 crore in FY26 (CFO repeated INR 4 crore); FY27 at least INR 25 crore from the first molecule and total Shalvis revenue INR 70-80 crore including the second block expected by September-October 2026. PEDA and Pretilachlor volumes expected to be better than FY26 with full use of capacity commissioned in March; no incremental revenue figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked for FY27 EBITDA margin guidance and working capital trajectory.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided EBITDA margin of 18-20%; net working capital days at 223 could improve by about 10-12 days by FY27, though inventory must rise as customers now buy on spot basis rather than quarterly planning.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the INR 68 crore capital work in progress and the INR 27 crore subsidiary term loan, plus cost of funds.
qa_highlights.answer: Of the INR 68 crore CWIP, INR 18 crore is at India Pesticides and most is at Shalvis, to be capitalised once the second Shalvis plant is operational; the term loan of about INR 27 crore at the subsidiary costs about 8%, and working capital borrowing is about 7.2-7.3% (50 bps over FDR). Credit rating is A+ and due for review in September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked whether the INR 3,000 crore FY31 target is intact and how it breaks down between Shalvis and existing plants.
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed the INR 3,000 crore target for March 2031; Shalvis expected to contribute about INR 1,000 crore and existing Dewa Road, Sandila and formulation plants about INR 2,000 crore. Management also said IMD forecasts 6-8% below-normal rainfall but production has held in past deficit years.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the dividend of INR 0.75 relative to profit and whether a higher payout or buyback is possible.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the dividend policy is 5-15% of net profit and the company chose to keep the existing payout to fund subsidiary capex and working capital from internal accruals; CEO said small dividend increases would not materially change investor returns and the focus is on revenue and profit growth.

capex_capacity: FY27 capex budget: INR 45 crore for India Pesticides standalone and INR 90 crore for the 100% subsidiary Shalvis, mainly funded through internal accruals; a small loan may be taken at the subsidiary.

Shalvis: first technical product started with about INR 4-5 crore revenue in FY26; at least INR 25 crore expected in FY27 from that molecule plus two more molecules this year; second block expected operational by September-October 2026; total Shalvis revenue guided at INR 70-80 crore in FY27.

Hamirpur facility: development work progressing with infrastructure and operational blocks; two entirely new molecules targeted this year, primarily for export; management expects about 10% share of a herbicide market it says is large, though no timeline or market size in rupees was given.

Sandila site is full with no space for expansion; FY27 plan is one intermediate and one technical-grade product there plus balancing equipment to augment capacity, hence lower capex. Q4 capital work in progress was INR 68 crore, of which INR 18 crore at India Pesticides and the balance mainly at Shalvis; part to capitalise in Q4 FY27 and the rest in FY27-28.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 domestic sales rose more than 50% YoY to INR 183 crore (from INR 118 crore), driven by herbicides and intermediates; management cited about 30% volume growth in the quarter.

Q4 exports were INR 84 crore vs INR 89 crore; management said exports were about 5% lower QoQ and attributed the dip to geopolitical issues in March 2026 and pricing pressure in certain products. FY26 exports INR 408 crore (about 39% of revenue) across more than 35 countries.

Price increases taken to pass on raw material and freight costs; management could not give an average increase across the portfolio, said sulphur-based inputs rose more, and said some customers agreed to pass-through while prices are expected to hold in coming months.

Pretilachlor and PEDA: management said domestic production now fully replaces imports after antidumping duty; new capacity expected to cover Indian requirement, leaving room for one or two new producers; margins on these products are slightly below company average but expected to hold.
Japanese partner forecast for FY27 and FY28 about 30% higher than last year; one more molecule sample submitted and awaiting feedback.
Management said China is also raising prices, the company is seeing supply-chain strain from Middle East tensions, and demand is described as okay with limited price variation for these molecules.

543311|2026-06.headline: India Pesticides Q1 FY27 revenue fell 9.2% YoY to INR 256 crore and EBITDA margin to 15.4%, on weak domestic Pretilachlor demand from erratic rains.

543318|2026-03.headline: Clean Science Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 8% QoQ to INR193 crore with 46% EBITDA margin; FY26 standalone revenue fell 12% to about INR796 crore.
543318|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8% QoQ to about INR193 crore on volume recovery, with EBITDA of INR88 crore (46% margin) and PAT of INR77 crore (40%), but revenue fell 19% YoY. For FY26, standalone revenue declined 12% from INR900 crore to INR796 crore, attributed to loss of an FMCG key account (4-MAP), lower offtake and pricing pressure. Consolidated Q4 revenue rose 14% to about INR246 crore, led by HALS (Clean Fino-Chem), with EBITDA of INR96 crore (33%) and PAT of INR58 crore. Management said Clean Fino-Chem reached its first positive EBITDA (INR7 crore) and that the Hydroquinone/Catechol plant is still stabilising at about 10-15% utilisation.

segments.commentary: Contributed 19% of FY26 standalone revenue. The pharma intermediate plant was refurbished for HALS intermediates, and the older pharma intermediate was dropped.

Subsidiary EBITDA margin was about 15% in Q4 versus about 1% in Q3.

Management said it is not pencilling in any price hikes; it expects to benefit in an inflationary environment, as it did in FY23.

Anisole: management said it is the largest producer and consumer globally and India; competition from China does not affect its sales, as anisole is mainly used captively.

Management declined to share product-wise revenue, geographic split, or product-level volumes, citing competitive sensitivity.

543318|2026-06.headline: Clean Science Q1 FY27 consolidated sales hit a record INR264 crore (+10% YoY, +7% QoQ), with standalone EBITDA at INR87 crore (43% margin).

Standalone revenue rose 5% QoQ to INR203 crore on realisation gains, while standalone sales fell 6% YoY on volume loss from raw-material and shipping disruptions, including about two weeks of production stoppage. HALS is now 22% of sales and legacy top-4 products fell to 60% of sales from 85% in Q4 FY23. Management announced a Geneus Chem (Swiss) collaboration for advanced NOR HALS and a 5-year Kemin supply contract, and said CFCL became operationally self-sustaining.

qa_highlights.question: What drove HALS volume and pricing, and is the INR250-300 crore annual run-rate comfortable?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume about 1,000 tonnes in Q1; average price rose from about INR440 to INR550/kg on mix shift (HALS 770 share fell from about 50% to 35%). Management said the INR250-300 crore annualised run-rate is comfortable.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 43-45% HALS gross margin sustainable, or helped by cheap acetone?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no real benefit from cheap raw material; margins came from higher grades and operational efficiencies, and should be sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Geneus Chem transaction and its revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Tech transfer for NOR HALS with no transfer fee or royalty (capex only); joint, co-branded marketing with geographic split. Management guided INR300-350 crore additional revenue cumulatively over 3-4 years, separate from direct sales outside the partner.

qa_highlights.question: What was the cause of the YoY decline in legacy volumes, and will volumes recover in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Propylene shortage at a primary Indian supplier forced about two weeks of shutdown. Management said volumes are not an issue now; raw material pricing and shipping availability remain challenges.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Kemin and Geneus deals preempt new entrants?

Quality growth, which meaningfully also takes the business towards profitability and sustainability, that is the only non-negotiable here.
We are not, therefore, constraining ourselves in a certain way of thinking about the business.
The objective is to optimize for growth of absolute profit and not the profit margin percentage.

543320|2026-06.headline: Eternal's Blinkit quick commerce guides long-term EBIT margin to top of range, now 6%, with Q1 flagged as peak competitive intensity.
543320|2026-06.overview: Management spoke almost entirely to Blinkit (quick commerce), with questions also covering food delivery, Bistro, District, Nugget and payables. Management said competition is high but more predictable because it is now mostly subsidies on products and delivery fees, and that discount-led growth is unsustainable. Blinkit net order value (NOV) growth was described as robust, with NAOV expected to stay flat year on year. Management declined to guide Q2 volume growth, and said current EBIT margin is negative, so there is no ROCE yet. The call did not give reported quarterly financial figures beyond those cited in questions.

segments.commentary: Dining-out and movies are the largest categories, with retail stores and events the more promising newer ones. Customer base is smaller than food delivery or quick commerce, with fewer cities and higher NAOV.

Blinkit NAOV is flat YoY. Management said mix, assortment and price matching drive NAOV, and it is not a focus metric.
Blinkit retention and cohort spend: older cohorts spend about 3x versus three years earlier, mostly through frequency; the figure covers the full cohort, including churned customers.
Blinkit growth is mostly from existing cities; non-metros are growing faster on a smaller base.
Quick commerce MTU pareto is much flatter than food delivery (top 15-18% of customers drive 80% of revenue in food delivery).
Management said the pricing-led strategy is not sustainable, and that discounting is less effective in quick commerce than in e-commerce due to limited shelf space in dark stores.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise the quick commerce long-term margin guidance to 6% amid competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshant Goyal said capex per store and efficiency gains, plus larger store sizes, give higher margin visibility, so the company expects to finish at the higher end of the earlier range.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 the peak of competitive intensity, and what does predictability mean?
qa_highlights.answer: Albinder Singh Dhindsa said Q1 was the peak seen to date because more players were aggressive. Competition now mainly takes the form of product and delivery-fee subsidies, which he said cannot go much deeper without large losses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Blinkit AOV fall for two quarters, and will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the drop is in line with last year and mostly reflects category mix and price matching. NAOV is an outcome, flat YoY, and not expected to grow meaningfully. Q3 may rise on seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Blinkit contribution margin not rise with take rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher minimum wages in several states and larger new stores with lower early contribution. Q1 last-mile costs are seasonally high, and YoY gross profit gains have largely flowed to contribution.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Blinkit capex around INR 700 crore for 200 stores when the stated capex per store is INR 2.5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshant Goyal said warehouse capex is lumpy, so the per-store figure should be read over 6-9 months or longer. Over those periods capex per store is below INR 2.5 crore, and management expects that to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the net working capital reduction to 14 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshant Goyal said lower inventory days, from better replenishment and throughput, drove the cut from 18 to 14 days, with a steady-state target of 12 days. Kunal Swarup said the Q1 OCF lift came from a one-off tax refund on higher advance tax.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the slight dip in food delivery restaurant count?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshant Goyal attributed the dip to the LPG situation last quarter, which took some restaurants offline. He did not cite rationalisation.

risks_watch: Competition from Toing and Ownly in food delivery, and quick commerce subsidy intensity, which could put pressure on margins or MTU growth.
Q2 Blinkit volume trends, since no guidance was given; the analyst's historical 18-20% 1Q-to-2Q range was not addressed.
Blinkit contribution margin trajectory as store formats and minimum wages change; Q1 was described as seasonally weak.
Inventory losses held at about 1.8% of NOV, with management not expecting much improvement.

Nugget losses (manpower-driven) and limited disclosure; Bistro is expanding cautiously, with unit economics still being proven.
Payables growth (about INR 1,650 crore QoQ increase) and whether terms with brands are improving; management said it is scale-driven.

543320|2026-09.headline: Eternal's Q2FY27 call was Q&A-only: management kept FY29 $1B Adjusted EBITDA guidance and flagged food margins flat for 1-2 years while reinvesting in growth.

Management said competitive intensity in food delivery rose in Q2 and that Eternal is investing more in customer acquisition and frequency, with margins expected to stay broadly flat over the next 1-2 years. In quick commerce, management said the 12-month competitive spike is over, which gives it confidence to re-accelerate store expansion, mainly in smaller cities, starting October-December quarter. Management also discussed dark.ai, a privacy-focused AI application for power users, which is unmonetised and carried in the Others segment.

qa_highlights.question: Why accelerate quick commerce store additions in FY28, and where?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Blinkit contribution margin trend despite NOV per store rising?

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY29 $1B Adjusted EBITDA guidance more comfortable given better competition visibility?

543321|2026-03.headline: Tatva Chintan Q4 FY26 operating revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,341 million, with EBITDA of INR281 million (about 21% margin); FY27 guidance held at ~25% growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin.
543321|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue was INR1,341 million, up 24% YoY and 2% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR281 million, up 214% YoY and 10% QoQ, which management attributed to better product mix and operating leverage. Electrolyte Salts was the standout segment, at INR131 million (up 1,378% YoY), while PTC fell 20% YoY and PASC fell 24% QoQ on dispatch delays after the new Dahej block was commissioned. Management maintained FY27 guidance of about 25% revenue growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin despite raw-material and freight cost inflation linked to the geopolitical conflict, which is being partly passed on to customers. The Jolva greenfield project is set to break ground within about 60 days, with commercial production targeted for early 2028.

Q4 revenue was INR1,926 million (about 4% YoY, about 7% QoQ), EBITDA INR559 million at 29% margin, and Q4 reported PAT about INR417 million (over 101% YoY). Management said Q4 profit was supported by a roughly INR222 million Apulki valuation gain, and receivable days fell to 139 from 155 in Q3. Rajasthan PPP contributed nothing this quarter and is guided to start from Q1 FY27, with an annual revenue range of INR100–150 crore that was below the earlier INR250–300 crore aspiration.

ROCE fell to 16% (18% excluding capital work in progress) and net debt/EBITDA rose to 0.8x. Management announced a Board-approved INR600 crore plan for an epoxy resin and formulations plant (125,000 tpa) and a multipurpose plant (MPP).

+25% vs adjusted PAT of INR79 crore in Q1 FY26; Q1 FY26 reported PAT INR160 crore incl. INR81 crore deferred tax

segments.name: Chlor-alkali (caustic soda/ECU)
segments.commentary: Caustic soda capacity utilisation about 75% in Q1 FY27. ECU realisation about INR35,000-36,000 in Q1, easing to about INR31,000-32,000 currently; chlorine realisation about negative INR4,000.

segments.name: Epichlorohydrin (ECH)
segments.commentary: ECH utilisation about 70-75% in Q1. Current ECH realisation about INR180-185/t, down from INR200-210 during the war-time peak. Capacity expansion from 50,000 to 100,000 tpa is progressing on time and within budget, with commissioning expected in a couple of months.

segments.name: CPVC
segments.commentary: CPVC utilisation about 50-55% in Q1 as pipe customers managed PVC inventory amid volatility. Realisation about INR110-115/kg currently. Management expects demand to pick up from Q3 with monsoon seasonality; a 75,000 tpa expansion is underway.

segments.name: Chlorotoluenes / chloromethanes / peroxide
segments.commentary: Chloromethanes running about 100%; hydrogen peroxide about 85-90%. Chlorotoluenes capex of about INR250 crore done; expected revenue INR300-350 crore at optimum level, with the combined chlorotoluene and MPP top line targeted at INR700-800 crore.

guidance_outlook: Long-term growth target of 15-20% CAGR over 3-5 years in top line and bottom line, with an internal aspiration of about 20%.
Epoxy and MPP projects together: peak revenue of INR1,300-1,500 crore once plants reach optimum levels; ROCE target about 20%, with margins lower than the existing 22-24% range.
Capex of about INR400 crore each in FY27 and FY28; the INR600 crore epoxy and MPP project funded about 40% internally and 60% debt.
Pilot facility for epoxy and MPP expected to be operational by September 2026 (Q2 FY27); MPP completion targeted in FY28.
Chlorotoluene and MPP derivatives target of INR500 crore revenue within about three years, with ramp-up likely in FY29-FY30.
Tax rate expected at about 25%.
capex_capacity: Epoxy resin and formulations: 125,000 tpa, with more than 50% of raw material value sourced internally (ECH and caustic soda). Management said LER will be a smaller share of the mix.

Multipurpose plant (MPP) for chlorotoluene and ECH downstream derivatives (pharma/agrochemical intermediates, water treatment chemicals); the combined epoxy and MPP project is INR600 crore, with no split given.
ECH capacity doubling from 50,000 to 100,000 tpa; post-expansion, about 50% of ECH is to be consumed in-house and 50% sold.
CPVC expansion of 75,000 tpa underway, progressing on schedule and within budget.
Power: no further captive power plant; energy to come from long-term solar and wind hybrid contracts (two 20 MW contracts).
demand_pricing: Epoxy demand estimated at 2.5-3 lakh tonnes, expected to grow at double-digit rates; management expects export opportunities to Europe after an India-EU FTA.
Caustic: management expects India to remain a net importer given alumina capacity growth; short-term oversupply risk for a couple of years.

CPVC: management said near-term overcapacity is likely as Grasim and others add capacity; pricing of CPVC is about INR110-115/kg and ethylene-based PVC pricing is not expected to be materially affected by the recent MIP.
Glycerin/ECH: management said glycerin prices are driven by palm oil and biodiesel policy as well as crude and propylene, and that ECH prices are volatile.
Management said the 2.5-3 lakh tonne epoxy demand is growing at double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Is the epoxy capacity announcement mainly LER or does it include value-added products, and what is the market size split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 125,000 tpa capacity includes LER plus value-added and formulations, with LER a smaller share of the mix. Epoxy demand is estimated at 2.5-3 lakh tonnes, growing at double-digit rates, with Europe seen as an export opportunity after an India-EU FTA.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Q1 FY27 and Q4 FY26 ECU realisations and utilisation levels?
qa_highlights.answer: ECU was about INR35,000-36,000/t in Q1 FY27 and about INR30,000 in Q4 FY26, easing to about INR31,000-32,000 currently. Utilisation was about 75% for caustic soda, 70-75% for ECH, 50-55% for CPVC, about 100% for chloromethanes and 85-90% for peroxide.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of the INR600 crore capex between epoxy and MPP, and peak revenue from both projects?
qa_highlights.answer: No split was given; the INR600 crore is a combined figure. Peak revenue from both projects together is expected at INR1,300-1,500 crore once plants reach optimum levels, with ROCE targeted around 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the epoxy margin dilution change the 22-24% combined margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said epoxy margins will be lower in percentage terms because turnover per unit of investment is about 3-4x that of the existing portfolio. Project evaluation focuses on ROCE, which epoxy still meets.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR600 crore project mean peak total revenue of INR4,000-4,500 crore, given current revenue of about INR2,500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management rejected that reading. It said existing capacity can still ramp up and the ECH and CPVC expansions are due in a couple of months, and that epoxy and MPP together add INR1,300-1,500 crore at peak.

qa_highlights.question: What growth rate should be expected and is the target on top line or bottom line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 15-20% CAGR over 3-5 years, with an internal aspiration of about 20%, for both top line and bottom line.

qa_highlights.question: How do the CPVC and PVC pricing respond to the recent MIP, and what is the outlook for CPVC demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the MIP mainly hit carbide-based PVC, not the ethylene-based PVC Epigral uses, so no major impact is expected. CPVC realisation is about INR110-115/kg. Demand is expected to pick up from Q3 with monsoon seasonality, though near-term overcapacity is likely as new capacity comes on.

qa_highlights.question: What are the chlorotoluenes and MPP capex, revenue and margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Chlorotoluenes capex of about INR250 crore is done, with expected revenue of INR300-350 crore at optimum. Including MPP, the combined top line is targeted at INR700-800 crore, at an estimated margin of about 22-23%, with 1.5-2 years to optimum utilisation.

risks_watch: Epoxy and MPP margins will be lower than the 22-24% range, with ROCE of about 20% the stated offset; the margin trajectory of the combined business is not guided numerically.
CPVC overcapacity as Grasim and others add capacity, with utilisation at 50-55% in Q1 FY27 and a demand recovery expected only from Q3.
Caustic oversupply risk for a couple of years from domestic capacity additions, with utilisation at about 75% and ECU easing from INR35,000-36,000 to INR31,000-32,000/t.
ECH realisation fell from INR200-210/kg at the war-time peak to about INR180-185/t currently; ECH and glycerin prices are volatile, linked to crude, propylene and biodiesel policy.
Execution: the pilot facility is due by September 2026, ECH capacity doubling to 100,000 tpa and the 75,000 tpa CPVC expansion are due in a couple of months, and the MPP is targeted for FY28.
Leverage and returns: net debt/EBITDA rose to 0.8x from 0.6x, ROCE fell to 16% from 24%, and the INR600 crore project is 60% debt-funded.
Capex of about INR400 crore each in FY27 and FY28 keeps balance-sheet strain and the ROCE trajectory in focus.
key_quotes: Quarter 1 FY27 presented a highly challenging operating environment across all the segments, including chemicals.
Even against this volatile backdrop Epigral demonstrated a resilience, delivering a revenue growth of 15% and EBITDA margin of 25%.
So definitely, EBITDA margin in terms of percentage, definitely, it is coming lower.
Rather than giving guidance on margin, I can tell you that ROCE, we are targeting in the range of 20%.
