543333|2026-03.headline: CarTrade Q4 FY26 PAT rose 54% YoY to INR70.8 crore; FY26 PAT INR243 crore (+68%), with management targeting INR1,000 crore profit in 4-5 years.
543333|2026-03.overview: CarTrade reported a strong Q4 FY26 with consolidated EBITDA up 55% and margin at 35% for the quarter, and FY26 revenue up 22% with EBITDA margin at 33%. Consumer group (CarWale, BikeWale) grew revenue 25% in the quarter and 30% for the year. OLX India total income grew 16% in the quarter, below the ~18% of the prior quarter, which drew repeated analyst questions. Management pointed to new OLX monetisation products (Elite Buyer, Verification, Super Dost) as the next growth driver, but disclosed that these were still insignificant in revenue terms (under 5% of FY26 revenue).

financial_highlights.change: up 54% YoY; first time above INR70 crore in a quarter
about INR300 crore added in FY26
EBITDA +96%, PAT +55% (aided by higher deferred tax provisions)

financial_highlights.value: INR1.7 million listings; about 3 lakh volumes

segments.name: Consumer group (CarWale, BikeWale)
segments.commentary: Revenue +30% for FY26 and +25% in Q4; FY26 EBITDA margin about 38% per analyst, and management said margin will expand in FY27. Revenue split is roughly 70% OEM and 30% dealer.

segments.name: Remarketing (Shriram Automall)
segments.commentary: Revenue +22% in both FY26 and Q4; FY26 margin 28%, PAT +66%. Around 130 auction sites. Value-added and inspection fees are mostly auction-linked; inspection is under 10% of fees.

segments.name: OLX India
segments.commentary: Q4 total income +16% YoY, below the prior quarter's ~18%; FY26 +22%. Margin rose from 23% to 31%. Elite Buyer and Verification contributed under 5% of FY26 revenue. Employee cost up 4% for the year to INR73-75 crore, and total cost up 1%.

guidance_outlook: Management gave no numerical guidance for FY27 revenue, PAT or quarterly growth; it declined to comment on a INR350 crore FY27 PAT figure raised by an analyst.
Long-term goal: take PAT from INR243 crore to about INR1,000 crore (roughly 4x) within 4-5 years.
Consumer group EBITDA margin expected to expand in FY27; management said margins across all businesses will expand in the current year and costs should be broadly stable.

Management expects Elite Buyer and Verification to become significant revenue lines in FY27, with impact visible from Q1 or Q2 FY27; management said April trends were better than other months but gave no quantified figure.
Management expects new cash generation of around INR300 crore per year for 2-3 years; cash return to shareholders is possible in 2-3 years, subject to tax shelter and carry-forward loss rules.
capex_capacity: Shriram Automall: about 130 physical auction sites; the company is building new supply sources, including a trade-in partnership with one OEM for commercial vehicles and a farm equipment push.
Elite Buyer agent suite (matchmaking, pricing, negotiation, condition check) is at various stages of rollout; Super Dost instant-sale tool for dealers launched about 30 days before the call.
Verification product launched in the last weeks of Q4 FY26, about 45 days later than planned.
Financing product for used-vehicle buyers and marketplace dealer financing (on transaction turnover of about INR4,000-5,000 crore) are under development; no timelines given.
demand_pricing: Industry: car industry grew about 20% in April 2026 and steep growth was seen over the prior seven months, helped by GST rate cuts on cars and bikes.
OLX: about 31 million monthly users; CarWale/BikeWale about 50 million; about 2 million monthly used-car buyers and sellers; buyers outnumber sellers six to one.
Dealer pricing described as largely static; growth comes from volume and relevance, with inflationary price increases only.
Traffic: management said traffic grew YoY in Q4, with Q3 seasonally the highest quarter; the company said about 95% of traffic is organic.
Advertising revenue is insignificant: under 5% in CarWale, under 10% at OLX, and nil at Shriram Automall (per management).
Management said the OLX Q4 slowdown reflected two fewer days in the quarter and a later Verification launch.

qa_highlights.question: Why did OLX growth slow from about 18% to 15.5-16% QoQ despite guidance of stronger momentum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to two fewer days in the quarter, typical October-December seasonality, and Verification launching about 45 days later than planned. It said it was more optimistic than last quarter, with no change in outlook.

qa_highlights.question: What share of OLX revenue comes from Elite Buyer and Verification, and how big could it become in three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Elite Buyer and Verification were under 5% of FY26 revenue. Management said they will become significant in FY27 but gave no sizing; it said the revenue could be more than 30-40% over time, with no ceiling.

qa_highlights.question: How has the remarketing mix (repossession vs retail) and value-added fee share changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said institutional (repossession) volumes are not cyclical and both segments should keep growing. Inspection fees are under 10% of revenue; other fees are mostly auction-linked. Financing is a planned new fee line.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI or ChatGPT-style search threaten the traffic and consumer business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said traffic has grown as search has grown, that proprietary data, OEM/dealer integrations and brand give defensibility, and that AI is a net opportunity for the company.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ROE about 10% and what is the plan for the cash of about INR1,244 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cash balance is the main reason for the low ROE. Returning cash or M&A is possible in 2-3 years once tax shelters and loss carry-forwards allow; no specific M&A is in view.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company plan any acquisitions, such as the AutoMall stake?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is nothing to report on M&A or cash utilisation; it has done three major acquisitions and remains open to strategic deals with synergy value and reasonable valuation.

risks_watch: OLX growth decelerated to about 16% in Q4 from about 18% in Q3, and management has repeatedly pushed monetisation timing out; watch Q1 FY27 OLX growth and Elite Buyer/Verification revenue disclosure.
AI-led search and assistants (ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode) could divert traffic or lead to direct dealer dealings; management disputed this but gave no quantified traffic data.
Consumer and remarketing growth relies on auto industry momentum (post-GST cut); management said steep cost pressures were noted across the industry.
Cash of INR1,244 crore and ROE of about 10%: capital allocation (M&A vs returns) remains undecided and tax-constrained for 2-3 years.
Management guidance is largely qualitative; no FY27 revenue or PAT target was given.

543334|2026-03.headline: Nuvoco posted record FY26 volume of 20.4 Mt and Q4 EBITDA of INR590 crore, but guided Q1 fuel cost to INR1.51-1.55/mn kcal and ~INR200/t cost inflation.
543334|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 volume of 20.4 million tons and EBITDA of INR1,881 crore, with Q4 the first 6 Mt quarter and a record quarterly EBITDA of INR590 crore. Price hikes of INR8-12/bag (trade) and INR10-15/bag (non-trade) were taken in April to offset fuel, packaging and gypsum inflation. Management said the hikes only just cover current cost inflation, leaving a gap of roughly INR200/t against the full cost increase. Net debt rose to INR4,445 crore at FY26-end, driven by the Vadraj acquisition, CCD and VEGL investments.

financial_highlights.change: first time a quarter crossed 6 Mt
vs INR3,640 crore at start of FY26; Dec-25 INR4,817 crore

segments.name: East
segments.commentary: Accounts for over 70% of sales; C/K ratio above 2.1; petcoke share targeted down from ~25% to below 20% at Arasmeta and Sonadih and from 35% to below 30% at Risda. East debottlenecking of ~4 Mtpa (1 Mt from debottlenecking at four plants) is nearing completion.

segments.name: North

April packaging bag cost up ~INR100/t (granule price moved from INR99/kg in February to INR155/kg); May-June outlook uncertain.

AFR share targeted to rise from ~10% to above 13% in FY27.

Kutch clinker unit: equipment upgrades and electrical panel testing underway; Kutch grinding unit civil works and VRM installation progressing.
East debottlenecking (~4 Mtpa, 1 Mt from four plants): Jojobera and Panagarh hardware done, awaiting CTO; Jajpur in 2-3 months; Arasmeta by end-2026; full completion expected by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for East debottlenecking given earlier plan for end-FY26/FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Current kcal cost and Q1/Q2 fuel outlook?

qa_highlights.question: Packaging cost impact in March and April, and petcoke flexibility?

qa_highlights.question: Are April price hikes sustainable through monsoon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is fairly confident hikes will hold near term if cost inflation stops; further inflation would be passed on, and it is not 1-to-1 pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt rose in Q4 and FY26 — why?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: FY26 net debt rose INR900 crore to INR4,445 crore due to Vadraj (INR1,800 crore) and VEGL (INR200 crore) investments, offset by INR900 crore CCD. Chairman-level comment: like-for-like debt fell ~INR300 crore from operations.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 capex and debt guidance?

qa_highlights.question: FY27 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry growth 7-9%; Nuvoco aims to match it, with North at ~95% utilisation and possible cement shortfall in North for some months after Vadraj until commissioning.

And hence, at INR200 per ton with the kind of price increase, net of GST, there is still going to be some gap.
We will not drop price to increase market share.
Our goal has been to maintain that debt level to 2 x to 2.5x EBITDA.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 fuel cost guided up to INR1.51-1.55 from INR1.44, April packaging cost up ~INR100/t, mineral gypsum up ~INR20/t and total inflation ~INR200/t against price hikes that only partly cover it; management declined to quantify the gap or the diesel impact.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: East debottlenecking (~4 Mtpa, 1 Mt from four plants) is hardware-complete at Jojobera and Panagarh awaiting CTO, Jajpur in 2-3 months, Arasmeta by end-2026; Vadraj clinker and grinding units commissioning in phases Q3 FY27 to Q1 FY28 with INR627 crore capex in FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides FY27 industry volume growth of 7-9% and aims to grow in line; FY26 volume was 20.4 Mt vs 19.4 Mt, and North runs at ~95% utilisation.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is already guided at INR900 crore for FY27 and INR960 crore for FY28, and the new Viramgam/Sachana bulk terminal (~1.5 Mtpa) is planned for FY28; North runs at 95% utilisation, so further announcements are plausible, though no new project beyond the guided plan was named.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects FY27 industry volume growth of 7-9% and aims to grow in line, with East debottlenecking and Vadraj adding capacity, but the upside depends on price hikes holding and cost inflation stopping.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cost inflation is about INR200/t against April price hikes of INR8-12/bag trade and INR10-15/bag non-trade, a gap that is only partly covered; Q1 fuel is guided up to INR1.51-1.55/mn kcal from INR1.44, and Q2 is guided higher still.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA to 2x-2.5x within FY27
rows.why: Net debt rose to INR4,445 crore at FY26-end from INR3,640 crore at the start of FY26 after Vadraj (INR1,800 crore) and VEGL (INR200 crore) investments, and management guides to the 2x-2.5x EBITDA target within FY27, with debt elevated for a few quarters.

rows.label: AFR share rise to above 13% in FY27 and petcoke cut
rows.why: AFR share is targeted to rise from ~10% to above 13%, and East petcoke is to fall 300-500 bps from Q4 levels, but Q2 fuel cost is guided higher as later-booked petcoke arrives in July-August at INR2.01.

rows.label: Further price hikes if costs rise again
rows.why: Management is fairly confident April hikes hold if cost inflation stops, and would pass on further inflation, but gave no size for any further hike and the pass-through is not 1-to-1.

tone.note: Management was confident on record volume, capacity commissioning and FY27 industry growth of 7-9%, but cautious and at times evasive on the price-versus-cost gap and diesel impact; analysts pressed on pass-through and leverage.

543334|2026-06.headline: Nuvoco Q1 FY27: volume up 5% YoY to 5.3 mt and EBITDA up 7% to INR572 crore, highest-ever Q1 for both.
543334|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 volume rose 5% YoY to 5.3 million tons and EBITDA rose 7% YoY to INR572 crore, the company's highest-ever first-quarter volume and EBITDA. Realisation rose about INR320 per ton QoQ, largely offset by about INR230 per ton of cost inflation (power and fuel, raw material, packing bags, freight, fixed-cost deleverage), leaving a net EBITDA gain of about INR90 per ton. Management said the Surat grinding unit (2 mtpa) was inaugurated on 11 July 2026, ahead of schedule, and Kutch clinker and grinding remain on track for phased start from Q3 FY27. Management guided Q2 cost increase of about INR100 per ton, with power and fuel up INR30-40 per ton and packing and freight easing.

financial_highlights.value: Up about INR320 per ton QoQ (Q1 vs Q4)
financial_highlights.change: Cost inflation about INR230 per ton; net EBITDA impact about INR90 per ton
vs INR5,274 crore a year earlier (about INR600 crore lower)
FY27 capex guidance INR900 crore unchanged

segments.name: North (Chittorgarh, Nimbol, Rajasthan)
segments.commentary: Petcoke share cut from over 50% to about 40% by moving open-market coal from Chhattisgarh and Varanasi; Rajasthan capacity to be freed up for the North as Surat comes online.

segments.commentary: Risda petcoke share cut from about 37% to about 25% and Arasmeta at zero petcoke, using Sonepur Bazari coal and sweetener. Jojobera and Panagarh CTOs are nearly done; Jajpur awaits NIPL certificate; Arasmeta targeted for end FY27.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 total cost expected to rise about INR100 per ton QoQ (give or take INR20-30); power and fuel up INR30-40 per ton due to kiln and mill shutdowns, with packing bag costs seen cooling INR20-25 per ton and freight easing with the lean-season discount from 1 August.
Fuel cost expected to stay broadly flat in Q2 (1.52 could move to 1.55); petcoke inventory adequate for the quarter at similar cost; Q3 may carry higher-cost inventory.
FY27 volume growth target of about 7-8%, in line with market demand expectations of 7-8% over the next three quarters.
FY27 capex INR900 crore unchanged; FY28 capex INR950-1,000 crore including Vadraj expansion, Sachana terminal and routine capex.
Gujarat EBITDA per ton expected to be below company average in year 1 and to match rest-of-North in years 2-3; no EBITDA-per-ton guidance given.
Kutch clinker earliest start about January 2027 with Kutch clinker supply to Surat from start of FY28; East capacity (Jojobera, Panagarh, Jajpur, Arasmeta) to be ready by end FY27 for FY28 volumes.

Kutch clinker unit: major equipment delivered; kiln rotation complete; overhaul and trial preparation within Q2 FY27; phased operations from Q3 FY27.
Kutch grinding unit: civil works targeted for completion by Q2 FY27; Kutch railway siding ballast and sleeper laying in progress.
Sachana bulk cement terminal with dedicated railway siding: work commenced, targeted operational by Q2 FY28.

No price drop in the first 14 days of July 2026; company has not taken a further price increase but will raise prices if costs fall.

qa_highlights.question: Given Surat is online, what volume is expected this year and what is the clinker source before Kutch starts?
qa_highlights.answer: Gujarat sales of about 1.3-1.4 mt now; target about 2 mtpa annualised by Q4 FY27. Clinker for the incremental volume comes from the Chhattisgarh cluster and bartering; Kutch clinker expected to supply Surat from start of FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of East debottlenecking (CTOs for Jojobera, Panagarh, Jajpur, Arasmeta)?
qa_highlights.answer: Jojobera and Panagarh CTOs almost done; Jajpur awaits NIPL certificate; Arasmeta technical design done and ball mill procurement underway. All four to be ready by end FY27 and needed for FY28; no delay per management.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 realisation gain was price versus trade mix and geo-mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Three drivers: price increases (biggest), premium mix with Concreto, Duraguard Microfiber and Uno (about 5 mt premium and super-premium), and geo-mix shift toward high-realisation states (Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Western MP). Trade mix unchanged at 75%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost outlook for Q2 and fuel and packing trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Total cost up about INR100 per ton QoQ (plus or minus INR20-30). Petcoke inventory covers Q2 at similar cost; packing bags to ease INR20-25 per ton; rake availability improving to about 4 per day; power and fuel up INR30-40 per ton from shutdowns.

qa_highlights.question: Will Gujarat (Surat and Kutch) EBITDA per ton converge with the company average, and how fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Year 1 EBITDA per ton will be lower due to high costs and aggressive volume push, with no dilution of price intended; modelling shows Gujarat EBITDA per ton equal to rest-of-North in years 2-3. Kutch, Sachana and Surat form a hub-and-spoke network.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any change to FY27 capex and what is the FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex unchanged at INR900 crore with about INR370 crore spent in Q1; FY28 capex INR950-1,000 crore including Vadraj, Sachana terminal and routine spend.

Premium share fell from 44% to 42% QoQ; watch whether it recovers.

543334|2026-09.headline: Nuvoco Q2 FY27: volume up 9% YoY and revenue up ~14%, but energy cost rose ~INR90/ton QoQ; Q3 fuel guided to INR1.8/mn kcal from INR1.59.
543334|2026-09.overview: Management described a challenging quarter driven by a renewed Middle East escalation, petcoke and domestic coal price spikes, and monsoon disruption in the East. Volume grew 9% YoY, revenue about 14% and EBITDA about 11%, supported by premiumization at a record 45% and trade mix of 75%. Fuel cost rose from INR1.52 to INR1.59 per million kcal in Q2, and management guided Q3 to INR1.8 with about INR100-120/ton net cost inflation QoQ, offset by an October price hike of about INR20/ton. Vadraj's Surat grinding unit (2 MTPA) was commissioned in late September, and net debt rose above INR5,000 crore on working capital and capex, with a guided return to 2-2.5x net debt/EBITDA in the next 4-6 quarters.

segments.name: Gujarat (Vadraj / Surat & Kutch)
segments.commentary: Surat 2 MTPA grinding unit commissioned in late September; running at ~1.5 MTPA annualised, targeting 2 MTPA in Q4 FY27 with 50-60% utilisation in Q4 and 70-75% in FY28. Kutch clinker line expected in Q4 FY27, with jetty operational by first week of December.

segments.name: North
segments.commentary: Strong volume growth in Q2 per management. Around 1 million tons of cement capacity to be released from Rajasthan from Q4 for North sales, as Surat supplies Gujarat.

segments.name: East
segments.commentary: Erratic monsoon weighed on demand in Q2; East expansion deferred from Q3-Q4 FY27 to Q1-Q2 FY28. Price hike of about INR20/ton in trade and non-trade taken in October.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 fuel cost guided at INR1.8 per million kcal vs INR1.59 in Q2, adding ~INR70-80/ton energy cost QoQ; Q4 could add a further INR70-80/ton in a worst case.
Q3 FY27 net cost inflation guided at INR100-120/ton QoQ (energy ~INR70-80, packing bags ~INR20, busy-season surcharge waiver ~INR10), offset by ~INR20/ton price increase taken in October.
Industry demand expected at ~8% growth in H2 FY27; company guides 8-9% blended volume growth across North, West and East.
FY27 capex ~INR1,200 crore (INR780 crore spent in H1, ~INR420 crore in H2); FY28 capex INR800-900 crore.
Net debt expected to return to around March 2026 levels by end FY27; 2-2.5x net debt/EBITDA in the next 4-6 quarters, and below 2x once Vadraj volumes scale.
Surat incremental costs of ~INR30-40 crore expected in Q3 (interest and depreciation), partly above and below EBITDA.
Vadraj/Gujarat EBITDA per ton expected to match Nuvoco's all-India EBITDA per ton around FY29 (possibly FY28 Q4 to Q1 FY29).
Company targets 35 MTPA cement capacity by FY28.
capex_capacity: Surat (Vadraj) 2 MTPA grinding unit at Limla, Surat commissioned late September 2026; ~3,500-3,600 tons/day peak output against ~5,500 tons/day capacity.
Kutch clinker/grinding project on track: phased operations from Q3 FY27, clinker line December, Kutch clinker to Surat via barge once jetty is operational.
Viramgam (Sachana) bulk cement terminal with railway siding under construction; INR50 crore spend planned in H2 FY27.
East debottlenecking delayed from Q3-Q4 FY27 to Q1-Q2 FY28 to prioritise Vadraj cash flow and management bandwidth.
CleanMax agreement for 46.4 MW wind-solar hybrid project in Rajasthan, expected ~100 million units/year.
demand_pricing: Industry demand grew in Q2 but varied regionally; monsoon disrupted the East while low-rainfall regions performed better. Prices did not improve as expected in Q2.

Price action: non-trade up ~INR20-25/ton in North after 15 September, trade cut INR5-7/ton in North in late September, then ~INR20/ton increases in non-trade (North and East) and trade (East) in October.
Premium product mix at 45%; Duraguard Microfiber and Concreto Uno each crossed 1 million ton volumes, with Concreto Uno reaching it in under 18 months.
Management expects post-Diwali demand pickup and believes price increases will hold through the balance of the year.
Management sees 5% demand impact only if back-to-back adverse monsoon or drought years occur; assumes this does not happen in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What was average fuel cost in Q2 and what is the spot impact at petcoke near $187?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel cost rose from INR1.52 to INR1.59 per million kcal (energy ~INR1,080/ton vs INR1,005 in Q1). Q3 is guided at INR1.8, adding ~INR70-80/ton, with petcoke covered for Q3 and Q4 through mid-February.

qa_highlights.question: What is the overall Q3 vs Q2 cost outlook and how will it be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Net cost inflation of INR100-120/ton: energy +INR70-80, packing +INR20, raw materials ~+INR10, offset by ~INR20/ton price increase plus fixed-cost leverage from higher volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What is Surat's utilisation and run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Running at ~1.5 MTPA annualised; target 2 MTPA in Q4 FY27 with 50-60% utilisation in Q4 and 70-75% in FY28, as Kutch grinding is not available in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex ~INR1,200 crore (INR780 crore in H1, ~INR420 crore in H2, of which INR1,000 crore for Vadraj); FY28 INR800-900 crore. East expansion delayed 6-8 months to FY28 H1.

qa_highlights.question: How will net debt evolve and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt crossed INR5,000 crore (INR200 crore working capital build plus capex). Expected to return to March 2026 levels by end FY27, and to hover at 2-2.5x EBITDA over 4-6 quarters, with the long-term target below 2x.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest expense fall and will it continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowing costs for Surat were capitalised until commercial operations started in late September; interest and depreciation will rise QoQ from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 reported tax rate 41.6% because MAT credit is unavailable under the old regime; the company will decide on regime transition within 3-4 months and share the implications.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Vadraj EBITDA per ton outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Gujarat and Western Maharashtra EBITDA per ton expected to match Nuvoco's all-India level in year 3 (FY29, possibly FY28 Q4 to Q1 FY29), subject to cost inflation being offset by prices.

risks_watch: Petcoke prices near $190 with potential to exceed $200/ton; full impact of high-cost petcoke expected from March 2027 onwards.
Domestic coal auction premiums and rake shortages; linkage coal supply expected to ease from early November.
Price hikes must hold post-Diwali; any reversal would erode the expected Q3 benefit.
Surat clinker is currently sourced from Chhattisgarh and Chittor at high cost until Kutch clinker starts; the Q3 to Q4 margin dent was not quantified on the call.
Net debt at above INR5,000 crore vs the INR3,500-4,000 crore comfort range; deleveraging depends on H2 working capital release.
Tax regime transition decision pending; affects tax rate from FY28.
Geopolitical developments (Middle East) remain a watch item.
543334|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on operational execution and pricing actions, and candid about the cost shock. Management was evasive on specifics where variables were still moving: Q4 fuel cost, Surat clinker delta and regional growth splits were deferred to follow-up.
key_quotes: Overall, we are looking at as a company, from the current run rate of 1.5 annualized tons per annualized volume, we'll go to 2 million tons in Q4 this year.
And once the monsoon ends and the festival ends, I think construction activity will pick up speed going forward.
So, the average INR20 price increase should totally defray the cost increase, and we'll have a delta benefit in realization in Q3 versus Q2.

rows.why: Surat 2 MTPA grinding unit commissioned late September, running ~1.5 MTPA annualised with target 2 MTPA in Q4 FY27 at 50-60% Q4 utilisation; Kutch clinker line due December and ~1 MT released from Rajasthan from Q4.

rows.why: Management holds 8-9% blended volume growth for H2 FY27 vs industry ~8%, with Q2 volume up 9% YoY and Surat/Kutch adding capacity; East growth weak with monsoon disruption.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex raised to ~INR1,200 crore (INR780 crore spent in H1 vs original INR450-460 crore plan) and FY28 guided at INR800-900 crore, with Viramgam terminal (INR50 crore) under construction; capex is front-ended rather than newly announced.

rows.why: Prices did not improve as expected in Q2 and fuel cost is rising INR1.52 to INR1.59 to INR1.8, so upside to margin or revenue guidance looks limited.

rows.why: Q3 cost inflation of INR100-120/ton vs ~INR20/ton price hike leaves a gap, petcoke near $190 could exceed $200, and any reversal of post-Diwali price hikes would erode the Q3 benefit.

rows.why: Net debt rose above INR5,000 crore vs INR4,500-odd crore in March 2026 and guidance is 2-2.5x net debt/EBITDA within 4-6 quarters, dependent on H2 working capital release.

rows.why: Management expects Gujarat EBITDA/ton to converge with all-India around year 3 (FY29), subject to cost inflation being offset by prices, with Surat utilisation at 70-75% only in FY28.

543336|2026-03.headline: Chemplast Q4 FY26 net loss of INR45 crores on INR898 crore CCVL impairment; consolidated EBITDA rose to INR194 crores from INR37 crores.
543336|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 9% YoY to INR1,256 crores and EBITDA jumped to INR194 crores from INR37 crores, but the company posted a net loss of INR45 crores. The quarter absorbed an INR898 crore non-cash impairment on the investment in CCVL (suspension PVC) and a INR150 crore exceptional charge at CCVL for onerous contracts and raw material write-down. Management said suspension PVC spreads are at roughly breakeven on a replacement-cost basis because of Chinese carbide PVC imports, while specialty chemicals grew 13%. The Board also formed a committee of three independent directors to review strategic priorities, reorganisation and M&A.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR37 crores in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR898 crores vs book value INR1,556 crores

financial_highlights.metric: CCVL exceptional charge (onerous contracts, RM write-down)

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals (Paste PVC, CMC, refrigerant gases)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR475 crores, up 13% YoY, with volumes up 17% YoY mainly from paste PVC; Cuddalore paste PVC ran at 100% of capacity through the year. Revenue share was 38% of Q4 total.

segments.name: Value-added Chemicals (caustic soda, chloromethanes, hydrogen peroxide)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR120 crores vs INR169 crores a year earlier (about 29% decline), with 9% share of Q4 revenue. Caustic volumes fell YoY due to membrane change at Mettur, though they improved sequentially from Karaikal.

segments.name: Suspension PVC (CCVL)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR661 crores, up 18% YoY from INR560 crores, 53% of Q4 revenue. Spreads are near breakeven on replacement cost; Chinese carbide PVC at about $820/t CFR India is pressuring prices.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the commodity business including CCVL to face a volatile near-term environment in FY27, while expecting stronger performance in specialty.
Management hopes the 7.5% customs duty on PVC returns at end-June 2026; it said this could add about $60-70 per tonne to realisations.
Anti-dumping duty on paste PVC imports from EU and Japan is expected to be implemented in H1 FY27, pending notification by the Finance Ministry.
R32 capacity expected to reach 14 kt by end of calendar 2026, with commissioning in phases through the year after the 2 kt Mettur swing plant started commercial production.

543358|2026-06.headline: Sansera Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to INR10,213 million, with EBITDA margin at 19.2% and ADS order book lifted to about INR57.5 billion.
543358|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue hit a record INR10,213 million, up 33% YoY, with non-auto sales of INR1,998 million up 129.9% and 20.8% of sales. EBITDA excluding exceptionals was INR1,961 million (19.2% margin, up about 200 bps YoY), after a INR126 million provision for US import duty recovery. A INR169 million exceptional litigation settlement cut reported PAT to INR874 million (8.6% margin, up 39% YoY); PAT excluding the exceptional post-tax impact was about INR1,000 million. Management raised FY27 growth commentary to high-teens, with a possible 20% plus, and said the ADS order book rose to about INR57.5 billion after a post-quarter SEM order win.

segments.commentary: INR6,275 million, +20.8% YoY on a high base; record quarter across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles and scooters.

Build-to-suit facility of about 100,000 sq ft near the existing site under negotiation (targeted for August), ready in about 10 months.

Auto capex: crankshaft and connecting rod forging/machining at Pantnagar (Plant 6) and Manesar (Plant 4); machining at Bangalore Plant 2 for xEV; new multi-storey building at Plant 2; projects to commission from start of Q3 FY27, completion within about a year.

Management said Sansera's motorcycle revenue grew about 12.5% and it is gaining share at TVS, Yamaha and Suzuki; it supplies about 75% of Maruti's volumes for the components it makes.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ADS order book about INR45 bn or INR57 bn, are incremental orders from existing or new customers, and where does ADS revenue go in 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR44.4 bn book at quarter end rose to about INR57.5 bn after a post-1 July SEM order from an existing customer, about $75 mn annual business, about INR5,700 crore executable over five years (to FY31). Revenue ramp is gated by mother-machine lead times, with significant revenue from calendar 2027 and peak in calendar 2029.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR129 million impact included in the 19.2% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vikas Goel confirmed the US import duty provision is included in EBITDA, treated as a cost.

qa_highlights.question: ADS asset turns and capex implications for semicon and aerospace capacity?

qa_highlights.question: Can non-ADS grow mid-teens and total top-line reach high-teens to 20%+ in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Preetham said non-ADS should grow mid-teens easily, moving toward mid-to-high teens as momentum allows, and overall growth of high-teens to 20% is a good possibility if trends sustain. He noted 2-3 year visibility of 20%+ is too early to say.

qa_highlights.question: How did material costs and pricing pass-through play out, and was the gross margin expansion from mix alone?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Goel said material inflation was modest, mainly aluminium and some consumables, with limited steel inflation. Steel and tool/labour pass-through is under negotiation with nothing booked in Q1. Mix and forex both supported gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why are ICE crankshaft and connecting rod capacities expanding, and what is the updated capex number?
qa_highlights.answer: Preetham linked the expansion to two-wheeler OEMs outsourcing crankshafts, plus PV indications. Rahul Kale described a fully automated Pantnagar crankshaft facility, forging, heat treatment and Bangalore conrod machining. Vikas Goel said the FY27 capex plan given last quarter has not been updated.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20%-plus growth through FY29 prudent, and does ADS margin reach 20-25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Preetham said it is too early to call 20%+ for two to three years, since auto expansions take 18-24 months and need two-year customer visibility. On margins, he said Q1 may be elevated by mix and currency, exports and ADS target 25-30% EBITDA, and FY26 margin was 18.1%.

543363|2026-03.headline: Prevest DenPro FY26 revenue rose 13.9% to INR71.81 crore and PAT rose 12.9% to INR20.49 crore, with PAT margin at 26.7%.
543363|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations grew 13.9% to INR71.81 crore, with exports up 17.58% and domestic up 9%. EBITDA rose 13.3% to INR29.62 crore, though the EBITDA margin of 38.6% moderated slightly year on year. Q4 FY26 revenue grew only 2.63% to INR18.94 crore due to geopolitical disruption and shipping issues, but Q4 profitability outpaced sales, with EBITDA margin at 40.87% and PAT up 13.23% to INR5.82 crore. Management launched disinfectant commercialisation and set up a UAE subsidiary, whose operations were delayed by the Middle East conflict.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: FY26 domestic sales grew 9%; H2 domestic sales rose 12.72% YoY and 16.19% HoH. Management cited floods and GST changes as H1 drags.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 export sales grew 17.58%; H2 exports rose 11.66% YoY and 3.56% HoH. The company says it covers about 90-92 countries.

segments.name: US (Axiodent and private label)
segments.commentary: US business grew about 37.58% (also cited as 38%) in FY26, driven by online sales, direct orders and private-label business won at US exhibitions.

segments.name: Oradox oral care
segments.commentary: Sales declined about 2% in FY26 because US MoCRA-related exports and a planned Dubai consignment did not ship. Management expects 2-3 new launches and a recovery.

segments.name: 3D printing (resins and printers)
segments.commentary: 3D resin revenue rose about 40.5% YoY. 3D printers (brand Omni, sales started November 2025) rose about 162% from a low base.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Oradox to compensate for the FY26 shortfall this year, supported by 2-3 new product launches.
UAE subsidiary expected to start online sales in Dubai the following month, after product registration; commercial operations were delayed by the Middle East conflict.
Company aims for a fully indigenous 3D printer by 2028.
Management expects at least 40% of dental-office procedures to have a digital workflow within five years.
Management is cautious on global uncertainty but sees the domestic market, Tier 2/3 expansion and disinfectants as growth drivers.
capex_capacity: Traditional capacity utilisation is about 67-68% of installed capacity; at full installed capacity, turnover would be about INR125 crore (Vinay Jamwal).
New production lines (digital dentistry, resins, disinfectants, oral health) are running at about 18-20% utilisation and are expected to rise.
Four R&D test licences for new agents (caries removal, endodontic irrigants, self-etching resins, periodontal gels) are at TRL 7, with two products launched in the market in the month of the call.
Import substitution of raw materials is in progress through in-house development.
Subsidiaries in the UAE (opened February 2026) and the US (Axiodent) are operating; two sales staff employed in Dubai.
demand_pricing: Management says Indian manufacturing cost advantage and high import duties make it hard for MNCs to beat the company on price; it also cites quality certifications.
The company is an OEM supplier to about 3-4 large companies and expects to add a couple more in the next two years.
Competitors named for digital dentistry include Ivoclar, Dentsply and 3Shape; management says digital dentistry is a level playing field, unlike legacy products where MNCs have first-mover advantage.
Disinfectants launched this year, with an early customer response described as highly encouraging; no revenue figure given.
Oradox was hit by US MoCRA cosmetic-regulation requirements and by the Middle East conflict, which blocked a planned Dubai consignment.

qa_highlights.question: Why has growth slowed over the last 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 export growth of 17.5% is satisfactory given geopolitical headwinds, and that the company is shifting share from disrupted Asian markets to other geographies across 90-92 countries.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue is spent on R&D?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Sai Kalyan did not give a figure and said it would be provided later. He described two products launched, four licences at TRL 7 and import substitution work.

qa_highlights.question: What do the UAE and US subsidiaries do, and how is Dubai responding?
qa_highlights.answer: The US subsidiary, Axiodent, drove US growth of about 37.58% through online sales, direct orders and private labelling. The Dubai subsidiary opened in February 2026, hired two sales staff and is registering products for online sales expected next month.

qa_highlights.question: What is current capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinay Jamwal said traditional capacity runs at 67-68% utilisation, which would imply about INR125 crore turnover at full installed capacity. New lines run at 18-20%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove domestic performance and what steps were taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Vaibhav Munjal cited expansion of Tier 2/3 distribution, a larger in-house sales team and new products such as disinfectants and Rotoflex. H1 was hit by floods and GST changes, and H2 recovered.

qa_highlights.question: How is Oradox trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Sai Kalyan said sales fell about 2% because US and Dubai exports were blocked by MoCRA rules and the war. Management expects recovery through marketing, direct-to-doctor programmes and 2-3 launches.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 3D printing opportunity and right to win?
qa_highlights.answer: Sai Kalyan said digital dentistry is a level field where the company has a slight edge, with 3D resin revenue up about 40.5% and printer sales up about 162%, and an indigenous printer targeted for 2028.

543364|2026-03.headline: Markolines reported FY26 revenue of Rs 348.49 crore (up from Rs 307 crore) and PAT of Rs 26.23 crore (about 15% higher), with EPS up 17% to Rs 11.90.
543364|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of Rs 348.49 crore against Rs 307 crore a year earlier, EBITDA of Rs 48.54 crore and PAT of Rs 26.23 crore, with EPS rising from Rs 10.16 to Rs 11.90. Q4 revenue was about Rs 105 crore with a stated PAT margin of about 10.81% and EBITDA margin of about 18%. Management said West Asia-related disruption weighed on performance during the year. The call centred on the pending merger with Markolines Infra, a targeted FY27 growth of at least 30% on a standalone basis, and an active pipeline of about Rs 2,000 crore. Several answers on margins, order book and merger timing were qualitative or repeated.

segments.name: Highway maintenance (pavement)
segments.commentary: About 65% of revenue as of March 2026, per management; Rs 350 crore pavement revenue cited for FY26. Covers preventive, major (5 to 7 year cycle) and rigid pavement maintenance.

segments.name: Specialized construction
segments.commentary: About 35% of revenue as of March 2026, up from about 25% per analyst question; includes micro-surfacing, cold in-place recycling (CIPR), soil stabilisation, FDR, tunnelling and bridges. Management says it carries higher margins.

segments.name: Markolines Infra (proposed merger)
segments.commentary: Cited at about Rs 150 crore FY26 revenue; operates about 60 work orders across about 30 projects including 28 toll projects. Management said its PAT margin is 9 to 10%, above pavement, and monthly billing is about Rs 14 to 15 crore.

segments.name: School and sports infrastructure
segments.commentary: Newly entered; one open school infrastructure order and two smaller sports complex rehabilitation orders in Andhra Pradesh. No value disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of at least 30% on a standalone basis, per management; Markolines Infra revenue would be additional on merger.
Merger with Markolines Infra expected to be completed by end of FY27; management cites about six months for NCLT processes, with all queries answered and none pending.
Target closing order book of at least Rs 1,000 crore by end of FY27.
Target of Rs 1,000 crore revenue scale in about three years, with possibility to bring it forward.
Capex of about Rs 10 crore in FY27 for one or more pavers and possibly one HMP; policy of not exceeding Rs 10 crore per year.
Management expects monsoon at about 90% of average this year; first two quarters to see lower revenue.
capex_capacity: No major capex in FY26, per management.
Plan for one or a few additional pavers and possibly one HMP, about Rs 10 crore in FY27.
Company owns three sets of machinery; other machinery is rented locally where cheaper.
Plants and equipment are churned about every 3 to 4 years to maintain efficiency.
Eligible to bid up to Rs 500 crore projects on its own following completion of a Maharashtra tunnel project.
demand_pricing: Order book about Rs 600 crore plus, split roughly 45-50% maintenance and 50-55% specialized construction (management gave both 50-50 and 45-45 figures). Infra order book is separate and recurring.
Active pipeline of about Rs 2,000 crore across four to five projects of Rs 300 to 500 crore each; management says it wins at least 50% of targeted orders.
L1 position on a Rs 120 crore maintenance contract with a corporation, per management.
Management says it works on a cost-plus basis with clients, so PBT and PAT margins are steady (7 to 8%), while EBITDA varies with client capex pass-through.
Management says maintenance is about 15% of road cost in India versus about 40% globally, which it sees as a long-term driver.
Government allowed sovereign and international funds to participate in PPP highway construction, which management sees as increasing demand for O&M partners.

qa_highlights.question: Status of merger with Markolines Infra and expected completion?
qa_highlights.answer: Applications filed and all queries answered in March, with few recently answered; management expects about six months to completion and a merged entity by FY27 end.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA margins of Infra and combined FY27 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Infra results to be released within a week after final audit; Infra margins are higher than pavement, with PAT of about 9 to 10% for services. Management later said PBT and PAT margins stay at 7 to 8%.

qa_highlights.question: FY26 and FY27 capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: No major capex in FY26; about Rs 10 crore planned in FY27 for pavers and possibly one HMP, with equipment churned every 3 to 4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Win ratio and closing order book expectations for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Win ratio of at least 50% on targeted active orders; management targets a closing order book of at least Rs 1,000 crore, versus an 18-month typical coverage norm.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 growth and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth of at least 30% standalone, driven by higher eligibility after the tunnel project; margin guidance was not given, as EBITDA is said to vary with client capex pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall in Q4, and what drove the 62% QoQ PAT jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said other expenses and material consumption must be viewed together because outsourcing shifts costs between heads, and margins should be similar. Q4 is seasonally strongest as billing concentrates in March.

risks_watch: Merger timing relies on NCLT approval; management expects completion within about six months.
Q4 seasonality: first two quarters are weaker due to monsoon, and management expects below-average rainfall this year.
Order book conversion: management's 50% win-rate claim and Rs 1,000 crore closing order book target are unverified.
Specialized construction share rising (about 35%), with the 50% of order book in multi-year contracts, which affects visibility and execution timing.
Margin variability: EBITDA is described as variable with client capex pass-through; PAT margin guidance is only 7 to 8%.
West Asia crisis cited as a drag on FY26 performance; no detail given on impact.

543374|2026-03.headline: ABSLAMC Q4 FY26 revenue rose 7% YoY to ₹458 crore, while PAT fell to ₹187 crore from ₹228 crore on lower other income; FY26 PAT ₹975 crore.

Reported PAT fell to ₹187 crore from ₹228 crore, which management attributed to lower other income from mark-to-market actions. For FY26, revenue was ₹1,845 crore (₹1,685 crore), operating profit ₹1,015 crore (₹944 crore) and PAT ₹975 crore (₹931 crore); the Board proposed a dividend of ₹25.5 per share. Average AUM including alternates reached ₹4.74 lakh crore (up 17% YoY), with equity MF AUM up 17% to about ₹1.97 lakh crore. Management said flows and SIP registrations improved QoQ, but market share is still slightly down.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mitigation plan for the 3-5 bps regulatory impact from April 1 and the net impact on AMC books?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated the impact at about 3-4 bps and said structures will be redesigned across commissions and other expenses to keep AMC profitability neutral or positive, without quantifying the number.

qa_highlights.question: How have flows and market share moved this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Flows improved QoQ with better acceptance and banking approvals; the market share decline has narrowed significantly and management expects to come close to market growth soon.

qa_highlights.question: Key data points: SIP AUM, ETF AUM, PMS/AIF revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: SIP book about ₹76,000 crore (down QoQ purely on MTM); ETF about ₹11,500 crore of ₹41,200 crore passive AUM; PMS/AIF revenue about 6% of gross revenue and 3.5% net.

qa_highlights.question: Why did equity yield decline about 2-3 bps QoQ and is it structural?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to telescoping pricing and product mix (including growth in passives), not a specific one-off; versus last year the drop is 2-3 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Expected employee cost growth and ESOP impact?
qa_highlights.answer: ESOP impact of ₹8-10 crore per quarter from FY27; headcount at 1,650 with normal attrition of about 50 and onboarding of 80-100 off-role staff; cost increase expected to be marginal.

qa_highlights.question: Is ₹250-300 crore of monthly net equity inflows now a steady base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the trend supports it and the number would be much higher than indicated, though it would not give a figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the banking channel strategy and product pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Two products are on HDFC Bank's recommendation list and two or three on Kotak's; banking flows had fallen when products were off lists. Pipeline includes SIF launch soon, lifecycle funds, REIT/InvIT funds pending SEBI approval, and open-ended GIFT City EM fund.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.why: PMS and AIF assets nearly ₹2 lakh crore incl. EPFO flows, alternates ~7% of gross revenue and ~4% of net revenue, and a three-year PMS long-only target of ₹20,000-21,000 crore; AIF credit and money market funds targeted at ₹5,000-7,000 crore each.

543374|2026-09.headline: ABSLAMC Q2 FY27 PAT fell 8% YoY to ₹221 crores on ₹526 crores revenue, while average AUM including EPFO/ESIC mandates reached ₹11.06 lakh crores.
543374|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 total revenue rose about 4% YoY to ₹526 crores, but PBT fell to ₹296 crores from ₹316 crores and PAT to ₹221 crores from ₹241 crores, as employee costs rose on ESOPs and a base effect. H1 FY27 PAT was ₹530 crores versus ₹518 crores. Mutual fund quarterly average AUM grew 4% YoY to ₹4.42 lakh crores, while the EPFO and ESIC mandates lifted total average AUM to ₹11.06 lakh crores. Management said flows in core funds such as Flexi Cap and Balanced Advantage are improving quarter-on-quarter, and SIF and passive products are being pushed.

financial_highlights.metric: Overall average AUM incl. alternates and EPFO/ESIC mandates

segments.name: Mutual fund (ex-alternates)
segments.commentary: Quarterly average AUM ₹4.42 lakh crores (+4% YoY); equity AUM about ₹2.09 lakh crores (+9% YoY). Equity yield about 63-64 bps, debt 24-25 bps, liquid 12-13 bps, ETF about 8 bps.

segments.name: Passives
segments.commentary: Quarterly average AUM about ₹39,860 crores (+10% YoY), with about 17.9 lakh folios. ETF quarterly average AUM grew about 42% YoY versus industry growth of about 27%.

segments.name: Alternates (PMS, AIF, real estate)
segments.commentary: PMS and AIF assets rose from ₹30,300 crores to ₹6,57,109 crores, including the EPFO mandate. Real estate AUM about ₹860 crores (+43% YoY). Gross yield on non-MF revenue 7.4% (from 7.1% in Q1), net 4.3% (from 4.0%).

segments.name: SIF (Specialised Investment Fund)
segments.commentary: Three SIF products with about ₹700 crores AUM as of September 2026; Equity Long-Short and Equity Ex-Top 100 Long-Short launched in the quarter. Management said the industry SIF category is about ₹31,000 crores.

guidance_outlook: Employee cost in coming quarters expected to be in a similar range to Q2, with inflationary increases on top.
New ESOP scheme launched recently: about ₹14-15 crores per year (₹3-3.5 crores per quarter). Existing schemes add about ₹55-60 crores yearly impact over the next two years.
EPFO and ESIC mandates are expense-neutral; the company expects the mandates to build credibility and bring rub-off into other private EPFO and overseas mandates.
Six new funds planned for launch in the coming quarter across retail and non-retail categories at GIFT City; Real Estate Credit Opportunities Fund Series II targeted to close by December.
Management said incremental growth will not come at the cost of profit margins.
capex_capacity: Direct channel: about 80 dedicated people across 14 locations, with a focus on existing direct customers and referral programmes.
GenAI capabilities expanded across chatbots, voice and WhatsApp during the quarter.
Treasury investment book about ₹2,890 crores, mostly debt mutual funds and corporate bonds, with about 17-18% in equity schemes.
Birla Passives launched as a dedicated brand; BSE Total Market Cap Index Fund and ETF launched.
demand_pricing: Flexi Cap, Balanced Advantage, Multi Asset, Multi Cap, Small Cap and Mid Cap funds show quarter-on-quarter improvement in gross and net sales. Flexi Cap net flow market share reportedly about 4.5-4.8%, versus about 3-3.5% in AUM terms.
Channel mix for equity funds: MFDs about 52%, national distributors about 20%, banks about 10%, direct about 18%. Digital contributes 55-56% of SIF/SIP count but only 18-20% of amount.
Retention ratio on redemptions reportedly rose to 25-30% from 4-5% earlier, per management's internal analysis.
SIP AUM about ₹86,000 crores; September 2026 SIP flows ₹1,094 crores from 41.7 lakh SIP folios; new SIP registrations about 7.05 lakh in the quarter.
Industry: MF AUM ₹87.21 lakh crores (+13% YoY); industry SIP flow ₹32,490 crores in September 2026 (+11% YoY); folios 30 crores (+17%).

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee expenses rise sharply YoY, excluding ESOPs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to ESOP cost of about ₹12-13 crores (about 13% growth), a ₹6 crore provision reversal in the base quarter (about 6%), plus normal increments and headcount added for the passive team.

qa_highlights.question: What are the gross flows and market share trends in key schemes like Flexi Cap and Balanced Advantage?
qa_highlights.answer: No gross or net flow figures were given. Management said each focus fund saw higher gross and net sales QoQ, and Flexi Cap and Balanced Advantage net flow share is about 4.5-4.8%, up from a lower level last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How will the mandates affect profitability and what other benefits do they bring?
qa_highlights.answer: The mandates are expense-neutral and use existing staff, with a dedicated team added. Management expects rub-off into private EPFO and overseas mandates, plus a small margin benefit over time.

qa_highlights.question: How does SIF's unit economics compare with equity and debt funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SIF yields sit between debt and equity categories. Long-short equity variants could approach equity fund margins; fixed-income SIF variants could be around 55-60 bps, similar to dynamic bond funds.

qa_highlights.question: What is being done to lift flows and SIPs, and is the company paying up for growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Initiatives include QoQ sales targets and incentives for SIP drives, a brand campaign, and bank recommendation-list additions (four or five banks in the quarter). Management said incremental growth will not come at the cost of margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ESOP cost outlook and direct channel plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The new ESOP scheme adds about ₹14-15 crores a year; existing schemes add ₹55-60 crores a year for two years. The direct channel has about 80 people across 14 locations, with segment-based coverage for ₹1 crore+ and ₹25 lakh-1 crore clients plus chatbot RMs.

risks_watch: PAT declined 8% YoY in Q2 despite revenue growth, with costs rising on ESOPs and inflation; watch whether employee and business costs stay near Q2 levels.
Expected ESOP cost of about ₹55-60 crores a year plus ₹14-15 crores from the new scheme over the next two years.
Core equity flow share gains depend on sustaining the 4.5-4.8% Flexi Cap and Balanced Advantage net-flow share and channel additions.
Direct channel share at about 18% of equity AUM, which management itself described as a gap versus peers.
Rising interest rates (RBI repo raised 25 bps to 5.5%) and potential lumpsum flow constraints; SIF category size remains uncertain.
543374|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on fund performance, flows momentum and the mandate wins, but cautious on profitability, with costs rising. Management was less specific on SIF economics and on the direct-channel gap, which it acknowledged as an area needing more focus.
key_quotes: Our overall average AUM, including alternate assets, which is EPFO mandate, crossed ₹11 lakh crores milestones this quarter, and now stands at ₹11.06 lakh crores, a growth of 140% year-on-year.
any incremental growth that comes in, is not going to come at the cost of my profit margins, profitability going down.
In fact, 85% of our funds are in the peer group in addition to beating the benchmark as well.

rows.why: Q2 PAT fell 8% YoY to ₹221 crores and PBT fell 6% to ₹296 crores on rising employee costs, with employee cost guided to stay at Q2 levels plus inflation and a new ESOP scheme adding ₹14-15 crores a year on top of ₹55-60 crores a year from existing schemes for two years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management says Flexi Cap, Balanced Advantage, Multi Asset, Multi Cap, Small Cap and Mid Cap gross and net sales improved QoQ, Flexi Cap net flow share is about 4.5-4.8% versus about 3-3.5% AUM share, and ETF AUM grew about 42% YoY against industry about 27%.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric revenue or margin guidance was given, and management said incremental growth will not come at the cost of margins while employee cost and ESOP costs are rising.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 PAT fell 8% YoY on ESOP and employee cost increases, and the guided ESOP burden of ₹55-60 crores a year plus ₹14-15 crores from the new scheme will keep pressuring profit growth if flows stay weak.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans six new funds across retail and non-retail categories at GIFT City in the coming quarter, and the Real Estate Credit Opportunities Fund Series II is targeted to close by December; SIF AUM is about ₹700 crores across three products.

rows.label: EPFO and ESIC mandates lift total AUM to ₹11.06 lakh crores
rows.why: Total average AUM including alternates and EPFO/ESIC mandates reached ₹11.06 lakh crores (+140% YoY), and management expects rub-off into private EPFO and overseas mandates, while the mandates are expense-neutral.

rows.label: Direct channel build-out
rows.why: Direct channel is about 18% of equity AUM with about 80 dedicated people across 14 locations, which management itself called a gap versus peers, but no target was given.

rows.label: SIF category expansion
rows.why: Three SIF products have about ₹700 crores AUM against an industry SIF category of about ₹31,000 crores, with Equity Long-Short and Equity Ex-Top 100 Long-Short launched in the quarter; management was less specific on SIF economics.

tone.note: Management was confident on flow momentum in core equity funds, the mandate wins and the new GIFT City launches, but cautious on profitability as employee and ESOP costs rise; analysts pushed on employee expense growth, flow and market share data, SIF unit economics and the direct-channel gap.

543384|2026-03.headline: Nykaa Q4 FY26 net revenue rose 28% YoY to INR 2,648 crore with EBITDA margin of 8.4% and PAT of INR 79 crore.
543384|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 GMV and net revenue both grew 28% YoY, with net revenue of INR 2,648 crore and gross margin of 45.4%. EBITDA reached INR 223 crore (8.4% of net revenue, up 67% YoY) and PAT INR 79 crore. FY26 net revenue crossed INR 10,000 crore, with EBITDA at 7.5% and PAT at 2.0% of net revenue. Fashion turned EBITDA positive at 0.3% in Q4, and Beauty EBITDA margin was 10.3% in Q4. Management said April and May were good, but flagged oil prices, currency and inflation as reasons for caution for the next year.

segments.name: Beauty (vertical)
segments.commentary: FY26 GMV close to INR 15,000 crore (+27%), NSV about INR 8,500 crore, EBITDA margin 9.6% (+70 bps). Q4 GMV +27%, NSV +29%, EBITDA margin 10.3%.

segments.name: House of Nykaa (owned brands)
segments.commentary: FY26 GMV INR 3,176 crore (~+50%); Beauty part INR 2,788 crore (+65%). Dot & Key INR 1,790 crore GMV, Kay Beauty ~INR 380 crore (3x in 3 years), Nykaa Cosmetics ~INR 400 crore.

segments.name: Superstore (B2B)
segments.commentary: Business of ~INR 1,200 crore GMV built in 4 years, ~0.5 million retailers across 1,300 cities, 220+ brands. Almost 30% of orders self-placed by retailers. Management said EBITDA margin improved by more than 500 bps.

segments.name: Nykaa Fashion
segments.commentary: FY26 GMV almost INR 5,000 crore (+30%), NSV INR 1,447 crore (~+30%). EBITDA margin improved from -8.3% to -2.6% for FY26; Q4 EBITDA was +0.3% with Q4 NSV growth of 42%.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical guidance given; management said April and May growth momentum was good.

Beauty: each sub-business (multi-brand retail, House of Brands, B2B Superstore) to keep improving margin; management expects similar year-over-year margin trajectory in coming years while reinvesting in growth.
B2B Superstore expected to be a single-digit margin business at steady state; owned brands could have higher margins than multi-brand retail.
Beauty retail store additions planned at about 50-60 per year, with about 170-180 more doors over 2-3 years toward a 500-store target in 3-4 years.
Fashion: management expects margin trajectory to remain positive; did not give long-term numbers.
Nykaa Now (quick commerce) to be marketed more actively in FY27 after building about 75-80 dark stores across top 7 metros.
Company annual day in about six weeks to detail the house-of-brands plan.
capex_capacity: Capex utilisation at about 1% of revenue, with investment in beauty retail store expansion, fulfilment and technology.
Beauty store network about 313 stores across 99 cities, over 3 lakh sq ft; more than doubled over 3 years. Like-for-like growth double digit in FY26.
Earth Rhythm: acquired additional 24% stake to complete 100% ownership (had 76% from FY23-FY25) at pre-agreed terms.
Took over Kiehl's India boutique and online operations in the quarter; also building Charlotte Tilbury exclusive brand stores.
Fixed asset turnover improved to 9.9x in FY26 from 9.1x in FY25.
demand_pricing: Beauty: 1.8 billion visits to website/app in FY26 (+28%); 45 million monthly active unique visitors; 19.7 million annual transacting customers; 66 million orders vs 36 million in FY23.
Korean beauty brands grew 58% YoY on platform; dermacosmetics GMV grew over 40% YoY.

Fashion: new customer acquisition up 41% YoY; over 1,200-1,300 brands added in the last year; men's category +60%, kids +50%, home +40%. H&M is now the number one brand on Nykaa Fashion since its November launch; Nike onboarded and Nykaa manages Nike.com and app in India from February.
Management said AOV growth has been muted in recent quarters because new customers (lower AOV) form a larger share of transacting customers; focus is on frequency and annual consumption value.
Brands may pull back on digital ad spend if inflation persists; management said no single brand accounts for double-digit revenue.
Imports are a small share of direct sourcing; forex is fully hedged for the next 2-3 months.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for next year across segments, and the impact of inflation on demand and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Falguni Nayar said April and May were good, but high oil prices, a weaker currency and inflation make management cautious. She added that beauty is a small luxury and AI is helping both top line and costs.

qa_highlights.question: How are new visitors rising while marketing spend is controlled?
qa_highlights.answer: Anchit Nayar cited a focus on new customer acquisition for 4-6 quarters, app experience improvements, and AI-driven efficiency in paid acquisition on Meta and Google and in personalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Steady-state margins for Beauty sub-businesses and Fashion, and freight/fuel cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said each beauty business is improving margin, but reinvestment in growth continues, and B2B is a single-digit margin business. Brands have not yet passed on price increases, though a price rise is possible.

qa_highlights.question: What drove Fashion growth to 30% while marketing fell, and has competition eased?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhijeet Dabas credited higher repeat frequency, new-customer acquisition and marquee brands such as H&M and Nike. He said competition has not abated, but Nykaa Fashion focuses on premium online fashion, with a $55 billion TAM.

qa_highlights.question: Can private label rise to 30% of BPC without hurting third-party brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Anchit Nayar disputed the 20% figure and said owned brands do not account for 20% of retail revenue. Adwaita Nayar said the aim is building an independent house of brands, not raising Nykaa's share.

qa_highlights.question: Growth outlook for Dot & Key and other owned brands after a high base, and AUTC vs AOV growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Adwaita Nayar said growth will come from existing brands plus breakout brands (4 meaningful brands now). Anchit Nayar said customer acquisition headroom remains large and AOV growth is expected to come from personalisation and premiumisation.

qa_highlights.question: Rupee exposure of imported brands, and Nykaa Now salience?
qa_highlights.answer: P. Ganesh said direct imports are a small share and forex is hedged for 2-3 months. Anchit Nayar said about 75-80 rapid stores cover the top 7 metros, with a 30-minute to 2-hour promise, and that marketing starts in FY27.

risks_watch: Macro: high oil prices, currency depreciation and inflation could hit consumption and brand ad budgets.
Brands may pass on price increases or reduce digital ad spend, affecting AOV and marketing revenue.
Owned-brand growth at 65% from a concentrated base (Dot & Key ~INR 1,790 crore GMV) may slow; management avoided a numeric growth target.
Margin trajectory depends on mix: B2B Superstore is lower-margin and could dilute the Beauty vertical.
Fashion EBITDA only just turned positive (+0.3% in Q4); sustainability is unproven.
Inference cost and AI spend were raised as a margin pressure but not quantified.
Store additions of ~50-60 a year and the Nykaa Now marketing ramp in FY27 need monitoring.

543384|2026-06.headline: Nykaa Q1 FY27: net revenue up 29% YoY to INR 2,782 crore, EBITDA up 68% to INR 236 crore at 8.5% margin, PAT INR 80 crore.
543384|2026-06.overview: Nykaa reported GMV of INR 5,590 crore (+34% YoY) and net revenue of INR 2,782 crore (+29% YoY) for Q1 FY27, with gross margin up 123 bps to 45.9%. EBITDA rose 68% to INR 236 crore (8.5% margin, up about 196 bps YoY) and PAT reached INR 80 crore (2.9% margin). Beauty NSV grew 29% with a 10.3% EBITDA margin, while Fashion NSV grew 54% and turned breakeven at the EBITDA level (0.1% margin) with the business profitable overall. Management also announced the acquisition of a 51% stake in dermocosmetic brand Aminu, with the balance to follow over several years.

financial_highlights.change: Profitable overall; 627 bps YoY improvement in profitability

segments.name: Beauty (incl. Nykaa Online, retail, House of Nykaa)
segments.commentary: NSV INR 2,371 crore (+29% YoY) with EBITDA INR 244 crore at 10.3% margin. Transacting customers crossed 20 million annually and AOV rose about 5% in aggregate.

segments.name: Fashion
segments.commentary: NSV INR 451 crore (+54% YoY); women's +40%, men's +83%, kids ~+57-60%. Marketing and S&D expense fell 534 bps to 22.9% of revenue and overheads fell 292 bps; business profitable overall.

segments.name: House of Nykaa
segments.commentary: Annualised GMV INR 3,760 crore (+39% YoY) and annualised NSV about INR 2,200 crore (+36%). The 7 beauty brands delivered Q1 NSV of INR 508 crore (+40%); Dot & Key runs at about INR 1,300 crore annualised NSV, Kay Beauty INR 300 crore and Nykaa Cosmetics INR 270 crore.

segments.name: Nykaa Superstore (B2B)
segments.commentary: NSV grew 28% with GMV slightly lower due to GST-led MRP impact. EBITDA improved by more than 300 bps, with 0.5 million retailers and 240+ brands (18 added in the quarter).

segments.name: Nykaa Retail (stores)
segments.commentary: 324 stores across 100+ cities after 11 openings in Q1, with double-digit same-store sales growth; 50% of stores are in Tier 2 and beyond.

guidance_outlook: Nykaa Now (quick commerce, 60-minute delivery) to expand from 13 cities to over 25 cities by end FY27.
Superstore: GST-led GMV gap expected to normalise from Q3 FY27 so NSV and GMV growth converge; management still targets a 35%+ GMV CAGR, reached by FY2030.
Fashion: Investor Day guidance of 3-3.5x growth over 4-5 years retained, with management saying the core platform could outperform it.
Festive demand expected to fall mainly in Q3 FY27 this year, with some possible spill into Q4.
Aminu acquisition: 51% acquired now; the remaining 49% to be acquired over the next few years under agreed terms.
capex_capacity: Opened the largest Nykaa store at Ambience Vasant Kunj, Delhi (over 5,000 sq ft, 100+ brands, with services such as makeovers and skin diagnostics).
Lower-capex formats (Kay Kafe, Nykaa Wanderlust Cart, Nykaa Kiosk) are being used to add footprint quickly.
Nykaa Now is live in 13 cities with over 1,000 brands and 60-minute delivery; the fulfilment cost per order is higher than mainline and is being monitored.
Superstore network covers 1,200+ cities, with 100 more cities added in the quarter.
Capital employed rose to INR 2,211 crore from INR 1,658 crore in Q1 FY24.
demand_pricing: Beauty visits reached about 0.5 billion in Q1 (+22% YoY); annual unique transacting customers crossed 20 million (20.8 million cited) out of about 60 million lifetime buyers.
Beauty orders grew close to 20% YoY; management said the QoQ order dip cited by an analyst (17.5 million to 17.3 million) reflects seasonality.
New launches included Rare Beauty (top-5 prestige brand within weeks), K18, SK-II and Anua. The brand count is 10,000+, with about 160 added in the quarter.

Fashion customer acquisition rose 44% YoY at a 30% lower CAC over two years. Nike D2C platform crossed 1.5 million app installs in under six months; Virtual Closet saw over 200,000 avatars created with more than 2x conversion.
Nykaa Now is priced the same as mainline, since brands fund discounts; the mix is beauty-led, with personal care subcategories growing incrementally.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economic arrangement with Nike, and how is customer data handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Nykaa runs Nike's D2C sites (Nike.in and the iOS/Android apps) end-to-end, including fulfilment, under a retailer-like arrangement with commission-style and service income and inventory protection. Financial terms were not disclosed; the marketplace listing is a standard arrangement.

qa_highlights.question: How will Nykaa Now's EBITDA drag trend as it expands to 25+ cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no margin dilution at current scale; purchase frequency is rising and AOV is consistent with mainline. Fulfilment cost per order is higher and is the cost being watched.

qa_highlights.question: When does Superstore GMV growth normalise toward the 40-45% CAGR ambition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the GST effect normalises from Q3 FY27, after which NSV and GMV growth should converge. The stated target is a 35%+ CAGR reached by FY2030, driven by more retailers, wellness categories and data-led brand placement.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the growth acceleration and how much is market versus company-specific?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a strong market plus execution: penetration and premiumisation in Beauty, assortment and brand additions (1,200+ brands in a year) and new business lines in Fashion. Both businesses said they had grown faster than the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Are marketing efficiency gains structural and how much more is available?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said marketing spend is being held steady while acquisition is pushed, with repeat customers rising as a share of revenue. Fashion CAC is improving, with 44% more new customers acquired YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term TAM and can AUTC growth be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put the relevant online fashion TAM at 65-100 million consumers over five years and said there is no price filter for beauty. The growth lever is frequency and AOV on the 60 million lifetime buyers, not just new acquisition.

risks_watch: GST-led MRP impact on Superstore GMV and the gap between NSV and GMV growth until Q3 FY27.
Nykaa Now fulfilment costs as the network grows from 13 to 25+ cities.

543386|2026-03.headline: Fino Payments Bank's Q4 FY26 total revenue fell 31% YoY, while CASA base rose 22% to 1.75 crore accounts and renewal income hit a record ₹62.2 crore.

543399|2026-03.headline: Tarsons Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 7.3% to INR120.9 crore, but margins compressed on raw material spikes and new-plant costs; FY27 PAT guided moderate.
543399|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, with standalone revenue up 4.4% YoY to about INR97 crore and domestic growth of 11.7% offsetting a 13.4% decline in exports tied to Middle East disruptions. Gross margin fell to 58.5% standalone in Q4 as raw material prices spiked from mid-March, and EBITDA was pressured by commissioning costs at the Amta and Panchla plants. Management said the large capex programme is nearly complete, with full commissioning expected in H1 FY27, and that no major new capex is planned beyond about INR20 crore of maintenance spend. Management guided FY27 PAT to remain at a moderate level, with operating leverage expected to improve from FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Management would not commit; raw material spikes have made Indian producers less competitive versus US manufacturers, and stronger growth needs normalised conditions.

543401|2026-03.headline: Go Fashion Q4 FY26 revenue fell to INR196 crore with EBITDA margin at 25.3%; management guides FY27 SSSG positive and margin recovery from Q2.

Full-year FY26 pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin was 11.5% versus 16.8% in FY25, with EBITDA down about INR40 crore to INR96 crore. Management is closing small EBOs (50-plus in FY26, about 50 more in Q1 FY27) and shifting to 700-plus sq ft stores, while the LFS channel recovered from about minus 30% in Q3 to about minus 7% in Q4 after adjusting for a INR5 crore credit note. 543401|2026-06.headline: Go Fashion Q1 FY27: EBITDA before exceptionals down 2% to INR67.4 crores on marketing spend, while EBO SSSG turned positive at 0.6%.

Management attributed the EBITDA moderation mainly to higher marketing spend, including the brand ambassador partnership. A one-off exceptional charge of INR6.5 crores was booked for write-off of capex on 66 closed stores, and PAT was about INR16 crores. Management presented the quarter as early progress against five FY27 priorities but repeatedly cautioned that one quarter does not make a trend.

segments.commentary: Grew 2% YoY to INR50 crores after a difficult FY26; management says supply-chain disruption with a key LFS partner in Q3-Q4 FY26 has largely normalised.

segments.name: Everyday wear (daily wear concept)
segments.commentary: 15 stores live; 12-13 stated as profitable, with about 12 double-digit EBITDA positive. Sales around INR1,000 per sq ft per month. Target of 25-30 stores by end FY27. Size requirement 1,500-2,000 sq ft.

543411|2026-03.headline: Hi-Tech Pipes Q4 FY26 volume rose 27% to 1.47 lakh tons and revenue rose 102% to INR1,480 crores, while FY27 volume guidance is 6.5-7 lakh tons.
543411|2026-03.overview: Management reported strong Q4 FY26 volume growth of 27% YoY to 1.47 lakh tons and revenue of INR1,480 crores, up 102% YoY. FY26 volume rose to 5.32 lakh tons from 4.85 lakh tons, and EBITDA grew 8% to INR174 crores. Total comprehensive income in Q4 was INR18 crores against INR17.5 crores a year earlier. Management reiterated a 2 million ton capacity roadmap with 1 million tons to be added by FY29, and the call drew heavy questions on a large stock-in-trade cost line that analysts saw as depressing per-ton margins.

qa_highlights.question: What products Hindupur will make and the FY27 volume guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Hindupur is a coated steel tube facility of about 1.5 lakh tons, making coated, pre-galvanised and galvanised tubes mainly for solar. FY27 volume target is 6.5-7 lakh tons.

qa_highlights.question: Greenfield vs brownfield split of the extra 1 million tons.
qa_highlights.answer: Sanand is brownfield and Hindupur greenfield, a 50:50 split; capacity reaches about 1.4 million tons by end FY27.

Management said trading will fall as three newly operational plants (Secunderabad, Gujarat, Jammu) ramp up, and that stock was sold in March to avoid price-volatility losses.

543412|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 GWP rose 17% YoY (N basis) to Rs 6,259 crore, with fresh retail growing 38% and the loss ratio improving to 65.2% from 69.2%. Full-year GWP crossed Rs 20,000 crore (Rs 20,369 crore, up 16%) and FY26 underwriting profit turned positive at Rs 206 crore versus a Rs 165 crore loss in FY25. Reported Q4 PAT was a Rs 55 crore loss against a Rs 271 crore profit a year earlier, driven by the equity-market MTM loss. Management introduced a normalised investment yield of 8%, under which FY26 PAT was Rs 1,222 crore (up 45%) and ROE 13.1%.

segments.commentary: Fresh retail grew 38% YoY in Q4 and 37% for FY26 (N basis); retail policies grew 11% in Q4 and 8% for FY26. Market share was 31.3% in FY26; retail loss ratio 64.8% in Q4 and 68.2% for FY26.

segments.name: Group Health / SME
segments.commentary: Management said SME was 78% of group business in FY26 versus 58% in FY25, with a recalibrated strategy that drove the group loss ratio improvement. No explicit group GWP figure was given.

Reporting moves to 1/n basis for business and growth from FY27.
NEP growth is expected to lag GWP growth because of long-term policy sales, with catch-up expected in coming quarters.
Management expects the long-term share of NEP to keep rising next year.
Agent network to reach 1 million in two years, adding about 1 lakh agents a year.
capex_capacity: Home Healthcare, telemedicine and condition management usage rose 4-5x over the year, with Q4 consumption up about 9x. FY26 included over 90,000 telemedicine calls and over 40,000 pure telemedicine calls.
Claims platform migration to the Medi Assist platform is nearly complete, with the last product set to shift by Q1 FY27 end.
Customer app has over 14 million downloads and more than 1.5 million monthly active users; 95% of fresh premium is collected digitally.
demand_pricing: Retail Health premiums grew 30.2% YoY in H2 FY26 versus 11.2% for non-life. For full FY26, retail health grew close to 20% and non-life 9.3%.
New-to-insurance share of fresh premium was 94% in Q4 (90% a year earlier) and 93% for FY26 (89% in FY25).
Volume retention improved 1-1.5% YoY; the company cited about 86-87% volume retention and a renewal ratio of 99%. GWP-based renewal retention rose 300 bps and NOP-based 100 bps.
Agent productivity rose about 37% on fresh and 18% on total business. Over 90% of retail comes from agency and D2C channels.
Senior citizens are about 20% of the portfolio; the senior citizen commission reduction took effect April 2024 (FY25) and drove part of the commission ratio gain.
Long-term vs annual NEP split is about 80:20, moving 100-150 bps toward long-term on premium basis.
