qa_highlights.answer: Management said frequency and severity were managed in the high-single digits for FY26 and that Q4 benefited from lower frequency. It cited telemedicine and home healthcare usage growth and repricing of about 80% of the book from Q4 FY26 to Q1 FY27, but gave no numerical target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is retail growth lagging the industry, and how should the gap evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prioritises quality and profitable geographies over market share. Its market share was 31.3% in FY26, growth on N basis was 39% for FY26, and the company is not chasing share at the cost of profit.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the loss ratio improvement: renewal book, new business, severity or fraud controls?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gain is a sum of parts: renewal repricing, sourcing quality, geography selection, and fraud, waste and abuse controls. Q4 frequency improvement cut across the whole book.

qa_highlights.question: Is the retention ratio uptick linked to long-term policies?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed the Q3/Q4 retention noise to renewals pulled into September after the GST cut, with some spillover into Q1. Volume retention improved 1-1.5% for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a need for a major repricing in FY27, and is the current price rise enough for the target combined ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no need for above-normal increases. It expects the current annual pricing strategy to be sufficient to hit the target combined ratio.

qa_highlights.question: How is Bima Sugam expected to affect sourcing and renewals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Bima Sugam is a consumer platform for affordable plans, that it will not be zero-cost, and that Star Health is a shareholder and supportive of it.

qa_highlights.question: Did the GST cut lift renewals and sum insured?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Walia said GWP-based renewal retention rose 300 bps, with customers opting for higher sum insured and riders, and that distributor income had risen over 50% since the GST announcement.

543412|2026-06.headline: Star Health Q1 FY27 underwriting profit rose to Rs 111 crore from Rs 16 crore, with CISR improving to 97% and normalised PAT up 44% to Rs 386 crore.

Management guided insurance revenue growth to rise towards 15-16% and expense ratio to fall 30-40 bps a year, while declining to give loss ratio guidance.

Management described upcoming pricing as maintenance-level rather than step-up, with some discounts for non-claimants.

543412|2026-09.headline: Star Health Q2 FY27 underwriting profit rose to Rs 99 crore from a Rs 40 crore loss, with PAT up over threefold to Rs 265 crore.
543412|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 marked the fifth successive quarter of improving loss ratios and underwriting results, with CISR improving 2.9 points to 98%. Gross written premium on a reported 1/n basis grew 19% YoY to Rs 5,275 crore in Q2 and Rs 9,562 crore in H1, while fresh retail health GWP grew 35% in the quarter. Normalized PAT (at an 8% investment yield) rose 70% YoY to Rs 390 crore in Q2. Management flagged that headline growth will moderate in H2 as last year's GST-led surge enters the base, and that regulatory proposals on distribution commissions and expense of management (EoM) are the next key uncertainty.

segments.name: Retail health (fresh)
segments.commentary: Fresh retail GWP grew 35% YoY in Q2 and 36% in H1 on reported 1/n basis; new-to-insurance mix rose to 93% from 89%, with new-to-insurance policies up over 10% and average sum insured up 13%.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Network reached 8.7 lakh agents after adding 39,000 in H1; agency productivity up 19% YoY; agency contributes about 70-75% of fresh business and grew about 25% in Q2 per management.

segments.name: Digital D2C
segments.commentary: D2C grew 137% YoY in H1 and its share of business rose from 8% to 13%; management says D2C has superior combined ratios. Proprietary channels (agency plus D2C) account for over 90% of retail business.

segments.name: Renewal book
segments.commentary: Management says the standalone renewal book now operates below 100% combined ratio; vintage book is about 80% of portfolio. Group business is now a very small share of premium.

guidance_outlook: Company aspires to grow fresh business at 20%+ consistently over a long period and hopes to maintain that for FY27, though optical growth moderation is expected in Q3 and Q4 due to GST-led base.
ROE ambition to move from mid-teens to higher-teens over time, with combined ratio as the key lever.
Retail market share and like-for-like comparability under 1/n reporting expected to be restored only by FY28.
Management believes it has a credible path to the proposed EoM limits through operating leverage, productivity and digitization, but will give more detail once regulation is final.
Company will not disclose point-to-point guidance on individual loss ratio metrics.
capex_capacity: Equity allocation about 14% (slightly less than 14%), with internal strategy to cap at around 15%; management may go beyond 15% if markets are very attractive.

Portfolio duration increased toward a target of about 4 years after G-Sec yields rose; management said it has taken some long-duration G-Sec calls and may extend duration further if yields keep rising.
REITs and InvITs: fully invested against the 3% regulatory limit with a small margin of safety; AIF allocation about 2.1-2.2% of funds and growing slowly.
Digital SBU created last year; Salesforce CRM upgraded; AI bots processed over 7.5 million minutes of call volume at under 20% of human cost.
demand_pricing: Fresh growth is driven by a mix of price, volume and higher average sum insured; management did not split the contribution.
Around 80% of the book was repriced in the last cycle; the remaining portion is being repriced this year, with further correction as needed based on loss ratios.
Packages account for about 80% of claims; hospital negotiations described as business as usual, with the Supreme Court drug-pricing order not yet notified.
Management estimates a fresh-to-insurance market share near 40% (not a reported figure) and notes the reported fresh figure includes portability.
Commission ratio moderated YoY because the senior citizen commission cut (15% to 10%) and other efficiencies now show a full 12-month impact.

qa_highlights.question: How is fresh growth tracking in October and by channel, now that the GST-led base is in place?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects optical moderation in Q3 and Q4 but aims for 20%+ fresh growth; it tracks policies sold, agent activations and digital activations.

qa_highlights.question: Is the loss ratio improvement driven by fresh business or by the older book?
qa_highlights.answer: Improvement is driven by the vintage book (about 80% of portfolio), since the fresh book at about 20% of the portfolio could not drive it alone; renewal book now operates below 100% combined ratio. Fresh and renewal loss ratios are not disclosed separately.

qa_highlights.question: Loss ratio decomposition in Q2 (frequency, severity, pricing) and its sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Loss cost held at mid-single-digit growth while earned premium grew close to double digits; management did not give point-to-point metric guidance and will focus on combined ratio going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Equity and duration positioning, and whether there is an equity cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity about 14%, no incremental purchases this quarter; the 15% level is an internal strategy, not a formal cap. Duration lengthened toward about 4 years via G-Sec calls.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company responding to the Rs 59 crore investment-related loss and its FVTPL classification?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity, ETFs, REITs and InvITs are classified as FVTPL; debt is held to maturity. No breakdown of the Rs 59 crore between realized and unrealized was provided in the call.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the insurance finance income and expense restatement, and will it stay nil?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance finance income and expense (significant financing component on long-term policies) was discontinued as an optional treatment; it is now nil and has no PAT impact because the offsetting income sits in restated insurance revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How are multi-year policies commissioned, and what is the impact of the proposed distribution rules?
qa_highlights.answer: Multi-year policies are around 50% of the fresh book; good agents are paid upfront under Indian GAAP and the amount is deferred under IFRS; clarification is awaited on whether years two and three count as fresh or renewal under the new rules.

risks_watch: Optical moderation of fresh growth in Q3 and Q4 as the GST-driven base builds.

IRDAI distribution reform (commission linked to renewal rates, agent exclusivity, higher rural commissions) and whether the EoM cap of 20% can be met without major OpEx changes; the calculation was not disclosed.
Treatment of multi-year policy commissions (years two and three) under the new distribution rules; about 50% of fresh book is multi-year.
Dark-pattern and data consent norms for D2C, which is growing rapidly.
Supreme Court drug-pricing order and its effect on itemized hospital bills (about 20% of claims are non-package).
Investment book sensitivity to rising yields and a planned RBI policy rate hike cycle.
543412|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on underwriting turnaround and structural sustainability, but guarded on specifics: management declined to split growth drivers, disclose the loss ratio by fresh and renewal, quantify telemedicine savings, or give the Rs 59 crore investment-loss breakdown. On regulation it is supportive of the direction but explicitly awaiting final rules.
key_quotes: Quarter 2 of FY27 has marked the 5th successive quarter of improvement in our loss ratios and underwriting results.
The fresh book at around 20% slice of the portfolio could not have driven outcomes on its own.
As a company, we aspire to grow at 20% plus on fresh business consistently for a long period of time.

rows.why: Proposed commission linkage to renewal rates and a 20% EoM cap were not quantified by management, and multi-year policies (about 50% of fresh book) make the outcome uncertain until regulation is final.

rows.why: Fresh retail GWP grew 35% in Q2 against a GST-led base that enters the comparison, so optical moderation is expected even as the 20%+ aspiration is held.

rows.why: Vintage book is about 80% of portfolio and the standalone renewal book now runs below 100% combined ratio, with five successive quarters of improving loss ratios and CISR at 98% in Q2.

543413|2026-03.headline: Tega Q4 FY26: FY26 revenue up 5% to INR17,736 mn, adjusted EBITDA 22%; consumables flat as orders slipped to Feb–Mar, and Molycop acquisition closed 1 June 2026.
543413|2026-03.overview: Tega reported FY26 revenue of INR17,736 mn (up 5% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of INR3,967 mn (22% margin), after exceptional items of INR775 mn (Molycop deal costs) and INR64 mn (labour code), with a further INR839 mn total labour-code charge cited. Consumables revenue was flat for the year, with Q4 consumables revenue down INR162 mn YoY, which management attributed to orders landing late in Q3/Q4 and shipping delays from container and vessel constraints. Equipment grew 25% to INR2,688 mn for FY26. The Molycop acquisition completed on 1 June 2026 with Apollo Funds as a minority partner; consolidation starts from Q1 FY27, and management flagged about USD30 mn of transaction costs payable in Q1 and a target of 3x leverage in 3 to 4 years.

vs 58% in the same period last year
vs INR5,428 mn in Q4 FY25
vs INR1,566 mn, 29% in Q4 FY25
down INR162 mn vs INR4,568 mn

segments.name: Consumables (Tega)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue flat YoY (FY24 +10%, FY25 +11%); Q4 revenue INR4,406 mn vs INR4,568 mn. Management says Q4 consumables EBITDA margin normally runs 27–28%, and an analyst estimated 27.7% excluding the INR776 mn one-off.

segments.name: Equipment (Tega)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR2,688 mn, +25% YoY; Q4 revenue up INR69 mn (+9%). Management guides 25% growth in FY27 and 12–13% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Molycop (grinding media, acquired 1 June 2026)
segments.commentary: Management's FY26 (July–June) estimate: revenue ~USD1,539 mn in the prior year, ~1% growth and ~12% EBITDA margin. FY27 planning assumption of ~3% growth, under reassessment.

guidance_outlook: Consumables: management reiterates 15%+ long-term CAGR; FY27 Equipment growth of about 25% and 12–13% Equipment EBITDA margin.
Blended group EBITDA margin guided at 21–22%, held despite FY26 at the low end.
Molycop acquisition costs of about USD30 mn to be paid in Q1 FY27; more deal costs possible in later quarters.
Molycop FY27 maintenance capex budgeted at USD20 mn; growth capex not yet factored in. Chile plant capex of USD25–30 mn to complete in FY27.
Sustaining and modernisation capex for Tega of INR50–60 crore, funded from internal accruals.
Synergy framework (revenue synergies at Tega, cost synergies at Molycop, non-core asset sales) is being re-evaluated; 100-day and 200-day plans in progress; no numbers yet.
capex_capacity: Chile plant: civil works about 50–60% complete; commissioning targeted for early Q3 FY27, subject to regulatory approvals. Revenue booking may start end of Q4 FY27 or slip to FY28.

Acquisition debt: about USD838 mn of Molycop debt consolidated from 1 June (down from over USD1,050 mn after about USD220 mn paydown); INR1,500 crore raised at the parent level from Standard Chartered, Axis and EXIM, already drawn.
Molycop capex about 2–3% of revenue; management says it is cash-flow funded with no new borrowing needed.
Tega sustaining capex INR50–60 crore a year, funded from internal accruals; Chile funded from accruals and existing borrowings.
demand_pricing: Order book INR12,060 mn at 31 March 2026, of which INR9,060 mn executable within 12 months; pending orders up about 18% YoY (17% in another reference).
Q4 orders came mainly in February and March, so revenue lags 3–6 months given bespoke design-led execution.

Consumables shipments were held up by Middle East disruption (vessel and container availability), lifting finished goods by about INR50 crore, equal to about INR100 crore of potential revenue; alternate routes being sought.
Market backdrop cited: gold demand above 5,000 tonnes in CY2025; copper demand growth about 3% vs supply about 2%.
Molycop FY27 growth may be weaker than the earlier ~7–8% view, as Cobre Panama and Grasberg restarts are now expected in FY28 rather than FY27.

qa_highlights.question: When will Molycop be consolidated, and how much debt is added?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidation starts 1 June 2026, with the first full quarter in Q1 FY27 (one month of Molycop). About USD838 mn of debt is added at the group level, and INR1,500 crore of parent-level debt was already raised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consumables revenue stay flat when guidance was ~8% and the 15% CAGR has been missed in recent years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed late-quarter order intake and logistics disruption. It said the 15% long-term CAGR guidance still holds, citing cyclicality, and that executable orders are up about 17%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Molycop acquisition cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About USD30 mn of acquisition and financing-related costs will be paid in Q1 FY27, including debt refinancing and preference costs. Management says these are one-offs and not a loss, and more costs may follow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Chile capex of USD25–30 mn completes in FY27, Tega sustaining capex is INR50–60 crore, and Molycop maintenance capex is USD20 mn. Growth capex is not yet set.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 25% Equipment growth in FY27 and what is the new product?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites a new aggregate product with a Japanese partner to launch in Q3 FY27, plus tailwinds from capex, power and mineral beneficiation, and export pushes into Canada, CIS and the Middle East.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital improve, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Payables improved and debtor days fell. Management guides 100–105 days DSO to be maintained, with absolute receivables varying with sales volume.

risks_watch: Consumables execution: Q4 shortfall and FG build-up of about INR50 crore need to convert to revenue in Q1–Q2 FY27.
Molycop integration, synergy quantification and deleveraging to 3x within 3–4 years.
Further Molycop acquisition costs in Q1 FY27 and beyond; reported profit could be depressed in the consolidated P&L.
Chile plant commissioning slipping because of regulatory approvals, which would push revenue into FY28.
Molycop volume recovery deferred from FY27 to FY28, with uncertainty over the 3% FY27 growth assumption.

Molycop has a financial year ending at 30th June.
We remain firm on our guidance of 15% plus on a long-term basis.

543413|2026-06.headline: Tega Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR17.2bn with 15% adjusted EBITDA margin, including one month of Molycop; consumables grew 36% YoY.
543413|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first quarter consolidating Molycop, but only for June 2026 after the June 1 closing. Consolidated revenue was about INR17.2bn and adjusted EBITDA about INR2.6bn (15% margin) before INR1.9bn of one-time acquisition and integration costs. Legacy Tega consumables delivered strong growth and margin expansion, while the equipment business fell sharply on delayed customer clearances. Management stressed that one month of Molycop is too short to draw full-year conclusions, but said June was directionally ahead of acquisition expectations.

qa_highlights.question: How will revenue ramp from cross-selling across Tega and Molycop networks, beyond the USD20mn cost synergies?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mohanka said the revenue ramp is expected from Q3 to Q4 FY27; it is early days, and quantified guidance will come in a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is Molycop's margin seasonal, is the current margin steady state, and are there one-off RM or macro items?
qa_highlights.answer: Patrick Koley said there is little quarter-to-quarter seasonality, June was historically Molycop's strongest quarter, and margin should be relatively flat in coming quarters. Molycop manages to per-ton margin because about 85% of contracts are steel-index linked.

qa_highlights.question: Chile plant commissioning status?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mohanka said the plant is on track for soft commissioning around January 2027 and commercial production around March 2027, subject to local regulatory clearances expected within a two-month window.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any further one-time costs beyond the current quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mohanka confirmed the Q1 one-time costs are the full amount. The analyst tallied INR110cr this year plus about INR75-80cr last year, totalling about INR190cr, which management confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Group and Molycop debt levels and year-end expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Ravi Joshi said group total debt is INR112bn including about INR26bn of redeemable preference shares. Patrick Koley said Molycop net debt was USD672mn at June 30 and is expected to fall by year-end, with ABL swings driven by bar payments.

qa_highlights.question: Molycop capex and volume outlook, plus Latin America competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Patrick Koley said 10-month capex is about USD28mn, normalised capex is in the low USD30mn range, and volume is expected up about 5% and EBITDA up about 4% on a 10-month comparable basis. Volume was 1.204mt for the 12 months to June 2026 vs 1.223mt prior year. Lance Dawber said Molycop has competed with China for decades and retains its lead through lead times and local support.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 finance cost, Tega capex, and consumables growth and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Ravi Joshi guided FY27 finance cost to INR110-120cr and Tega capex excluding Molycop to about USD40mn including Chile. Mehul Mohanka maintained about 15% consumables CAGR and said pass-through of costs has a one-quarter lag, supporting a 20-23% margin.

543415|2026-06.headline: Anand Rathi Wealth Q1 FY27 underlying PAT rose 24% YoY to INR116 crore, with AUM up 21% to INR1,06,300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 800-store guidance and franchisee mix stay?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, 800 net stores at net level are maintained; 131 of 146 net additions in Q1 were franchisee stores, and the internal split was broadly 50:50.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Minimum wage increases from 1 June (about 60% in Karnataka and 25%+ in Telangana vs typical ~4%) only had one month in Q1; the retention bonus plan was stopped for new joiners from 1 March, and incentives are being restructured.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA fall YoY despite flat private label sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mix and higher costs, predominantly employee cost, drove the EBITDA decline; gross margin fell on mix.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the ~200 bps sequential gross margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: About 100 bps from lower private label mix, about 70 bps from a smaller inventory provision release versus Q4, and about 40 bps from year-end supplier discounts not repeated in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the promoter pledged debt outstanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said close to INR1,150 crore including interest; repayment decisions rest with the family office, not the listed company.

Edible Oil volume grew only 2% due to channel destocking and supply chain issues amid palm oil volatility, while Industry Essentials grew volume 13%. Management said July trends had improved and reiterated FY27 segment operating guidance, and changed segment disclosure to revenue, volume growth and margin for Food and FMCG.

543463|2026-06.headline: Vedant Fashions Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 7.2% to INR3,014 mn, with PAT up 14.7% to about INR81 crore and domestic SSG at 3.8%.

Revenue from operations was about INR3,014 mn (INR301 crore), up 7.2%, with gross margin of 65.7% and EBITDA margin of 44.6%. EBITDA grew 10.8% and PAT margin was 26.7%. segments.name: Twamev (premium)
segments.commentary: Management said Twamev outperformed the company in overall growth in Q1.

segments.name: Diwas

segments.commentary: Together about 5% of revenue today; new leadership team built and growth targets described as aggressive. SIS is a few hundred sq ft versus EBO average of about 3,000 sq ft.

Marketing will shift from top-of-mind branding to consideration and conversion-led social campaigns for Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory days?

qa_highlights.question: Share of MBO, SIS and e-commerce in revenue?

543470|2026-03.headline: Softtech Q4 FY26 revenue rose 50% YoY to INR 46.6 crore and FY26 revenue hit INR 132.9 crore, with management targeting INR 300 crore by FY29.

FY26 revenue was INR 132.9 crore (up 40%), EBITDA INR 32.2 crore (24% margin) and PAT INR 5.3 crore. Management highlighted the TDR exchange mandate in Mumbai (BMC), an Airport Authority of India mandate, first CivitSUSTAIN order, and early German and US traction. Order book is about INR 232 crore against a pipeline of about INR 436 crore. This was the company's maiden earnings call.

vs INR 0.1 crore in Q4 FY25; +133% QoQ

segments.name: CivitBUILD, BIM/GIS services and others
segments.commentary: Together about 15-20% of revenue. CivitBUILD has won private construction-enterprise projects; Middle East and African work exists.

Mandatory on the platform from 10 May 2026; management cites 70-80% margins. Revenue recognised in FY27 expected to be partial.

Germany prototyping with customers over the next three months, with a dual launch of the twinning platform and permitting portal planned.
CivitTwin AI platform (12 agents) launched in Mumbai; a German version has been launched.

Gratuity liability was increased by provisions tied to the revised Labour Code effective November 2025.

qa_highlights.answer: Order book about INR 200-odd crore, about 60% to be booked this year, roughly 40% of that recurring. Pipeline conversion probability is above 60%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did provisions rise from INR 45 lakh to about INR 2.5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Government retentions and deposits of 1-2% of invoice value are held for long periods. qa_highlights.question: Details of the CivitSUSTAIN order with Mitsubishi and the GIFT City pipeline?

qa_highlights.answer: About 100 registrations and some transactions so far. Revenue is 0.5% of TDR exchange transaction value. FY26 BMC volume was about INR 8,000 crore; MMRDA, MSRDC, Navi Mumbai, Vasai-Virar and Thane are additional and are being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 revenue reach about INR 170 crore including TDR?

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a 15-year permit dataset as a moat and the enterprise penetration as a barrier. Team growth will be slower than revenue growth, with some specialist hiring.

543482|2026-03.headline: Eureka Forbes Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.6% YoY to INR 684 crore with record 13.2% adjusted EBITDA margin; FY27 margins guided to hold.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 13.1% to INR 90 crore at a 13.2% margin, the company's highest ever, despite intensifying input cost inflation. A calibrated 6-7% price increase was taken in April 2026 to offset West Asia-driven cost and currency pressures. Management guided to holding FY27 margins at least and stepping up revenue growth, while service revenue growth is expected to show up more visibly in FY27 and beyond.

segments.name: Air purifiers

segments.name: Water softeners
segments.commentary: Maintained strong double-digit growth; three years of strong growth, with IoT-enabled products in the portfolio.

segments.name: Service and AMC
segments.commentary: AMC bookings grew double digits in FY26, with the fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit booking growth; a higher multi-year AMC mix is building deferred income (liability up about 9% in aggregate). Service revenue growth is expected to step up in FY27 but management did not disclose service revenue separately.

segments.commentary: New simplified filter assortment, new distribution system and consumer education launched; influencer campaign has generated over 1 billion views. Management described this as a multi-year build.

543498|2026-06.headline: Motherson Sumi Wiring Q1 FY27 revenue grew 37% YoY, but copper and minimum-wage costs hit profitability; ~INR600 crore employee cost line flagged.
543498|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as resilient, with revenue growth outpacing the industry despite cost headwinds from elevated copper prices and sharply higher manpower costs after government-mandated minimum wage increases. Of the 37% revenue growth, management attributed 7 percentage points to copper pass-through and the rest to volume, content, premiumisation and new model launches. Greenfield plants held their prior-quarter run-rate of about INR450 crore and remained at break-even, with no meaningful profit contribution yet. Copper pass-through is still on a 3 to 6 month lag, with the quarter-on-quarter lag delta reduced to about 7% from 17% previously. EVs were 8.5% of revenue.

segments.name: Greenfield plants (three new plants)
segments.commentary: Revenue run-rate held at ~INR450 crore, same as prior quarter, with break-even maintained; some plants still ramping and expected to contribute to profit in one or two quarters. Management declined to disclose plant-level EBITDA or revenue split.

segments.name: EV vs ICE business
segments.commentary: EV-related business was 8.5% of Q1 revenue. Management said this is EV versus ICE business, not high-voltage alone, and gave no further breakdown.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical guidance given. Management targets return on capital employed above 40%.
Staff cost trajectory depends on other state governments' minimum wage actions; nothing concluded yet, and the current mandated increase is fully reflected in Q1 results.

Customer recovery of wage increases is under 'constructive discussion' with no timeline. Management said most customers are on a 3-month pass-through cycle, with some pending price hikes from March and June quarters expected to flow into the September quarter.
Copper pass-through lag remains 3 to 6 months; management aims to reduce it to about one month or 15 days.
Capex for the current year is budgeted to be funded from internal accruals.
Management indicated new expansion plans may be announced in coming quarters once the 80% utilisation threshold is approached and customer forecasts firm up.
capex_capacity: Greenfield plants are ramping up; utilisation is at the same level as the prior quarter, with improvement noted and some plants still scaling.
Management said it expands capacity once overall utilisation reaches about 80%; it expects to announce new expansion in the next few quarters, but no specific new plant was named.
Current-year capex budget to be funded from internal accruals; no new debt planned for it.
Management said greenfield plants should merge into the regular business after a few months and deliver margins similar to existing plants, with the scalability gap attributed to productivity.
demand_pricing: Revenue grew 37% YoY, with ~7 pp from copper inflation and the remainder from volume growth, content increase, premiumisation and new OEM model launches.
Customer-specified components are priced through mutual negotiation with suppliers and customers; plastic and other input increases are not an automatic pass-through.
Management said the company has seen content per vehicle rise, not fall, under new architectures, and it is a design partner for future Japanese OEM vehicles.
Management is engine-agnostic, supplying leading ICE and EV platforms in India.

qa_highlights.question: How have greenfield plants performed in Q1 in revenue and EBITDA, and has break-even held?
qa_highlights.answer: Break-even was achieved last quarter and maintained at ~INR450 crore run-rate. Profit contribution is expected in one or two quarters as plants ramp. Plant-level profitability is not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Will wage hike impact be passed through, and by when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said talks are constructive but no timeline can be given. It declined to quantify expected recovery, citing confidentiality, and said customers recognise the cost as manpower-linked.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR600 crore employee cost is attributable to minimum wage hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase was largely from minimum wage hikes, with NCR wages up 30-40%, and the change QoQ is largely due to this. It did not give a specific number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the copper pass-through shortfall now?
qa_highlights.answer: The lag delta is about 7% in the current results, versus 17% in the prior quarter. Quarterly resets are done; 6-month-cycle customers are still pending. Most customers are on a 3-month basis.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin return to 34-35% in six months if raw material costs stay flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first priority is to recover costs to normalised levels. It added that after cost recovery, the sales-to-raw-material ratio will not match the past, and margin improvement is a medium-term goal.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of new zonal or 48V architectures on content per vehicle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is ready to supply any architecture, has not seen de-contenting in India, and sees content rising with features. It acknowledged that long-term simplification is possible but said it would take a very long time.

risks_watch: Copper pass-through lag of 3 to 6 months; a 7% QoQ delta remains in Q1 results and will flow into Q2 as some price hikes are pending.
Minimum wage increases in other states remain unresolved, so the staff cost line may rise further.
Greenfield plants are not yet profit-accretive; watch whether they turn profitable in the next one or two quarters.
Management gave no quantified recovery of wage cost; customer negotiations are open-ended.
Long-term risk from zonal and 48V architectures simplifying harnesses, though management sees limited near-term impact.

543514|2026-03.headline: Veranda FY26 revenue rose 35% to INR 482 crore and PAT turned positive at INR 130 crore; FY27 guidance is INR 670 crore revenue and INR 144 crore PAT.

FY26 PAT of INR 130 crore compares with a loss of about INR 252 crore in FY25, and this was the fifth consecutive PAT-positive quarter. Management said FY26 guidance was broadly achieved, with non-commerce well ahead and commerce broadly in line. The J.K. Shah Commerce Education demerger is awaiting final NCLT approval, with listing targeted for end-July or mid-August 2026. FY27 guidance is revenue of about INR 670 crore and PAT above INR 144 crore.

543523|2026-06.headline: Campus Activewear Q1 FY27: revenue up 12.2%, volume up 11.7%, EBITDA margin 15.9%, PAT up 17.7%, with ASP drag from temporary accounting and mix effects.
543523|2026-06.overview: Campus reported 12.2% revenue growth, 11.7% volume growth, 15.9% EBITDA margin and 17.7% PAT growth in Q1 FY27. Reported ASP growth was held back by a Walmart (Flipkart/Myntra) GT-charge netting change (about 2.5%) and a school-shoe mix shift (about 2%), both described as Q1-only effects. An 8% MRP hike effective 1 April 2026 gave underlying core-category ASP growth of about 5%. Management guided to mid-double-digit FY27 growth, split between ASP and volume, and reiterated a 17-19% EBITDA margin aspiration. Record Q1 production and record distributor orders were highlighted ahead of the festive season.

financial_highlights.change: Management says about 4.5-5% was temporary (GT netting ~2%, franchise SOR transition ~2.5%); normalised growth about 4%-plus ex these factors per management's framing
Analyst-cited figure; management did not dispute it

Underlying ASP increase, core Stuck-On category
Additional depreciation from Paonta Sahib and Pantnagar plants
Minimum wage cost in other expenses

segments.name: School shoes
segments.commentary: Revenue up nearly 50% YoY; about 40% of Q1 volume growth came from this category, expected to normalise from Q2.

segments.name: Sneakers
segments.commentary: Q1 contributed about 12-13% of volume; management targets about 30% growth for the category in FY27, down from near-100% historically.

segments.name: Open footwear (sandals/slippers)
segments.commentary: Slower growth, about 4-5% below rest of category, attributed to CNG/LPG supply constraints affecting hot-and-cold machines during the war-related period.

segments.name: Franchise (FOFO/SOR)
segments.commentary: Management cited about 25% de-growth in franchise revenue in Q1 from the outright-to-SOR model transition across 158 stores (about 2.5% revenue impact); 18 EBOs opened in Q1, the highest in 6-8 quarters.

segments.name: Marketplace and brand.com
segments.commentary: Marketplace operations up mid-double digits; brand.com up over 100% YoY; company-owned stores SSG about 20%.

segments.name: General trade Gujarat
segments.commentary: GT grew at least 20-25% faster than rest of country over the period; Maharashtra now second-largest GT state after UP.

segments.name: Elan by Campus
segments.commentary: Neo-casual launch about 60 days old, priced Rs. 1,899-2,599, selling in about 100-110 own stores plus Amazon, Myntra and brand.com; next set planned for festive season.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target: mid-double-digit overall revenue growth, split between ASP and volume; management said volume is expected to be high single digit and ASP growth of at least 6-7% from Q2 onwards.
Management is '100% confident' of delivering the 17-19% EBITDA margin band for FY27.
Store additions target: about 90-100 stores by end FY27 (guidance range 80-120).
Employee cost as % of sales expected to be proportionate to FY26; no further incremental wage cost expected beyond what is already baked in.
Festive timing: Diwali in November 2026; BBD shifts to October from September, so some marketplace revenue may move from Q2 to Q3.
Management does not plan further MRP increases; expects raw material cost relief to flow into P&L as volatility subsides.
capex_capacity: Record Q1 production, with July 2026 the highest-ever production month, to build festive inventory.
Installed annual capacity cited at about 31 million pairs, down from 36 million two years ago, due to shutdown of about 4-5 million pairs of old DIP capacity.
New manufacturing facilities at Paonta Sahib and Pantnagar commissioned and ramping up; sneakers production also from Haridwar and Pantnagar.
Franchise EBO ROI cited at 18-30% depending on store economics; franchisees pay deposit on inventory, company controls inventory, discounting and replenishment.
Franchise master partners to rise from about 8-9 to about 16; about 8 new partners added this year.
demand_pricing: 8% MRP hike effective 1 April 2026 across key categories; management says volumes grew despite it and resistance has been limited. No further hikes planned.
Management said some demand tapering was seen in the last quarter, citing geopolitical factors and floods in Maharashtra and Gujarat, but its demand reading remains positive.
Record orders at the distributor meet held in May 2026, giving visibility on festive demand.
Management sees some constraints at smaller organised and unorganised competitors due to working-capital stress, though impact on festive supply is unclear.

Price-point mix: management said Rs. 999-1,500 remains the core shoe segment; analyst pointed to about 7% two-year CAGR decline in sub-Rs. 1,500 revenue, which management attributed to the 8% price hike shifting products above Rs. 1,500 and reporting changes.

qa_highlights.question: Vidisha Seth (Ambit): Is the 8% MRP hike, above industry levels, risking volume or share given elasticity in economy key products, and will there be another hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 8% is a fair hike, accepted with limited resistance, and volumes grew despite it; RM inflation has been fully absorbed and no further MRP hikes will be taken. Raw-material relief is expected to flow back into P&L as markets stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Avinash (Motilal Oswal): Why did sub-Rs. 1,500 revenue decline about 7% on a two-year CAGR basis, and is the company exiting price points?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not exiting price points and Rs. 999-1,500 remains the core; the decline reflects products moving above Rs. 1,500 after the 8% hike, a change in reporting, and faster closed-shoe growth versus open footwear. Gaps at economy price points are being filled over the next couple of months before the season.

qa_highlights.question: Avinash: Why did installed capacity fall from 36 million to 31 million pairs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 4-5 million pairs of old DIP capacity were shut as uneconomic; school shoes were moved from DIP into Stuck-On, which has higher ASP and margin. Stuck-On capacity is growing.

qa_highlights.question: Umang Mehta (Kotak): How much did school shoes contribute to volume growth, and is the margin 17-19% band still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: School shoes contributed about 40% of Q1 volume growth and will normalise from Q2. Management targets FY27 mid-double-digit growth split between ASP (at least 6-7% from Q2) and volume, and said it is 100% confident of the 17-19% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Umang Mehta: What drove the faster growth in other expenses excluding A&P?
qa_highlights.answer: Neeraj Gupta said about Rs. 5 crore was minimum-wage cost, about Rs. 2.5 crore was advertising and marketing (distributor meet and logo launch), and about Rs. 2.5 crore was depreciation/indirect cost from the new Paonta Sahib and Pantnagar plants.

qa_highlights.question: Devanshu Bansal (Emkay): Why is EBITDA growth 11% when revenue growth is about 15-16% ex-accounting changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Walmart GT netting is an accounting change with no absolute EBITDA impact. Employee cost rose about 15% (10% annualisation and increments, 5% new hiring) plus higher SG&A, which drove the gap. FY27 employee cost as % of sales is expected to be in line with FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Shraddha Kapadia (SMFS): Can volume growth stay double-digit for FY27, and what is the Elan by Campus traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not promise double-digit volume but said volume will be high single digit, with ASP and volume together delivering mid-double-digit revenue growth. Elan, about 60 days old at Rs. 1,899-2,599, sells in about 100-110 own stores plus Amazon, Myntra and brand.com, with a second set planned for festive season.

qa_highlights.question: Prerna Jhunjhunwala (Elara): What is the store opening plan, and how do franchise economics work under the SOR model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 90-100 openings in FY27 (range 80-120), with master franchise partners rising from about 8-9 to about 16. Under SOR, the company controls inventory and discounting, franchisees pay an inventory deposit and bear rent, and EBO ROI is about 18-30%.

qa_highlights.question: Ajay Nandavar (individual investor): Why is open footwear growing slower, and how does Gujarat franchise growth coexist with trade growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandals use hot-and-cold machines dependent on CNG/LPG, which were constrained during the war period, so growth is about 4-5% below the rest of the category. Management said franchise stores have not cannibalised GT, which grew at least 20-25% faster than the rest of the country in Gujarat.

qa_highlights.question: Devanshu Bansal (follow-up): Is the 8% hike in line with industry, and what signs show consumer acceptance and lower competitive intensity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peers took similar or slightly lower hikes; the May distributor meet recorded record orders after the hike. Management cited marketplace growth in the mid-double digits, company-owned store SSG of about 20% and brand.com growth above 100%, and said some smaller and unorganised players faced production constraints due to working-capital stress.

risks_watch: Sustainability of ASP recovery to 6-7% from Q2: the 2.5% Walmart GT netting and 2% school-shoe mix effects must reverse as stated, and the 8% hike must hold without volume loss.
Volume normalisation after school shoes (about 40% of Q1 volume growth) taper, against a high-single-digit FY27 volume target.
EBITDA growth (11%) lagging revenue growth; the 17-19% margin band depends on employee cost (about 15% growth) and SG&A staying in line with FY26 and on raw-material relief.
Demand tapering noted in the last quarter (geopolitics, Maharashtra and Gujarat floods); record festive inventory built in Q1 and July raises inventory-risk exposure if festive demand disappoints.
Franchise transition: about 25% franchise de-growth in Q1 across 158 stores; the SOR model's accounting and store-opening pace (90-100 target) need to be tracked.
Sub-Rs. 1,500 revenue two-year CAGR decline of about 7%; management says economy price-point gaps will be filled before the season.
Elan by Campus and sneaker growth (about 30% target) are early-stage; the Diwali and Big Billion Day shift (October) may move some marketplace revenue from Q2 to Q3.
key_quotes: So, we are, yes, we will be close to double-digit. We cannot promise a double-digit volume growth, but it will be high single digits for sure, right?
Absolutely, Umang. Yes, we are 100% confident of delivering that. There is no reason not to deliver the margin.
RM inflation has been fully absorbed.
So, it is just a recalibration of the DIP.

Cautious and somewhat evasive on the precise drivers of the 11% EBITDA growth gap, on the sub-Rs. 1,500 revenue decline and on demand tapering; several answers were deferred to offline follow-up.

543524|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 24% to INR459.9 crores and PAT 38% to INR78.2 crores, but FY26 revenue growth slowed to 12% amid weak seasonal demand.
543524|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue reached INR459.9 crores (up 24% YoY), EBITDA INR144.7 crores (up 26%, 31.5% margin) and PAT INR78.2 crores (up 38%, about 17% excluding a deferred tax adjustment). Full-year FY26 revenue was INR1,703 crores (up 12%), EBITDA INR544 crores (up 11%, 32% margin) and PAT INR282 crores (up 15.3%). Management attributed the weak full-year growth to the absence of seasonal volume uplift in Q2 and Q3 and weaker international patient flows, and said ~20% growth is targeted for FY27. Occupancy was 45.3% group-wide in Q4, with mature hospitals at about 52%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 IP discharge growth was organic, and what did acquisitions contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquired and newly added units contributed about 9–10% of IP growth; Guwahati and Warangal contributed about 7–8% of revenue growth, with volume mix said to be similar.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the recent volume improvement is due to digital and marketing initiatives?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is implementing a new CRM and Hospital Information System; early signs are visible but not all of the volume uplift is attributed to them. More visible results are expected by end of Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can ALOS be reduced further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ALOS is clinically driven, at about 2.7 days for three years; changes in case mix could move it to 2.7–2.8 days.

qa_highlights.question: Indore arrangement: who funds the capex and what is the structure?
qa_highlights.answer: The partner builds base structure and leases a semi-warm shell for 20–30 years; Rainbow pays lease rent and invests in fit-outs and equipment at about INR65–70 lakh per bed.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the decline in mature-hospital occupancy and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Absence of seasonal uplift in Q2 and Q3 was the main reason; Q4 mature occupancy rose to about 52%. Management expects mature hospitals at about 60% in the coming year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the M&A strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Target assets with at least 50 operational beds that can scale to 100+; the search is pan-India, with no fixed geographic preference.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance capex is about INR45 crore a year; growth capex is INR400–500 crore for Gurugram over two years plus INR300–350 crore for other projects. The company has no debt and expects to fund the pipeline internally.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive impact of maternity consolidation among top players?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rainbow is the leader in pediatrics and is likely second- or third-largest in maternity; it competes on larger hospitals (minimum 50 beds) rather than boutique players.

Mumbai Malad 100-bed brownfield hospital (definitive agreement signed); Nellore 70-bed Prime Children's Hospital acquired; Guntur 50-bed leased hospital.
Management said it is 'not far' from breakeven at Rajahmundry and Electronic City; Hennur and HRBR are still in investment phase.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 revenue growth remain in the mid-20s after the higher base?

qa_highlights.question: Organic growth ex-acquisitions?

qa_highlights.question: Mature-cluster ARPOB up about 10%: why?

qa_highlights.question: Mumbai margin expectations and doctor model?

qa_highlights.question: Bengaluru hospital breakeven timing and losses?

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% growth the medium-term revenue target?

Entry into high-cost markets (Mumbai, NCR) with higher employee and doctor costs; Mumbai margins are not yet defined.
Integration of acquired hospitals (Nellore, Guntur, Malad) and the Malad JV structure with three doctor-promoters; ownership and lock-in terms were not disclosed.
Execution across multiple new geographies with management bandwidth and doctor-recruitment constraints, particularly in the Northeast.

Inpatient discharges up 28%, outpatient consultations up 25%, deliveries up 23%; occupancy over 41%; ARPOB up 6%.

Q2 FY27 revenue growth guided to the 20% range and above 20%; management said about 20% annual growth would double revenue in roughly four years, described as directional, not a formal target. Expects to cross INR 2,000 crore revenue by FY27 end.

Newer hospitals: Rajahmundry at about breakeven; Electronic City expected to break even in 2-3 months; new Bengaluru hospitals (HRBR, Electronic City) break even within 12-15 months, all within about 18 months.

Acquisitions (Guwahati, Warangal) are EBITDA-positive; Guwahati near company-average margins; Warangal to reach company-level margins within a year. Management does not expect acquisitions to dilute EBITDA.
Mumbai (Malad): no precise margin given; EBITDA margins should eventually exceed 20%. Core doctors to stay full-time, with hybrid model possible for some specialty doctors.
key_quotes: we remain confident of delivering revenue growth in the 20% range during the second quarter as well. We expect growth to remain above 20%.

We continue to expect EBITDA margins to return to the 24% –25% range on a pre -Ind AS basis by the end of the year.

543526|2026-03.headline: LIC FY26 net VNB rose 41.63% to ₹14,179 crore, with VNB margin up 360 bps to 21.2% on non-par mix and economic assumptions.
543526|2026-03.overview: LIC reported record FY26 PAT of ₹57,419 crore (up 19.25% YoY) and net VNB of ₹14,179 crore (up 41.63%), with margin at 21.2% versus 17.6%. Non-par share of individual APE rose to 35.11% from 27.69% a year earlier, and the solvency ratio improved to 2.35 from 2.11. Embedded value grew only 1.58% to ₹7,89,185 crore because of ₹1.00 lakh crore-plus of equity and debt MTM declines in the year. Management flagged upcoming risk-based capital (RBC) rules as the reason it is cautious on dividend payout, even after raising the final dividend to ₹20 per share pre-bonus.

segments.name: Individual business
segments.commentary: Individual APE ₹43,335 crore; non-par APE rose 43.78% to ₹15,214 crore, 35.11% of individual APE. Individual market share fell to 36.6% from 37.46%.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group premium ₹1,96,609 crore (+16.26%); group APE ₹23,626 crore. Group market share 70.11% vs 71.19%. Group contributed about 19% of VNB per the Appointed Actuary's breakdown.

segments.name: Bancassurance and alternate channels
segments.commentary: NBP ₹5,076 crore (+45.19%): banks ₹3,151 crore (+22.30%), alternate channels ₹1,925 crore (+109.36%). Share of individual NBP 7.51% vs 5.59%. Policy count fell sharply, which management attributed to a microfinance corporate agency issue.

segments.name: Agency channel
segments.commentary: Agency sourced 91.75% of new business premium and 98.42% of policies. Individual agents fell to 14,57,045 from 14,86,851.

guidance_outlook: No formal numeric guidance. Management expects VNB margin to keep improving, driven by higher ticket size and better persistency, but said further expansion will be gradual and slower from here.
Management said it is not looking for major changes in the business mix from here and aims to consolidate, with VNB growth coming from either margin or volume.
Management said maturity outgo will stay high through January 2027 from 25-year-old Jeevan Shree-type assured-benefit policies.
Dividend payout policy will be finalised only after RBC outcomes are clear; management expects the increased payout to be sustained.
April 2026 sales were described as good, ahead of the prior year, across participating and non-participating products.
risks_watch: RBC framework timing and calibration, which is likely to be equity-sensitive and could constrain capital and payout.
Equity and debt MTM volatility: ₹53,698 crore equity and ₹46,853 crore debt fall in FY26 hit EV growth (only +1.58%).
Persistency on a premium basis softened in the 13th and 25th months, and the 61st-month figure fell to 59.31% from 63.12%. The positive persistency variance (₹3,509 crore) may not repeat.
Margin sustainability: the GST charge, RFR tailwind and mix benefit may not recur, and management said margin could be challenged in the next three years.
Agent count down to 14,57,045 from 14,86,851, and bancassurance policy count down about 36%.
Upcoming Ind AS/IFRS transition and its effect on VIF-to-CSM translation, which is still being worked on.
Heavy maturity outgo through January 2027 from high sum assured legacy policies.
543526|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on headline growth (VNB, margin, PAT, bancassurance), but noticeably cautious on dividend policy and margin outlook, deferring to RBC clarity. Evasive on the FY27 margin level and product-level IRR questions.
key_quotes: We are now very confident that having achieved significant directional changes, we are now on a path of superior growth with sharper focus on enhanced performance parameters.
We do not want to create expectations which cannot be sustainable for future, as a responsible organization, we would like how the RBC pans out.
This journey possibly can be very gradual and slow from here because we have seen even for the industry, the margins have been around between 20s to maximum 30s for a very short period of time.
This is the highest PAT in our history.

qa_highlights.question: Which products drove the non-par individual savings growth in Q4, and how much of that momentum continues into FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Uthup Joseph said savings bucket grew about 48.40%, led by Jeevan Utsav on ticket size; Jeevan Labh contributed about 40% of par savings premium. No FY27 momentum figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the VNB margin bridge from 17.6% to 21.2%, and what were the operating assumption and EV walk items?
qa_highlights.answer: A.K. Srivastava: business mix +3%, RFR +3.4%, operating assumption changes including GST -2.8%. EV walk: unwind ₹74,748 crore, operating assumption changes -₹1,663 crore, operating experience variance +₹92,639 crore, equity MTM -₹53,698 crore, debt MTM -₹46,853 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the operating variance positive for several years, and what is the persistency variance breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Persistency variance +₹3,509 crore, largely from participating and group business; par 13th-month persistency improved (+₹2,463 crore). Group persistency assumption was strengthened. Expense variance positive net of GST; mortality roughly flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the solvency-driven dividend payout cautious even with solvency at 2.35, and how should the payout ratio be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Dinesh Pant said the company wants clarity on RBC because equity exposure is high, and it does not want to create expectations it cannot sustain; growth also consumes capital. Doraiswamy said the payout will depend on regulation, with the increased payout (₹20 per share pre-bonus) expected to be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: Will non-par IRRs or offering rates be revised in FY27, and why did bancassurance policy count fall about 36%?
qa_highlights.answer: Pant said IRRs depend on investment opportunities, competition and margin balance; hedging for long-duration non-par is limited. Hemant Buch attributed the bancassurance policy decline to one microfinance corporate agency issue and a conscious move to bigger tickets; Q4 sales count rose about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for the next year and the building blocks for expansion from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Pant said margins could be challenged over the next three years and the journey will be gradual; the company will not chase margins at the cost of insurance-for-all. Doraiswamy said ticket size and persistency are the drivers, with product mix to consolidate.

capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning discussion on the call; the call covered insurance sales, margins, capital and dividend.
Capital position: solvency ratio 2.35 at 31 March 2026 vs 2.11 a year earlier; management said it wants to build reserves ahead of risk-based capital (RBC) and that growth will also consume capital.

Digital capacity: 23,00,983 policies completed via the agent-assisted ANANDA app in FY26 vs 14,74,208 in FY25 (+56.08%); active agents on ANANDA up 29.56%. New MyLIC customer app launched (15 April 2026) and LIC Super Sales Saathi app for sales personnel under the DIVE programme.
Bima Sakhi scheme: 3,45,000 Bima Sakhis appointed, 21.94 lakh policies sold and ₹2,848 crore new business premium in FY26; coverage at 1,43,924 of 2,44,876 Gram Panchayats (59%).
demand_pricing: Market share by first-year premium 56.6% in FY26 vs 57.05% in FY25; individual market share 36.6% (vs 37.46%); group 70.11% (vs 71.19%).
Individual new business premium ₹67,676 crore (+8.29%); individual renewal premium ₹2,71,699 crore (+5.91%); group new business premium ₹1,92,912 crore out of group total ₹1,96,609 crore (+16.26%).

Non-par individual APE ₹15,214 crore (+43.78%), 35.11% of individual APE vs 27.69%. Jeevan Utsav was the main contributor to savings growth (management cited ~48.40% savings bucket growth); Jeevan Labh contributed about 40% of par savings premium.

VNB margin bridge 17.6% to 21.2%: business mix +3%, RFR +3.4%, operating assumption changes (expense and persistency realignment plus GST) -2.8%. Individual par ~42% of APE contributes ~28% of VNB; individual non-par ~22.7% of APE contributes ~53% of VNB; remainder group (~19%).

Operating experience variance of ₹92,639 crore; persistency variance +₹3,509 crore (group line strengthened, par 13th-month persistency improved, +₹2,463 crore); mortality roughly flat; expense variance positive, net of GST.

Economic variance: equity MTM fall ₹53,698 crore and debt MTM fall ₹46,853 crore. Bond-amortisation accounting change impact of about ₹11,000 crore gross, of which ~₹9,000 crore sits in participating business (no direct PAT impact per management).

Bancassurance and alternate channels NBP ₹5,076 crore (+45.19%): banks ₹3,151 crore (+22.30%), alternate channels ₹1,925 crore (+109.36%). Policy count via bancassurance fell about 36%; management attributed this to a microfinance corporate agency issue and a conscious move away from login-based low-ticket sales; Q4 policy count reportedly up ~10%.

Agency: individual agents 14,57,045 vs 14,86,851 (down ~30,000); agency sourced 98.42% of policies and 91.75% of new business premium. Management said recruitment, training and younger-age agent focus will follow.

April 2026 sales described as good and ahead of FY26 pace across participating and non-participating products; management said it is too early to judge the effect of recent market volatility on ULIP and guaranteed demand.
Pricing: management said non-par IRRs depend on investment opportunities and competition and are balanced against margins; long-duration hedges are limited. Expense ratio 11.91% (-51 bps).

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: VNB margin rose 360 bps to 21.2% in FY26, but management says further expansion will be gradual and slower, and the bridge included a one-off RFR (+3.4%) and GST-related assumption charge (-2.8%) that may not recur; margin 'could be challenged over the next three years'.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Individual NBP grew only 8.29% to ₹67,676 crore and market share slipped to 56.6% from 57.05%; April 2026 sales described as good and ahead of prior year, but agent count fell to 14,57,045 from 14,86,851 and bancassurance policy count fell about 36%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex, capacity or commissioning discussed; solvency rose to 2.35 from 2.11 and management is building reserves ahead of RBC, so capital is being retained rather than deployed into new capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric guidance; management is cautious on margin outlook and says it is not looking for major mix changes, aiming to consolidate.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Positive FY26 operating variance of ₹92,639 crore and persistency variance of ₹3,509 crore may not repeat, and RBC rules (equity-sensitive) could constrain capital and payout, with EV growth only 1.58% after ₹1 lakh crore-plus MTM hits.

rows.label: Dividend payout increase pending RBC clarity
rows.why: Final dividend raised to ₹20 per share pre-bonus and management expects the higher payout to be sustained, but finality is deferred until RBC outcomes are clear and solvency is 2.35.

rows.label: RBC framework timing and calibration
rows.why: Management explicitly flagged upcoming RBC rules as the reason for caution on payout and capital, with equity exposure high and the framework's calibration still unknown.

rows.label: Bancassurance and alternate channel momentum
rows.why: Bancassurance and alternate channels NBP rose 45.19% to ₹5,076 crore, with alternate channels up 109.36%, though bancassurance policy count fell about 36% and Q4 policy count was up about 10%.

tone.note: Management was confident on VNB, margin, PAT and bancassurance growth and on the 2.35 solvency ratio, but cautious on dividend payout and the gradual margin outlook pending RBC clarity; analysts pressed on FY27 IRRs, persistency and the sustainability of margin gains.

543526|2026-06.headline: LIC Q1 FY27 net VNB margin rose 750 bps YoY to 22.9% and VNB grew 61.32% to ₹3,136 crore; profit after tax up 22.81% to ₹13,492 crore.
543526|2026-06.overview: LIC reported Q1 FY27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) with total premium of ₹127,250 crore (+6.75% YoY) and individual new business premium of ₹14,351 crore (+14.48% YoY). Net VNB margin expanded to 22.9% from 15.4%, driven mainly by business mix (non-par savings and protection growth) and a 2.9% positive assumption impact, partly offset by a 1.9% negative expense impact from loss of GST input tax credit. Overall market share by first-year premium fell to 60.10% from 63.51%, with group share down to 70.90% and individual share up to 38.89%. The company also disclosed the 6.5% government OFS, taking public float to 10%.

segments.name: Individual business
segments.commentary: Individual new business premium ₹14,351 crore (+14.48%); individual renewal premium ₹61,065 crore (+3.61%); individual APE ₹7,532 crore with non-par share rising to 32.49% from 30.34%. ULIP premium declined YoY.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group total premium ₹51,834 crore (+8.61%); group APE ₹6,160 crore; group market share fell to 70.90% from 76.54% on a comparable basis.

segments.name: Par vs non-par (APE)
segments.commentary: Par individual APE ₹5,085 crore (67.51% of individual APE); non-par ₹2,447 crore (32.49%). Management cited non-par savings growth of 59.24% and non-par protection growth of 43.59%.

segments.name: Bancassurance and alternate channels
segments.commentary: NBP ₹907.14 crore (+5.25%); bank channel NBP ₹483.39 crore (-8.62%) due to delayed bank marketing plans and West Asia related remittance pressure on annuities; alternate channels ₹423.75 crore (+27.27%).

capex_capacity: The call did not discuss capex, capacity, utilisation, or commissioning timelines; no capex plans were stated.

Product pipeline: two new products launched since April 2026 (New Jeevan Sathi single premium and limited premium); Nav Jeevan Shree single premium withdrawn. Total of 59 products available for new business as of 30 June 2026.

Digital and distribution capacity: MyLIC and Super Sales Saathi apps launched in April 2026 under the DIVE initiative; agent-assisted Ananda application completed 436,925 policies in Q1 FY27 (+25.56% YoY).
Bima Sakhi rollout: 2.87 lakh women designated, covering 151,620 of 244,876 gram panchayats (62%) as of 30 June 2026; target is at least one Bima Sakhi per gram panchayat.
Agent force: 1,445,692 agents as of 30 June 2026 (-2.73% YoY); management said non-serious Bima Sakhi recruits are being weeded out, which will continue.
guidance_outlook: Management does not normally give guidance but expects VNB margin to keep improving over the next few quarters, subject to RFR movements.
Management said VNB margin should settle around the industry average and is working toward mid-20s VNB margin by year end.
Non-par growth expected to continue from Q1 to Q4 pattern; ULIP recovery expected when market normalises.
Expense ratio expected to fall with operational efficiency; GST ITC-related expense impact to be compared against last year in Q1 and Q2 only.
Bancassurance expected to recover in subsequent quarters after delayed bank marketing plans.
APE growth expected to strengthen in subsequent quarters as new business focus increases through the year.
demand_pricing: Individual protection growth above 40% YoY on a small base; individual agents drove most protection policy volume.
ULIP premium declined YoY due to market volatility; management said it expects recovery only when markets normalise and denied cannibalisation of non-par.
Average ticket size rose after minimum sum assured for the major regular-premium product was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh (October 2024) and annuity single-premium sales grew.
Agent count fell 2.73% YoY to 1,445,692 (market share by agent count 43.69% vs 47.11%) as non-serious Bima Sakhi recruits quit; agency sold 98.51% of policies and 93.07% of new business premium.
Renewal commission growth declined YoY, attributed to agents no longer in the books and not eligible to renew commission.

qa_highlights.question: What are the assumption changes in the VNB walk and is the cost impact GST-led?
qa_highlights.answer: Assumption changes contributed +2.9% (RFR, persistency alignment, CRNHR, TVOG); expense assumptions including loss of ITC contributed -1.9%. Business mix contributed about +6.5%. The GST exemption removed ITC, adding to expenses, but higher volumes should dilute per-policy expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ULIP decline deliberate and will it recover in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly market-driven due to volatility; management focused on margin-accretive non-par lines. ULIP recovery depends on market improvement; no cannibalisation expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why does RWRP differ from individual APE?
qa_highlights.answer: APE annualises new business premium by frequency and excludes first-year renewal premiums received after policy completion; RWRP captures actual premium received, so the gap reflects strong first-year renewal premium.

qa_highlights.question: Why is APE growth soft despite strong VNB growth, and what is the medium-term aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Prior-year base had higher regular-premium share; management expects APE growth to pick up in later quarters. No numeric medium-term target given; management agreed to examine monthly APE disclosure.

qa_highlights.question: Split of VNB margin by line of business?
qa_highlights.answer: Par: 37.1% of APE with 19.4% margin; individual non-par: ₹1,678 crore APE with 49.3% margin; group: 45% of APE with 29.4% margin (figures given as shares of VNB as well as APE by the Appointed Actuary, clarified as proportion of VNB by segment).

qa_highlights.question: Why is the solvency ratio high and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: 2.42 is pre-dividend; 2.32 after subsequent dividend. Higher solvency supports protection growth, but management will await regulatory changes before deciding on any change to solvency strategy.

qa_highlights.question: Why is bancassurance individual NBP growing much slower than policy count?
qa_highlights.answer: Bank channel faced pressure from West Asia conflict affecting remittances (annuities) and market volatility (ULIPs); low-ticket policies were withdrawn after minimum sum assured rose to ₹2 lakh.

qa_highlights.question: Is VNB margin on track for mid-20s by year end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working toward that target.

risks_watch: Assumption and RFR movements: RFR contributed positively, but management said it is outside LIC's control and could change the margin trajectory.
Persistency weakness: 61-month premium persistency fell to 61.12% from 63.85%; 13-month number-based persistency rose to 66.45% from 64.35%; group persistency contributed negatively to assumptions.
Market share erosion: overall first-year premium share fell to 60.10% from 63.51%; group share fell sharply.
Expense ratio up 16 bps YoY to 10.63% after loss of GST input tax credit; volume growth must outpace expense growth.
Maturity claims up 12.88% YoY to ₹57,099 crore; agent count down 2.73% YoY.
Bancassurance bank channel NBP down 8.62%; recovery timing uncertain.
Solvency pre-dividend 2.42, post-dividend 2.32; any capital needs for protection growth require monitoring.
Shareholder profit from ASM funds (₹180,000 crore book value) and par surplus transfer timing (mainly Q4) affect quarterly profit comparisons.
IEV unwind and EV not disclosed quarterly; next disclosure at half-year.

rows.why: Bank channel NBP fell 8.62% to ₹483.39 crore on delayed bank marketing plans and West Asia remittance pressure, while management expects recovery in subsequent quarters.

rows.why: ULIP premium declined YoY on market volatility; management expects recovery only when markets normalise and denies cannibalisation of non-par.

543527|2026-03.headline: Prudent Q4 FY26: record ₹4,300 crore quarterly equity net sales offset MTM hit; AUM rebounded to ₹1.33 trillion by 5 May 2026.

Closing equity AUM fell 8.2% QoQ to ₹1,15,480 crore on ₹14,550 crore of mark-to-market losses. Revenue grew 5.1% QoQ and operating profit 19.5% QoQ, but PAT growth slowed to 2.6% QoQ because other income turned negative (₹-4.7 crore). Management flagged two regulatory items for FY27: SEBI's TER change (GST now inside the expense ratio) and withdrawal of the 5 bps exit-load benefit, with industry clarity expected by end-May.

543527|2026-06.headline: Prudent's Q1 FY27 PAT rose 44.4% YoY to INR74.8 crores, with average AUM up 21% to INR1.33 lakh crores despite a 2.8 bps gross yield cut.

Operating profit rose 32.4% YoY to INR89.1 crores and PAT rose 44.4% YoY to INR74.8 crores, helped by treasury gains. New SEBI/AMC regulatory changes from April 2026 (GST treatment, exit load removal) cut gross yield by about 2.8 bps to around 88 bps and shifted commission expense lower, which management called a one-time reset. 543529|2026-03.headline: Delhivery FY26 revenue reached ~10,486 crore with 7.3% service EBITDA and first full-year FCF positive at ~89 crore, a year ahead of plan.
543529|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was about 2,848 crore with PAT of about 87 crore (~3% margin) and adjusted EBITDA of 151 crore. FY26 was the first year of the Ecom Express integration, with over a billion express packages and about 2 million MT of PTL freight. Supply chain services (SCS) reached breakeven on adjusted EBITDA after a service EBITDA turnaround to 10.9%. Management said the company turned FCF positive, one year ahead of plan, despite integration costs; cash stood above 4,500 crore.

segments.name: Express
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ~1,832 crore, up 46% YoY, with volumes of 306 million (up ~72-73% YoY, sequentially up on Q3). FY26 revenue ~6,685 crore and about a billion parcels; service EBITDA at upper end of 16-18% normative range.

segments.name: Part Truck Load (PTL)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ~622 crore and 549 thousand MT, both up ~20% YoY. FY26 about 2 million MT and ~2,254 crore revenue; management cited gross margin rising from 14% to 28% over roughly 2.5-3 years.

segments.name: Supply Chain Services (SCS)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ~729 crore with service EBITDA of 10.9% (~79 crore), up ~4x; segment at breakeven on adjusted EBITDA. Two mandates signed and activated in Q4.

segments.name: Delhivery Direct (intracity and intercity)
segments.commentary: Intracity on-demand service live in six cities; FY26 investment about 76 crore, with FY27 investment guided at 130-160 crore toward a 200+ crore external GMV run-rate.

guidance_outlook: Long-term transport ROIC target of 25%+, with adjusted EBITDA rising from ~6.3% toward at least 10%, and PTL service EBITDA moving toward ~18% and corporate overheads falling to ~7% of revenue.
Capital intensity (capex plus working-capital items) of ~21.5% of revenue could fall by 2-3 percentage points.
Capex to reach the 4% of revenue target from 4.7%; AGV and automation spend not expected to materially change capex guidance.
Net working capital at 11 days seen as sustainable; further reduction possible via faster billing and prepaid mix, though with limits.
FY27 new-business investment of 130-160 crore guided in the shareholder letter.
Management expects e-commerce industry to grow 15-20% in the medium term.
Management said the company does not plan a broad price increase now, though diesel pass-through clauses apply to PTL and some customers.
capex_capacity: Capex fell to 4.7% of revenue (from 7.8% in FY23); management reiterated a 4% target and said it is moving slightly ahead of plan.
Fleet metric: the 20,000 daily average fleet figure covers only contracted monthly vehicles; the decline reflects a shift to per-kilo variable fleet, while tractor-trailer count rose QoQ.
AGV pilots in Mumbai (Bombay) to be expanded to other mega gateways within FY27.
Delhivery Labs launched about a year ago; AI and automation deployed in claims, documentation and customer communication.
Company is the first in India to get a road train, after a 46-foot tractor trailer launch.
demand_pricing: Management said market structure is more settled after the Ecom Express deal, with less short-term price gouging than in the two years before FY26.
Share of 1P (first-party) logistics declined over the last year, per a listed marketplace; management expects a gradual shift towards 3P.
Long-tail D2C/SME share described as stable to slightly up YoY; heavy shipping share described as dominant.
Single largest customer was ~16% of revenue last year; management said it is well below its informal 35% concern threshold.

Diesel price hikes of about Rs 3/litre at pumps: prices indexed for PTL; express pass-through is via DPH clauses assessed customer by customer. Rs 1-2 price increases seen in some air-network pockets via surcharges.
Management dismissed Amazon's reopening of its 3PL offering as an old product with limited strategic value.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of rising fuel prices on consumption and costs, and has Delhivery raised prices?
qa_highlights.answer: PTL prices are diesel-indexed; express uses DPH clauses. Pump prices rose about Rs 3, and no broad price hike is planned. Q4 margins rose over Q3 despite fuel, and a volatile environment is seen as favourable to the market leader.

qa_highlights.question: Is Amazon's 3PL push a competitive threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it an old product in a new wrapper; first-party orders get priority at last mile and first-party logistics costs more than 3PL when fully loaded.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the working capital reduction, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers included faster and more accurate billing, client selection (declining some RFQs), and more-than-monthly billing for preferential pricing. NWC was 11 days versus 38 three years ago; management called it sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Will SCS pipeline remain margin accretive, and how much of new initiatives' investment is opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Each SCS project must clear an internal hurdle rate and the pipeline is in focus sectors. Short-term start-up costs can weigh on P&L. Management did not give a split of the 130-160 crore FY27 spend between opex and capex in the call.

qa_highlights.question: Will capex intensity rise with express growth, and will the industry overbuild?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex intensity is expected to stay around the 4% target; growth is mainly PTL and heavy, and management does not expect irrational pricing like three or four years ago.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Delhivery Direct opportunity and investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Intracity service live in six cities; FY26 spend ~76 crore; FY27 guided at 130-160 crore toward 200+ crore external GMV run-rate. Management described the TAM as very large without quantifying it.

qa_highlights.question: Is PTL leadership achievable, and what capabilities are missing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited PTL growth from ~280-290k tons to ~550k tons per quarter over 2-3 years with gross margin from 14% to 28%. Varun Bakshi said the playbook is share-of-wallet expansion with key accounts.

Competitive dynamics from 1P marketplaces insourcing or reopening 3PL offerings, plus possible share shifts in key accounts.
Labour cost inflation from minimum wage and gig worker laws, and potential increase in service costs.

543529|2026-06.headline: Delhivery Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to nearly Rs.3,000 Cr, with PAT of Rs.17 Cr after a Rs.15 Cr-plus cost drag from two new contracts and unused assets.
543529|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 as a record quarter for revenue but a weak one for profitability, hit by chronic labour shortages, election and weather disruptions, and start-up costs for two large new contracts. Express acquisition consolidation drove much of the 55% YoY growth in the reported figures. PTL yield rose to nearly Rs.12 per kg (per management's wording), and management attributed most of the improvement to organic gains rather than pass-through. Diesel price hikes in May are being passed through to customers with a lag, and management said FY27 outlook is unchanged at 20-30% growth.

financial_highlights.change: Management said PAT before unused-asset costs was ~Rs.62 Cr in press release; reconciliation given on call
