segments.commentary: Local ARR is at Rs.150 Cr in July, versus an earlier target of Rs.250 Cr exit ARR for FY27; management revised its expectation to Rs.160-175 Cr. Ahmedabad Local is expected to break even around month three. NBFC approval received in July.

guidance_outlook: Management maintained the FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-30%; the range is wider because the outcome depends on Q2 and early Q3 trends.
FY27 profitability and medium/long-term targets were said to be unchanged, with no major structural headwinds seen by management.
Diesel: management says the pass-through is almost 100% covered (97-98% per Varun Bakshi). July is expected to reflect the May diesel hike with the lag gone.
Corporate manpower costs estimated at Rs.371 Cr for FY27 (as stated on call).
Unused-asset (lock-in/ROU) costs of around Rs.17 Cr are expected to continue until disposal, per management, and are treated as ongoing rather than one-time.
capex_capacity: Two new large SCS contracts required build-up of multiple fulfilment sites with a 45-60 day lead to inbound stock before outbound billing ramps.
Automation: in-facility movement and automated storage/retrieval being introduced at key transportation and fulfilment facilities.
Maps (proprietary GIS) launched on 8 August for internal deployment, with external availability planned later.
Expansion of cross-sell development teams for truck and LCV businesses; coverage now 100% of India versus earlier top-3 cities.
demand_pricing: Demand continued into Q2, with festive-season sales starting to lift volumes; August to date is said to be robust.
D2C volumes are running at 40-45% of PTL volumes and skew to heavier packages, which supports yields.
Pricing contracts are indexed to the prevailing month's diesel rate. Diesel-driven revisions were under negotiation from late April to mid-May, and pass-throughs are expected to show in Q2.
Management said pricing pressure has eased, with no price cuts for customers and reduced irrational competition. Competitor price cuts were disputed by management as not matching its own contracts.
New customer adds were mainly D2C and SME; management said self-serve sign-up through DelhiveryOne is growing.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 20-30% revenue growth guidance range, and what is the trend in new customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was soft seasonally but robust after adjusting for Express, and the range is wider because Q2 and early Q3 trends are still forming. New customers are mostly D2C and SME, with festive demand building.

qa_highlights.question: Is the PTL yield increase seasonal or sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yield gains are planned and organic, with about 37 paise per kg of improvement, of which 6 paise was fuel pass-through; the sustained QoQ improvement is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 300 bps margin pressure is from diesel versus other costs, and how quickly can it be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fuel is about 0.6 pp of revenue for PTL; the bigger hit is labour-related minimum wage and rider payout linkage, which lacks a pass-through clause. Diesel revisions have been mostly passed through, and the effect should be evident in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the NBFC (asset-light lending) plan matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not lend heavily from its own balance sheet, but will partner with lending firms and underwrite a part of exposure to help fleet owners get insurance and financing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT difference between the press release and reported figures (Rs.62 Cr vs Rs.32 Cr vs Rs.17 Cr)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs.17 Cr relates to unused lock-in assets and facilities; the stat P&L shows about Rs.30 Cr after ROU and depreciation items. Shah queried recurrence, and management said the unused-asset costs are recurring until disposal.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SCS margins decline and what is the new-contract economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two new large contracts started together and are in an inbound-heavy build-up phase with negative cash flows, but they are expected to stabilise in Q2 and early Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is Delhivery exposed to competition from in-house or 3PL consolidation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has gained share, with volumes retained through the uncertain environment, and that in-house consolidation is an encouraging but unproven trend.

543534|2026-06.headline: Aether Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 27% YoY to INR3,266 million, with EBITDA up 31% to INR1,028 million and margin at 31%.
543534|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 27% YoY to INR3,266 million and EBITDA rose 31% to INR1,028 million, with EBITDA margin at 31% versus 30% a year ago. PAT grew 33% YoY to INR627 million, a 19% margin. Management highlighted the Dow Chemical silicones research partnership, Site 5 (Magnum, Panoli) starting commercial LSM sales, and a mix shift toward CEM and CRAMS. The company also received the final insurance claim for the November 2023 fire-related fixed asset losses, and working capital remains elevated due to inventory build.

segments.commentary: Management targets CEM plus CRAMS at 70%+ of revenue in the next couple of years, versus about 50% currently. Management said CRAMS is 'about 50%' already.

segments.name: LSM (Large-scale manufacturing)
segments.commentary: Volume fell 22.5% YoY as some lines at Site 3 moved to CEM; management said pricing rose 22.5% and demand is intact. LSM expected to be about 35% of top line in coming years.

segments.name: Oil and Gas
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR1,000 million in the quarter per analyst question, roughly 20% of business per management. Baker Hughes is the largest customer; Site 4 producing about INR70 crore currently versus about INR45 crore at the start.

qa_highlights.answer: Dow is an exclusive multi-year research partner for silicone manufacturing technologies in India, with R&D and pilot scale-up at Surat; management gave no revenue date and flagged pilot completion, a commercial framework, and a possible dedicated site as milestones.

qa_highlights.question: What is the semiconductor chemical commercialisation timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Site 3 has one stream making semiconductor chemicals with qualification batches complete and small orders being delivered; the large Site 5 stream of 45 tonnes/month is targeted for end-September 2026.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said LSM market share was held even when prices fell 30-35% post-COVID; the company says it remains competitive after recent price corrections, and LSM will be about 35% of revenue.

qa_highlights.answer: LSM volume fell 22.5% as lines moved to CEM at Site 3, while pricing rose 22.5%; management says demand is intact and no margin split was given.

543539|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 84% to INR189 crore and PAT 26% to INR29.14 crore, but margins compressed on construction-cost inflation and new-project start-up costs.
543539|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue of about INR189 crore (up ~84% from INR102 crore) and EBITDA of INR38.46 crore (up 35%), with PAT of INR29.14 crore (up 26%). Margins moderated on project mix, war-related construction input inflation, and early-stage costs on newly started projects. Two projects (Rashmi Vasudev and Rashmi Celestia) received OC and were handed over during the year, and the company remains debt-free. Management guided that margins will return to prior levels in FY27 and that Rashmi Square and Rashmi Signature are the key cash-generating projects.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said only Rashmi Square and Rashmi Signature were hit minorly; other projects are unaffected and the overall impact is limited at the current execution stage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended realisation and will it rise?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 realisation was about INR25,000 to 27,000 per sq ft; management said it will not fall and Rashmi Square is targeted at INR27,000 to 28,000.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins decline and when will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited construction cost inflation from the war and early-stage costs of two new projects, expecting margins to return to prior levels in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a need for structured debt for Icon or Avenu?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no; funding will come from internal cash flows of Rashmi Square and Rashmi Signature, and borrowings are minimal.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy and capital employed?
qa_highlights.answer: No dividend under consideration for now as the board prioritises projects; capital employed estimated at INR80 to 90 crore as on 31 March.

543539|2026-06.headline: Modis Navnirman Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27.92% YoY to INR58.26 crore; PAT up 25.81% to INR8.54 crore, though EBITDA margin fell to about 20%.
543539|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 27.92% YoY to INR58.26 crore and 13.15% QoQ, with EBITDA up 14.25% YoY to INR11.65 crore and PAT up 25.81% YoY to INR8.54 crore. The company added Khar (Rashmi Icon/redevelopment) to its Mumbai footprint, bringing the portfolio to 25 projects (six ongoing, 14 completed, five upcoming). 543547|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 13% and PAT reached INR202 crore (+9%); FY27 guidance is 2.31 lakh tonnes volume at 73% utilisation, with BESS excluded.

Volumes were 2,01,370 tonnes at 77% capacity utilisation, with exports up 30% and export volumes up 23%. Management said the Israel-Iran conflict from 28 February 2026 raised raw material costs by 50%-plus and briefly hurt demand, but supply and pricing have stabilised since April. The company guided FY27 volume to 2.31 lakh tonnes, 13% revenue growth and ~11% EBITDA margin, and announced a foray into battery energy storage systems (BESS) targeting 5 GWh.

rows.why: Q1 EBITDA/t of about INR19.6 is elevated by war-risk premium of INR2.5-3/t that management expects to shrink, versus long-term target of INR16-17/t (10-12% margin), and Q1 margin was 10%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q1 FY27 (commissioned April 2026); HFFR to 20,000 t by Q4 FY
rows.why: The 48,000 t Bhiwadi XLPE plant is already commissioned, taking installed capacity to 316,400 t, with 334,400 t targeted by year-end and HFFR expansion to 20,000 t by FY27 end.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management is confident in 15% FY27 volume growth to 231,000 t, requiring about 60,000 t per quarter, but Q1 volume was up only about 1% YoY at 52,163 t and utilisation is about 66%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Committed FY27 capex of INR150-175 crore is already set, with about INR77 crore spent in Q1, and utilisation at about 66% is below the 80% threshold that would force a new capex call; BESS and PVC addition (about 25,000 t) are planned but not yet dated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says it expects to beat the 13-14% revenue guidance, but guidance assumes FY26 prices with no increase and Q2 export revenue may be below Q1's INR300-330 crore given spot orders with 10-20 day visibility.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 revenue growth of 29% was mostly export pricing, volume rose only about 1%, and July prices eased marginally; the 15% volume target needs about 60,000 t per quarter against Q1's 52,163 t.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: BESS phase 1 (about 1 GW / 1 GWh, INR150-200 crore capex plus working capital) is planned at 6-8% margin, but timing has slipped a couple of quarters with mid-FY29 cited for 1 GW.

rows.label: Resin and war-risk premium normalisation
rows.why: Management expects resin prices to take 3-6 months to normalise, and the INR2.5-3/t war-risk premium to shrink, which would compress the Q1 EBITDA/t of about INR19.6.

rows.label: Bhiwadi ramp for Rajasthan and Delhi share gains
rows.why: Bhiwadi is at 20-25% utilisation and assumed at about 50% average in FY27 (INR200-250 crore revenue), serving Rajasthan and Delhi customers, with management citing 2-3% share gain as the basis for the extra volume.

rows.label: Cash conversion cycle return to 55-60 days
rows.why: Cash conversion cycle widened in Q1 on higher inventory and debtors and finance cost rose; management says it has eased since July but the CCC has not yet been verified.

tone.note: Management was confident on the full-year 15% volume target, capacity and approvals, and expects to beat guidance, but cautious on forward pricing, Q2 exports and BESS timing, declining to guide beyond August; analysts pushed on EBITDA/t sustainability, the volume gap and the Bhiwadi ramp.

543573|2026-03.headline: Syrma SGS Q4 FY26 revenue rose 56% YoY to INR1,477 crore at 11.9% operating EBITDA margin; FY27 EBITDA guided to INR700 crore.
543573|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter to date: consolidated revenue INR1,477 crore (+56% YoY, +16% QoQ), operating EBITDA INR174 crore (+51% YoY) at 11.9% margin, and PAT INR119 crore (+67% YoY). FY26 revenue reached INR4,857 crore (+27%), operating EBITDA INR545 crore (+68%, margin 11.3%), and the company moved to a net cash position of INR467 crore. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 30-35%, operating EBITDA margin of 10-10.5% (said to be conservative) and EBITDA of about INR700 crore, and is investing in a large PCB project. The Ksolare acquisition via the Premier Energies JV was dropped, and a greenfield renewable-inverter plan is being evaluated instead.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: 31% of Q4 revenue; grew about 30% in FY26 including Elcome. Growth expected from power management, UPS and industrial electronics; about 24% of order book.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: 26% of Q4 revenue; about 31% of FY26 revenue (INR1,452 crore). Management caps it below 35% and pegs it near 30%, growing about 8-10% in FY27; about 30% of order book.

segments.name: Auto
segments.commentary: 24% of Q4 revenue; grew 39% in FY26. Auto exports crossed INR125 crore; about 29% of order book; FY27 growth expected to be mainly domestic.

segments.name: Healthcare (MedTech)
segments.commentary: Grew 36% in FY26 from INR291 crore to INR395 crore; management expects it to exceed INR500 crore in FY27. About 5% of order book.

segments.name: IT and railways
segments.commentary: Grew 182% YoY in Q4 and 74% in FY26; annualised revenue rose from about INR240 crore to INR476 crore. IT covers laptop, motherboard and memory products. About 11% of order book; management expects 30-40% growth going forward.

segments.name: ODM
segments.commentary: Revenue rose about 80% from INR453 crore to INR825 crore in FY26; share about 17% of revenue versus 12% a year earlier.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Revenue of about INR1,200 crore+ in FY26 (24-25% of revenue), up 41%; Q4 run rate about INR125 crore per month. FY27 target about INR1,500 crore (20-30% growth).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 30-35%; management says the blended growth will be near 30-35% with individual verticals ranging from about 28% to 35%.
FY27 operating EBITDA margin guided at 10.5-11% (earlier stated as at least 10-10.5%), kept conservative despite FY26 margin of about 12%.
Targeting about INR700 crore of EBITDA in FY27, a 30% absolute increase per management.
FY27 exports targeted at about INR1,500 crore; FY27 capex of INR100-150 crore organic plus PCB project spend.
FY28 onwards, PCB business to add incremental revenue (management cites possibly INR300-700 crore); FY28 growth expected above 30-35%.
Working capital days to be pushed down further, but management said it will not chase growth at the expense of working capital.
capex_capacity: PCB multilayer line project: about $90 million (INR800 crore) over multiple years, in two phases. Phase 1 INR400 crore, of which about INR50 crore was spent in FY26, about INR250 crore planned in FY27 and INR100 crore in FY28. Phase 2 runs into mid-FY29.

Commissioning of the first PCB phase expected towards the end of FY27 or start of FY28; partial government incentive claims thereafter, with at least a one-year lag. Management says the subsidy is expected at 50-60% of the spend.
ECMS approvals received for CCL (copper clad laminate), HDI and flex PCB; about INR800 crore capex expected to be executed between FY28 and FY30.
FY26 capex was about INR140 crore; FY27 organic capex planned at INR100-150 crore.
Real-time monitoring system being rolled out across assembly lines in phases; management reports a 5-7% improvement in operational efficiency so far.

Renewable energy/inverter: Ksolare acquisition via Premier Energies JV dropped after the seller did not meet conditions precedent; minimal expense charged to P&L. Management now plans a greenfield project and is evaluating technology partner proposals, with an update expected in the coming quarter.
demand_pricing: Order book of about INR6,600 crore at March-end 2026 (auto 29%, consumer 30%, industrial 24%, healthcare 5%, IT and railways 11%). Net addition of about INR200 crore after Q4 deliveries; Elcome is about 5% of the order book.
Q4 run rate is about INR500 crore per month. Management says the second half is seasonally stronger than the first half.
Customer concentration (FY26): top 5 about 34% of revenue, top 10 about 47%, top 20 about 63%.
32 new customers onboarded in FY26 (about 7 in industrial). Management says they could add about INR1,000 crore to FY26 revenue and about INR2,500 crore per year long-term.

Pass-through clauses exist in customer contracts for metal and logistics cost variation, but recovery is negotiated and is not immediate. Management expects partial cost increases to be offset by better buying and efficiency, with costs shared across vendor, customer and end consumer.

Smart metering: about INR250-260 crore of revenue in FY26, with a gross material margin of about 12-15%; management is being selective given working capital intensity. Elcome has a 3-6 month working capital cycle, and defence is a high-margin ODM business.

Competition: management said competitive intensity will rise as Tier-2 global EMS players and large Indian groups enter; it claims a cost advantage. Global addressable market is cited at over $600 million, against about $500 million of current revenue.
EU FTA: about a 1-1.5% duty benefit in select cases; management says the longer-term impact is positive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex profile for the PCB and other projects, and when do the government incentives start?
qa_highlights.answer: PCB phase 1 is INR400 crore (INR250 crore in FY27, INR100 crore in FY28). Organic capex is INR100-150 crore a year. Commissioning is expected towards the end of FY27 or the start of FY28, with incentives claimed in part and typically lagging by a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw-material and inflation outlook, and how are costs passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Metal prices, logistics and shipping routes are affected by the Middle East crisis. Contracts have pass-through clauses but recovery is negotiated and takes time. Management says better buying and efficiency can offset part of the increase.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 margin guided at 10.5-11% when Q4 was 11.9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is being conservative given geopolitics, shipping and metal-price volatility. It says it prefers to beat its guidance and will revise it at the Q1 call if conditions stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company fund the PCB capex without running short of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the project will be funded through debt, internal accruals and a 25% JV partner contribution, with subsidies of 50-60% expected. It says cash will not fall short over the project life. Balance-sheet cash is INR829 crore against a net cash position of INR470 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much growth comes from market share gains versus industry growth, and how does the PCB business affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the growth to market share and wallet-share gains, portfolio expansion (MedTech, defence) and larger customer contracts. PCB revenue is incremental, starting in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EU and export outlook, and what is the PLI benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Export guidance is INR1,500 crore for FY27, about 25-30% growth. Management expects at least 25% growth over the coming years. FY26 gross PLI was about INR80 crore and net about INR38 crore; Q4 net PLI was about INR10-12 crore.

Pass-through of metal and logistics cost increases is negotiated, not immediate; the lag and the share borne by Syrma, customers and end consumers remain unquantified.

PCB project: about INR800 crore capex, with INR250 crore planned in FY27; commissioning is expected towards end-FY27 or start-FY28, and government subsidy claims lag by at least a year. Funding relies on debt, accruals and a 25% JV partner contribution; the analyst's cash-shortfall concern was answered but not quantified.

Working capital at 63 days (58 ex-Elcome); management will not chase growth at the expense of working capital, but Elcome and defence carry 3-6 month cycles, and smart metering is being limited for the same reason.

Order book grew only about INR200 crore net in Q4 to about INR6,600 crore; the analyst noted it covers about 24% of the 30-35% growth target on its own, and management said the order book is continuously refreshed, with many orders running only 3-6 months.
Rising competition from Tier-2 global EMS players and large Indian groups; management says competitive intensity will increase.
Ksolare acquisition dropped; a greenfield renewable inverter project is being evaluated, with technology partner choice and an update expected in the coming quarter.
key_quotes: We would like to err on the side of caution and we have guided 10.5% to 11% margin despite having delivered 12% margin.
We are willing to sacrifice top line growth if the working capital cycle is elongated. We are not chasing growth at the expense of working capital cycle.
We are competing with the Tier 2 level global EMS companies. Competition -- competitive intensity would increase.
We'll not fall short of cash. You see, what we spent, we have projected about $40 million, which is about INR400 crores or whatever, INR360 crores, INR400 crores for the current year.
543573|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and the FY27 revenue and EBITDA targets, but deliberately cautious on margin, guiding 10.5-11% against a roughly 12% run-rate and citing geopolitics and metal costs. Evasive on PCB funding detail, the renewable-energy project and the margin cushion; several answers were deferred to later quarters.

rows.why: FY27 revenue guided at 30-35% on a INR6,600 crore order book, 32 new customers onboarded in FY26, and exports targeted at INR1,500 crore+ (about 25-30% growth on FY26 exports of about INR1,200 crore).

rows.why: Utilisation rose significantly over FY25 and FY27 organic capex of INR100-150 crore is planned on top of the INR800 crore PCB/ECMS programme; a greenfield renewable-inverter project is under evaluation with an update expected next quarter, though no capex is quantified.

rows.label: Net cash position sustained despite PCB capex
rows.why: Net cash of INR467 crore at FY26 end versus cash of INR820 crore, but PCB Phase 1 needs INR250 crore in FY27 and INR100 crore in FY28, funded by debt, accruals and a 25% JV partner contribution with 50-60% subsidy expected.

rows.label: EU FTA duty benefit
rows.why: The EU FTA gives about a 1-1.5% duty benefit in select cases, with management calling the longer-term impact positive on exports targeted at INR1,500 crore in FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 delivery, the 30-35% FY27 revenue growth and the INR700 crore EBITDA target, but cautious on margin (10.5-11% guide vs 11.9% Q4) and vague on PCB funding detail and the renewable project; analysts pressed on the cash need for PCB, order book cover and margin cushion.

543573|2026-06.headline: Syrma SGS Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 67% YoY to Rs 1,604 crore and PAT rose 112% to Rs 106 crore; FY27 guidance of 35%+ growth reaffirmed and possibly exceeded.
543573|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was Rs 1,604 crore (+67% YoY), with operating EBITDA of Rs 162 crore (+69%, 10.1% margin) and PAT of Rs 106 crore (+112%). Growth was led by consumer ramp-ups, exports (+61% to about Rs 387 crore) and ODM (Rs 270 crore, about 115% YoY but down sequentially from Rs 345 crore in Q4). Management attributed the quarter to normal run-rate business rather than one-time items, and said supply-chain constraints (PCB chemicals, component lead times) led to a deliberate build in inventory, pushing net working capital days from 63 to 71. Management reaffirmed 10.5-11% full-year EBITDA margin guidance and said FY27 revenue growth would be 35%+, with a view to exceed guidance.

financial_highlights.change: approx +115% YoY; down from Rs 345 crore in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Rs 122 crore; cash and investments above Rs 800 crore
financial_highlights.change: short-term borrowings up about Rs 340 crore in quarter

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 90 crore (of which about Rs 50 crore on PCB project)

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: Largest vertical at 34% of business mix; growth from faster customer ramp-ups and front-loaded schedules. Management guides about 30% of annual revenue, with quarterly variation.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: About 25% of business mix (about one-fourth of revenue); growth driven by EV penetration and charging infrastructure. Five new auto clients onboarded in the quarter.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Sequentially moderated; ex-defence/maritime it was about Rs 325 crore vs about Rs 320 crore last quarter (Rs 460 crore total last quarter including about Rs 140 crore defence/maritime). Smart metering slowed, and maritime is second-half loaded.

segments.name: Healthcare / MedTech
segments.commentary: Healthcare order book about Rs 500 crore. Syrma Johari MedTech did about Rs 210 crore last year and is expected to grow about 50%. Target 7-8% of total business.

segments.name: IT and Railways
segments.commentary: Together about 9% of order book; management said IT business is growing at a fast pace, including server motherboard work under a C-DAC approval.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 35%+, with management expecting to exceed guidance based on Q1.
Full-year operating EBITDA margin guided at 10.5-11%; consumer-mix seasonality may put the full-year figure in the 30-32% range for that segment, per management.
Exports expected to grow 30-40% in FY27, taking exports to about Rs 1,500-1,600 crore (FY26: about Rs 1,200 crore).
ODM share target of 17-19% in the short term, with a long-term aim of 25%.
Growth of 30-35% expected to continue in FY28 and FY29, per management.
Net working capital elevated for at least the next quarter or two as inventory is held as a strategic asset.
New clients onboarded in the quarter may add more than Rs 1,000 crore of revenue at full ramp-up, with volumes starting next year.
capex_capacity: PCB project: building about 65-70% complete; equipment from October onwards; power-on January-March 2027; commercial production expected by April 2027. Phase 1 cost about Rs 400 crore, of which about Rs 130 crore funded so far.
PCB economics: asset turn about 1.5x at full utilisation; year-one utilisation 40-50%, rising to 80%+. EBITDA 15-18% at full ramp ex-PLI, and about 10% or lower in the initial year.
Ex-PCB capex guided at Rs 100-150 crore for FY27; about Rs 40 crore spent in Q1.
Current capacity utilisation 65-70%. Expansion underway at Bangalore and Pune, and a new MedTech facility at Jodhpur with plastic injection moulding and SMT lines.
Phase 1 PCB funding: 50-60% debt, plus a 50% government capex subsidy; Phase 2 and 3 expected to start around end-FY27 or early FY28.
Kaga JV (Syrma 60%, Kaga India 40%): initial investment about Rs 24-25 crore combined; opportunity estimated at Rs 300-500 crore over 3-5 years.
demand_pricing: Order book about Rs 6,770 crore at June end (about Rs 6,400 crore at March end); about Rs 5,400 crore to execute in the next 12 months; average execution period about 10-10.5 months. Q1 order intake about Rs 1,781 crore.
Order book mix: automotive about 29%, consumer about 30%, industrial about 24%, healthcare about 7%, IT and railways about 9%.
Customer concentration: top 5 about 38%, top 10 about 51%, top 20 about 66% of revenue.

Pass-through of memory and component cost increases: management said absolute margin rupee amounts are unaffected but percentage margin would dip as there is no markup on pass-through cost.
Exports by geography: USA about 22%, Europe about 40%, rest other countries; North America including Mexico and Canada adds about 15 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any one-time revenue booking in Q1, and what is the outlook for the next three quarters, especially consumer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no one-time transaction in the quarter; numbers are normal run-rate, with consumer up from about 30% to 34% of mix and the gain absorbed by exports and ODM growth. No quarterly outlook number was given; management said it does not view numbers quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Board resolution for a roughly Rs 1,000 crore QIP a specific fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it is an annual enabling resolution taken at the AGM, with no immediate need; management framed it as a war chest for opportunities such as semicon.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs 400 crore PCB Phase 1 need external funds, and how will Phases 2 and 3 be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 cost about Rs 400 crore, of which about Rs 130 crore is funded so far; 50-60% debt is planned, plus a 50% government capex incentive. Funding is from internal accruals, subsidies, debt and a treasury balance above Rs 800 crore. Phases 2 and 3 start around end-FY27 or early FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What asset turn and EBITDA margin should be expected for the PCB plant in its first year, ex-PLI?
qa_highlights.answer: Asset turn about 1.5x at full utilisation, with year-one utilisation of 40-50% rising to 80%+. EBITDA is 15-18% at full ramp ex-PLI and about 10% or lower initially. The 1-1.5x asset turn is on a gross basis, before subsidies.

qa_highlights.question: Given order book growth and the Rs 1,604 crore quarter, should the current run rate be extrapolated or will revenue accelerate? Is the 10%+ margin the floor at a 33-34% consumer mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 10.5-11% full-year EBITDA margin. Order book rose to about Rs 6,770 crore from about Rs 6,400 crore, with Q1 intake of Rs 1,781 crore. Q4 operating EBITDA margin was 11-11.3% versus 10.1% now; the full-year consumer-driven margin may be 30-32%, with seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 guidance be exceeded, and how much pass-through of memory and component inflation would hit margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects to exceed the 35%+ revenue guidance, with the size left to another quarter. On pass-through, absolute rupee margin is unaffected but percentage margin dips because there is no markup on pass-through costs. It did not quantify the full-year inflation impact.

risks_watch: Supply-chain constraints (specialty PCB chemicals, component lead times, West Asia geopolitics) could slow execution; management said a war room was set up and guidance is still held.

Sequential softness in ODM (Rs 270 crore vs Rs 345 crore in Q4) and industrial ex-defence/maritime (about Rs 325 crore vs Rs 320 crore); smart metering slowed and maritime is second-half loaded.
PCB project execution: about 65-70% building complete, power-on targeted January-March 2027, commercial production by April 2027, with ramp-up EBITDA initially about 10% or lower.
Margin dilution from pass-through of memory and component cost inflation, since no markup is earned on pass-through costs.

Watch next quarter: whether the company raises the 35%+ growth or 10.5-11% margin guidance, export run-rate (Rs 1,500-1,600 crore target), and the consumer share (about 30% annualised).
key_quotes: So, what we are focused on in Syrma SGS is to ensure that our customers don't suffer because of these supply chain constraints.
We have also taken a cautious call that we will not treat inventory as a working capital, at least for the next quarter or two.
I will answer the first question in an affirmative that there has been no one-time transaction which has been booked into the quarter.
So, we are very confident of scaling up this business and have a positive growth in the current year.

543591|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue fell to INR 660.6 crore from INR 1,291.9 crore and Q4 Gross Profit turned negative at INR -6.1 crore as domestic lounge model reset.
543591|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a transition year: domestic lounge volumes fell after banks shifted from unlimited to spend-based lounge access, cutting consolidated revenue roughly in half. Adjusted EBITDA fell to INR 25.0 crore from INR 102.1 crore and PAT to INR 11.6 crore from INR 65.1 crore. Q4 FY26 was loss-making at the gross profit, EBITDA and PAT level. Management pointed to global lounges (transaction volumes up 140% YoY), the Ten11 Hospitality railway lounge acquisition, the ongoing ETT acquisition and B2C membership (DreamFolks Club 2.0) as the growth drivers. Management said FY27 would be a transition year with breakeven possibly about a year later.

segments.name: Domestic airport lounges
segments.commentary: Previously more than 90% of revenue; structural reset from unlimited to spend-based access drove the FY26 decline. Management said the business is now largely new in nature. Management did not give a quantified split.

segments.name: Global lounges
segments.commentary: Transaction volumes grew 140% YoY, and the network covers over 1,000 airport touchpoints. Clients onboarded in Southeast Asia, with Middle East work ongoing. Management did not disclose revenue for this segment.

segments.name: Railway lounges
segments.commentary: Acquired Ten11 Hospitality in November 2025, giving direct control of premium railway lounges. Operational at Chennai, Mumbai and Vadodara; Lucknow expected soon. Management reiterated an INR 500 crore revenue target over 5 years and said at least 50 lounges are needed to reach that scale.

segments.name: Lifestyle services and B2C
segments.commentary: New lifestyle services include spa, social clubs, room upgrades, app-based airport transfers, star-hotel meals and mall coffee. DreamFolks Club 2.0 B2C membership launched about 5-6 months ago, with spend kept deliberately modest.

543591|2026-06.headline: Dreamfolks Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR39 crore (from INR52.6 crore in Q4) and adjusted EBITDA was negative INR16.4 crore, hit by Middle East war and an MMG payment.
543591|2026-06.overview: Revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was INR39 crore, down from INR52.6 crore in the previous quarter and well below INR348.9 crore in Q1 FY26. Management attributed the sequential drop mainly to lower global lounge traffic from the Middle East conflict, partly offset by India business. Gross profit was negative INR0.9 crore, reflecting an upfront minimum guarantee payment for global lounge expansion, and PAT was negative INR13.8 crore. Cash rose to INR193.3 crore on collections, and net worth stood at INR300.4 crore. Management guided to adjusted EBITDA breakeven by next year, while holding the earlier H2 FY28 commitment.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR500 crore railway lounge opportunity over 4-5 years built up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management tied it to the government's announced railway investment plan over 3-4 years and said it had calculated the figure; no station or per-customer assumptions were shared.

qa_highlights.question: Club 2.0 paid membership count, ARPU and retention?

qa_highlights.question: Why did cash rise by about INR44 crore and why did revenue fall from INR56 crore to INR39 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited collections of about INR40-plus crore from multiple customers. Revenue fell because of lower Middle East-linked outbound traffic from the war; the CFO said Q1 was better than Q4 on the global mix in some respects.

543596|2026-06.headline: TMB Q1 FY27 net profit rose 34.97% YoY to a record INR412 crores, with total business up 23% to INR1,21,715 crores.
543596|2026-06.overview: Tamilnad Mercantile Bank reported its strongest quarter on record: net profit of INR412 crores (up 34.97% YoY), NII up 32.01%, and operating profit of INR611 crores (up 48.22%). Total business grew 23%, driven by advances up 27.01% (gold-heavy, with agri at 40% of the book) and deposits up 19.71%, with term deposits up 20.73% and CASA down 2.95% QoQ as the bank prioritised resource mobilisation. Management raised FY27 guidance for deposits, advances and total business by 2 percentage points each, and cut its cost-to-income guidance, while stating that ECL transition provisioning (INR276 crores set aside so far) will be phased in. Asset quality improved on a YoY basis, with GNPA at 0.69% and NNPA at 0.17%.

segments.name: Agri (incl. gold loans)
segments.commentary: 40% of advances; yield raised to 10.54% from 9.75%, which management attributes to deliberate gold loan repricing. Gold loan portfolio yield is 10.58%; management says the book can absorb about a 20% fall in gold prices.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: 28% of advances; YoY growth of 20.09% (earlier cited 14.89%), adding about INR500 crores per quarter. Yield fell to about 10% from 10.5% as the bank widened its customer base with finer pricing.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: 25% of advances. Home loans are declining but the decline is arrested; vehicle loans grew 25.7%. Retail shows a QoQ decline, which management partly attributes to migration from retail to agri gold loans.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: 5.62% of advances; grew 6.69% YoY. Unsecured exposure is 10 bps of the book, with NPA of about INR56 lakh.

guidance_outlook: FY27 CASA growth guidance of 17-18% reiterated; management expects CASA to recover from Q2 with 60 branch openings planned this year (6 opened in Q1).
FY27 deposit growth guidance raised to 18% from 16%; advances growth guidance raised to 21-22% from 20%; total business growth guidance raised to 20% from 18%.
NIM guidance: management expects to be well past 4% for the year versus the earlier 3.90% guide. ROA now expected to be well above 2% versus the earlier 1.9% guide.
ROE guidance revised to 15% (stated as a revised guidance). GNPA to stay below 1%.
Cost-to-income: earlier 46-47% range; management says it is revising this downwards by about 2 percentage points, after Q1 at 39.10%.

ECL: INR324 crores additional provision requirement at 30 June 2026; with INR250 crores COVID contingency provision and INR26 crores added in Q1, INR276 crores is set aside. No further provisions planned in Q2; phasing over 4-5 years permitted by RBI, with the bank aiming to complete it earlier.
FY27 IT budget of around INR280 crores; cybersecurity about 10% of this, with management signalling it will not be a constraint on spending.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 628 after 6 additions in Q1 (3 in Tamil Nadu, 3 outside); 171 branches are outside Tamil Nadu. Plan to open 60 branches in FY27 versus 44 in FY26.
IT spend of about INR280 crores in FY27: infrastructure 21%, new software acquisition and enhancement about 20%, cybersecurity about 10%, others about 35% (as stated).
Business per employee INR23.75 crores; profit per employee INR32.12 lakh; 325 new employees recruited in Q1.
CD ratio 88.97% against a stated maximum of 99% on the bank's net worth; management expects term deposit focus to moderate CD ratio gains.
Leverage ratio 12.5% (regulatory minimum 3.5%); LCR 140.74%; NSFR 150.74%.
demand_pricing: Management expects gold loan growth to slow in H2 FY27 as gold prices stabilise around $4,000 per ounce; growth will be driven by tonnage and new customers rather than price.
Gold loan LTV: average 56.98%; consumption loans capped at 85% (principal plus accrued interest); agri gold loans have no LTV cap. Gold loans are 6-month or 1-year bullet structures, not EMI.
Gold loan share of advances is 46.97% (the transcript corrected 47.82%), with an informal internal cap of 50%.
Retail growth to come from vehicle loans (about 25% growth) and home loans (8-10% growth targeted for FY27) and LAP. MSME is targeted to grow 21-22%, combined with gold loans.
MSME to be grown through a hybrid CGTMSE-plus-collateral model; CGTMSE described as one of the ways to grow, not the main route.

financial_highlights.change: up 48.22% YoY; up from INR522 crores QoQ
CASA balance up 16.94% YoY, down 2.95% QoQ

qa_highlights.question: Digant Haria (GreenEdge Wealth) asked for FY27 guidance on loan growth, margins, ROA and ROE.
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept the April guidance structure but raised it: deposits 16% to 18%, advances 20% to 21-22%, total business 18% to 20%, CASA 17-18% reiterated, NIM well past 4% (vs 3.90%), ROA well over 2% (vs 1.9%), ROE revised to 15%, GNPA below 1%.

qa_highlights.question: Digant Haria asked when MSME and other retail would pick up, given the quarter was gold-heavy.
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to MSME (YoY growth now above 20% vs 14.89% earlier, about INR500 crores added per quarter) as the lever to fill the gap as gold loan growth slows in H2 FY27 with gold prices stabilising near $4,000 an ounce.

qa_highlights.question: Laksh (Share India Securities) asked for MSME growth guidance and whether El Nino or the war had affected the book.
qa_highlights.answer: No specific MSME guidance yet; management said it would come back after the quarter, but expects growth well above the 20%-plus number put on the table. No stress seen so far from El Nino or the war, based on cash-flow studies and customer outreach.

qa_highlights.question: Parth (360 ONE Capital) asked what drove the QoQ rise in SMA 0, 1 and 2, and the divergent agri and MSME yields.
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loan portfolio at-risk-one-day rose by roughly INR100-150 crores, now being contained by a corrective mechanism. Agri yield rose to 10.54% from 9.75% through deliberate gold loan repricing; MSME yield fell to about 10% from 10.5% as the bank widened its customer base with finer pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Parth asked about the Enforcement Directorate order on the foreign-investor shares and whether they are now free of encumbrance.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was too early to comment; the bank is not party to the case between the ED and the investors. It has engaged a top legal firm to advise on the order, and the ED can still appeal.

qa_highlights.question: Parth asked why the retail portfolio declined QoQ.
qa_highlights.answer: Vincent M D said vehicle loans grew 25.7%, home loan decline has been arrested and is roughly at its 2025 level, and the bank expects home loans to grow 8-10% in FY27. Salee S. Nair attributed part of the QoQ retail decline to migration from retail gold loans to agri gold loans.

qa_highlights.question: Arvind (Sundaram Alternates) asked about MSME slippages and non-gold retail growth drivers.
qa_highlights.answer: The INR37 crore MSME slippage relates to only 2 accounts and is expected to be resolved in Q2. Gross NPA is INR160.35 crores vs INR202.34 crores in June 2025. Growth focus is home loans, vehicle loans (about 25% growth) and LAP.

qa_highlights.question: Vinith Jain (Siddhi Capital) asked about FY27 IT spend and ECL phasing.
qa_highlights.answer: IT budget is about INR280 crores: infrastructure 21%, software about 20%, cybersecurity about 10%, others about 35%. ECL: INR276 crores set aside (INR250 crores COVID contingency plus INR26 crores in Q1) against INR324 crores required; no further provision planned in the current quarter, with completion targeted in FY28 and possibly earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Vinith Jain asked whether there is an internal ceiling on the gold loan share, now 46.97% (corrected from 47.82%).
qa_highlights.answer: Management has an informal internal cap of 50% on the gold loan share. It expects the share to rise slightly but not significantly, and wants non-gold segments to grow in tandem.

qa_highlights.question: Nishit Shah (ViSolitech) asked whether CGTMSE is a route to grow MSME and whether a sub-40% cost-to-income ratio is sustainable.
qa_highlights.answer: CGTMSE is one route, used as a hybrid with collateral as skin in the game, not the main strategy. Management had earlier guided 46-47% cost-to-income, now revised down by about 2 percentage points; the sub-40% Q1 print included one-offs.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor (Kapoor & Co) asked how the gold loan tonnage strategy differs from today and whether operating profit can hold near INR611 crores.
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is shifting from price-led to tonnage and new customers, with branch advertising and gold loans delivered in under 10 minutes. On sustaining profit, management said MSME at a 10%-plus yield and other segments would support profit growth; it deferred a direct answer to the Q2 call.

risks_watch: Gold loan growth slowdown in H2 FY27 as gold prices stabilise near $4,000 per ounce; the bank says growth will need to come from tonnage and new customers. Gold loans are about 47% of advances against an informal 50% cap.
SMA 0/1/2 rose QoQ, driven by a INR100-150 crore uptick in gold loans at risk; management says it is under control but gave no figure. Watch the Q2 SMA trend.
ECL transition: INR324 crores required, INR276 crores set aside; RBI allows phasing over 4-5 years. Q2 provisioning and any trigger-based top-up need monitoring.

So, the portfolios are going to go in different directions.
So it is going to be a tonnage game going forward.

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: MSME slippage resolution
rows.why: INR37 crores of MSME slippage relates to only 2 accounts, with management expecting resolution in Q2, against gross NPA of INR160.35 crores (vs INR202.34 crores in June 2025).

543596|2026-09.headline: TMB posted record Q2 FY27 net profit of INR451 crore (+42.09% YoY) on 27.25% business growth, with net NPA at 0.14%.
543596|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 as its eighth straight quarter of beating the prior quarter's growth, with total business up 27.25% YoY to INR1,30,237 crore and net profit at a record INR451 crore. Net interest income rose to INR807 crore and NIM was 4.19%, down about 10 bps QoQ as term-deposit mix and refinance (about INR1,000 crore at 7-7.5%) pushed up funding costs. The bank made full provisions for SMA-1 and SMA-2 ahead of ECL norms effective 1 April 2027, with provisions of INR304.24 crore against an estimated INR385 crore ECL requirement. Management raised FY27 floors for deposits (20%+) and advances (22%+), and guided NIM at 4.10% plus or minus 5 bps for the rest of the year.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book about INR29,280 crore, of which agri about INR22,000 crore and retail about INR6,084 crore. Portfolio LTV 62.35%; about 3.1% of book would be above market value on a 20% gold price fall; gold loan SMA-0-to-3 at risk about INR28 crore (0.10%).

segments.name: Advances and MSME
segments.commentary: Advances up 29.32% to INR60,691 crore; MSME growth 23.62%. Unsecured exposure about 20 bps; the uptick was a loan to Kerala State Electricity Board secured against cash flows. About 52% of advances are repo-linked, 43% MCLR-linked, about 5% treasury-linked.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Deposits up 25.49% to INR69,546 crore, with term deposits up about 29%. Non-callable deposits were 40.62% of incremental term deposits (INR7,570 crore in H1). FCNR(B) raised about USD51.94 million; 1-year FCNR(B) rate now about 4.25%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 deposit growth floor raised to 20%+ from earlier 18%+; advances growth floor 22%+; CASA growth about 17% in H2.
NIM guided at 4.10% plus or minus 5 bps for the rest of FY27, versus the earlier 4% guidance.
Cost to income expected to rise from 38.28% but stay well below 44% as branches open and IT investment continues.
Target of 60 branch openings in FY27 (9 opened in H1), with 20+ outside Tamil Nadu by year-end.
Long-term aim is to grow 4-5 percentage points faster than the industry over the next 3-5 years.
CD ratio can rise to 98% against 87.27% currently, given net worth of 12.53% of the balance sheet.
capex_capacity: Nine branches opened in H1 FY27; 60 planned for the year, with 37 opened YoY (15 outside Tamil Nadu).
Business per employee at INR25 crore; profit per employee about INR35 lakh.
Ongoing IT investment and data/process automation cited as drivers of productivity and cost pressure.
Leverage ratio 11.99% vs 3.50% requirement; LCR 139.43%; NSFR 146.15%.
demand_pricing: Investment portfolio rose to about 22% of the balance sheet, yielding about 7% vs about 10.3% on advances, which weighed on margin mix.
Repo cut passthrough is automatic at each loan's quarterly reset; the 25 bps repo move flows to the 5.5% benchmark over about three months.
Refinance of about INR1,000 crore taken from SIDBI at 7-7.5% during the quarter.
Bulk deposits are 19% of total deposits; the bulk share of the INR7,570 crore incremental term deposits was not disclosed on the call.
Management sees no material oil-price impact so far on export credit or MSME books; drought risk is being monitored through daily gold LTV tracking.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of gold loans between agri and retail, and how much of the book is repo-linked?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loans total INR29,280 crore: agri about INR22,000 crore and retail INR6,084 crore. About 52% of advances are repo-linked (reset quarterly), 43% MCLR-linked, about 5% treasury-linked.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank sustain high growth and how is the oil price affecting it?
qa_highlights.answer: The target is to grow 4-5 percentage points above industry growth over 3-5 years, not a fixed 20-30% rate. No oil-price impact seen yet in export credit or MSME.

qa_highlights.question: How has NIM and yield on advances moved, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Yield on advances rose to 10.32% from 10.10% as advances were repriced to offset higher deposit costs. NIM guided at 4.10% plus or minus 5 bps for the rest of FY27, with management calling it a floor.

qa_highlights.question: Will the cost to income ratio rise, and what is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost to income is expected to move up from 38.28% due to branch openings and IT spend, but to stay well below 44%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the IRDAI insurance norms?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance commission is only about INR9 crore in H1. Management estimated about a 20% reduction in that income, which incremental business would offset.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the disputed share ownership matter, and would it block a bonus or split?
qa_highlights.answer: The Appellate Tribunal order dated 9 July has not been appealed by the bank or ED within the window. The bank has applied to RBI to regularise the share transfer, and management said this does not block a bonus or split.

risks_watch: Funding cost pressure from term-deposit mix shift and refinance; NIM guided lower to 4.10% plus or minus 5 bps.
ECL norms from 1 April 2027: estimated INR385 crore requirement vs INR304.24 crore provisions held (about 80% cover).
Gold price volatility: gold traded above USD4,000 an ounce; the bank cut per-gram valuation by about INR800 in recent days.
Pending RBI decision on regularising the disputed share transfer (FEMA issue).
Cost-to-income drift upward from branch expansion and IT spend, plus IRDAI commission impact.
543596|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, profit and asset quality, with a repeated message that guidance numbers are floors. Noticeably defensive on NIM mix, the FCNR(B) deposit size and the bulk-deposit breakdown, which management said it would follow up on later.
key_quotes: And this growth has driven a strong net profit, the highest ever, INR451 crores highest ever net profit.
What we are looking for is to exceed the industry growth by a certain percentage.
And I would say 4.10% plus/minus 5 basis is what we are looking for the rest of the year.
We have provided a provision available of INR304.24 crores against the INR385 crores that is required to cover the expected credit loss.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not a relevant metric for a bank, and no new capex beyond the existing branch rollout was discussed; capital adequacy is 32.39% and leverage 11.99%, so capital is not a constraint.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said guidance numbers are floors; advances growth was raised to 22%+ and deposits to 20%+, while business grew 27.25% YoY in Q2.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: NIM guided down to 4.10% plus or minus 5 bps, cost-to-income to rise from 38.28% toward 'well below 44%', and ECL norms from 1 April 2027 require about INR385 crore against INR304.24 crore already provided (about 80% cover).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launch was discussed on the call.

rows.label: Cost-to-income drift upward from branch expansion and IT spend
rows.why: Cost-to-income at 38.28% is expected to rise from here as branches open and IT investment continues, though management says it stays well below 44%.

rows.label: ECL norms effective 1 April 2027
rows.why: Estimated INR385 crore ECL requirement vs INR304.24 crore provisions held, so about INR81 crore of further provisioning is needed; SMA-1 and SMA-2 are already fully provided.

rows.label: RBI decision on regularising disputed share transfer
rows.why: Bank has applied to RBI to regularise the FEMA-linked share transfer; management says it does not block a bonus or split, but RBI outcome is pending.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, profit and asset quality (net NPA 0.14%, credit cost 9 bps) and framed guidance as floors, but was defensive on NIM mix, FCNR(B) size and the bulk-deposit breakdown; analysts pushed on NIM, the oil-price and IRDAI impact.

543597|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 18% to INR823 crore and EBITDA reached about INR86 crore (10.4% margin), with Q4 revenue at about INR317 crore.
543597|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a recovery year after a difficult H1, with consolidated revenue of about INR823 crore (up about 18%), EBITDA up from about INR60 crore to about INR86 crore, and margin up from 8.6% to 10.4%. PAT rose to about INR15 crore (1.8% margin) from about INR12 crore, while PBT was flat, which management attributed partly to the first year of Ind AS (including right-of-use asset effects). Q4 revenue was about INR317 crore versus INR240 crore a year earlier. Management is guiding to a 35-40% revenue CAGR over three to five years and is expanding capacity in EMS, AC, refrigeration and compressors, with the new compressor line in commercial production since January 2026.

financial_highlights.change: from INR240 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: described as normal, in line with expectations

segments.name: Air conditioners (AC)
segments.commentary: Share of revenue fell from about 70-75% to about 60% in FY26; ODM share of AC revenue was 40-50%. Company now has 4 AC customers and expects 1-2 new names next season. Average realisation about INR20,000-20,000-odd per unit.

segments.name: EMS and lighting
segments.commentary: About 15% of revenue; running at 70-80% utilisation through the year. Capacity to rise from 4 lakh CPH to 8 lakh (phase 1, by about end-August 2026) and 12 lakh (phase 2, by FY-end).

segments.name: Commercial refrigeration / defreezers
segments.commentary: About 10% of revenue; utilisation about 60%. Capacity 1.5 lakh units to 2.5 lakh (phase 1) and 4 lakh (phase 2); glass-top range added alongside hardtop. Target RAC-type growth of 30-40% in FY27.

segments.name: Components
segments.commentary: About 7% of revenue and rising; a major contributor to margin protection in the first nine months.

segments.name: Compressors (reciprocating, new subsidiary Virtuoso Compressors)
segments.commentary: Commercial production began January 2026 at about 60% utilisation on 2.8 million capacity, targeting about 80% in 2-3 months; expansion to 6 million by March 2027. Average realisation INR1,400-1,500; FY27 margin guided at 6-7%; value addition 5-10%.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of 35-40% over three to five years, applied to the INR825 crore base; management said it is not revising guidance, with exact numbers to be shared during the year.
EBITDA margin for FY27 guided at 9-10%, described as 'closer to double digits'; management called 12% a wishful number.
PAT margin expected to improve by 50-100 bps over the next two years as Ind AS adjustments fade.
Compressor margin 6-7% in FY27, potentially above double digits over 2-4 years as Chinese imports restrict and backward integration rises (11-12% in 4-5 years).
RAC utilisation target of 60-65% and volume growth of about 30-40% in FY27.
Chennai plant expected to contribute about 5-6% of volume in its first year.
Peak-utilisation revenue capacity from the current expansion is good for beyond INR2,500 crore, but management said reaching that from INR800 crore in two years is a big ask and will take more time.
HoldCo net debt addition of about INR50-60 crore in FY27; INR150 crore debt at the compressor subsidiary; INR250 crore equity approval is a blanket enabling approval, not a fundraising commitment.
capex_capacity: Compressors: capacity 2.8 million to 6 million by March 2027 (9-10 month build), INR150 crore phase-1 investment, already tied up; long-term target 8-8.5 million, with 7.5 million or 9.5 million considered if demand and contracts materialise.
AC: capacity about 1 million to 1.8 million by end FY27, with 1.3 million targeted before the next AC season; investment INR40-50 crore, mainly debt-funded, with some debt already tied up.
EMS: new advanced facility; phase 1 by end-August 2026 and phase 2 by FY-end; investment about INR25 crore, tied up.
Refrigeration: two phases at about INR20-25 crore each (INR25-50 crore total); first phase to be completed before the next AC season.
Compressor separate manufacturing facility planned at Nasik; development work to start shortly. New Nasik tool room operational.
demand_pricing: Raw-material pass-through about 10-15% across the industry from manufacturers to brands and to consumers; management said margin pressure was offset by customer price hikes, new customers, old inventory, subsidies and product diversification.
Management expects AC margins to hold at current levels in FY27 barring macro shocks, while noting ODM margins are not yet ideal.

Government restricts reciprocating compressor imports to 40% of FY24-25 base-year levels, meaning 50-60% of OEM/ODM requirement must be sourced locally; the company says it is the only OEM/ODM player currently doing this.

Two competitors expected to start local compressor manufacturing (one by end-Q3/Q4 FY27, one mid-2027). Management estimates a market gap of 14-15 million units against total planned capacity of 15-18 million.
Demand described as strong for AC; April-June 2026 expected to be an excellent quarter for RAC. Management said AC demand runway is long because the base is small.
PLI: no concrete roadmap for renewal beyond this year; government said to be considering options.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes have been taken in AC and will margins hold in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Price hikes have covered raw-material pressure but not added real gains; management expects margins to stay at current levels absent macro shocks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and funding for the capacity expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: EMS phase 1 in about 3 months, AC to 1.3 million before the season and 1.8 million within FY27, refrigeration phase 1 before the next season, and compressors 2.8 to 6 million by March. Compressor (INR150 crore) and EMS (INR25 crore) are funded; AC (INR40-50 crore) will largely be debt-funded.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 margin and realisation expectations for compressors and the company overall?
qa_highlights.answer: Compressor margin 6-7% in FY27; company EBITDA margin 9-10%. Compressor realisation about INR1,400-1,500 per unit. Management said 12% margin is wishful.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 revenue guidance lower than the INR1,200 crore target previously mentioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not revising guidance; the 35-40% CAGR on the INR825 crore base implies a figure near INR1,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will the compressor capacity to 6 million be enough, and how does the QCO affect the 7.5 million plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 6 million is the first target; the drop from 7 million was line optimisation, not government action. Further growth to 7.5-9.5 million depends on long-term contracts; the INR150 crore subsidiary debt is enough for the 6 million target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mainboard migration timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: BSE in-principle approval received; NSE expected within a week, followed by 4-6 weeks for migration and listing, so possibly by end-August per management.

risks_watch: Execution risk on the expansion plan: management said in the call that 100% execution is not in its control, and an earlier 150K-to-400K capacity plan was not delivered.
Competitive entry in compressors (two new local players in 2026-27) could affect utilisation and pricing once the 40% import allowance is revised.
Raw-material volatility with only 10-15% pass-through; margins below peers in ODM AC business.
Dependence on AC is still about 60% of revenue; demand is seasonal and utilisation figures are highly seasonal.
Revenue guidance ambiguity: the 35-40% CAGR implies about INR1,000 crore base, while the earlier INR1,200 crore target was not revised explicitly.
Debt and equity plans (HoldCo debt INR50-60 crore; INR250 crore equity blanket approval) need monitoring; the company said it will look at funding requirements over the next 1-3 months.
Possible PLI expiry after FY26 with no roadmap yet.
Product-wise FY26 revenue split was given only for nine months in the presentation; management said this would be corrected to a 12-month basis.
543597|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on demand, capacity and the compressor opportunity, with a clear focus on diversification. Cautious and hedged on margins, RM pass-through and the competitive landscape, and noncommittal on the FY27 revenue target and the timing of expansion, repeatedly saying plans are not fully within management's control.
key_quotes: Going forward in this year also, we expect the margins to remain where they are, unless of course there are any other macroeconomic jolts.
AC should remain around 50%.

So, we believe there will be two or three players in this segment active in a year or two, which also makes for healthy competition, but we still believe that 6 million is a number that we will be able to fill.
This is a very wishful number. I think we will try and keep it closer to double digits.

rows.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin at 9-10% versus 10.4% in FY26, but PAT margin is guided up 50-100 bps over two years as Ind AS adjustments fade; compressors at 6-7% margin dilute mix.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: EMS phase 1 by end-Aug 2026; AC 1.3m before next AC season;
rows.why: Compressor capacity under construction with INR150 crore phase-1 tied up; EMS INR25 crore tied up; AC capacity 1m to 1.8m by end FY27 with INR40-50 crore; utilisation at about 60% for compressors and RAC, so the adds are already in motion.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Guided 35-40% revenue CAGR on INR825 crore base and RAC volume growth of 30-40% in FY27, backed by Q4 revenue of INR317 crore versus INR240 crore a year earlier (about +32%).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: AC utilisation is high and the 1.8m target is only partly funded (AC debt-funded at INR40-50 crore); Nasik compressor facility development is starting shortly, and the company will review funding over the next 1-3 months.

rows.why: Management said it is not revising guidance, the 35-40% CAGR implies about INR1,000 crore, below the earlier INR1,200 crore target, and 12% margin was called wishful.

rows.why: Management admits 100% execution is not in its control, an earlier 150K-to-400K capacity plan was not delivered, and compressor capacity was already trimmed from 7m to 6m.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Glass-top refrigeration range added alongside hardtop, Nasik tool room operational, and 1-2 new AC customers expected next season.

rows.why: Imports capped at 40% of FY24-25 base, so 50-60% of OEM/ODM need must be local; management estimates a 14-15 million unit gap versus 15-18 million planned industry capacity, though two competitors enter in FY27.

rows.why: BSE in-principle approval received; NSE expected within a week, then 4-6 weeks for migration and listing.

543597|2026-06.headline: Virtuoso Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 85% YoY to INR 376.6 crore, with PAT up about 103% to INR 9 crore; FY27 guidance of 35-40% growth and 9-10% EBITDA margin maintained.
543597|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR 376.6 crore, up about 85% YoY and about 18.7% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at about 9.3%, similar to Q4 FY26. PAT rose about 103% YoY to about INR 9 crore from INR 6.4 crore. Management said raw material (copper, aluminium, imported compressor inputs) and logistics pressure squeezed margins, with pricing expected to stabilise over the next couple of quarters. Commercial refrigeration was slower in Q1 as buyers deferred purchases after price hikes. Management kept FY27 guidance of 35-40% growth and 9-10% EBITDA margin, and said an upward revision depends on Q3.

financial_highlights.change: ~103% YoY vs INR 6.4 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue mix Q1 FY27: deep freezers
financial_highlights.change: Similar to EMS; balance from components

segments.name: Room AC (ODM)
segments.commentary: About 70% of Q1 FY27 revenue; FY27 expected at 55-60% of revenue. Largest AC customer (Voltas) about 40-45% of AC segment, expected 25-35% in FY27; AC capacity going from 1.0 mn to 1.8 mn units over 12-15 months. Margins are under pressure; management expects improvement from FY28.

segments.name: Compressor
segments.commentary: Production began late Dec 2025 and runs at over 50% utilisation; capacity going from 2.8 mn to 6 mn, targeted Dec/Jan. Expected ~15% of FY27 revenue; EBITDA margin about 6-7% currently. Captive use only 2-3% of sales; works with 8-9 customers, with no single customer above 20-23% expected.

segments.name: Commercial refrigeration
segments.commentary: Q1 slower due to price increases and deferred buying; management says Q2-Q3 projections have been pushed out, not cut. Capex INR 20-25 crore this year; capacity 400,000 units, with a potential INR 360 crore revenue at 60% utilisation.

segments.name: EMS
segments.commentary: Capacity going from 4 lakh to 12 lakh cph; first 8 lakh cph phase expected by mid/end September, commercial production by end Q3. About 10% of FY27 revenue; little top-line impact this year, with revenue expected from FY28.

segments.name: Deep freezers
segments.commentary: Capacity going from 1.5 lakh to 2.5 lakh units by mid/end Q3 FY27; second phase to 4 lakh units in FY28.

segments.name: Components and washing machines
segments.commentary: Expected ~5% of FY27 revenue; Chennai and Sanand picking up. Washing machine work is mainly with one anchor customer this year.

guidance_outlook: Maintains FY27 revenue growth guidance of 35-40%; management said an upward revision depends on Q3 performance, with an update at end of Q3.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 9-10% maintained; management said Q1 margin of 9.3% is healthy and margins could move closer to 10% once pricing stabilises.
Net margin guidance of 2-3% (answering a 2.5-3% query), with tax timing noted.
Margin improvement expected mainly in FY28 as raw material pressure eases over 6-12 months.
Long-term ambition of 35-40% revenue CAGR over the next three to five years; peak revenue at current expansion estimated at INR 3,500-4,000 crore within 12 months.
Total FY27 capex INR 80-100 crore at VOEPL; commercial refrigeration capex INR 20-25 crore.
capex_capacity: EMS: 4 lakh cph moving to 12 lakh cph in two phases; first 8 lakh cph expected mid/end Sept 2026, commercial production by end Q3.
AC: 1.0 mn to 1.8 mn units in two phases (1.0 to 1.3, then 1.3 to 1.8) over 12-15 months; 27-28 season expected to utilise 50-60% of the increased capacity.

Compressors: 2.8 mn to 6 mn units, targeted Dec/Jan with commercial production by Q4 FY27; compressor utilisation target above 75% by next year; INR 500 crore total project, INR 150 crore raised via OCD, first phase funded by equity issue; 22-acre land bought for consolidation.
Deep freezers: 1.5 lakh to 2.5 lakh units by mid/end Q3 FY27; 4 lakh units in FY28.
Vertical capacity is generally expanded only after 50-70% utilisation for seasonal products and 70-80% for non-seasonal ones; new capacity needs 12-24 months to reach target utilisation.
demand_pricing: RAC industry growth expected at 8-10% in the coming season; management said prices have stabilised and inventory levels are normal.
Market is absorbing price hikes slowly in commercial refrigeration; B2B buyers deferred purchases in Q1.
Import restriction on compressors at 40% per government policy, expected to ease in 1-2 years; management sees this as an opening for market growth.
Raw material pressure (copper, aluminium, imported compressor components, logistics) persisted; PCB/chip cost impact limited so far.
PLI benefit worth about 1% of EBITDA, mainly in AC; management is negotiating with customers to share the impact over the next 12 months.
Customer concentration: top AC customer at over 60% in FY26, expected 25-35% in FY27; AC customer count is four.

qa_highlights.question: Will Virtuoso make AC compressors after the Voltas-linked startup win, and what is the plan for the 22-acre land?
qa_highlights.answer: Only refrigeration compressors are confirmed so far; no AC compressor plan has been finalised, and the 22-acre parcel is for consolidating the refrigeration compressor business at one location over 1-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What underpins the 35-40% growth guidance, and how does it compare with the 43% CAGR over FY21-FY25?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth rests on high-growth AC and compressor verticals, first-mover advantage in compressors, the 40% import restriction easing over 1-2 years, and an AC order book; management said the market is growing 10-15% and value-add can drive 35-40%.

qa_highlights.question: Will AC margins improve as the ODM mix rises, and how do OEM and ODM margins differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material pressure may persist for 6-12 months, with margin improvement expected mainly in FY28; OEM vs ODM margin difference is about 1-1.5 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: Given Q1 growth, will FY27 guidance be revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is unchanged for now; Q1 and Q4 are the biggest quarters and a possible upward revision depends on Q3, with an update at end-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AC capacity utilisation outlook for FY28 and how much is from existing versus new customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Expected 50-60% utilisation of the increased capacity in the 2027-28 season, a combination of existing customer projections and new onboardings; full capacity live before that season.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR 500 crore compressor project funded beyond the INR 150 crore raised?
qa_highlights.answer: The first phase is covered by the equity issue in progress, with INR 150 crore via OCD; the next phase's debt versus equity mix will be decided over the next 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commercial refrigeration capex, revenue potential, and the medium-term CAPEX plan?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant capex in Q1; INR 20-25 crore planned this year and a similar amount next year for the 400,000-unit capacity; at 60% utilisation revenue is about INR 360 crore, with another large capex needed beyond that.

543600|2026-06.headline: Harsha Engineers Q1 FY27 consolidated Engineering supply up 25% YoY to Rs 421 crore, but EBITDA margin compressed on a 6-7% raw material spike pending pass-through.
543600|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Engineering supply rose to Rs 421 crore from Rs 382 crore QoQ and Rs 349 crore YoY, with India Engineering growing about 21% YoY and 6% QoQ. Consolidated Engineering EBITDA was Rs 69.8 crore versus Rs 77 crore QoQ and Rs 65.3 crore YoY, so margin fell QoQ. Management attributed the squeeze to an ~8% rise in average raw material cost (lagged pass-through of one to two quarters), about Rs 4 crore of FX hedge accounting loss, and about Rs 3 crore of higher indirect material costs after the West Asia conflict. Management kept FY27 guidance of high-teens India growth and low-teens consolidated growth, with India Engineering EBITDA margin of 22-24%.

543638|2026-03.headline: Tracxn Q4 FY26 revenue from operations Rs 20.5 crore; EBITDA negative Rs 6.6 crore, PAT marginally negative Rs 0.6 crore, adjusted PAT positive Rs 2.5 crore.

Management described the deal environment as weak in deal volume (near a 10-year low) while M&A and IB activity was rebounding, and it is adding GTM headcount and AI distribution channels for FY27. Blended ASP per account fell, driven mainly by mix shift toward lower-priced accounts rather than price cuts.

543644|2026-09.headline: InfoBeans Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to Rs 165 crore and PAT grew 16% YoY, with 6% QoQ revenue growth, the seventh straight quarter of sequential growth.
543644|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 165 crore, up 28% YoY from Rs 129 crore, and up 6% QoQ; PAT rose 16% YoY and 21% QoQ to Rs 26 crore. Operating margin was about 24%, against a stated target of 24% and PAT margin of 14-15%. Excluding the prior-year H1 Employee Retention Credit (Rs 6.3 crore), H1 revenue grew 30% in INR and 22% in USD terms. The call also covered Claude Select Services partner status with Anthropic, a net addition of 43 employees on a base of about 1,800, and an M&A search with no deal announced.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company devoting capacity to strong growth, and which industries are performing well?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is spread across BFSI, manufacturing, logistics and HR with no single industry standing out; healthcare compliance was the only softness.

qa_highlights.question: How much net hiring was done and what are the plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Net addition of 43 in the quarter on a base of 1,800+ (about 2-3%); the year-level guidance is 10-15% net addition, with AI used to raise efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Is pricing pressure seen from AI or outcome-based pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no pricing pressure and that outcome-based pricing has not hurt the top line; AI is also used internally to cut evaluation and appraisal cycles from weeks to days.

qa_highlights.question: Explain the Rs 9 crore capitalised intangibles and the director loan.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook, US concentration and visa risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to raise US share (49% now) and to expand the US sales team; visa restrictions have little impact since about 50 of nearly 1,900 people are on visas. Management declined to forecast.

543653|2026-03.headline: Bikaji Q4 FY26 revenue grew close to 18% to about INR720 crores, with FY26 revenue of INR2,994 crores and 9.5% volume growth.
543653|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 top-line growth of close to 18%, with revenue from operations around INR720 crores, EBITDA about INR88 crores (roughly 12.2% margin) and PAT about INR56 crores. For FY26, revenue was about INR2,994 crores on 9.5% volume growth, with consolidated gross margin of 35.1% and EBITDA margin of 13.7%, up over 120 bps. Q4 EBITDA was pressured by a step-up in advertising linked to the Bhujia and Kya Baat Hai Ji campaigns, plus a Bengal-election labour exodus and a 2.5-day factory shutdown. Management took a price rise of about 3% in April 2026 to offset edible oil and packaging inflation.

segments.commentary: Family pack grew about 20% in Q4 and impulse about 14%. Family pack price was raised and impulse grammage cut.

Consolidated gross margin target is to maintain FY26 level (35.1%) in FY27; EBITDA expected to improve through fixed-cost leverage and CMU (co-manufacturing) output.

Production shift from Bikaner to co-manufacturing units (CMU) expected to add operational efficiency in FY27.
Sweets capacity at 100%+ utilisation in festive months but very low utilisation off-season.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 EBITDA margin fall to about 11% from about 13.5-14% in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to advertising, which was about 3.2-3.3% of sales in Q3/Q4 versus about 1% in H1, plus about 50 bps of one-time doubtful-debt provisions in the last two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the difference between consolidated growth of 19% and standalone growth of 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap is mainly THF retail, worth about 2.2 percentage points of growth, with Bikaji USA and Ariba also contributing; management confirmed there is no inorganic contribution this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin outlook and the price hike plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to hold consolidated gross margin at FY26 levels and says EBITDA will improve on fixed-cost leverage and CMU volumes; one price rise of about 3% was taken in April.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sweets growth constraint?
qa_highlights.answer: Sweets is capacity-constrained in festive months and under-utilised off-season; a new Bikaner factory and small all-season SKUs at INR5-10 are planned, with FY27 sweets budgeted at about 12.5% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlet split and the target for 5 lakh outlets?
qa_highlights.answer: Current direct reach is 3.5 lakh outlets; the next 1.5 lakh are expected mainly from focus states, with core states moving toward direct distribution rather than wholesalers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Western snacks slow in Q4 and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Western snacks grew about 8.5% in Q4 after 25% in Q3; management attributed it to weaker family-pack traction and a soft category, and expects 20%+ growth going forward from a base of 1.1% national share.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation: edible oil and packaging costs are volatile due to the war; further price increases may be needed to protect gross margin.
