543653|2026-06.headline: Bikaji Q1 FY27 revenue grew ~12.5% (volume +7.7%) despite a 3–4 day Bikaner plant/dispatch shutdown and labour exits; EBITDA margin ~13.5% vs 12.2% QoQ.
543653|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 as a story of two halves: April to mid-May was hit by a 3–4 day shutdown after the Chairman's passing and a loss of Bengali labour around the Bengal elections, while the last ~45 days saw strong recovery, with management citing ~20% growth in that period. Value growth of 12.5% was led by Western Snacks (+21.3%) and Ethnic Snacks (+11.4%), with exports the only weak channel (-2.2%). EBITDA margin was ~13.5% against ~12.2% last quarter, and management guided FY27 EBITDA margin to 13–13.5% including PLI, with festive-season ad spend rising. Price hikes are on hold until Diwali.

543663|2026-06.headline: Five-Star Q1 FY27 disbursements hit a record INR 1,496 crore (+23% QoQ, +16% YoY) while AUM grew 4% QoQ to INR 13,722 crore.
543663|2026-06.overview: Management reported a record quarterly disbursement of INR 1,496 crore and AUM of INR 13,722 crore, up 4% QoQ. Asset quality metrics improved modestly: 1+ current book rose to 83.30%, 30+ fell to 12.38%, and the 1.85% credit cost was slightly lower QoQ, while slippages were flat at 0.70%. Management guided to lower credit costs and NPLs in coming quarters, with opex staying flat in FY27 on an employee-cost reset. Q&A focused on yield compression, cost of borrowing, write-off run-rate, opex, and the timeline to higher leverage.

financial_highlights.change: Average cost of funds down ~15 bps, spread up 3 bps
Recoveries ~INR 35 crore incl. write-off and NPA settlements (vs INR 26-27 crore in Q4)

segments.name: Micro LAP (core product)
segments.commentary: Onboarding yields average ~22.5% (range 21.5%-23%); management sees yield settling near 22.25% after 10-15 bps further compression over next couple of quarters. Average ticket size ~INR 4.5-5 lakh, targeting 25/50/25 mix across ~INR 3 lakh, ~INR 5 lakh and ~INR 10 lakh tickets.

segments.name: Housing loans
segments.commentary: Launched about two quarters ago; management said focus has been on restoring micro LAP before pushing housing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance of ~20% reiterated; management expects FY27 disbursements of INR 6,500-6,800 crore (Q1 run-rate plus ~10%).
FY27 credit cost guided at 1.7%-1.9%; management said the trend is more likely toward 1.7%. Overall ECL coverage to be maintained at ~1.75%-1.8%.
Gross NPA to fall to sub-3% and a steady-state NPA of ~2.5%; steady-state Stage 1 ~91-92%, Stage 2 ~6-7%.
Write-offs for FY27 guided at INR 225-250 crore (~INR 55-60 crore per quarter).
Opex to stay largely flat in FY27 with 20-21% YoY growth; cost-to-assets ~5.75%-6% in FY27, moving to 5.25%-5.5% from FY28. Branch additions run-rate ~50-60 per year.
Incremental cost of borrowing guided at ~8.5%; spreads expected flat for next few quarters absent policy action. Repo rate increases are a downside risk.
FY28 credit cost expected at ~1.6%-1.7%. Debt-to-equity of 2x expected in 6-8 quarters; ROA steady state 6%-6.5% and ROE 18%-20% at ~3x leverage.
Management plans to launch one more product (beyond micro LAP and housing) within ~3-6 months, with details to be shared later.
capex_capacity: Branch network at ~856 after adding ~12 in Q1, mainly in Maharashtra and newer states; FY27 additions expected at ~50-60 branches.
Collections and business functions separated into different verticals; management says this lifted productivity without any change in credit filters.
Liquidity: ~INR 1,850 crore held on balance sheet at quarter end; ~INR 1,000 crore raised in Q4 and ~INR 450 crore raised in Q1.
Pending ADB tranche (ECB) to be raised, with hedging cost impact; timing to be managed.
demand_pricing: Management says demand was never the constraint; the slowdown over the past 3-4 quarters came from tighter approvals and deliberate disbursement pacing.
June disbursements were ~INR 670 crore; management expects a new normal of ~INR 600-650 crore per month on average, with intra-quarter seasonality being reduced.
Repeat-customer policy relaxed: top-up offered to best customers instead of requiring full prepayment, which management expects to reduce the repayment rate from ~30% toward 27-28%.
Microfinance overlap with Five-Star customers fell from ~20-21% to ~16-17% (per management, not measured for Q1).
Competition: management cited new competitors entering, requiring more competitive employee compensation.

qa_highlights.question: Renish (ICICI): Where will cost-to-assets settle and when does operating leverage kick in?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex to stay largely flat in FY27 with 20-21% YoY growth due to competitive employee pay; cost-to-assets ~5.75%-6% this year, moving to 5.25%-5.5% in steady state from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Renish: Has yield repricing largely finished, and what is the current lending rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Large part of contraction done; onboarding yields average ~22.5% (range 21.5%-23%); a further 10-15 bps compression expected over next couple of quarters, settling near 22.25% after NPA interest reversals.

qa_highlights.question: Viral Shah (IIFL): Further Stage 3 flow-through expected, any ARC sales, and rollback rates in early buckets?
qa_highlights.answer: No ARC sales. Slippages expected to trend down; recoveries ~INR 35 crore vs INR 26-27 crore in Q4. Rollbacks ~4-5% in 1-60 DPD buckets and ~2-3% in 61-90 DPD; management frames it as stabilisation, with unique customer collection efficiency key.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit Tibrewal (Motilal Oswal): How many more quarters until slippages decline and what is a normalised slippage rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Expects slippages, credit cost and NPLs to trend down in September, December and March quarters; credit cost trending toward 1.7%. Will wait 1-2 quarters of slippage trend before giving a steady-state slippage number.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit: What drives the disbursement acceleration (demand, approvals, productivity, geography)?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand was never the constraint; earlier slowdown reflected tighter approvals and deliberate pacing. Vertical split of business and collections lifted productivity with no change in credit filters; login and sanction traction strong.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit: What is the outlook for cost of borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental cost of borrowing ~8.5%, leaving room for 20-30 bps further compression on the book; pending ADB ECB tranche carries hedging cost; assumes no repo hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Chandrasekhar Sridhar (Fidelity): Is gold loan growth masking underlying stress via repayments by overlapping customers? Also ticket size and diversification?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says gold loans are fully secured and repayments via gold loans are seasonal; microfinance overlap down from ~20-21% to ~16-17% (not measured for Q1). Ticket size mix target 25/50/25 across ~INR 3 lakh, 5 lakh, 10 lakh; one more product within 3-6 months. Spreads to stay flat for next few quarters absent policy action.

qa_highlights.question: Raghav Garg (Ambit): Why have repayment rates risen, and how does that reconcile with a rising 3-5 year duration share?
qa_highlights.answer: Repayments rose on stronger collections and a policy change: top-up offered to best customers instead of full prepayment. Repayment rate currently ~30%, expected to trend to 27-28%; behavioural tenor ~4-4.5 years. Management said 85-90% of loans are disbursed on 7-year tenure; the vintage shift reflects seasoning and higher disbursements.

qa_highlights.question: Rajiv Mehta (Yes Securities): Trajectory of write-offs, coverage build-back, and FY28 credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 write-offs guided INR 225-250 crore, roughly flat at ~INR 55-60 crore per quarter; steady-state write-off view in 2-3 quarters. Overall ECL coverage ~1.75-1.8%, whichever mix of Stage 1/2/3. FY28 credit cost ~1.6-1.7%. Growth achieved with no change in credit filters.

qa_highlights.question: Kunal Shah (Citi): Steady-state bucket mix and employee cost drivers, attrition?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady state: Stage 1 ~91-92%, Stage 2 ~6-7%, Stage 3 ~2.5%; current book to reach ~85% by end FY27 from 83.3%; 30+ below 12%. Employee cost rise is salary realignment and incentives for branch staff, not ESOPs. Attrition flat so far; trends in 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Nischint (Kotak): Expense growth this year and whether 20% loan growth guidance stands?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex growth ~20-21% YoY, similar to Q1; increments and appraisals already in Q1 base. ECL coverage ~1.75-1.8%; write-offs INR 55-60 crore per quarter; 20% AUM growth guidance reconfirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Divyansh Gupta (Latent PMS): Why did debt decline from March, cost of funds for levering up, and timing of D/E of 2x?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 borrowing was muted as banks awaited results; INR 1,000 crore raised in Q4 and INR 450 crore in Q1; INR 1,850 crore liquidity held. Guide 8.5% incremental cost. D/E of 2x in 6-8 quarters, as net worth adds ~INR 1,100-1,200 crore PAT annually.

qa_highlights.question: Chirag Fialoke (MS Capital): Are incremental disbursements averaging INR 5-7 lakh, and what is the 60-90 DPD bucket?
qa_highlights.answer: Average ticket ~INR 4.5-5 lakh, expected to hold around INR 5 lakh; mix guidance unchanged. Management deferred the 60-90 DPD figure to the IR team.

qa_highlights.question: Darshan Deora (Indvest): Steady-state ROE target, and will yields be raised back given higher collection costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Current ROA ~8-8.5% on AUM (7-7.25% on total assets); steady-state ROA 6-6.5% and ROE 18-20% at ~3x leverage. Management says the cost increase will be recovered through lower credit cost, not higher lending rates; the 200 bps cut in Oct 2024 tracked borrowing costs falling from 11%+.

qa_highlights.question: Renish: What was June disbursement and is INR 600-650 crore a monthly run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: June disbursements ~INR 670 crore; management is working to reduce intra-quarter seasonality and agreed an average of ~INR 600-650 crore per month is a fair assumption for the rest of the year.

risks_watch: Yield compression: onboarding yields ~22.5% with a further 10-15 bps decline expected over the next couple of quarters, and NPA interest reversals weigh on yields.

Cost of borrowing: guidance of ~8.5% incremental assumes no repo hikes; a rate increase or ADB ECB hedging costs would hit spreads. Management flagged energy costs and possible regulatory liquidity moves.

Asset quality: slippages flat QoQ at 0.70%; credit cost guidance 1.7-1.9% and gross NPA sub-3% depend on slippages turning down in September, December and March quarters. Write-off run-rate ~INR 60 crore per quarter gives little relief in FY27.
Opex and employee cost: opex growth 20-21% YoY and cost-to-assets ~5.75-6% in FY27; attrition is flat and too early to call, with more competitors entering.
Disbursement sustainability: H1 run-rate of ~INR 600-650 crore per month and reliance on a new product within 3-6 months; leverage target of 2x D/E is 6-8 quarters away.
key_quotes: We clocked our historical best in disbursement with quarterly disbursements coming in at INR 1,496 crores, a growth of 23% over the previous quarter and 16% over the previous year.
So our request is, can you please keep yourself mute so that the background noise is too much.
So it's not like we are completely removing the DNA of collections from the business people.
Srikanth Gopalakrishnan: Interest reversals on NPAs, Renish.
543663|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on disbursements, collections and asset-quality direction, but cautious on the near-term outlook: management hedged on borrowing costs, energy and rate risks, and deferred several data questions (rollback, 60-90 DPD, collection efficiency) to the IR team.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Asset quality stabilisation
rows.why: Management expects slippages, credit cost and NPLs to trend down in these quarters; current book at 83.30% (vs 82.69% in Q4) to reach ~85% by end FY27, and 30+ DPD at 12.38% (vs 12.69%).

rows.label: No yield re-pricing up

543663|2026-09.headline: Five-Star Q2 FY27: record disbursements of Rs 2,078 crore (+74% YoY) and PAT of Rs 299 crore, but management flags spread compression ahead.
543663|2026-09.overview: Disbursements hit a historical high of Rs 2,078 crore, up 39% QoQ and 74% YoY, while AUM reached Rs 14,640 crore (+14% YoY). Collection efficiency improved to 98.2% and 30+ DPD fell to 11.5% from 12.38%, though GNPA was sticky at 3.48%. PAT was Rs 299 crore, including a Rs 19 crore one-time tax benefit (about Rs 281 crore underlying). Management guided to tighter spreads as cost of funds rises, partly offset by a roughly 1% yield hike on incremental loans effective October 2026.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 299 crore (Rs 281 crore excluding Rs 19 crore one-time tax benefit)
about 7.5% in Q2; about 7.35-7.40% for the year

segments.name: Core geographies (Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana)
segments.commentary: Together more than 80% of AUM; management reports no drought-like stress and collections holding up. Tamil Nadu collects best, followed by Andhra and Telangana.

segments.name: Karnataka
segments.commentary: Management says collections are improving month-on-month after the state ordinance impact, and disbursements are being pushed more firmly there.

segments.name: Ticket-size mix (disbursements)
segments.commentary: Sub Rs 3 lakh about 26-27%, Rs 3-5 lakh about 51-52%, above Rs 5 lakh the balance. Target steady state is about 25/50/25.

guidance_outlook: Expect flattish credit slippages and credit cost for the rest of FY27; slippage around 70 bps for the next couple of quarters.
Incremental yields up about 1% from October 2026, but absorbing it across the book will take roughly 24-36 months (about 8 quarters per management on one question).
Incremental cost of borrowings expected 8.70-8.75% in H2 FY27; book cost of funds to exit FY27 about 12-15 bps higher, near 8.90%.
Spread compression expected: about 10-12 bps for H1 and about 10-15 bps by FY27 exit; margin expansion ruled out.
Growth guidance to be comfortably exceeded; any revised guidance likely after Q3. Opex to AUM to fall 50-75 bps over the next couple of years, to 6.75-7%.
October disbursements about Rs 550 crore (muted), with November and December expected to pick up.
capex_capacity: Added 19 branches in Q2 and 75 over the last year, focused on deepening presence in core geographies.
Active loans about 5.1 lakh, up 5% YoY.
Liquidity about Rs 1,300 crore at September 30; unavailed sanctions about Rs 1,100 crore.
Raised incremental debt of Rs 825 crore at an all-in cost of 8.43%; bank borrowings about 69% of total (67% in Q1).
Second tranche of ADB facility still pending, with hedging cost on the higher side.
demand_pricing: Customer rates raised about 1% on incremental disbursements across risk categories, from about 21-23% to about 22.5-23.9%, effective October 2026.
Top-up loans are about 10-15% of disbursements (Rs 200-300 crore per quarter); incremental top-up disbursal about 50% of the outstanding.
Management says yield hikes will not raise defaults, citing that loans above Rs 5 lakh earlier carried the same yield as sub-Rs 3 lakh loans.
Insurance commission impact from the IRDAI circular is nil, as Five-Star passes insurance premiums through without earning commission.
Gold loan overlap: 40-50% of customers have some gold loan; meaningful overlap about 30-40%.

qa_highlights.question: How will asset quality move given the rainfall deficit, and any stress signs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no drought stress in core states; collections in October are in line with July and September, with October D1C1 expected near 98%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the repayment rate rising, and what is the behavioural tenure?
qa_highlights.answer: Repayment rises due to adjusting outstanding on internal top-ups (about 1-2% extra repayments); behavioural tenure to move closer to 4 years, from the 36-37% repayment rate.

qa_highlights.question: How much have customer rates been raised, and when does yield bottom?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1% on incremental disbursements; management agreed that yields have bottomed this quarter, but margin expansion is not expected.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the write-off recovery trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Recoveries take about 18-24 months given no SARFAESI access on loans below Rs 20 lakh; H1 recoveries were about Rs 20 crore and NPA resolutions Rs 35 crore in Q2 (Rs 25 crore in Q1).

qa_highlights.question: How will cost of funds and spread move?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental cost of borrowing to rise 20-25 bps vs Q2, with book cost up 12-15 bps by FY27 exit; H1 spread hit about 10-12 bps, roughly 8 bps post-tax.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Legal expenses from the scaled-up legal recovery vertical and CSR spend based on the 3-year average profit.

risks_watch: Rate cycle: a further 25-50 bp repo hike would add to cost of funds beyond the 10-15 bps built in; December policy is a key watch point.
Stage-3 at 3.48%, with Stage-3 rising about 7-8% in absolute terms; management expects a trend-down only in a couple of quarters.
61-90 DPD bucket slippages flat, leaving a sticky stock in the bucket that drives the 70 bps slippage run-rate.
Written-off pool recovery slow (about Rs 300 crore written off in the last 8 quarters vs Rs 150 crore earlier); management has agreed to consider more disclosure.
MFI exposure about 35-40% of customers and no fresh scrub done; a sector relapse would test the collections set-up.
Revised guidance to come only after Q3; new product line still undisclosed, with details promised next quarter.

We expect flattish credit slippages and credit cost for the rest of the year, despite the industry headwinds.

rows.why: Opex to AUM guided to fall 50-75 bps to 6.75-7% from about 7.35-7.40% for FY27, though Q2 ran at about 7.5%.

543664|2026-03.headline: Kaynes FY26 revenue rose 33.2% to INR3,626 crore, but missed the INR4,500 crore then INR4,000 crore guidance, with operating cash flow of about INR600 crore negative.
543664|2026-03.overview: Management attributed the revenue shortfall to West Asia-related customer deferments, supply chain delays and one large EV two-wheeler customer cutting volumes by about 90%. Consolidated FY26 EBITDA was INR5,741 million (15.8% margin) and PAT INR3,639 million (10% margin), with Q4 revenue of INR12,426 million (+26% YoY) and PAT of INR912 million. Cash flow weakened sharply, driven by the smart metering subsidiary (Iskraemeco) with receivables of about INR1,365 crore, while the standalone EMS business turned cash positive. Management declined to give a specific FY27 revenue number and instead guided to outgrowing the market at roughly twice the market growth rate.

financial_highlights.change: PBT hit by about INR32 crore of quarterly intangible amortisation
from 83 days FY24; management also cited 64 to 54 days

segments.name: EMS (standalone/KEMPL)
segments.commentary: FY26 EMS revenue about INR2,655 crore (Q1 INR442 crore, Q2 INR683 crore, Q3 INR667 crore, Q4 INR862 crore), growing about 26-30%. Standalone EMS operating cash flow INR250 crore positive versus INR65 crore last year; EMS receivables INR399 crore at year end versus INR379 crore at start.

segments.name: Smart metering (Iskraemeco subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR971 crore (roughly 24-25% of group revenue), with receivables about INR1,365 crore, of which about INR250 crore non-current. Installation delays in rural areas and state-government/DISCOM payment cycles are holding up collections; securitisation has discounted only about INR40 crore so far.

segments.name: OSAT
segments.commentary: Unit 1 fully operational; Unit 2 to commercialise by Q2 FY27. Management cites revenue visibility above INR25,000 million over five years. Sanand facility inaugurated by the Prime Minister; FY27 production estimate INR250-300 crore, export-oriented.

segments.name: PCB
segments.commentary: Management sees a confirmed demand pipeline for five years with customers seeking more capacity. FY27 production estimate INR300-400 crore; first year of operation.

segments.name: Rail (Kavach)
segments.commentary: Kavach has initial approval and trial orders; approvals expected in H1 FY27, with bulk orders in H2. Management expects rail revenue to grow about 20-25% with margins above 30%.

segments.name: EV / automotive
segments.commentary: EV segment grew about 28% in FY26 despite the large two-wheeler customer falling about 90%. Company is moving from PCB supply into assemblies and products.

qa_highlights.question: Nitin Arora: Why no guidance, and what will move the INR600 crore negative OCF to breakeven?

543669|2026-03.headline: Keystone Realtors FY26 presales rose 33% to INR4,022 crore, with FY27 presales guided at INR5,000 crore and a INR10,000 crore presales target by FY30.

Revenue from operations was INR1,596 crore in Q4 and INR2,635 crore for FY26, with OCF of about INR715 crore. The company transitioned from completion method to percentage-of-completion accounting from 1 April 2025, and management says legacy low-margin projects are largely behind it. Gross debt was INR755 crore at March 2026 (gross D/E 0.26:1), and CRISIL assigned AA- with stable outlook.

segments.name: Residential sales and launches

segments.name: Business development
segments.commentary: Five projects added in FY26 with GDV of INR10,400 crore (1.74x INR6,000 crore guidance). Since FY23, 25 projects worth over INR27,800 crore added, 21 of them redevelopment; each underwritten at about 35% gross margin with equity capped near 10% of GDV.

segments.name: Legacy projects (Crown, Virar affordable)
segments.commentary: Legacy projects were 62% of FY26 revenue and are guided to 12% in FY27. Crown has about INR180 crore inventory and about INR450 crore sold receivables, with exit expected by December 2026.

segments.name: Commercial annuity
segments.commentary: Target of about INR100 crore recurring rental income by 2030. Current assets are 33Fifteen (strata sales underway), a 2 million sq ft Thane project (phases of 4.5 lakh sq ft, expected next FY), and Dhuruwadi in Prabhadevi.

543669|2026-06.headline: Keystone Realtors Q1 FY27 revenue rose 72% YoY to INR 470 crores, with EBITDA margin at 21.3% and PAT of INR 52.4 crores, its highest-ever Q1 PAT.

Revenue, EBITDA and PAT all grew sharply, helped by the shift to percentage-of-completion recognition and a richer product mix. Two projects were added (Igatpuri plotted development of about 62 acres and a Dindoshi cluster addition, together about INR 547 crores GDV), and the company reiterated its launch pipeline of about INR 8,000 crores-plus GDV for the year. Operating cash flow was INR 68 crores, which management said will pick up from Q2 and more visibly in Q3 and Q4, while the INR 1,000 crore OCF guidance was reaffirmed.

Sold share so far is only about 8%.

rows.why: Gross debt INR 876 crores vs free cash INR 803 crores (net D/E 0.02:1), gross D/E at 0.3:1 vs 0.75:1 ceiling, and management says it does not intend to stay net cash.

rows.label: Unrecognised sold revenue conversion
rows.why: About INR 6,300 crores of sold but unrecognised revenue (INR 63 billion) recognised over 2-2.5 years on average; legacy ~95% recognised in FY27 and POC ~98% of revenue from FY28.

rows.label: OCF pickup from Q2 into Q3-Q4
rows.why: Q1 OCF INR 68 crores vs INR 1,000 crore FY27 guide; management reaffirmed the guide and said pickup visible from Q2, more in Q3 and Q4.

tone.note: Management was confident on collections, margins, ratings, the INR 1,000 crore OCF guide and the INR 8,000 crore-plus launch pipeline, but cautious on OCF timing and MHADA launch dates and reticent on luxury demand; analysts pushed on net debt trajectory and OCF ramp.

543686|2026-03.headline: Sirca Q4 FY26 revenue rose 33.07% YoY to INR134.29 crore and FY26 EBITDA margin reached 20.08%, with management guiding 25-30% growth and 19-21% EBITDA margin for FY27.
543686|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 33.07% YoY to INR134.29 crore, EBITDA rose 35.69% to INR25.74 crore (margin 19.17% vs 18.8%), and PAT rose 25.07% to INR17.71 crore. For FY26, revenue was INR492.48 crore (+31.79%), EBITDA INR98.88 crore (+46.62%) and PAT INR65.05 crore (+32.48%). Management flagged short-term raw material margin pressure from crude-linked inputs, offset by two price increases totalling about 10% on Sirca range, and a March NC raw material shortage that cost Wembley about INR4-5 crore of revenue. The company has shifted from pure trading to manufacturing, with about 95% of previously imported products now targeted for Indian production.

segments.name: Core Sirca wood coatings
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue of about INR372 crore, of which about INR124 crore came from Italy-imported products and about INR252 crore from products made in India. Sirca gross margins are higher than Wembley/Welcome by about 10-15 percentage points.

segments.name: Wembley and Welcome (acquired brands, mass segment)
segments.commentary: Combined FY26 revenue of about INR120.5 crore: Welcome about INR46.5 crore and Wembley about INR74 crore. Wembley was roughly flat YoY after INR4-5 crore of orders were lost in March to an NC raw material shortage, and about INR5-6 crore was billed to distributors before the acquisition closed.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY25 exports were about INR9 crore, mainly Nepal plus one or two Sri Lanka customers. Wembley Valentino polyurethane exports are expected to start in Q1 FY27, with management targeting exports of about 3-4% of revenue.

segments.name: Acrylic coatings (Sirca brand)
segments.commentary: Acrylic sales contributed about INR120 crore in FY26 per management. Made-in-India production is expected to roll out in Q1 FY27 after the December 2025 know-how transfer from Sirca Italy.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-30% CAGR, described as a minimum.
EBITDA margin guided to stay in the 19-21% range, with raw material pressure expected to be temporary after two price increases.
Management said the INR1,000 crore revenue vision is achievable in about three years (FY29) and that Sirca and Wembley capacities are broadly sufficient for that journey.
FY27 capex limited to about INR5-6 crore, mainly for acrylic production expansion.
Expects inventory to fall by about INR15-20 crore and debtors to decline in the coming quarters as import stock is consumed by June end.
Expects NC supply constraints from supplier Nitrex to ease from June with a new Nitrex unit starting operations.
Expects exports to Middle East including Dubai to begin in FY27, and export contribution of about 3-4% of revenue.
capex_capacity: Sirca core facility capacity raised by 1,750 tons per annum to about 17,750 tons; about 12,000 tons utilised in FY26, with full utilisation expected by year-end in single shift at Unit 1.

Wembley capacity consolidated from four old distributor units into one new integrated facility with about 3x earlier capacity; management expects a turnover of INR250-300 crore from this setup using nitrocellulose and polyurethane products.
Wembley manufacturing facility is fully operational, consolidating multiple production lines.
Formula transfers for acrylic and polyester systems are complete; commercial trials underway with production expected in Q1 FY27. UV technology transfer is on track for Q1.
FY27 capex of about INR5-6 crore planned for acrylic production; most FY26 capex went to consolidating Wembley and Welcome sites.
demand_pricing: Two price increases of about 5% each (April and May 2026) on the Sirca range, totalling about 10%; Wembley and Welcome prices raised by about INR35 per litre. Management said this is enough to offset RM inflation so far.
Polyurethane is replacing melamine; melamine is about INR230-240 per litre vs PU about INR450-460 per litre, with PU about 10% higher per square foot on coverage.

Premium segment competition from large players is seen as limited because specification is driven by architects and designers; mass segment competition is more intense and is addressed through retailer margins and exclusivity.
About 80% of revenue comes from North India (Delhi NCR, Punjab, Haryana, UP, UK, Rajasthan, MP) and about 20% from West and South; 5 of 20 depots opened last year in South and West.
Management said the Indian furniture industry is shifting to local manufacturing after BIS implementation, which supports OEM and institutional demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between Sirca Italy-imported, Sirca India-made, Wembley and Welcome?
qa_highlights.answer: Core Sirca about INR372 crore (about INR124 crore imported from Italy, about INR252 crore made in India); Welcome about INR46.5 crore and Wembley about INR74 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook given crude-linked raw material volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Short-term pressure for about 10-15 days before price increases took effect; gross margins expected to be maintained after two price hikes; in-house production of previously imported products to add margin benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 revenue growth and margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth of 25-30% CAGR, EBITDA margin in the 19-21% range; INR1,000 crore revenue target achievable in about three years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Wembley growth story and why was it flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Flat YoY due to about INR5-6 crore pre-acquisition billing and a March NC shortage costing about INR4-5 crore; management expects real growth from FY27 as the transition period completes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material mix and price exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Resins and solvents make up about 95% of RM (solvents such as toluene, butyl acetate, PMA), with additives about 5% from BYK, Dow and Bayer; solvents and resins are sourced largely from dealers and reputed suppliers, with some resins made in-house.

qa_highlights.question: Why is working capital about twice that of Asian Paints?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition-related inventory build for the transition, slower Wembley/Welcome receivables tied to old owner payments, and about six months of imported acrylic inventory; about INR15-20 crore inventory reduction expected and receivables to ease.

qa_highlights.question: What is the parent company royalty and brand agreement term?
qa_highlights.answer: Parent receives 0.75% of total reported revenue, including Wembley; brand agreement with Sirca Italy runs till 2041.

risks_watch: Crude-linked raw material volatility from the Middle East conflict could keep gross margins under pressure until price hikes fully pass through.
NC cotton supply constraints from supplier Nitrex (diversion to defence) affect Wembley's nitrocellulose range until the new Nitrex unit is commissioned, expected from June.
Export logistics and vessel availability for flammable material are difficult; the 3-4% export contribution target depends on normalisation.
Working capital intensity is high; the company expects inventory and debtor reduction but has not quantified receivable days.
Wembley and Welcome gross margins are about 10-15 percentage points below Sirca; management expects EBITDA to be broadly unchanged, so mix shift is a margin watch point.
Competitive pressure in the mass segment from large paint companies.
543686|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the 25-30% growth and 19-21% margin guidance, but cautious on near-term margins and Wembley, which management attributed to raw material and transition issues. Answers on Wembley's flat growth and margin mix were direct, while export timelines were framed as conditional on the geopolitical situation.

we are looking at a growth of almost 25-30% based on, you know, CAGR growth.
the margins should the EBITDA margins should remain in the category of, say, 19-21%.
we expect a minimum, considering the market situation and being, you know, being a little on the restricted side, we still see that 25% to 30% CAGR growth is what we expect as minimum.

rows.why: Management guided FY27 capex to only about INR5-6 crore mainly for acrylic expansion, and utilisation is about 68% (12,000 of 17,750 t), well below the 80%+ level that would trigger a new capex announcement.

rows.why: Management calls 25-30% growth a minimum, and the INR1,000 crore vision is targeted for about FY29 (from FY26 revenue of INR492.48 crore), so upside depends on Wembley recovery and exports.

rows.why: Crude-linked RM pressure lasted about 10-15 days before two ~5% price hikes (about 10% total), and Wembley was flat YoY after INR4-5 crore of orders lost to the March NC shortage, with Nitrex supply easing only from June.

rows.label: Inventory and debtor reduction
rows.why: Management expects inventory to fall by INR15-20 crore as import stock is consumed by June end, and debtors to decline, though receivable days are not quantified.

rows.label: Middle East and Dubai exports from Wembley PU
rows.why: Exports expected to begin in FY27 at 3-4% of revenue (vs about INR9 crore FY25 exports, mainly Nepal), but management framed timing as conditional on logistics and geopolitics for flammable material.

rows.label: Wembley recovery on Nitrex NC supply
rows.why: Nitrex new unit expected to start in June, easing NC constraint that cost Wembley INR4-5 crore of orders in March, with management expecting real Wembley growth from FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on 25-30% growth and 19-21% margin guidance and the INR1,000 crore vision, but cautious on near-term RM margins, Wembley's flat growth, and conditional export timelines; analysts pressed on the revenue split, working capital (about twice Asian Paints), and Wembley's flat gro

543687|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 20% to Rs 1,138 crore and EBITDA 34% to Rs 101 crore, while branded formulation grew only 3%.
543687|2026-03.overview: Dharmaj Crop Guard reported FY26 revenue of Rs 1,138 crore (+20% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 101 crore (+34%) and net profit of Rs 55 crore (+57%). Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs 234 crore (+11% YoY) against a stronger base. Growth was driven by domestic institutional formulation (+15%), exports recovery and a 37% rise in domestic active ingredient sales, while branded formulation was muted at 3% due to uneven monsoon and channel destocking. The technical plant reached PBT break-even in FY26, and management guided FY27 revenue growth of 18-20%.

segments.name: Branded formulation (B2C)
segments.commentary: FY26 growth of 3%, with Q1 the strongest quarter and Q2 and Rabi weak due to erratic monsoon and channel inventory. Management guides 20-25% growth if monsoon is normal; new states contributed 14% of sales vs 7% last year.

segments.name: Domestic institutional formulation
segments.commentary: FY26 growth of 15%, described as consistent across the year.

segments.name: Domestic active ingredient (technical)
segments.commentary: Domestic sales up 37% in FY26; capacity utilisation 65-70%; EBITDA about 5% (vs negative in FY25); GP margin 22% vs 19%; PBT break-even reached.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Strong comeback in FY26 after weak FY25; GP margin 15-20%, EBITDA margin 10-12%; registrations in 2-3 new countries; Iran and Iraq shipments disrupted.

guidance_outlook: FY27 overall top-line growth guided at 18-20%, with each vertical targeted at similar growth.
Company EBITDA margin (9% currently) to improve by 0.5-0.75 percentage points in FY27.
Technical plant EBITDA to reach 8-10% at optimal utilisation, but over 2-3 years; utilisation expected near 75% in FY27.
Herbicide facility in Kerala GIDC, Ahmedabad expected to be commissioned in Q3 FY27.
FY27 capex about Rs 50 crore; employee cost growth 5-8%, fixed costs broadly flat.
Management expects the branded formulation seasonal headwind to normalise in FY27.
capex_capacity: Technical plant utilisation 65-70% in FY26 (58% in the first year of operation), targeted near 75% in FY27.
New dedicated herbicide facility at Kerala GIDC, Ahmedabad: machinery being ordered, installation 4-5 months, commissioning Q3 FY27.
Existing herbicide unit to be converted to insecticide and fungicide production, freeing space at the formulation site.
FY27 capex about Rs 50 crore; management said it would be spent in the current year and would support growth for about three years.
demand_pricing: Branded formulation hit by erratic late-Q2 monsoon in August-September and weak Rabi pest pressure; channel inventory was liquidated.
Technical realisations were under pressure through most of FY26 and recovered only after February 2026, driven by input cost increases linked to the West Asia crisis.
Company says price increases pass on raw-material cost inflation with a 1-2% non-recoverable portion; prices revised frequently.
Management said paraquat ban in Andhra Pradesh would have no material volume impact (not even 1%).
Early-season (April-May) sales were on plan, with June sales dependent on the monsoon onset.

qa_highlights.question: What is the branded formulation B2B/B2C split outlook and marketing spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2C marketing is about 3% of B2C business; B2B share has risen; tolling outside the company will be brought in-house as herbicide capacity comes on line.

qa_highlights.question: Technical plant margins and utilisation path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said technical EBITDA is about 5% at 65-70% utilisation, improving about 75 bps a year, reaching up to 10% in four to five years. Analyst notes differ on the 8-10% optimum level, which management says takes two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: How does the herbicide shift affect margins and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the herbicide move is a relocation to a separate site with capacity improvement, and the Rs 50 crore capex covers units 2 and 3 this year; margin improvement is expected to reach double digits in two years.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of El Nino and monsoon on H1 FY27 demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no impact so far in Q1 and that even distribution of rain is key; a 2-4% rainfall shortfall would not hurt the season, but an extended dry spell could.

qa_highlights.question: Export growth drivers and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exports have GP of 15-20% and EBITDA of 10-12%, with new country registrations continuing and a new team created; Gulf shipments are affected but not stopped.

qa_highlights.question: Why did branded formulation grow only 3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to continuous rain in Gujarat, Rajasthan and MP in August-September, where the company is strongest; other states grew.

risks_watch: Monsoon timing and distribution for Kharif 2026; June sales depend on early onset.
Raw material and input cost volatility from the West Asia crisis; inventory build raised working capital and cash conversion cycle to 87 days.
Margin dilution as lower-margin B2B and technical volumes grow faster than branded formulation.
Branded formulation recovery to 20-25% growth needs to show up in Q1 and Q2 FY27 numbers.
Herbicide facility commissioning in Q3 FY27 and ramp-up before the next Kharif season.
Export disruption in Gulf, Iran and Iraq; regulatory actions such as state-level pesticide bans.

rows.why: Guidance of 18-20% FY27 growth is new and management is cautious on the near term citing input-cost pressure and monsoon dependence; branded growth of 3% in FY26 leaves little cushion.

rows.why: Existing herbicide unit is to be converted to insecticide and fungicide production and the new Kerala herbicide facility is due Q3 FY27; new state registrations in 2-3 export countries are ongoing.

rows.why: Cash conversion cycle rose to 87 days from 67 days and inventory to Rs 2,074 million from Rs 1,385 million, with no explicit reduction target given.

rows.why: A 2-4% rainfall shortfall is seen as harmless but an extended dry spell could hurt; Andhra Pradesh paraquat ban is said to have under 1% volume impact.

tone.note: Management was confident on the medium-term and FY27 18-20% growth and herbicide commissioning, but cautious on near-term monsoon and input costs; analysts pressed on the technical plant's 8-10% margin timing and the GP vs EBITDA margin split, which management restated during Q&A.

543689|2026-03.headline: Uniparts Q4 FY26 revenue rose 34% YoY to INR339 crores with EBITDA margin of 24%; management guides FY27 growth in line with FY26's 21%.
543689|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR339 crores, up 34% YoY and 21% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR81 crores (about 24% margin) and PAT of INR51 crores. FY26 revenue grew 21%, above the mid-teens guidance given earlier. Management said the agriculture and construction cycle is turning, with new business wins of over INR225 crores annualised in the trailing 12 months. A fire at the Ludhiana finishing shop in Q3 was handled via interim arrangements and is covered by insurance, with normal operations expected by year-end. Management said the company remains net debt free with INR160 crores net cash.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA grew north of 55% in FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR170 crores, including special dividend of INR101 crores in Q3

segments.name: 3PL (agriculture and construction, warehousing/nearshoring channel)
segments.commentary: Warehousing channel delivered about 51% of FY26 sales; management said the 3PL and PMP revenue mix is now roughly 50-50, versus 50%+ 3PL and about 45% PMP two years ago. Mexico ramp-up has 3 customers in talks, 2 in ramp-up.

segments.name: PMP (precision machine parts: pins, bushings)
segments.commentary: PMP and large ag together account for about 70% of new business wins. Management said the company is a 100% or large-share supplier to top 3 global construction OEMs.

segments.name: Large agriculture
segments.commentary: Large ag is about 20% of FY26 revenue. New programme wins in Europe; North American large tractor volumes are tracking down mid-to-high teens YoY, with Q4 FY26 seen as the trough by OEMs.

segments.name: Small agriculture
segments.commentary: Industry expected to grow about 5% in FY27 in North America; Europe recovering with momentum building in H2. India tractor demand described as stable, dependent on monsoon.

segments.name: Construction
segments.commentary: Management described construction as more stable and visible; North America expected to grow in FY27 with H2 stronger, and Europe seen past cyclical low with modest growth.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Aftermarket described as a stable contributor in FY26 across North America and Europe; Q4 performance better than Q3, though not back to earlier share of revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected in line with FY26 (about 21%), driven by industry recovery, new business execution and gradual end-market recovery.
Q1 FY27 revenue expected to be in line sequentially with Q4 FY26; H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1.
EBITDA expected to remain comfortably above 20% over the cycle; exact level depends on volume ramp-up and delivery channel mix.
Capex expected to stay within 2.5% to 3.5% of revenue.
Fire-affected Ludhiana facility expected to be back online by end of FY27 (year-end); insurance covers fixed assets, inventory and loss of profit including incremental costs.
Trailing 12-month new business wins above INR225 crores annualised potential, up over 12.5% QoQ.
capex_capacity: Capex about INR12 crores in Q4 FY26; policy is 2.5% to 3.5% of revenue, mainly balancing capex once new business is won.
Capacity is set by bottleneck processes; some processes are fungible between 3PL and PMP, others are not.
Investments in last two years include in-sourcing at the US factory and Mexico warehousing/nearshoring build-out.
Ludhiana finishing shop fire in Q3 FY26; rebuild underway, insurance claim filed, online by year-end.
Management said it is not constrained to any peak revenue level given the capex approach.
demand_pricing: Management said Q4 FY26 growth was largely volume-led, with currency a small part; no price escalation cited.
Material cost in Q4 was about 35% of revenue, within the normal 34% to 37% range; freight and raw material are passed through to customers.
Management said FX pass-through is netted against inflation in customer contracts.
Inventory valuation gain from euro-INR depreciation was about 2% of material cost in Q2 and a similar amount in Q4 FY26, per management.
Order-win run-rate has held above INR200 crores for several quarters, per management; the company does not disclose a total order book.
West Asia escalation in March 2026 raised input prices; some inflation offset by favourable exchange rates.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 24% Q4 EBITDA margin sustainable, and is there any one-off (FX, mix, tariff refunds)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tariffs are P&L neutral. Q4 margin was driven by volume-led 18% QoQ growth giving operating leverage, and higher warehousing sales, the highest-margin channel. Management reiterated 'comfortably above 20%' as the steady-state, depending on volume and channel mix.

qa_highlights.question: Will the fire affect margins, and when will the plant be back?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance covers loss of profit including additional costs incurred due to the fire. Rebuild is underway with the plant expected to be online by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 3PL revenue share down because of tractor weakness, and has market share been lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company grew with construction customers as a derisking step; 3PL and PMP are now about 50-50, and no market share has been lost.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 85% working capital improvement sustainable (155 to 136 days)?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days fell from 146 in FY25 to 134 in FY26; receivable and payable days are now close to par. Management expects these levels to be sustainable, though absolute inventory is rising with OEM backlog orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the acquisition and how should capital allocation be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about a dozen targets were evaluated since IPO, with two near-deals that fell through. Any target must add a third platform, be manageable in size, and be ROE/ROCE accretive. The Q3 special dividend followed a deal that was not pursued.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total order book and how has win conversion changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR225 crores figure is a rolling annualised potential of trailing 12-month wins, held above INR200 crores for several quarters. Past slowdowns reflected OEM destocking and delayed or smaller execution of wins.

qa_highlights.question: Geographic split and large ag share?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 sales: about 53% North America, 25% Europe, 14% US, 5% Japan, 1.5% Asia, under 1% rest of world. Large ag is about 20% of revenue. Sales by delivery channel: warehousing 51%, direct exports 26%, India local 14%, US local 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Cost measures versus the last peak, and whether FY23 EBITDA (near INR300 crores) can be surpassed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the approach as cost-conscious rather than cost-cutting. Variable employee cost rose, while fixed-cost inflation is partly offset by currency and volume. Management said FY26 turnover of about INR1,200 crores is the highest since the prior peak, with better margins than then.

risks_watch: West Asia escalation and rising steel and freight costs; management says these are mostly passed through, but timing is uncertain.
Currency-driven inventory valuation gains (~2% of material cost in Q2 and Q4) may reverse if INR appreciates.
Ludhiana plant rebuild timing (year-end target) and whether insurance recovery covers the full loss of profit.
North American large tractor volumes down mid-to-high teens YoY; monsoon outcome for Indian tractor demand.
Employee cost increases (reported 20-25% in North India) and the new wage code impact of INR3.4 crores.
Whether Q1 FY27 sequential flatness holds and H2 FY27 acceleration materialises.
Mexico ramp-up with 2 of 3 customers in ramp-up; delivery channel mix will drive margin.

543689|2026-06.headline: Uniparts Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR347 crore and EBITDA 55% to INR90 crore, with management guiding FY27 growth a few points above FY26's 21%.
543689|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR347 crore (+27% YoY), with EBITDA of INR90 crore (+55% YoY, +10% QoQ) and PAT of INR57 crore (+64% YoY, +11% QoQ). Management said the quarter was in line with its quarterly guidance and above its annual guidance. Construction equipment is now 45% of revenue and drove growth, while large ag is at its cyclical trough and growth there comes from new wins. Aftermarket was flat YoY in absolute terms but fell to about 12% of revenue as OEM business grew faster. Net cash is about INR190 crore and the company is debt-free, with about half a dozen acquisition targets under review.

segments.name: Construction equipment
segments.commentary: Now 45% of total revenue and the main growth driver in Q1 FY27; momentum that began in 2H CY2025 has continued, supported by US and European infrastructure spend.

segments.name: Large agricultural equipment
segments.commentary: Conditions subdued; management expects about a 15-16% decline in CY2026 after about 30% in CY2025. Growth is from new wins, particularly in Europe, not market recovery.

segments.name: Small agricultural equipment
segments.commentary: India performing well on government subsidies and mid-to-high HP adoption, with strong new wins. Western small ag still soft but volumes have started recovering after three years of decline.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: About 12% of Q1 FY27 revenue (vs 15% in FY26 and 20% in FY25), flat YoY in absolute terms; tariff-driven price volatility deferred channel purchases.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth to be a couple of percentage points above FY26's 21% growth, per management; Q2 FY27 expected to be in line with Q1.
Management expects FY27 EBITDA margin comfortably above 20%; long-run cycle margin guidance remains about 20% (peak to trough).
Second half expected to be better than first half, linked to the ag recovery.
Mexico facility: first customer deliveries from the warehouse expected in Q3 FY27; FY27 Mexico revenue in mid-single-digit USD million.
Warehouse sales expected to stay in a 52-56% range over the next 12-18 months.
Material cost range of 34-37% of revenue is considered sustainable; fabrication vertical expected to become meaningful in 18-24 months.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex of INR12 crore; organic capex (fresh equipment plus repairs and maintenance) guided at 2.5-3.5% of revenue.
Fabrication facility for small and medium-sized fabrication set up about 2.5 years ago; now in deep discussions with OEMs to supply fabrications.
Restoration of the Ludhiana finishing shop is on schedule; customer supply uninterrupted.
Mexico operations on track; Phase 2 may add manufacturing in Mexico.
demand_pricing: Channel mix: warehouse sales about 56% of Q1 FY27 revenue (vs 50-52% in Q1 FY26); locally made and locally sold about 22% (vs about 25%); the balance is direct exports.
Margin hierarchy by channel: locally made and sold is lowest; direct exports are the base (about 20% margin); warehouse sales are highest.
Product margins stated as broadly similar across three-point linkage, precision machined parts and fabrication; material consumption differs by product mix.
New business order book over INR225 crore on a trailing 12-month basis; new wins split roughly equally between Europe and US, with the majority of wins in ag and construction.
Above-70 HP three-point linkage is a single-digit market share with a major European OEM win in FY26; below-70 HP is dominant share globally.

qa_highlights.question: Will the construction share of revenue structurally rise and can it be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said construction is 45% of revenue; drivers (new wins, industry recovery, wallet expansion) are multi-quarter. Mix will rebalance as ag recovers.

qa_highlights.question: Is construction higher margin than tractors?
qa_highlights.answer: Product margins are fairly similar; differences come from channel. Warehouse sales are highest margin, direct exports about 20% base, and locally made/sold lowest.

qa_highlights.question: What is the update on acquisitions and their revenue timing?
qa_highlights.answer: About a dozen targets evaluated since IPO in hydraulics, fabrication and PTO; about half a dozen currently under close review. Targets must be ROCE/ROE accretive within 18-30 months, manageable, and not deeply distressed.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the 33.3% material cost and the gross margin level?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly product mix (three-point linkage, precision machined parts, fabrication have different material consumption), plus channel mix; inventory gain only about INR1 crore. Material cost range 34-37% is typical.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the aftermarket?
qa_highlights.answer: Flat in absolute terms YoY; demand deferred by tariffs and inflation. Management expects normalisation over the next 12 months as tariffs have come down.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company plan to gain share in large ag?
qa_highlights.answer: Share is lower due to OEM validation and testing cycles; FY26 wins are now flowing into P&L, and deep discussions are ongoing on several opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2.5-3.5% capex guidance inclusive of acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: No. It covers organic capex (fresh equipment and R&M). Acquisitions would use the INR190 crore cash and could involve debt; the balance sheet is strong.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 and H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 expected to be in line with Q1 and robust; H2 expected to be better than H1, tied to the ag recovery.

Input cost and supply chain pressure from the West Asia situation.
Margin sensitivity to warehouse sales mix, currency movements and industry recovery pace.
Acquisition execution: no deal yet despite about a dozen targets evaluated since IPO; timing and value accretion uncertain.
Mexico warehouse ramp: first deliveries expected Q3 FY27.

33.3% of revenue (includes about INR1 crore inventory gain)

543709|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 30.41% YoY with 46% operating margin; FY26 revenue reached INR149.40 crores, and management reiterated a ~35% revenue CAGR.
543709|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue growth of 30.41% YoY, operating profit up nearly 54% at a 46% operating margin, and net profit of INR5.14 crores (up 25.88% YoY, 17.41% margin). FY26 revenue was INR149.40 crores, up about 48% reported and about 20% after adjusting for a one-time INR25.74 crore sale in FY25 from a change in operating method. The company ended FY26 with about INR78 crores of liquid balance, zero debt, and 126 points of sale after adding 32 stores in the year (18 in Q4). Management kept its ~35% revenue CAGR guidance and said at least 20 new stores are planned for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: ~48% YoY reported; ~20% excluding INR25.74 crore one-time FY25 sale

financial_highlights.value: 126 as on 31 Mar 2026 (38 EBOs, 34 PNGS SIS, 54 third-party SIS)
~250 kg raw silver; ~7 kg fine gold in studded inventory

segments.name: PNGS Gargi SIS (in PNGS Gargi Stores / P.N. Gadgil & Sons)
segments.commentary: 34 SIS points as of FY26; management said SIS SSSG is around 30-32% and that PNGS SIS is about 75-80% of revenue currently. Dependence targeted to fall to about 65% by FY28.

segments.name: EBOs (exclusive brand outlets, FOCO)
segments.commentary: 38 EBOs at FY26 end versus 0 in FY22; management expects EBO growth to drive most incremental revenue. Breakeven is 6-9 months in Maharashtra and 15-18 months outside Maharashtra.

segments.name: Shoppers Stop and other third-party SIS
segments.commentary: 54 third-party SIS points at FY26 end versus 0 in FY22; management said Shoppers Stop expansion is passive and follows its new store openings.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: 14KT studded diamond jewellery is about 35% of revenue (HI colour diamonds). Silver jewellery is 92.5% sterling silver with CZ stones and IGI-certified natural diamonds.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of approximately 35% over the next few years, maintained; management said FY27 revenue would be about INR190 crores and FY28 about INR260 crores.
At least 20 new stores in FY27; management said it is not capping the count and has cash to fund at least 25 more EBOs without debt or equity.
EBITDA margin expected to stay in the same range in FY27-FY28, with 100-150 bps upside if earlier stores mature faster.
PAT margin of about 20% expected to hold in the near term; management hopes for higher over time.
Marketing spend is about 4-5% of revenue; no change in the expense outlook was given.
capex_capacity: Per-store capex for a FOCO franchise is about INR30-50 lakh for fit-out and premises; total with silver and diamond inventory deposits is about INR80 lakh to INR1 crore. COCO economics are similar.

Breakeven for new stores outside Maharashtra is 15-18 months; within Maharashtra it is 6-9 months. Contribution from outside-Maharashtra stores starts within 8-12 months and inside Maharashtra within 4-6 months.
Maharashtra store count rose from 47 (Mar 2024) to 67 (Mar 2026); management sees room for 8-10 more EBOs in Pune alone.
Store roll-out is about 53% in Maharashtra and about 47% outside, per management. Focus is on north India, with South entry (Hyderabad started; Chennai and Bangalore being evaluated).
Local karigar manufacturing is replacing imports of ready silver jewellery after a government ban on imports; company buys raw silver for in-house making.
demand_pricing: Management said price changes are made only when silver moves by about INR30,000-40,000/kg, given MRP-based pricing and no per-gram pricing; it said a 30% rise in precious metal prices would not materially hit margins.
Management cited double-digit industry growth and low organised-sector penetration; it said millennials and Gen Z are driving demand for lightweight, personalised everyday jewellery.
Management said the South is an early-stage test and it will comment after 4-5 stand-alone South stores by next year-end.
Customer retention runs through discount schemes (monsoon, anniversary, Diwali, Valentine's, year-end), telecalling and WhatsApp CRM.

qa_highlights.question: How will the 35% growth split across PNGS SIS, EBOs and Shoppers Stop in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue would be about INR190 crores and FY28 about INR260 crores. Management expects the PNGS SIS share to fall to about 65% by FY28 from about 78%, with EBOs and other channels making up the rest.

qa_highlights.question: What are the EBO/SIS capex and FOCO economics?
qa_highlights.answer: FOCO franchise capex is about INR30-50 lakh for fit-out and rent, and about INR80 lakh to INR1 crore including inventory deposits. The PNGS SIS sells at markdown and is paid within 2-3 weeks; Shoppers Stop remits monthly.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold as more stores are added and the mix shifts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects PAT margin of about 20% to hold for now. New stores weigh on profit until about 300 locations, after which only about 8-9% of stores are new each year. EBITDA margin should stay in the same range, with 100-150 bps upside.

qa_highlights.question: Could growth exceed 35% and can the company fund growth without new equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth could exceed 35% if new EBOs reach maturity faster than the 15-18 month breakeven outside Maharashtra. Management said no equity is needed for organic growth; acquisitions could change that.

qa_highlights.question: How do gold and silver price spikes affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices are adjusted only when silver moves by INR30,000-40,000/kg, and a 30% precious metal rise would not significantly affect margins because of the cushion built in.

qa_highlights.question: Why were store additions accelerated to 32 in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it added more stores because good locations became available, and with its cash it can set up at least 25 FOCO stores without debt or equity.

risks_watch: Growth depends on new EBOs, especially outside Maharashtra, reaching breakeven in 15-18 months; slower maturity would pressure the 35% CAGR.
PNGS SIS dependence is still about 75-80% of revenue, and SIS expansion depends on the parent's own store openings.
Precious metal price volatility; the FOCO/MRP pricing model absorbs moves only above a threshold.
Rising other expenses and marketing (4-5% of revenue) and new-store drag on margins.
The FY26 growth (~48%) is flattered by a one-time INR25.74 crore FY25 sale; underlying growth is about 20%.

543711|2026-03.headline: Sula Q4 FY26 revenue rose 7% YoY to INR 142 crore, but gross margin pressure from grape mix kept EBITDA roughly flat in absolute terms.
543711|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue returned to growth at 7% YoY to INR 142 crore, driven by a 5% rise in Own Brands and 17% growth in Wine Tourism revenue. Gross profit fell 3% YoY as a shift to wine grapes and higher wine carryover cut gross margin by about 350-400 bps, and the absence of a prior-year INR 3.5 crore Karnataka inventory gain added about 150 bps of pressure. Management cut operating costs 3% YoY, holding EBITDA at similar absolute levels, and PAT fell 34% on a high prior-year tax credit. Full-year FY26 revenue fell 2% to INR 596 crore excluding a prior-year one-off, with Own Brands down 5%.

Operating cash flow stayed negative with inventory rising to about INR62 crore, and management pushed meaningful cash flow to FY28.

543928|2026-03.headline: Cosmic CRF H2 FY26 revenue rose 77% YoY to INR412 crore, but FY26 PAT margin slipped to ~7% and Amzen LOI is still pending CoC approval.

Full-year consolidated revenue rose about 78% to roughly INR722 crore, EBITDA about 77% and PAT about 74%, though management conceded PAT margin was about 7% versus a restated ~6% base. Installed capacity reached 133,600 MT with actual production of about 106,370 MT, and the order book stands at INR760 crore. The H1 bidder status for Amzen Transportation was described as reinstated after Supreme Court rulings, with the CoC approval and LOI still awaited.

segments.commentary: Installed capacity 55,000 MT per annum; four plants on 14 acres covering about 75% of wagon and coach body manufacturing. Capacity added via two new sheds (6,000 and 11,000 sq ft) and cutting and slitting lines, with capex of over INR30 crore in the year.

segments.name: NS Engineering Projects (NSEPL, 74% owned)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 65,000 MT, up from about 12,500 MT when acquired. Produced 56,380 MT in FY26; galvanizing bath running at about 24,000 MT per year, with a plan to scale to about 85,000 MT in the same space.

segments.name: Cosmic Springs and Engineers (CSEL, wholly owned)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 13,600 MT, produced about 7,300 MT per management. Springs output about 2,300 MT at near-zero margin pending RDSO licence; forging unit targeted for commercial production within about nine months.

segments.name: Amzen Transportation (pending acquisition)
segments.commentary: Wagon capacity 3,600 per annum, targeted to rise to 7,200 with capex; also bridge girders up to 20,000 MT per RDSO approval. Management estimates the total project cost at about INR400-odd crore and plans sea freight containers at about 7,500 to 10,000 units.

West Bengal government infrastructure expansion (metro, bridges, cofferdams, sheet piles, crash barriers) cited as a potential order source; no specific orders named.

qa_highlights.answer: Springs volume about 2,300 MT and total fabrication plus steel about 4,500 MT. Springs revenue INR67 crore but profit only about INR1.5 crore because RDSO licence is pending and sales go to traders, not railways. Forging has not started.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT margin dilute in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three reasons: weak springs profitability, about INR2-2.5 crore carrying cost of Amzen KMPs, and about INR10 crore legal and related costs on Amzen, which auditors did not allow to be capitalised. Total hit about INR8 crore to PAT.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Supreme Court set aside the NCLAT order, restoring the H1 bidder status it held when the NCLAT order came; the CoC must now scrap the new Form G and resolution plans and negotiate with the company.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth of no less than 100% is the promoter's aspiration but could not be assured because raw material prices and government spending are outside its control; it framed FY27 at 30% or more.

qa_highlights.answer: Stock levels, price variation clauses on railway contracts, traders for smaller purchases, and future hedging once volumes reach about 200,000 MT, plus liquid metal initiative for diversification.

543936|2026-03.headline: Senco Gold Q4 FY26 revenue up 45% YoY to INR1,997 crore, but management guides FY27 growth of only 18-20% and a 7.5-7.8% EBITDA margin.
543936|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR1,997 crore (up 45% YoY), EBITDA INR274 crore (up 116%) and PAT INR157 crore (up 151%), with reported EBITDA margin of 13.7%. FY26 sales reached INR8,430 crore (about 33% growth), with gains driven by gold price rises, new stores and old gold exchange. Management said the 13.7% Q4 and 11.5% full-year margins include a customs-duty inventory gain and gold price effects, and that sustainable EBITDA is 7.5-7.8%. Post the PM's appeal in late May, footfalls fell for 7-10 days and May was broadly flat YoY, and the call left the inventory build (188 days) and negative free cash flow as the main open questions.

543936|2026-06.headline: Senco Gold Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 67% YoY and EBITDA margin fell to 7.0% (INR213 crores) on gold-price, discounting and one-off cost effects.
543936|2026-06.overview: Senco crossed INR3,000 crores of sales in a single quarter, with consolidated revenue up about 67% YoY and retail up 50%, same-store sales growth around 39%. April was the strong month (about INR1,500-1,600 crores), while May and June moderated to roughly INR500-600 crores a month amid West Bengal elections, Adhik Maas and heat wave. Reported EBITDA was INR213 crores at 7.0% margin and consolidated PAT INR101 crores at 3.3%, with margin pressure from other expenses (about INR195 crores vs about INR80 crores a year earlier), a gold-price decline, discounting and GML-related finance cost. Management retained FY27 guidance of 20%+ value growth and a 7.5%-7.8% sustainable operational EBITDA margin, and said July and August are running about 25% YoY ahead.

543942|2026-03.headline: Utkarsh SFB posted a net loss of INR188 crores in Q4 FY26 on legacy MFI provisioning, while GNPA fell ~330 bps QoQ to 7.7%.
543942|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed early signs of recovery: JLG disbursements rose 58% QoQ, fresh NPA slippages (net) fell to ~INR170 crores from ~INR710 crores a year earlier, and collection efficiency improved. The bank still booked a Q4 net loss of INR188 crores, driven by provisioning on the legacy stressed book. Management is shifting the mix toward secured lending (51% of gross loans) and reducing JLG exposure (~28% of gross loans). FY27 is framed as a consolidation year, with a medium-term target of 25-30% loan growth, NIM above 8% and ROE around 15% by FY28.

segments.name: JLG / Micro-banking
segments.commentary: JLG book fell ~10% in the quarter and is ~28% of gross loans (~30% incl. BC JLG), down from ~88% in March 2020. JLG disbursements grew 58% QoQ and 2% YoY; collection efficiency (X-bucket) reached 99.7% in March 2026.

segments.name: MBBL (micro-banking business loan)
segments.commentary: MBBL portfolio grew 122% YoY and 40% QoQ to 27% of the micro-banking book; penetration is below 15%.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME book grew 15% YoY to INR4,456 crores, supported by Micro LAP at ~18% disbursement yield. Retail MSME GNPA was 3.4% as on March 2026.

segments.name: Housing and BBG
segments.commentary: Housing loans grew 8% YoY to INR990 crores; BBG (fully secured by immovable collateral) grew 19% YoY.

segments.name: CV/CE (Wheels)
segments.commentary: Book contracted 1% QoQ to INR1,090 crores. Used-vehicle share of disbursements rose to ~30% in FY26 from under 15% a year earlier; management called Wheels the main contributor to non-MFI slippages.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Management expects gold loans to grow bigger in FY27, but gave no figures.

guidance_outlook: FY27 is a consolidation year; priorities are sustaining collections, calibrated disbursements into higher-quality segments, deepening secured lending and mobilising liabilities.
Medium-term targets: loan book growth 25-30%, secured lending ~55% of the portfolio, NIM above 8%, ROE around 15%. Management said ROE of 15% would be reached in FY28 and exited above that level.
Credit cost guidance: ~3% for FY27 and 2-2.5% for FY28 (previously 2.5-3.5% for FY27 and 2-2.5% for FY28, as stated on the call). Management called this conservative.
Net NPA target below 1% by FY28, from ~3.3% in FY26.
Cost of funds expected to fall further as deposit repricing continues.
Reverse merger of holding company UCL into the bank: second motion petition filed with NCLT on April 5, 2026; completion expected in the next few months, subject to NCLT.
New CBS launch planned in Q2/Q3 FY27.
No equity capital raise planned near term; any shortfall to be met through Tier-2 capital or balance sheet offloading.
capex_capacity: Collections workforce for JLG and MBBL expanded to more than 1,200 as on March 2026; specialised call centre for overdue accounts set up and larger micro-banking branches split.
Utkarsh 2.0 technology transformation is in progress, covering digital underwriting and 360-degree control parameter mapping.
Rights issue of INR950 crores completed in November 2025.
Management said it is only at ~70% of optimum disbursement capacity in micro-banking.
demand_pricing: JLG disbursements rose 58% QoQ to ~INR1,310 crores (first increase after three quarters of decline); non-JLG disbursements rose 41% QoQ and 51% YoY.

Management said the post-October 2024 portfolio has NPAs below 2%.
Retail deposits: total deposits grew ~0.4% YoY and ~3% QoQ; retail term deposits grew 20% YoY; CASA grew 11% YoY and 13% QoQ.
Legacy stress: PCR 59.3% overall, 39.0% on secured and 65.4% on unsecured; JLG/MBBL PCR 66.3%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the PCR levels for secured, unsecured and JLG?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall PCR is 59.3%, secured 39.0%, unsecured 65.4% and JLG 66.3%. Management said 85% provisioning and part of the 70% provisioning are still to be recognised on JLG and MBBL.

qa_highlights.question: How ready is the bank for ECL and what is the credit cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said SFBs are exempt from Ind AS from April 2027, but accounting provisions would be equal to or higher than ECL-based numbers. Credit cost guidance is ~3% for FY27 and 2-2.5% for FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did JLG disbursements rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Virender Sharma said collections stabilised by October-November 2025, after which sales resumed under MFIN 2.0 guidelines. Disbursements are still at ~70% of optimum capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Is CGFMU cover generating any benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management has expensed only the premium, with no claim, NPA adjustment or capital relief recognised. About 70% of the MFI book is covered as of March 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Can the bank grow 30% amid the Prime Minister's comments on credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees ~30% growth as achievable from a low base and said it does not foresee a credit cost challenge, since most of the book is small-ticket income-generation lending.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to ROE of 15% and net NPA below 1%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROE of 15% is achievable by FY28 and net NPA below 1% by FY28, supported by recoveries and provisioning on the legacy book. It said the worst is behind the bank.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for non-MFI slippages, which run at ~4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Acharya attributed the slippages mainly to Wheels (CV/CE), with used vehicles now ~30% of disbursements. He expects Wheels to normalise over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the write-off recovery rate and how is the collection team being used?
qa_highlights.answer: The write-off recovery rate is 12-14%. Around INR50 crores was collected from the NPA and write-off pool in Q4 with ~900 staff; management expects the collection team to be redeployed toward legacy recovery.

543942|2026-06.headline: Utkarsh SFB narrowed Q1 FY27 net loss to INR34 crore (down over 80% YoY and QoQ), with GNPA at 5.9% and credit cost at 2.3%.

Cost of funds fell to 7.7%, and PPOP rose to INR64 crore from INR12 crore in Q4. Profitability is not yet normal; the bank is still loss-making, and CGFMU guarantee benefit of about INR75 crore supported the P&L. Management guided to 25-30% loan growth, NIM around 8% and ROE around 15% by FY28, while analysts pressed on the quality of the legacy book and the growth push.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned JLG portfolio run-down and the overall growth outlook for this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects JLG to hold around 25% of the book over the next 2-3 years, with Micro Banking plus business loans growing 15-20%, overall loan growth 25-30%, and JLG growth below 20%. Sarjukumar said the book will keep growing rather than run down, with the JLG/Micro Banking cap around 25%.

qa_highlights.question: What credit cost and NPA guidance applies for the rest of FY27, and are further fundraises planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost guided at the upper end of 3-3.5%, described as conservative. The INR500 crore Tier 2 NCD adds about 250 bps to CRAR, while the INR195 crore 12.5% tranche is being redeemed early in mid-August, saving about INR20 crore. No equity raise is expected until at least end-FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the asset quality of the post-guardrail book and how is CGFMU coverage positioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Post-April 2025 book is the majority of outstanding JLG book with GNPA of about 1.85-1.9%. CGFMU coverage is 60% for disbursements up to Q4 FY26 and about 80% including Q1 FY27 disbursements.

qa_highlights.question: How is MBBL sourced and underwritten, and is it going to new-to-bank customers?
qa_highlights.answer: About 99.9% of MBBL is existing customers with 2-3 prior cycles; new-to-bank is a small pilot of no more than about 100-200 accounts. MBBL outstanding is about INR2,246 crore, of which INR2,036 crore is post April 2025, with only 0.3% NPA in that pool. A separate underwriting team and a dedicated MBBL collection team are used.

qa_highlights.question: Why are recoveries slow, and how much of the slippage/NPA pool is in Micro Banking?
qa_highlights.answer: Slow retail recoveries are due to SARFAESI-linked legacy cases, with processes taking 6-7 months to auction. About INR28 crore of the recoveries pool was from Micro Banking. Recoveries are expected to pick up in Q2 and Q3, with about 1,100 JLG collection staff being redeployed to recoveries and write-offs.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the growth guidance given weak Q1 growth and how credible is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to Q4 FY26 disbursements up 30% YoY and Q1 FY27 up 49%, with H2 expected to carry the 25% growth target. Govind Singh said the 25-30% range is partly because write-offs shrink the reported book and the base is small after two years of no growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PPOP growing slowly and what is the path to profitability and cost-to-income?
qa_highlights.answer: PPOP moved from negative about INR44 crore in December to INR12 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR64 crore in Q1 FY27. Management expects cost-to-income to improve as income recovers with flat costs, with 2-digit ROE exiting FY27 and about 15% ROE in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank keep growing microfinance, and what is the risk weight on incremental MFI loans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will keep MFI at about 25% of the book. Under CGFMU, only about INR15 of every INR100 of incremental MFI book gets zero risk weight, because the benefit is capped at 15% of crystallised disbursements; the remaining INR85 carries risk weight.

Profitability: still a net loss of INR34 crore; PPOP of INR64 crore needs to rise further to reach 2-digit ROE by Q4 FY27; cost-to-income remains elevated.
