demand_pricing: Channel mix: offline retail about 70% of turnover; online (e-commerce and quick commerce) about 30%, primarily via Flipkart and Myntra on a marketplace model.
Management cites RedTape as the number two footwear brand on Flipkart and Myntra; online repeat customers at 54-58%.
Pricing: no MRP hikes yet; company works on cost-plus and has about six months of POs and LCs covered.
Management said the Q4 volume lift was not only GST-driven, citing wedding season, healthy footfalls and same-store growth; SSSG was 17.8% in Q4.
Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns hold the majority of stores; consumer shift to organised branded product cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory high (about 175 days on sales, over 300 days on COGS) and where will it settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory peaked above 250 days and is now about 170, driven by marketplace warehouse build-out and offline expansion. The target is 120-150 days, with 150 as the ideal near-term level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall while EBITDA improved, and what is the medium-term EBITDA view?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said e-commerce rebates are now netted against revenue, so the gross margin decline is top-line driven, with no PBT impact. CFO said EBITDA has hovered around 16-18%, with 19% described as a new normal.

qa_highlights.question: What is the other income of INR133 crores and the FY25 restatement?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR88 crores is e-commerce discounts/rebates and the rest is claims from platforms. The FY25 restatement was an accounting change, applied to the prior year as well.

qa_highlights.question: What is the apparel margin and the operating cash flow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not report footwear and apparel margins separately and did not give a figure. On cash flow, CFO said operating cash flow reached INR175 crores and debt fell about INR200 crores since September.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin, the COCO/FOFO split, and the accessories strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin is about 16.4%. About 25-27% of stores are COCO. Accessories expansion is framed as raising wallet share and SSSG, building on belts, wallets and caps.

qa_highlights.question: Payable days appear to have dropped sharply; what is driving this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management initially deferred the question and the CFO said he would revert, citing payable days history of about 171-188 days in recent years.

risks_watch: Inventory at about 170 days versus the 150-day target; operating cash flow and short-term borrowings depend on this.
Payable days reportedly fell sharply (about 55 days per an analyst's reading); management has not yet explained this.
Raw material cost pressure; price increases are deferred until after September, and no price hikes are taken.
Gross margin optics shaped by e-commerce rebate accounting; EBITDA margin band is wide (16-19%).
Apparel margin not disclosed, and the segment is now 34% of revenue and the focus of FY27 investment.
Store expansion of 200-250 outlets in FY27 must clear return thresholds from day one, per management.
543957|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 results and brand momentum, but guarded on specifics: management deferred several questions (payable days, apparel margin, footwear vs apparel split) and gave no multi-year revenue target.
key_quotes: What comes through clearly is that the business has held its shape through all of that and then accelerated.
It is not the store count that we are chasing. Every location we open has to clear our return thresholds from day one.
We are pleased to announce that the Board has recommended a final INR2 per equity share on the face value of INR2.
We are the number two footwear brand on Flipkart and Myntra.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin band guided at 16-19% (FY26 at 19%, Pre-Ind AS 16.4%), no MRP hike planned for 3-6 months despite raw-material cost volatility, and new stores must clear return thresholds from day one.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Plan to open 200-250 stores in FY27 (500-1,500 sq ft), store count already above 550, with two more marketplace warehouses planned after seven existing; management has committed to the store rollout and is scaling Ozark stores.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q4 SSSG was 17.8%, six months of POs and LCs are covered, and 200-250 store additions planned, with revenue up 19.6% in FY26 to INR2,415 crores; no FY27 volume number was guided.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is tied to the store rollout and warehouse build-out, but no FY27 capex figure was given and the prior INR450 crore breakdown was not provided, so a new formal capex number is conditional.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided EBITDA margin to a 16-19% band described as a new normal rather than a peak, and gave no multi-year revenue target, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Payable days reportedly fell to about 55 from roughly 171-188 days historically, unexplained by management, and inventory at about 170 days is above the 150-day target, which could pressure cash flow and margins if not corrected.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is investing most in apparel for FY27 including women's apparel, and Bond Street and Mode were launched in FY26 with Ozark rollout being scaled, though no specific launch dates or figures were given.

rows.label: Inventory reduction to 150 days
rows.why: Inventory at about 170 days versus 150-day ideal and earlier peak above 250 days, with management saying 150 days is what it is trying to achieve; the target is described as 'very near future' with a 120-150 day range.

rows.label: Debt reduction continuing
rows.why: Debt fell about INR200 crores from September to March and operating cash flow was INR175 crores, though the payable-day drop may reverse part of this cash benefit.

rows.label: No MRP hike; price review after September
rows.why: No MRP increase planned for 3-6 months with raw-material cost volatility to be reassessed after September, so pricing is not a near-term lever.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 results, store rollout and SSSG of 17.8%, but deferred questions on payable days, apparel margin and footwear vs apparel split; analysts pressed on inventory days, gross margin optics and the sharp fall in payable days.

543957|2026-06.headline: Redtape Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 19.4% YoY to INR47 crore on 3.7% revenue growth to INR480 crore, with no price hikes and e-commerce deliberately de-prioritised.
543957|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 3.7% YoY to INR480 crore, with gross margin at 47.5% and EBITDA margin at 20.4%. PAT rose 19.4% to INR47 crore, the company's highest-ever Q1 profit in absolute terms. Management held MRPs flat and absorbed minimum wage and input cost inflation through sourcing, supply chain and retail efficiencies. E-commerce declined as management refused to match marketplace deep discounting, and online share of revenue fell to 22% from 30%. Management described the e-commerce dip as a one-off, but gave no quantified guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited >200 bps improvement; management attributed it to retail margins, operating leverage and supply chain
down from around INR28 crore in Q1 FY26, due to lower e-commerce platform rebates

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: 56% of Q1 turnover; management says footwear carries Q1 and Q2 while apparel peaks in Q3 and Q4. Open footwear ASPs improved sequentially.

segments.name: Apparel
segments.commentary: 39% of Q1 turnover; seasonally stronger in Q3 and Q4. Category-wise YoY growth not disclosed.

segments.name: Accessories
segments.commentary: 5% of Q1 turnover. Sunglasses are in about 80% of stores; hard luggage in only 10-15% of stores as the category has shifted online.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Declined YoY because management declined incremental marketplace discounting. Online share fell to 22% from 30%. Management aspires to return to 30%.

segments.name: Core India retail
segments.commentary: Softer early in the quarter, improved as the quarter progressed. Management credits store-led model and better product/category mix for margin gains.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: UAE franchise stores were hit early in the quarter and recovered in the last month. UK master distributor Style Label Manchester appointed; transactions started. No export revenue guidance given.

segments.name: Sprandi (new brand)
segments.commentary: Sports brand acquired in April 2026 for India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and other countries. Shoes first, then apparel. Launch in India online and retail by end-September 2026.

guidance_outlook: Store additions: 33 opened in Q1 FY27; aspiration of about 150 (150-plus) by FY27 end, versus an earlier 200-250 aspiration. Management says it will 'remain close to that number'.
EBITDA margin to be kept stable at around 20% for the year; management also expressed aspiration to increase margins.
Revenue growth: management hopes to continue the growth rate of the last 3-4 years; no quantified FY27 guidance.
E-commerce share expected to recover towards 30% of revenue; management called the Q1 dip a one-off.
Inventory target to reduce from 173 days to 150 days. Inventory build-up expected in Q2 ahead of festive season.
No MRP increases planned; management aims to offset cost inflation through efficiencies.
capex_capacity: New stores: 33 opened in Q1 FY27, with an aspiration of about 150 for FY27. Ramp-up takes 45-50 days for a 1,000 sq ft store and about 75 days for a 3,000-4,000 sq ft store.
New store formats are mostly 800-1,500 sq ft, as expansion into South, East and West India is more store-count intensive.
Store in Forum Mall, Kolkata opened; malls to be used where they are stronger than high streets, particularly in South and West India.
Inventory at 173 days; Q2 build-up expected, then reduction in Q3 and Q4.
No acquisitions in the pipeline at present; management is open to opportunities in footwear and apparel.
demand_pricing: Demand was soft early in Q1 due to macro headwinds and cautious consumer spending, then improved through the quarter.

Marketplaces pushed higher discounting; Redtape declined to match beyond levels it considered appropriate for the brand. Management said there is no fixed discount ceiling and that it decides event by event (for example BBD).

ASPs rose sequentially across footwear and apparel from product and category mix, not broad-based price hikes. MRPs were held flat despite minimum wage and input cost inflation linked to the ongoing war.
Management declined to quantify inflation, calling it 'a regular business'.
Non-BIS inventory remains; the industry has an extension of one year, with management expecting a further extension.
A September 2025 income tax search is ongoing; management says no material claim or risk has been identified so far.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the e-commerce weakness, and what is the discount level beyond which Redtape will not participate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline was a deliberate choice, not a structural weakness. It declined to set a fixed discount threshold, saying it depends on event size and margin impact, and that it expects e-commerce to recover.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inflation burden and will price hikes follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said minimum wage and war-related costs were absorbed, MRPs were not raised, and it would not quantify the inflation as it is a regular business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the lower other income?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vivek Agnihotri said lower e-commerce platform rebates cut other income to around INR8-9 crore from about INR28 crore in the prior-year quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement above 200 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said retail margins were stronger, with operating leverage and an optimised supply chain. No category-level margin split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Does Q1 margin mean moderation is likely for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intent is to keep margins intact and aspire to improve them, while noting that it will not sacrifice margins for top-line growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the income tax search from September 2025?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the process is ongoing and could take 2-3 years, with no material claim or risk identified to date.

risks_watch: E-commerce recovery to 30% of revenue is an aspiration; online share is 22% and management gave no timeline or quantified discount threshold, and the Q1 dip could persist into the BBD/festive season if marketplace discounting stays deep.

Margin stability: management aims to hold EBITDA margin around 20% and gross margin gains (>200 bps per analyst) were attributed mainly to retail margins without a category-level split, so sustainability is unverified.

Inflation exposure: minimum wage hikes in manufacturing states and war-linked input costs were absorbed without MRP increases; no quantification given, so a squeeze on margins if efficiencies fade is a watch item.
Store rollout: 33 stores opened in Q1 versus a FY27 aspiration of about 150-plus (earlier 200-250); new 800-1,500 sq ft formats in South, East and West India may ramp more slowly.
Inventory at 173 days with a Q2 build-up planned ahead of festive season; reduction to 150 days targeted, and non-BIS inventory remains outstanding.

Income tax search (September 2025) ongoing; management said it could take 2-3 years, with no material claim identified so far. Other income fell to INR8-9 crore from about INR28 crore on lower e-commerce rebates.
key_quotes: So we don't see this as a weakness. The degrowth in e-commerce was largely a conscious outcome of our channel strategy during the quarter.
We would like to believe it's a one-off thing.
Not really. It's a regular business for us.
We would like to remain as it is now. We'd like to be stable.
But as of now there's been no claim of any material and there's no risk of any material.

rows.why: Inventory at 173 days, with a Q2 build-up ahead of festive season and reduction planned in Q3 and Q4 to a 150-day target.

rows.why: Management said the process could take 2-3 years, with no material claim or risk identified so far, so no near-term resolution is expected.

tone.note: Management was confident on profitability, margin stability and brand protection, but evasive on quantification (discount threshold, inflation, category YoY, SSSG, FY27 revenue guide), while analysts pressed on e-commerce, gross margin drivers and the store target cut from 200-250 to 150-plus.

543959|2026-03.headline: SBFC Q4 FY26: AUM up 29% YoY to INR 11,270 crore, PAT up 30% to INR 123 crore, credit cost steady at 1.38%.
543959|2026-03.overview: SBFC reported Q4 FY26 AUM of INR 11,270 crore, up 29% YoY and 8% QoQ, with gold loans reaching 21% of the book. Spreads widened 56 bps YoY to 9.09% as cost of borrowing fell 83 bps to 8.52%, and opex fell 69 bps YoY to 3.93%. PAT rose 30% YoY to INR 123 crore, with FY26 PAT at INR 451 crore (+31%). Management kept FY27 guidance broadly unchanged: 5-7% quarterly growth, flat spreads, opex down 20-25 bps and credit cost range-bound around 1.38%. Branch count reached 251 with a plan to stabilise near 275.

financial_highlights.metric: Return on average AUM / average tangible equity

segments.name: MSME loans
segments.commentary: AUM INR 8,873 crore, 79% of book, with Q4 disbursements of INR 785 crore. Average ticket size remains below INR 2.5 lakh and LTV is about 56-57%.

segments.name: Loan against gold
segments.commentary: AUM INR 2,374 crore, 21% of book, growing 63% YoY; management says growth is mainly price-driven and the share may move toward 25%. Around 220 of 251 branches are pure gold branches.

segments.name: Co-origination (with ICICI)
segments.commentary: Co-origination was 16% of Q4 disbursements and 18-19% of AUM, and is expected to hold similar levels through FY27.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance unchanged at 5-7% per quarter; management says the segment could double the book in 3-3.5 years.
Spreads expected to hold at around 9% current level; over 90% of the book is variable-rate.
Opex expected to fall 20-25 bps through FY27 as new branches mature.
Credit cost expected to stay range-bound around 1.38%, with possible benefit of about 5 bps.
Branch network to stabilise at about 275 (from 251) during the year; 46 branches were added in FY26 against 25 guided.
Portfolio mix between MSME and gold expected at 75:25; co-origination at 18-19% of AUM.
Capital: at 33% CRAR, growth could run about 2 years before needing fresh capital, with CRAR falling to about 24-26%.
capex_capacity: Branches: 251 at March 2026 after adding 21 in Q4 and 46 in FY26; target to stabilise at about 275 in FY27.
Branch expansion is gated by state profitability; new states are run slowly for 18-24 months before scaling, with about 60% of branches older than 3 years.
Currently present in about one-fourth of districts in operating states (about 30% per Aseem Dhru) across 15 states.
Management says it will not add DSAs or connectors for at least two years; direct model retained.
Leverage at 1.9x debt/equity; management says capital is sufficient for roughly two years of growth.
demand_pricing: Management said growth in gold has been mostly price-driven rather than tonnage-driven; gold prices are expected to stay range-bound or flat.
Disbursements have been soft YoY; management said it paused momentum in some South, East and West pockets, and could return to around INR 300 crore per month when conditions improve.
South disbursals and AUM grew more slowly last year, which lifted the West's share of AUM (management said mix to stay similar for two quarters).
Early April data showed no new stress in sectors hit by LPG and fertilizer pressures; bounce rates marginally lower.
Management expects no increase in cost of borrowing in FY27; G-Sec volatility and a temporary liquidity squeeze were flagged.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee and branch opex per unit flat for many quarters, and how long can that continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Dayani said upfront investment in state, regional and supervisor layers is already in place, so incremental cost is mainly front-end staff at low unit cost; opex is still guided down 20-25 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Will SBFC need DSAs or connectors to sustain growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said the current distribution can deliver about 20% disbursal growth next year, with no need for indirect channels for at least two years.

qa_highlights.question: Sensitivity of growth and gold mix to gold prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Dayani said gold growth is mostly price-driven; FY27 gold growth is pencilled in on full-year benefit from branches added in FY26, not on higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is credit cost guidance conservative given early delinquency improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Dayani said guidance is cautious given the macro (fuel, rainfall, heat); April numbers show no stress in LPG- and fertiliser-linked sectors.

qa_highlights.question: Path to ROE of 18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said ROE is an outcome of ROA and leverage (about 4.57% ROA, 3.17x leverage, ~14.5% ROE); management called 18% optimistic and cited more than 15% ROE on 25% growth if ROA compresses about 25 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ARC sell-down a driver of reported GNPA?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said ARC sales are used to clean up hard-to-collect assets and recoveries under SARFAESI; benefits flow to P&L. No extra provision overlay was held beyond the March model refresh.

risks_watch: Macro shocks: oil price pass-through, weaker rupee, poor monsoon/El Nino, Gulf remittance risk, all flagged by management.
Gold price reversal would slow the gold book, which is 21% of AUM and the main driver of growth.
Credit cost guided flat at 1.38% while stage 2 rose from about 6% to 16% (per Mahesh Dayani); watch slippage and 1+ DPD (benchmarked 7-9%).
Disbursement volumes are down YoY and branches added in gold and MSME may not reach productivity targets as planned.
Rating upgrade is possible but not guided; management declined to comment.

543959|2026-06.headline: SBFC Q1 FY27: PAT rose 29% YoY to INR 130 crores and spreads widened 39 bps QoQ to 9.48%, while 0+ DPD rose 70 bps and AUM grew 6% QoQ.
543959|2026-06.overview: AUM reached INR 11,922 crores (up 27% YoY, 6% QoQ), with MSME AUM at INR 9,271 crores and gold loan AUM at INR 2,631 crores. Spreads improved to 9.48% and NIM to 10.6%, helped by a 90 bps YoY drop in cost of borrowing to 8.42%. Management cited headwinds: lower gold-loan eligibility after April 1, 2026 rules, a regulatory cap on bank collateral for sub-20 lakh MSME tickets that hit co-origination, and softer login-to-disbursal conversion (34% vs 42%). Asset quality weakened QoQ, with 0+ DPD up 70 bps and GNPA at 2.66%, but Stage 2 ECL was raised to 16% from 6% and total provisioning reached 1.91% of assets.

financial_highlights.change: up by similar bps as spread (QoQ)
Stage 2 ECL raised to 16% from 6%; about 2x regulatory minimum

segments.name: MSME / small-ticket LAP
segments.commentary: MSME AUM INR 9,271 crores (+4.5% QoQ) and disbursements INR 809 crores (+3% QoQ). Co-origination, about 20% of disbursals and book, reset to about 10% after RBI collateral rule for sub-20 lakh MSME tickets; management expects a return to usual run rate from this quarter.

segments.name: Gold loan
segments.commentary: AUM INR 2,631 crores (+11% QoQ). Gold yields rose in the quarter and were the main driver of the 29 bps QoQ yield increase; management expects gold yields to stay range-bound, with at most a marginal decline.

guidance_outlook: Opex to average AUM to fall 25 bps in FY27 (reiterated), and to be closer to 4% or below by year-end as new branches mature.
Credit cost expected at 1.4%-1.5% for at least the next two quarters; Q1 was 1.45%.
Yield expected to stabilise in the 17.50%-17.75% range; spreads to be held above 9%.
Cost of borrowing expected to stabilise at current levels after upfronting borrowings and liquidity build-up.
Branch expansion limited to 10-15 in FY27, after 5 branches added in Q1 (total 256), with further expansion tied to returns from recent branches.
Management says guidance for the coming quarter is unchanged; AUM target path to INR 15,000 crores with higher liquidity held on balance sheet.
capex_capacity: Branch count 256 as of June 2026 after adding five in Q1; roughly 52 branches opened over the last year, with the bulk in H2 FY26.
Plan for FY27 is 10-15 new branches, with expansion gated on profitability of recently opened branches.
Closing liquidity INR 1,864 crores; management intends to hold higher liquidity as it grows toward INR 15,000 crores AUM.
Capital adequacy ratio 32%; tangible net worth INR 3,613 crores.
demand_pricing: Login-to-disbursal conversion fell to 34% from 42%; management expects it to hold near 35% as higher logins and co-origination recover.
Around 1,400 applications per quarter (about 7% of roughly 21,000 logins), or about INR 140 crores of disbursals, were not passing filters; management will not push loans that fail screens.
Sub-10 lakh household segment showing leveraged stress; CIBIL scores above 700 for about 90% of the portfolio, but eligibility is the binding constraint.
Competitors pricing aggressively or offering larger loan amounts; management chose to walk away from some business to protect spreads.
Gold-loan eligibility norms reset from April 1, 2026, and falling gold prices reduced the loan amount reaching customers.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the sub-10 lakh segment in its credit cycle, and how does that affect FY27 growth and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said conditions there have not improved and it is watchful. Aseem Dhru cited household DSR near 14% per CLSA, and said the company does not know whether it is early or mid-cycle.

qa_highlights.question: Will SBFC add new products in the next 12-18 months beyond small-ticket LAP and gold loans?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it will focus on getting better at the existing two products and sees no need for new products or geographies to meet FY27 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Increments were rolled out, and about 20-25 branches opened in Q4 FY26 plus 5 in Q1 brought their full-year staff costs into this quarter. Cost to AUM should fall as those branches mature over the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Was the 30 bps yield increase driven by higher risk-taking?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said gold yields rose this quarter, adding to the yield improvement. Company yield is expected to stabilise at 17.50%-17.75%, with spreads held above 9%.

qa_highlights.question: Is credit cost stable at about 1.4% for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management expects credit cost of 1.4%-1.5% for at least the next two quarters; Q1 was 1.45%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for incremental yield and gold yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental yield is in the same 17.50%-17.75% range, slightly up because of gold. Gold yields are expected to be range-bound with at most a marginal fall; the recent 25-30 bps rise should not be extrapolated.

risks_watch: Sub-10 lakh household segment: management says conditions have not improved, CLSA household DSR near 14%, and the company cannot tell whether the cycle is early or mid; watch the disbursal mix and ticket size there.
Asset quality: 0+ DPD rose 70 bps QoQ and management called it homework for the current quarter, expecting stabilisation this quarter and rollbacks in later quarters; GNPA 2.66%.
Co-origination recovery: management expects co-origination to return to its usual run rate this quarter after the RBI collateral rule cut its share to about 10%; verify in Q2 disbursals.
Cost to AUM: opex 4.29% needs to fall to about 4% or below by year-end as branches opened in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 mature; employee cost stays elevated in the near term.
Funding and rates: management flagged an upward bias in Indian interest rates from crude above $100 and deposit rates, while saying cost of borrowing should now stabilise at current levels.
Gold yields: management says the 25-30 bps rise should not be extrapolated and gold yields may drift marginally lower; spread floor of 9% depends on holding yields at 17.50%-17.75%.
key_quotes: We'd rather over-insulate the P&L now than explain a surprise later, call it prudence with a margin of safety.
So, we don't want to, at this stage look at anything different or new.
But I think the only parameter that one should probably look at is whether we've been able to maintain our spreads.
My sense is that the 25-30 basis increase you shouldn't pencil-in and extrapolate the numbers from here.
543959|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on spreads, NIM, PAT and provisioning, with a cautious tone on the household segment and on macro, rates and oil. Management repeatedly stressed that guidance is unchanged and that it would rather slow growth than push loans that fail screens.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Spread at 9.48% (+39 bps QoQ) and management guides spreads above 9% with yield at 17.50%-17.75%, but gold yield gains are not to be extrapolated and cost of borrowing is stable at 8.42%; opex/AUM at 4.29% must fall about 25 bps in FY27 to ~4% by year-end as Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 branches mature.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch count 256 after 5 added in Q1, with 10-15 more planned in FY27; this is a modest, profitability-gated addition, not a major capacity step-up.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM 11,922 crores (+6% QoQ, +27% YoY) with a path to 15,000 crores, but login-to-disbursal conversion fell to 34% from 42%, about 1,400 applications per quarter (~INR 140 crores of disbursals) failed filters, and management will not push weak loans.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says it will 'go slow' with 10-15 branches in FY27 and gates expansion on the profitability of recent branches; no utilisation or capacity constraint is cited and liquidity is being built up instead.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says guidance is unchanged and it would rather slow growth than push loans that fail screens; the household segment is still stressed with no sign of improvement.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: 0+ DPD rose 70 bps QoQ, GNPA is 2.66%, and credit cost of 1.45% sits at the top of the 1.4-1.5% range, with the sub-10 lakh household segment stressed and rate risk from crude above $100.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said it will focus on the existing two products (small-ticket LAP and gold loans) and sees no need for new products or geographies to meet FY27 guidance.

rows.label: Co-origination recovery to usual run rate
rows.why: Co-origination was reset to about 10% of disbursals and book (from about 20%) after the RBI collateral rule for sub-20 lakh tickets; management expects a return to normal run rate this quarter, which is not yet proven.

rows.label: Gold-loan eligibility reset and falling gold prices
rows.why: Eligibility norms reset from April 1, 2026 and falling gold prices reduced loan amounts reaching customers, though gold AUM still grew 11% QoQ to INR 2,631 crores and gold yields are expected to stay range-bound.

rows.label: Opex/AUM down 25 bps in FY27 to about 4%
rows.why: Opex/AUM was 4.29% (+36 bps QoQ); management reiterated the 25 bps FY27 reduction as Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 branches mature over the next nine months.

543959|2026-09.headline: SBFC Q2 FY27 PAT rose 27% YoY to INR 139 crore, with ROE at 15.04% and AUM up 27% YoY to INR 12,592 crore.
543959|2026-09.overview: SBFC reported its 36th consecutive quarter of sequential AUM and profit growth, with AUM at INR 12,592 crore (up 6% QoQ, 27% YoY) and PAT of INR 139 crore (up 7% QoQ, 27% YoY). Credit cost eased to 1.37% from 1.44% and Opex fell to 4.07%, while spreads widened to 9.63%. Management said the gold-loan delinquency rise after the RBI circular was the main source of higher Stage 2 assets, and that the MSME book has stabilised rather than improved. Management kept its 5-7% quarterly AUM growth guidance and warned against treating 9.6% spreads as a new norm.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME AUM INR 9,669 crore (77% of AUM), up 18% YoY and 4.3% QoQ; on-book grew 20% and co-origination 10%. MSME disbursements INR 855 crore, up 6% QoQ, the third straight quarter of growth.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan AUM INR 2,906 crore (about 23% of AUM); added INR 275 crore in Q2, roughly INR 40 lakh net growth per branch per month across 236 gold branches. Management is deliberately cautious on volume and LTV expansion.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 5-7% per quarter going forward; management said MSME disbursements should grow in double digits second-half over second-half.
Opex expected to fall by a further 25 bps in FY27, with a further reduction over the next two quarters.
Spread guided around 9-9.25%, but management asked investors not to model 9.6% as the norm due to rising gold competition and likely pricing rationalisation.
Credit cost seen stabilising at around 1.37% or marginally lower unless El Nino or state waivers materially change the outlook; 1.45% in Q1 described as likely peak.
Capital sufficient to an AUM of about INR 20,000 crore before the next capital raise; ROE expansion expected as leverage rises.
PLR raised 25 bps in October 2026; management expects spreads to hold as variable-rate MSME assets reprice.
CARE and India Ratings revised outlook from stable to positive.
capex_capacity: Branch count 257 as of September 2026 (1 added in Q2, 6 in H1); 236 branches do gold loans.
Collection team about 850 including supervisors (about 700 front-end), up 150-200 in the period.
LCR at 194%; closing liquidity INR 1,782 crore in Q2 versus INR 1,864 crore in Q1.
AI voice ran the first full pre-due collection cycle in October: more than 4 lakh calls to 35,000 accounts, 84% reached, 53% paid, replacing roughly a 60-person team.
demand_pricing: Banks are moving to higher-ticket prime borrowers at single-digit pricing, leaving INR 10-25 lakh and INR 25+ lakh MSME segments with headroom for SBFC.
Sub-INR 7 lakh book is being run down and is no longer originated; it is under 6% of AUM per management.
Gold competition rising as large players open branches; gold yields range 18-21%, with management expecting roughly 23% and possibly 25%.
Co-origination rose to INR 112 crore from INR 78 crore in Q1.
Management expects MSME disbursements to stabilise and grow; Q2 was the highest disbursement level in the MSME business since listing per management.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan stress and how the industry is positioned, given larger players entering gold.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not chase high-volume gold growth, as it expects pricing to be compromised; it said gold yields are 18-21% and competition has risen in the last 1-1.5 months, with some large players opening 500-1,000 branches.

qa_highlights.question: Why slippages (GS2+GS3) rose QoQ, and whether the ARC sale was gold or MSME.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise in Stage 2 is entirely from gold loans after the RBI circular reset scheme design, as customers move from bullet to monthly interest payments. The ARC sale was a lower-ticket vintage LAP portfolio; no gold loans were sold.

qa_highlights.question: Gold price sensitivity and LTV risk.
qa_highlights.answer: LTV fell to 67% from about 70% last quarter (versus about 60s in June 2025). Auctions are triggered after 85-90% LTV and delinquency, with a 7-30 day window per management; out-of-money risk described as not significant.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of MSME disbursement pick-up.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the repositioning is done and restaffing is complete in most locations; it expects second-half over second-half disbursement growth of at least double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Steady-state 0+ DPD and credit cost.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 0+ rose from around 7% to above 9% and is now stabilising; it expects 0+ to hold in the 8-9.2% range, not return to 7%, and credit cost to stabilise near 1.37%.

qa_highlights.question: Whether 4.5% ROA can be sustained as guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROA has held above 4.5% for 7-8 quarters despite higher leverage; holding 4.6% over the long run will be difficult, but it should hold in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: Collection headcount and bandwidth.
qa_highlights.answer: About 700 front-end collectors and 850 including supervisors; average caseload of 40-45 per collector, varying from 25-30 in Assam to about 50 in South India.

risks_watch: Gold: competitive pricing pressure, possible yield compression, and a possible fall in gold prices (LTV fell to 67%; October saw a drop).
El Nino and drought: rainfall deficit concentrated in Karnataka and Maharashtra; state-level waivers could affect repayment behaviour.
Rising rates: 25 bps repo hike and cost of funds expected to rise; management expects spreads to hold, but pass-through of MCLR-linked debt is still to come.
Draft regulatory circular that management said may affect profitability.
Stage 2 and 0+ DPD trends, with 0+ above 9% versus about 7% historically; track whether they keep stabilising in Q3.
543959|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on operating metrics and conservative in outlook: management stressed consistency and 'boring' results, repeatedly cautioned on gold and macro risk, and said asset quality has stabilised rather than improved. It was evasive on the precise gold-loan granularity an analyst asked for, promising to consider adding it to future presentations.
key_quotes: We are building SBFC to deliver consistent quarterly performance despite the noise.
Please do not pencil in 9.6% in your models as the new norm, since competitive intensity in gold is rising and some pricing rationalization is likely.
So to say that will it go below 7% will be a tall ask. We don't think it will reach there.
In our case, we've been able to hold on to more than 4.5% ROA for now more than 7 - 8 quarters despite increase in leverage.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Spread guided at 9-9.25% versus 9.63% in Q2 and management asked not to model 9.6% as the norm; opex to AUM down 22 bps QoQ to 4.07% with a further 25 bps FY27 reduction guided, but credit cost is seen flat at about 1.37%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Only 1 branch added in Q2 (257 total, 6 in H1) and no further openings quantified; capital is sufficient to about INR 20,000 crore AUM versus INR 12,592 crore today.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM guided at 5-7% per quarter (about 22-32% annualised) versus 27% YoY now; MSME disbursements at INR 855 crore, third straight quarter of growth, with second-half over second-half growth guided at double digits.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capital is sufficient to about INR 20,000 crore AUM before the next raise, against INR 12,592 crore today, and no new capex was discussed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held AUM and opex guidance and warned against treating 9.6% spreads as the norm, pointing to spread compression rather than an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gold competition rising with yields at 18-21%, possible pricing rationalisation, and 0+ DPD at above 9% versus about 7% historically could pull spreads or credit cost off guidance.

rows.label: Draft regulatory circular may affect profitability
rows.why: Management flagged a draft regulatory circular it said may affect profitability, with no quantified impact given.

rows.label: Gold pricing pressure from large entrants
rows.why: Large players opening 500-1,000 branches each and gold yields at 18-21%, with management expecting pricing to be compromised; SBFC is choosing not to chase gold volume.

rows.label: Banks retreating to prime segments
rows.why: Banks moving to higher-ticket prime borrowers at single-digit pricing leave INR 10-25 lakh and INR 25+ lakh MSME segments open, supporting MSME disbursement growth.

tone.note: Management was confident on operating metrics and held AUM and opex guidance but cautious on gold competition, 0+ DPD above 9%, and spread normalisation; analysts pushed on gold-loan granularity and slippage drivers, which management answered only partly.

543960|2026-03.headline: Concord Biotech FY26 revenue fell 12% to a level where API sales were INR 829 crores, with management guiding to growth slightly above its ~18% historical rate in FY27.
543960|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a difficult year: revenue declined about 12% and Q4 revenue fell 24% YoY, driven by a roughly three-month CDSCO-related halt in European supplies, a Middle East tender held in abeyance, and a US Veterans Affairs tender on hold. Management attributes the shortfall to timing rather than demand, pricing or market share loss, and says deferred volumes are spilling into FY27. Profitability held up better than revenue: reported FY26 EBITDA was INR 367 crores at about 35%, and PAT fell 30% to INR 260 crores. The company remains debt-free with over INR 414 crores of cash.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: FY26 API revenue INR 829 crores (-12%); Q4 INR 264 crores (-27%). Management said there was no price growth and the decline was volume-driven. Anti-infectives and oncology are expected to grow faster than immunosuppressants in FY27.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue fell about 13% in FY26 and 8% in Q4, mainly from the European halt and Middle East formulation tender. Management says the domestic and US formulation businesses grew.

segments.name: Injectables (new facility)
segments.commentary: Expenses of about INR 38-39 crores in FY26 (about INR 10 crores per quarter). WHO-GMP certified; filings are under way with Southeast Asia and Africa as first targets. Management said full breakeven is more likely in FY27.

segments.name: Stellon Biotech (US subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Set up in FY26 with licences for direct US marketing. Management expects first supplies in H1 FY27 with orders already in place, and expenses were fully booked in FY26.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Management classes only third-party IP work as CDMO; it expects 1-4% of FY26 revenue, with one advanced-stage opportunity that could change this.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth expected to be slightly better than the historical ~18% rate, with visibility in H1 and growth expected from Q1-Q2.
No formal EBITDA margin guidance. Management cited a 1-1.5% EBITDA tailwind from solar/renewable power, partly offset by higher LPG and furnace oil costs.
Gross margin expected to be in a similar range to historical levels for the full year.
API:formulation mix expected around 80:20 with a plus or minus 2-3% range.
Capex guided at INR 20-30 crores per year maintenance. A smaller topical facility may come in FY27; larger capex only for new customer projects.
Working capital intensity expected to be in line with historical levels; inventory days should normalise in FY27 H1.
capex_capacity: Unit 1 is at optimal utilisation at 77%; Unit 2 at 30%; Unit 3 at about 53% (close to 50%).
Unit 4 expected to reach breakeven by next year.
Four units support peak revenue potential of about INR 3,000 crores.
FY26 capex of INR 65 crores included the soft gel facility and modifications for a larger-volume innovator project; CWIP is INR 79.3 crores.
Management expects another INR 50-100 crore capex cycle in 2-3 years and anything above INR 100 crores in 4-5 years.
demand_pricing: Customers shifted from bulk buying to staggered quarterly procurement in H2 FY26, pushing revenue into later quarters.
Management says there is no pricing pressure on new second-source launches (Nystatin, Fusidic Acid); some mature products face price pressure from certain customers, offset by new regions.
Middle East exposure is about INR 50 crores at company level. The major tender was about INR 25 crores (formulation) and remains in abeyance; API supplies to the region are gradually resuming.
US Veterans Affairs tender not finalised and remains on hold; exposure was about INR 25 crores.
Fuel supply shortages in April 2026 were resolved, but LPG and furnace oil prices remain higher; about 10% of total costs are LPG or furnace oil based.
Commenced supplies of APIs to 2 innovator companies; 2 CDMO opportunities in discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Is there visibility on FY27 growth starting in H1, and what size is the growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is a fair amount of visibility in H1 and expects FY27 growth slightly better than the historical ~18%, starting from Q1-Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East exposure and tender size?
qa_highlights.answer: The tender was about INR 25 crores, mostly formulation. Total current Middle East exposure is about INR 50 crores at company level, with API supplies gradually building up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the contribution of the injectable and Stellon losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Injectable expenses were about INR 38-39 crores for FY26, roughly INR 10 crores a quarter. Stellon costs were fully booked in FY26; management said full breakeven for both is more likely in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days rise to 480 from 286?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited staggered customer procurement, shipments pushed into Q1-Q2 FY27, and higher fermentation utilisation with longer cycles. It expects this to moderate in the first half.

qa_highlights.question: Is the formulation inventory at risk of write-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not hold formulation inventory for the Middle East because of shelf-life issues; inventory is mainly API, so write-off risk is low.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan and CWIP of INR 79.3 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance capex is INR 20-30 crores a year. CWIP reflects soft gel and modifications for an innovator project; no major growth capex is planned in H1 FY27.

risks_watch: Recovery depends on Middle East tender timing and the geopolitical situation; management said it has no clarity on timing.
US Veterans Affairs tender remains on hold with no timeline.
Injectable and Stellon breakeven timing is uncertain; management declined to quantify.
Inventory days rose to 480 from 286, with INR 326 crore of inventory versus INR 240 crore; the company expects this to normalise in H1 FY27.
Fuel costs (LPG and furnace oil) remain elevated and could offset the 1-1.5% power savings.
CDMO contribution is small (1-4%) and depends on the pending advanced-stage opportunity.
543960|2026-03.management_tone: Management was confident about FY27 recovery but cautious on specifics: it declined to give EBITDA guidance or a breakeven date for new units, and repeatedly tied the outlook to H1 visibility. Explanations for the miss were detailed and consistent, though the timing-versus-demand argument rests on deferred volumes that have not yet shown up in revenue.
key_quotes: So we have a very good amount of visibility in the first half.
It is important to note, however, that this was not a case of pent-up demand where all deferred supplies could be immediately executed upon resumption.
The factors mentioned above were largely beyond our control and were not related to lower demand, loss of market share or pricing pressure.
So all the expenses that have been there for these 2 entities have been fully booked in the last financial year.

financial_highlights.value: Q4 FY26 and FY26 degrowth of about 8% and 13% respectively

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA margin excl. injectable and Stellon costs

financial_highlights.value: More than INR 414 crores at 31 March 2026; zero debt

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management cites a 1-1.5% EBITDA tailwind from solar/renewable power, partly offset by higher LPG and furnace oil costs (about 10% of total costs), and gives no formal EBITDA margin guidance; FY26 EBITDA margin was about 35% reported, about 39-40% excluding injectable and Stellon costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Unit 1 is at 77%, Unit 2 at 30% and Unit 3 at about 53%, so there is spare capacity; the only new facilities (injectables, soft gel) are already commissioned or under construction, and the next INR 50-100 crore capex cycle is 2-3 years out.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides FY27 growth slightly above the historical ~18% rate, with visibility in H1 and deferred volumes spilling into FY27 after the three-month CDSCO-related European halt and the Middle East and US VA tenders; Stellon first supplies are expected in H1 FY27 with orders in place, but the revenue timing has not yet shown up.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Maintenance capex is guided at INR 20-30 crore a year, no major growth capex is planned in H1 FY27, and utilisation is well below the 80% threshold (Unit 1 at 77%, Unit 2 at 30%, Unit 3 at 53%).

rows.why: FY27 growth is guided slightly above ~18%, but that is only an initial guide, and an upgrade depends on Middle East and VA tender timing, which management says it has no clarity on.

rows.why: FY26 revenue fell 12% (Q4 -24%) and the recovery rests on deferred volumes not yet visible in revenue; the Middle East tender is in abeyance (about INR 25 crore), the US VA tender (about INR 25 crore) is on hold with no timeline, and LPG/furnace oil costs remain high.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Stellon Biotech expects first supplies in H1 FY27 with orders in place under direct US marketing licences; injectable filings are under way for Southeast Asia and Africa; second-source launches (Nystatin, Fusidic Acid) and two innovator API supply starts have begun.

rows.label: Injectables and Stellon breakeven in FY27
rows.why: Injectable expenses were about INR 38-39 crore in FY26 (about INR 10 crore a quarter) and Stellon costs were fully booked in FY26; management says full breakeven for both is more likely in FY27 but declined to quantify.

rows.label: Inventory normalisation in H1 FY27
rows.why: Inventory days rose to 480 from 286 and inventory to INR 326 crore from INR 240 crore as shipments were pushed into Q1-Q2 FY27; management expects this to moderate in the first half.

rows.label: No price growth; mature-product price pressure
rows.why: Management says FY26 API decline was volume-driven with no price growth, and some mature products face price pressure from certain customers, offset by new regions and no pricing pressure on Nystatin and Fusidic Acid second-source launches.

tone.note: Management was confident about a FY27 recovery from H1 visibility and deferred volumes, but cautious on specifics: it gave no EBITDA margin guidance, no breakeven date for injectables or Stellon, and no clarity on Middle East or VA tender timing; analysts pushed on the timing-versus-demand argument

543960|2026-06.headline: Concord Biotech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 26% YoY to INR257 crores, with EBITDA margin at 32% and PAT at INR58 crores.
543960|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue reached INR257 crores (+26% YoY), led by API at INR219 crores (+42%) while formulations fell 23% to INR39 crores, which management attributed to lost Middle East supplies. Exports grew 46% and domestic grew 12%. EBITDA rose 34% to INR82 crores (32% margin, +190 bps), and gross margin was 78.9%. Management said part of the growth was spillover from Q4 FY26 procurement delays, and that the injectable facility and Stellon Biotech are still at a nascent stage.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Revenue INR219 crores, up 42% YoY. Growth reported across immunosuppressants, anti-infectives, oncology and antifungals; anti-infectives and oncology grew faster than immunosuppressants.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR39 crores, down 23% YoY. Management attributed the decline to Middle East customers buying API instead of formulation in Q1; ex-Middle East, domestic double-digit growth in both Intra (nephrology) and INCA (critical care) divisions.

segments.name: CDMO (fermentation)
segments.commentary: Currently about 1-2% of revenue. One product commercialised in animal health (US, ANDA), currently a couple of million dollars in sales; management aims for double-digit share over time.

segments.name: Injectables
segments.commentary: Facility commercialised; utilisation about 5% in the quarter. Own branded generics supplied in-house; contract manufacturing discussions advanced, with some commercial onboarding expected in 2H FY27. Emerging-market sales expected from next year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects growth in FY27 to exceed the company's historical growth rates, citing visibility for coming quarters.
Spillover from Q4 FY26 procurement delays expected to continue into subsequent quarters; not quantified.
Long-term view: INR3,000 crores revenue from existing infrastructure in about 5-6 years, split roughly INR600-700 crores formulations and INR2,200 crores API.
EBITDA margin expected to exceed sales growth in FY27; 40% margin target expected to be reached partly in FY27 and more fully in FY28, dependent on injectable and Stellon ramp-up.
Two to three new product launches planned annually; a couple of advanced-stage products expected to commercialise in coming quarters.
Injectable facility expected to reach emerging-market sales next year after 12-15 month approval processes.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation: Unit 1 about 80% (analyst later cited 78%); Unit 2 about 25% (analyst later cited 55%); Unit 3 about 55% (includes some KSM manufacturing).
Unit 3 has about 160 acres, with only 20-25% of land used; capacity expansion decision expected at around 80-85% utilisation.
Approximately 1,250 m3 (cited as 1,250-metre cube) fermentation capacity; oncology products run in 5,000-litre fermenters at Unit 1.
Injectable facility: WHO GMP set, validation batches completed, customer audits underway; facility can do close to INR600 crores top line; utilisation about 5%.
Softgel facility added in oral solids; Unit 2 formulation facility at Valthera received NDA Uganda and PPB Kenya inspections; Limbasi facility passed ANVISA inspection.
Possible dedicated fermentation capacity for peptides and veterinary products if growth is needed ahead of the 80-85% threshold.
demand_pricing: Wallet share gains in the quarter were primarily price-driven on existing products, based on economies of scale from fermentation capacity; seeds were sown 8-12 months earlier.
Exports up 46% across Europe, Japan, LatAm and the US; US ANDA approvals received for mycophenolate mofetil and tofacitinib tablets.
Nystatin and fusidic acid (launched FY26, Europe-focused, awaiting CEP) cited as growing products with limited competition.
Management reported no customer concerns on the reported proposed US tariff on generics.
Constant-currency context: USD movement about 10-12% YoY; net impact after input costs about 3-5% flowing to EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: How much of growth is normalisation of delayed procurement versus structural gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Some spillover from Q4 FY26 procurement delays contributed; most growth came from new products across all geographies. Similar spillovers are expected in subsequent quarters, though not quantifiable.

qa_highlights.question: Roadmap to INR3,000 crores revenue from existing infrastructure?
qa_highlights.answer: INR600-700 crores from formulations and INR2,200 crores from APIs, expected in about 5-6 years at the current CAGR. Unit 3 has room to expand once utilisation reaches 80-85%.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation and CDMO contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit 1 about 80%, Unit 3 about 55%, Unit 2 about 25%. CDMO is about 1-2% of revenue, with a target of double digits over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic formulations decline?
qa_highlights.answer: The prior-year quarter included Middle East supplies that did not recur. Ex-Middle East, domestic formulations grew double digits in both divisions.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the wallet share gain attributed to pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing advantage from fermentation scale was passed to customers, and margins were held. Softer factors, such as fermentation partnership, were secondary.

qa_highlights.question: When will the injectable facility reach EBITDA breakeven and emerging-market sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Injectable utilisation is about 5%; breakeven utilisation was not given and will be followed up. Emerging-market sales expected next year after a 12-15 month approval process; contract manufacturing sales expected in 2H FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company reach 40% EBITDA margin by end of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating leverage and renewable energy should drive margins above sales growth. Full 40% depends on injectable and Stellon ramp-up, so it may slip into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How can API revenue reach INR2,200 crores without new capacity, given Unit 1 and Unit 2 utilisation?

543963|2026-03.headline: Shelter Pharma FY26 revenue rose 44% to INR 73.13 Cr with PAT of INR 9.03 Cr; management targets INR 200 Cr revenue by FY2030.

543965|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record Rs 3,032 crore (+21.3% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA rose 37.5% to Rs 222 crore, with a record Rs 524 crore of new business wins.

Adjusted EBITDA margin widened 80 bps YoY to 7.3%, driven by the Europe turnaround in ISCS and India volume growth in GFS. Full-year revenue grew 10.1% to Rs 11,003 crore and adjusted PBT rose 166% to Rs 99.3 crore. Management guided ISCS margin to 9.5-10% and group margin to about 7.3-7.4% for FY27, with GFS rates the key swing factor. The CEO-designate's first call also marked the retirement of MD Ravi Viswanathan.

segments.name: GFS (Global Forwarding Solutions)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 748.8 crore (+34.8% YoY) on India ocean freight volumes; FY26 revenue Rs 2,764.1 crore (+11.4%). Margin 2.4% in Q4 on volume growth and cost actions, but freight rates remain under pressure.

543984|2026-03.headline: FY26 total income rose to INR 1,279 crore with 12.3% revenue growth; net debt/EBITDA ~3x (3.07x) and FY27 revenue guided at 10-11%.
543984|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue growth was 12.3% against a 9-11% guidance band, with same-store RevPAR up 9.5%, despite several one-off disruptions that cut revenue by an estimated INR 45-52 crore. Consolidated EBITDA rose 8.8% to INR 463 crore at a 36.2% margin, and the GST slab change weighed on H2 margins. Q4 EBITDA fell 6% YoY to about INR 120 crore, which management attributes to GST, FF&E charges, pre-opening costs and the Middle East conflict hitting March revenue. Net debt fell to INR 1,450 crore after the GIC infusion, and a deferred tax credit of about INR 330 crore lifted reported PAT to about INR 567 crore. Management guided FY27 same-store revenue growth of 9-10% and total revenue growth of 10-11%, and a 38%-plus group margin.

Variable lease payments (1.5-2% of revenue) go through P&L; lease-treatment impact on EBITDA margins is about 150-170 bps higher.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROCE target, net debt/EBITDA path and capex funding for FY31?

Free cash base of about INR 310 crore assumed flat; management assumes no operating leverage and no EBITDA from Navi Mumbai or One Financial District; W Hyderabad and Ingka expected to add INR 400-500 crore EBITDA by FY31.

543984|2026-06.headline: SAMHI Q1 FY27: same-store RevPAR up 9.6% to Rs 5,220 at 79.3% occupancy, while reported EBITDA fell 4% YoY on a one-time base and GST impact.

Same-store revenue grew about 9.1% and same-store RevPAR grew 9.6%, with occupancy up to 79.3% from 74.2%. Reported EBITDA fell about 4% YoY, which management attributes to a one-time Rs 9.2 crore GST impact and a prior-year one-time item; comparable EBITDA margin was about 12.1%. Management also sought a board enabling resolution for a Rs 750 crore capital raise, which drew heavy analyst questioning.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Khanna (Ambit): Why acquire the Itmenaan estate given weak revenue history, how is Leisure capital allocation growing, and what RARE opportunities are being evaluated?

Total RARE capital is about Rs 47 crore, about Rs 60 crore with Itmenaan, and leisure should stay near 10% of capital allocation.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Khanna: How much of FY27 growth is rate versus occupancy, and has July shown a sharp recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said occupancy drives growth in the first six months, with rate recovering in H2 as domestic mix rebalances from 82% toward a higher-premium international mix. July is 'trending far ahead' of Q1 exit, with rate growth now visible, but management declined to give numbers and cautioned one month is not representative.

qa_highlights.question: Jinesh Joshi (PL Capital): Are RARE sign-ups to the Marriott Outdoor Collection program on track, and why must the Rs 750 crore enabling resolution be taken now?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40 of 75 RARE hotels have agreed to join; management said sign-ups are ahead of its expectations and the pace is the issue, with 10-12 hotels on rival platforms. On the resolution, management said it will be taken every year so the Board can act in time; no specific deal is identified.

qa_highlights.question: Vikas Ahuja (Antique): Is the ADR slowdown (about 2.6-2.7% growth) due to West Asia disruption and Marriott-led inventory, and is occupancy at about 79% a tactical rate trade-off?

qa_highlights.question: Vikas Ahuja: Why an equity-linked enabling resolution rather than debt, given the investment surplus discussed at the Analyst Day?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the resolution is a general enabling step to respond to unknown problems or opportunities and keep the balance sheet strong. It added that the Rs 1,200 crore to Rs 3,000 crore revenue path has no assumed acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Shrinjana Mittal (MS Capital): Is upper upscale underperforming midscale because of downtrading, and why is GST drag above 2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw ARR growth was about 3.5%-4% across segments, and midscale RevPAR grew 13.7% at 81.3% occupancy versus 78.4% for upper upscale. GST drag is larger in Q1 and Q2 from volume sales below Rs 7,500, is lower in H2, and is about 2% per management.

qa_highlights.question: Vaibhav Muley (Haitong): Why did F&B growth slow to about 4%, and what is the GIC partnership scope?
qa_highlights.answer: F&B grew about 3.5%-4% against room revenue growth of 14%, due to a shift to domestic guests (80%-83%), a Bangalore restaurant renovation, and West Asia-related event cancellations moved to July-August. GIC has a right to 35% of new upscale deals post-JV, with no talks on existing assets; Navi Mumbai and W Hyderabad are 100% SAMHI-owned.

qa_highlights.question: Prashant Biyani (Elara): Timing for Grand Hyatt pre-positioning at Hyatt Regency Pune, W Hyderabad and Courtyard Pune openings?
qa_highlights.answer: Grand Hyatt repositioning is not being pursued. W Hyderabad is targeted for full operation in 2H FY28 or calendar 2027, with regulatory delays possible. Courtyard Pune public areas and guest room renovation is deferred to about April 2027 for 5-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Gupta (Asit C Mehta): How does RARE revenue recognition work, and what are RARE's revenue, margin and EBITDA targets?
qa_highlights.answer: RARE earns booking commission and, in some hotels, higher revenue share akin to franchise fees; hotel room revenue stays with owners. Management guides Rs 100-120 crore top line at about 35% margin and Rs 35-40 crore EBITDA once stabilised in about 1.5-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Viraj Mahadevia (Moneygrow): Can RARE ROCE double the group's roughly 10%, and why is EBITDA flat while PBT is up 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RARE could reach 5x group ROCE and target 50%-55% ROCE, with about 95% EBITDA-to-PBT flow-through and no finance cost. On EBITDA, it cited the Rs 9 crore one-time other income in the prior-year base and about Rs 9 crore GST drag, with YoY relief from Q3.

segments.name: TaxSpanner (to be rebranded Z.tax)

segments.commentary: Added 83,262 domestic connections in FY26; Diu and Gir Somnath has crossed 10,000 domestic PNG connections.

segments.name: PNG Commercial and Industrial
segments.commentary: Added 496 commercial and 223 industrial connections in FY26. Industrial volume is affected by the Fatehgarh Sahib NGT order and gas cuts; management expects industrial growth of 23-24% in FY27 if the order is implemented.

segments.name: GA-wise: Banaskantha (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: About 49% of FY26 revenue and 47% of volume, with about INR 420 crore invested; CNG-centric with higher margins.

segments.name: GA-wise: Fatehgarh Sahib (Punjab)
segments.commentary: About 36% of FY26 revenue (mainly industrial PNG) and 39% of volume, with about INR 200 crore invested.

segments.name: GA-wise: Namakkal and Trichy (Tamil Nadu)
segments.commentary: About INR 257 crore gross block invested to date; FY27 capex planned at INR 150-180 crore. Management expects around 90% CNG volume mix initially, moving toward 70:20 CNG to PNG over one to two years. 71 TNSTC PNG buses running with 50 more due in May 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth expected at 30%+ over FY26 in management's words, with volume crossing 250 MMSCM 'or maybe much more'; the CEO also said 'double-digit' growth, and the CFO said 14-15% was not out of line.
EBITDA per SCM to improve 10-15% in FY27 from current levels of more than INR 5 per SCM; CFO guided to INR 5.3-5.5 per SCM.
Gross margin and EBITDA margin expected to be maintained in the 25-26% gross margin range, subject to how the Gulf situation unfolds.
Peak debt for FY27 expected at INR 70-80 crore, against about INR 49 crore of term loans at end March 2026 and a INR 45 crore sanctioned term loan.
Namakkal and Trichy capex funded from IPO proceeds (about INR 194 crore available at end March 2026); other GAs funded from internal accruals plus the term loan.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR 184.35 crore, including INR 81.33 crore in Q4 FY26 alone.
Cumulative investment to date: Banaskantha about INR 420 crore, Fatehgarh Sahib about INR 200 crore, Namakkal and Trichy INR 257 crore gross block.
FY27 target: 36 new CNG stations (39 added in FY26); Namakkal and Trichy capex of INR 150-180 crore.
Network of 6,695 inch-km pipeline as of FY26; about 35% of the cascade fleet is Type 3 cylinders. Trichy bus stand CNG station planned.
First LNG dispensing facility commissioned at Rasipuram (Namakkal and Trichy GA).
demand_pricing: Gas cost pressure from APM ceiling rising to USD 7/MMBTU (from USD 6.75) and higher NWG-linked prices; management says the increase was passed through to CNG, industrial and commercial customers from April.
HPHT gas price via IGX reduced from USD 9.72 to USD 8.92 per MMBTU, offsetting some cost pressure.
CNG sales for April 2026 were in line with budget after the price pass-through, per management.
Fatehgarh Sahib industrial supply cut to 80%, then 65% and 55% of contracted quantity during the Gulf disruption, now restored to 80%; demand destruction is occurring in industrial.

Namakkal and Trichy: CNG demand nearly doubled YoY after the OMC CNG model rollout; 92-95% of new three-wheeler sales are CNG; CNG share of passenger vehicle additions above 15% in that GA (vs over 40% in Banaskantha).
Management says EV penetration in its GAs is negligible; CNG auto and taxi demand continues to grow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 given the Gulf crisis and sourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: gross margin of 25-26% has risen YoY; management expects margins to hold in that range, depending on how the situation unfolds.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profit fall from Q3 to Q4 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a INR 1.34 crore JV receivable provision (Ni Hon Cylinders) and a INR 2.86 crore bank charge, both expected to reverse in Q1 FY27. The analyst noted PBT of about INR 17.7 crore in Q4 vs INR 22 crore in Q3, still a gap after adding back these items.

qa_highlights.question: When will the NGT order for Fatehgarh Sahib be implemented?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not pushing for immediate enforcement given demand destruction and gas cuts; it will press PPCB and CPCB once supply stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance for FY27 volume and EBITDA per SCM?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth expected above 30% (to above 250 MMSCM); EBITDA per SCM to rise 10-15% from current levels of more than INR 5.

qa_highlights.question: How much CNG is spot-sourced?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about 4% of CNG volume was spot purchase in FY26; about 40% comes from APM/NWG gas, and the rest from long-term contracts and HPHT bids.

qa_highlights.question: What funds the Namakkal and Trichy capex?
qa_highlights.answer: IPO proceeds of about INR 194 crore at end March 2026; other GAs are funded through internal accruals and a term loan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the treasury income and cash flow treatment?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury income from liquid and overnight funds was about INR 68 lakh in Q4 FY26, per management, versus about INR 2 crore cited by the analyst as the quarter figure.

risks_watch: Gas sourcing: APM ceiling increase, NWG price rise and Gulf supply disruption could pressure margins if pass-through slows; management says CNG and domestic are insulated.
Fatehgarh Sahib industrial volumes: NGT-linked restrictions, demand destruction and gas cuts; implementation timing is uncertain.
Q1 FY27 must show reversal of the INR 1.34 crore JV provision and INR 2.86 crore bank charge, as management stated.
Execution of 36 CNG station additions and INR 150-180 crore Namakkal and Trichy capex; the new Tamil Nadu government's policy stance was flagged as a source of difficulty.
Employee cost rise (headcount from 214 to 256) and a INR 60 lakh labour code provision; license fee at 2% of net revenue.
Management declined to give firm numeric guidance, citing an evolving situation; several outlook figures were given as ranges and 'maybe' targets.
544004|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the FY26 operating record and the CNG and network expansion, but cautious on near-term guidance, which management described as hard to predict given the Gulf disruption. Management was defensive when questioned on the Q4 profit decline, attributing it to one-time items, and gave a hedged, range-based outlook.
key_quotes: So the gross margins that we see, they are in the range of 25% to 26%. They have increased from previous year.
We are expecting that in all four segments, we will be growing more than 20% year-on-year.
CNG remains the largest contributor to the volume, accounting for 61% of total operational revenue in FY'26.

rows.why: Network goes from 150 to about 186 stations with 36 targeted in FY27 after 39 added in FY26, and INR 150-180 crore Namakkal/Trichy capex is planned with IPO proceeds of about INR 194 crore available at end March 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volume guided above 250 MMSCM against 223.67 MMSCM in FY26 (about 12%+ on the stated floor, 30%+ per management), backed by 36 new CNG stations and Namakkal/Trichy CNG demand nearly doubling YoY, offset by industrial demand destruction.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY26 capex was INR 184.35 crore (INR 81.33 crore in Q4 alone) and management guided a further INR 150-180 crore for Namakkal and Trichy in FY27, so further capex disclosures are expected, though the brief does not give a utilisation figure.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided volume above 250 MMSCM (30%+ growth) but also said 'double-digit' and the CFO said 14-15%, so the range is wide and the upper end depends on how CNG demand holds in Namakkal and Trichy, where CNG demand nearly doubled YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gas supply was cut to 55-65% of contracts for industrial customers during the Gulf disruption (now 80%), and industrial volume growth of 23-24% in FY27 depends on the Fatehgarh Sahib NGT order being implemented.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First LNG dispensing facility was commissioned at Rasipuram and 50 more TNSTC PNG buses are due in May 2026, but no new product launch programme was discussed.

rows.label: Peak debt capped at INR 70-80 crore in FY27
rows.why: Total debt fell from INR 140 crore in FY25 to INR 72 crore at end FY26 with net cash of INR 170 crore, and management guided peak FY27 debt of INR 70-80 crore against about INR 49 crore of term loans at end March 2026.

rows.label: Reversal of Q4 one-time items in Q1 FY27
rows.why: Management said the INR 1.34 crore JV receivable provision and INR 2.86 crore bank charge would be reversed or resolved in Q1 FY27, which would lift the INR 17.7 crore Q4 PBT against INR 22 crore in Q3.

rows.label: Fatehgarh Sahib NGT order implementation
rows.why: Management is not pushing for immediate enforcement given demand destruction and gas cuts, and will press PPCB and CPCB once supply stabilises, so timing is uncertain and industrial growth of 23-24% depends on it.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY26 record, CNG network growth and Namakkal/Trichy demand, but cautious and range-based on FY27 guidance given the Gulf gas disruption and was defensive on the Q4 profit dip; analysts pressed on the Q4 PBT gap and treasury income.

544004|2026-06.headline: IRM Energy Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR 326 crore, with EBITDA ex-other income up 139% YoY to INR 62 crore and PAT of INR 34 crore.
544004|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with volumes at an all-time high of 50.9 MMSCM (up 8% YoY). Margin expansion was attributed to sourcing (HPHT and long-term contracts priced below spot), price realisations, and cost control, with management stating there were no one-time items. Industrial PNG volumes were hit by a 9 March 2026 government notification that cut industrial gas allocation to around 80%. Management guided FY27 EBITDA of INR 7-8/SCM for the remaining three quarters and says the current margin level will likely moderate.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY27 capex about INR 67 crore

segments.name: Banaskantha (GA)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 48% of Q1 volume and about 46% of profitability; CNG is about 51% of vehicle sales here. Station additions limited to 10-15 in FY27 as the GA is nearing saturation.

segments.name: Fatehgarh Sahib (GA)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 38% of profitability. CNG penetration only 6%; volumes hit by the industrial gas cut linked to the NGT order. Plans for 2 new stations in FY27.

segments.name: Diu & Gir Somnath (GA)
segments.commentary: CNG is 60% of vehicle sales; contributed about 8-9% of profitability. Entire commercial segment converted to PNG, with commercial connections now on PNG. Plans for about 5 new stations in FY27.

segments.name: Namakkal & Trichy (GA)
segments.commentary: Q1 volume about 6 MMSCM, up 102% YoY from 2.84 MMSCM; contributed about 5% of profitability. FY27 volume guidance 25-30 MMSCM (vs 14.2 MMSCM in FY26); about 15-17 new stations planned; more than 80 TNSTC buses running, with a target of 200+ buses.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA expected at about INR 7-8/SCM for the next three quarters; management later indicated overall FY27 around INR 7/SCM and said the 19% EBITDA margin may not be sustained.
Revenue growth of about 25% in FY27 guided; management said a safe range is around 20% or more.
Volume growth of 10-12% in FY27, with total volume targeted at about 250 MMSCM by year-end (FY26: 224 MMSCM).
FY27 capex of about INR 250 crore in total (INR 150 crore for Namakkal and Trichy, INR 50 crore each for Banaskantha and Diu & Gir Somnath / Fatehgarh).
Long-term goal of 20-25% revenue CAGR over the next five years.
Management said same-level performance as Q1 will not be repeated every quarter; performance will be subdued going forward, though it expects QoQ and YoY improvement.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR 67 crore; cumulative capex about INR 1,090 crore.
FY27 capex plan about INR 250 crore; management said it will not exceed this, of which INR 150 crore is for Namakkal and Trichy.
CNG stations at 153 as of 30 June 2026 (up 37% YoY), with 564 dispensing points across four GAs.
Station model mix: franchisee (DODO), OMC and company-operated; the company is moving away from daughter booster and LNG-based models toward online stations.
Diu & Gir Somnath: tap-off from GSPL pipeline and hookup with IOC and GAIL in progress; currently drawing LNG from HPCL's Chhara terminal.
demand_pricing: Pricing: Realisations up about 15% YoY and QoQ per an analyst's calculation (not disputed by management); management said price hikes are linked to sourcing cost and it will not pass on further hikes now that Brent is cooling.

Sourcing mix in Q1 FY27: APM and NWG about 32-33% (APM 21%, NWG 11%), HPHT about 35%, long-term (Reliance, GAIL and others) about 32%, CBG blending 1%, spot about 1%. Q1 FY26 was APM 27%, long-term 27%, HPHT 38%.
HPHT gas at about USD 9/MMBtu versus spot of USD 14-20; industrial volumes benefit from GSPC and Shell long-term contracts running to 2030.
Industrial PNG volumes were hit by the 9 March 2026 notification (about 80% allocation); CNG and domestic/commercial PNG not affected.
Customer base: 86,590 domestic PNG (+13% YoY), 589 commercial (+36% YoY), 228 industrial (+5% YoY).
Management said it is a price taker; competitors and alternative fuel prices are high, supporting margins.

qa_highlights.question: Were there one-time items behind the sharp rise in EBITDA per SCM, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no one-time items; gains came from pricing, gas sourcing and opex optimisation. It guided FY27 EBITDA of INR 7-8/SCM for the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sourcing mix and how has it changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27: APM+NWG about 32%, HPHT about 35%, long-term about 32%. Q1 FY26 was APM 27%, long-term 27%, HPHT 38%; Q4 FY26 APM about 26%.

qa_highlights.question: Namakkal and Trichy volumes and FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 volume about 6 MMSCM (up 102% YoY); FY27 target 25-30 MMSCM, towards the upper end, vs 14.2 MMSCM in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan for FY27 and station additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR 250 crore; stations to be added: 10-15 in Banaskantha, 15-17 in Namakkal and Trichy, about 5 in Diu & Gir Somnath, 2 in Fatehgarh Sahib.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the NGT order in Fatehgarh Sahib?
qa_highlights.answer: The NGT order (February 2026) has not been enforced by the Punjab pollution board; supply cuts began 9 March. Management expects ramp-up once enforced and says new industries must use natural gas to get consents.

qa_highlights.question: Is the promoter license fee a concern and how might it change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a 2% license fee disclosed in the IPO document, not profit to promoters, worth about INR 20-25 crore for the year and already included in PAT; it cannot promise the rate will stay unchanged.

risks_watch: Sustainability of EBITDA per SCM: management guided INR 7-8/SCM for the next three quarters and said the 19% EBITDA margin may not hold, versus Q1 at about INR 10/SCM.

Sourcing dependence: HPHT (about 35%) and long-term industrial contracts (GSPC, Shell to 2030) underpin margins; HPHT supply runs only to a stated date and spot exposure is about 1%, so future gas price moves could compress margins.

Industrial PNG volumes: the 9 March 2026 notification capped allocation at about 80%; Fatehgarh Sahib ramp-up depends on Punjab pollution board enforcement of the NGT order, which has not happened yet.

Namakkal and Trichy execution: FY27 volume target of 25-30 MMSCM (vs 14.2 MMSCM in FY26) depends on spot LPG/LNG supply from IOCL, BPCL, Kochi terminal until GAIL and tap-off lines arrive, which management says takes 9-18 months.

Promoter license fee: 2% of revenue paid to promoters, about INR 20-25 crore for the year; management could not promise the rate will remain unchanged, and minority shareholders have raised the question of a ceiling or absolute cap.
key_quotes: We can say that for industrial, we had two long -term contracts, one is the GSPC, the other is Shell.
Saket, it'll be highly optimistic to say that same performance, as scale up as in Q1, will be repeated every quarter. But it will be definitely subdued going forward, not up to this extent.
We hope and pray, but we can't guarantee 19% always.
As of now, I can't promise you whether this will continue at a reduced rate or same rate or maybe abolished altogether.
