544008|2026-03.headline: Max Estates FY26 presales hit INR5,305 crore, second straight year above INR5,000 crore, with Q4 bookings of INR3,300 crore the strongest quarter ever.
544008|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 residential presales of INR5,305 crore and collections of INR1,578 crore (up 61% YoY), with Q4 bookings of INR3,300 crore driven by Estate 105 and Max One launches. Total revenue from launched projects yet to be recognised stands at INR16,310 crore, of which INR12,500 crore is already sold, with embedded PBT of INR4,200-4,900 crore. Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR200 crore, PBT INR23 crore, and net debt about INR100 crore. Management declined to give FY27 presales guidance, citing a moderating NCR market and West Asia-related cost and sentiment pressure.

strongest quarter ever, driven by Estate 105 and Max One

of which INR970 crore is lease rental discounting

segments.commentary: Fully sold, cumulative presales INR2,700 crore, collections INR1,100 crore to date. Delivery on track for CY2027; Phase 1 at 35th-36th floor slab.

segments.commentary: Cumulative presales INR4,800 crore, collections INR1,600 crore; ground floor complete for Towers 1-2, first-floor slab for Towers 3 and 5.

segments.commentary: Estate 105 launched 20 March 2026, about INR1,800 crore sold in 10 days; GDV doubled from INR3,000 crore to INR6,000 crore with serviced apartments, Phase 2 in FY28. Max One contributed INR1,400 crore to FY26 presales after RERA approval in March 2026; GDV over INR3,200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will management give FY27 presales guidance and launch pipeline by GDV and timing?

qa_highlights.question: How is demand across Terraces (about INR2.5 crore tickets) and Max One (INR20-25 crore tickets)?
qa_highlights.answer: Sentiment cautious across all segments, longer decision cycles, but no complete slowdown; more end-user demand coming through.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 rental income rise about 43% when leased area and rents look flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly an Ind AS rent equalisation adjustment after rent-free periods; rentals reset on 3+3+3 leases with 15% escalation every 3 years. FY26 rental income about INR155 crore; peak-occupancy run-rate for existing assets about INR210 crore over 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RERA status and why did Sector 59 GDV rise about 30%?

qa_highlights.question: What are the Max One cash flows and the inherited sales economics?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1.4 million sq ft of 2.5 million sq ft was sold by the erstwhile developer; company expects about INR550-600 crore incremental receipts on the INR1,221 crore base. qa_highlights.question: FY27 collections, deployment and operating cash flow?

qa_highlights.question: How is the balance sheet funded, and is debt used for land?
qa_highlights.answer: No land acquired from debt; residential RERA account surplus about INR1,200 crore sufficient for construction; commercial equity in place and construction finance to be taken out via LRD after leasing; LRD cover from lease rentals at 100% occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: How are inflation and cost pressures being managed?

544027|2026-09.headline: Fedbank Q2 FY27: PAT rose 63% YoY to INR130.8 crore and ROA hit a record 2.8%, but GNPA rose to 1.8% on gold-loan repayment-model transition.
544027|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's strongest quarter on profitability: PAT of INR130.8 crore (up 14.3% QoQ, 63% YoY), ROA of 2.8% and ROE of 17%, both records. AUM grew 37% YoY to INR22,035 crore, with gold AUM up 77% YoY to INR11,917 crore. Management attributed the rise in GNPA (1.6% to 1.8%) and Stage II (2.7% to 3.6%) mainly to the shift from bullet to periodic interest-due gold loans, which it called technical. Management flagged intense gold-loan competition in Q2 and said it would keep growing and guiding for Q3 and Q4.

capex_capacity: 74 gold branches opened in Q2, taking the total to 831; at least 150 more planned in H2 FY27, with about 100 gold branches cited.

Opex as a share of average total assets was 4.9% in Q2 vs 4.8% in Q1 and 5.5% in FY26, reflecting full-quarter branch and headcount costs.
AUM per gold branch rose from INR8 crore to INR16 crore (cited in the Q&A); management said cost-to-income should fall as AUM per branch grows.
demand_pricing: Gold-loan competition was heightened in Q2 across geographies, with NBFCs using yield, LTV and lending-practice strategies. Gold yield fell about 10 bps over Q1 and Q2 combined, per management. Management said bank competition is in a different yield segment.

Gold LTV is 68% overall; customers take the maximum LTV available (75-80% in most cases), and the portfolio has a mix of 71-74%. Income-generating loans (about 20% of disbursements) are priced on cash flow with LTV caps of 75-85%.
ST LAP origination yield has fallen from 16.1% to 14.9% over 5-6 quarters; management attributed this to state mix and competition, not ticket size, and said yields should improve in Q3.
Approval rates in ST LAP have recovered to mid-40% from about 30% after BRE tightening.
Medium-ticket LAP is partner-driven, runs at 11.5-12.5% yield, and is a steady, profitable business.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company manage gold loan growth and yields given rising competition from NBFCs and banks? Is an income-generating loan product ready?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 competition was the most intense yet, and it chose a balance of growth and yield. Gold yield fell only about 10 bps across Q1 and Q2. The IGL product has been live since April, with LTV structured at 75-85% based on cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Stage II and III rises in gold: is this the new normal, and will it deteriorate further in Q3-Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the Stage II rise technical, since most gold loans are 2.5-3 month tenor products and customers are moving to periodic interest. It said the change could take 1-2 more quarters to settle, and it declined to give a Stage II number. CFO said there have been no auction losses in six years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ST LAP yields fall, and how much will they rise with rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall mainly to state mix, not ticket size, and said Q3 yields will be higher than Q2 with higher disbursements. ST LAP ticket sizes have moved up to INR7-8 lakh, with a minimum of INR8 lakh now.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 AUM and ROE guidance be raised given H1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept AUM growth guidance at 20-25% for FY27 and said ROE could see upside. Target is ROA 3% and ROE about 18%. Management said upside depends on gold prices.

qa_highlights.question: How will rate hikes affect spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said pass-through will be limited, with the company absorbing part of the shock. Offsets will come from opex and credit cost. Fixed-rate borrowings are 33%, MCLR-linked 24%, and about 58% of the loan book is short-tenor gold loans that reprice at maturity.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for the mortgage business and its ROA as mix shifts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gold ROA will be maintained, not expanded, as AUM per branch rises and cost-to-income falls. ST LAP ROA is expected to move toward gold ROA over time, and the gold mix will not drop in the next cycle.

544044|2026-03.headline: India Shelter Q4FY26: AUM up 29% YoY to Rs 11,044 crore, PAT Rs 138 crore (+27% YoY), ROE 17.6%, Stage-3 down to 1.2%.

Asset quality improved, with 30+ DPD down 100 bps QoQ to 4%, gross Stage-3 at 1.2% and net Stage-3 at 0.9%. Management guided to a more cautious 25-30% AUM growth for the next three years, with disbursement growth of about 20% in FY27, citing the macro environment (LPG disruption, geopolitical stress). Management framed a Rs 30,000 crore AUM target by 2030 as achievable at 27-28% CAGR.

544044|2026-06.headline: India Shelter Q1 FY27: PAT up 23% YoY to INR 143 crore and ROE 17.5%, but Stage 3 rose to 1.5% and reported AUM growth slowed to 24%.
544044|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR 143 crore (23% YoY, 4% QoQ) with ROE of 17.5% and net worth of INR 3,353 crore. Gross AUM reached INR 11,284 crore, up 24% YoY, after a one-time switch to recognising disbursements on cheque realisation rather than handover, which cut reported disbursements to INR 641 crore. Stage 3 rose to 1.5% (up 30 bps) on seasonal and early-bucket delinquency, and management guided Stage 3 to stabilise in Q2 and recover from Q3. Management reiterated FY27 guidance for 25-30% AUM growth, 40-50 bps credit cost, more than 6% spreads and 40-45 branch additions, though analysts questioned the credit trend and the disbursement ask rate.

stable QoQ; marginal cost of funds 7.9%

Around 1,000 collection employees across 300+ branches; total headcount about 4,700-4,800, with about 160 added in Q1 across collections and head office (AI and tech).

Loan book: about 15% variable, 35% semi-variable and 50% fixed rate; fixed rate carries about a 50 bps premium over variable.
guidance_outlook: AUM growth of 25-30% for FY27, reiterated despite Q1 AUM growth of 24%; management expects catch-up over the remaining nine months.
Credit cost of about 40-50 bps for FY27; management aims for about 50 bps in Q1 and Q2.
Spreads to be maintained above 6% in the medium term; incremental spreads are higher than portfolio spreads.
Branch additions of about 40-45 in FY27.
Stage 3 expected to stay around the Q1 level (about 1.5%) in Q2 and fall from Q3 as SARFAESI actions take effect; 30+ DPD expected to decline from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% AUM growth guidance still achievable given the cheque-realisation disbursement change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the change is one-time and disbursement growth above 20% is still expected, supported by July's INR 400 crore; AUM growth of 25-30% is retained.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Stage 3 and 30+ DPD rise, and is it company-specific?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to seasonality and stress in the self-employed, sub-INR 7 lakh ticket cohort (above 2% Stage 3 versus 1.4-1.45% three years ago), and to the cohort's 16%+ yields. It said there was nothing internal, and that April collections were 96.2-96.4% and June slightly above 97%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company hold credit cost at 50 bps with Stage 2+3 at multi-year highs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of holding 50 bps, citing low LGD on this cohort and management overlays. Stage 3 is expected to stay flat in Q2, with recovery from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no branch addition in Q1 and why is disbursement growth only about 18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said branch openings are phased by strategy, with most of FY27's 40-45 coming from Q2. It said peers' Q1 numbers were on a different base and that the full-year target is what matters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is incremental yield up 30 bps while incremental cost of funds is stable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bankers are asking 20-25 bps higher cost of funds, with the overall impact limited to about 10 bps, so the company is passing on some cost to new disbursements. Incremental yield is 14.9%.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the gap in the Q1 FY26 AUM base?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap is about INR 450 crore of co-lending book, which was not previously included in AUM. From March 2026 it is included, so the correct YoY AUM growth is 24%.

544045|2026-03.headline: DOMS Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18.7% to INR604 crore, but West Asia raw-material inflation (15-20%) against only 4-5% price pass-through means Q1 FY27 margins will be under pressure.
544045|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 21.6% to INR2,326.4 crore and EBITDA rose 15.5% to INR402.6 crore, with EBITDA margin at 17.3% versus 18.2% in FY25. Q4 revenue grew 18.7% to INR604 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 16.7% from 17.3%, partly from baby hygiene seasonality and higher e-commerce costs at Uniclan. Management said raw-material costs have risen about 15-17% on average since the West Asia conflict, against pricing actions of roughly 4-5%, and expects Q1 FY27 margins to be slightly under pressure year-on-year. FY27 capex is guided at INR250-275 crore.

Pricing: about 4-5% realised increase so far, taken mainly by cutting channel margins and schemes/discounts, applied across products. Management is avoiding aggressive MRP hikes to protect shelf space and market share.

Competition: Chinese and Vietnamese imports are a factor. A weaker rupee against the RMB makes imports costlier, which management sees as a share-gain opportunity. Natural hedge from USD-denominated imports and exports.

qa_highlights.question: Was Q4 core stationery growth (about 19%) driven by channel stocking ahead of price rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no channel stocking; primary and secondary sales are monitored closely. Growth reflected back-to-school demand. Price increases of about 4-5% were passed on across products.

qa_highlights.question: Could EBITDA margins fall below the 16.5-17.5% band if the crude-driven inflation persists?

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin compress while gross margin held steady in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin was steady. The compression came from higher selling, distribution and digital marketing costs as Uniclan's e-commerce mix grew, along with weaker fixed-cost absorption in baby hygiene.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue guidance and does it include the new plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated revenue growth is guided at 17-20% for FY27. Management confirmed this includes the new 45-acre plant capacity ramping from H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did capex guidance rise, and how is it funded?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase reflects new land parcels near Umargam and Jammu plus some cost inflation. Management said capex will be funded mainly from internal accruals, with room for prudent additional debt; FY26 free cash flow was limited.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR850-1,000 crore total for the 45-acre project separate from Phase 1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 45-acre project total (land, buildings and plant) is INR850-1,000 crore over about 3 more years. The INR292 crore FY26 capex is at company level and spans several projects.

544057|2026-06.headline: Happy Forgings Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% to Rs.449 crore and PAT 39.2% to Rs.91 crore, with EBITDA margin at 31.3%.
544057|2026-06.overview: Record quarterly revenue and profit, driven by 23.1% volume growth and 3.2% higher realisations to Rs.253/kg. EBITDA rose 39.3% to Rs.141 crore, margin up about 275 bps YoY, the fourth straight quarter above 30%. Management says customer price revisions are partly in Q1 (about 30%) and will fully reflect from Q2. Exports were hit by transit delays, with the domestic CV business up about 18%.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicles

segments.name: Farm equipment
segments.commentary: 32% of revenue; grew mid-20s. Domestic up over 20%; exports grew despite weak US and Europe tractor demand. Export share about 5% of revenue.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: 16% of revenue; around 50% growth in both domestic and export. Export share about 9% of revenue. Drivers cited: power generation, wind, railways, oil and gas, digital infrastructure.

segments.name: Off-highway
segments.commentary: 11% of revenue; over 40% growth in both domestic and export. Domestic construction equipment up about 9%. Export share about 5% of revenue.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: About 8% of revenue; growth over 70%, domestic over 40%, exports more than doubled as earlier-secured orders began executing. Export share about 8% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth trajectory hold across industrial, export and PV, and can the high gross and EBITDA margins sustain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to strength across CV, farm, PV; a ~Rs.950 crore order book; and new high-realisation products. It said the last price increase was three years ago, supporting margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the price-revision benefit flow from Q2, and is it permanent?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% came in Q1. Domestic: 2% taken in Q1 versus 4.5-5% total, with OEMs passing on from Q2. Increases are on a three-year-old base and described as permanent; currency gains supported exports.

qa_highlights.question: Will solar benefit come in Q4 FY27 and can margins stay above 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar expected on stream from January, with some generation in Q4 and connection through April. Management is confident of upwards of 30% EBITDA margin, citing a 1-1.5% power benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CV revenue grow only ~7% against ~10% industry production growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic CV grew ~18% against ~10% production growth; exports fell ~12% because DDP contracts (Europe, Turkey) saw about a month of deliveries delayed by transit issues.

qa_highlights.question: What is the freight cost impact and recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Container costs rose from about USD 2,000 to USD 6,000. About 75% of contracts are pass-through; company expects a 15-20% hit and is negotiating recovery of about USD 4,500 per container.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export mix by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximate export share of revenue: CV ~7%, PV ~8%, farm ~5%, off-highway ~5%, industrial ~9%.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the Rs.950 crore order book and the Rs.650 crore capex, and plant-level margins for the new industrial line?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book roughly 35-40% industrial, 25-30% PV, 25-30% CV, rest off-highway/farm; 60% export, 40% domestic. New heavy-line gross margins expected around 60-65% with EBITDA about 50% of gross; plant-level margins not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: receivable and inventory days as of June 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days improved with no big change; inventory days about 50 as of date; overall working-capital days improved.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 guidance be revised given strong Q1 volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is high-teen volume growth and it should perform better than that, without giving a revised number.

qa_highlights.question: Asset turns and high base in PV and CV as capex comes on stream in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not worried about a temporary six-month to one-year dip in asset turns, since capacity is being built for future growth; PV growth is from two to three customers with customer acquisition ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Inorganic plans and funding of growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Open to acquisitions and JVs, mainly for technology in energy and aerospace; cautious on expensive valuations in farm/CV. Growth to be funded largely by internal accruals, possibly with a one-year bridge loan for LCs.

544058|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6% YoY to INR162 crore with EBITDA flat at INR42 crore; management guides FY27 to flat store count and mid-single-digit same-store growth at best.
544058|2026-03.overview: Credo Brands (Mufti) reported Q4 FY26 revenue up 6% YoY to INR162 crore, with gross margin of 58.8% and EBITDA flat at INR42 crore (25.6% margin) as advertising was stepped up to about 8% of revenue. FY26 revenue was flat at INR592 crore, with EBITDA of INR154 crore (26% margin). The company closed 24 stores and opened 7 in the quarter, reducing the network by 17. Management said FY27 is a consolidation year with roughly 20 openings and 20 closures, with ad spend rising to 8-10% of revenue and margins likely lower.

segments.commentary: Online channel is about 9% of revenue, of which the company's own platform is about 5%. Website business grew about 75% YoY in FY26; online EBITDA margin is lower because it is still discount-driven.

Advertising and branding spend to rise to about 8-10% of revenue; Raman KV's 9-10% framing was confirmed as the broad direction, but not fixed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the store growth and revenue outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About 20 openings and 20 closures, so the store count stays flat. Management would be happy with mid-single-digit same-store growth, but visibility is poor.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 margins hold at 26%?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The CFO said FY27 EBITDA margin may be about 23-24% because marketing spend is rising. Gross margin is expected in the 56-58% range.

qa_highlights.question: How has the debtor-days position changed and is it overdue?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtor days are in line with the business model and may move 5-10%. Receivables are not overdue, and the company expects to stay structurally above some peers.

qa_highlights.question: Will ad spend fall to 4-5% in FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not say. Ad spend should pay back more before it is escalated further, and it will respond to market conditions.

qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said FY26 gross margin expansion was mainly product mix. Management said it will pass costs through, with no forward hedging, and sees the 56-58% range holding.

544067|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 31% to INR1,630 crore and Q4 revenue grew 42% to INR447.8 crore; management guides to 20%+ volume growth in FY27.
544067|2026-03.overview: Innova Captab reported its highest-ever annual performance, with FY26 consolidated revenue of INR1,630 crore (+31% YoY) and Q4 revenue of INR447.8 crore (+42% YoY). Growth was led by the CDMO business (INR1,133 crore, +24% for FY26) and Branded Generics (INR497 crore, +51%), with the Jammu facility's first full year of ramp-up a major contributor. FY26 EBITDA rose to INR250.3 crore (15.4% margin) from INR198.2 crore, while PAT grew 10% to INR140.9 crore. Management said Jammu is near EBITDA breakeven and expects it to turn EBITDA-positive in the coming quarter.

segments.name: Branded Generics
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR497 crore (+51%); Q4 INR133 crore (+46%). Domestic is trade generics, roughly 70% domestic and 30-35% exports per management; not tracked by geography at segment level.

segments.name: Jammu facility
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR300 crore revenue in FY26; Q4 exit run rate above INR90 crore. Management says EBITDA is near breakeven and expects EBITDA-positive in the next quarter.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR240 crore; export regulated markets (Canada, UK, Europe, Australia); margin above company average per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RAC utilisation level in FY26?

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Delhi factory and Pune and Kolkata warehouses were already commissioned this year, and management said it is comfortable with current capex and that the infrastructure supports above INR 100 crore revenue, so no new capacity was flagged for the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: April-May sales are flat YoY, customers are holding back orders, and management guides 25-30% annual growth only if geopolitics normalise; the only concrete backing is about INR 1.5 crore of airport orders.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said there are no FY27 capex plans and it is quite comfortable with current capex; utilisation was not disclosed, and 10% of capacity is affected by RM and LPG shortages rather than full use.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 revenue of INR 69 crore missed the INR 85 crore internal expectation, and management declined to confirm the INR 115 crore FY27 figure, with flat demand in April-May.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY26 missed INR 85 crore by about INR 16 crore, LPG cuts were about two months, PP is up about 60%, and fuel costs are rising 10-15%, so FY27 growth could fall short of the 25-30% aspiration.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Roto moulded fountains launched in March 2026 with 15-20 days of order backlog, and new export markets in Canada, USA and the Netherlands were opened this year, though exports are only about 2% of revenue.

rows.label: Airport orders worth about INR 1.5 crore
rows.why: Three airport orders (Lucknow, Mumbai, Visakhapatnam) worth about INR 1.5 crore are the only large concrete backing, against FY26 revenue of INR 69 crore, so they cover about 2% of annual revenue.

rows.label: Inventory up 62% and receivables up 51% YoY
rows.why: Management gave no target for working capital days and attributed the build to capacity growth, sudden orders and credit to large customers, so the stress may persist until the RM shortage normalises.

rows.label: Solar on Pune factory
rows.why: Management expects savings of about INR 10-15 lakh per month from the installed solar panels, though MW capacity was not disclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on H2 earnings, the Delhi factory and long-term 25-30% growth, but cautious and evasive on FY27 numbers, PP pass-through and the B2C split; analysts pressed on the FY27 INR 115 crore figure and working capital.

544111|2026-03.headline: Apeejay Surrendra Park Hotels FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12% to INR 707 crore, with PAT of INR 66 crore; Q4 revenue up 4% to INR 184 crore.
544111|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated operating revenue was INR 184 crore (up 4% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 53 crore (28.85% margin) and PAT of INR 12 crore (6.44% margin). Management blamed Q4 cancellations in Delhi and Hyderabad on the Middle East war, saying occupancy there has recovered to over 90%. For FY26, revenue grew 12%, EBITDA was INR 218 crore (30.82% margin) and PAT was INR 66 crore (9.21% margin), with profitability hit by the Middle East war and higher depreciation and finance costs. Management reiterated the plan to double hotels to 85 and keys to 6,635 over four years, and said the EM Bypass Kolkata apartment sales are ahead of plan on cash flow.

financial_highlights.change: resilient despite high base; YoY not stated
ARR up 9% YoY; RevPAR up 7% YoY

segments.name: Hotels
segments.commentary: Park Calcutta ran at 100% occupancy for Q4 and FY26; Park Chennai (95%) and Park Navi Mumbai (93%) were the other top-three occupancies. Delhi and Hyderabad saw large Q4 cancellations, now recovered to over 90% occupancy.

segments.name: Flurys (F&B retail)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 29% YoY and the brand has 110 outlets. Management said it is profitable but did not share segment EBITDA. Plans to add 30+ outlets in 10 months (NCR 8, Pune 5, Bangalore 4).

segments.name: F&B overall
segments.commentary: F&B revenue crossed INR 300 crore in FY26, about 43% of total revenue.

segments.name: Real estate (EM Bypass Kolkata)
segments.commentary: 29 of 34 apartments sold in the first block at an average INR 20,857 per sq ft. Cash flow improved by over INR 11 crore up to April 2026, with a further ~INR 70 crore expected this year; second block launch planned for Sep-Oct 2026.

guidance_outlook: Reach over 3,000 keys by FY27 after adding 12 hotels (472 keys), of which 8 are asset-light.
Over four years: hotels from 42 to 85, keys from 2,677 to 6,635; owned hotels to double, asset-light to triple.
Flurys to reach 140 outlets (or slightly more) after 30 additions in 10 months, and 40-50 more outlets by 2030.
Park Mumbai Juhu (78 rooms) construction to start June 2026, completion by about March 2027.
Malabar House (Cochin) acquisition expected to close in June 2026; Vizag (100 rooms) moved to early 2030 opening due to environmental clearance delays.
Interest cost at about 8.35% (MCLR), expected to stay below that level; capex and acquisition needs of about INR 1,500 crore over five years, mainly funded by internal accruals.
Management said earlier mid-teens top-line growth guidance was missed; FY26 came in at 12%.
capex_capacity: Five projects (Pune, Mumbai, Vizag, EM Bypass, Jaipur) totalling 950 rooms at about INR 1.2 crore per room, about INR 1,100 crore before the EM Bypass reduction.
EM Bypass expected to contribute INR 350 crore, of which INR 70 crore is expected this year.
Zillion and THALI acquisition/project cost about INR 330 crore; normal capex about INR 40 crore per year; Flurys capex about INR 30-40 crore per year.
Q4 FY26 launches: Zone by the Park Darjeeling, Zone Connect by the Park Gangtok and Zone Connect by the Park Katra; 7 properties (283 keys) launched in FY26.
Flurys moving from central kitchen to an outsourced manufacturing vendor (agreement signed).
Room renovations planned at Chennai, Bangalore, Kolkata and Vizag; 20 rooms at Park Calcutta to be refurbished.
demand_pricing: Management cited limited branded supply in India (about 216,000 rooms) and said supply growth is 200-300 bps below demand growth.
Kolkata has 5,101 keys with about 1,702 keys expected over five years; management said the outlook is positive, helped by the change of state government.

Ran Baas The Palace (Patiala, leased) ran at ARR of about INR 31,000 in FY26; Lotus Palace Chettinad at about INR 12,000 ARR and about 30% occupancy; Patiala targets about 50% occupancy in the Oct-Dec season.
Cancellations in Delhi and Hyderabad in Q4 due to the Middle East war; management said contracts with ministries and corporates have been re-established.
Park Calcutta has about 30% repeat customers and T-RevPAR near INR 24,000, which management said is above luxury peers in its CBD.
Management said the Operation Sindoor disruption hit Q1 FY26 and the Middle East war hit from late February into April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ADR decline sequentially and grow only 3% YoY in Q4, and why was FY26 growth 12% against a mid-teens expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 weakness to large cancellations in Delhi and Hyderabad from the Middle East war, which have since stabilised. It said 12% growth was good given two disruptions (Operation Sindoor in Q1 and the Middle East war).

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Flurys outlet count below earlier guidance, and what is the achievable expansion plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan is 30+ outlets in the next 10 months (from 110 to about 140), largely cafes, with flagships in each new market; 40-50 more outlets by 2030. Management said the asset-light model with outsourced production allows faster rollout.

qa_highlights.question: How is 100% occupancy at Park Calcutta calculated when the website shows rooms available?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 100% means all rooms occupied every day, that the hotel has delivered near-100% occupancy for about 10 years (excluding COVID), and that its revenue management and repeat base (about 30%) drive this.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kolkata outlook and how is the EM Bypass sales progress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kolkata supply is limited and the state government change is positive. Apartments were launched at about INR 18,225 per sq ft and are now selling near INR 21,000; second block expected around the festive season.

qa_highlights.question: How will Flurys maintain quality with the central kitchen dropped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the central kitchen plan was dropped in favour of an outsourced vendor, with recipe standardisation, quality checks and quality chefs on site at the production facility.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company keep interest costs under control during the capex cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Atul Khosla said the interest rate is about 8.35% (MCLR) and will stay below that. Capex of about INR 1,500 crore over five years is mostly funded by internal accruals, with about INR 80 crore cash on hand; project interest will be capitalised as IDC.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the Vizag delay to 2030 and the status of Malabar House?
qa_highlights.answer: Vizag was delayed by environmental clearance, which is now in place; the project has no basement, so it may be faster, but management kept a 2030 timeline. Malabar House acquisition is expected to close in June 2026 after bank approval for foreign payment.

risks_watch: Q4 cancellations in Delhi and Hyderabad and whether occupancy holds above 90% in the coming quarters.
Geopolitical and LPG supply disruption, and its effect on costs and travel demand.
Flurys execution: 30 outlet additions in 10 months and the shift to outsourced production.
Vizag delay to 2030 and dependence on government permissions for new projects.
Pace of EM Bypass second-block launch (Sep-Oct 2026) and about INR 70 crore cash inflow expected this year.
Blended ARR and occupancy for the 336 leased keys not disclosed on the call; to be emailed to an analyst.
544111|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, pricing and the long-term pipeline, while being defensive on the FY26 growth miss and Q4 cancellations. Management was evasive on segment EBITDA (Flurys) and on the leased-hotel blended metrics, and on the Calcutta 100% occupancy calculation.
key_quotes: Consolidated operating revenue stood at 707 crores, registering a growth of 12% year-on-year
The sale of service apartments at EM Bypass Kolkata has exceeded expectations, resulting in substantial improvement in this year's cash flow.
So this year because of Operation Sindoor, the quarter was not very strong but now with things stabilizing we expect this quarter to be a good quarter and a stable quarter.
We do not share the segment analysis but Flurys is a profitable business.

rows.why: Occupancy was 91% for FY26 and Delhi and Hyderabad have recovered to over 90%, with FY26 RevPAR up 7% and ARR up 9%; new keys and Flurys outlets add to volume, though Q4 revenue grew only 4%.

rows.why: With 91% occupancy and capacity pipeline needs of about INR 1,100 crore for five projects plus about INR 330 crore for Zillion and THALI, management already has a multi-year capex plan; new announcements are likely as the four-year target is executed.

rows.why: Management missed its earlier mid-teens top-line growth guidance, delivering 12% in FY26, and gives no explicit FY27 revenue guidance.

rows.why: Flurys plans 30+ outlets in 10 months (NCR 8, Pune 5, Bangalore 4), taking it from 110 to about 140; 7 properties (283 keys) were launched in FY26 and Q4 launches included Zone by the Park Darjeeling, Zone Connect Gangtok and Katra.

rows.label: EM Bypass Kolkata cash inflow and second block
rows.why: About INR 70 crore of additional cash flow expected this year after INR 11 crore up to April 2026; 29 of 34 first-block apartments sold at an average INR 20,857 per sq ft.

rows.label: Malabar House Cochin acquisition closing
rows.why: Acquisition is approved and expected to close in June 2026 after bank approval for foreign payment.

rows.label: Vizag 100-room project delayed to early 2030
rows.why: Environmental clearance delays pushed the 100-room Vizag opening out to early 2030, so this capacity is outside the near-term window.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, pricing (ARR up 9%) and the long-term key pipeline, but defensive on the FY26 growth miss and Q4 Delhi and Hyderabad cancellations; analysts pressed on Flurys segment EBITDA, the Calcutta 100% occupancy calculation and leased-hotel metrics, which management was ev

544111|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10% to Rs.172 crore and EBITDA 8% to Rs.52 crore, while PAT fell 14% to about Rs.12 crore on finance costs and a tax-regime shift.
544111|2026-06.overview: Management reported operating revenue of Rs.167 crore (+8% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs.47 crore (+3%, margin 28.12%) for Q1 FY27, with consolidated revenue of Rs.172 crore (+10%) and EBITDA of Rs.52 crore (+8%). Occupancy held at 92%, but ADR growth was only about 2% amid West Asia disruption, weak international air traffic and flat domestic air traffic. PAT declined about 14% to close to Rs.12 crore, reflecting about Rs.2.5 crore higher finance charges from Zillion acquisition financing and a Rs.2.2 crore deferred tax provision on the move to the new tax regime. Management guided to a stronger ADR trend from Q2 onward, with the BRICS Summit, weddings and exhibitions cited as drivers.

segments.name: Food and Beverage
segments.commentary: F&B contributed about 43% of total revenue in Q1; Flurys stood at 111 outlets (cafes, kiosks, tea rooms) after adding one at Inorbit Mall Vizag, with first standalone North India cafe opened in Gurugram in August.

segments.name: Hotels (owned and managed)
segments.commentary: Portfolio stated as 42 hotels with 2,677 keys (one slide reference in call says 2,667). Ran Baas Patiala ARR about Rs.33,000 and Lotus Palace Chettinad about Rs.13,000, both still stabilising.

segments.name: EM Bypass Kolkata mixed-use project
segments.commentary: 33 of 69 service apartments sold at average about Rs.20,633 per sq ft; expected cash inflow Rs.70-80 crore this year, of which Rs.21 crore received.

guidance_outlook: ADR growth guided to high single digits for the coming season, supported by BRICS Summit in Delhi, about 40 wedding dates Nov-March, Aero Show Bengaluru and Bharat Mobility Expo.
Pipeline of 12 hotels with 472 keys in FY27, taking portfolio to 3,149 keys by end-FY27 from 2,677 keys.
Flurys target of 29 additional outlets in FY27, taking count to about 140; target of 400 outlets by 2030.
Long-term ambition of more than 6,000 keys by FY2030; management also cited 87 hotels and 6,719 keys over four years.
Other income guided at about Rs.3.5-4 crore per quarter; further cash inflow of about Rs.50 crore expected from EM Bypass by year-end.
Effective tax rate guided to fall to about 30-35% in Q2-Q4 FY27 under the new regime (from about 40% in Q1).
capex_capacity: EM Bypass Kolkata: 218 hotel rooms plus 69 service apartments, completion targeted early 2030; second Kolkata hotel referenced for opening in 2030.
The Park Juhu (78 rooms, converted from service apartments): design complete, launch targeted October 2027; long-term financing tied up for Zillion acquisition.
Vizag 100-room hotel: on site, launch expected in August 2026, completion early 2030.
Malabar House, Fort Kochi (17 keys, about half an acre): acquisition in progress, completion expected October-November 2026; acquisition cost about Rs.64 crore.
Pune FSI raised from 2.5 lakh to 6.7 lakh sq ft; plan of 2.5 lakh sq ft for hotel and 4 lakh+ sq ft for residential.

Capex for Pune (200 rooms), Navi Mumbai (250), Vizag (100), EM Bypass (220) and Jaipur (150) over 4-5 years: about Rs.1,140 crore at Rs.1.2 crore per room, plus Zillion acquisition about Rs.210 crore, Juhu renovation about Rs.80 crore and Kochi about Rs.64 crore (total about Rs.350 crore additional, cited with EM Bypass funding offset). Operating capex Rs.40 crore per year plus Flurys Rs.40 crore per year. Net capex about Rs.1,500 crore, to be funded from EBITDA of Rs.240-250 crore per year. About Rs.200-250 crore of capex expected within FY27.
Completed SAP S/4HANA implementation for Finance during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Occupancy 92%, described as India's leading occupancy; RevPAR leadership in upper upscale maintained.

Management said All-India ADR growth was 6% in the quarter, versus about 2% for the company as stated in analyst question; domestic passenger traffic flat and international inbound air traffic down about 10%.
City-level domestic passenger declines cited: Mumbai -3.5%, Hyderabad over -12%, Chennai -13%.
Juhu ARR about Rs.18,000-20,000; management expects Bombay ARR growth of 10-15%.
Management expects ADR to improve from Q2 onward; said Q2-Q4 should be distinctly better than Q1.
Pricing on EM Bypass service apartments: average about Rs.20,633 per sq ft; Juhu acquisition at about Rs.40,000 per sq ft versus market levels cited near Rs.1 lakh per sq ft.

financial_highlights.value: close to Rs.12 crore; PAT margin close to 7%
Rs.4.79 crore, of which about Rs.2.7 crore from mutual funds

qa_highlights.question: Given 92% occupancy, how should ADR evolve and what long-term ADR growth should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ADR pressure came from West Asia disruption, flat domestic passenger traffic and about 10% decline in international inbound traffic. All-India ADR growth was 6% in the quarter; it expects Q2-Q4 to be distinctly better and high single-digit ARR growth in the coming season, helped by BRICS Summit, about 40 wedding dates Nov-March, Aero Show and Bharat Mobility Expo.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Flurys still at 111 outlets versus aggressive plans, and how will the 29 additions be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Flurys has grown at a 21.5% CAGR since 2019 (17 outlets); five outlets opened so far with the rest mapped, including 3 Pune, 3 Mumbai, 5 Hyderabad, about 7 Delhi NCR, 4 Bengaluru and up to 10 PVR outlets under negotiation, targeting about 140 by year-end and 400 by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.4.79 crore other income run-rate sustainable over the next three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income of Rs.4.79 crore included about Rs.2.7 crore from mutual funds; management guided Rs.3.5-4 crore per quarter. About Rs.50 crore more EM Bypass cash is expected by year-end, to be added to mutual funds of about Rs.97 crore, so other income may rise.

qa_highlights.question: How mature is the existing portfolio and how long does stabilisation take for new hotels?
qa_highlights.answer: Ran Baas (ARR about Rs.33,000) and Lotus Palace Chettinad (about Rs.13,000) are entering maturity, with occupancy stabilising over the year; a 15-room Vembanad Lake property acquired this year is expected to stabilise with its Q3-Q4 season. Typical stabilisation is 2-3 years, but high-potential markets like Mumbai and Pune are expected to stabilise in 1-1.5 years or the first year.

qa_highlights.question: How does the EM Bypass service apartment model change return on capital and land evaluation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the model could lift RoCE from about 9-10% toward 20%+ as the project goes live, with cash flows of about Rs.70 crore this year, Rs.120 crore next year, Rs.100 crore in year three and Rs.30-40 crore in year four; sales of Rs.300-325 crore are meant to fund the hotel build, which management described as virtually free.

qa_highlights.question: What is the updated capex guidance for FY27 and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex for Pune (200 rooms), Navi Mumbai (250), Vizag (100), EM Bypass (220) and Jaipur (150) over 4-5 years is about Rs.1,140 crore at Rs.1.2 crore per room, plus about Rs.350 crore of Zillion, Juhu, Kochi and related items; net capex about Rs.1,500 crore against EBITDA of Rs.240-250 crore a year. About Rs.200-250 crore of capex falls within FY27, and Juhu's long-term financing is tied up.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall 14% when revenue rose 8%, and what is the tax outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance charges rose about Rs.2.5 crore YoY mainly on Zillion acquisition financing, and a Rs.2.2 crore deferred tax provision came from moving to the new regime. Q1 tax was about Rs.8.71 crore at roughly 40%; the effective rate is guided to about 30-35% in Q2-Q4, and management asked that PAT be compared with Q4 rather than Q1.

risks_watch: ADR recovery in Q2-Q4 depends on the BRICS Summit, wedding season and exhibitions; Q1 ADR growth was only about 2% for the company versus 6% for the market.
International inbound air traffic fell about 10% and city-level domestic traffic declined (Mumbai -3.5%, Hyderabad over -12%, Chennai -13%), so West Asia and air-connectivity pressure could persist.
Finance costs will rise with Zillion acquisition debt and capex of about Rs.1,500 crore net over 4-5 years; FY27 capex of Rs.200-250 crore must be funded from EBITDA and EM Bypass cash.

Execution risk on the EM Bypass sales (Rs.70-80 crore this year, Rs.21 crore received), the Juhu conversion (78 rooms, October 2027), Vizag launch in August 2026 and the Kochi acquisition (October-November 2026).
Flurys needs 29 net additions in FY27 to reach about 140 outlets; progress against the 400-outlet 2030 target and the Adani, DLF, Phoenix and PVR tie-ups still unconfirmed.

Tax rate step-down to 30-35% from about 40% is guided but not yet visible; the PAT trend depends on it. Mutual fund holdings (about Rs.97 crore) were questioned for being regular rather than direct plans, and an investor's request for the fund list was not answered on the call.
key_quotes: So, we expect that the quarters ahead are going to be distinctly better than the quarter which has gone by.

This decline is due to the impact of higher finance costs to propel expansion during this period as well as deferred tax provision of Rs.2.2 crores as the company shifts to the new favorable income tax regime.
And I would also request that if you are comparing PAT compare with the Q4 not to the tax rate with the Q4 not to the Q1.
So, we can expect definitely high single digit ARR growth as we go forward.
544111|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on the medium-term outlook, expansion pipeline and EM Bypass cash flows, but cautious on near-term ADR, citing West Asia disruption and weak air traffic. It was defensive on the PAT decline, attributing it to finance costs and the tax-regime shift, and asked analysts to compare with Q4 rather than Q1.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin was 28.12% (EBITDA +3% vs revenue +8%) and the effective tax rate is guided down to 30-35% from about 40%, but PAT is pressured by finance costs of about Rs.2.5 crore higher YoY and Zillion debt.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Pipeline of 12 hotels with 472 keys in FY27 takes portfolio from 2,677 to 3,149 keys by end-FY27 (+17.6%), with Vizag 100-room launch slated for August 2026 and Kochi acquisition completing October-November 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Keys guided to grow from 2,677 to 3,149 (+17.6%) by end-FY27 and occupancy is 92%, though Q1 ADR growth of only about 2% means volume gains are not yet matched by pricing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Occupancy at 92% with Rs.1,140 crore capex guided for Pune, Navi Mumbai, Vizag, EM Bypass and Jaipur over 4-5 years, and about Rs.200-250 crore of capex already slated within FY27, so further capacity announcements are likely to follow.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q1 ADR growth of about 2% and flat domestic air traffic (Mumbai -3.5%, Hyderabad over -12%, Chennai -13%) give management little room to raise guidance before Q2 numbers prove the recovery.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 ADR growth was only about 2% for the company (versus 6% for the market) with international inbound traffic down about 10%, so the high single-digit ADR recovery from Q2 depends on BRICS, weddings and expos that are not yet visible.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Flurys targets 29 additional outlets in FY27 to reach about 140 from 111 (5 opened so far), including a first standalone North India cafe in Gurugram opened in August, and the 78-room Juhu hotel targets October 2027.

rows.label: EM Bypass Kolkata cash inflow
rows.why: Rs.70-80 crore expected this year with Rs.21 crore received so far and about Rs.50 crore more by year-end, which funds capex and offsets finance costs.

rows.label: Tax rate step-down to 30-35%
rows.why: Effective tax rate guided down from about 40% in Q1 (Q1 tax Rs.8.71 crore) under the new regime, though it is not yet visible in reported numbers and a Rs.2.2 crore deferred tax provision was taken in Q1.

rows.label: EM Bypass Kolkata 218 rooms plus 69 service apartments
rows.why: Completion is targeted for early 2030, so it adds no keys within the 2-4 quarter window despite the Rs.70-80 crore sales cash flow this year.

tone.note: Management was confident on the pipeline, Flurys expansion and EM Bypass cash flows but cautious on near-term ADR (Q1 about 2% vs 6% market) and defensive on the 14% PAT decline; analysts pushed on the ADR gap, the mutual fund holdings and the tax-rate step-down.

544117|2026-03.headline: Signpost India FY26 revenue rose 27% to INR576 crore with EBITDA margin up ~590 bps to 25.5%; management guides 20%+ growth and 25-27% margin for FY27.
544117|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 46% YoY and 14% QoQ to INR162 crore, with operating EBITDA more than tripling YoY to INR42 crore at a 26.3% margin. FY26 revenue rose 27% to INR576 crore, EBITDA rose 65% to INR147 crore and net profit more than doubled to INR70 crore. Receivables rose about 80% YoY to INR317 crore, which management attributed to multi-city campaigns requiring regional compliance approvals, and it targets faster collections by Q3 FY27 through milestone-based billing. This was the company's maiden earnings call.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 net profit / net margin

financial_highlights.change: more than doubled from 7.5% margin in FY25

segments.name: Transit media
segments.commentary: Management calls transit the primary focus on long-term contracts; industry transit segment grew 22% in 2025 to INR20.2 billion. Bangalore Metro stations under contract rose from 18 to 25 against 67 stations on the line.

segments.name: Digital out-of-home (DOOH)
segments.commentary: Management cites DOOH as a higher-margin contributor; digital ad space reportedly rose from 25,000 sq ft to 80,000 sq ft between Q3 and Q4. Transit and digital together are about 48% of FY26 top line.

segments.name: Street furniture / bus queue shelters
segments.commentary: Mumbai contract requires 20% of about 3,000 bus queue shelters to be upgraded within 3 years; about 11% completed so far. Digitisation is not a binding commitment.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided to be in double digits; management also cited 20%+ growth in one answer.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 25-27%, supported by operating leverage, better utilisation and rising DOOH mix.
FY27 capex of about INR60-75 crore across infrastructure, capacity and technology.
Targets 6-7% cost saving on cost of services without hurting top line; management said this would flow directly to PBT.
About 48% of FY26 revenue (INR576 crore) is already contracted for FY27 per management.
Working-capital cycle targeted to improve via milestone-based billing by Q3 FY27; industry norm 90-120 days.
Mid-term ambition of 100 cities nationwide from more than 30 currently; asset-light model with data layer planned.
capex_capacity: Footprint grew from 4 cities at 2024 listing to 32 cities; about 866,000 sq ft added in FY26.
FY27 capex planned at INR60-75 crore across infrastructure, capacity expansion and technology implementation.
Kolkata Streetscape Renaissance project expected to reach 60-70% implementation by Sept-Oct 2026, before Durga Puja.
Bangalore Metro expansion ramping: 18 to 25 stations now generating revenue against 67 stations on the line.
Electric premium bus fleet additions across Mumbai, Hyderabad and Goa.
Management says new assets typically take 4-6 months to mature; some (e.g., Shimla) take 5-6 months.
demand_pricing: Management says around 3/4 of revenue is direct from advertisers; anchor client share about 29% of revenue; over 1,600 active advertisers.
Management cites FICCI-EY data: organised OOH market grew 13% in 2025 to INR66.9 billion, projected about INR85 billion by 2028; DOOH about 18% share, transit about 30%.
Management says customer mix includes PSUs and fintech/banking (e.g., SBI, NPCI, PNB), with FMCG, education, MSME and BFSI as other key categories.
Management says it is shifting from short-term intermediary-led campaigns toward multi-month and annual brand contracts; average remaining contract tenure about 14 years.

qa_highlights.question: How will receivables increase (noted as higher this quarter) be addressed?

segments.commentary: Growing 20.6% YoY; management guides 25-30% growth for this year and next, citing PLI and Make in India demand.

segments.name: Vehicle loans (2-wheeler and used car)
segments.commentary: Grew 76% YoY; 2-wheelers offered in 135 cities and used cars in 50 cities; Q3 expected to be strongest on Diwali demand.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Up 81% YoY but only 0.3% QoQ; 65-70% of the Jan-Mar 2026 6-month loans came up for renewal in Q2. Management expects growth of about 10% a quarter from Q3.

segments.name: Micro LAP
segments.commentary: Growth slowed to about 3% (management expects 7-8% at best); no loosening of credit criteria.

segments.name: Microfinance (MFI)
segments.commentary: Now 26% of gross loan book; collections at 99% including BC book; growth subdued given weak bureau histories among borrowers. 97% of customers have two or fewer MFI lenders vs 93% industry.

segments.name: Unsecured advances
segments.commentary: Up 17% YoY but down 0.3% QoQ; all new disbursements placed under the CGFMU guarantee programme. Uncovered gross NPA of INR 296 crore sits under guarantee cover of INR 319 crore.

segments.name: NBFC term loans
segments.commentary: Growth of 0.7% YoY; management does not expect significant growth.

segments.name: Liabilities
segments.commentary: CASA up 13% YoY; TD up 17.5% YoY; 96.1% of deposits have contractual tenor of 1 year and above.

guidance_outlook: PAT growth guidance raised to 100% YoY for FY27 from earlier 80%; management expects H2 PAT at least equal to H1 for this to hold.
Advances growth guidance maintained at 19-21%; deposit growth guidance maintained at 23-25%.
Full-year credit cost expected below 2%; H2 credit cost expected lower than H1's 0.92%.
Secured share of book expected to reach about 75% by year-end, versus 73.7% at Q2 and a long-term target of about 80%.
Cost-to-income targeted toward 60% over coming quarters; management says FY27 achievement is unlikely, with 57% (March 2024 level) as the first goal.
NIM expected to stay around current levels (about 7.5%) in H2 with cost of funds around 7.4%.
Guarantee claims of INR 68 crore expected to be received within about 2 months (by end-November); remaining INR 251 crore to be lodged in Q3 next year.

Branch expansion: 78 branches planned, 40 opened so far; launches planned for credit line on UPI (Q2 proof of concept), loans against shares and mutual funds (November), and trade FX via AD-1 licence (December).
capex_capacity: About 820 branches across India; 78 branch openings planned for FY27, with 40 completed by the call date.
Digital onboarding for non-face-to-face CASA accounts expected by January.
AI-led processes introduced in collections, welcome calling and cross-sell, reducing headcount and cost.
Headcount in September 2026 lower than March 2026 despite asset and liability growth.
demand_pricing: Q2 disbursements of INR 4,414 crore, up 7% YoY and 5% QoQ.
Affordable housing average ticket size INR 11.9 lakh; top seven states make up 67% of concentration, top three 37%.
Insurance income for H1 about INR 45 crore; 80-90% linked to credit life and 10-20% to retail products. IRDAI consultation impact not yet fully assessed.
Management says deposit pricing is fairly competitive; interest rates were harder in Q2 than Q1 and the market shows no sign of weakening rate regime.
Customers in the petroleum supply chain and related MSMEs show marginal impact; some export-linked sourcing paused because of higher shipping costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will slippages trend up or down in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects lower slippages in Q3 and H2. Q2 had one-offs: a secured loan slippage adding about 0.2% and drought-related MFI slippage of about 0.3%. SMA has graduated down in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How much of H1 insurance income is credit life and what is the IRDAI consultation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: 80-90% is credit life, 10-20% retail products. Initial IRDAI assessment done; full assessment pending. Management will push penetration and AI-led cost efficiency to offset lower commissions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cost-to-income decline sustainable and can it fall below 60%?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost-to-income expected to stay at or below the September level; management is cautious that sub-60% is unlikely this year. Drivers are productivity, RPA/AI processes and more direct sourcing over DSA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CASA outlook and cost of funds risk from rate hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: CASA fell 2% QoQ in ratio terms but grew 13% YoY; management targets about 20% CASA in H2 via affluent offers and digital onboarding by January. Cost of funds targeted to stay near 7.4%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the guarantee scheme cover the full book and what if it does not?
qa_highlights.answer: Claims of INR 68 crore lodged; NGC expected to pay within about 2 months. CGFMU is not open for fresh guarantees yet, but 1% cover cost has been accrued. If the scheme fails, the accrual becomes a buffer.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gold loan and micro LAP flat, and when will growth pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold flat due to 6-month loans from Jan-Mar 2026 renewing in Q2 and gold price drop; growth expected to resume in Q3 at about 10% a quarter. Micro LAP may reach 7-8% growth but not much more.

qa_highlights.question: Any risks to achieving 100% PAT growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no visible constraint on H2 profit matching H1; credit costs, asset growth and liability growth were all cited as on track.

qa_highlights.question: How will NIM move in H2 amid rising rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects NIM around current levels, as MFI share is not rising faster and secured share only reaches about 75%; cost of funds should not fall.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth outlook by segment and do drought and geopolitical risks affect the book?
qa_highlights.answer: MSME 25-30% growth, affordable housing and vehicles continue strongly. Drought declared in 29 Karnataka districts and 34 Maharashtra districts; slippage impact expected to be immaterial. No material impact from the Iran war so far.

risks_watch: CGFMU guarantee scheme not yet open for fresh guarantees; if it does not reopen, the INR 296 crore uncovered unsecured NPA and future MFI risk rest on the bank's own buffer.
Net NPA at 1.08% is above the 1% comfort level until the INR 68 crore claim is received, expected by end-November.
CASA ratio fell and CASA growth (13% YoY) trails TD growth; deposit growth of 17% YoY is below the 23-25% guidance.
Drought in Karnataka and Maharashtra may lift slippages and moratorium requests; geopolitical oil and shipping cost impact on MSME exporters.

IRDAI insurance commission consultation could cut non-interest income; full impact not yet assessed. Media speculation about a merger, which management said it would evaluate if strategically sensible.

rows.why: CASA grew 13% YoY and fell 2% QoQ in ratio terms; management targets about 20% CASA via affluent offers and digital onboarding by January, but rate environment is tough and deposit pricing is competitive.

rows.label: AI-led headcount and cost reduction
rows.why: Headcount in September 2026 was lower than March 2026 despite asset and liability growth, and cost-to-income fell from 67.0% to 64.3% QoQ, with opex up 15% YoY against NII up 35%.

544119|2026-03.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 51% YoY to INR 4,489 crores, with PAT up 65% to INR 87 crores.
544119|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations grew 51% YoY to INR 4,489 crores, EBITDA rose 41% with margin at 2.95%, and PAT grew 65% to INR 87 crores (1.93% margin). For FY26, revenue grew 15% to INR 15,827 crores, EBITDA rose 53% to INR 459 crores (2.90% margin, up 72 bps), and PAT rose 35% to INR 282 crores. Management attributed H2 growth mainly to price increases in the PES category, with H1 growth driven by volume and customer additions. Management guided to a ~20% CAGR and said the PC super cycle could last another 1-2 years, while flagging a possible 5-10% unit decline in CY26 and H2 consumer softness.

financial_highlights.change: Described as healthy vs prior-year outflows

segments.name: PES (Personal computing / enterprise)
segments.commentary: About 58% of business; grew 37% YoY in FY26, aided by higher H2 PC demand and ASPs. Management expects ~20% average price increase in this category going forward.

segments.name: LIT (Lifestyle IT)
segments.commentary: About 42% of business; grew 24% YoY in FY26. Price increases described as routine only; management says LIT is growing about 2x the industry.

segments.name: Semiconductor
segments.commentary: Grew 131% YoY from a small base; customers include large automotive, robotics and IoT manufacturers. Operations moved into a newly created subsidiary; management says meaningful P&L impact is a few years away.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated a ~20% CAGR (sustained for 20 years) and expects to maintain this trajectory in FY27; regular-business growth aspiration of 15-20% YoY.
Management estimates PES unit market could degrow 5-10% in CY26 (IDC concurs), but with 20-25% price growth, PES revenue could still grow 10-15% on an as-is basis.
Consumer demand could soften in H2 FY27 on affordability; management is discussing 24- and 36-month interest-free EMI schemes with vendors.
Working capital days expected to stay in a similar range in FY27 (CFO).
Distribution PAT margin range of 1.5-1.75% considered applicable to the industry absent mix change; margins described as intact despite price hikes.
Management said the super cycle could continue for another 1-2 years.
Project business (AI data centre) planned for FY27 subject to viability and ROI; funnels of INR 20,000-25,000 crores under consideration.
capex_capacity: Branch network expanded to 55 city branch offices with three new branches added (Nanded, Baramati, Solapur, Maharashtra); 10,000-plus customers across 700-plus towns.
Working capital was increased on inventory to capture demand; management said inventory days cannot fall while regular business grows ~30%.
Project business: FY24-25 included INR 2,000 crores of AI data centre project (Yotta, 512 servers, 4,000 GPUs); no substantial project business in FY26; FY27 plans subject to ROI.
Semiconductor business moved into a separate subsidiary to focus operations and accelerate partnerships and customer acquisition.
Management says it has post-IPO capacity to pick up data centre projects on a selective ROI basis without compromising regular growth.
demand_pricing: Price increases began mainly in H2 FY26; management estimates roughly half of H2 growth (46-47% H2-on-H2) came from pricing, i.e. ~20-22 percentage points.
Management says FY26 growth ex the one large AI project was 31%; FY26 growth without large deals was 15% reported.
Q3 and Q4 FY26 growth reported at 42% and 51% respectively (non-project business).

AI PCs are about 25% of PCs and notebooks sold in India; NVIDIA DGX Spark and Dell (server, storage, PCs, monitors) partnerships cited; Dell described as at low-single-digit share of revenue, expected to reach close to double digits next FY.
IDC: India traditional PC shipments 15.9 million units in CY2025 (+10.2%); IDC flags possible 5-10% dip in CY2026 shipments.
Enterprise refresh delayed by some large corporates during price hikes is reversing as buyers see 30-40% higher prices a year later.
Management said demand is not softening currently; affordability risk in consumer segment in H2.

qa_highlights.question: How much of top-line growth came from pricing vs volume, and what is normalised growth for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases were minimal in H1 and substantial in H2; H2 growth of 46-47% H2-on-H2 included about 20-22 points from price. Management reiterated 20% CAGR for 20 years and expects to maintain it.

qa_highlights.question: What is a PC classified as an AI PC, and how big is that segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Devices with an NPU or high-end processors/GPUs capable of AI workloads; about 25% of PCs and notebooks sold in India are AI PCs, expected to grow further over 1-2 years, lifting ASPs.

qa_highlights.question: Is refresh demand being delayed by price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Some corporates extended refresh cycles initially, but the trend is reversing as buyers realise delay could cost 30-40% more; refresh expected to normalise as in prior years.

qa_highlights.question: Does the semiconductor business carry high working capital, and when will it affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is higher (100-plus days cited), but gross margins and ROCE are higher than the regular business; the business is small, so meaningful margin impact is a few years away.

qa_highlights.question: How will RP Tech participate in AI data centre projects given capital needs and lower margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Funnels of about INR 20,000-25,000 crores are under consideration; the company will pick projects selectively on ROI without compromising 15-20% regular growth; margins vary by project.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of revenue from large deals, enterprise and core distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 had no large AI deals (only INR 5-15 crore deals); enterprise non-AI growth is high, driven by NVIDIA solutions; growth ex-Yotta was 31%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the ST Finserv channel finance programme affect working capital and credit risk?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a non-recourse channel finance programme for channel partners; the company bears no credit risk or funding cost unless it draws funds early, which it normally does not.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT margin aspiration, and what caused the Q4 gross margin dip?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution PAT margin range of 1.5-1.75% is typical absent mix change; Q4 gross margin dip was due to additional provisioning for slow-moving inventory, not a structural decline.

risks_watch: Possible 5-10% unit decline in PC market in CY26 and H2 FY27 consumer softness from affordability as prices rise further.
Potential supply shortages in PES due to component (DRAM, NAND, GPU) pricing firmness.
Data centre project participation is capital-intensive with lower margins; scale of funnel conversion uncertain.
Inventory days (56) unlikely to fall while regular business grows ~30%; slow-moving inventory provision taken in Q4.
Semiconductor working capital cycle of 100-plus days; benefits to margin a few years away.
Dependence on Dell ramp-up (low-single-digit share now, expected near double-digit next FY).
544119|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the PC super cycle and multi-year growth, with growth targets reiterated. Evasive on specifics: declined to give Dell revenue numbers and deferred distribution-channel and margin-trajectory questions offline, and clarified several analyst misreadings of its figures.
key_quotes: So we are very confident to maintain our trajectory of 20% CAGR in the coming year as well.
This is not a 1-quarter tailwind. It is a structural multiyear upgrade super cycle.

Rashi will pick up proportionate to our capacity amongst these opportunities and obviously not run after everything because they are, one, capital intensive, and second, the margins are also lower on this front.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says distribution PAT margin of 1.5-1.75% is the industry-applicable range absent mix change; FY26 EBITDA margin 2.90% (+72 bps) was driven by price hikes, and Q4 gross margin was dented by slow-moving inventory provisioning, so further expansion is not guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Three new branches (Nanded, Baramati, Solapur) already commissioned, taking the network to 55 city branches; no plant or fixed-capacity capex is described, and the AI data centre project is subject to ROI with FY27 timing.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: IDC flags a possible 5-10% dip in CY26 PC shipments and management flags H2 FY27 consumer affordability softness, so unit volumes are expected to fall even though revenue grows about 10-15% on 20-25% price increases.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was only held at a ~20% revenue CAGR and 15-20% regular-business growth, with no raise, and FY26 growth was 15% reported (31% ex the large AI project).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Consumer affordability risk and a possible 5-10% PES unit decline in CY26 could weigh on the 20% CAGR, and DRAM/NAND/GPU component pricing could cause supply shortages.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Dell ramp (low-single-digit share now, near double digits next FY) and AI PC mix (about 25% of Indian PCs/notebooks) are rising, but no specific product launch dates were given.

rows.label: AI data centre project funnel
rows.why: Funnels of INR 20,000-25,000 crores are under consideration, but projects are subject to ROI and FY26 had no substantial project business (FY24-25 included INR 2,000 crores Yotta project).

rows.label: PES price increases of ~20-25%
rows.why: Management expects ~20% average price increase in PES going forward; H2 FY26 pricing added about 20-22 points to H2 growth of 46-47%, and this supports PES revenue growth of 10-15% even as units fall 5-10%.

rows.label: Working capital days held
rows.why: CFO expects working capital days in a similar range (inventory 56, debtors 46, creditors 44, net 58 days), since inventory cannot fall while regular business grows about 30%.

tone.note: Management was confident on the PC super cycle, the 20% CAGR and the 1.5-1.75% PAT margin range, but evasive on Dell revenue numbers and deferred channel and margin questions offline; analysts probed price vs volume split, the Q4 gross margin dip and the AI data centre funnel.

544119|2026-06.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 62% YoY to Rs 5,102 crore, with PAT up 69% to Rs 105 crore and ROCE near 19.5%.
544119|2026-06.overview: Management reported record consolidated revenue, EBITDA, PAT and annualised ROCE for the quarter ended June 2026, driven by price increases in memory, storage and CPUs plus a rise in unit volume. Management said about 30-35% of the revenue growth came from price, 20-25% from quantity, 5-10% from new products and brands, and about 10% from market share gains. Pillars cited were the core distribution engine, the VDA Infosolutions acquisition (67% stake) and a semiconductor JV with Restar Japan (74:26). Management guided to similar growth in Q2 but a slower pace of price increases.

financial_highlights.change: up 55% YoY (CEO cited 50% on the opening remarks)

segments.name: Consolidated group
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 5,102 crore and PAT Rs 105 crore; management stated all-time highs on topline, EBITDA, PAT and annualised ROCE.

segments.name: Commercial vs consumer (B2B mix)
segments.commentary: Management estimates 30-35% consumer-centric and 60-65% commercial (SMB and enterprise). Consumer demand is slowing on affordability, with laptop prices reportedly about 2x year-on-year.

segments.name: Semiconductor / embedded
segments.commentary: Semiconductor revenue in Q1 grew about 70% versus the Q1 FY26 base (not 70% of full-year revenue, per clarification). Growth is described as near double-digit and sometimes higher.

segments.name: VDA Infosolutions (acquired)
segments.commentary: Majority stake (67% in year one) in a pan-India system integrator; FY26 revenue was about Rs 850 crore. Management expects integrated services and value-added solutions to be about 5% of revenue, with Q2 as the next update point.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 growth expected to be similar to Q1 (about 60%), with price increase speed roughly halving; management described Q2 as on a strong footing.
Management expects the price uptrend to continue through FY27, with some slowdown in trajectory.
Management cited third-party reports of about a 10% unit decline in the overall PC market, offset by price increases.
Management reiterated a 20% CAGR track record over 20 years; cited about Rs 3,000 crore as 20% of a Rs 16,000 crore base.
Semiconductor JV targets more than US$100 million revenue within three years; the JV numbers will be reported with Q2 results.
Large AI data centre deals not pursued aggressively in Q1 due to working-capital needs; management said the pipeline should last at least three quarters.
capex_capacity: Two new branches planned in Udaipur and Dhule to extend reach into C and D class cities.
Presence across 57 towns in India, per management.
Semiconductor JV Rashi Restar Semiconductor Solutions Private Limited to be formed as a step-down subsidiary; Restar to take 26% stake, with the existing embedded business moving into the JV.
Plans to add 50+ local engineering hires over the next two years for the semiconductor JV.
Debt-to-equity ratio cited at around 0.5; management said large data centre projects could push it to at least 2x.
demand_pricing: Memory, hard drive and CPU shortages are pushing prices higher; management expects the uptrend to continue through FY27.
Management said about 10% market share gain contributed to growth; unit growth ex-SanDisk was about 20%, with SanDisk unit declines pulling reported units lower.
Entry-level laptops face about 50% shortage per management; medium and premium notebooks available if prices are accepted.
T2 partners are holding elevated channel inventory to earn double-digit margins; management said it is not a concern given demand.
Refurbished PCs are seen as small: management estimated the refurbished pool at 0.5-1 million units against a 15-16 million PC TAM in India.
Management said Dell commercial business contributed about 5% of revenue in the quarter, and is above target for FY27.
Management said the company has allocations from NVIDIA, Intel and AMD; supply risk is tracked weekly ('orange alert').

qa_highlights.question: Why is India demand strong relative to global peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited economic strength, digitisation and education focus, plus data centre-related demand; commercial demand is holding up while consumer demand is slowing on affordability.

qa_highlights.question: Split of Q1 growth between price, volume and mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Price 30-35%, quantity 20-25%, new products and brands 5-10%, market share about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 growth match Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 should show a similar trend (about 60%), but the speed of price increases should roughly halve.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin decline: price or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to mix (higher PES share, lower margin than LIT) and to last year's hived-off subsidiary whose service cost sat in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a supply constraint risk in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is potential risk, but allocations so far are good given supplier relationships; the company tracks it weekly.

qa_highlights.question: Why not pursue large AI data centre deals aggressively?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prioritised run-rate business with higher ROCE and working-capital needs; it still participates through smaller Rs 20-70 crore supplies and focuses on neo-clouds and smaller operators.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY28 look after the tailwinds fade?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 20% CAGR track record and cited VDA and the Restar JV as longer-term growth levers.

qa_highlights.question: Semiconductor JV economics and Restar's investment amount?
qa_highlights.answer: Restar's investment depends on fair valuation at SPA signing, so it is not quantified; management targets over US$100 million JV revenue in three years and said the JV margin profile is higher than co-distribution.

Consumer affordability: consumer demand slowing with laptop prices about 2x YoY; management flagged possible consumer pressure in H2.
Channel inventory: T2 partners holding elevated inventory to earn double-digit margins; management said it is not a concern, but it is a watch item for price-driven sell-through.
Price increase pace: Q2 price increases expected to roughly halve; management said unit market may fall about 10% and growth depends on price offsetting volume.
Working capital and leverage: large AI data centre deals not pursued aggressively; management said debt-to-equity (around 0.5) could reach at least 2x if such projects are taken on.
Semiconductor JV: Restar's investment amount unquantified (depends on SPA valuation); JV numbers to be reported with Q2; VDA integration and contribution still undefined until Q2.

The only correction will happen on the speed of the price increase. Price increase speed should be half.
But yes, this is an orange alert for us. We track it on a weekly basis.
So, we are very optimistic that similar trend will continue in July-August-September also.
So, it is not that we are not there. It is only that we have not prioritized to do INR 500 crores or INR 1000 crores of deals

544120|2026-03.headline: Capital SFB Q4 FY26 PAT rose 17% YoY to ₹40 crores, with NIM up to 4.06% and FY27 ROA guided to 1.35%–1.4%.
544120|2026-03.overview: Gross advances reached ₹8,687 crores (+20.9% YoY, +6.4% QoQ) and total deposits crossed ₹10,000 crores (+20% YoY). Q4 PPOP rose 28% YoY to ₹62 crores and cost of deposits eased to 5.75% from 5.86% QoQ, with NIM at 4.06% versus 4.01% in Q3. Asset quality was broadly stable: GNPA 2.54%, NNPA 1.24%, with Q4 credit cost of 0.26% driven by higher provisioning (PCR 51.89%) rather than losses. Management guided to FY27 advances growth of 22%+, ROA of 1.35%–1.4%, and credit cost of 0.15%–0.25%.

segments.name: MSME / business banking
segments.commentary: Growth driver: +9% QoQ and +46% YoY in Q4. Management expects it to remain a growth leader in FY27.

segments.name: LAP (loan against property)
segments.commentary: +5% QoQ and +19% YoY; yield 12.33% in Q4 vs 12.56% in Q3. Named as a FY27 growth leader.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Book grew 7% QoQ but net NPA was static at 2.76% vs 2.75%. Growth to be slower than the overall book, limited to Punjab and Haryana.

segments.name: Mortgage / housing
segments.commentary: Housing yield 9.85% in Q4 vs 9.83% in Q3. Cited as a driver for growth in newer states.

segments.name: NBFC-MFI
segments.commentary: Outstanding net NPA ₹5.49 crores vs ₹6.08 crores a quarter earlier; total exposure about ₹39 crores. No fresh lending in Q4; an OTS was signed with one lender.

segments.name: Out-of-Punjab advances
segments.commentary: 24% of advances at March 2026 vs 21% a year earlier; growing more than twice the Punjab rate YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 secured advances growth of 22%+; advances above ₹16,000 crores by FY29.
Branches: target of 235 by end of FY27 (current year) and 300+ by FY29.

FY27 ROA target of 1.35%–1.4%, rising to 1.6%+ by FY29; ROE of 15%+ by FY29.
FY27 opex/average assets guided to 2.9%–3.0% (lower bias), with opex/average assets below 2.85% over the medium term.
FY27 credit cost guided to 0.15%–0.25% with negative bias; target of about 0.3% up to FY29.

capex_capacity: Branch network at 211 across 5 states and 2 union territories at March 2026; 77.3% are SURU branches.
Target of 235 branches by end of FY27 and 300+ by FY29; 50% of new branches to be opened outside Punjab and 40–45% in Punjab.
Management said cost of new branches in FY27 is mainly last-mile branch cost, as senior and head-office costs are already built in.
Business per branch (5+ year branches) is ₹106 crores in Punjab vs ₹73 crores outside Punjab; PPOP of 5+ year branches is 2.75%–3.25% vs 2.1% entity level.
demand_pricing: Disbursements were ₹919 crores in Q4 (+20% YoY) and ₹3,508 crores in FY26 (+23% YoY).
