Yields: agriculture 12.54% (vs 12.62%), business 10.55% (vs 10.6%), corporate 10.77% (vs 10.8%); overall advance yield fell to about 10.8% from about 11.1%, partly due to a 25 bps rate cut and agri accounts moving to NPA with interest reversals.
Fee income was ₹25.8 crores in Q4 vs ₹26.1 crores in Q3 (0.9% of assets, vs 1.0% a year earlier); treasury income fell due to weaker market opportunities.
Cost of deposits 5.75% in Q4 vs 5.86% in Q3; average CD ratio 82.3%, period-end 86.7%; retail deposits above 90%.

qa_highlights.question: Gross NPA additions and provisioning: are provisions increasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ₹22 crore FY provision figure includes tax; PCR was raised to 51.89% from 50.45%, so provisioning was increased within the profit outlook.

qa_highlights.question: Agri NPA stickiness: will it fall back toward 2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not target 2%; it expects agri NPA to stay range-bound with a lower bias. Recoveries concentrate in Q1 and Q3 cash-flow periods.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the new ECL framework on credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial view is P&L neutral to positive, as current provisions are considered sufficient against the ECL requirement; detailed evaluation is ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Co-lending / BC model and FLDG cover?
qa_highlights.answer: The bank runs a business correspondent lending model (not co-lending) with more than one partner, and the FLDG cover is 5% per regulation. Branches are to remain 90–95% of disbursements.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of the NII margin expansion and CD ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Term deposit repricing (53% repricing in Q1–Q2) and an improving CD ratio are the two NIM levers; management expects an opex/average assets ratio of 2.9%–3.0% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost and cost-to-income guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost for FY27 is 0.15%–0.25%. The Q4 credit cost of 0.26% was provisioning-driven, linked to NBFC-MFI slippage. Cost-to-income is expected to improve, with opex/average assets at 2.9%–3.0%.

risks_watch: Agri asset quality: net NPA at 2.76%, and monsoon or input-cost stress could affect the book, although management cites Punjab irrigation and collateral.
Pace of deposit repricing and whether NIM reaches the guided improvement in Q1–Q2 FY27.
Yield pressure: advance yields fell to about 10.8% amid rate cuts and NPA reversals; 8–10 bps of the decline is described as temporary.
Fee income and treasury income momentum; Banca and fee targets depend on new product approvals.
ECL transition impact, which management expects to be P&L neutral to positive but is still under evaluation.
Growth outside Punjab through business correspondent partners, which is early-stage and carries FLDG exposure.

544120|2026-06.headline: Capital SFB Q1 FY27 PAT rose 29% YoY to INR 41.3 crore, with NIM at 4.21% and GNPA down to 2.47%.
544120|2026-06.overview: Gross advances reached INR 9,074 crore, up 22% YoY and 4.5% QoQ, while deposits grew 16% YoY to INR 10,596 crore with CASA at 36.7%. NIM improved to 4.21% from 4.06% a year ago, helped by deposit repricing and a higher average CD ratio of 83%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 2.47% and NNPA at 1.14%, as the bank raised PCR to 54.5%. Management guided to stable NIM near 4.2% for FY27, ROA of 1.35-1.4% for FY27, and 22% advance growth.

broadly in line with last year

qa_highlights.question: Split of MSME growth between Punjab and Haryana, and how it is trending
qa_highlights.answer: MSME (INR 28 lakh average ticket, middle-income, collateralised) grew 49% YoY and 11% QoQ; growth within Punjab and outside Punjab, and between Punjab and Haryana, is similar. Advances outside Punjab are 25% of the book vs 24% a quarter ago and 21% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Why PCR has been rising over recent quarters and whether it will stay stable
qa_highlights.answer: PCR was raised to 54.5% to move net NPA towards the medium-term 1% target; management says most of that action is done and it expects a stable PCR from here.

qa_highlights.question: Headroom for cost of deposit repricing and ROA path
qa_highlights.answer: Remaining repricing is not material; the bulk was done in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27. ROA is targeted at 1.35-1.4% in FY27 and 1.6%+ by FY29; Q1 ROA was 1.3% vs 1.18%, and PPOP margin rose to 2.04% from 1.94%.

qa_highlights.question: What keeps NIM stable at around 4.2% given cost-of-deposit and yield pressure
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,597 crore of term deposits reprice in Q2 FY27 for a 10-12 bps benefit, which management expects to be offset by higher incremental deposit costs. Advance yield fell to 10.9% from 11.1%; 50% of the book is fixed and 50% floating; NIM expansion is expected in FY28-29 as average CD ratio (83%) rises to mid-to-high 80s.

qa_highlights.question: Why PSU competition in housing eased and whether mortgage growth will pick up
qa_highlights.answer: Deposit repricing helped the bank compete with PSBs in the INR 20-25 lakh housing ticket; mortgage grew 3% QoQ and 10% YoY at a 9.87% yield vs 9.85% in Q4, but management says growth will stay moderate with some portion still to be recovered.

Universal bank conversion depends on getting net NPA to about 1%, which the bank currently reports at 1.14%.

544122|2026-03.headline: Entero FY26 revenue rose 31.5% like-for-like to INR6,591 crore with 4% EBITDA margin; FY27 guidance is 23% growth and 5% margin excluding new acquisitions.
544122|2026-03.overview: FY26 met all three initial targets: like-for-like revenue growth of 31.5% (organic 15.6%, inorganic 16%), 4% EBITDA margin (+67 bps) and operating cash flow of INR96.2 crore. Q4 revenue grew 42.6% YoY, with organic growth of 17.1% and acquisitions contributing 26%, and Q4 EBITDA margin reached 4.5%. Minority interest jumped sharply in Q4 (about 38% of PAT) due to an abnormal, pulled-forward MedTech sale at a partly-owned subsidiary, which management says will normalise. FY27 guidance is 23% consolidated revenue growth excluding new acquisitions (about 11 points from calendarisation), 5% EBITDA margin, and at least 50% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion.

segments.name: MedTech
segments.commentary: Now above INR1,000 crore annualised revenue after 3 MedTech acquisitions in FY26 (Anand Chemiceutics, Ace Cardiopathy, Bio de Technology). Management says MedTech is over 15% of revenue, could reach about 20% in 2-3 years, and earns higher margins than pharma due to commercial/agency role.

segments.name: Pharma distribution
segments.commentary: Remains the core business with about 100,000 retail pharmacies, 3,600 hospitals, 97,500 SKUs and 3,300+ manufacturers. Management expects pharma and MedTech to contribute equally to FY27 organic growth.

segments.name: GLP-1
segments.commentary: Management says current GLP-1 sales are about INR10-12 crore per month, roughly 5% of industry GLP value, with a share above its overall India share due to cold-chain warehouses; included in FY27 guidance.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 23% YoY excluding new acquisitions; about 11 points from calendarisation of FY26 acquisitions and the rest organic (management also cited about 22% in one answer).
FY27 EBITDA margin of 5%, about 50 bps above Q4 FY26's 4.5%, from MedTech mix, operating leverage and exiting low-margin businesses.
EBITDA-to-operating cash flow conversion of at least 50% in FY27.
Tax rate of about 22-23% for FY27.
Minority interest to be about 25-27% of PAT before minority interest in FY27, down from about 38% in Q4.
Finance cost to stay relatively stable for a couple of quarters, then decline over the next couple of years as IPO funds were used up.
No new acquisitions assumed for the next 6-8 months; guidance would be revised upwards if acquisitions are made. Acquisitions are priced at 5-7x EV/EBITDA.
capex_capacity: Seven acquisitions closed in FY26, including 3 in MedTech; management says no new acquisitions are planned for the next 6-8 months, focusing on organic growth.
Some MedTech IVD machines are placed at customer sites on 5-year reagent rental contracts and are depreciated; cardiology and other MedTech lines carry little depreciating equipment.
Cold-chain facilities in all warehouses support GLP-1 distribution.
Depreciation rose about 50% QoQ in Q4, and interest costs rose because acquisitions were debt- or investment-funded after IPO proceeds were used up.
demand_pricing: Organic growth outperformed IPM by 1.6x for FY26 (15.6% vs IPM); Q3 and Q4 multiplier fell to about 1.4x as IPM grew about 12% versus 7-8% earlier, while organic growth stayed at 16-17%.
FY27 like-for-like growth is about 15% (1.5x IPM) per management; some low-ROIC businesses are being exited and some are now booked on a net-revenue basis, lowering reported revenue.
Gross margin gains come from scale purchasing and a commercial/agency role; full commercial role accounts for 10-15%+ of sales, with margins at least double normal distribution margins.
Management pointed to the 8-15% gross margin band on slide 28 for distribution; Q4 gross margin was 10.9%.
Middle East conflict: direct imports are a very small share of sales, so management says the company is largely insulated.

qa_highlights.question: Why did minority interest jump in Q4 and how much will it be in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 minority interest was abnormally high, about 38% of PAT, due to a customer pulling forward equipment sales at a partly-owned subsidiary. FY27 minority share is guided at about 25-27% of pre-minority PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 23% FY27 growth include calendarisation and GLP-1?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Calendarisation is about 11 points, and GLP-1 is built into guidance, with the company taking a disproportionate share given its cold-chain network.

qa_highlights.question: Why is working capital falling, and how much working capital will FY27 growth need?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop mainly to higher payables from MedTech, which has longer credit terms than pharma. Q4 annualised revenue of about INR7,600-8,000 crore means most working capital is already in the balance sheet, so incremental needs should be small.

qa_highlights.question: Will acquisitions continue, and at what valuations?
qa_highlights.answer: No new acquisitions are assumed for 6-8 months. Valuations remain 5-7x EV/EBITDA, and call options on remaining stakes are pre-agreed, typically over 3 to 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROCE outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 ROCE above 20%, with further upside possible over time, though not necessarily in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the company's competitive moat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a two-way network: about 100,000 customers and over 3,000 manufacturers. It said retail consolidation will stay limited, with chains under 15,000 stores versus over 1 million pharmacies.

risks_watch: Minority interest of 25-27% of PAT in FY27 materially reduces attributable earnings; watch for further put-option liability effects on net worth, which was flat in FY26.
Finance cost is expected to stay stable for a couple of quarters before declining; interest and depreciation rose sharply in Q4.
IPM growth outperformance has narrowed to about 1.4x as IPM rose to about 12%; FY27 organic growth depends on sustaining this.
FY28 growth not guided; management will provide more visibility in H2 FY27.
Payables-driven working capital improvement may reverse if MedTech mix or credit terms change; the 50% EBITDA-to-OCF target depends on this.

rows.why: GLP-1 sales are INR10-12 crore per month (about 5% of industry GLP value) and built into FY27 guidance, but no new product launch dates were given.

rows.label: MedTech mix lifts gross margin
rows.why: MedTech is over 15% of revenue, could reach about 20% in 2-3 years, and commercial/agency margins are at least double normal distribution margins; Q4 gross margin was 10.9%, up 110 bps YoY.

rows.label: Finance cost to decline after stable period

rows.why: IPO funds are used up and acquisitions were debt- or investment-funded; Q4 depreciation rose about 50% QoQ, so finance cost relief is not near-term.

544122|2026-06.headline: Entero Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 38.2% YoY to INR1,940 crore and EBITDA margin reached 5.0%, already meeting full-year FY27 margin guidance.
544122|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 38.2% YoY to INR1,940 crore (40% like-for-like), with organic growth of 17.8% reported and 19.6% like-for-like versus an underlying pharma market growth of 13.8%. Gross margin expanded 147 bps to 11.4% and EBITDA margin expanded 143 bps to 5.0%, with EBITDA up 94% YoY. PAT rose 72% YoY to INR52 crore, but PAT attributable to owners was INR38 crore (up 37%) after INR14 crore of non-controlling interest. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of ~23% revenue growth ex-acquisitions, 5% EBITDA margin and 50% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion, and said no major acquisitions are planned in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: entirely calendarisation of prior-year acquisitions; no new acquisitions in Q1

financial_highlights.value: INR14 crore (~27% of PBT before minority interest)
financial_highlights.change: Q4 was about INR17 crore per the call

segments.name: Core pharma distribution
segments.commentary: Majority of business is demand fulfilment with lower gross margins; margin gains attributed to scale-driven procurement. Low-margin sub-distribution accounts exited, which reduced reported growth by about 2.5%.

segments.name: MedTech
segments.commentary: Organic MedTech revenue on track to exceed INR1,000 crore in FY27 and carries higher gross and EBITDA margins than core pharma. Management said the business plays a demand-generation role, not only fulfilment.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance maintained: consolidated revenue growth of ~23% YoY excluding new acquisitions (about 11-12 points from calendarisation of prior acquisitions, rest organic).
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 5% maintained; management aspires to improve further and said H2 could beat guidance depending on H1 performance.
EBITDA to operating cash flow conversion of 50% on an annual basis; OCF is after working capital changes.
FY27 effective tax rate guidance of 22.5%; FY28 guidance to be given near FY27 close.
Interest cost expected to stay broadly in the same range as Q1 for the rest of the year.
Employee cost increments fell mainly in Q1 (effective 1 April); no major increase expected thereafter.

Medium-term: management said it can grow at over 20% in the next 3-4 years, organically and inorganically, and modelling 20% is a safe assumption; ROCE of 25-30% was cited as possible in that period; internal aspiration EBITDA margin above 6%.
No revision to working capital days guidance; management will review after H1.
capex_capacity: Platform: 138 warehouses across 475 districts in 19 states; 72,000+ retail customers, 2,300+ hospital customers, 83,400+ SKUs, 3,000+ manufacturer relationships.
Depreciation: Q1 level expected to be the going-forward run-rate, subject to any major new capex; Q4 included depreciation on certain machines given to customers.
No major acquisitions planned for FY27, though a pipeline exists; a small Andhra Pradesh surgical consumables deal (with Sai Pharma) was completed and is immaterial to revenue.
Around INR200 crore of debt was taken for the last acquisition, disbursed late Jan/early Feb 2026.
demand_pricing: IPM growth has moved to double digits in the last two quarters (earlier 7-9%), driven mainly by volume; management could not isolate a specific cause.
Management said it cannot forecast future IPM growth and built its organic forecast on a lower industry growth assumption.
Growth above market is attributed to wallet share gains from better fill rates, product availability, range and more principal collaborations.
Q1 revenue was partly pulled into Q4 FY26 through preponed government/diagnostic PPP billing, which made the sequential inorganic contribution look lower.
Management said MedTech has limited distributor competition and offers more scope for demand-generation contracts with higher gross margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth outlook for the next 3-5 years without acquisitions, and what ROCE is possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes it can grow at over 20% in the next 3-4 years, organically and inorganically, and sees ROCE of 25-30% possible at the end of that period.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the minority interest exist and when will the call options on it be exercised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said call options were agreed at deal signing at a valuation multiple matching the original acquisition, with exercise windows of 2-5 years; the minority is reinvested rather than paid out. Not all options fall due this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the sequential inorganic revenue contribution decline from Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said part of Q1 government project revenue was billed early in Q4 FY26 because of budget timing, so Q1 had a high base effect.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q4 one-off items recurring in other opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only part of the INR11.5 crore one-offs sat in other expenses; run-rate other expenses of about INR55 crore are expected to be sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 5% EBITDA margin be a floor for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained 5% for the full year but said it targets quarter-on-quarter improvement and may revise guidance after H1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did minority interest fall QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said minority share depends on subsidiary profit; Q4 had a revenue preponement at one subsidiary that boosted its profit share (INR17 crore in Q4 vs INR14 crore in Q1).

risks_watch: Growth in IPM has been unusually strong for two quarters and management cannot explain the cause, so sustainability is uncertain.
Non-controlling interest is about 27% of PBT and call-option buyouts (2-5 year horizon) will need funding, possibly from parent or subsidiary cash.
Q1 revenue was partly pulled into Q4 through government billing timing, so quarterly comparisons may be distorted.
Quarterly OCF is not disclosed; balance-sheet items (gross debt, net debt, OCF) will be given only at half-year and full-year, in September and March.
Interest cost is expected to stay at the Q1 run-rate after the INR200 crore debt drawdown.
Further exits of low-margin sub-distribution businesses could reduce reported growth again (about 2.5% impact in Q1).
544122|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the top line and margins, and clear on the strategy to consolidate and grow organically. Management was evasive on IPM growth drivers, on the quantum of OCF and net debt, and on non-controlling interest funding.
key_quotes: We have started FY27 on a very strong footing. Consolidated revenue grew 38.2% year-on-year to INR1,940 crores.
We are pleased to have delivered our full year FY27 EBITDA margin guidance in the very first quarter of the year.
We always retain full operational and cash flow control over every one of these entities and minority share of profit is always reinvested in the business and not paid out.
When I say 50% of EBITDA getting converted to OCF, means EBITDA minus working capital changes, whatever is the remaining is supposed to be 50% of EBITDA.

We should not be looking at OCF on a quarter-to-quarter basis. We should be looking at an annual basis because -- and that's how I have given the guidance that on an annual basis, we will convert 50% of our EBITDA to OCF.

rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 143 bps YoY to 5.0% in Q1 and gross margin rose 147 bps to 11.4%; management targets QoQ improvement and said H2 could beat the 5% FY27 guide, though run-rate other expenses of ~INR55 crore and the Q4 one-offs of INR11.5 crore weigh on the base.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: MedTech is on track to exceed INR1,000 crore organic revenue in FY27 with higher margins and demand-generation contracts, but no specific new product or brand launch was named.

rows.label: Minority call-option buyouts need funding
rows.when: 2-5 year exercise windows; not all fall due this year
rows.why: Non-controlling interest is ~27% of PBT (INR14 crore in Q1) and options exercise over 2-5 years; ~INR200 crore of debt was drawn for the last acquisition, and funding source is unclear.

rows.label: Net working capital days down to 61
rows.why: NWC days fell to 61 from 66 a year ago, but management made no revision to working capital guidance and OCF is only disclosed at half-year and full-year.

rows.label: Medium-term 20%+ growth and ROCE 25-30%
rows.why: Management said it can grow over 20% organically and inorganically and ROCE of 25-30% is possible, with ROCE at 21.1% in Q1 (from 11.5%) and internal EBITDA aspiration above 6%; this is an aspiration, not guidance.

tone.note: Management was confident on top-line growth (19.6% like-for-like organic) and the 5.0% margin, but evasive on what is driving IPM growth in double digits, on OCF and net debt quantum, and on how minority call options will be funded; analysts pressed on the sustainability of Q1 and the Q4 revenue pul

544124|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16% and EBITDA 26% YoY; management targets new products (poles, towers, guardrails) at 25-30% of revenue this year.
544124|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue up 16% YoY and EBITDA up 26%, with H2 revenue up 18% and EBITDA up 21%. The call centred on diversification: the Jharsuguda (Odisha) unit now produces highway guardrails, octagon and high-mast poles, and transmission line towers, with about 2,300-2,400 tons of tower orders on the books. Management said new products carry higher margins than pipe, but EBITDA margin remains around 4% today. Capex is limited to about Rs 10 crore in FY27, with no new debt planned, and CRISIL upgraded the rating from BBB to BBB+.

segments.name: Pipe (black and galvanized, water line)
segments.commentary: About 85% of revenue and the largest volume product; management ranks it lowest on margin per ton. Pipe installed capacity exceeds utilisation, with a 10-15% per year utilisation increase targeted; Jharsuguda pipe expected to reach about 60% in 1.5-2 years.

segments.name: Highway guardrail / crash barrier
segments.commentary: About 12% of revenue; Hyderabad order book about twice production capacity, and a second galvanizing line is being added there. Current crash barrier orders about 2,000 tons (about 1,000 each in Hyderabad and Jharsuguda).

segments.name: Transmission line towers
segments.commentary: Early-stage; about 2,300-2,400 tons of orders mainly from Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, with a target of 1,000 tons per month. Management says capacity and orders are roughly equal today; the orders are expected to clear in about two months.

segments.name: Octagon and high-mast poles / monopole
segments.commentary: Pole capacity about 150 tons, with machines arriving in about 10 days to lift it to 300 tons and a target of 500 tons per month this year. Order book about 300 tons, with orders being held for about 45 days; monopole certification expected by Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: New products (poles, towers, guardrails) targeted at 25-30% of revenue this year, versus 15% today.
Management said EBITDA margin should rise by at least 1% above the current 4%, and called its figures conservative; steel price swings and new-product pricing are the key variables.
Revenue target of around Rs 1,300-1,400 crore, with management calling this subjective; an analyst's FY28 Rs 1,700 crore reference was not confirmed.
Pole target of 500 tons per month; tower target of 1,000 tons per month; EBITDA margin on new products estimated at about 7-8%, not yet verified.
No new debt planned for FY27-28; capex about Rs 10 crore in FY27, to be spent only when demand is confirmed.
Jharsuguda galvanizing tank to be added in about 1-1.5 months; Hyderabad galvanizing expansion also underway.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 3,77,000 MT per annum: Maharashtra (Bombay) about 1,25,000 tons at 74% utilisation; Hyderabad about 96,000 tons at 67%; Jharsuguda is the growth site.
Galvanizing lines in Maharashtra and Hyderabad are described as running at about 100% of installed galvanizing capacity.
Jharsuguda: second galvanizing tank being installed in about 1-1.5 months (machines arrived, civil work ongoing); Hyderabad adding another galvanizing line for crash barriers.
Pole capacity to go from 150 to 300 tons with machines arriving in about 10 days, targeting 500 tons per month this year; monopole certification pending with CPRI.
FY27 capex about Rs 10 crore, to be spent only once demand is confirmed (for example, poles going from 500 to 800-1,000 tons).
demand_pricing: Pipe price: about Rs 52,000 per ton last year (black), now about Rs 65,000 per ton; management said steel prices could rise further if geopolitical tensions persist.
Order book: about 5,000 tons of pipe across all three units (about 2,000 Maharashtra, 1,800 Hyderabad), expected to be delivered within about 4 days.
Jindal Steel offtake agreement runs April 2023 to March 2029 with a minimum offtake of 1 lakh metric tons; the company produces ERW pipe for Jindal.

Middle East conflict raised transportation and furnace oil costs (galvanizing uses furnace oil); exports to Europe disrupted, with a shift to Australia shipped from Bombay. Management says costs are being passed through to customers so far.
Management says India demand is growing about 9% a year in utilisation, and the company has PWD registrations in Chhattisgarh and UP for poles and towers.
Management said that the new products are order-based, so they are less exposed to steel-price inventory swings than pipe.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected at the Rs 1,700 crore revenue level by FY28, given 4% today?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new products (monopole, octagon/high-mast poles, towers, guardrails) carry higher margins than pipe, so margin should exceed 4% by at least 1%; tower orders are at about Rs 10,000 per ton margin versus Rs 3,000-4,000 per ton on galvanized pipe.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA per ton on galvanized pipe (about Rs 3,000) well below some peers (Rs 6,000-7,000)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its figures are conservative and that the company makes water-line pipe, while peers make higher-margin API pipe and export, which Vibhor is not targeting.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and EBITDA contribution from new products in FY26, and what margin can they reach?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined an exact FY26 figure, saying the products are new; it targets 25-30% of revenue from new products and estimates new-product EBITDA margin at about 7-8%, not yet verified.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any impact from the Middle East war?
qa_highlights.answer: Transport costs and furnace oil prices have risen and are being passed on to customers; export to Europe is disrupted and redirected to Australia, but domestic demand is said to be healthy.

qa_highlights.question: What are the current order book and delivery timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Pipe about 5,000 tons (delivered within about 4 days); crash barriers about 2,000 tons (about one month); towers about 2,400 tons (about two months, given audit and inspection); poles about 300 tons (about 45 days).

qa_highlights.question: Was there any one-off or inventory gain in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said inventory gains are a regular process since finished product prices are reset monthly, so there is no major exceptional item; management said steel price spikes around the US-Iran conflict may reflect in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for FY27, and what is the debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 10 crore of capex in FY27, to be deployed only when demand is confirmed, and no new debt, as existing financing is already in place.

risks_watch: Margin uplift from new products depends on pricing for a new entrant; management said current prices are not a premium, and the 7-8% margin estimate is unverified.
Steel price volatility; inventory gains on pipe could reverse, and management flagged the Middle East conflict as a driver.
Pipe utilisation is well below installed capacity (Jharsuguda target 60% in 1.5-2 years), and pipe remains about 85% of revenue.
Monopole certification from CPRI is pending, with expected clearance by Q2 FY27; several department permissions are still pending.
Export disruption to Europe, plus higher freight and furnace oil costs from the Middle East conflict.
Concentration: Jindal offtake agreement (minimum 1 lakh MT per year) and tower orders tied to a few state electricity customers.

Management was vague or deferred on hard numbers (FY26 new-product revenue, peak revenue at current capacity, product-wise margins), and attributed margin and revenue uncertainty to steel price volatility.

rows.why: About 5,000 t across three units (about 2,000 Maharashtra, 1,800 Hyderabad) with Jindal offtake minimum of 1 lakh MT per year to March 2029.

rows.why: Pipe prices rose from about Rs 52,000/ton to about Rs 65,000/ton, and management says steel price spikes around the US-Iran conflict may reflect in Q1 FY27 while costs are being passed to customers.

544124|2026-06.headline: Vibhor Steel guides ~20% Q1 revenue growth, driven by Jharsuguda; Q1 pipe dispatch only 1,500 t against 1,800 t pipe order book.
544124|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 20% YoY, with growth coming almost entirely from the Jharsuguda (Odisha) plant, while Mumbai and Hyderabad were broadly flat versus last year. Order books for pipe, crash barrier, transmission line towers (TLT) and poles were described as well above normal, but the second galvanizing tank at Jharsuguda (expected around 1 September) is the binding constraint. Management said new-product contribution would start in Q2 and smooth out in Q3 and Q4. Figures on EBITDA, PAT and margins were not quantified in the call; the company also said it is planning a North India plant via a newly incorporated subsidiary, starting with crash barrier.

segments.name: Crash barrier / highway guardrail

segments.commentary: RSJ pole first order ~500 t, processed as job work with ~Rs 1 crore revenue; Monopole certification pending, expected Q3. Monopole has highest margin per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan to grow revenue from east and north India?

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split by product?

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from Jindal Steel, and what is the reduction target?

544133|2026-03.headline: Exicom Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 46% YoY to INR 388 crores and consolidated EBITDA turned positive at INR 0.3 crore for the first time since Tritium acquisition.

Consolidated revenue of INR 388 crores (+46% YoY) included Tritium, and consolidated EBITDA turned marginally positive. For full FY26, consolidated EBITDA was still negative at INR 103 crores and adjusted PAT was negative at INR 258 crores, with higher finance cost and one-time exceptional costs (VRS, Tritium retention, labour code). Management flagged a temporary inventory and receivables build as Hyderabad ramped up alongside Gurgaon.

segments.commentary: Grew 60% YoY in Q4 and 40% for FY26; record quarterly EV charging revenue of INR 88 crores (management figure, basis not specified). Full-year EVSE consolidated growth 72%; Q4 consolidated EVSE +83% YoY.

544133|2026-06.headline: Exicom Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 57% YoY to INR237 crore with EBITDA margin at 8.8%; consolidated EBITDA loss narrowed to INR22 crore.

Consolidated revenue rose 61% to INR331.1 crore, but consolidated EBITDA was a loss of INR21.9 crore (down from INR38.6 crore loss), as Tritium margins normalised after drawing down low-cost acquired inventory. Management guided to consolidated EBITDA breakeven within two quarters and Tritium breakeven by Q4 FY27, while working capital rose on parallel Gurgaon and Hyderabad plant operations and higher receivables.

544134|2026-03.headline: Platinum Industries Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 37% YoY to INR 132 crore, EBITDA up 95% to INR 15.3 crore; FY27 guidance above 40% revenue growth.

Full-year consolidated revenue was INR 450 crore (+15%), but EBITDA (INR 59.8 crore, +4.2%) and PAT (INR 51.2 crore, +3.7%) grew far slower. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth above 40% and a 35% CAGR over FY26-29, with the Egypt plant slated for Q3 FY27 and oleo chemicals sales starting April 2026. Raw-material inflation from the March geopolitical events created a temporary margin pressure that management expects to pass through over time.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the resin capacity is complementary, since additives are about 25% of a CPVC compound and resin about 75%. The company has supplied Supreme and Prince Pipes for 1-2 years, and the transition will take time.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no direct CPVC additive competition in India apart from one other Indian company. In lead-free, Baerlocher and Reagens are the main competitors, Goldstab is mainly lead-based, and pricing levels are understood by all players.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook versus the roughly 23% margins of FY23-FY24?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the change to a mix shift from high-margin lead-free to lower-margin CPVC, which started at a 3-7% contribution margin. Guidance is PAT margin of 11-12% and EBITDA margin of 13-15%, reiterated from the previous call.

qa_highlights.question: Project-wise capex, timelines and revenue potential for Egypt and Palghar?
qa_highlights.answer: Egypt is expected by December 2026, with INR 250-300 crore top line over three years. Palghar peak potential is INR 700-800 crore over three years, and top-line CAGR is about 35% over three years.

qa_highlights.question: What bottlenecks could delay commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not expect much delay.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the stearates plant and its effect on revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: The 6,000 tpa stearates plant has slipped to September/October 2026 from August due to a delay in one equipment item. Management said it would not materially affect FY27 revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Rivadu Lifesciences pharma and the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Business model is still being defined. Some revenue started this quarter, with collaborations with overseas companies under negotiation. No figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material inflation pass-through and contractual mechanisms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can pass on raw material price rises in normal conditions, but in the current war and shipping environment it cannot pass on sudden freight, CFS and transport costs. Lower lead-free PVC offtake was cited as the main Q1 margin driver.

qa_highlights.question: Egypt versus Palghar capex and why revenue potential differs?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR 67 crore for Egypt and INR 71 crore for Palghar. Both have about 60,000 tpa capacity, but Egypt is mainly lead stabilisers, priced at INR 110-150 per kg versus INR 250-300 for CPVC and INR 170-220 for calcium zinc in India.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects roughly a three-month working capital cycle.

qa_highlights.answer: Margins are expected to rise after the company builds its own manufacturing facility; for now it is using CDMO for seed marketing.

Grammage cut of about 4% taken in mid-April 2026 on small packs, with price hikes on larger SKUs; further action depends on competitor response.
Raw material basket: palm oil 26-27%, chana 21-22%, laminate 18-19%, potato about 6%. RM inflation impact about 4-4.5% so far, largely offset by grammage cuts, price increases and BOM changes.
Chana stock sufficient to about November 2026; H2 purchases to be made from market or imports if cheaper.
Distributor count 953 at end-Q4 versus 884 at end-Q3; 97% of business through direct distributors; DMS live at 90% of dealers.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY27 top line shape up now that supply is restored?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets Rs 330-350 crore revenue delta in FY27: Rs 170-180 crore core Gujarat, Rs 125-130 crore focus states, Rs 35 crore other channels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did focus states grow more slowly than core states in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Core states were hit harder by the fire, depleting the base. Q4 beat Q3 this year, reversing the usual 6-7% seasonal dip, and focus-state growth is expected to rebuild on distributor additions. Growth is expected at par near term and higher on an annualised basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is EBITDA margin guidance of 8-9% conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management held the 8-9% average guidance, citing raw material volatility. Exit run-rate is expected near double digit. Trade spend will be cut only gradually, with no major cut in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much more insurance will be received?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance claim expected at Rs 35-40 crore, higher than the Rs 10 crore gap, with receipt expected around Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital and debt rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher chana inventory bought ahead of expected price rises raised bank borrowing. Receivable days rose by 9 days, but the working capital cycle is within the comfort zone.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company cut prices or pack sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: A 4% grammage cut was taken in mid-April 2026. Further action depends on how the industry responds.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation in palm oil and packaging (cited as 15-20% basket increase); H2 FY27 chana purchases exposed to pulse prices, with El Nino raising rain-deficit risk to rural demand.
Unorganised Rs 5 price-point players under pressure; no action seen yet. Industry pricing discipline may change.
Insurance balance claim timing (Q2 FY27 expected) and asset restatement progress.
Focus-state growth recovery and distributor additions versus the target of 250 for CY26.
Rising debt and finance cost (about Rs 10 crore expected in FY27) on higher inventory.
Trade spend and advertising step-up (2.2-2.3% of revenue) could compress margins if market-share recovery needs more spend.
544140|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and specific on recovery metrics, distributor adds and capacity; more cautious and hedged on margin drivers and raw material inflation, with the 8-9% margin guidance held despite analyst pressure to raise it. Some answers were vague on pricing and on how industry players will react.
key_quotes: Rigan Raithatha: Yes, next year for the margin front as we have been guiding, we still speak to the same guidance that is 8% to 9%.
Rigan Raithatha: So, as far as trade spend is concerned, we would be obviously looking on that front but that our reduction on the trade spend would be in a very gradual phase wise manner.

rows.why: EBITDA margin guided at 8-9% for FY27 versus 6.7% in FY26 and 7.7% in Q4 FY26, with exit run-rate near double digit; offset risks are ad spend rising to 2.2-2.3% of revenue from about 1.7% and 4-4.5% raw material inflation so far.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at about 43% (FY26 level, FY27 guided 43-45%) is far below the 80% threshold, and FY27 capex is held at Rs 40-45 crore, mostly maintenance plus a Rajkot corporate office.

rows.label: Focus-state and UP expansion

tone.note: Management was confident on distributor adds, supply recovery and the Rajkot capacity, but cautious on margin drivers and raw material inflation, holding 8-9% EBITDA guidance despite analyst pressure to raise it; analysts pushed on focus-state growth, pricing discipline and the margin outlook.

544140|2026-06.headline: Gopal Snacks Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR 422.3 cr (+31.1% YoY) with EBITDA margin up to 7.4%; FY27 EBITDA guided at 8-9%.
544140|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 delivered record quarterly revenue from operations of INR 422.3 crore, up 31.1% YoY and 3.1% QoQ, with the fifth consecutive quarter of sequential growth. EBITDA more than doubled YoY to INR 31.5 crore (7.4% margin vs 4.7%), and PAT was INR 12.8 crore. Rajkot main facility restarted after the Gondal consolidation, though April saw about 5-6 working days of disruption (gas shortage and plant shift) that cost INR 12-13 crore of revenue in core markets. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20%+ growth (INR 1,800-1,900 crore revenue) and 8-9% EBITDA margin with exit near double digits.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 5.3 crore in Q1 FY26
No exceptional items in Q1; prior quarter had insurance gain, so QoQ not comparable
May and June at this level

segments.name: Core market (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Flat sequentially in Q1 due to April disruption that cost INR 12-13 crore; management targets INR 100-plus crore per month from here. Gathiya is the leading product, followed by namkeen, snack pellets and potato wafers; wafers grew 15% YoY in core markets. About 65% of Gujarat Gathiya market is still unorganised.

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 41% YoY; 100% of UP top line comes from two SKUs, Champakali Gathiya and Papdi Gathiya.

segments.name: Focus and other states
segments.commentary: Focus-state distributors rose from 440 (Q1 FY26) to 530 (Q4 FY26) to 567 (Q1 FY27); other states rose from 110 to 129. Maharashtra distributors went 194 to 205 to 198, with focus on Marathwada and the Nagpur belt.

segments.name: Other snack products
segments.commentary: Revenue in the other snacks bucket went from about INR 10 crore last year to about INR 23-24 crore per quarter, including Shot Go noodles, rusks, wafer biscuits, wafer rolls, jeera biscuits and washing bar.

segments.name: Alternate channels
segments.commentary: E-commerce was INR 2.79 crore in Q1 FY27 vs INR 2 crore in Q4 FY26. Modern trade was flat at INR 1.85 crore.

segments.name: Nagpur plant
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation is below 30%; 159 distributors were mapped to Nagpur, of which about 60 have moved to Modasa for logistics reasons. Third-party units at Kashipur (about INR 2 crore per month) and Manendragarh support other regions.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR 1,800-1,900 crore (20%+ growth), reaffirmed; management says it has held the stance on 20%+ growth.
FY27 EBITDA margin 8-9% for the full year, with exit run rate near double digits.
FY28 EBITDA margin guided at 10-11% with exit near 11%; sustainable target 11-11.5%; average reaching that level around mid-FY28-29.
FY28 PAT margin around 7-7.5%; minimum 20% revenue CAGR over the medium term.
Insurance claim of about INR 30-40 crore on the fire loss expected in Q2 FY27; management says documents are submitted.
Seven NPIs planned across Q2 and Q3, five of them non-palm-oil with better margins; 6 lakh outlets targeted by end of CY2026 (from 5.25-5.5 lakh).
capex_capacity: Rajkot main facility restarted; production consolidated from Gondal to Rajkot, with expected savings in power, fuel, logistics and operating costs as utilisation improves.
Modasa and Nagpur plants contribute to the network; Nagpur utilisation is below 30%.
Double-service coverage now reaches 38% of outlets; run rate up 14-25% where it has been rolled out. Pilot of ARS (auto replenishment) started; DMS covers most of the distributor network.
Retail touchpoints on DMS at 4.24 lakh; another 60-70k outlets are served but not on DMS.
demand_pricing: Raw material inflation was 5% in Q1; 4.2% passed on through price hikes and grammage cuts, 0.8% absorbed in P&L. Another 0.2-0.3% hit is pending and will be passed through.
Q2 inflation is slightly lower than 100 bps additional, per management.
Management says the company now runs at par or lower grammage than competitors and relies on distribution automation rather than grammage to drive volume.
Management expects roughly 75-80% of growth from volume and about 20% from price in the rest of FY27.
Chana stored till Q3-end; potato stored; palm oil and laminate are bought from the market with no major near-term increase foreseen.
INR 5 price point remains about 60% of sales (down from ~80% in FY22); management says no visible industry shift.
Regional brands in core states (Balaji, Gokul, Shri Hari) remain present; Miraj and Star brands shut, and Miraj has restarted.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 330-350 crore FY27 incremental revenue guidance still intact, and what is the festive run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the run rate is INR 150 crore+ per month, April was lower due to the Gondal to Rajkot shift, and 20%+ growth guidance stands.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin and when will it ramp up?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable target is 11-11.5%. FY27 exit near double digits, FY28 exit near 11%, and an average of that level around mid-FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core market run rate target and how is the Gujarat business growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of INR 100-plus crore per month in core markets. Double service is being scaled up, and more products are planned to lift margins.

qa_highlights.question: What are the A&P and trade spend trends?
qa_highlights.answer: A&P was about 1% of sales in Q1 against a 2.2% annualised budget; trade discount is 2.5% of sales versus about 3.5% earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Nagpur utilisation below 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: 159 distributors were mapped to Nagpur, about 60 were moved to Modasa for logistics, and the 250-distributor-a-year addition is below plan for the 300-400 km catchment.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an FMCG business with no order book, and daily run rate is steady with no month-end billing.

risks_watch: April disruption (gas shortage at Gondal plus Gondal-to-Rajkot shift) cost INR 12-13 crore of core-market revenue; watch whether May-June run rate of INR 150 crore+ per month holds and core Gujarat reaches the INR 100-plus crore per month target.

Raw material inflation: 0.8% of 5% Q1 inflation absorbed in P&L, another 0.2-0.3% pending pass-through, and management said Q2 inflation could be slightly below 100 bps additional; margin delivery depends on further price hikes and grammage cuts.
Insurance claim of about INR 30-40 crore on the fire loss is expected in Q2 FY27 from a PSU insurer; timing has slipped before and any delay affects reported profit.
Nagpur plant utilisation below 30% for over two to three years, with about 60 of 159 mapped distributors moved to Modasa; distributor additions below plan for the 300-400 km catchment.

Execution of FY27 guidance (INR 1,800-1,900 crore revenue, 8-9% EBITDA) and FY28 ramp to 10-11% depends on Rajkot savings, double-service coverage (38% of outlets) and seven NPIs in Q2-Q3, five non-palm-oil.

Competitive intensity: management says it now runs at par or lower grammage than peers, and A&P is about 1% of sales versus a 2.2% annualised budget, so any step-up in spend ahead of festive season could move margins.
key_quotes: So we strongly stand by our earlier guidance given of, you know, minimum 20% growth in this financial year over last year.
As of now, we are either at par or we are giving lesser grammage versus competition, but still we are able to maintain our revenue momentum because distribution automation is helping us a lot
So from May onwards, there is 0% disturbance in terms of operations.
So, we are FMCG company, Adarsh-Bhai, and typically we are not B2B company.
544140|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the top line and the 20%+ growth and 8-9% EBITDA guidance, which management reaffirmed several times. More cautious and less specific on the April disruption, Nagpur utilisation, Maharashtra distributor count and the insurance claim timing, where answers were partial and follow-ups were promised.

544144|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue up ~28% YoY and FY26 EBITDA up 16% to INR203.4 crore, but FY26 reported PAT still a loss of INR12.5 crore.
544144|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew about 28% YoY and total income reached INR1,758.8 crore (up 27.8%), with EBITDA of INR57.5 crore (margin about 3.3%) and a loss of INR5 crore versus INR13.7 crore loss a year earlier. FY26 total income was INR6,401.1 crore (up 15.1%) and reported EBITDA INR203.4 crore (margin 3.2%), while PAT was a loss of INR12.5 crore against INR10.5 crore loss in FY25. Management said the FY26 revenue and EBITDA were hit by acquisition costs, a cess provision and the new labour code impact, and it apologised for an error in the April 17, 2026 business update that misstated Q4 growth figures. Management guides FY27 to high double-digit top-line growth and consolidated EBITDA margin of about 4.8-5%, with sustainable profitability from Q2 FY27.

up 28% YoY, after adjusting Honda/Piaggio divestment, acquisition impact and one-off provision

financial_highlights.value: loss of INR13 crore (before exceptional items loss of INR27 crore on reported basis)
financial_highlights.change: adjusted PBT loss about INR5 crore; adjusted PBT before exceptional items positive INR8.8 crore

up 19% YoY; organic INR4,493 crore, up 16%

segments.name: Passenger Vehicles (new)
segments.commentary: Q4 volumes 8,090 units (up 20%), income INR654 crore (up 18%). FY26 volumes 32,572 units (up 9%), income INR2,551 crore (up 9%). Management cited entry-level supply shortages and OEM supply constraints in Keralam.

segments.name: Passenger Vehicle services
segments.commentary: Q4 service volumes 1,80,989 units (down 14%), income INR154 crore (up 2%). FY26 service income INR607 crore (down 2%) with volumes 7,39,794 (down 12%); ASP growth offset the volume decline.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicles (new)
segments.commentary: Q4 volumes 3,716 units (up 59%), income INR645 crore (up 46%). FY26 volumes 12,546 units (up 30%), income INR2,125 crore (up 32%); BharatBenz Punjab acquisition contributed.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicle services
segments.commentary: Q4 service volumes 52,443 units (up 13%), income INR97 crore (up 75%). FY26 volumes 2,02,647 (up 10%), income INR351 crore (up 28%).

segments.commentary: Q4 new vehicles 3,079 units (up 138%), income INR50 crore (up 113%); service volumes 11,261 (up 81%), income about INR3 crore. FY26 new vehicles 8,154 units (up 89%), income INR137 crore (up 72%); service volumes 39,659 (up 79%), income about INR9 crore (up 18%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 target of high double-digit top-line growth and consolidated EBITDA margin moving to about 4.8-5%; PAT approaching FY24 levels.
Sustainable profitability expected from Q2 FY27; Q1 FY27 still expected to be loss-making due to Maruti and JLR supply constraints.
PV service volumes guided to grow at least 10-12% in FY27, with ASP growth of about 12-13%; CV service volumes guided up 7-8% with ASP up 8-10%.
Standalone sales margin guided at about 3-4% in FY27; spare parts margin guided back to 5.5-6% with revenue growth of 6-8% (ex-BKT).
JLR volume guidance of 550-600 vehicles in FY27 after about 380 Audi/JLR volume shortfall in FY26 (guided about 450); Audi expected to break even this year.
Non-Keralam revenue share to exceed 50% in FY27 from about 47% in FY26; no high-value acquisitions planned in FY27, focus on consolidating FY26 acquisitions.
Inventory to be held at or below 30 days for passenger cars; debt increase attributed to acquisitions, with ~INR520 crore of INR600+ crore debt inventory-linked.
capex_capacity: Three acquisitions in FY26: BharatBenz dealership in Punjab, Maruti Suzuki dealership in Telangana, and Audi dealership operations in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh; Honda and Piaggio businesses divested (volumes counted to August 2025).

Bank loan facilities increased from INR468 crore to INR643 crore; CRISIL A/Stable rating extended to March 2027.
Management said capex spends will be more monitored and no additional debt is planned beyond what is needed to run the current business.
Acquired Audi and Telangana assets totalled about INR85-90 crore of equipment and showroom assets, with acquisition cost approximately equal.
demand_pricing: Management said demand improved in H2 FY26 after GST reforms in September 2025, with stronger footfall, conversion and entry-level recovery; discounting moderated.
Shortages of entry-level vehicles in Jan-Mar 2026 eased in April-May; Baleno and Fronx have waiting periods.
Post OEM price increases, management reported no noticeable change in demand so far; some pre-ponement of bookings was seen.
Luxury segment: Q4 delayed by UK FTA price-cut expectation; price cuts applied to Range Rover SP and Autobiography, with bookings rising from April.
Service volume: running repair fell about 17-18% as the company deprioritised low-value jobs; collision repair volumes flat; free service volumes recovered in last 6 months.
Maruti share of service volumes about 65-70%; Maruti service volume decline narrowed from -7% (to Q3) to -2% in Q4.
Overall Maruti ASP up about 13% YoY; PV new vehicle weighted ASP up to about 6.5% from about 5.5% three years earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why did service volumes fall and what service volume and ASP growth is guided for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 service volumes fell about 6% and ASP rose about 14%, with revenue up over 8%. For FY27 it guided 10-12% PV service volume growth and matching ASP growth; CV service volume growth of 7-8%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the service EBITDA margin gap versus peers close?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated margin will not reach 18% because of CV and Ather mix, but the Passenger Car business should reach 18-19% service margin.

qa_highlights.question: How will standalone margins move from about 3% to 5% consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin drag to acquisitions and Telangana expansion; growth is to come from PV service volumes and ASP, plus JLR and Audi ramp-up, with consolidated EBITDA guided to 4.8-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add acquisitions and how will debt be reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: No high-value acquisitions planned in FY27. About INR520 crore of the INR600+ crore debt is inventory-linked; term loans will be repaid on schedule, and debt will fall if inventory release generates free cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is inventory under control and what is the demand reaction to OEM price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days fell from 49 to 36 (FY25 to FY26); management aims to keep it below 30 days. Post price hikes, demand was flat and supply has normalised in April-May.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company turn sustainably profitable and what happened in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable profitability from Q2 FY27. Q1 remains affected by Maruti and JLR supply constraints; service volumes expected to grow Q1 over Q1.

risks_watch: Reported FY26 PAT loss of INR12.5 crore; Telangana loss of about INR26-27 crore and cess provision weigh on profitability, with Ind AS depreciation on acquisitions.
Debt rose after acquisitions; management says inventory debt is about INR520 crore of INR600+ crore total, with inventory days to stay below 30.

Service volumes in running repair down 17-18%; management needs to show Q1 FY27 volume growth.
Fuel price and geopolitical uncertainty (referred to as a war situation) flagged as demand risks.
key_quotes: Before moving to the business performance, I would like to sincerely apologize for the error in the business update published on April 17 , 2026, for the quarter and the year ended March 31 , 2026, and take this opportunity to clarify the same.
Post the price increase announcement by the OEMs, we have not seen much of a change actually.
In terms of profitability from Q2 of FY '27, we should be having sustainable profitability.
Out of the INR600 odd crores, around INR520 crores is related to the debt on inventory.

544144|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~44% YoY to INR1,890 crore and reported EBITDA rose ~87% to INR71.5 crore (3.8% margin), with reported PBT turning positive at INR1.9 crore.
544144|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 44% YoY to INR1,890 crore, with new vehicle volumes up about 81% reported and about 91% like-to-like. Reported EBITDA rose about 87% to INR71.5 crore, margin 3.8% vs 2.9%, helped by a one-off ~INR5 crore lease-modification gain in other income. Organic revenue grew 33% YoY, indicating the existing network contributed alongside the FY26 acquisitions (RKS Maruti, Globe CV BharatBenz, Audi/Olympus). Management said the acquired businesses are now EBITDA-positive in aggregate (~INR9.4 crore) but still loss-making below EBITDA due to depreciation and finance costs; reported PAT was INR1.4 crore vs a loss of INR8.8 crore a year ago.

segments.name: Passenger Vehicles (ex-luxury)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR836 crore (+73% YoY reported, +54% excluding luxury per call); new vehicles 10,475 units (+83%); service volumes 1,90,801 (-5%) while service income INR169 crore (+11%). Organic PV revenue +49%. PV EBITDA margin ~4% per management, with Maruti ~15.5-16% and JLR ~17-18% at segment level.

segments.name: Luxury (JLR and Audi)
segments.commentary: Reported revenue +42%; new vehicles +39%; service volumes +87%. Organic luxury revenue +21%, service volumes +9%. JLR EBITDA INR10.5 crore vs INR8.2 crore a year ago; Audi EBITDA ~nil, with margin dip attributed to Audi.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicles
segments.commentary: Revenue INR564 crore (+33% reported, +35% per call; organic +21%); new vehicles 3,495 units (+41%); service volumes 52,647 (+15%), service income INR107 crore (+47%). Sequentially volumes moderated vs Q4. Management cites CV EBITDA ~3.6-3.75%.

segments.name: EV (Ather two-wheelers and e-VITARA)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR55 crore (+122% YoY; reported EV revenue +113%); new vehicles 3,330 units (+153%); service volumes 13,232 (+60%), service income ~INR3 crore. EBITDA ~INR2 crore; margin ~3.4%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects acquired businesses to be PAT-positive from Q2 FY27 onwards; RKS and Olympus targeted for PAT profitability by end of Q3, with Olympus possibly one more quarter.
RKS service volumes expected on track by Q4 FY27.
PV service volume growth expected at ~6-7% from Q2 (not the 15% previously guided), with ASP continuing to rise; Maruti service volumes expected to reach double digit from Q2.
Blended EBITDA margin: management hopes to reach ~4% and says ~4.3-4.4% by year end; 5% unlikely this year unless mix changes.
FY27 revenue targeted at INR8,200-8,300 crore vs ~INR6,400 crore in FY26 (~20-25% growth).
H2 PV growth so far running ~80-90% YoY in most months, expected to moderate on high base; Q3 flagged as key with Audi launch.
Capex limited to replacement and ongoing projects; no acquisition or expansion planned; surplus cash to be used first for debt reduction.
capex_capacity: Q1 network additions: new Maruti Suzuki service centre at Koyilandy (Kerala), two Tata CV outlets at Perumbavoor and Kazhakuttam, and a JLR sales and service facility in Nagpur.
New vehicle inventory ~32 days vs ~50 days a year ago; absolute inventory up only ~14% YoY despite higher revenue; sequential build ahead of festive season and OEM launches.

544161|2026-06.headline: D.P. Abhushan Q1 FY27 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR853.6 crore and PAT rose 77% to INR64 crore, but volume growth was only about 1-2%.
