544162|2026-03.headline: Bharti Hexacom FY26 revenue grew 9.4% and EBITDAaL 17.9%, with Q4 revenue at Rs 2,414 Crores (+2.3% QoQ) and EBITDAaL margin of 47.9%.
544162|2026-03.overview: Bharti Hexacom reported strong FY26 operating leverage, with EBITDAaL margin up 3.4 points to 47.6% and a record 395,000 net homes adds. Q4 revenue grew 2.3% sequentially to Rs 2,414 Crores, while ARPU of Rs 252 was dented by two fewer days and was about Rs 257-258 on an EDB basis. Management flagged handset price rises, lower international roaming and 5G pack consumption as ARPU headwinds, and a Rs 4,000 Crore-range regulatory provision was booked on a changed interpretation of an existing issue. The call was largely a joint Airtel-Hexacom webinar; Hexacom questions focused on lagging mobile growth versus Airtel, FWA versus fiber strategy, and payout.

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 operating free cash flow (EBITDAaL minus capex)

segments.name: Mobile
segments.commentary: Ended Q4 with 28.8 million mobile customers; net adds about 370,000 and smartphone adds about 478,000, the highest in four quarters. Management said the ARPU gap to Airtel has narrowed but Hexacom lags Airtel on FY26 revenue growth (8.3% vs close to 12%).

segments.name: Homes and office
segments.commentary: Record net adds of 148,000 in Q4 and 395,000 for FY26; FY26 homes and office revenue grew 51%. Q4 homes revenue rose about 21% sequentially, helped by FWA expansion to new pin codes, FTTH deepening and IPTV rollout.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given; management said it does not provide guidance and that Hexacom remains committed to progressively increasing dividend payout.
ARPU headwinds expected to persist from lower international roaming, handset price rises and 5G consumption packs; management said there are no red flags on ARPU.
Management expects Hexacom to stay competitive and look for ways to grow faster, including new convergence offers; smartphone upgrades could see some stress.
Hexacom will not give up on homes acquisition; in difficult terrain FWA is used to reach homes where fiber is costly, with fiber-first where available.
capex_capacity: Q4 capex was Rs 586 Crores, described as acceleration as planned.
FY26 capex directed to 5G densification, network modernization and homes and IPTV growth.
Management noted that Hexacom's growth is restricted to mobile and FTTH, which is fully funded, with fewer growth engines available compared to the parent.
demand_pricing: Smartphone upgrades and feature-phone-to-smartphone shift face pressure from rising handset prices; management said FWA connection costs have risen versus fiber in the last three to four months.
Competitive market; management described the ARPU headwinds as similar to other operators, citing lower international roaming and unlimited 5G packs that break the price ladder.
Homes ARPU on new adds is slightly lower than the traditional base, but acquisition ARPU has not declined materially, per the parent's commentary.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Hexacom mobile revenue growth (8.3%) lagged Airtel (close to 12%), and should it accelerate?
qa_highlights.answer: Soumen Ray said Hexacom is underpenetrated in its two circles and the ARPU gap has closed; postpaid and international roaming differences and smartphone upgrade stress may cause some lag, and convergence offers are being launched.

qa_highlights.question: Should Hexacom have a sharper payout ratio given limited growth engines and funded capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said dividend moved from Rs 3-4 to Rs 10-18 per share and it remains committed to a progressively rising payout, while growth engines available to the parent are not open to Hexacom.

qa_highlights.question: Could homes growth slow due to chipset and memory cost issues affecting FWA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FWA remains useful for reaching homes in difficult terrain such as the North East, and it will not give up on home acquisition, pivoting to fiber where available.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the ARPU shortfall beyond international roaming?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 5G pack adoption that breaks the price ladder, handset price increases pressuring 2G to 4G upgrades, and lower roaming; the quarter-average ARPU is not a red flag per management.

qa_highlights.question: Should homes subscriber additions continue at the current pace?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined forward-looking guidance but said the objective is to keep growing homes and there is no fundamental reason to ease efforts, though competition exists.

qa_highlights.question: What does the regulatory charge in Q4 relate to and is it new demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not new; an existing matter was re-interpreted with auditors and the audit committee and a provision was taken under prudent accounting, with no specifics disclosed.

risks_watch: ARPU trajectory with handset price increases, lower international roaming and 5G unlimited packs; Q4 ARPU was Rs 252 reported.
Homes momentum if chipset and memory costs keep FWA more expensive and push the company toward slower fiber rollout in difficult terrain.
Regulatory provision booked in Q4 on a changed interpretation of an existing matter; amount not disclosed in the call.
Mobile growth gap versus Airtel (8.3% vs close to 12% revenue growth in FY26) and whether it narrows.
544162|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 operating leverage and homes growth, but cautious on ARPU and handset-driven headwinds; management avoided guidance and deflected competitor comparisons.
key_quotes: Revenues and EBITDAaL growth came in at about 9.4% and 17.9% respectively.
We have increased the dividend payout significantly and we have been committed that we will be looking at a progressively increasing dividend payout and we continue to remain on that.
I would say it is competitive, it is not lagging the market and we continue to look at opportunities as to how to grow faster.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY26 EBITDAaL margin rose 3.4 points to 47.6% and Q4 margin was 47.9%, but ARPU headwinds and rising FWA and handset costs could offset operating leverage, and management did not guide on margins.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or store capacity was discussed; capex is directed to 5G densification, network modernization and homes/IPTV growth, which is fully funded and does not signal new capacity coming live, with Q4 capex at Rs 586 Crores described as on plan.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Record homes net adds of 148k in Q4 and 395k in FY26 with homes revenue up 51%, plus mobile net adds of about 370k in Q4 and smartphone adds of about 478k, the highest in four quarters; management says there is no fundamental reason to ease homes acquisition.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure was disclosed and management said Hexacom's growth is restricted to mobile and FTTH, which is fully funded, so no new capex programme or board-approved expansion was flagged.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or margin guidance exists to raise, and management said ARPU headwinds are expected to persist while mobile revenue growth trails Airtel at 8.3% vs close to 12% in FY26.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management gave no formal guidance, and flagged ARPU headwinds from lower international roaming, handset price rises and 5G packs (Q4 ARPU Rs 252, about Rs 257-258 on EDB basis), plus FWA connection costs up over the last three to four months.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said convergence offers are being launched to grow faster, and IPTV rollout and FWA expansion to new pin codes are under way, though no specific product dates were given.

rows.label: Rs 4,000 Crore-range regulatory provision on changed interpretation
rows.when: Q4 FY26 booked; cash and P&L impact over coming quarters unc
rows.why: Provision booked in Q4 on a re-interpreted existing matter with amount not disclosed beyond the Rs 4,000 Crore range, so further charges or a payout could follow.

rows.label: Progressively rising dividend payout
rows.why: FY26 dividend raised to Rs 18 per share from Rs 10 and management reiterated a progressive payout, with FY26 operating free cash flow at Rs 2,935 Crores and net debt about Rs 2,000 Crores.

rows.label: ARPU pressure from handset prices and 5G packs
rows.why: Q4 ARPU Rs 252 (about Rs 257-258 EDB) was hit by handset price rises, lower international roaming and unlimited 5G packs that break the price ladder, though management says there is no red flag.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 operating leverage, homes growth and the rising dividend, but cautious on ARPU, handset-driven upgrade stress and FWA cost increases; analysts pushed on mobile growth lagging Airtel (8.3% vs close to 12%), the payout ratio, and the nature of the regulatory provision.

544162|2026-06.headline: Bharti Hexacom Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4% QoQ to Rs2,510 Cr with EBITDAaL margin of 48.2%, while homes net adds slowed to 75k.
544162|2026-06.overview: Bharti Hexacom reported Q1 FY27 revenue of about Rs2,510 Crores, up 4% sequentially, with EBITDAaL of about Rs1,210 Crores at a 48.2% margin. Mobile added about 210,000 net customers on a 29 million base, with ARPU at Rs259 helped by one extra day. Homes, office and other business net adds were 75k and revenue grew about 8% sequentially; management attributed the slower homes intake to a deliberate tightening of acquisition quality. Operating free cash flow (EBITDAaL minus capex) was about Rs830 Crores and net debt excluding leases was about Rs960 Crores (0.2x EBITDAaL). The call was a joint Bharti Airtel and Bharti Hexacom webinar, and most Q&A addressed group-level topics.

financial_highlights.metric: Operating free cash flow (EBITDAaL minus capex)
Homes, office and other net adds

segments.name: Mobile
segments.commentary: Added about 210,000 net customers and 344,000 smartphone customers; ARPU Rs259 with one extra day. Management flagged seasonality, expecting stronger customer additions in the second half of the year.

segments.name: Homes, office and other
segments.commentary: Net adds of 75k, with revenue up about 8% QoQ. IPTV rollout is adding depreciation; EBIT margin for the CPE-based homes business is negative or immaterial until scale is reached.

guidance_outlook: No numerical guidance given for Hexacom. Management expects homes acquisition quality to recover, with momentum seen in the last few weeks and some unwinding expected in the next one to two quarters.
Management said it cannot give a timeline for the homes EBIT margin turning positive, but says unit economics are the same as peers and it will turn positive at scale.
Capex priorities are 5G densification, network modernisation, fiberisation and homes/IPTV; management said it will spend adequately if needed for competitive growth.
Management said it would provide the count of the roughly 15-17 of the 400 relevant cities that fall in the Northeast and Rajasthan circles, a figure it did not confirm on the call.
capex_capacity: Capex directed to 5G densification, network modernisation, and growing the homes and IPTV business; the quarter's capex figure was not disclosed separately.
Fiberisation remains a large ongoing task; Hexacom does not have the B2B/data-centre capex that sits in Bharti Airtel.
Depreciation rose 4.9% QoQ, driven by one extra day and rising IPTV rollout costs.
Hexacom operates in the Northeast and Rajasthan circles, where it uses a mix of wireless and wired lines because of terrain.
demand_pricing: Mobile ARPU Rs259 with one extra day; the group-level pricing debate centred on the need to repair the tariff architecture to charge for data, with the group expecting ARPU growth of 4-5% over five to seven years.
Homes acquisition was tightened after the FWA push brought weaker quality and higher churn; management said fundamentals of the homes market have not changed.
Rajasthan was described as extremely competitive, while the Northeast position is comfortable; intensity on customer acquisition is said to be no different from other circles.
Management said refurbished phones are circulating more with smartphone inflation, but no impact on data sub-additions is seen so far.
International roaming is improving from the prior-quarter West Asia-related decline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did mobile net adds weaken this quarter versus history, and was it circle-specific?
qa_highlights.answer: Soumen Ray said there is normal seasonality in customer depletion across the industry over 16-20 quarters and that additions typically pick up in the second half of the year. He declined to call out a circle-specific cause.

qa_highlights.question: Has the homes outlook changed given acquisition-policy changes and rising chipset costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no change in the market size, share-gain or pricing assumptions. The slowdown reflects a one-quarter correction in acquisition quality, which management expects to unwind in the next quarter or two.

qa_highlights.question: Why are energy costs lower year on year despite higher diesel prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Karthikeyan Velu cited seasonal solar-powered tower benefits and some one-offs. Soumen Ray added that diesel stock in DG sets means the full diesel price impact has not yet flowed through, and that the underlying sequential trend is as planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation rise 4.9% QoQ, and when will homes turn profitable at EBIT?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation rose because of one extra day and the IPTV rollout. Management gave no timeline for homes EBIT turning positive, but said it will once the business reaches scale, and that fiber rental versus owned fiber makes little difference at the EBIT level.

qa_highlights.question: How many of the 400 relevant cities are in Hexacom's circles, and how big is the homes opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Soumen Ray estimated about 15-17 of the 400 cities are in the Northeast and Rajasthan circles, and said the figure would be confirmed later. Wireless plus wired is the chosen strategy in these terrain-heavy circles.

risks_watch: Homes net adds stayed weak this quarter because of tighter acquisition quality; the next one to two quarters need to show a recovery.
FWA economics face pressure from higher memory and chipset prices, and the FWA pivot to fiber could slow rollout in some areas.
Homes EBIT remains negative or immaterial, and no timeline has been given for it turning positive.
Diesel price impact has not fully flowed through; energy-cost tailwinds may reverse in coming quarters.
Smartphone inflation and refurbished phone circulation could affect the customer wallet over time.
544162|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the underlying franchise and the quarter's numbers, but cautious and somewhat defensive on homes, where management described a deliberate, temporary slowdown in acquisition. Answers on Hexacom-specific margin and timing were brief and non-committal.
key_quotes: We ended the quarter with mobile customer base of 29 million with net customer additions for the quarter coming in at about 210,000.
Our operating free cash generation, which is EBITDAaL minus capex, came in at about Rs.830 Crores.
There is no fundamental change either in the assumption of how big is the market to how we need to gain share and three, how we need to price our offerings and give converged solutions.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 FY27 EBITDAaL margin was 48.2% but the energy-cost tailwind is partly one-off and diesel price impact has not fully flowed through (DG stock), while depreciation rose 4.9% QoQ from IPTV rollout and homes EBIT is negative or immaterial with no timeline to turn positive.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capex is directed to 5G densification, network modernisation, fiberisation and IPTV, but no capacity count or capex amount was disclosed for Hexacom and the quarter's capex was not separated out.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects stronger mobile net adds in H2 (Q1 added about 210k on a 29 million base) and homes acquisition quality to recover to old growth rates within one to two quarters after the 75k homes net adds this quarter.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed and no new capex plan or land/approval was announced; capex priorities were listed only in general terms.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numerical guidance was given for Hexacom, and management described homes as a one-quarter acquisition-quality correction rather than a source of upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Homes net adds were 75k with a deliberate tightening of acquisition quality, and FWA chipset and memory cost pressure plus diesel pass-through could weigh on margins if the recovery slips.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: IPTV rollout is under way in the homes business with no launch date or count disclosed, so a launch is hinted rather than dated.

rows.label: Homes acquisition quality recovery
rows.why: Management expects homes growth to return to old rates in the next quarter or two after homes net adds of 75k this quarter, with momentum seen in the last few weeks.

rows.label: Northeast and Rajasthan city count (15-17 of 400 cities)
rows.why: Management estimated 15-17 of the 400 relevant cities sit in these circles but did not confirm the figure and said it would be provided later.

rows.label: Diesel and energy-cost tailwind reversal
rows.why: Diesel stock in DG sets means the full diesel price impact has not flowed through yet, so the year-on-year energy cost benefit may reverse.

tone.note: Management was confident on the mobile franchise and quarter numbers but cautious and somewhat defensive on homes, calling the slowdown a deliberate one-quarter correction; answers on homes EBIT timing and Hexacom-specific margin were brief and non-committal, and most Q&A was group-level.

544166|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR113 crores and EBITDA 28% to INR23 crores (~20% margin), with PAT near INR8 crores held back by H2 hiring.
544166|2026-03.overview: Emmforce reported FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) revenue of about INR113 crores, up 27% YoY, with EBITDA of about INR23 crores (up 28%) and PAT of about INR8 crores. Management attributed the PAT moderation to manpower hired ahead of the US export programme and higher depreciation from EMSPL and capacity capex. The US OEM export order contributed only about INR5.5-6 crores, all in March 2026, after production started in December 2025 and final customer go-ahead came end-February. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR195 crores (INR165 crores automotive plus INR30 crores agri) and FY28 of about INR240 crores, with EBITDA margins of 20-22% and PAT near 10%.

financial_highlights.change: Moderated YoY due to hiring and depreciation

financial_highlights.metric: US export order revenue in FY26
Employee cost, H1 to H2 FY26
financial_highlights.change: Mainly attributed to US export order hires

segments.name: Automotive (drivetrain, US OEM and aftermarket)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity about INR200 crores with utilisation of 50-55%. FY26 automotive revenue about INR105 crores; FY27 target INR165 crores, with the ~INR60 crores increment mainly from the US export order. About 40% of automotive revenue expected from OEMs by end-FY27; management sees OEM share reaching ~60% over time.

segments.name: Agri (rotavator blades, parts, EMSPL)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity about INR150 crores with utilisation of 8-10%. Revenue run-rate about INR4 crores per half in FY26 (commercial sales from July 2025 per analyst question, TAFE sales from January 2026); FY27 target INR30 crores and FY28 target about INR50 crores. TAFE initially ordering about INR15 lakh per month, with its total monthly requirement of about INR35-50 lakh.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target about INR195 crores: INR165 crores automotive and INR30 crores agri; management said the INR190-195 crore figure is tracking in line for the current two months.
FY28 revenue target about INR240 crores, with agri contributing about INR50 crores.
EBITDA margin target 20-22% and PAT margin around 10% for coming years.
Order book exceeds INR500 crores, but management said only about INR60 crores per annum is executable, spread over the next eight years.
Asset turnover (gross basis) about 3x in FY26, rising to 3.5-4x in FY27.
Working capital to be funded from sanctioned bank lines and US export credit of up to six months; management said equity dilution is not needed and is open to invoice factoring.
No new product category planned for at least the next year; hydraulic gear pumps to become a separate division, though no numbers disclosed yet.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about INR350 crores (automotive ~INR200 crores, agri ~INR150 crores) against FY26 revenue of INR113 crores.
Dedicated greenfield US OEM facility commissioned; mass production started 15 December 2025.

EMSPL (agri and forging subsidiary) completed first year; houses a 1,600-tonne forging press and a fully automated rotavator blade line with major equipment from Japan; turned from cash loss to modest cash profit.
Facilities total about 150,000 sq ft in Baddi, Himachal Pradesh, with 600+ staff; R&D spend about 2% of revenue.
Capex in FY26 executed ahead of revenue ramp (capacity, backward integration, automation, forging, infrastructure) across automotive and agri.
demand_pricing: Management said the US customer visit (about two weeks, roughly 10 days before the call) showed positive response; orders above expectations and no recession signs seen.
Management said there is no dampness in demand so far; OEM business running at over INR5 crores per month and aftermarket doing well.

FY26 H2 revenue flat versus H1 on the base business; management attributed this to US customers running down inventory after the 25% tariff, with inventory rationalisation still ongoing while new orders came in.
Freight cost rose only slightly despite West Asia conflict; shipments on time; dollar realisations better per management.
TAFE blade order: initial share of about INR15 lakh per month, potential to reach 70-80% of its INR35-50 lakh monthly requirement.

New business of INR10-12 crores with PPAP samples submitted, commercial production expected Q3 FY27; another US bid order close to INR10 crores annually; long-term drivetrain order worth about INR10.5 crores per year.

qa_highlights.question: What was the final FY26 revenue from the large export order, and does it explain the margin hit?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR5.5-6 crores, all in March 2026. Management said the H2 employee cost increase (~INR6 crores to ~INR8 crores) was 90-100% due to this order's hires, with some senior hires for future expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Why is base business flat in H2 and what is the outlook excluding the export order?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers reduced inventory after 25% US tariffs hit their cash flows. Management said orders have since picked up more than expected and there is no visible slowdown.

qa_highlights.question: What gives visibility to scale agri from about INR4 crores per half to INR30 crores in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited full-season sales through Diwali, TAFE approvals and consistent ordering, distributor orders in Maharashtra, Karnataka and MP, and talks with large OEMs on blades and contract manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR500 crore order book is executable in FY27-28, and why is FY27 base growth absent from guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR60 crores per annum, spread over eight years. Management said guidance was kept conservative; the INR60 crore export increment is the only increase in the automotive FY27 figure over FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is working capital funding need and will equity be diluted?
qa_highlights.answer: Bank working capital is already sanctioned; US export transit is about two months and credit up to six months. Management said no equity dilution is needed and it is looking at factoring.

qa_highlights.question: Is there margin pressure from OEM business or input-cost headwinds (crude, war)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets niche parts with no pricing pressure, sees no margin dampness, and freight increase has been minor. Margin drag was attributed to manpower cost for the new project.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the group company merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the entity is a group company, not a subsidiary, and merger work is ongoing with a possible announcement in the coming months.

risks_watch: FY27 guidance requires automotive to rise from ~INR105 crores to ~INR165 crores; the ~INR60 crore increment depends mainly on one US export order, with its run-rate ramp still early.
Agri target of INR30 crores (vs ~INR8 crores in FY26) rests on TAFE scaling and on OEM talks that management would not detail; seasonality limits sales to about Diwali.
Working capital is elevated and rising with US export receivables; funding relies on bank lines and possible factoring.
Utilisation is only 50-55% in automotive and 8-10% in agri; margin recovery depends on hitting volumes.
Customer inventory rationalisation is still ongoing per management; watch H1 FY27 order flow.
Pending merger of the group company; no timeline or terms given. Hydraulic pump division has no disclosed numbers yet.

Answers on margin and risk were generic, and the call had audio issues that interrupted several questions.

544167|2026-03.headline: JNK India Q4 FY26 revenue rose 69.2% YoY to Rs 344.6 crore, with EBITDA margin at 15.2%; FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-30%.
544167|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs 344.6 crore (+69.2% YoY), with EBITDA of Rs 52.3 crore (+89.9%) at a 15.2% margin and PAT of Rs 33 crore (+149.5%). FY26 revenue reached Rs 838 crore (+68%), PAT Rs 64.8 crore (+114.6%), and the order book ended the year at Rs 1,961.4 crore after Rs 1,694.4 crore of FY26 inflows. Management attributed margin expansion mainly to project mix (legacy orders completed in Q1-Q2) and guided 14-15% EBITDA margin as sustainable. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 25-30%, with Dangote refinery and fertilizer reformer awards as key near-term catalysts.

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 order inflow / order book (31 Mar 2026)

segments.commentary: Contributed 72.7% of FY26 revenue and about 94% of order book value.

segments.name: Process plant
segments.commentary: Contributed 17.4% of FY26 revenue and 3.5% of order book.

segments.name: Special fabricated equipment
segments.commentary: Contributed 3.1% of FY26 revenue and 1.3% of order book; described as a new segment.

segments.name: Flares, incinerators and others
segments.commentary: Contributed 6.3% of FY26 revenue and about 1.2% of order book.

segments.name: JNK Chemdist Technologies (JV)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 7% of group revenue in roughly six months of its first year; JV order backlog about Rs 67-70 crore, bid pipeline about Rs 200 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at around 25-30% YoY, implying roughly Rs 1,050-1,090 crore on the FY26 base; management also called 25-30% feasible for FY28.
EBITDA margin expected in the 14-15% range going forward, based on Q3 and Q4 FY26 run-rate, with conservatism due to commodity price risk.
Revenue phasing: Q1 expected to be lowest, Q4 highest; H2 expected at roughly 40-60% of FY27 revenue.
Order book expected to cross about Rs 2,000 crore by end of FY27.
Operating cash flow expected to remain positive in FY27, though not on a large scale.
Dangote refinery fired heater award expected in Q1 FY27 and reformer award in Q2 or Q3 FY27; fertilizer reformer bid submission in Q1 with finalisation in Q2 or Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for yields and spreads in FY27 given the rate environment?

544177|2026-03.headline: Aztec H2 FY26 revenue up 12.4% YoY to ₹47.61 cr; FY26 revenue up 9.2% to ₹96.53 cr with EBITDA margin at 14.3%.

Health: management plans to grow group health only if pricing improves by about 5%, and expects growth of 50-60% if loss ratio also falls by about 2%.

Competition: new non-life entrants are coming; management said it is not losing sleep over them and that EOM relief for new insurers should be split between commission and management expenses.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the discounting benefit and will long-run Ind AS investment yield match IGAAP?

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the 11 June 2026 Supreme Court TP ruling on TP loss ratio and reserving, and is the step-up recurring?

544192|2026-09.headline: ixigo Q2 FY27 GTV rose 22% to INR 5,304 crore and PAT hit a record, but adjusted EBITDA fell 17% to INR 23.6 crore on a stepped-up hotel investment.
544192|2026-09.overview: Consolidated GTV grew 22% YoY to INR 5,304.47 crore and revenue from operations rose 13% to INR 320.96 crore, with contribution margin up 14% to INR 124.86 crore. Adjusted EBITDA fell 17% to INR 23.58 crore from INR 28.48 crore as management deliberately funded hotel people and technology spend. Reported PAT was an all-time high of INR 63.42 crore, aided by a INR 40.66 crore exceptional gain on the partial sale of Freshbus. Flights were weak: GTV grew 37% on higher fares, but revenue fell 8% as take rate compressed from 9.4% to 7%. Hotels were disclosed as a separate segment for the first time.

financial_highlights.change: All-time high; includes Freshbus exceptional gain of INR 40.66 crore
vs INR 5.17 crore a year ago; treasury income, excluded from adjusted EBITDA

segments.name: Trains
segments.commentary: Passenger segments up about 7% to 2.9 crore; revenue up 16% to INR 149.14 crore; CM up 29% to INR 47.23 crore (32% of revenue). OTA rail market share close to 64%. Food on trains moved into trains segment.

segments.name: Buses
segments.commentary: GTV up 32% to INR 752.65 crore; revenue up 24% to INR 81.04 crore; CM up 27% to INR 43.14 crore (53% of revenue).

segments.name: Flights
segments.commentary: GTV up 37% on higher fares, but revenue down 8% to INR 82.66 crore; CM down 10% to INR 35.68 crore, held at 43% of revenue. Take rate fell from 9.4% to 7%. International flight GTV up 59%.

segments.commentary: GTV up 2.6x YoY to INR 111.34 crore (up 39% QoQ), about 4.7 lakh room nights, take rate above 12%, revenue INR 8.1 crore. Contribution loss INR 1.21 crore vs INR 0.71 crore a year ago; CM -15% of revenue vs -55% a year ago. Brevistay consolidated from this quarter, so part of growth is inorganic.

guidance_outlook: Hotel investment (above and below CM) was about INR 11 crore this quarter; management expects a similar range of INR 10-12 crore per quarter over the next couple of quarters, not a firm guidance.
Hotel take rate expected to edge up over the next 3-4 quarters; no guidance given on the level for next year.
Hotel room night ambition to keep growing at triple digits over the next four quarters; aim to be largest budget-to-mid-market hotel OTA by room nights in 4-5 years.
Flights: management is not guiding to aggressive growth; October started softer than expected with capacity not yet back, and festive demand is a shade below expectations.
Management says it will not step up flight discounts beyond current fare levels.
Profitability for hotels not targeted near term; investment expected for 2-3 years, with company-level EBITDA kept around mid-single-digit levels.

Management says it is not in a rush to grow the directly contracted base faster than its own growth.

demand_pricing: Overall flight market volume down nearly 6% in the quarter; ixigo flight segment grew 7%.
Flight fares up about 30% YoY on several routes due to oil prices; capacity slow to return; load factors edging down.
Flight take rate compression attributed to higher discounts for NBU users, growing international mix and convenience fees forming a larger share of income.
Hotel take rate above 12% blended, versus the 16-17% level seen at other OTAs; higher take rates in mid-tier and independent hotels are the structural argument.
About 86% of hotel bookings came from existing platform users; 94% of transactions involve Tier 2 and 3 cities.
Hotel ATV around INR 2,200 per room night; management does not guide to a specific ATV level.
Trains: festive advance bookings helped; management wants to see momentum persist beyond the festive season before calling the recovery sustained.
Bus growth described as ahead of the overall OTA bus market for close to three years.
AI platform traffic is a low single-digit percentage of traffic for the category; agentic booking flow demoed at GFS, launch awaiting regulatory clarity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did flight revenue per ticket fall 13-14% against the recent average; is this a permanent share-gain strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher discounts were needed to keep NBU flight users affordable given the 30% fare rise, and international mix and convenience fees also compressed take rate. It said it would not step up discounts further at current fares.

qa_highlights.question: Is there early visibility on Q3 flight trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Festive demand is a shade lower than expected; management is cautious on flights and not guiding to aggressive growth, but says it will keep growing.

qa_highlights.question: When will hotel take rate reach 16-17% and when will the segment be profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: Take rate will edge up over the next 3-4 quarters as direct supply grows, with no next-year guidance. Profitability is not targeted near term; investment is expected for 2-3 years, with spending tied to observed returns and payback periods.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors frame hotel investment within guardrails?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment was INR 1 crore-plus above CM and about INR 10 crore below CM this quarter. Guardrails are customer payback periods and keeping company-level EBITDA in the mid-single-digit range, with a near-term range of INR 10-12 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What GTV mix can be expected over 3-4 years, and will rail share gains continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Hotels could be the second-largest GTV contributor in 4-5 years. Management expects rail GTV share to decline from the early 40s given 4-5% annual capacity growth; buses to be the second-fastest growing line after hotels.

qa_highlights.question: How much of a threat do consumer AI agents pose, and which segments are most exposed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI-platform traffic is still a low single-digit share and sees specialist vertical agents, and ixigo's proprietary data and peace-of-mind products as differentiators. Building products is easy; trust and distribution are the hard parts.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bus growth of about 28% too slow given supply and rail constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is comfortable with the current pace, trading growth for margin and a sustainable business, and noted bus CM is about 53% of revenue.

Hotel economics: blended take rate of 12% is well below the 16-17% at peers; contribution loss is widening in absolute terms and profitability is 2-3 years away.
Adjusted EBITDA down 17%; the reported PAT includes a one-time Freshbus gain, so underlying earnings are weaker than headline.
Rail: management says recovery is not yet proven beyond the festive season; rail GTV share may decline.
AI agents: consumer AI platforms could disintermediate bookings; the agentic booking flow awaits regulatory clarity before launch.
Inorganic: Brevistay consolidation adds to hotel growth; future acquisitions are unspecified.

544198|2026-03.headline: DEE Development FY26 revenue rose 38% to Rs 1,142 Cr and PAT 76.9% to Rs 77.2 Cr; order book Rs 2,040 Cr with FY27 inflow guided above Rs 2,000 Cr.
544198|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first year after most of the growth capex cycle, with Anjar fabrication and the seamless pipe plant commissioned. Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs 361.6 Cr (+26.3% YoY) and PAT Rs 27.7 Cr, against a high Q4 FY25 base that included Q3 spillover. Management split the business into core (piping, heavy fabrication) and non-core (power, biomass pallets), with core EBITDA of Rs 210.5 Cr (+64.2%) excluding non-core losses. The company guided to a Rs 1,500 Cr revenue commitment for FY27, a Rs 2,500 Cr revenue target by FY30, and a consolidated EBITDA margin above 19%, while the Malwa Power tariff revision and the Thailand HRSG job-work order were the main new items.

segments.name: Core business (piping, heavy fabrication, others)
segments.commentary: FY26 core EBITDA incl. other income Rs 210.5 Cr, up 64.2%, driven by execution, utilisation and operating leverage. Management expects consolidated EBITDA margin above 19%, with heavy fabrication margins similar to piping.

segments.name: Non-core power (Malwa Power)
segments.commentary: Tariff revised to Rs 5.22/kWh from Rs 3.5/kWh with retrospective recovery of about Rs 5.52 Cr; Rs 5 Cr of the retrospective benefit is in the quarter per analyst Q&A. Appellate challenge pending; plant still carries a qualified audit opinion.

segments.name: Non-core biomass pallets
segments.commentary: Biomass pallet facility recently commissioned, expected to offset current cash burn. Combined power and pallet revenue guided at about Rs 47.71 Cr in FY27.

segments.commentary: Unit works purely on job-work basis; about 60% of its roughly 14,500 capacity reserved for HRSG orders, with revenue of about Rs 150 Cr per year implied. Management said no capex is needed for this order beyond minor machinery.

Seamless pipe sold externally expected to earn about 20% margin, lower than captive use.

Gross margin decline in Q4 attributed partly to trading activity with about 95-100% material value; no clear commodity-inflation split given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Thailand HRSG order linked to the GE/Siemens/Mitsubishi gas turbine backlog, and does the Rs 150 Cr revenue need capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most orders are linked to the overseas HRSG market. Thailand works on job-work basis, so the Rs 150 Cr figure is mostly value-add rather than full revenue, with EBITDA margin above 20% and only minor capex.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the gross margin decline is commodity inflation versus mix, and what are the alloy and job-work splits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined a quarterly split, citing project-based business, and pointed to trading activity at 95-100% material value in Q4. Job-work orders are about 30% of the book; about 55-60% of thermal and HRSG work is alloy steel.

qa_highlights.question: Are order flows and margins sustainable with the new Anjar and seamless plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Anjar fabrication expected to be near optimal in FY27 and seamless 60-70% utilised. Consolidated EBITDA margin should stay above 19% even if percentage margin falls in heavy fabrication.

qa_highlights.question: Why is order book up about 50% while guidance is 20-25% growth, and why did inventory stay flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance was called conservative; capacity expansion may be needed. Flat inventory despite a higher order book was attributed to power-sector raw material arriving late, after orders were placed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is capex held back given strong HRSG demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is on the drawing board for new capacity, aiming for assets sustainable over 10-15 years, and will publish a blueprint soon.

qa_highlights.question: Malwa Power: how will the qualified audit opinion be resolved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects both plants to be slightly positive at current tariffs, so no impairment or contingency is needed. Audit finding expected to clear by Q3 FY27, per the CFO.

risks_watch: BHEL's slow release of thermal boiler-turbine-generator orders could delay domestic power orders and hit the Rs 2,000 Cr inflow target.

Rising debt and possible equity raise, with no decision yet.
Margin dilution from more material-supply jobs and trading activity; gross margin declined YoY and QoQ.
Dependence on Thailand job-work revenue, which is concentrated in HRSG orders.

544198|2026-06.headline: DEE Development Engineers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 31.6% YoY to Rs 294.5 crore and EBITDA margin hit 16.9%, despite ~Rs 25 crore of dispatches slipping into Q2.
544198|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs 294.5 crore, up 31.6% YoY, with operating EBITDA of Rs 49.7 crore (16.9% margin vs 16% a year earlier). Management said about Rs 25 crore of oil and gas dispatches, deferred by export customers amid Middle East disruption, moved into Q2. Profit after tax was Rs 16.1 crore, and the Rs 300 crore preferential issue (net ~Rs 293 crore, ~Rs 225 crore earmarked for debt repayment) closed in July. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of Rs 1,500 crore+ revenue, EBITDA margin above 19%, and order inflow of at least Rs 2,000 crore.

segments.name: Piping and heavy fabrication (core)
segments.commentary: Management guides Rs 1,150-1,250 crore from piping for FY27, with the balance from subsidiaries including Thailand. Piping and heavy fabrication are the large majority of revenue and order book.

segments.name: Thailand subsidiary
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about Rs 130 crore; target Rs 170-200 crore. Management says it is practically 100% booked for three years and no expansion is planned.

segments.name: Power PPA / non-core (Malwa, biomass pellets)
segments.commentary: Pellet plant (72,000 MT p.a., Muktsar) commissioned mid-Q1 FY27, so only partial contribution this quarter. Target combined non-core revenue around Rs 80 crore. Management said PPA EBIT went slightly negative (about Rs 1 crore) as fuel was diverted to the pellet plant; full operation expected from October.

segments.name: Seamless pipe plant (Anjar)
segments.commentary: Commissioned in FY26. Existing orders include about Rs 68 crore from L&T and a Rs 200 crore BHEL order, of which Rs 80-90 crore is expected to use in-house pipe. Management targets about 20% EBITDA on seamless pipe.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 1,500 crore+ reiterated; management called it a minimum and said the plan is to exceed it. Q1 is the weakest quarter, with Q4 typically the strongest.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided above 19%; management said it is 'absolutely on track'.
FY27 order inflow expected at least Rs 2,000 crore; Rs 700 crore already received, with Rs 1,300-1,800 crore expected in the rest of the year.
Net debt expected to be no more than Rs 400-425 crore by FY27 end; no plans for new debt this year.
Anjar plant utilisation expected at 60-65% this year and near 100% by end of FY28. Anjar revenue target of about Rs 1,500 crore by FY28-29.
Inventory days targeted at 150-160 by Q2 and 180-200 days for the overall working-capital cycle.
capex_capacity: Anjar pipe fabrication facility fully operational; seamless pipe plant commissioned in FY26. Plan is roughly 50-50 split between captive and outright-sale use of Anjar capacity.
Biomass pellet plant (72,000 MT p.a.) at Malwa Power Plant, Muktsar, commissioned in Q1 FY27.
Nuclear sector entry planned via a partner; management aims to finalise the partnership agreement in Q2 FY27.
No capex or capacity expansion planned at Thailand facility.
Preferential issue proceeds of about Rs 293 crore net: about Rs 224-225 crore for debt or working-capital repayment, balance for general corporate purposes.
demand_pricing: Revenue slippage: about Rs 25 crore of oil and gas dispatches deferred to Q2 as export customers delayed take-offs due to the Middle East situation; material is ready.

Siemens: MoU for GT piping starting at 10 units next year, then 15, then 25-30 units. Each GT unit is about EUR 1-1.5 million. Siemens team to visit Anjar in the third week of August.
BHEL: slower than expected, but about Rs 200 crore order received last quarter and more tenders expected to be finalised next quarter. L&T has awarded all orders offloaded so far.
Export mix: about 50% export and 50% domestic for FY27. The order book includes about Rs 400 crore of India HRSG work and about Rs 200 crore from Thailand.
Gross margin pressure attributed to higher material content in power-sector jobs (versus job-work) and the mix shift. Management said conversion costs are lower for power jobs.
Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited domestic order of Rs 386.82 crore received in the quarter, described as one of the largest single orders in recent history.
Gulf reconstruction: inquiries are coming via OEMs; not yet direct, and not included in projections for five years.

qa_highlights.question: Status of GE HRSG orders and Siemens GT piping?
qa_highlights.answer: GE GT orders continue, HRSG order yet to come despite agreement for 15-16 units. Siemens MoU for 10 units next year, 15 the year after, then 25-30. Each GT unit about EUR 1-1.5 million.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 2,000 crore order inflow guidance still valid given delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said inflow may exceed Rs 2,000 crore. Rs 700 crore already received, with Rs 1,300-1,800 crore expected in the remainder of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PPA EBIT turn negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Limited fuel meant the company prioritised the pellet plant over the power plant. Full operation of both is expected from October when new fuel arrives.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt trajectory and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt Rs 718 crore at Q1 close versus Rs 733 crore at FY26 close, expected to fall to Rs 400-425 crore by FY27 end. Rs 224 crore used for working-capital limits reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher material content in power-sector jobs and a mix shift away from job-work. Management still expects EBITDA above 19%.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate for modelling?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone rate 25.17%; consolidated effective rate about 20-21% because of the Thailand subsidiary and subsidy income.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 62.5% and management said the focus for FY27 is asset turns, cash generation and return ratios; Thailand has no expansion planned and net debt is to fall to Rs 400-425 crore with no new debt.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said FY27 revenue of Rs 1,500 crore+ is a minimum and the plan is to exceed it, and order inflow may exceed Rs 2,000 crore against Rs 700 crore already received.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Rs 25 crore of oil and gas dispatches slipped into Q2 on Middle East delays, GE HRSG order (agreement for ~15-16 units) is not yet placed, BHEL is slower than expected, and creditor days fell to 34 from 66.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Nuclear sector entry via a partner is planned with the partnership agreement targeted for Q2 FY27, but no product revenue figure was given.

rows.label: Order inflow of at least Rs 2,000 crore in FY27
rows.why: Rs 700 crore already received with Rs 1,300-1,800 crore expected in the remainder, plus Siemens GT piping MoU ramping from 10 units next year and a Rs 386.82 crore BPCL order in the quarter.

rows.label: Net debt down to Rs 400-425 crore by FY27 end
rows.why: Net debt fell to Rs 718 crore at Q1 from Rs 733 crore at FY26 close, and about Rs 224-225 crore of preferential issue proceeds are earmarked for debt or working-capital repayment.

rows.label: Inventory days down to 150-160 by Q2
rows.why: Inventory days are 174 versus 243 a year ago, and the overall cycle is targeted at 180-200 days, but debtor days rose to 123 from 99 and creditor days fell to 34 from 66.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 revenue (Rs 1,500 crore+), margin (above 19%) and order inflow (at least Rs 2,000 crore), but less definite on timing for GE HRSG, BHEL tenders and PPA fuel supply; analysts probed working capital, gross margin and tax rate.

544202|2026-03.headline: Stanley Lifestyles FY26 gross margin rose 151 bps to 57.5%, but Q4 revenue fell on B2B export pull-down and management guides only conservative FY27 growth.
544202|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a transition year spent acquiring franchise markets (Chennai, Hyderabad, Pune) into company-owned stores and consolidating subsidiaries into one listed entity. Q4 FY26 saw a decline in B2B demand from mid-Q4, with roughly Rs. 15 crore of B2B revenue pulled down due to West Asia conflict disruptions to a large export client. Gross margin for FY26 improved to 57.5% from 56.3%, while cash was about Rs. 200 crore versus Rs. 215 crore a year earlier despite capex above Rs. 60 crore. Management opened 11 stores and closed three over 12 months, and guided to aspirational double-digit growth but a conservative stance for FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Order book at start of FY27
Higher depreciation and finance cost (lease front-loading under Ind AS)

financial_highlights.value: about 4% for mature stores (over 3 years); Stanley Level Next +11.6%, Sofas & More +3.5%, Stanley Boutique -8.1%

financial_highlights.change: as franchise markets were converted to COCO

segments.name: B2C (retail, COCO and FOFO)
segments.commentary: About 70% of Q4 FY26 revenue; roughly 75% of B2C business is driven by confirmed customer orders. Store network is 49 COCO and 22 FOFO stores, with 33 stores under 3 years and 38 over 3 years.

segments.name: B2B / export
segments.commentary: About 30% of Q4 FY26 revenue. Around Rs. 15 crore pulled down in Q4 due to delays from West Asia conflict on exports to a large global furniture brand; management expects recovery around Q2 FY27 and is targeting high-end B2B and some exports.

guidance_outlook: Management is aspirational about double-digit growth in FY27 but says it will be very conservative given global conditions, prioritising profitability and cash.
B2C and B2B supply chain and export disruptions expected to flow into FY27; B2B export recovery hoped for by Q2 FY27.
QCO regulation on furniture imports effective 15 August 2026, expected to deter imports, the main competition.
Flagship 60,000+ sq ft Hyderabad store (Stanley Superlative Living) now scheduled to go live around July 2026 after regulatory delays.
Sri Lanka first store (Sofas & More brand, pilot with Singer Group) to open at start of Q2 FY27, with possible expansion to five or six shop-in-shops.
Management expects handovers in top six cities to accelerate and peak in FY28 and FY29; new digital platform and revamped website targeted by end FY27.
capex_capacity: Capex in FY26 exceeded Rs. 60 crore, the highest ever; management says investment will continue for some time while consolidating mature markets.
Opened 11 new stores and shut three underperforming stores in the last 12 months; five additional stores expected to commence operations shortly.
Over half of stores are still in gestation/ramp-up; ROI on a store is about 3 years (15-18 months in some catchments, 24-36 months in Bangalore micro-markets).
Three to four legacy stores to be relocated or consolidated into larger formats; consolidation to be completed by end FY27; store count may fall.
Around 85-90% of store furniture is now made in India versus about 70% three to four years ago; delivery in 6-8 weeks versus 4-5 months for imports.
demand_pricing: Mature stores over three years grew about 4% annually over the last four years; management expects 10-15% going forward as kitchen and cabinetry is added.
Project handovers across top six cities are delayed; footfalls are steady but conversion cycles longer.
Competition mainly from import traders (Europe, Turkey, China high-end); local manufacturer-designers are secondary; low-end B2B is not targeted due to unorganised competition.
Gross margin supported by best-cost country sourcing; USD and EUR appreciation raised input costs.
Marketing spend has historically stayed below 10% of revenue; management plans to increase event and fair participation (AD, ELLE Decor) and possibly social media influencers from 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Growth of stores open over three years and why company-owned store revenue looks flat since 2023 despite more stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Mature stores have grown about 4% a year; the flat revenue reflects a 35% drop in franchisee business and about Rs. 18-20 crore lost from leather trading moved to cash-and-carry, plus Rs. 24 crore cited in total.

qa_highlights.question: What were the short-term disruptions in the last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: A large global furniture brand's B2B exports to the Middle East were halted by the war-related logistics standstill; orders were postponed and recovery is expected by Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why not pursue low-end B2B inquiries given low plant utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its back-end is built for premium B2C and it cannot compete with unorganised low-end B2B; it is pursuing high-end B2B inquiries from MNCs and considering exports.

qa_highlights.question: Store economics and when stores start generating cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says ROI, including interest on capex, is about 3 years; some catchments take 15-18 months and Bangalore micro-markets 24-36 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross margin down sequentially in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 to raw material delays due to the US-Iran war and about Rs. 15 crore B2B revenue pull-down; it said full-year gross margin improved and B2C margins are secure.

qa_highlights.question: Digital discovery, website and pricing policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management admitted it has been slow on digital, said SAP is implemented, and promised a new AI-assisted website, with AR/VR tools, by end FY27.

risks_watch: Q4 FY26 revenue decline and continued B2B export disruption from West Asia conflict; management expects recovery only from Q2 FY27.
Franchisee business down 35%, and conversion of franchise markets to COCO adds capex and lease-related depreciation and finance cost.
Store ramp-up: over half of stores are immature and 3-year ROI is management's own metric; watch for store closures and relocations.
Subsidiary merger into a single listed entity, with the Rs. 3.3 crore labour code exceptional charge and KMP compensation overlap.
Effectiveness of QCO from 15 August 2026 in curbing imports, and Hyderabad flagship going live around July 2026.
544202|2026-03.management_tone: Confident about long-term positioning and the debt-free balance sheet, but cautious and defensive on near-term top-line growth, with management repeatedly attributing weakness to external factors. Answers on digital capability, pricing and the franchise-to-COCO transition were candid about past slowness but light on hard numbers.
key_quotes: We are not building Stanley for the next quarter; we are building Stanley for the next decade.
In the luxury segment, scale without control leads to dilution. We have consciously chosen control.
So, we are very prudent in our investment.

While we are quite aspirational to deliver definitely double-digit growth, I hope that in terms of how the global situation is, we are reserving ourselves and I would say we will be very conservative.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY26 gross margin rose 151 bps to 57.5% from 56.3%, but Q4 gross margin fell sequentially on raw material delays and the Rs. 15 crore B2B pull-down, and the Rs. 14.7 crore higher depreciation and finance cost (Ind AS lease front-loading) plus the Rs. 3.3 crore labour code charge weigh on EBITDA.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Five additional stores are to start shortly, the 60,000+ sq ft Hyderabad flagship is due around July 2026 after regulatory delays, and a Sri Lanka store opens at the start of Q2 FY27, though three to four legacy stores are being relocated or consolidated and store count may fall by FY27 end.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management is aspirational about double-digit FY27 growth but calls its stance very conservative with no number given; mature stores grew about 4% a year, the franchisee business fell 35%, and the order book is about Rs. 62 crore versus Rs. 45 crore a year earlier, with B2B export recovery hoped for only by Q2 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY26 capex exceeded Rs. 60 crore (highest ever) and management is prioritising profitability and cash, with cash at about Rs. 200 crore versus Rs. 215 crore, while over half of stores are still ramping up and consolidation of legacy stores runs to end FY27; no new capacity beyond committed stores was flagged.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says FY27 will be very conservative given global conditions, with Q4 revenue down on a Rs. 15 crore B2B pull-down and export recovery not expected before Q2 FY27.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: B2B export disruption from the West Asia conflict and the 35% franchisee decline could carry into FY27, and the Hyderabad store timing and QCO effectiveness from 15 August 2026 are dependent on outside events.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: A new AI-assisted digital platform, website with AR/VR tools and revamped site are targeted by end FY27, and kitchen and cabinetry addition is expected to lift mature-store growth to 10-15%, though no product launch date is given.

rows.label: Sri Lanka first store (Sofas & More, Singer Group pilot)
rows.why: Store is scheduled to open at the start of Q2 FY27, with possible expansion to five or six shop-in-shops if the pilot works.

rows.label: B2B export recovery from large global furniture brand
rows.why: About Rs. 15 crore of Q4 B2B revenue was pulled down by West Asia logistics delays, and management hopes for recovery by Q2 FY27, which is conditional on the conflict easing.

rows.label: QCO regulation on furniture imports
rows.why: The QCO takes effect 15 August 2026 and is expected to deter imports, the main competition, supporting the Rs. 62 crore order book and B2C share gains.

tone.note: Management was confident on the debt-free balance sheet, the 85-90% India-made furniture mix and the QCO tailwind, but cautious and defensive on near-term top-line growth, attributing weakness to the West Asia conflict and giving no hard FY27 number. Analysts pushed on store ROI, the franchise-to-CO

544202|2026-06.headline: Stanley Lifestyles Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR 9,935 lakhs (from 10,861 lakhs) and PAT was just INR 65 lakhs, on delayed handovers and B2B shipment disruption.
544202|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations declined about 8.5% YoY to INR 9,935 lakhs in Q1 FY27, driven by slower retail conversions as residential handovers slipped 12 to 18 months and by B2B billing that stalled due to West Asia freight disruption. Management said gross margin was maintained and EBITDA was INR 1,722 lakhs (17.3% margin), with PAT of INR 65 lakhs. The company opened 3 Bangalore stores and closed 4 (3 Bangalore, 1 Mumbai), entered Sri Lanka via a JV, opened a Jaipur store, and announced a store-format overhaul (Stanley Superlative Living) plus a proposed amalgamation of subsidiaries. An internal audit flagged a fraud by the company secretary, under investigation.

financial_highlights.change: Down from INR 10,861 lakhs in Q1 FY26 (about -8.5% YoY)

financial_highlights.value: Maintained (no figure given on Ind AS basis)

financial_highlights.metric: Pre-Ind AS gross margin (average, all formats)
Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin (average, all formats)

financial_highlights.value: About INR 90 lakhs per month (about 2.25% of annual revenue)
financial_highlights.change: Expected to stay roughly flat as company adds people
Up from INR 62 crores as on March 2026

segments.name: Retail (COCO and franchise)
segments.commentary: Customer inquiries and footfall are encouraging but conversions are slower as buyers (80-85% new premium/luxury home buyers) await possession. Network: 47 COCO stores, of which 35 are store-level EBITDA positive per management. FOFO franchisees are on a cash-and-carry model with no credit given.

segments.name: B2B / export
segments.commentary: Products are produced and held, but invoicing did not happen in Q1 due to freight and logistics disruption from the Middle East conflict; management called the B2B visibility the highest ever. US tariffs have stalled export talks, and the company is pinning hopes on BIS certification enforcement for imports from 14 August 2026.

segments.name: Sofas & More / Stanley Boutique / Stanley Level Next
segments.commentary: Average annual revenue per store: Sofas & More INR 4.5 to 6 crores; Stanley Boutique INR 4 to 6 crores; Stanley Level Next INR 10 to 14 crores (some stores up to INR 20 crores). Boutiques to be converted into Sofas & More over 2 to 3 years in the six metros.

guidance_outlook: Brand architecture change (3 brands into one Stanley and one Sofas & More) expected to complete in about 3 to 4 quarters; conversion of Boutiques to Sofas & More is gradual, taking 2 to 3 years.
Target of 15% to 20% YoY same-store growth for mature stores; Q1 SSSG was slightly negative due to format changes.
Store-level EBITDA break-even expected 6 to 12 months after opening; ROI (capital with interest) expected in 24 to 36 months.
Management says manufacturing can scale to about 2x current revenue by recalibrating the factory with a few added machines.
No explicit margin guidance given; corporate costs expected to stay roughly flat as the company adds people for the new formats.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity utilisation about 68% to 70%; over 1,000 skilled artisans said to be fully utilised.
Sofas & More capex about INR 2 crores per store (5,000 to 6,000 sq ft). Large single-city flagship stores (Stanley Superlative Living) capex up to INR 20 crores.
Hyderabad Jubilee Hills (Road No. 45) Superlative store said to be 2 to 3 weeks from opening; large-format plans for Mumbai, Bangalore and Delhi, with one city one mega store in four cities.
Q1 openings: 3 Bangalore stores (2 Varthur, 1 Mysore Road). Closures: 4 (3 Bangalore, 1 Mumbai); management said 2 of the Bangalore closures had already been relocated.
New stores: Stanley Boutique Colombo, Sri Lanka (July 2026, JV with Singer Sri Lanka PLC) and Sofas & More Jaipur (first Rajasthan store).
demand_pricing: Demand demand: customer inquiries and footfall encouraging, but conversions slowed as residential handovers were delayed 12 to 18 months in several projects; West Asia supply chain issues constrained construction material availability.
Stanley Superlative Living targets buyers with budgets of INR 3 to 5 crores and above, aiming for average ticket size up to about 10x current levels with full home design, build and install.
Management said 6 COCO cities (Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Delhi, Chennai and one other) account for about 80% of India's luxury housing, per company claim.
Sofas & More: about 95% of customers are direct buyers without designers or specifiers; Stanley relies more on specifiers and design-led purchases.
Export exposure is small; management said the business is mainly domestic and US tariffs have stalled talks with large US buyers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is depreciation about INR 15 crores per quarter (above INR 50 crores a year)?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Sudhir Iyer attributed it to Ind AS accounting; IGAAP depreciation would be lower, and the charge is front-loaded in the earlier years of asset lives. He did not give asset-class detail.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company report pre-Ind AS margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said only Ind AS numbers will be published, but pre-Ind AS figures are available offline. Management then gave pre-Ind AS averages: gross margin 56% to 60%, EBITDA margin 11% to 13%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the order book and B2B billing?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book stood at INR 68 crores on 30 June 2026, up from INR 62 crores at March 2026. Products are produced but cannot be invoiced until logistics clear.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Stanley Superlative Living format?
qa_highlights.answer: A large-format store in mature markets, replacing smaller Stanley stores. Management said Hyderabad is the proof of concept; the format consolidates Boutique and Level Next. Sofas & More becomes the value-premium brand.

qa_highlights.question: How many COCO stores are store-level EBITDA positive?
qa_highlights.answer: 35 of 42 mature COCO stores are EBITDA positive, after cash rent (the answer refers to 42 stores out of 47 total). Break-even takes 6 to 12 months and ROI 24 to 36 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are same-store sales growth and mature store revenues?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 mature-store SSSG was slightly negative due to format changes; target is 15% to 20% YoY. Average annual revenue: Sofas & More about INR 5 crores, Boutique INR 4 to 5 crores, Level Next about INR 10 crores plus.

risks_watch: Conversion recovery depends on residential handovers, which management says slipped 12 to 18 months in several projects; West Asia supply chain is constraining construction materials.
B2B billing stalled despite a record order book (INR 68 crores at 30 June 2026); watch whether logistics clear and invoicing resumes after BIS enforcement from 14 August 2026.
Internal audit found fraudulent activity by the company secretary, with misappropriation of funds acknowledged on the call; investigation outcome and disclosure pending.

Brand architecture change (Stanley Superlative Living, Boutique conversion to Sofas & More over 2 to 3 years) and store relocations/closures; execution and same-store sales recovery (Q1 mature-store SSSG slightly negative) to monitor.
Depreciation of about INR 15 crores per quarter under Ind AS, with the company declining to publish pre-Ind AS figures routinely; management did not give asset-class detail.
key_quotes: Residential project handovers have been delayed by 12 to 18 months in several cases.
As a result, while customer inquiries and store footfall remains encouraging, conversions are slower as customers await possession of their homes.

So we found that in the Q1 audit on the internal controls, so we found some fraudulent activity has been done by the company secretary, and the investigation is going on, and we will let you know to the public in short while once we complete the investigations.
We should report Ind AS numbers only. But as a CFO, I can carry to you what the IGAAP looks like offline.
544202|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term demand and brand strategy but cautious on near-term trading, attributing the revenue decline to handover delays and West Asia logistics rather than demand. It was evasive on the depreciation breakdown, on export revenue figures, and on the nature of the fraud, giving only brief answers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 17.3% on Ind AS, but management gave no margin guidance and corporate cost of about INR 90 lakhs per month (about 2.25% of revenue) is expected to stay flat while revenue fell 8.5% YoY, so operating leverage is not visible.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Hyderabad Jubilee Hills Superlative store is 2 to 3 weeks from opening, Sofas & More Jaipur and Colombo are already commissioned, and large-format mega stores are planned for Mumbai, Bangalore and Delhi; manufacturing can reach about 2x revenue with a few machines at 68-70% utilisation.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 revenue fell 8.5% YoY to INR 9,935 lakhs and mature-store SSSG was slightly negative, but management targets 15-20% YoY same-store growth and the B2B order book rose to INR 68 crores from INR 62 crores, conditional on handovers and logistics clearing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Manufacturing utilisation is only 68-70%, so capacity is not the constraint; the capex pipeline is store-led (about INR 2 crores per Sofas & More store, up to INR 20 crores per Superlative flagship) and the mega-store plans for four cities are not yet dated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no revenue or margin guidance, Q1 revenue fell 8.5% YoY and PAT was only INR 65 lakhs, and conversions are slowed by handover delays of 12-18 months.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Handovers slipped 12-18 months in several projects, B2B invoicing of a INR 68 crore order book stalled on West Asia freight disruption, and Q1 PAT was only INR 65 lakhs on revenue of INR 9,935 lakhs.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Stanley Superlative Living (Hyderabad Jubilee Hills, 2-3 weeks from opening) and the brand consolidation into one Stanley and one Sofas & More over about 3-4 quarters are underway; Sofas & More Jaipur and Colombo are already live.

rows.label: B2B order book conversion to billing
rows.why: Order book reached INR 68 crores on 30 June 2026 (up from INR 62 crores in March 2026) but nothing was invoiced in Q1 due to freight disruption, so revenue recognition depends on logistics clearing and BIS enforcement from 14 August 2026.

rows.label: Internal audit fraud by company secretary
rows.why: Internal audit flagged misappropriation of funds by the company secretary, acknowledged on the call with the investigation outcome and disclosure still pending.

rows.label: Sri Lanka entry via Singer JV
rows.why: Stanley Boutique Colombo opened in July 2026 as a JV with Singer Sri Lanka PLC, with no capex figure disclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term demand, the record B2B order book and the Superlative format, but cautious on near-term trading and evasive on depreciation detail, export figures and the fraud; analysts pressed on margins and the depreciation charge.

544203|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 21.2% to a record ₹182 crore with margin up 179 bps to 17.9%; FY27 margins guided flat to FY26 at 14.4%.
544203|2026-03.overview: Consolidated income from operations for Q4 FY26 was ₹1,020 crore, up 9.1% YoY, with P&A volume up 20.5% to 4.4 million cases. Gross margin expanded 480 bps YoY to 48.2%, partly reinvested in brand-building. For FY26, consolidated revenue grew 11.5% to ₹3,949 crore, EBITDA rose 25.8% to ₹568 crore and reported PAT was ₹220 crore (adjusted ₹266 crore after ₹45.45 crore of tax items). Management guided FY27 mid-teens top-line growth, with a Q1 and early Q2 margin squeeze from the West Asia conflict before recovery from FTA, Telangana price hike and backward integration.

segments.name: P&A (Prestige & Above)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume up 20.5% YoY to 4.4 million cases, 57.7% of sales. FY26 share was 47.2% of volume and 57.3% of value. ICONiQ White sold 10.7 million cases in FY26 (up about 88%).

segments.name: Mass premium and other
segments.commentary: Q4 volume up 5.6% QoQ, driven by South and East, but flat YoY as management prioritised profitable state brand mix. Officer's Choice brandy has begun in Andhra Pradesh.

segments.name: ABD Maestro (super premium to luxury)
segments.commentary: Launched 10 brands, now in about 11 states and 4 travel retail locations. FY27 target to cross ₹100 crore revenue; year 1 EBITDA negative.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 export revenue up 14.1% to ₹235 crore; markets rose from 23 to 36. Q4 was partly hit by geopolitical disruption.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated top-line growth guided to mid-teens, in line with stated guidelines.
P&A expected to grow at high teens by FY28; mass premium and other to grow low to mid-single digits.
FY27 overall EBITDA margin guided to be at least equal to FY26 (14.4%); Q1 and early Q2 to see margin pressure from West Asia conflict.
Phase 1 and 2 backward integration expected to add about 300 bps to EBITDA margin by FY28 and about 100 bps more by FY29; FY28 EBITDA margin target raised to 18% from 17%.
UK FTA expected in Q2 FY27; Telangana price increase planned for H2 FY27 base case.
Management expects leverage to stay within guardrails on an annualised basis through the capex cycle; does not intend to breach covenants.
ESOP charge of about ₹5-6 crore per quarter in FY27.
capex_capacity: Phase 1 PET bottling facility in Telangana commissioned in Q2 FY26 and EBITDA accretive from Q3; it meets about 70-75% of requirement.
Malt distillery in Telangana (4 million litres, 12 KLPD per Amar Sinha) expected operational in H1 FY27.
ENA distillery expansion in Maharashtra expected operational in H1 FY28.
Phase 2 backward integration covers bottling and ENA in Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh; UP bottling plant expected in H2 to avoid ₹27 franchise fee on own brands.
Accelerated depreciation on certain plant assets, including the PET facility, raised Q4 and FY26 depreciation.
demand_pricing: Telangana: receivables and overdue receivables fell QoQ in Q4; management says FY24 and FY25 dues are cleared. Telangana price increase committee formed; management hopes for Q2 but plans for H2.
Karnataka: slab reduction policy not yet implemented; management sees neutral to positive for Officer's Choice (about 300,000 cases a year), with ICONiQ a potential opportunity.
Price increases taken in several markets; management says gross margin gain came from price, trade-spend control, state brand mix and about 30 bps from PET unit.
The Prestige & Above whisky segment is about 120 million cases, with ICONiQ, OC Blue and SRB7 at about 18-20 million cases combined. Management acknowledges some cannibalisation.
OC Blue and SRB7 are over 10 years old; SRB7 test marketing showed low single-digit growth. OC Blue packaging refresh due Q2 FY27.
CSD industry size about 12 million cases a year; ICONiQ, SRB7, Kyron and Jolly Roger approved. Management says ABD Maestro's 1% volume share equals about 9% value.

qa_highlights.question: How much FY27 margin upside from UK FTA, Telangana price hike and backward integration, and will H1 margins hold given glass and fuel inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 margins to be broadly equal to FY26, with pressure in Q1 and early Q2 and expansion from H2. Telangana hike is seen as a significant upside.

qa_highlights.question: Amar Sinha's vision and leadership transition timing?
qa_highlights.answer: He outlined a 3-year plan: premium-and-above above 50% of volume, high-teens revenue growth, 48-50% gross margin, EBITDA margin above 20% and ROCE about 25%. Alok Gupta said the transition announcement is expected within this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ICONiQ expansion plan and ABD Maestro ARR?
qa_highlights.answer: ICONiQ is distributed nationally, approved in CSD, and exported to 9 countries. ABD Maestro is targeting over ₹100 crore in FY27 across 11 states.

qa_highlights.question: Will leverage stretch with accelerated capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex funded by internal accruals and borrowing; management does not intend to breach covenants.

qa_highlights.question: Why are OC Blue and SRB7 declining and when do they return to growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Both are over 10 years old in competitive segments. Management is resetting A&P and packaging, with SRB7 showing low single-digit growth in test markets.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 300 bps gross margin expansion comes from backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30 bps in FY27 from the PET unit; the rest is price increases, trade-spend control and brand mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Proactive scotch buying ahead of rupee depreciation against the pound, stored under FTWZ, plus smaller-batch ABD Maestro production.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict driving input cost and export disruption; Q1 and early Q2 FY27 margin pressure.
Telangana price hike timing and Karnataka slab policy implementation.
Officer's Choice Blue and SRB7 decline; success of Q2 FY27 OC Blue relaunch.
Rising leverage during capex cycle (net debt/EBITDA 1.7x vs 2x ceiling); ESOP cost from FY27.
Execution of malt, ENA and UP bottling projects against H1 FY27 and H2 timelines; leadership transition announcement.
544203|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term margin and premiumisation targets, but candid that Q1 and early Q2 FY27 margins will be pressured. Answers on Karnataka and Telangana timing were hedged ('conservative but optimistic'), and the leadership-transition answer was brief.
key_quotes: So, the guidance that we are giving is that the FY27 overall margins, we should be hold on to the FY26, if not better it.
ABDM will not necessarily move the volume growth lever, but it substantially impacts the value growth lever.
Our entire capex investment will be a combination of internal accruals and borrowing whenever required, but we do not intend breaching these covenants at all.

544203|2026-06.headline: ABD Q1 FY27 revenue rose 5.8% to ₹984 crore and reported EBITDA was flat at ₹120 crore, as ₹24 crore of supply-chain disruption cost offset gross margin gains.
544203|2026-06.overview: Consolidated income from operations grew 5.8% YoY to ₹984 crore on 6.2% volume growth to 9 million cases, with Prestige and Above (P&A) volumes up 10.7%. Gross margin expanded 277 bps to 46%, but a ₹24 crore global supply-chain disruption hit profitability, leaving reported EBITDA at ₹120 crore (12.2% margin) versus ₹119 crore and PAT at ₹45 crore versus ₹56 crore. Management presented like-to-like EBITDA of ₹144 crore (14.7% margin, +21.4% YoY) excluding the disruption. Net debt fell ₹33 crore QoQ to ₹947 crore, with net debt to EBITDA at 1.7x.

segments.commentary: Volume share 48.2% (vs 46.2%) and value share 59.3% (vs 55.8%); segment volume grew 10.7% YoY. Management said ABD outgrew an industry where P&A grew low single digits.

qa_highlights.question: Is the guidance building in a Telangana price hike and a resolution to supply-chain and glass inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the two-year guidance and said it could be stepped up. Telangana price hike talks are ongoing with guardrails built in. Management expects the war-related pressure to last until Q2 and then ease.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Officer's Choice Blue, Sterling Reserve B7 and B10 declining, and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed cash-flow constraints before the 2024 listing and said ICONiQ is the growth engine. OC Blue is being relaunched with new packaging in UP first; B7 gets a new look in H2 FY27 (packaging rollout targeted Q4 FY27). B10 was named as losing ground.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited ABD P&A growth of 11.6% vs industry mid-single digits, the full-year benefit of ICONiQ, brandy push in AP, OC volume in Telangana and AP, and vodka and premium whisky launches in H2 FY27.

544209|2026-03.headline: Bansal Wire FY26 revenue up 19% to INR 4,160 crore and volume up 33% to 4.58 lakh t, but gas disruption cut March output to 35% and Q1 FY27 is expected to be subdued.
544209|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 volume was 1.17 lakh t (+20% YoY, slightly down QoQ) and revenue was INR 1,136 crore (+21% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 80 crore (7% margin) and net profit of INR 40 crore (+21%). For FY26, revenue rose 19% to INR 4,160 crore, EBITDA rose 17% to INR 325 crore and PAT rose 10% to INR 161 crore. A natural gas disruption linked to Iran-Israel tensions cut production to 35% in March, and management said April volumes were recovering to about 80-85% of normal. Management kept a 20% medium-term growth target once conditions normalise, and said cash flow reached INR 333 crore against a INR 250 crore target.
