Steel Cords first trial order expected in FY27 H2 with other customers by year-end; management said about 20 kt run-rate could come within this financial year.

demand_pricing: Demand outside automotive is sluggish (consumer durables, infra and others), attributed to a steel price rise of 10-15% over three months and the geopolitical situation.

Payables rose sharply because of purchase inverse discounting with banks; management expects payable days to rise further as it reduces working capital days, with only a modest increase in interest cost.

qa_highlights.question: How much volume and gas-related disruption is expected in Q1 FY27, and can higher steel prices offset lower volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes were cut 35% last month and are recovering to 80-85% of normal. Management said higher prices may support revenue but EBITDA per ton would take a hit, and it could not quantify the figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% growth guidance at risk given the April production cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 20% growth is achievable only once conditions normalise, and it cannot give a number for the current period.

qa_highlights.question: What are the blended gas price increase and the expected April EBITDA per ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended gas escalation of at least 50% for Q1, with some units up to 300%. The INR 2,000-2,500 per ton hit applies only to the 30-40 day order book; management expects about 50 of 90 days at standard EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: How does the Steel Cords trial and approval process work and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The first trial order is from one of the top four Indian tyre makers, with one customer having removed the field trial. Other customers are expected by year-end, and about 20 kt run-rate could come within FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did payables rise sharply, and will this continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it reflects purchase inverse discounting with banks, while suppliers are still paid in advance. Payable days can rise gradually as working capital days are reduced.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% growth target conservative, and what is the FY26 utilisation and FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has grown about 20% over the last 10 years, with 30% in FY26 due to pent-up demand. FY26 utilisation was 67-68%; 80-85% is its preferred level, but at least 70% is the working target for FY27.

544209|2026-06.headline: Bansal Wire Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 25% YoY to INR 1,168 crore, with EBITDA of INR 57 crore and PAT of INR 20 crore after a gas-driven margin hit.
544209|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was hit in its first 45 days by a spike in gas and consumable costs (about INR 5,000 a tonne blended) linked to West Asia tensions, and management chose to absorb the cost on about 30-40 days of firm-price orders, cutting blended EBITDA to about INR 2 a kg. Margins recovered to about INR 7-8 a kg from around May 15, and management says operations are back to normal levels. Sales volume was 112,000 tonnes versus 104,000 tonnes a year earlier, and operating cash flow was about INR 121 crore. Management reiterated 20% volume and EBITDA growth for the rest of FY27 and kept capex at INR 200-250 crore a year.

segments.commentary: Absorbed a cost shock on about 30-40 days of firm-price orders; new orders were priced at INR 8 a kg blended. Management says volume growth lagged its 20% target because of a demand dip and customer destocking.

segments.commentary: Launched in the quarter and contributed about 10% of sales. Management targets B2C at 25% of total sales, which is 50% of the low-carbon business, and says B2C EBITDA per tonne is 20-30% above B2B low-carbon.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CFO guidance rise to about INR 800 crore across FY27 and FY28 from about INR 600 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 600 crore figure was a combined two-year target. FY26 delivered about INR 330 crore against a INR 250 crore target, and FY27's target is INR 350 crore, with INR 115 crore already generated in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What are the IHT and OHT margins and utilisation path?
qa_highlights.answer: IHT is at 35-40% utilisation, targeting about 50% next month. Break-even is at about 60% utilisation, with decent margins at 70-80%. Combined IHT and OHT EBITDA is expected at INR 10-20 a kg.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is capped at INR 200-250 crore a year to support 20-25% volume growth. Management said there will be no unusually high capex year apart from Speciality.

key_quotes: Now as of today, even with all of this crisis today, we see that the demand is there.

544209|2026-09.headline: Bansal Wire posted record Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 1,308 crore (+24% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 105 crore, with EBITDA/ton near Rs 8,000 aided partly by inventory gain.
544209|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a record quarter for revenue, EBITDA, PAT and EBITDA per ton, recovering from a Q1 hit from industrial gas disruption and higher input costs. Sales volume was about 1,29,000 tons versus 1,14,609 tons in Q2 FY26, and operating cash flow was Rs 218 crore in the quarter and Rs 339 crore in H1. Management said about Rs 200/ton of EBITDA was a one-time inventory gain and guided to Rs 7,000-7,500/ton for H2. Raw material (wire rod) shortages hit October output, which management said is a short-term issue.

segments.name: IHT / OHT specialty wire
segments.commentary: IHT wire reached positive EBITDA last quarter; management cites Rs 15,000-20,000/ton EBITDA for the specialty wire group. IHT capacity is 9,000 tons, with 6,000 tons OHT being installed to reach 15,000 tons in one to two quarters.

segments.name: Steel tyre cord
segments.commentary: Current capacity about 20,000 tons, with a goal of 2 lakh tons. Pricing is about Rs 130-140/kg. First trial order received in Q2, with a second trial order expected in 10-15 days; commercialisation possible within this year.

segments.name: Bead wire
segments.commentary: Nameplate capacity about 30,000 tons, with 10,000-15,000 tons currently run annually. Management cites Rs 12,000-15,000/ton EBITDA. Approvals not yet started; focus to resume in one to two quarters.

segments.name: LRPC
segments.commentary: Less than 1% of sales. Management said it earns modest margins (about Rs 5,000-8,000/ton typical) due to industry overcapacity.

segments.name: B2C (farming, fencing, poultry)
segments.commentary: About 10-12% of Q2 volumes; management says B2C EBITDA is at least 50% higher than B2B.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth of 20% YoY for H2 FY27 (Q3 and Q4 vs prior-year H2); management said Q1 losses cannot be recovered.
EBITDA per ton guidance of Rs 7,000-7,500/ton for H2 FY27; management said Rs 7,000-8,000/ton is achievable for FY27 barring major geopolitical change.
Operating cash flow target of about Rs 800 crore across FY27 and FY28 combined; about Rs 350 crore already generated in H1 FY27.
Capacity to rise from 6.8 lakh tons to about 8.3 lakh tons by end of next year (60,000 tons Dadri brownfield plus about 90,000 tons Sanand greenfield).
Indicative annual capex of Rs 200-225 crore (also cited as Rs 200-250 crore per year), funded from internal accruals.
Long-term EBITDA/ton target of Rs 8,000-10,000, and above Rs 10,000 as specialty wire scales.
capex_capacity: Dadri: 60,000 tons additional low and high carbon wire capacity, mostly built; capitalisation expected by end of Q3 or Q4 FY27. Also 6,000 tons OHT wire, expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27.

Sanand (southern Gujarat) greenfield: about 90,000 tons of stainless steel and low carbon wire, with about Rs 150 crore capex excluding land (land acquired about a year ago). Some capitalisation expected from next quarter or the quarter after.
CWIP closing balance Rs 177 crore.
Steel tyre cord: 20,000 tons current capacity, with a 2 lakh ton goal; a bigger capex will follow customer approvals.
Management expects 4-5x asset turnover on new capacity.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as healthy across automotive, infra, agriculture, power and transmission, and general engineering. Constraint is raw material supply rather than demand.
Wire rod shortage over the last 1.5-2 months as suppliers shifted output to TMT. Company holds about 1.5 months of inventory; October output was hit at some plants, which management says is now back.
Low carbon was about 55% of volume in Q2 (lower end of 55-60% target), supporting blended margin.
Gas prices are about 2.5x the regular level, passed through to customers. Availability has been stable for about one quarter.

Steel tyre cord India demand is 2.5-3 lakh tons, mostly imported. Management expects radialisation (about 60% in India truck/bus) to drive growth. Management says there is no Indian domestic competitor; Bekaert is the main competitor.
Management says it will cap any single customer at 20-25% of total sales for steel cord.

qa_highlights.question: When will steel tyre cord and IHT/OHT translate into revenue and EBITDA, and what is the EBITDA per ton for specialty wire?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel tyre cord is in trials, with a second trial order expected in 10-15 days and commercialisation possible within the year. Specialty wire EBITDA is about Rs 15,000-20,000/ton, and IHT has turned EBITDA positive.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 EBITDA/ton came from inventory gains, and is Rs 7,000-7,500 conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory gain was about Rs 200/ton, so underlying EBITDA was about Rs 7,800-7,900/ton. Management said its own strategy is Rs 7,000-7,500 and it is not guiding above that.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% volume growth guidance for H2 only, and is it at risk from raw material shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: It applies to H2 FY27, meaning Q3 and Q4 volumes up 20% YoY. Management said raw material shortages are temporary and that lost days can be made up the following month.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of Sanand and Dadri CWIP and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: CWIP is Rs 177 crore, mostly Dadri 60,000 tons. Sanand needs about Rs 150 crore capex excluding land.

qa_highlights.question: Steel cord capacity plan and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity is 20,000 tons, the target is 2 lakh tons, and realisation is about Rs 130-140/kg. Management said a major capex will follow customer approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Is Rs 7-7.5/kg the right base for H2 earnings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs 7,000-7,500/ton is the H2 EBITDA commitment, and a better outcome is possible but not guided.

risks_watch: Raw material (wire rod) availability: shortages in October and supplier breakdowns could cut Q3 and Q4 volumes below the 20% growth guidance.
Gas prices at about 2.5x normal; management says pass-through to customers is in place, but this is a margin risk.
Q2 EBITDA/ton includes about Rs 200/ton inventory gain, so sustainability of the Rs 7,800-8,000 level is uncertain.
Steel cord commercialisation depends on customer approvals; management expects the first two quarters of ramp-up to be slow.
Sanand greenfield and Dadri ramp-up execution; capex may move beyond the stated timelines.
LRPC is loss-making at the margin due to industry overcapacity; management says it is less than 1% of sales.
544209|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on results and guidance, with management saying it prefers to guide conservatively. It was candid about near-term raw material disruption and the Q1 gas hit. Answers on steel cord timelines were more hedged, using phrases such as "hopefully" and "if everything goes well".
key_quotes: We have achieved our highest ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA, and profit after tax.
So, we will rather be a little conservative than not delivering on our guidance.
Sir, our thought process is that we should maintain our margins at about Rs. 7,000 to Rs. 7,500.
In the long run, yes, we would definitely look at Rs. 8,000 to Rs. 10,000.

rows.why: Management guides H2 EBITDA/ton at Rs 7,000-7,500 but says a better outcome is possible and is not guiding above it, with underlying Q2 at about Rs 7,800-7,900 excluding a ~Rs 200/ton inventory gain.

rows.why: Wire rod shortages hit October output and suppliers shifted to TMT over 1.5-2 months, and the company holds only ~1.5 months of inventory, putting the 20% H2 volume guide at risk even though management says lost days can be made up.

rows.why: Steel tyre cord had a first trial order in Q2 with a second expected in 10-15 days at Rs 130-140/kg, and commercialisation is possible within the year, though management says the first two quarters of ramp-up will be slow.

rows.when: within 10-15 days of the call, then commercialisation within
rows.why: First trial order received in Q2 and a second trial order expected in 10-15 days, with Indian steel cord demand at 2.5-3 lakh t, mostly imported, and no domestic competitor per management.

rows.label: Debt reduction and cash generation
rows.why: Total debt is ~Rs 300 crore with D/E about 0.2 after a ~40% cut in H1, operating cash flow was Rs 339 crore in H1 against a ~Rs 800 crore target for FY27-FY28 combined.

rows.label: IHT/OHT specialty wire scale-up to 15,000 t
rows.why: IHT capacity is 9,000 t with 6,000 t OHT being installed, and specialty wire earns Rs 15,000-20,000/t EBITDA, but timing is hedged as 'hopefully'.

544210|2026-03.headline: Emcure FY26 revenue crossed INR9,204 crore (+16.6%), but Q4 domestic growth slowed to 5.2% on Zuventus disruption; FY27 guided to low-to-mid-teen growth.
544210|2026-03.overview: Emcure reported FY26 revenue of INR9,204 crore (+16.6% YoY), with adjusted PAT up 41% to INR1,008 crore and EBITDA margin up 80 bps to 19.4%. Q4 revenue rose 16.7% to INR2,470 crore, but domestic growth slowed to 5.2% because of attrition and restructuring at the newly consolidated Zuventus business. International markets grew 25.7% in Q4, with Europe and Canada leading. Management said April is on plan and guided FY27 to low-to-mid-teen revenue growth and 75-100 bps of EBITDA margin expansion.

financial_highlights.change: +24.5% YoY; margin up from 18.4% in Q4 FY25
Up YoY due to Manx payouts and Zuventus minority stake buyout

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR4,027 crore (+10%), led by women's health, cardio, CNS and oncology. Q4 revenue INR977 crore (+5.2%) was hit by Zuventus. Management said ex-Zuventus Q4 growth was below 8% and the full-year ex-Zuventus base growth was high single digit.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR5,177 crore (+22.2%). Q4 revenue INR1,493 crore (+25.7%); currency added roughly 7-8% overall, about 11-12% in Europe.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,850 crore (+25.5%). Q4 revenue INR538 crore (+35.8%), helped by Manx and Amphotericin B. Management expects mid-teens CAGR over the next two years.

segments.name: Canada
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,487 crore (+18.7%). Q4 revenue INR399 crore (+28.6%), driven by market share gains and launches.

segments.name: Rest of World / Emerging markets
segments.commentary: FY26 ROW revenue INR1,840 crore (+21.8%), with ARV and non-ARV both contributing. Q4 emerging markets revenue INR556 crore (+15.5%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at low-to-mid-teens.
EBITDA margin expansion of 75-100 bps in FY27, assuming stable regulations, macro conditions and no major geopolitical upheaval.
Domestic target: grow faster than industry (8-9% expected), at low double-digits.
FY27 capex guided at roughly INR400-425 crore.
FY27 average currency assumption of INR92/USD.
Gross margin expected to stay around 60% for the full year.
Employee expense growth expected at about 10% in FY27 versus about 7% in FY26.
Canada semaglutide launch via Dr. Reddy's partnership in Quebec, expected around Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at roughly INR400-425 crore.
Field force around 4,000 MRs; about 40% sit in Zuventus. Field productivity rose from INR5.4 lakh to INR7 lakh per MR over two years.
Amphotericin B launched in select European markets in H2 FY26; expansion to Europe and rest of world planned for FY27.
Bevacizumab ophthalmic biosimilar endorsed by CDSCO SEC; launch planned H1 FY27 pending approval.
Lenacapavir: DMF filed; product registration sought in FY27.
demand_pricing: Zuventus: Q4 restructuring (new management after October minority buyout, portfolio and team reorganisation) drove high field attrition; management says April is on plan. Normal MR attrition is 20-30%.

Poviztra (Novo Nordisk rDNA semaglutide, India exclusive): early uptake promising after April 2026 price cut; about 1,000 sales reps promoting it. Management says the product is differentiated versus synthetic generics.
In-licensed products make up about 15% of domestic sales. The Roche nephrology brands (2-3 key brands) are under INR50 crore annualised with no upfront payment.
Market share in covered markets was roughly flat for FY26 after the Q4 impact.

Raw material and solvent prices have risen with the Middle East conflict. Freight and insurance costs are also up. Company holds 1-2 quarters of inventory and says there are no supply issues yet. IPA is seeking a domestic price hike.
Canada: Dr. Reddy's partnership via Mantra subsidiary in Quebec, where pricing is expected to be more favourable. Apotex and Reddy's received semaglutide approvals recently.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify Zuventus impact on India growth and whether restructuring will weigh on the next few quarters.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full-year ex-Zuventus base growth would have been 9-10%, and Q4 ex-Zuventus was below 8%. It expects the impact to fade, with April back on track.

qa_highlights.question: What operational synergies are expected from Zuventus?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manufacturing synergies are limited because the plants serve different products. Gains are expected in sales and marketing organisation and support functions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 domestic growth outlook and the currency assumption behind guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry growth is expected at 8-9% and Emcure aims for low double digits. The guidance assumes INR92/USD.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the raw material and geopolitical cost pressure is in guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory covers 1-2 quarters, so impact is limited near term. Management said guidance includes current pricing, and the industry is facing solvent and freight cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Canada semaglutide path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Quebec partnership with Dr. Reddy's aims for an early launch around Q2 FY27, and its own filing will target the rest of Canada in the medium term. Deal terms were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is Emcure open to more in-licensing deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the focus is organic growth but in-licensing will continue where it is accretive.

risks_watch: Zuventus recovery: whether April's on-plan trend holds through Q1 FY27 after high attrition.
Poviztra price war and whether market share recovers after the April 2026 price cut.
Raw material, solvent, freight and insurance inflation if the Middle East conflict persists beyond the 1-2 quarters of inventory.
Rising debt (net debt INR1,054 crore) after the Manx and Zuventus payouts.
Q4 Mantra earn-out exceptional charge of INR43 crore, which was above initial expectations.
Currency: a weaker rupee supports international revenue, but the INR92/USD assumption needs monitoring.
544210|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and optimistic on FY27 and on the Zuventus recovery, though Q4 domestic softness was openly acknowledged. Management was noticeably evasive on monthly April growth and on the semaglutide market-share recovery. It was also cautious on cost pressures, saying the impact is hard to quantify.
key_quotes: FY26 marked the start of our 5-year strategy, focusing on turning last year's operational changes into measurable outcomes.
Ex of the Zuventus impact for the full year would have been close to the 9% - 10% base business growth that we have been talking about, that we delivered even in the first 9 months.
I think we continue to expect industry growth to be around 8% to 9% , and for us, the target, is to grow faster than the industry – probably at low double-digits.

In FY27, we project low to mid -teen revenue growth and as I have been explaining in the last meet and a few calls that I have had the privilege of addressing to you guys that EBITDA margin expansion will happen as committed between 75 to 100 basis points going forward, assuming stable regulations and macroeconomic conditions.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided 75-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion in FY27 after FY26 margin of 19.4% (+80 bps), with gross margin held near 60% and employee cost growth of about 10% vs about 7% in FY26; raw material and freight inflation is a watch item.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to low-to-mid-teens (midpoint about 12.5%) with domestic targeted at low double-digits vs industry 8-9%, and International +25.7% in Q4 led by Europe +35.8% and Canada +28.6%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex of INR400-425 crore is already guided, but no new capacity or utilisation figure was disclosed, so no further capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was set as a fresh low-to-mid-teen range with April described only as on plan; no sign of a beat that would prompt a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Ex-Zuventus Q4 growth was below 8% with high field attrition (normal 20-30%), and raw material, solvent and freight costs are rising with only 1-2 quarters of inventory cover, while net debt rose to INR1,054 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Bevacizumab ophthalmic biosimilar launch planned H1 FY27 pending approval, Canada semaglutide via Dr. Reddy's in Quebec around Q2 FY27, and Amphotericin B expansion to Europe and RoW planned for FY27.

rows.label: Zuventus recovery after Q4 restructuring
rows.why: Ex-Zuventus full-year base growth was 9-10% and Q4 ex-Zuventus below 8%; management says April is on plan, but monthly April growth was not quantified and field attrition was high.

rows.label: Poviztra semaglutide uptake after April 2026 price cut
rows.why: About 1,000 sales reps are promoting Poviztra and early uptake is called promising, but management was evasive on market-share recovery and the price war risk is open.

rows.label: IPA domestic price hike for raw material inflation
rows.why: Solvent and freight costs are rising with the Middle East conflict and the industry body is seeking a domestic price hike, but no approval is confirmed and inventory covers only 1-2 quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 guidance, the Zuventus recovery and International growth, but was evasive on April monthly growth and semaglutide share recovery and cautious on cost pressures; analysts focused on Zuventus drag and quantifying it.

544210|2026-06.headline: Emcure Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.8% YoY to INR 2,580 crore, with EBITDA of INR 508 crore (19.7% margin) and PAT up 35-36%.
544210|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 22.8% YoY to INR 2,580 crore, led by international markets (up 34.2% to INR 1,485 crore) while India grew 10.2% to INR 1,095 crore. EBITDA rose 25.8% to INR 508 crore with margin up 50 bps to 19.7%, and PAT grew about 36% to INR 292 crore. Gross margin fell to 58.4% on geographic and product mix, and net debt rose to INR 1,103 crore. Management reiterated low-to-mid teens FY27 revenue growth (now toward the higher end) and 70-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion. Board changes were announced: Chairman Berjis Desai retires at AGM and CEO Satish Mehta becomes Chairman; Samit Mehta becomes COO and CEO of Gennova, which is now 100% owned.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,095 crore, +10.2% YoY. Ex-Sanofi OAD and Roche in-licensed brands, growth was about 6-7%. Price contributed about 4-5%, new launches 1-2%. Management says no channel filling in the quarter.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 537 crore, +32.8% YoY, driven by base business and liposomal amphotericin B (Ampho). Ampho is introduced in pretty much all countries, but tender-based procurement means lumpy orders.

segments.name: Canada
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 427 crore, +24.6% YoY, on new launches and share gains. Semaglutide filing expected in the next few months; Quebec launch via Dr. Reddy's is uncertain.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 522 crore, +44.8% YoY, led by ARV. About two-thirds of ROW was ARV this quarter; management expects ARV at about 50-55% of ROW for the full year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at low-to-mid teens, with management now more comfortable at the higher end of that range, driven by ARV order book visibility.
EBITDA margin expansion of 70-100 bps for FY27 reiterated.
FY27 gross margin guided at about 59% (earlier 60-61% framing), as higher international and ARV mix dilutes gross margin while EBITDA is accretive.
R&D for FY27 guided at 4-5% of revenue; spend expected to pick up in the rest of the year.
India growth expected in line with industry in Q2 FY27 and faster than industry in H2 FY27 as the Zuventus base effect eases.
Net debt expected to rise to about INR 1,450 crore by end-Q2 FY27 after the Mantra and Gennova payouts (INR 450-500 crore), then turn net cash by end-FY28.
Management expects sequential improvement each quarter.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were given on the call.
Gennova consolidated to 100% after acquiring a 12.05% minority stake; Mantra acquisition payout completed in July 2026.
demand_pricing: International constant-currency growth about 12% (about 12-13% per later answer), against about 6-7% FX tailwind at company level.
India price growth about 4-5% YoY; new launches 1-2%; the remainder is volume.

Poviztra (semaglutide biosimilar with Novo Nordisk) is growing month on month, but management says 40-50 brands have launched in the market and it is hard to separate channel stocking from consumption. Pricing was set very competitively.
Gross margin pressure reflects B2B-type international businesses (lower gross margin, higher EBITDA contribution), with Europe and ARV growing faster.
Management says Zuventus is stabilised and consolidated, now moving to acceleration.

qa_highlights.question: Is India's double-digit growth clean, or is there channel filling after Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no channel filling this quarter; growth is normalised and expected to improve further in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What share of ROW is ARV, and does FY27 base make FY28 harder?

544213|2026-03.headline: Aelea Commodities H2 FY26 standalone revenue Rs 189.50 cr with 13.10% EBITDA margin and Rs 12.35 cr PAT; FY26 revenue up 112% to Rs 363.12 cr.
544213|2026-03.overview: Management reported H2 FY26 standalone revenue of Rs 189.50 cr, EBITDA of Rs 24.82 cr (13.10% margin) and PAT of Rs 12.35 cr (6.52% margin), versus losses a year earlier. For FY26, standalone revenue rose 112.07% to Rs 363.12 cr, EBITDA was Rs 40.20 cr (11.07% margin) and PAT Rs 21.19 cr, with EPS of Rs 10.40 versus Rs 0.65. Consolidated FY26 revenue was Rs 381.50 cr (up 109.46%) and PAT Rs 21.32 cr. The call was dominated by a 10-year (FY37) strategy presentation, with the Q&A focused on higher finance costs, working capital and inventory build, CNSL plant timing, and FY27 guidance, which was not quantified.

segments.name: Cashew kernel processing (core)
segments.commentary: Processes raw cashew nuts (RCN) into wholes and pieces; average mix 63% wholes and 37% pieces, with average kernel realisation of about Rs 590-595/kg. Around 16,000 tonnes of RCN processed in H2 and a similar volume in H1. About 95% of raw material is African-origin, sourced via merchant traders.

segments.commentary: CNSL extraction facility of above 50 MT is under construction, with management guiding to benefits from around H2 FY27 and a product-level EBITDA margin of about 10%. Rooftop solar is installed; ground-mounted solar awaits government approval. B2C consumer pouches are about 1% of sales.

EBITDA margin: management says the company normally operates at around 10-11% EBITDA margin, which it says it has broadly met.

CNSL plant: construction nearly complete with about 30 days of works remaining; commissioning depends on government approvals. Phase 3 capex is expected later in the year.
B2C: targeted at roughly 13-15% EBITDA margin in the long run, pursued through a product basket rather than e-commerce.
capex_capacity: Capacity scaling from 40 MT/day to 140 MT/day, which management says is backed by IPO proceeds; current utilisation about 94-95%.
Phase 2 (CNSL) capex is already committed and underway, with only a small amount pending; Phase 3 capex is expected in the later part of the year.
Ground-mounted solar is pending government approval because of changes to norms for consuming solar power; rooftop solar is complete.
Long-term 2037 strategy targets 1,000 MT/day cashew capacity, plus almond, walnut, pistachio and makhana processing (makhana with a 50-tonne capacity plan).
A Maharashtra cultivation project and capex was flagged by an analyst as not updated; management said it is still being worked on and not crystallised.
demand_pricing: Management said processing is constrained by raw-material quality rather than machine capacity; the company says it fully used its enhanced capacity during H2.
Raw-material sourcing has moved deeper into the value chain (direct sourcing at about 60-65%), which lifted margins but raised working capital and finance costs.
Geopolitical disruption: longer sea transit from Africa, currency swings of around 50 paise a day, and higher RCN price volatility, with no material price impact yet.
Institutional clients are a stated priority for longer-term visibility, but institutions are about one-fifth the size of general trade in the market.
Inventory rose to about Rs 100 cr and management expects it to increase further with growth.

544222|2026-03.headline: Akums Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA rose 61.6% YoY to INR152 crore (13.1% margin), with FY26 revenue up 5.8% to INR4,359 crore.
544222|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR1,158 crore, up 9.7% YoY and flat QoQ, while adjusted EBITDA reached INR152 crore, driven by CDMO profitability and trade generics turning EBITDA positive. Reported Q4 PAT of INR81 crore was held down versus the prior year by a large deferred tax asset benefit in the base; PBT rose to INR121 crore from INR75 crore. FY26 PAT fell to INR256 crore from INR344 crore, which included a INR106 crore DTA benefit in FY25. Management guided to double-digit CDMO volume growth in H1 FY27, a sharp narrowing of API losses, and a Zambia supply contract of about $25 million per year from Q2 FY27.

544223|2026-03.headline: Ceigall Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 30.5% YoY to INR1,294 crores; FY27 guidance is minimum 15% revenue growth and 11-12.5% EBITDA margin.
544223|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's strongest execution quarter of the year, with standalone revenue of INR1,294 crores (up 30.5% YoY) and standalone EBITDA of INR183 crores (14.1% margin). Full-year standalone revenue grew 14.3% to INR3,869 crores, while FY26 order inflow of INR11,332 crores far exceeded the INR5,000 crore guidance, taking the order book to INR18,554 crores. Management guided FY27 to at least 15% revenue growth, 11-12.5% EBITDA margin and at least INR5,500 crores of order inflow. Working-capital stretch (trade payables and unbilled revenue days both up sharply) and a large pending equity commitment for HAM and renewable projects were the main analyst focus, alongside the INR13,000 crore Romania bid.

Morena BESS project awarded but not started: PPA not yet signed and transmission line tender not yet received; work depends on government land, transmission connectivity and PPA.
Velgaon 400 KV substation in Maharashtra in progress; transmission orders placed and T&D construction underway.

Sobha project in Dubai (about AED250 million) was also bid.
NHAI pipeline about INR2 lakh crores per management; company is bidding projects above INR2,000 crores and has a INR21,160 crore project and a INR600 crore Zirakpur bypass project.
Escalation clause changed from quarterly to monthly by MoRTH; billing plan eased to monthly payments after the recent war-related notifications.

qa_highlights.question: Pipeline for domestic and international business, and targets over one to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Offices opened in Singapore and Dubai, and a CEO International appointed. International expansion was slowed by the war; the company will bid abroad only if EBITDA margins and concessional IRRs are adequate.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue guidance of 15% looks low given the order book; what is the internal target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is being conservative; it had previously guided 10-15% and achieved it, and 15% minimum is intended as an easy-to-achieve floor.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables and working capital plan?
qa_highlights.answer: MoRTH notifications moved billing from milestones to monthly payments; more than INR400 crores from NEO asset sales is expected, so management says cash flow is not a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade payable days jump from 79 to 138 and unbilled revenue days from 94 to 133?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed it to March billing being paid by the department only in April, with creditor payments linked to receivables; about INR300 crores was paid to creditors in April. Unbilled revenue rose because milestone billing on large projects (10% per milestone, over INR100 crores each) lagged, and should improve with monthly billing.

qa_highlights.question: Margin drivers in Q4 and risk from iron ore and raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 margin was helped by four HAM projects started last year and higher turnover. Management said escalation is now paid monthly, so cost increases are passed through to the EPC contractor.

qa_highlights.question: Margins falling over three years as per the presentation slide 41?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said pure-operations EBITDA has stayed at 11-12.5% for three years; the earlier-year figures included bonus and royalty income (INR20 crores in FY25 and a Karnal-Pehowa bonus in FY24), which are included in revenue from operations.

qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,937 crores is needed over three years (about INR800 crores renewable, rest HAM roads). Management cited unencumbered cash of about INR166 crores and FDR of about INR75 crores at March 31 (corrected from figures stated on the call), plus cash accruals and NEO proceeds.

risks_watch: Receivable and unbilled-revenue days rose sharply (unbilled 94 to 133 days; trade payables 79 to 138 days); watch whether monthly billing reverses this in coming quarters.

HAM monetisation timing: only the Malout-Abohar-Sadhuwali deal is binding, and the other two sales remain at non-binding offer stage.
Margin guidance of 11-12.5% is excluding other income, which management said is volatile; FY26 standalone PAT margin was 7.9%.

544223|2026-06.headline: Ceigall Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 10.2% YoY to INR901 crore, with EBITDA margin at 13.4% and order book at INR18,568 crore.

The company completed its first HAM divestment (Malout-Abohar-Sadhuwali) and started three new projects, while management kept FY27 margin guidance of 11-12.5% and raised revenue growth guidance to at least 15%. Q1 order inflow was modest at about INR600 crore against a INR6,000 crore full-year target.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said progress is steady and milestones are being met early; payment is only received on milestone achievement, and rain over the last 1.5 months affected timing.

qa_highlights.answer: PPA and land are in place; the transmission line tender has been floated and the company expects it soon, after which the project can start quickly.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation and other income fall sharply?

544224|2026-03.headline: Afcom Q4 FY26 revenue rose 87.8% YoY to INR191.88 crore and PAT to INR44.66 crore, on war-driven charter demand.

544225|2026-03.headline: Ola Electric Q4 FY26 consolidated gross margin rose to 38.5% and first positive operating cash flow (Rs 91 crore CFO), but revenue was low on depressed deliveries.
544225|2026-03.overview: Management framed Q4 FY26 as a reset quarter: gross margin reached 38.5% (33.5% excluding PLI) versus 13.7% a year earlier, and consolidated OpEx including leases fell to Rs 428 crore from Rs 844 crore. Revenue was weak because deliveries were depressed by internal service and operations fixes, with FY26 consolidated revenue at Rs 2,253 crore on 173,794 deliveries. Management says registrations have recovered for three months, orders are running ahead of registrations, and Q1 FY27 guidance is 40,000-45,000 orders and Rs 500-550 crore revenue. The Gigafactory's first 3 GWh is in ramp-up with the remaining 3.5 GWh slated for June, and the company is pushing Shakti and Roadster bike growth.

qa_highlights.answer: Own cells are already cheaper on pure BOM even at low volumes; at 6 GWh with overheads the advantage is expected to be 10-15%.

qa_highlights.answer: Company prefers word-of-mouth and does not do TV or IPL sponsorship; may advertise in coming months. Cell monetisation requires a subsidiary-level capital raise; management has inbound PE interest but gave no timing beyond 'in due course'.

544225|2026-06.headline: Ola Electric Q1 FY27 deliveries nearly doubled QoQ to ~39,200 units, Auto revenue ₹455 crore (+72% QoQ), Auto gross margin 30.5%.
544225|2026-06.overview: Ola returned to volume growth in Q1 FY27, with deliveries of ~39,200 units (nearly 2x QoQ) and orders of ~44,000, while electric two-wheeler registrations grew 97% against a market up ~17% QoQ, lifting share from 5.1% to 8.4%. Auto revenue rose 72% QoQ to ₹455 crore with gross profit of ₹139 crore and Auto gross margin held at 30.5%. Consolidated opex fell 22% QoQ to ₹333 crore (including a ~₹55 crore one-time reversal of a Cell ACC PLI penalty provision), and adjusted operating EBITDA improved to –₹195 crore from –₹326 crore in Q4 FY26. Management pivoted Auto distribution from company-owned to a multi-channel model with dealers, with the first batch slated to go live on Janmashtami (4 September), and reiterated a Cell gigafactory ramp to 6 GWh.

544226|2026-03.headline: FirstCry Q4 FY26: consol revenue up 12% to ₹8,547 Cr for FY26; Q4 adjusted EBITDA up 18% to ₹118.7 Cr amid India gross margin pressure.
544226|2026-03.overview: Brainbees (FirstCry) reported Q4 and FY26 with consolidated FY26 revenue up 12% to ₹8,547 Cr, adjusted EBITDA up 24% to about ₹486 Cr, and free cash flow positive for the full year. India multi-channel grew 11.4% in Q4 but gross margin fell on diaper price competition from quick-commerce and horizontal players, plus a transitory manufacturing hit from rupee depreciation and crude-linked inputs. Management says the offline channel grew about 15% in Q4 after a product-mix shift, and that RocketBees and Qwik delivery initiatives are lifting service levels, with the benefit expected to show in FY27. International losses fell 35% in FY26 and GlobalBees core categories grew 28%.

segments.name: India multi-channel
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +11.4% and FY26 revenue +9%; GMV +11% in FY26, crossing $1 billion for the first time. Management says the segment stayed PAT and cash flow positive in FY26. Non-diapering is over 85% of GMV; diapering (about 15% of business) faces heavy price competition.

segments.name: International (UAE and KSA)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue above $100 million, growing about 10% in FY26; Q4 revenue +9%. Gross margin rose 240 bps for FY26 (470 bps in Q4). Management did not give a timeline for reaching break-even.

segments.name: GlobalBees
segments.commentary: FY26 consolidated revenue +20% (organic, after brand rationalisation) and core categories +28%. Adjusted EBITDA post-corporate expenses was 5.8% of revenue in Q4 (₹26.5 Cr) and about 3% for FY26 after ESOP cost. Brand rationalisation is expected to finish by end Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Others (preschool)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue +11% with EBITDA margin about 27% (vs 24% in FY25). Preschools more than doubled from 208 at end FY24, and enrolled students are almost 3x in two years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 India multi-channel GMV and revenue growth guided to be much superior to FY26; management expects sequential quarterly improvement to continue.
India multi-channel FY27 EBITDA (rupee terms) guided to grow double digits, per management's 'should' answer; margin expansion expected outside diapering.
Gross margin loss from the Q3 diaper competition (about 140 bps) expected to take 4-6 quarters to reverse; manufacturing-related loss expected to be recovered from Q2 FY27 via pass-through.

capex_capacity: RocketBees own-network coverage grew from 13 cities (Q2) to 22 (Q3) to 62 cities (Q4); management aims to cross 50 cities by next quarter-end.

Q4 online GMV grew about 10.5%, and online growth held at about 11-12% across all four quarters of FY26. Offline GMV grew about 15% in Q4.
Annual unique transacting customers in India multi-channel: 11 million.
India multi-channel Q4 orders +10% and GMV +12%; AOV in International is about 4x India's.
Management says the Middle East has seen some moderation in consumer sentiment and import complexities, but it is 'beyond anyone's control'.
Ages 6-12 is the fastest-growing age cohort in India multi-channel.

qa_highlights.question: What share of orders now goes through FirstCry's own delivery network, and what is the logistics cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Share rose from about 28% at end Q3 to over 40% at end March 2026, with a target of 45-50% by mid-year. Logistics cost is front-loaded by about 40-60 bps for a few quarters until networks mature.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company pause COCO store openings in FY26, and what is the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Openings were paused for capital efficiency given macro conditions. Management plans about 100 stores in FY27 across COCO and FOFO formats, citing the best offline growth in seven quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How is the gross margin pressure in diapering split between competition and input inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: The 140 bps Q3 competitive hit has continued into Q4. The remaining manufacturing-related hit from rupee depreciation and crude-linked inputs is transitory and expected to be recovered from Q2 FY27 as prices are passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the online growth slowdown structural, given offline grew faster than the 11% overall?
qa_highlights.answer: Online GMV grew about 10.5% in Q4 and 11-12% through FY26. Management expects RocketBees and Qwik to lift online growth in FY27, with results lagging. Product mix between online and offline has not changed.

qa_highlights.question: Can India multi-channel EBITDA grow double digits in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing recovery of the manufacturing hit by Q2 (three quarters of benefit), continued margin expansion in the non-diaper categories, and operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Middle East situation affecting international revenue and break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumer sentiment has moderated and import complexities have emerged. Management sees this as an opportunity to optimise discounting and marketing and to improve home-brand mix, and says the focus remains sustainable growth over top-line chasing.

risks_watch: Diaper price war from quick-commerce and horizontal platforms could keep gross margins under pressure beyond the 4-6 quarter window management has given.
Management has tied the FY27 recovery to a Q2 pass-through of manufacturing costs, with rupee depreciation and crude prices as the swing factors.
Middle East consumer sentiment and import complexities could slow International, where revenue growth was about 9-10%.

GlobalBees brand rationalisation is due to finish by end Q1 FY27; the consolidated growth figure will lag until then.
Management declined to quantify AI-driven savings, saying the number will come in later quarterly updates. It also said there have been no buyback or acquisition discussions.

544226|2026-06.headline: Brainbees Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to ₹2,106 crore, but India multi-channel gross margin fell ~260 bps YoY, holding adjusted EBITDA margin at 4.24%.
544226|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to ₹2,106 crore, with GMV up 12% to ₹2,807 crore and AUTC up 10% to 11.8 million. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 4.24% from 4.98%, and gross margin dropped to 36.5% from 38.5%, mainly from India multi-channel diapering competition and manufacturing cost pass-through lag. Management said diapering competition is easing and that the crude/rupee cost pass-through completes by end-Q2, but gave no firm timeline for margin recovery. Growth drivers cited were RocketBees (over 50% of online shipments), FC Qwik (125,000 shipments in June across 12 cities) and offline GMV growth of 15%.

segments.name: India multi-channel
segments.commentary: Revenue +18% YoY, best in seven quarters; GMV +12%, orders +12%, AUTC +10%. Non-diapering is ~85% of GMV; gross margin down ~260 bps YoY and EBITDA margin down ~290 bps YoY on diapering competition and manufacturing input costs. Remains PAT positive.

segments.name: International (Middle East)
segments.commentary: Revenue +12% YoY, AUTC +7%, GMV +9%. Adjusted EBITDA loss reduced 22% YoY; loss-to-revenue improved from 10% to 7%. Management targets EBITDA neutrality but gave no timeline.

segments.name: GlobalBees
segments.commentary: Revenue roughly flat due to a planned warehouse and inventory transition for one core brand, expected to complete in Q2 with growth recovering from Q3. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 3.9% from 1%.

segments.name: Preschool (FirstCry Intellitots)
segments.commentary: Revenue +47% to ₹19 crore and adjusted EBITDA +65% to ₹5 crore. Over 500 preschools; management targets at least 1,000 over the next couple of years, organically, with no M&A being evaluated.

guidance_outlook: Management expects India multi-channel growth to stay elevated for subsequent FY27 quarters, citing RocketBees, FC Qwik and offline store expansion.

RocketBees expanded from 62 to 72 cities and now handles over 50% of online shipments, a target set two quarters ago and met by June 2026. Delivery turnaround time improved ~20%.
FC Qwik (2-hour quick delivery) grew from ~60,000 shipments in five cities in March to 125,000 in 12 cities in June. Management targets 10% of total shipments on FC Qwik and 20% in specific pincodes.
Manufacturing business is passing crude-linked raw material and rupee-depreciation cost increases to customers.
demand_pricing: Diapering faces heightened competition from quick commerce discounting and new entrants. Management says branded diapering has started improving in Q1 and competitive intensity is softer in July and August.
Non-diapering categories (~85% of GMV, fashion >50% of GMV, home brands >50% of business) are performing well; management said gross margin is expected to improve through home brand and fashion mix.

Offline GMV grew 15% in Q1 after the width-to-depth assortment change, which added lower price points without a material gross margin impact.

qa_highlights.question: Jay Laddha asked how much of the manufacturing-related gross margin loss was recovered in Q1 and whether International breakeven timing or FY27 guidance had any update.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India multi-channel gross margin recovered about 20 bps of the 280 bps Q4 drop, with full pass-through of crude and rupee costs by end-Q2. On International, Abhinav Sharma declined to give a breakeven quarter, pointing to inputs (home brand mix, high-margin brand curation, quality customer acquisition); the loss-to-revenue ratio moved from -16% in March 2025 to -7% in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Kumar asked whether India multi-channel growth can be sustained next quarter and when margin will recover.
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth to remain elevated for the next few quarters on RocketBees, FC Qwik and offline stores. Margin recovery is expected faster than the 4-6 quarter diapering normalisation, with diapering competition easing in July and August and crude/rupee pass-through complete by end-Q2, full recovery likely from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Ranodeep Sen asked about the company's right to win in diapering against pharmacy and private-label entrants, and whether M&A is being considered in preschool.
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goel said diapering retention is hard for private labels and that quick commerce discounting is temporary; branded diapering showed some improvement in Q1. Supam Maheshwari said FC Qwik and the full-destination model support retention. On preschool, he said organic growth to at least 1,000 preschools over a couple of years, with no M&A being looked at yet.

qa_highlights.question: Percy Panthaki asked whether the sequential India multi-channel EBITDA margin decline is due to crude-linked inflation and whether H2 EBITDA margin will at least match last year.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 280 bps Q4 drop had two components: diapering competition (expected to take 4-6 quarters to normalise) and manufacturing input costs (full recovery by end-Q2, normalised from Q3). Gautam Sharma bridged the 290 bps YoY India EBITDA margin decline as 260 bps gross margin loss plus 30 bps from logistics costs, partly offset by marketing and fixed-cost leverage. Supam Maheshwari said the 280 bps gap should 'dramatically' reduce, without a quantified target.

qa_highlights.question: Percy Panthaki asked why India revenue growth (18%) exceeds GMV growth (12%).
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the revenue line combines online, offline and manufacturing, while GMV is at MRP. GST 2.0, effective Q2, reduced MRP and contributed to the gap.

qa_highlights.question: Harsh Gokal Gandhi asked for the profitability delta between diapering and non-diapering and the company's share of the diapering category.
qa_highlights.answer: Supam Maheshwari said the delta between diapering and non-diapering has widened, with over 50% of GMV in fashion and over 50% of business in home brands. He said the delta should shrink as diapering margins recover; no market share figure was given. Archana Menon asked about store expansion and non-diapering consumables; management said about 100 net new stores in FY27 (90-100 per Gautam Sharma, net of attrition) and that non-diapering consumables are about 15% of GMV with healthy margins.

544227|2026-03.headline: Unicommerce FY26 revenue rose 51.6% to INR204.3 crore, but Q4 adjusted EBITDA growth slowed to 7.8% as investments step up.
544227|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 51.6% to INR204.3 crore and adjusted EBITDA rose 54.5% to INR43.9 crore, with FY26 being the first full year consolidating Shipway. Q4 revenue grew 14% YoY to INR51.6 crore, but adjusted EBITDA grew only 7.8% to INR9.6 crore and PAT grew 1.6% to INR3.4 crore after management began stepping up growth investments in Q4. Management guided to lower adjusted EBITDA and PAT over the next two quarters, while expecting higher full-year operational profitability in FY27 than FY26. Management also disclosed it is evaluating a merger with Shipway Technology Private Limited.

Standalone adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 37.5% in FY26 from 25% in FY25. Management said the business turned around from about 8% growth in Q3 to double digits in Q4.

segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 growth of 17.7% YoY, with management targeting double-digit growth in FY27 at a faster pace than Uniware. Shipway is not EBITDA positive in Q4 due to sales, marketing and AI investments; management says gross margin is around 20%.

segments.commentary: Turned profitable in FY26 and is growing faster than India, but contributes about 6-7% of revenue, up from 4-5%. Operates in 7 geographies, with Dubai, Philippines and Malaysia as the priority markets.

segments.commentary: Entry point into the pre-purchase journey; Catalyst AI voice bot is live. No separate financials were disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ARPA fall 11% in FY26 despite price escalation clauses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth now relies on new clients and new product adoption as market growth softened; price escalation was added to new contracts from last year and will be extended to existing contracts with benefits in later years.

qa_highlights.question: What is Shipway's FY26 EBITDA margin and steady-state margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give Shipway's margin; it said Shipway is not EBITDA positive in Q4 due to investments, while standalone adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 37.5%. Shipway gross margin is about 20% and standalone gross margin about 80%.

qa_highlights.question: What is NRR and the incremental sales and marketing spend?
qa_highlights.answer: NRR remains above 100% excluding the top-10 churn; new client contribution is 7-8% of revenue. Management did not quantify incremental sales and marketing; it cited investment across sales and marketing, AI talent, AI tools and mid-to-senior hires.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company rely on acquisitions for growth, and what is the target profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisitions are a core strategy: targets should be relevant to existing customers, AI-relevant, profitable or near profitability, and reasonably valued. Pre-purchase (ConvertWay adjacency) and post-purchase (analytics, loyalty) are white spaces.

qa_highlights.question: How is ESOP expense rising and what dilution should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ESOPs were issued to existing and new mid-to-senior talent, increasing share-based expense; it aims to avoid dilution from acquisitions by using cash instead.

qa_highlights.question: Any slowdown from the Middle East conflict?
qa_highlights.answer: India business has seen little disruption; the Middle East, a small contributor, saw slightly longer sales cycles in recent weeks, which management said are normalising.

risks_watch: Lower adjusted EBITDA and PAT in Q1-Q2 FY27 from investment ramp; FY27 full-year profit recovery depends on H2 operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Why are some energy-sector orders on 15-16 month execution periods, and what is the export contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: The orders are for HVDC valve halls from EPC contractors on variable-price terms, and site clearances take about 6 months versus 2-3 months normally. qa_highlights.question: Why was finance cost up sharply, and what is the debt position?

544238|2026-03.headline: Premier Energies FY26 revenue rose 20.7% to INR8,026 crore and PAT 61.1% to INR1,510 crore, with order book at INR14,010 crore (+66% YoY).

Non-DCR orders surged after the ALMM extension to December; management says non-DCR business is not profitable currently with over 200-250 GW module capacity against about 30 GW non-DCR demand, though prices improved slightly for the coming quarter.
DCR module realisations stable: Surya Ghar about 24-24.5 cents/W, KUSUM about 22 cents/W, C&I slightly lower; no change expected over 12-15 months as orders are booked.
Cell pricing (mono-PERC) stable; long-term cell contracts have variable wafer, silver and FX pass-through. Most orders are USD-linked.

Management said the cell-to-DCR-module mix will shift steadily over the next 18-24 months; cell sales expected at about 50-50 internal vs external split historically, skewing to internal use as ALMM Phase 2 and DCR demand grow.
US minimum import price proposal on cells and modules cited as making US manufacturing attractive; Europe tenders in Italy and France and expected in Germany.

qa_highlights.question: How much DC overloading should be assumed for PM KUSUM, and what is the demand outlook for the next nine months?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended overloading of 1.2-1.25x (KUSUM B at 1.0x, KUSUM C at 1.3-1.5x). Management expects about 1.2-1.3 GW per quarter of rooftop and 6-8 GW AC (possibly more than 8 GW) of KUSUM over nine months; total about 23-24 GW DC over nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Why sell cells rather than convert them into DCR modules and capture the margin?

qa_highlights.question: Will C&I demand be deferred by the ALMM extension, and is DCR capacity blocked?

qa_highlights.question: Is 29-30% EBITDA margin sustainable over the next two to three years?

qa_highlights.question: What is the transformer revenue ramp for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the initial ramp to be slightly below the analyst's INR600-700 crore FY27 estimate; business to treble over three years versus last year's INR400 crores; margins targeted slightly above the historical 15% EBITDA / 8-10% PAT cycle average.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses and employee costs jump sharply?

544239|2026-03.headline: ECOS Q4 FY26 revenue up 16.65% to INR2,067.6 million, EBITDA down to INR241.5 million; FY27 guided to 18-20% growth at 11-13% margin.
544239|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 16.65% YoY to INR2,067.60 million, while EBITDA declined to INR241.53 million from INR264.67 million in Q4 FY25, reflecting continued investment in people, technology and leadership. For FY26, revenue rose 23.58% to INR8,081.58 million and EBITDA was INR939.29 million, with margins hit by higher manpower cost, tech spend, ETS price competition and a one-time doubtful-debt provision of about INR80 million. Management said the Middle East crisis dented CCR growth in March, and guided FY27 revenue growth of 18-20% and EBITDA margin of 11-13%, with cost growth expected to be lower than revenue growth. Analysts pressed on margin compression, falling revenue per trip and competitive pricing in ETS; management attributed the trend partly to shorter trips and airport transfers.

vs 4.04 million in FY25, approx. +29% YoY

Direct web booking portal launched in Q4 FY26 for pre-scheduled rides, aimed at premium individuals and SMEs rather than mass B2C.

55% of FY26 revenue from clients associated with ECOS for more than five years. Churn among top 200 clients is about 2-3%, per management.
Demand from GCCs and manufacturing facilities is a notable driver of ETS enterprise wins; CCR growth is diversified across sectors.
Competitive price pressure is mainly in ETS, led by new entrants; management says prices should rise once operations prove unsustainable.

Average revenue per trip fell from about INR1,600 in FY25 to about INR1,550 in FY26, versus about INR1,750-1,780 in FY24. Management cited pricing pressure plus shorter ETS trips and more CCR airport transfers.
No demand impact seen yet from the government's work-from-home appeal.

qa_highlights.question: How is the West Asia crisis affecting demand, and what is FY27 growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CCR growth slowed in March after the Middle East crisis, with a bounce back expected if the disruption is short. Management aspires to 18-20% growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can fuel price hikes be passed on, and what is the margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Most contracts have pass-through clauses triggered above roughly 5%, with lags of days to weeks. Management says the 6-7% increase has been fully passed on.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the INR8 crore receivable provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Legal proceedings for recovery are ongoing and management is hopeful. Recovery may come in FY27 or later.

qa_highlights.question: What are the expected growth rates for employee and other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is budgeted to grow about 13-16% and other expenses about 8-9%, both below the revenue growth target. Management expects operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue per trip declining, and is pricing pressure easing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited ETS pricing pressure and shorter trips plus airport transfers. Pressure appears to have stabilised in the last quarter, while the company is also winning larger enterprise contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins recover to the earlier 14-16% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 11-13% for FY27 and the next couple of years. It expects CCR brand premium to offset ETS price competition over time.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin in FY26 was about 11.6%, down from roughly 15% at IPO, and Q4 EBITDA fell YoY despite 16.65% revenue growth.
Falling revenue per trip (about INR1,550 in FY26) indicates pricing pressure in ETS from new entrants.
Pending legal recovery of the roughly INR80 million doubtful debt; timing is uncertain.
Middle East and fuel-price volatility affecting CCR demand and the lag in fuel pass-through.
Cost growth versus revenue growth in FY27: the company needs to deliver operating leverage against its 13-16% employee cost budget.
Dividend decision pending a separate board meeting.

rows.why: Asset-light model with about 20,000 vendor vehicles (vs about 14,000 in FY25) and EV capex kept cautious at roughly INR30 million a year; no utilisation figure or board capex plan was disclosed.

rows.why: Direct web booking portal launched in Q4 FY26 for pre-scheduled rides and a new core backend platform launched, but no further product launch dates were given.

rows.why: Legal recovery proceedings are ongoing and management is hopeful, but the roughly INR80 million provision may only be recovered in FY27 or later, so timing is uncertain.

rows.why: Employee cost is budgeted at 13-16% and other expenses at 8-9% against 18-20% revenue growth, with fuel increases above about 5% passed through to clients with lags of days to weeks.

tone.note: Management was confident on client wins, GCC-driven ETS demand and the CCR brand premium, and cautious on near-term margins, the March CCR slowdown and EV capex. Analysts pressed on margin compression (FY26 about 11.6% vs roughly 15% at IPO), falling revenue per trip and ETS pricing competition.

544239|2026-06.headline: ECOS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.7% to INR2,113.7 mn, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.3% and FY27 margin guidance was cut to ~10%.

EBITDA was flat YoY at INR218.47 million, and margin fell to 10.3% from 12.0% a year ago and 11.7% in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the drop to higher operating costs, a higher ETS mix and more intense pricing pressure, especially in ETS. The FY27 EBITDA margin guidance was lowered to around 10% from the earlier 11-13% range, while revenue growth guidance of 15-18% was retained.

544240|2026-03.headline: Raymond Lifestyle FY26 total income hit record INR7,034 crore (+11% YoY) and EBITDA rose 23% to INR804 crore; Q4 EBITDA up 53% to INR152 crore.

Q4 FY26 total income was a record INR1,810 crore (+15% YoY), with EBITDA up 53% to INR152 crore and margin up 210 bps QoQ to 8.4%. 544248|2026-06.headline: Mach Travel Q1 FY27 revenue rose 538% YoY to INR144.33 crore, with EBITDA margin compressing to 6.09% from 7.17%.
544248|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR144.33 crore versus INR22.62 crore a year ago and INR83.25 crore in Q4 FY26, with GMV of about INR252 crore disclosed for the first time. EBITDA rose to INR8.92 crore and PAT to INR6.17 crore, but margins were lower YoY, which management attributed to investment in new verticals, hiring and technology. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR500-plus crore and said it is working on bank overdraft lines because of working capital pressure from payment cycles. Much of the quarter's growth came from a few large government and MICE programmes, and several answers were vague or deferred.

segments.commentary: Launched in April 2026 with more than 100 corporate clients signed; management put it at about 10-15% of revenue. Billing cycles run 1st-15th payable on the 20th and 16th-30th payable on the 6th-7th of the next month.

segments.commentary: Punjab Yatra contract worth about INR92 crore covering 1.85 lakh yatris, at about INR4,950 per person for a 2-night, 3-day trip. Management said about 15% of Q1 revenue came from it; about 1.15 lakh travelled to date and the contract runs to about November.

segments.commentary: Empanelled as one of four or five A-listed vendors, with a first order of about INR75 lakh to INR1 crore. Empanelment term was stated as two years, extendable, but the executive director was not certain.

segments.commentary: B2B tool lets smaller travel agents book tickets. B2C app Machtravel.com is in testing and its launch was pushed from late August to September 2026. Leisure was described as doing very well, with no figures given.

Management said quarter-on-quarter growth will not be substantial because October-December is a festival and Christmas lull for corporate travel; Q2 is seasonally heavier than Q1 overall.
Management would not commit to a date for EBITDA margins returning to the roughly 10% level mentioned by an analyst, and would not say margins will be under pressure in Q2.
Markups may be compressed in aggressive pursuit of business, but management said the company will not burn money.

capex_capacity: Operating presence expanded to Noida, New Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Bhubaneshwar and Ahmedabad; more southern offices planned.
Investment in technology, talent and offices over the past year is cited as the cause of lower margins; no quantified capex figure was given.

Captive audience of about 1.25 lakh travellers a year is to be moved onto the B2C portal and app.
demand_pricing: Management attributed the growth to the transition beyond MICE into corporate, B2B, leisure, government and B2C, and said the policies were implemented from 1 April 2026.
TTV (total ticketed volume) was about INR259-260 crore versus about INR143 crore in revenue; the call did not reconcile TTV with GMV of INR252 crore.
Management said pricing on the B2C app is at par with large B2C players.
Punjab Yatra daily flows are about 1,100 travellers out and 1,100 back, with about 3,300-3,500 people handled at any one time.
Management said it is not clear whether the Punjab yatra will be repeated; three other Punjab yatra programmes were not won. Management is in talks with other state governments.

qa_highlights.question: How did revenue grow from INR22 crore to INR140-plus crore, and what steps were taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company spent about 1.5 years building new teams and technology and implemented the policies from April 2026. Revenue now comes from MICE, corporate, leisure, government and B2B; TTV was about INR259-260 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital be managed to support growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is debt free with about INR3 crore of debt, but payment-cycle issues have created a working capital need. It is working toward bank overdraft facilities and will update the market if availed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between core MICE and the new verticals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management was unsure of the exact split. It said about INR50-60 crore came from MICE in one answer and about INR100 crore in another, with corporate at 10-15% and the Punjab Yatra at about 15%.

qa_highlights.question: When will EBITDA margins recover to about 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no firm date. It said margins will improve as business scales, buying power rises and markups increase, but that it will be aggressive in the market and may give up some markup.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR500 crore guidance conservative given Q1 was about 29-30% of it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the figure is an annual average and cited seasonality. It said it hopes to surpass INR500 crore, but expects no substantial quarter-on-quarter growth in Q2 and Q3 because of festival periods.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Punjab Yatra contract repeatable, and how is it paid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the contract is for 1.85 lakh yatris at about INR4,950 per person and runs to about November. Payment is about 7 days after travel, roughly 15 days in total. It was unsure whether the programme would be repeated.

544252|2026-03.headline: Bajaj Housing Finance Q4 FY26 PAT rose 14% to INR669 crore (20% ex one-time tax benefit), with AUM up 23% and GNPA steady at 27 bps.
544252|2026-03.overview: AUM crossed INR140,000 crore, growing 23% YoY, with quarterly AUM additions of INR7,294 crore and disbursements up 23% YoY to INR17,506 crore. Spreads compressed 10 bps QoQ to 1.7% and NIM fell 12 bps to 3.8% on lower acquisition yields and a 15 bps PLR pass-through in December. Asset quality held (GNPA 27 bps, NNPA 11 bps), but annualised credit cost rose to 19 bps from 11 bps YoY on a deliberate Stage 2 provision top-up. Management guided to ROA compression of about 10 bps in FY27 (towards upper end of the 2.0-2.2% medium-term range) assuming no policy rate change, and said it will firm up guidance with Q1 results.

544252|2026-06.headline: Bajaj Housing Q1 FY27: record AUM addition of INR8,918 crore (AUM up 24% to INR1.496 lakh crore) and PAT up 23% to INR715 crore, but NIM fell 14 bps to 3.7%.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 20-25 bps FY27 NIM compression, and is there any pricing relief or PLR hike possibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the compression mainly to yield decline: high-yield book is running off while new business comes in at lower yields in a stable rate regime. Acquisition pricing has been stable, and no large-scale upward pricing move is assumed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 credit cost drop to 5 bps? Are there one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, two one-offs: a Q4 FY26 Stage 2 provision build that was not repeated, and a roughly INR2,300 crore assignment that released Stage 1 provisions. Management said to treat it as about 5 bps; the FY27 guide stays at 10-15 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM fall 13-14 bps when spreads were flat and cost of funds fell 7 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: The spread is computed on period-end portfolio yield versus average cost of funds, so it moved only 3-4 bps. The margin decline is from portfolio yield compression, which will continue through FY27 and offset the cost-of-funds benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of funds outlook for Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds is expected to be sideways in Q2 FY27 with a downward bias, helped by hedging, repayment of older high-cost borrowings and resets of some older borrowings to lower rates.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the LAP and DF Stage 2 to Stage 3 movement not raising provisions, and is there stress in LAP?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP provisions are formula-based on DPD, so roll-backs and roll-ins net off; the LAP movement was INR18 crore in total, not one account. DF provisioning was already held at 48-49% on the account. Management cited LAP GNPA in a 46-76 bps range over seven quarters and said there is no segment or geography concern.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Stage 1 provisions stay flat despite a INR7,500 crore rise in Stage 1 assets?
qa_highlights.answer: The annual January ECL recalibration lowered Stage 1 rates on most portfolios because credit performance was stronger, and the mix of new and attrited customers also shifted. Management said there is no simple pool-to-pool calculation.

544252|2026-09.headline: Bajaj Housing Finance Q2 FY27: PAT up 18% YoY to INR757 crore, AUM at INR1.58 lakh crore growing 25%, with management flagging ~25 bps NIM compression ahead.
544252|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 showed AUM crossing INR1.5 lakh crore, disbursements up 25% YoY to INR19,900 crore, and stable asset quality (GNPA 29 bps, NNPA 12 bps). Cost of funds fell 17 bps QoQ to about 7.0% from fixed-to-floating NCD conversion, offsetting a 10 bps portfolio yield decline, so NIM dipped 2 bps to 3.7%. Management said the repo hike will pass through roughly 80% to both liabilities and assets, but acquisition pricing from banks is still unclear and is the main margin and attrition risk. Guidance on AUM growth (21-23%) and NIM compression (~25 bps for the year) was not revised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did developer finance decline QoQ, and what is the strategy for the DF book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher repayments from project cash flows plus slower disbursements drove the decline, not a conscious strategy. DF sanctions rose sharply in H1, and the target is 15-17% of the portfolio, with recovery expected in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the repo hikes compress margins and how much pass-through is possible on the prime side?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80-82% of repo hikes flow through to cost of funds and to portfolio pricing, so the main margin risk is on acquisition pricing. If prime acquisition pricing lags, attrition and BT-out rise and the company shifts toward non-prime.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the fall in fee income?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income rose on higher insurance income (attachment rates higher with Sambhav growth) and higher foreclosure income in the quarter, not a decline. Fee-related expenses are marginal and range-bound.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20 bps cost of funds decline a one-off, and what is the exit COF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a starting point, not a one-off, though part came from one-time maturity of high-priced borrowings. Three 25 bps hikes would take COF up about 61 bps, from roughly 7% in September to about 7.6% by March.

qa_highlights.question: Why did home loan originations decline QoQ, and what is the YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly movements are seasonal and the company tracks AUM rather than disbursals. Home loan disbursal growth was 24% YoY, close to the company's 25% disbursement growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will guidance be revised given NIM expansion this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no revision for now. NIM compression of about 25 bps is still expected, and AUM growth could slow to 22-23% if acquisition pricing lags, given the rise in BT-out rates.

544253|2026-03.headline: Kross Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 225.4 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.9%; management guides 14-15% margins and FY27 growth near 22%.
544253|2026-03.overview: Kross closed FY26 with revenue of INR 673.2 crore (+8.5%) and PAT of INR 55.2 crore (8.2% margin), after a slow H1 and a stronger H2 (H2 revenue 49.2% above H1). Q4 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 225.4 crore, EBITDA rose 25% to INR 33.6 crore and PAT rose 31% to INR 22.4 crore. Management says the Middle East conflict caused LPG shortages and commodity and consumable cost increases in Q4, with steel price hikes of INR 3-5/kg expected from April and a retrospective OEM pass-through lagging by about one quarter. The company has raised prices about 5% in trailer axles and suspensions and says it has fully deployed IPO proceeds.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA growth stated as 8.2% (transcript reads 87.9%, likely a transcription error)

financial_highlights.value: Trailer axles and suspension 43%; other components 57%

segments.name: Trailer axles and suspension
segments.commentary: Q4 volumes were over 10,500 trailer axles and over 3,500 suspension units, with air and mechanical suspension leading the pick-up. Q4 mix was about 60% suspension and 40% axles, and FY26 axle to suspension mix was about 70:30.

segments.name: Tipping Jacks (new)
segments.commentary: Launched and validated in Q4 FY26, with 75-80 kits sold in Q4 and 150-200 kits guided for Q1 FY27. Management targets 300 units by end-Q1 and 500 units each in Q2 and Q3, and says revenue will pick up at 300-400 kits a month.

segments.name: Tractor and Agri
segments.commentary: Tractor is about 9% of revenue, with a target of about 15% within two years. A third large tractor OEM is to start revenue from Q1 FY27, alongside diversification with existing two OEMs into forgings, shafts and castings.

segments.commentary: Exports were 4% of FY26 revenue. Management cites secured orders from European Tier-1 customers and aims to raise the share over two years; export of extruded axles will wait until the line runs above 5,000 beams a month.
