544253|2026-06.headline: Kross Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32.3% YoY to INR184.3 crore, with EBITDA margin at 12.23% (up 63 bps) and PAT up 24.4% to INR133.12 million.
544253|2026-06.overview: Kross reported its best-ever Q1 top line, with revenue of INR184.3 crore (up 32.3% YoY) and EBITDA up 39.5% YoY to INR225.54 million. Management attributed growth to volumes across M&HCV, trailers and tractors, and said the extrusion axle beam line is now in production. Steel and conversion-cost pass-throughs are being settled, with the tractor industry already settled from April 1 and CV settlement pending. Management said Q1 is in line with its FY27 targets, though June-July demand is seasonally subdued.

financial_highlights.change: +32.3% YoY vs INR139.3 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue mix: trailers, axles, suspensions and tipping

financial_highlights.change: Management targets 40-45% export growth this FY

segments.name: M&HCV / CV
segments.commentary: Momentum from Q4 FY26 continued into Q1; OEMs indicate a strong September quarter and stronger Q3 and Q4, backed by order books. Tractor-trailer and tipper segments expected to grow well.

segments.name: Trailer axles and suspensions
segments.commentary: Q1 axle volume about 9,500 numbers and suspension volume about 3,200-3,300 (mechanical and air). Volumes up about 30% YoY; management attributes this to Q4 FY26 order spillover and capacity that capped Q4 sales.

segments.name: Tipping jacks
segments.commentary: About 200 kits (management also cited 226 sold in Q1) against 800 per month capacity; management expects 65-70% utilisation by Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Tractor
segments.commentary: Demand described as consistent; management expects the tractor contribution to rise meaningfully over coming years.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Existing supply to a European tier 1 is on plan. Four to five product lines are in play; one is in mass production and three are scheduled from H2 FY27. Target of about 8% export share in two years, from about 4-4.5% now.

guidance_outlook: Export growth of 40-45% targeted for FY27.
Export share target of at least 8% of revenue in about two years.
Price increase of about 3-5% on axles from April 1, with a further 1-2% planned in staggered fashion.
Steel settlement at INR4,700 per kg, applied retrospectively, around July 15. Conversion-cost increase still under negotiation with customers.
Seamless tube plant to be commissioned by Q4 FY27, with production trials by end of FY27. Imported piercing mill and other mills are on high seas.
Axle shaft facility using material gathering and press forging technology on track for commissioning by September 2026.
High-pressure mould line for foundry expected in Q3 FY27, doubling foundry capacity.
Management expects margins to expand quarter-on-quarter as pass-throughs flow in.
capex_capacity: Axle beam extrusion line commissioned and in production; volumes ramping.
Tipping jack capacity of 800 numbers per month, with lines set up; 65-70% utilisation targeted by Q4 FY27.
Seamless tube facility: piercing mill received; sizing and straightening mills on high seas; term loan of about INR100 crore taken and to be drawn as machines arrive.
Forging and casting capacity expansion from IPO proceeds is complete; management says no further forging/casting capacity needed for current ramp-up, with utilisation around 70%.
Machining capacity additions continue for new OEM product lines.
demand_pricing: Management says CV volumes will grow well this year, with OEM schedules indicated from September through March; June-July is seasonally subdued due to monsoon.
Trailer-axle growth of about 34% YoY was attributed to Q4 FY26 order spillover and capacity constraints in Q4; management declined to comment on market share.
Prices on the trailer business were raised from April 1. Management says pricing will track competitors, who also face steel inflation.
Management said there was no business loss from the top five customers over the last two years. Top-five share is about 58-59%, versus about 60-63% at DRHP.

Government Parivartan scheme effective October 30, 2026 bars BS4 and older vehicles from Delhi NCR. It offers 10-year road tax holiday, free registration, and roughly 13% discount (5% subsidy plus 8% OEM discount).

qa_highlights.question: How are cost pressures evolving, and have OEM steel and conversion settlements been done?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel settlement of INR4,700 per kg was applied retrospectively around July 15. Tractor industry settled a conversion percentage retrospective from April 1; CV settlement expected soon. Export plans are on track.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export target and the size of the European tier 1 order?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of at least 8% export share in two years. One product is in mass production; three more start from H2. Export growth of 40-45% is targeted this FY.

qa_highlights.question: Is the trailer-axle growth of about 34% share gain, given single-digit industry growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was largely Q4 FY26 order spillover. Management declined to comment on market share; capacity expansion should allow further growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the worst margin quarter behind us, with QoQ expansion ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects QoQ margin expansion. Steel pass-through is retrospective but will come in gradually. Conversion cost increase is the larger factor.

qa_highlights.question: Why did top-five customer revenue fall between DRHP and FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the top-five share fell from about 60-63% to 58-59% through diversification, and it would check the INR figures.

qa_highlights.question: What are utilisation and debt plans, and does capex need to increase?
qa_highlights.answer: No further forging or casting capex is needed; utilisation is about 70%. No new debt for the existing business. Seamless term loan of about INR100 crore is only partly drawn.

qa_highlights.question: What price increases are planned for axles?
qa_highlights.answer: Axle prices rose about 3-5% from April 1. A further 1-2% is planned, phased to customer acceptance.

Competitive pricing: management said pricing tracks competitors, including a larger player in trailer axles.
Seamless tube commissioning slipping past Q4 FY27 and the ramp-up of the high-pressure foundry mould line in Q3.
Ramp-up of tipping jacks (65-70% utilisation by Q4) and whether axle beam volumes build.
Export H2 order inflows from the new tier 1 supplier are still under validation.
Inconsistency on top-five customer revenue: management could not confirm figures on the question about the DRHP versus FY26 numbers and said it would check.
Monsoon-related seasonal softness in June-July.

key_quotes: I am pleased to report that Kross Limited has concluded its best top line in Q1 FY27 with a sale of INR185.35 crore s, registering a growth of 32% year -on-year, building on the strong momentum of Q4 FY26.
We would not be requiring any more in the forging and casting for these volume ramp -up and we will still be operating at around a 70% utilization.
For our existing business, there is no plan on any debt in the immediate timeline.

rows.why: Four to five export product lines in play: one in mass production and three scheduled from H2 FY27, plus axle shaft facility by September 2026.

rows.why: Exports are about 4-4.5% of revenue now, with exports growth of 40-45% targeted for FY27 and a European tier 1 supply on plan; H2 order inflows still under validation.

544253|2026-09.headline: Kross Q2 FY27 revenue rose 80% YoY to INR235 crore with EBITDA margin of 13%, but reported PAT was a loss of INR19.7 million.
544253|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 was INR235 crore, up 80% YoY, with EBITDA of INR30.6 crore (13% margin). H1 FY27 revenue was INR419 crore versus INR270 crore a year earlier, with H1 EBITDA of INR53 crore. Management attributed growth to trailer and CV demand after monsoons, share gains with larger customers, and exports; margins were pressured by steel and consumable cost inflation, with price compensation expected in Q3 and Q4. The seamless tube backward-integration project (budget ~INR170 crore) is progressing, with production trials targeted for Feb-March 2027 (or end Q4 per another answer).

financial_highlights.value: INR(197) million per Sudhir Rai; INR19.69 crore per Kunal Rai (sign inconsistent in transcript)

segments.name: Components (incl. tipping jacks, exports)
segments.commentary: Contributed ~51% of Q2 revenue. Exports ~7.5-8% of component business, with management targeting ~45% export growth YoY this year. Tipping jacks: capacity ~800 units, 50-60% utilisation targeted by Q4; realisation ~INR1.4 lakh per set.

segments.commentary: Tractor exposure ~10-11% of Q2 revenue, all to OEMs. Management expects Q3 volumes similar to Q2; demand tied to inventory levels and post-Diwali seasonal dip.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q3 and Q4 volumes to be stronger than Q2; historically H2 is about 20% above H1.
Price revisions with OEMs and Tier 1s on conversion costs expected to support Q3 and Q4; steel compensation partial, with further steel increases expected in Q3.
Receivable days expected to fall to around 80, with working capital cycle below 90-95 days.

Seamless tube plant: equipment arrival end-Nov/Dec; production trials Feb-March 2027 (Sumeet Rai) vs end of Q4 (Kunal Rai in Q&A). Phase 1 ~30% of 1 lakh capacity, for captive use; targeted full backward integration by end H1 FY28.
Expected margin uplift of 3-4% on axles once in-house seamless tubes are used; tubes expected 8-10% cheaper than current buying price.
Trailer demand expected to sustain through FY27 unless unforeseen events, per management.

Preferential issue (warrants and preference shares) of ~INR63.6 crore to fund ~INR60 crore of near-term capex for CV and trailer capacity, to be spent over next two quarters.
Cold drawn tube forward integration: ~INR20-25 crore planned, for precision-size seamless tubes (incl. tipping jacks), in-house in Jamshedpur.
Other planned capex: axle shaft line expansion and robotic automation for forging and machining, to be financed through the preferential issue.
Debt: total term loan ~INR80 crore and CC/working capital ~INR32 crore as of 30 Sept; no further debt planned beyond seamless tube term loan.
Extruded axle beam line commenced commercial production ~August 2026, at ~80% utilisation of current output; ~7,500 axles per month expanded capacity referenced in analyst question.
demand_pricing: CV demand strong since GST rationalisation; monsoon-related deferment ended around July, with demand picking up in August per management.
Chhattisgarh market recovered after a long gap, contributing to trailer order growth; share gains with larger customers cited.
Q2 tractor volumes linked to TAFE planned production of 13,000-14,000 tractors in October; below-average rainfall noted by analyst.
Competition in trailer axles: York (market leader), Tata Motors, BPW and Hendrickson; components face product-family-specific competitors.

Rising steel and consumable costs compressed Q2 gross margin versus Q1 despite some price escalation; management says settlements with most OEMs/Tier 1s are underway with retrospective compensation expected.

qa_highlights.question: What drove growth above the industry for trailer axles and component segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the post-monsoon demand pickup from August, share gains with larger customers, new regional demand (e.g. Chhattisgarh), and export growth (~7.5-8% of component business).

qa_highlights.question: Volume and value growth for axles and suspensions in Q2 and H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 trailer axles above 10,500 and H1 nearly 20,000, up about 50-55% YoY; trailer value ~INR115 crore in Q2 vs ~INR58-60 crore a year earlier. Suspension volume not disclosed; to be shared later.

qa_highlights.question: Seamless tube capex spent and balance?
qa_highlights.answer: ~INR120 crore spent of ~INR170 crore budget as of Q2 (INR70 crore term loan plus ~INR50 crore further, with own contribution ~INR60 crore); remaining ~INR50 crore expected in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Will debt rise by end FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Only debt is the seamless tube term loan (~INR110-120 crore); no further debt planned. Current term loan ~INR80 crore plus ~INR32 crore working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Why gross margin fell sequentially in Q2 despite Q1 price escalations?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel prices rose every quarter and only partial compensation was received in Q1 and Q2; consumable and conversion cost settlements with OEMs/Tier 1s are coming in Q3-Q4. Management expects retrospective compensation but declined to give a timeline for returning to 14-15% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Phase 1 seamless tube capacity and margin benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 is ~30% of the 1 lakh capacity for captive use; axle margin expected to rise 3-4% once in-house tubes are used, with tubes 8-10% cheaper than current buying price.

rows.why: Utilisation is ~80% on the extruded axle beam line, and the ~INR63.6 cr preferential issue (about INR60 cr) funds axle shaft expansion and robotic forging/machining over the next two quarters; a cold-drawn tube project (~INR20-25 cr, Jamshedpur) is also planned.

544254|2026-03.headline: Tolins Tyres FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 12% to INR327.12 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR47.8 crore and PAT to INR35.69 crore.
544254|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue from operations grew about 12% YoY to INR327.12 crore, while EBITDA (excluding other income) declined to INR47.8 crore from INR57.91 crore, with margin at 14.6%. PAT fell to INR35.69 crore from INR38.67 crore, and basic EPS was INR9.03. Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 12% to INR77.99 crore, but Q4 EBITDA fell to INR11.22 crore (14.4% margin) from INR13.57 crore, with PAT of INR8.94 crore. Management attributed the pressure to a GST rate mismatch on retreading materials, higher inventory, longer receivable cycles and West Asia disruption, and gave only a soft FY27 outlook of maintaining FY26 performance.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR292.45 crore in FY25, about +12% YoY
vs INR57.91 crore in FY25, decline
vs INR38.67 crore in FY25, decline

segments.name: Retreading materials (tread rubber, PCTR)
segments.commentary: Management said about 60% of sales come from tread rubber; retread margins were hit by the GST mismatch (18% on retread materials vs 5% on new agricultural tyres), and dealer off-take fell. Industry association has sought a 5% GST rate on retreads, which the government is reportedly considering.

segments.name: Tyres (incl. agricultural, two-wheeler, tractor rear)
segments.commentary: Tyre production rose to 5,35,870 units in FY26 from 3,93,253 in FY25, about 36% growth, while top-line growth lagged. Utilisation in the Indian tyre segment was about 45%. A new heavy-duty tractor rear tyre has received an encouraging dealer response.

segments.name: UAE operations (Ras Al Khaimah)
segments.commentary: Plant capacity is 1,200 metric tons, with utilisation below 50%; management said margins are better than India, but GCC demand fell from the last quarter of FY26. Utilisation is expected to drop to 30-40% in the near term before recovering to 40-50%. Receivables are rising in the UAE.

segments.name: Exports, precured tyres and US business
segments.commentary: Management said US business started last year and repeat orders are slowly coming in, with a Europe push under way. Logistics are impacted by the Middle East war. No quantified export revenue was given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: management expects to at least maintain FY26 levels of performance, and will review this after Q2 FY27 depending on how the situation evolves.
Management expects West Asia and India-related disruptions to normalise by end of Q2 FY27 (pricing, raw material and shipping), which would support better Q3 and Q4.
EBITDA margin: management said 10% to 13% is an acceptable range, with a further 2-3% from waste and scrap reduction and operational efficiency.
Management expects a Terra Rubber recycling-linked margin benefit in FY26/FY27 through in-house offtake; no quantified synergy was given.
Management expects capex to be limited this year because existing capacity is sufficient to meet demand, and says the government is likely to correct the GST imbalance.
capex_capacity: Ras Al Khaimah (UAE) plant capacity is 1,200 metric tons, with utilisation below 50%; the plant has been operating for about 10 years.
Indian utilisation is about 45-55%: retread segment about 55% and tyre segment about 45%.
Gujarat depot commenced operations on December 1, 2025, serving tyre and retread products in Western India.
No significant capex is planned for FY27, as existing capacity is sufficient; cost reduction is focused on automation and AI-based planning tools.
Terra Rubber has started manufacturing and processing scrap into products trialled on road; management is scouting acquisitions but nothing is finalised and no numbers were shared.
demand_pricing: Tyre production volume grew 36% YoY in FY26 (5,35,870 vs 3,93,253 units) and PCTR grew about 10%; bonding gum and flaps grew 56%.
The GST cut on new commercial and agricultural tyres (from 28% to 18% and 5%, respectively) left retread materials at 18%, which narrowed retreading's 30-40% price advantage to about 20%.
Q4 tyre volumes fell QoQ due to dealer off-take hesitancy amid war-related uncertainty in March 2026.
Dealer credit was extended by about one month to 4-5 months, with a stated plan to revert to 3-4 months; China dumping in GCC is extending credit terms up to a year.
Management said competition is intense with tyre majors in retreading materials, but it believes its 40-year expertise gives it an edge.

qa_highlights.question: Why was top-line growth only about 12% against the 20% growth previously guided, and how do gross current assets of INR309 crore compare with revenue of INR327 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 20% was an optimistic projection and that actual growth was about 12%. It pointed to 36% growth in tyre volumes, with the gap explained by selling prices.

qa_highlights.question: When will operating cash flow turn positive, and what is the sales and marketing strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said credit periods were extended by about one month due to GST and geopolitical uncertainty, with the aim of reducing them over a few quarters. Management said branding spend is small and that it relies on a strong marketing manager team.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and margin of the Ras Al Khaimah UAE plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is 1,200 MT with utilisation below 50%. The CFO said UAE margins are better than India's, and utilisation could fall to 30-40% in the next three months before recovering to 40-50%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins decline in Q4 and FY26, and when will GST be corrected?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed the decline to margin pressure in retreads from the GST imbalance and weaker dealer off-take. The industry body has asked for a 5% retread GST rate, and the government is considering it.

qa_highlights.question: What are the three biggest growth drivers beyond FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Why did tyre volumes decline QoQ, and why did working capital rise from about INR230 crore to near INR300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 volumes fell because of March uncertainty. Working capital is driven by 3-4 months of dealer credit, about 4-5 months of inventory across more than 1,200 SKUs and seasonal rubber prices, and government retentions. IPO proceeds were partly used to fund inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 top-line guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects at least to maintain FY26 performance and will review after Q2 FY27, preferring to commit less and perform better.

UAE utilisation below 50% with receivable risk and China dumping in GCC; management is cautious on aggressive expansion.
Q4 volumes fell QoQ and EBITDA margin declined, so watch whether Q1 FY27 volumes and margins recover.

544256|2026-03.headline: P N Gadgil FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR10,000 crore to INR10,739 crore (+40% YoY); Q4 gross margin fell to 9.7% on a 40% bullion mix.

FY27 store plan of 25 new stores: 5-7 COCO and the balance FOCO (about 20 franchise), mostly outside Maharashtra (Gurgaon, Lucknow/UP, Gujarat).

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the customs duty hike and advance authorisation on sales and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the advance authorisation targets exporters, so it does not apply. The duty is passed to consumers, with no margin impact; it may shift demand from bars and coins toward exchanging old gold for jewellery.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging levels for FY26 and the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedging was 57% in Q4 FY25, 63% in Q3 FY26 and 67% in Q4 FY26, averaging about 60% for FY26. The target is 75-80% in FY27, held back by MCX margin and premium costs of 15-20% that tied up cash.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 revenue guidance raised from INR12,000 crore to INR13,500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 beat the INR9,500 crore guidance by about INR1,000 crore. Management cites non-Maharashtra demand (about 10% of business) and strong same-store growth, which pushed the range up to INR13,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why are the margin drivers one-off rather than structural, given likely repeat discounts and franchise growth?

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin split between bars and coins and jewellery?

qa_highlights.question: Inventory turnover decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the 3.8x FY26 turnover to about 8 COCO stores opened in Q4 that have not matured. It says turnover has been broadly flat, declining slightly over two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 store additions and non-Maharashtra plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan of 25 stores: 5-7 COCO and the balance FOCO, mostly outside Maharashtra (UP, Bihar, MP, Gujarat, Gurgaon). Demand for franchises is strong and under evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year bars and coins share and promoter shareholding timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Bars and coins were about 32% of FY26 sales. The promoter must reach 75% by September 2027, three years after the September 2024 listing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses grow only about 5% despite store expansion?

544258|2026-06.headline: Western Carriers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR465 crores, with PAT of about INR9 crores and domestic TEUs up 37%.
544258|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 12% YoY to INR465 crores from INR416 crores, with EBITDA of about INR19 crores (4.1% margin) and PAT of about INR9 crores, up about 13% QoQ. Total container throughput of 58,261 TEUs beat Q4 FY26 (57,754) for the first time, driven by domestic volumes up 37% YoY while EXIM grew only 3.2%. Management attributed EXIM weakness to Middle East war-linked vessel disruption and freight rate spikes, and said working capital days fell from 120 to about 111 and debt declined from INR217 crores to about INR197 crores since March. Analysts pressed on the lack of price pass-through, weak cash generation and receivables; management did not commit to a price hike.

It expects EXIM volumes to recover strongly once sea freight eases, and said it is learning to live with disruption.

544260|2026-03.headline: Northern Arc posted record Q4FY26 PAT of INR133 crore (up 251% YoY) and FY26 PAT of INR406 crore, with AUM at INR16,594 crore (up 22% YoY).
544260|2026-03.overview: Northern Arc reported its highest-ever quarterly profit of INR133 crore in Q4FY26, taking FY26 PAT to INR406 crore (up 33% YoY). AUM grew 22% YoY and 10% QoQ to INR16,594 crore, with direct-to-customer (D2C) at 59% of AUM. Credit cost fell to 2.2% in Q4 (from 3.5% in Q3) and 2.8% for FY26, helped by the RBI's FLDG-related ECL clarification, which management said contributed a one-off benefit. Management guided FY27 AUM growth of 22-25% and ROA above 3%, with ROE in the mid-to-late teens over 8-10 quarters.

qa_highlights.answer: Consumer finance is underwritten via scorecards with a 15% risk-adjusted return; MSME average ticket is INR11-15 lakh, yield 17-18%, all with 100% registered mortgage. Management acknowledged the small base inflates growth rates.

qa_highlights.question: Why has ECL coverage fallen, particularly Stage 2 and Stage 3?
qa_highlights.answer: The RBI FLDG clarification (Feb 2026) let the company count FLDG cover in ECL; over 50% of Stage 2 is FLDG-covered. Stage 3 is now mainly secured MSME, given 100% write-off of unsecured loans at 90 DPD.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FLDG reversal one-off, and what is the underlying Q4 credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q4 FLDG benefit was INR29 crore and the INR66 crore overlay is prudence. Adjusting for prior-year provision, the underlying Q4 credit cost would have been about INR120 crore (about 2.9-3%), with 2.7-2.8% as steady state.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for cost of funds and NIM given rate movements?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed-rate share rose from about 30% to 40%; incremental CoF 8.7% vs 9.3%; management expects to hold 8.5-8.6% and NIM to expand as D2C mix rises to 65%. Management expects RBI rate increases in the next couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said yield is 15-16% risk-adjusted; short-tenure book cut to near zero; APR cap introduced; no partner concentration figure given in the call.

qa_highlights.answer: Bank borrowings fell from about 65% of total in March 2025 to about 52% in March 2026, with more offshore, capital market and securitisation (PTC) funding.

544261|2026-03.headline: Arkade posted record Q4 FY26 pre-sales of Rs 303 crore (+40% YoY), but FY26 PAT fell to Rs 5 crore after a Rs 182 crore Filmistan tenancy-rights write-off.

Management flagged the Filmistan project (GDV Rs 3,500 crore) and a Kandivali cluster redevelopment MoU (GDV Rs 1,100 crore) as the next growth drivers. NIM expected in the 13-14% range.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on profitability for coming quarters?

qa_highlights.question: Why was QoQ AUM growth only ~1%?

qa_highlights.question: What are the Namma Loan AUM targets and breakeven?

544262|2026-09.headline: Manba Finance Q2 FY27 PAT rose 20% YoY to INR14 crores, NII up 40% to INR52 crores, AUM up 21% to INR1,811 crores.
544262|2026-09.overview: Manba Finance reported Q2 FY27 net interest income of INR52 crores (up 40% YoY) and PAT of INR14 crores (up 20% YoY), with H1 NII of INR94 crores (up 39%) and H1 PAT of INR27 crores (up 28%). AUM reached INR1,811 crores at September 30, 2026, up 21% YoY, while GNPA improved to 2.96% and NNPA to 2.19%. Management said a rating upgrade to A minus stable from CARE and lower borrowing costs (average cost 10.14%) should support margins, and reiterated 30-35% AUM growth guidance for FY27 despite H1 growth of about 20%. The call was hosted by Antique Stock Broking and included mostly retail-investor questions.

segments.name: 2-wheeler loans
segments.commentary: 83.10% of portfolio; main growth driver in the quarter, supported by dealer network expansion and new locations. Dealer base about 1,900-1,932 across 148 locations in 7 states.

segments.name: Top-up loans
segments.commentary: 5.70% of portfolio; secured against existing 2-wheeler customers, quoted IRR around 32%.

segments.name: 3-wheeler loans
segments.commentary: 3% of portfolio. Battery replacement loan for EV 3-wheelers launched about 2 months ago, limited to own customers and to be tested for 18 months.

segments.name: Used vehicle loans
segments.commentary: 1.60% of portfolio; used 2-wheeler loans quoted at 27-28% IRR, with 100-plus dealers added in the last 6 months.

segments.name: MSME LAP / small business loans
segments.commentary: Small business loan IRR about 27-28%, average ticket INR5 lakh, NPAs 3-4%. MSME LAP disbursement at INR2-2.5 crores per month, targeted at INR5 crores per month by January.

segments.name: Personal loans
segments.commentary: Unsecured, IRR similar to top-up (around 32%); being scaled cautiously through DSAs.

guidance_outlook: AUM and disbursement growth guidance for FY27 of 30-35%; management said H1 AUM growth was about 20% and H2 festive season should close the gap.
Management expects FY28 growth to continue but gave no numerical guidance.

Borrowing costs: about INR600 crores of high-cost borrowings to be repaid by March 2027; management expects about 25 bps overall impact in Q3-Q4 and a 50-75 bps reduction in cost of funds from the rating upgrade.
NIM concern raised by an analyst: prior guidance of 13-14% versus about 12.3% currently; management said NIM would not be hit by the RBI rate hike.
Capital from INR100 crore preferential issue expected by November 6, 2026; management expects capital to support growth for 4-6 quarters.
Interim dividend of INR0.25 per share declared for FY27 (face value INR10).
capex_capacity: INR100 crore preferential issue of equity and warrants; board approved in Q2, principal approval from NSE and BSE received, funds expected by November 6, 2026.

Operations in 148 locations across 7 states (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, UP, Karnataka); about 16 offices added in the last year and 5-6 more small business loan branches planned this quarter.
Karnataka launched about 60 days before the call, with 100-plus dealers onboarded; Karnataka season expected in January.
Technology spend about INR2 crores per year with a 28-person tech team; disbursement turnaround cut from 3.5-4 days to 1.5-2 days, targeted same-day by end of year.
Employee base about 2,061, of which 1,100-plus in sales; 2.45 lakh+ live customers after adding about 32,330 in the quarter.
demand_pricing: Industry: 2-wheeler registrations about 53 lakh units in Q2, with August and September both record highs; September retail registrations up 32% YoY per FADA.
Management expects Diwali and Navratri season to lift H2 disbursements; said October alone added INR120 crores of new AUM after run-down.
Competition in 2-wheeler loans named as IDFC, L&T and regional players such as Berar; management claims about 15% market share in locations operating for 4+ years.
Bounce rate about 18-20%, with 7-8% of customers remaining in bounce across tenure, per management.
NTC (new-to-credit) customers about 40% of the book; LTV capped at 75% for them.

qa_highlights.question: Growth timeline for newer states (UP, MP, Rajasthan) given Gujarat and Maharashtra hold about half the dealer base.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Maharashtra and Gujarat dealer tie-ups are largely complete; new dealer additions are coming from Rajasthan, UP, MP and Karnataka, with 100-plus dealers onboarded in Karnataka in the first 60 days.

qa_highlights.question: How many quarters the INR100 crore raise will support growth, and FY27-28 growth guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Capital should support growth for 4-6 quarters; FY27 guidance is 30-35% growth, with H1 at about 20% and festive season in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is 30-35% AUM growth achievable given H1 AUM growth of about INR98 crores, and any El Nino impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said October added INR120 crores of AUM and similar is expected in November; MSME LAP and small business loans, 5-6 new branches and 10-12 live BC partners were cited as additional drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Operating expenses up 28% YoY in Q2; drivers and cost optimisation.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to 16 new offices in the last year, Karnataka expansion and seasonal sales hiring, and said YoY cost comparison is not a fair measure given the expansion; NIM, average cost and credit cost were said to be improving QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Further cost-of-funds reduction and NIM trajectory (guidance 13-14% vs 12.3% currently).
qa_highlights.answer: About INR600 crores of old high-cost borrowings to be repaid by March 2027; overall impact of about 25 bps expected in Q3-Q4, and new borrowings are at lower rates.

qa_highlights.question: Share of NTC borrowers and delinquency comparison; used vehicle and high-yield products.
qa_highlights.answer: NTC share about 40%; behaviour broadly similar to other customers except those with CIBIL above 750. Used 2-wheeler IRR 27-28%, top-up and personal loan IRR about 32%.

risks_watch: AUM growth of 30-35% requires roughly INR400-450 crores of H2 additions versus H1 growth of about 20%; festive-season delivery is key.
Rising RBI repo rate versus management's expectation of 50-75 bps cost-of-funds reduction from the rating upgrade.
NIM at about 12.3% versus prior 13-14% guidance.
Operating expense growth of 28% YoY in Q2 with ongoing branch expansion.
Concentration in 2-wheeler (83.10%) and unsecured personal loans being scaled up; EV battery replacement product is untested.
Completion of the INR100 crore preferential issue by November 6, 2026.

544263|2026-03.headline: KRN Heat Exchanger FY26 standalone total income rose 57.36% to Rs.689.95 crore; Q4 standalone net profit up 22.69% to Rs.16.87 crore.
544263|2026-03.overview: FY26 standalone total income grew 57.36% YoY to Rs.689.95 crore, with EBITDA up 19.41% to Rs.84.79 crore and net profit up 42.11% to Rs.71.31 crore. Consolidated FY26 total income was Rs.609.81 crore (+38.06%), EBITDA Rs.112.48 crore (+59.52%) and net profit Rs.76.47 crore (+44.62%). Q4 consolidated EBITDA rose 77.56% to Rs.33.55 crore, while Q4 standalone total income rose 55.06% to Rs.204.93 crore. Management said the new Neemrana HVAC facility is still ramping up, with working capital building in inventory and receivables, and a board-approved enabling fund raise of up to Rs.500 crore whose objective is not yet finalised.

financial_highlights.value: Around 3x YoY (per analyst question, not disputed)

segments.name: Heat exchangers (fin and tube, KRN Heat Exchanger)
segments.commentary: Management said the old facility was fully utilised in FY26; fin and tube still accounts for about 95% of revenue, with other products about 5%. Fin and tube growth expected above 80-90%, mainly from data centres.

segments.name: HVAC / new facility (KRN HVAC Products)
segments.commentary: Utilisation of the new facility was about 15% in FY26 for HVAC. Management targets 50% in FY27 and 80% in FY28 across about eight new products and new geometries.

segments.name: Data centre
segments.commentary: Data centre was about 16% of revenue in FY26 per one answer and about 18.7-19% in Q4 per another answer; management expects this to rise quarter on quarter. Top-10 customers include three data centre customers.

segments.name: Bus AC
segments.commentary: Bus AC revenue was about Rs.10 crore in FY26; management targets at least 15% market share in FY27 and has a Rs.150 crore revenue target shown in the presentation, with two to three OEMs onboarded.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export was about Rs.100 crore in FY26 and management aims for roughly double in FY27; export order book is about Rs.120 crore including data centre orders. Geographies cited: UAE, US/North America and Europe.

segments.name: Railways / refrigeration
segments.commentary: Bar and plate heat exchanger approved by Indian Railways for field trial; company says it was L1 in three recent tenders. Full HVAC system for railways needs about 6-8 months of approvals, so limited FY27 contribution expected.

guidance_outlook: New facility utilisation targets: about 50% in FY27 and about 80% in FY28; old facility to stay fully utilised.
Management expects next eight quarters to be the highest ever, with Q4 described as an average quarter and quarter-on-quarter improvement expected.
Export to roughly double in FY27 versus about Rs.100 crore in FY26.

Margins expected to improve slightly, helped by a 5% PLI benefit in FY26, a likely RIFS state incentive of about 1.56% of top line for 10 years on the new facility, export mix and solar power savings, offset by higher depreciation and overheads.
Inventory expected to come under control within about three quarters; minimum six months to normalise per management.
Analyst cited a Rs.2,250-2,850 crore revenue target; management did not confirm the target or its timing.
capex_capacity: New Neemrana facility inaugurated 11 March 2026; production commissioning began May 2025 and the plant was shifted to fully in the week before the call.

Current facility is fully commissioned; about eight new products added, including WOT condenser, roll-bond evaporator, frost-free evaporator, skin condenser, bar and plate, dry air cooler, ammonia evaporator and bus AC, plus new fin geometries.
Further capex on existing facility is about Rs.30-40 crore over the next two years, mainly for line balancing for data centre geometry, per management's rough estimate.
Micro-channel (MCHX) product expected by end 2026 or early 2027; plate-and-plate heat exchanger (CDU) under study for next year.
Solar plant installed and operational.
demand_pricing: Raw material pass-through: management said copper LME, aluminium LME and USD-INR changes are passed to customers on a quarterly basis, with freight and logistics also passed through; it said close to 100% pass-through is possible.
UAE dispatches were disrupted in March 2026 due to the geopolitical situation; dispatches restarted in May 2026. Freight costs rose and are being passed on.
North America and Europe dispatches unaffected per management; Europe is early-stage and North America is larger than Europe for data centre exports.
Company says it competes with European and North American suppliers, not Chinese players, given customised, low-volume products.
Data centre demand: some Indian customers issue one-month firm orders on a rolling basis; one long-lead customer booked six to seven months.
Vertiv vendor approval received after QA audit; billing expected to start in coming weeks or months; Schneider Electric is the biggest domestic data centre customer.

qa_highlights.question: Are new products for liquid-cooled AI data centres in development?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said liquid cooling is early in India; fin and tube remains the core product for chillers and dry coolers, with micro-channel due by end 2026 or early 2027 and plate heat exchanger for CDUs under study.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company pass raw material costs to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said copper, aluminium and USD-INR movements are passed through quarter on quarter and close to 100% can be passed on under current contracts; there is a one-quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory up about 3x and receivables up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about Rs.15-20 crore of UAE material held after March dispatch was blocked, about Rs.8 crore of export dispatched in March but not billed, minimum stock for new products, BIS-related pre-buying of inner groove tube, and new customer onboarding. Normalisation expected in about six months, with inventory days around two and a half months currently.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when internal cash flow may suffice?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IPO proceeds were exceeded by investment in the current facility and working capital will be short; the board approved an enabling resolution up to Rs.500 crore, with objectives not yet concluded. Bank funding is also an option.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 revenue share from products other than fin and tube?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the figure on the call; it said non-fin-and-tube business is about 5% of revenue overall.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bus AC Rs.150 crore target backed by orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two to three OEMs have been onboarded and regular supply has started, with about 15% market share targeted; no specific Rs.150 crore order book was quantified.

risks_watch: Working capital and receivables build-up; inventory normalisation timeline (about six months) and the Rs.500 crore equity raise, whose use is unconfirmed.
BIS certification issue on inner groove tube (deadline around 20-28 May 2026) could drive imports and inventory build-up.
Copper and aluminium price volatility in recent weeks, which management said is beyond expectation; pass-through has a one-quarter lag.
Geopolitical disruption to UAE dispatches and freight costs.
Ramp-up pace of the new facility versus 50%/80% utilisation targets; Q4 incremental revenue from the new facility was about Rs.15-16 crore per an analyst's estimate.
Concentration of data centre revenue (about 16-19%) and dependence on a few large customers such as Schneider Electric.
Depreciation and overhead rising ahead of revenue.

544264|2026-03.headline: Diffusion Engineers Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 38.08% YoY to INR1,415.74 million, with FY27 revenue growth guided above 20%.
544264|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was INR1,415.74 million (+38.08% YoY) and EBITDA excluding other income was INR206.89 million (+39.96%), at a 14.61% margin. Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR4,066.28 million (+21.28%) with PAT of INR504.1 million (+39.87%). Standalone growth was weaker: Q4 revenue +12.18% and Q4 PAT down 3.05%, which management attributed to capacity constraints in wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering running at about 85-90% utilisation. Order book stood at about INR200 crores as of 30 April 2026, up from about INR100 crores a year earlier. New Unit 4 capacity is being commissioned from Q1 FY27 onward.

segments.name: Welding consumables (products)
segments.commentary: Management cited roughly 30% of revenue; under 3% (said 2-3%) of the business is conventional, with the rest special hard-facing and repair electrodes. Wires line at 85-90% utilisation; new wire line expected July 2026.

segments.name: Wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering
segments.commentary: Cited at roughly 30% of revenue combined with heavy engineering; running at 85-90% utilisation, and expected to grow faster than consumables. Roller-press rolls, steel mill rollers and VRM rollers are cited as growth areas; first VRM order won.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Roughly 10% of revenue per management. Covers on-site breakdown repair, hot kiln alignment and bulk deposition, with about 50-60 welding technicians deployed. UAE subsidiary set up for service and overlay work is now operational and expected to contribute from FY27.

segments.name: Railways (developmental)
segments.commentary: L1 in multiple contracts and some letters of intent received for Vande Bharat ecosystem components; execution 6-9 months, with substantial revenue expected from next year at likely lower initial margins.

segments.name: Defence (Tejorup Sunmay Systems)
segments.commentary: Investment made in February 2026 for VSHORADS work; still in prototype stage with a DRDO sanction order for 200 launchers and 1,200 rockets. No revenue expected in FY26 or in FY27 in any significant amount.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected to be more than 20%, supported by capacity additions, order inflows and higher-margin engineered products.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to rise by about 80-100 basis points, aided by operating leverage and cost consolidation; gross margin may come under pressure from raw material volatility.
Medium-term aspiration of INR650 crore-plus revenue at 15-16% EBITDA margin, expected to be reached in under 3 years (2-3 years on annual run-rate basis).

Capex of about INR100 crores from IPO proceeds (INR70 crores for wear part/plate/heavy engineering, INR30 crores for electrode and slitting facility) is expected to support INR800-900 crores revenue; no additional capex planned for INR650 crores.
Debtor days targeted at 80-85 for FY27 and inventory days at 60-65; FY26 debtor days were 98 and inventory days 66.
International revenue share expected to rise to about 15%, with international sales growing above 20%.
capex_capacity: New 10 tons-per-day electrode plant commissioned around November-December 2025, along with an in-house strip-slitting line for flux-cored wires.
Wear plate capacity expanded by about 25% and now commissioned.

Unit 4 (about 170,000-180,000 sq ft) for wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering: partial utilisation from May 2026, most capacity live by end of Q1 FY27 (quarter ending June 2026), with the facility expected to be fully commissioned by end of Q1 2027 per management.
Current utilisation: wires about 85-90%; wear plates and heavy engineering about 85-90%. Management expects utilisation to fall to roughly 50-60% once new shop floors are live.
New wire line expected to be delivered in July 2026.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR200 crores as of 30 April 2026, up from about INR100 crores on 31 March 2025; management expects 80-90% to execute in FY27, with staggered power-project deliveries extending beyond.
Over 80% of revenue from repeat customers; end-market demand from cement, steel, power, mining and engineering described as steady, with no project holds despite the West Asia crisis.

Raw material volatility (tungsten, nickel, cobalt, molybdenum, chromium) is affecting margins; price variation clauses cover under 10% of the order book, with the rest fixed-price contracts. Management books raw materials on order and gives short offer validity on volatile items.
Price increases are ongoing, linked to input costs; management says customers are aware of raw material conditions.

Exports reach more than 35 countries including Southeast Asia, Middle East and Africa; Turkey operations are maturing, a new West Africa partner has been identified, and Singapore sales rose significantly in FY26.
Competitors named: Ador Fontech (merged into Ador Welding) and EWAC Alloys (now part of ESAB) in welding consumables and wear plates; ThyssenKrupp, ISGEC and Walchandnagar in heavy engineering.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone growth flat relative to consolidated, and will it normalise in FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said standalone plants were already at about 85% utilisation, capping execution in wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering; new capacity from Q1 FY27 should lift standalone growth to match consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin volatility (13% to 14.8%) driven by?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to raw material price lags on fixed-price contracts; gross margin may fall, but fixed and operating costs have been consolidated, so net margins improved with scale.

qa_highlights.question: How is the debtor-day gap versus Ador Fontech explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors are at 98 days for FY26 due to large heavy-engineering shipments in March (about INR140 crores of Q4 sales, including roughly INR20 crores of rollers). Target is 80-85 days for FY27; welding consumables are cash-and-carry; heavy engineering is typically 60 days contractually but extends to 75-90 days in practice.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR650 crore revenue target be reached faster, with growth accelerating above 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth to rise as new facilities come online and expects INR650 crores in 2-3 years on run-rate basis; no additional capex is needed for that level, and INR100 crores of capex could support INR800-900 crores.

qa_highlights.question: When will railway and defence businesses contribute meaningful revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Railway developmental orders take 6-9 months to execute, with substantial revenue from next year after approved-vendor listing. Tejorup defence revenue is not expected in FY26 or significantly in FY27, pending prototype approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue contribution from new products such as steel mill rollers and VRM rollers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, citing confidentiality; said steel mill roller revenue was significant last year, a first VRM order has been won, and shredder spare parts are under development.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility (tungsten, cobalt, nickel) on fixed-price contracts; gross margin pressure in FY27 with a lag in passing through costs.
Standalone profitability: Q4 standalone PAT fell 3.05% YoY despite revenue growth, and standalone growth depends on Unit 4 commissioning on schedule by end of Q1 2027.
Receivable days at 98 in FY26 with heavy-engineering payment cycles of 75-90 days; management's 80-85 target needs to be met.
Quarterly concentration: Q4 is seasonally large, and management expects Q4 to remain the biggest quarter.
Tejorup defence and railway developmental businesses carry lower initial margins and long gestation periods.
Management's stated 20%+ FY27 growth and 80-100 bps margin expansion are to be tracked against Q1 FY27 results.

544264|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36.5% YoY to INR1,101.08 million, with order book up 20.4% QoQ to INR209 crores.
544264|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 36.5% YoY to INR1,101.08 million, with EBITDA excluding other income up 33.76% to INR141.54 million. EBITDA margin eased to 12.85% from 13.12%, which management attributed to higher raw material and employee costs as a share of sales. Standalone PAT fell YoY to INR99.79 million, but this reflects a one-time ~INR5 crore subsidiary dividend in the year-ago quarter. The order book reached INR209 crores at 30 June 2026, with more than 80% stated as executable in FY27, and a ~INR100 crore capacity expansion is coming on stream in phases at Nagpur.

segments.name: Heavy Engineering
segments.commentary: Order book of INR159 crores at 30 June 2026. Management says ~70% of heavy engineering is new project build and ~30% spare parts for installed base; capacity being raised from 9,000 to 18,000 metric tons.

segments.name: Wear Plates and Wear Parts
segments.commentary: Order book of INR26.42 crores. Management said growth in Q1 came across consumables, wear plates/parts and heavy engineering.

segments.name: Welding Consumables
segments.commentary: Order book of INR24.22 crores, described as a strong sequential increase driven by customers consolidating yearly requirements. Management said there was no one-off windfall.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Contributes approximately 1.5% to 2% of revenue. Management said it has not yet won competitive bids for subassemblies; Tejorup (10% stake) is developing a VSHORADS prototype.

segments.name: Exports / International
segments.commentary: Management said domestic drove most of Q1 growth because Q1 FY26 had large export orders; Turkey has turned out of loss, and UAE facility is expected to contribute revenue from Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects around 20% growth in FY27 and FY28 and continuing for 3-4 years, with an aim to double revenue in about three years.
EBITDA margin expected to rise 100-200 basis points over FY27 and FY28; management said Q1 margin should return to prior-year Q1 levels.
Management expects Q2 FY27 growth at similar levels to Q1, supported by seasonal monsoon-linked maintenance demand.
More than 80% of the INR209 crore order book is executable in FY27; customers are asking to prepone deliveries.
Railway (Vande Bharat, locomotives) revenue expected to convert within 9-12 months after workshop approval; management said new development items are a longer gestation cycle.
No new capex finalised; management wants to start the next expansion once newly installed capacity reaches 70-80% utilisation.
capex_capacity: Roughly INR100 crore expansion program across electrodes, wear plates and heavy engineering, with new strip slitting capability for backward integration.
Heavy engineering capacity being expanded from 9,000 to 18,000 metric tons (includes wear parts and flux-cored wires used internally); new Nagpur shop floor coming live in phases since Q1.
New capacity expected to contribute from the next quarter, but management said ramp-up will take 2-3 years; electrode capacity started in Q4 FY26 with similar 2-3 year ramp.
About INR67 crore of IPO proceeds still unutilised; management expects full utilisation by year-end, with savings to be redeployed subject to shareholder approval.
Units 1, 2 and 3 have no capacity change; utilisation there was described as 2-3% in one answer, while management said Units 1 and 3 operate at optimal levels.
demand_pricing: Finished steel production grew ~8.3% in April-June 2026 quarter; cement volume growth expected at 7-8% in FY27.

Named Q1 orders: INR9.88 crore VRM/separator parts (cement), INR8.16 crore roller-press rolls, INR10.63 crore roller assemblies, INR7.49 crore flux-cored wire (defence), INR26.31 crore RAPH rotor assembly (power); aggregate ~INR62.47 crore.
Raw material costs: steel up ~20%, some ferro-alloys like tungsten up several hundred percent; management said gross margin compressed by ~1-1.5% and customers have accepted higher prices.
Heavy engineering payment terms: 10-20% advance, 70-80% post-dispatch, balance after warranty documentation.
Top 10 customer concentration not disclosed on call; management said 60-70% expected, to be confirmed later.

qa_highlights.question: Growth drivers across consumables, wear parts, heavy engineering and trading; domestic vs export split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was 30%+ across the three segments, driven by a higher starting order book. Growth was mainly domestic because Q1 FY26 had large export orders that did not repeat.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material volatility and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices remain high but volatility has eased and customers have accepted higher prices. Gross margin contraction was about 1-1.5%, with steel up ~20% and some ferro-alloys up several hundred percent.

qa_highlights.question: Executable portion of the INR210 crore order book in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 80% is executable in FY27, and customers have asked to prepone some deliveries scheduled for next year.

qa_highlights.question: Share of profit from associate (LSN Diffusion) of INR4.4 crore: anomaly or steady?
qa_highlights.answer: Historical run-rate is INR1-2 crore per quarter, so management expects INR1-2 crore going forward and treats the rest of the Q1 amount as a one-off extra.

qa_highlights.question: FY27-28 revenue and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ~20% growth in FY27-28 and an aim to double in three years, with EBITDA margin up 100-200 bps over FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone margin fall from ~18% peak to ~13%, and is Q1 the bottom?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 FY26 standalone PAT included a one-time ~INR5 crore subsidiary dividend. Management expects margins to return to prior-year Q1 levels and rise 100-200 bps over the next 1-1.5 years.

544277|2026-03.headline: Waaree FY26 revenue rose ~84% to INR26,537 crore and operating EBITDA 117% to INR5,909 crore, but Q4 margin fell to ~18.6% on commodity, freight and mix pressures.
544277|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: revenue from operations of INR26,537 crore (+84% YoY), operating EBITDA of INR5,909 crore (22.27% margin vs 18.84%) and PAT of INR3,884 crore (+101%). Q4 revenue was INR8,480 crore (+111% YoY) and operating EBITDA INR1,576 crore, with margin down sharply from the prior quarter as silver and copper costs, freight spikes, lower overseas mix and in-house DCR cell shortfall weighed. Management guided FY27 operating EBITDA to INR7,000-7,700 crore and framed the Waaree 2.0 capex (~$3.5 billion) as the driver, with most cell and module capex completing in FY27 and benefits from H2 FY27 onward. Operating cash conversion fell to about 27% as export shipments were stuck on logistics delays and inventory built up.

segments.name: Module manufacturing
segments.commentary: FY26 production 12.6 GW (+77%), sales about 12 GW; Q4 production 4.2 GW (+104% YoY) and Q4 sales 4.1 GW. Capacity ~26 GW, described as the largest non-Chinese module maker.

segments.name: Cell manufacturing
segments.commentary: Operational cell capacity 5.4 GW (largest in India); Q4 cell production 0.7 GW. A 10 GW cell facility is due in H2 FY27, taking cell capacity to ~15.4 GW.

segments.name: Revenue mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: Utility/IPP/C&I 34.7%, overseas 33%, retail 20.8%, EPC 11.6%. Retail revenue INR5,515 crore (+84%). Q4 overseas share fell to ~21% from ~32% in Q3.

segments.name: US manufacturing
segments.commentary: 1.6 GW plant ramped; 2.6 GW more to go live within six months, taking US capacity to 4.2 GW. IRA benefit ~$0.07/Wp, ~$40 million in FY26, to rise with new capacity.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: ~INR53,000 crore excluding retail (~20% of revenue), up from ~INR47,000 crore a year ago but down ~INR7,000 crore QoQ per analyst. ~65-70% is overseas, to be delivered over 3-4 years. More than INR8,400 crore delivered already.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guided at INR7,000-7,700 crore (about 20-25% growth on FY26 INR5,909 crore).
Management says the margin benefit from in-house DCR cells starts in H2 FY27 when the 10 GW cell line goes live; H1 is a transition.
Long-range planning assumption: 19-20% EBITDA margin sustained for a decade.
Cell utilisation assumed 80-85% for FY28 on 15.4 GW capacity; 28 GW modules, 4 GW inverters, 20,000 MVA transformers and 1 GW electrolyser to run at full throttle in FY28.
Capex of ~$3.5 billion (INR30,000 crore) over the next two years; core module and cell capex complete in FY27, ingot wafer and part of battery in FY28; full Waaree 2.0 benefits seen in FY29.
Cell line transition from M10R to G12R expected to lift output and realisation by 10-12% within about a quarter; module output back to ~330 MW a month within two months.
Investor Day to be held; enabling board resolution for fundraise of up to ~INR10,000 crore approved, with shareholder approval to follow.
capex_capacity: Battery (BESS): 20 GWh planned, phase 1 of 3.5 GWh in FY27 (Gujarat), phase 2 of 16.5 GWh in FY28; capex ~INR10,000 crore.
Ingot wafer: 10 GW at Nagpur, capex ~INR6,200 crore (up from INR5,100 crore earlier with 6 GW to 10 GW); completion FY28.
PV glass: 2,500 TPD approved at ~INR3,900 crore capex, production expected within 24 months; supports ~16-17 GW of modules.
Inverters: 4 GW at Sarodhi, Gujarat (~INR180 crore); 3 GW commissioned, remaining 1 GW in FY27.
Transformers: current ~4,000 MVA; adding 16,000 MVA to reach 20,000 MVA at Alwar (~INR192 crore) in FY27.
Hydrogen: 1 GW electrolyser at Dungri, Gujarat (~INR676 crore capex); electrolyser PLI INR444 crore and hydrogen PLI ~INR510 crore.
Acquired ~55% of Associated Power Structures Ltd (APSL) for ~INR1,225 crore for T&D entry; Oman polysilicon stake acquired for non-Chinese supply.
Module lines: 3 lines converted to G12R (ramping), 3 lines remain Mono PERC, 5 lines still on M10R TOPCon, to convert over about one quarter.
demand_pricing: Domestic DCR module pricing INR21-22/Wp; non-DCR utility INR15-16/Wp, with retail carrying a premium; commodity increases are being passed through to new orders.
Silver and copper cost increases, freight spikes and a lower overseas share weighed on Q4 margin; management said customers are now accepting the higher commodity-linked prices.
ALMM-II (domestic cell mandate) takes effect June 2026; C&I and mid-market decisions were deferred pending clarity, which slowed local offtake.
India installed 44.6 GW of solar in FY26; module consumption was about 50-55 GW. Management sees DCR-compliant cell capacity at ~30 GW for ALMM-II.
US FEOC rules from April 2026 require non-Chinese cells and components, which management says is driving new US orders.
BESS pricing around $110-120/MWh cited for India and US; BESS margin guided at 18-20% before policy support.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating EBITDA margin fall sharply QoQ, and what are the DCR and non-DCR realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited silver and copper cost spikes, freight cost surge, a lower overseas mix and DCR cell shortfall. DCR modules INR21-22/Wp; utility non-DCR INR15-16/Wp, with a retail premium.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the export mix low in Q4 and what is the order book composition?
qa_highlights.answer: Export shipments were stuck on Middle East logistics delays, so inventory rose. About 65-70% of the INR53,000 crore order book is overseas, delivered over 3-4 years; retail (~20% of revenue) is excluded.

qa_highlights.question: How will the FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore be achieved, and what drives margin?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 is a transition from 5.4 GW to 15.4 GW of cells; the 10 GW cell line in H2 lifts in-house DCR supply. Pre-startup costs for new projects are included in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the ingot-wafer capex rise and its timeline move to FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity was raised from 6 GW to 10 GW and sites moved from Odisha to Gujarat and Nagpur, causing the delay. The new figure covers the full 10 GW.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash conversion cycle and working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory built up because overseas shipments were delayed. Customer advances stayed steady but production nearly doubled, diluting working capital days. Management expects cash conversion of 70-100% at normalised inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BESS unit economics and FY29 revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: BESS margin guided at 18-20% without policy support. Management declined to give FY29 revenue guidance, pointing to the 20 GWh capacity and $110-120/MWh pricing.

544280|2026-03.headline: Afcons posted its first-ever quarterly loss (Q4 net loss INR 89 crore) and FY26 PAT fell to INR 251 crore; no FY27 revenue or margin guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 so far below the mid-quarter confidence expressed on the Q3 call, and what drove the miss?

Battery target of about 10 GWh for the next calendar year: roughly 8.5 GWh merchant and 1.5 GWh in FDRE format. Management said the 10 GWh target is achievable on connectivity and financing; supply and geopolitics are the main uncertainties.
Around 2.5 GW of connectivity at operational substations (Fatehgarh-1, Fatehgarh-2 under STOA, Bikaner-3) is ready for BESS discharge at night.
Under-construction portfolio of 5.1 GW (total pipeline 8,071 MW) with PPA-signed capacity of 3,280 MW; PPA-signed projects expected to be commissioned by FY28.
Management expects a run-rate EBITDA jump as battery revenue starts; a 75-80% EBITDA margin is expected on merchant BESS at INR6 tariff arbitrage.
capex_capacity: Committed total capex INR12,475 crore: INR6,445 crore incurred in FY26 and INR6,030 crore in purchase orders. Battery capex was about INR1,000-1,200 crore in Q4.
Gross block rose about INR3,460 crore in FY26, of which about INR1,000-1,100 crore is battery.

Capital advances of about INR323 crore, mainly battery (10% advance against bank guarantee) and turbines (20% advance). Management said solar module capex is being deferred until the LTA is operational.
Under-construction portfolio added 301 MW of peak-power FDRE with SECI in the quarter; total under construction is 5.1 GW, requiring about 17 GWh of BESS.

Commissioning timeline: NTPC hybrid solar ready, LTA by December 2026; Pachora wind component a couple of quarters later; SJVN Fatehgarh full FDRE by FY27 end (LTA March 2027). Pavagada and Anantapur are targeted this year per CTU timelines.
demand_pricing: India peak demand hit 256 GW on 25 April 2026, against 250 GW in May 2024. Electricity consumption grew 8.9% in April 2026.

India added about 55 GW of RE in FY26 (cumulative 283 GW). Management expects peak-power and FDRE/BESS-linked bids to dominate, with 15-20 GW of bids this year (fewer than last year) and state plus central tenders of 20-30 GW.

Management said peak-power products sell fastest, followed by partial peak, then wind; plain solar sells slowest. Thermal-equivalent BESS pricing is cited at INR9-10 per unit at peak, with the annual realisation at INR7-8.
Receivable days have fallen to about 14-15 days from about 180 days in the past. Trade receivables fell 13% YoY. Central offtakers take a cash discount and pay in about 10 days.

qa_highlights.question: What battery capex was incurred and how much BESS capacity was commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Battery capex was about INR1,000-1,200 crore in the last quarter, and about 1.3 GWh was commissioned as of the prior quarter. Battery capacity reached 2.3 GWh by the time of the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the run-rate EBITDA from existing capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 EBITDA including other income was about INR2,200 crore, mainly from the PPA projects. BESS revenue at INR2.2 crore per day is over INR60 crore per month.

qa_highlights.question: Is there curtailment, and how is future project allocation shaped?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about 2 projects are connected to the state grid. FY26 curtailment impact was INR5-6 crore, plus INR3 crore of STU impact in Rajasthan. Nearly all of the portfolio is on CTU, with the goal that each project has a battery.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross block growing faster than run-rate EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,000-1,100 crore of the gross block increase is battery, and the battery was commissioned late in the year, so it is not yet in run-rate EBITDA. Wind is also still ramping in phases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk from LOA conversion and CERC connectivity rules?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 6.2 GW of signed PPAs are under construction, and 3.2 GW of LOA has converted to PPA. Management does not expect LOAs to be surrendered, and it has a backup plan of using connectivity for future bids or battery-linked projects.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the BESS arbitrage last?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the duration is uncertain. It estimated the national need at about 200-300 GWh, and said the peak price should stay at INR7-8 for four to five years given gas constraints.

qa_highlights.question: Are CTU substation delays affecting commissioning?

544283|2026-06.headline: ACME Solar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 63% YoY to INR954 crore and EBITDA 56% to INR831 crore, with BESS contributing INR226 crore.
544283|2026-06.overview: Management reported record revenue and EBITDA for Q1 FY27, with total revenue of INR954 crore (up 63% YoY), EBITDA of INR831 crore (up 56%) and PAT of INR235 crore (up 80%). Growth was attributed to a record CUF of 30.9%, BESS revenue and new renewable capacity. BESS commissioning reached about 3.62 GWh cumulative, and the BESS commissioning guidance was pulled forward to more than 10 GWh by FY27 from calendar 2027. Management also said it has locked in about INR1,400 crore of short-term BESS revenue for FY27 and addressed a fire at the ACME Suryodaya BESS site, attributing it to an AC cabling short circuit rather than the battery system.

financial_highlights.change: Lower due to charging power cost in opex

segments.commentary: EBITDA margin ~88-89% in Q1; ex-BESS EBITDA margin stated at ~91%, with seasonal range of 88-91% over recent quarters. Management cited repowering of existing plants as a margin support.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: Revenue INR226 crore in Q1 with ~82% EBITDA margin; cumulative commissioned capacity ~3.62 GWh (about 40% of India's cumulative commissioned BESS). Management cites an annual EBITDA-to-capex yield above 20%.

guidance_outlook: BESS commissioning target raised to more than 10 GWh by FY27 (earlier: 10 GWh by calendar 2027), roughly three quarters earlier.
Around 1.5 GW of contracted renewable capacity to be commissioned in FY27, subject to substation and transmission availability.
Full-year FY27 capex upgraded to approximately INR15,000-20,000 crore.
About INR1,400 crore of BESS revenue locked for FY27 on roughly 70-80% of the ~10 GWh target; management said it could be higher if more volume is contracted.
Management indicated a 2-3 year assumption of INR1,400 crore-plus BESS revenue is reasonable; BESS EBITDA margin expected within 2-5% of Q1 level (~82%).
Management said it may increase its 2030 target beyond 10 GWh, to be updated in coming quarters.
capex_capacity: Total portfolio 8,070 MW, with about 20 GWh of battery storage; under-construction capacity 5,080 MW.
PPAs signed for 3,880 MW, including 600 MW of new FDRE and hybrid PPAs with SECI this quarter; about 1,200 MW still awaiting PPA signing.
Debt tied up for about 85% of PPA-signed portfolio; INR6,000 crore financing secured for 700 MW of under-construction FDRE projects.
Battery procurement: more than 15 GWh ordered (CATL, Hithium); around 90% of the 20 GWh battery requirement contracted, with orders placed where PPAs are signed.

BESS capex ~INR93 lakh per MW including transformer, IDC and EPC; management said it could rise 5-10% for future batches. More than $300 million hedged at roughly $89-93 per unit of USD exchange rate.
Battery operations: round-trip efficiency ~89%, depth of discharge ~93%, state of health above 99.9%, availability above 99%; operating at one cycle per day.
demand_pricing: India power demand grew 8.8% YoY in Q1 to 485 billion units; peak demand hit a record 271 GW and was near 270 GW in July.
Short-term BESS realisations cited at INR8-10/kWh (publicly available DEEP portal and HP-TAM bids), sometimes higher; contracts are typically under one year, with 6-9 months' lead time.
Open (merchant) BESS capacity is about 600 MWh; management aims for zero open capacity outside PPA by end-2026, though a 300 MW plant is still open.

SECI is consolidating bids and will only bid with firmer power-offtake commitments, reducing near-term bid volumes; management expects large FDRE, peak power, CFD and state bids to follow over 6-9 months.
Management sees the peak-power market growing toward 300-500 GWh, potentially 1 TWh in a positive case, driven by rooftop and KUSUM solar (duck-curve effect).
Competition from other BESS entrants (including Adani) is rising, but management argues merchant supply will remain limited and that the market is still new to state buyers.

qa_highlights.question: How much open or early BESS capacity will there be in FY27 and the next couple of years, and what are realisations on the INR1,400 crore short-term contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is contracting well above 10 GWh and realisations are INR8-10 per unit, depending on month and volume. Only ~600 MWh is open today, with a target of zero open capacity outside PPAs by end-2026. Management plans for 10-12 GWh to remain available for short-term markets each year over the next five years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the curtailment impact and what drove EBITDA growth ex-BESS?
qa_highlights.answer: Curtailment was about 1% of revenue, only on state-based projects. EBITDA growth was attributed to CUF (30.9% vs 28.5%) and repowering of existing plants. Management is considering adding batteries to state projects to absorb surplus generation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR1,400 crore revenue sustainable for 2-3 years, given El Nino-driven pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees the 10 GWh base supporting INR1,400 crore-plus for the next 2-3 years based on PPA and GNA timelines. Beyond that, it depends on market pricing and new PPAs. It said the market is still untapped by most discoms.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core (ex-BESS) EBITDA margin and the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Ex-BESS margin was ~91% in Q1, with a seasonal range of 88-91%. Management expects FDRE projects may lift margins because their realisations are healthier than plain solar.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 6.28 INR/kWh PPA and the hybrid configuration changed?
qa_highlights.answer: The hybrid project was offered with 1 hour of battery, a change from the standard configuration. The other project at INR6.28 per unit has no change in configuration.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for C&I and data centres?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has started hiring for data-centre opportunities but is focused on profitability. It intends to target CTU-connected C&I customers and will not dilute mid-to-high teen return targets.

544285|2026-03.headline: Swiggy's Q4 FY26 call: Instamart dark-store CM turned positive at top cities (~3%), but Q4 quick-commerce overheads of ~INR700-715 crore per quarter and negative operating cash flow remain the key concerns.
544285|2026-03.overview: Management said the quarter's improvement came from a stop to the No Fee experiment (around the third week of January), fewer low-AOV orders (halved in the year), and reversal of monetisation experiments, which lifted NOV-to-GOV and contribution margin. Quick commerce contribution margin moved about 180 bps over the period, with a ~110 bps exit-March level, and management expects the ~180 bps level to be reached again in April. Management reiterated a profitability-first stance, saying it will not buy volumes, and framed a INR 1 lakh crore NOV ambition over 3.5-5 years (35-50% CAGR in the commerce business). Toing (a separate low-AOV app), 99 store, and EatRight are included in core financials and are in testing. Management declined to guide on MTU trajectory in Q1, noting that MTU is a net figure after churn.

544285|2026-06.headline: Swiggy guides Quick Commerce contribution margin to 0 to -100 bps for growth, with 4-week cumulative NOV growth at 10% vs 1% prior.
544285|2026-06.overview: Swiggy's Q1 FY27 call (held July 30, 2026) centred on a deliberate pivot from contribution-margin protection to growth in Quick Commerce (Instamart). Management said it reached contribution margin breakeven, closing the last quarter at -0.2%, and now guides to a 0 to -100 bps range to fund store expansion, speed, serviceability and assortment. Take-rate gains were attributed to brand monetisation, advertising and user-fee changes, with management calling them sustainable. Food delivery growth was about 18% adjusted for cancellations, with 18-20% YoY guidance maintained, and management dismissed zero-commission competition from Toing's rivals as unsustainable. Toing, the new value-led food platform, is loss-making and was a major focus, with a Capital Markets Day planned for the following week.

segments.commentary: Adjusted growth about 18% YoY; YoY guidance 18-20% maintained. Take rate about 3%, with a target of 5%; management expects steady margin accretion.

Capital Markets Day / Investor Day scheduled the following week to cover Toing in more detail.

Some hyper-local stores are capacity-constrained at 2,500-3,000 orders per day, driving the new store additions.

Toing uses lower commissions than Swiggy so restaurants can offer everyday low prices; management says commission will not be zero in practice.

Instamart delivery-fee line in fully loaded revenue appeared to be zero this quarter versus about INR3 per order previously (analyst observation); management did not confirm and referred to the adjusted revenue walk on page 16.

qa_highlights.question: How should we think about QC strategy: growth at expense of margin or vice versa, and what is the take-rate sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prioritises growth within a 0 to -100 bps CM band. Take-rate gains come from brand negotiations, advertising and user-fee monetisation, which management says will not reverse.

qa_highlights.question: Is the food delivery zero-commission model a threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit Kapoor argued zero commission is not sustainable; costs must be recovered from restaurants, consumers or delivery partners. Competition is expected in affordability, not premium.

qa_highlights.question: Wage hike and last-mile cost escalation?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual salary revision sits below CM. Minimum wage hikes in some states affect picking and packing; impact described as not material. Last-mile cost rose on seasonal factors including elections and harvest migration; efficiency offset kept the YoY dip to 20 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Are competitors capitalising costs or securitising payables?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Bothra said Swiggy does not capitalise employee, tech token or store costs, and is not aware of payables securitisation practices by peers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Instamart growth plan and store expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth from transacting users and frequency; more stores in existing cities as hyper-local stores hit 2,500-3,000 orders/day. Spend priorities are store expansion, speed and serviceability, and selection availability.

qa_highlights.question: Why did platform frequency decline and is private-label conflict with ads a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it culled low-value MTUs over recent quarters, and QC's lower frequency dilutes the blended metric. Private brands carry higher margins and are experience-driven, so conflict with ads was not seen as material.

544285|2026-09.headline: Swiggy Q2 FY27: Quick commerce NOV grew 13.4% QoQ with 1.3 million MTUs added, while Toing investment stays range-bound and food margin target of 5% of GOV is reaffirmed.
544285|2026-09.overview: Management reported a return to growth in quick commerce, with NOV up 13.4% QoQ, 1.3 million MTUs added, and orders per dark store per day up about 9% sequentially to close to 1,200. Food delivery guidance of 18-20% YoY growth on the standalone business was reiterated, with Adjusted EBITDA up about INR 50 crore for the quarter and take rate above 26%. Toing, the affordability platform, is being run as a range-bound investment; management asked for another quarter or two before judging whether it is a scalable model. Quick commerce contribution margin guidance is 0 to -100 bps, with 100 bps Adjusted EBITDA improvement guided for Q3, and a move to an inventory model starting mid-quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is Toing an experiment or ready to scale, and what metrics decide this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management asked for another one to two quarters before deciding. Metrics are repeat-user unit economics in early cities, customer acquisition cost as the base expands, and delivery cost reduction; investment is discretionary and range-bound.

544286|2026-03.headline: Niva Bupa FY26 GWP grew 27.4% to INR9,433 crores and IFRS PAT rose to INR366 crores; FY29 combined ratio target ~99%.
544286|2026-03.overview: FY26 closed with 27.4% overall GWP growth to INR9,433 crores (retail +35%) and Ind AS PAT of INR366 crores versus INR203 crores, with ROE at 10.7%. Expense of management fell to 33.7% from 39.2%, and the IFRS combined ratio improved 160 bps to 101.4% despite a 1.1 pt rise in loss ratio. Retail market share rose to 10.1% for the full year and 10.4% in Q4. Management set a long-term IFRS combined ratio target of about 99% by FY29, which it says translates to a mid-to-high teens ROE. Commission regulation remains an open question pending regulator guidance.
